Bautista says his plush toys are true summonings: pull the tag, and the real creature arrives. Carl's Kimaris is a demon.
Kimaris is one of the brothers of Sheol, and once summoned he stays for the rest of the floor. He is also one of Samantha's best friends, and she calls him Kimmy.

entities.name: The Midnight Epicure
aka: The Caprid Who Devours the Sky
entities.role: A caprid fable, and Prepotente's god

taglines.text: The Midnight Epicure, the Caprid Who Devours the Sky, is a fable used to frighten children into eating their dinner. His symbol, a goat's head, is worn as a ward against the night.
The Midnight Epicure is the god Prepotente worships, and on live television the caprid council panics and cries out that they shall manifest him.

According to Prepotente, the Midnight Epicure protects all prey by destroying existence, after releasing everything ever eaten back into the galaxy. It began as a xenophobic scare story about caprids, and caprids made it a symbol of hope.
York wrote the tenth edition of the Cookbook: pages of rambling philosophy, and a last entry about being surrounded by his hive and alone in it.
York came from a hive and felt alone all his life. The author of the eleventh edition read him, felt a kinship, and wondered whether he survived.
York is in orbit with a job from Rosetta: shoot down an orc yacht with children aboard. She hopes he does it, rather than writing a poem about it.
York, a level-71 tenodera, is the only living creature aboard the Homecoming Queen. He vaporised the orc yacht with a point-defence beam and hoped to feel something afterwards. He did not.
Princess Chandra, Esquire, has been assigned as Princess Donut's lawyer in Quasar's place. According to Quasar, she is also Carl's new wife.

Princess Chandra is Rishi's widow. She used an old Naga law to claim her husband's killer as her new husband and made herself Princess Donut's attorney. Donut read every filing and called her a sad little snake.
Princess Chandra has been in hiding since Princess Donut put a hit on her, and her filings keep coming. The Taurins she hired went after Quasar's family and found his niece armed.
Grigori the Placid is a level-93 human Fleshmancer, a mercenary hired by Team Meadow Lark, and a worshipper of Gula. He sits bolt upright with a cappuccino, flicking cookie crumbs off his blue robes.

Grigori now belongs to Carl's guild, hired to join the two halves of a split mantaur. The spell is not difficult if both halves are willing, he says, though he has never cast it and is looking forward to seeing the result. He has also been ordered to learn to drive.
Grigori joined the two halves of a mantaur in the back of a moving truck, upside down on the ceiling, while trying not to be sick.

Grigori has survived the race, though he has just been told that the court's mercenaries always die. He is no mere fleshmancer, he says, but the most renowned flesh sculptor this dungeon has ever known, and Samantha has dragged him off to examine her for a new body.
Grigori is a dungeon-born NPC, so at the parade the AI took him over. Now it speaks with his voice and looks out through his eyes.
The AI has let go of Grigori, and he stumbles, confused, back toward the crawlers' garage. Orren cannot pull a diagnosis off him: the AI has locked Orren out.

entities.name: Chalchiuhtlicue
entities.role: Goddess · among the children in Lucia Mar

taglines.text: Chalchiuhtlicue is a goddess newly present among the children inside Lucia Mar. She tells them she is kind and will protect them, and that the kindest thing may be to let them die.

Chalchiuhtlicue, whom Samantha calls Chachi, is a goddess of childbirth, water and fire who has never been sponsored. According to Samantha, she is always talking about saving children, right before she kills them all.
Lamashtu is so far only a name on a scroll in a list of prizes, the Milk of Lamashtu, and Carl has no idea what it does.
Lamashtu is a former god whom the AI has subjugated. With no worshippers left, her level has been halved, and she is now a parade mount in a showgirl headdress. Samantha recognises her as a friend.
Crawler Forkith left a comment in the twentieth edition of the Cookbook, confirming that a smoke curtain soaked in healing potion clears a room of undead.
Forkith wrote the twentieth edition of the Cookbook and reached at least the eleventh floor. One of his notes mourns his little sister, Barkith, who was all he had left.
Forkith is a small demon in Sheol who has separated himself from the code. He is friends with Pontiff, and sort of with Carl, and he has put a leech on Louis so that he can survive down here.
Mukta is Zev's substitute for the day. Zev had booked the crawlers on Dungeon Crawl Tactics, and Mukta has overridden her and picked a programme that pays a higher fee.
Administrator Mukta put two crawlers on the Maestro's show and told them to take their seats or be accelerated.
Mukta, the substitute who booked the Maestro's show, is a member of the Bloom, the party that runs Borant, and party members are treated much better.
Mukta, the kua-tin who booked the Maestro's show, is dead. One of Lucia Mar's dogs ate Mukta, and Zev can still hear the screaming.
Manasa is a cobra-headed pop singer. The real Manasa died long ago, and she contracted with the Valtay Corporation to keep her career going after her death.
Manasa traded trailers with the crawlers so that they could use her cleaning machine, and she died in theirs, hit by a pulse meant for them. Her final performance was a sad soprano, sung a cappella.
A Skull Empire pulse aimed at two crawlers killed Manasa instead, and the Valtay answered by killing the Maestro.
Gordo is the Bopca protector at the Belly-Rubbed Pug. He has just met the crawlers' manager, and he cannot believe that is really their manager.
Gordo fetches walnuts the moment Princess Donut asks. Mordecai dosed him with a potion so that he could search his kitchen for the newsletter.
Heather was once a black bear. She lies asleep in the road under a spell, with a pink clown hat grown into her head, and Signet has captured her many times but never yet used her blood.

Heather the Bear was a level-19 neighbourhood boss who had performed at Grimaldi's circus since she was a cub, caught in its loop for two centuries. Carl beat her alone, and her blood raised Signet's paper army.

entities.name: GumGum
entities.role: Orc · regular at the One-Eyed Narwhal

taglines.text: GumGum is a level-5 orc who drinks alone at the One-Eyed Narwhal, her shirt stained red like a butcher's. She asked the crawlers for help, and wept when she was turned down.
GumGum asked the crawlers to find out who was killing the town's women. Now she lies dead in an alley with her chest torn open.
GumGum carried the dead women out of town and asked why they were dying. The elves of the 201st tortured her for the crawlers' name, and she died in an alley.
Ricky Joe is a level-2 juvenile fathom dwarf whose pet salamander, Benjamin, went into Mongo twice. So did his right arm, below the elbow.
Ricky Joe has one arm and a twice-eaten salamander, and he has seen a skyfowl lady leave with a group of other women. Now his mother is in labour next door, and he is in charge of her left leg.
Burgundy is a young, dark-haired human carrying papers up the magistrate's stairs, with one pale blue eye and one brown. She wishes the crawlers luck.
Burgundy came to town for work at the Desperado Club. By day she was an assistant and by night a flying head, and she begged to be killed while she was still mortal.
Levi the Seventh is a level-7 Troll Flesher and Hobgoblin Skellie Symbiote, and the engineer of the Dismemberment Limited. He begs crawlers not to get on.
Levi the Seventh is still the seventh. One party held the fleshers off him for a whole trip and took the war mage's head, and he waved as the train pulled away.
Limp Richard is a level-36 Mole Man who runs Limp Richard's Sundries at transfer station 83. He reads in his doorway, as his kind do day and night.
Limp Richard has fifteen books, all read to pieces, and a Battery Fabricator in a dusty corner at seventy-five thousand gold, not negotiable.
Limp Richard let the Battery Fabricator go for a stack of westerns and a jug of moonshine, and practically begged Carl to take it.
Silfa is a level-25 Wisteria Fairy and Holistic Healer who rides with Brynhild's Daughters. She is plump, looks about fifty, is half the size of the cat, and heals only when she is told to.
Silfa held back her heals on Eva's orders, and Carl reckons she was left in the car as bait. She owns a bakery, and the two mages waiting outside are her own daughters.
Silfa formed a new party with Eva and took her two daughters with her, and according to Katia, Eva got all three of them killed.

Widget is a level-19 grease gremlin and steam engine technician, working a trainyard overrun with ghouls. His wife makes a nice stew, and he likes a lass with meat on her bones, which the cat hears as being called fat.
Widget told the crawlers about the Escape Velocity line and set them on their route. Then a ghoul that was not as dead as it looked ripped his head off.
Crawler Coolie wrote the nineteenth edition of the Cookbook, and his advice on deities is to avoid every kind of summoning. In his short experience, they all ended with the summoner dead.
Coolie hid bugbear paste in his boots and blew up a ship in orbit to kill two admins, and the two admins were only holograms. His last note was written looking down at his home planet, Qurux.
Coolie died after a failed attempt on two admins, and his last view was of his own planet from a ship in orbit. Now Carl is looking down on Earth the same way, and he thinks of him.
Priestly wrote the fourteenth edition of the Cookbook and is its single best source on the ninth floor. When Carl weighs his own plan, he knows that Coolie would do the same, and Priestly would not.
Priestly loved Larracos, a living, breathing poem of a city, and he broke when he saw it destroyed. His last entry is an incoherent jumble.
Priestly was conscripted into the bugbears' army in the final days of Faction Wars. According to another author's note, he never reached the battle.

Edict is a level-50 mantis merchant of the Dark Hive. Every choice left to him would ruin either him or his hive, so he found a fourth: he threw a punch at Carl and was teleported away naked, leaving a metric ton of gold behind.
Sierra was Viscount Fog's flying mount, a level-65 northropi vampire turned by the very thing they hunted. Carl fell out of the sky onto her and drove a jagged branch through her heart.
Prudence is a level-28 ursine barmaid, hiding behind her counter with her two cubs while Big Tina roams outside. Tina has already eaten her husband, and Prudence knows why Tina hunts.
Prudence, widowed by Big Tina, is sheltering with her cubs, Randy and Todd, in Carl's guildhall.
Prudence, the barmaid who told Carl the story of Tina's recital, died protecting two children when the mantises came.
Gideon is a crawler with some sort of human tank class who is active in the chats. Princess Donut likes him because he once said he was allergic to dogs.
Gideon is not in the top thousand, and he likes it that way. His team is waiting in the woods outside the castle, ready to assault the front if needed.
Gideon and almost thirty crawlers stayed in the woods outside the castle to sow chaos, because Carl asked them to. They died there.
Horton is a mushroom crawler at the queen's party who is afraid of Elle. When she shouts that Ferdinand's hat is his merch, he gives her the finger from across the room.
Horton was the talent show's second-to-last act. He played 'Wonderwall' on a guitar missing a string, and the building shook.
Horton, the mushroom crawler who played 'Wonderwall' at the queen's party, died in the fight that followed.

entities.name: Everly
entities.role: Author of the fifth edition of the Cookbook

taglines.text: Crawler Everly wrote the fifth edition of the Cookbook, and her verdict on hiring mercenaries is that it is a disaster: 1,500 gold a day each, payable for the rest of the floor even after they die.
Everly's last entries tell of a sponsor who kept her alive and a gift she dared to hope for. Then: I take it all back.

Everly was a Sward Mantis and an Explosives Engineer. Her sponsor's compass led her to the top of a tower on the eighth floor that was only an advertisement, and she was crushed to death on the way down.

entities.name: Toyotomi
entities.role: Sai mercenary · Sergeant in the Princess Posse

taglines.text: Toyotomi is a level-70 Sai mercenary leader, a rhinoceros inherited along with the Prism's castle. His squad died at the Desperado Club and he refuses to lead men now, and Rend has just eaten his boot.
Toyotomi is a sergeant in the Princess Posse, leading Li Na's builder squad, and his next job is the tall synergy tower they are calling the Nest.
Toyotomi died defending the Nest's door against a crawler with a dog, cleaved in half by a spell. Bomo will regenerate. Toyotomi will not.

Kandy "Bigs" Newton is a level-29 sluggalette of the Princess Posse who burst out of Carl's slugpox and planted a hatchet between Vinata's eyes. The System credits her with the kill on the Sepsis Whore.
Bigs rides in uninvited on other people's mounts, asking who she gets to chop, and she has to be told not to kill the prisoners.

Bigs has come down to the tenth floor with the Royal Court, where she counts as a mercenary and not a pet, so the enchanted hats are not for her. She has had girl talk with Samantha, got orange goo all over the borrowed carpet, and been invited to the bachelorette party.
The sluggalo code is unity, support, family, and kneecapping bitches. Bigs calls Carl daddy-o, and she holds him to all four.

Bigs is no longer the only sluggalo to come out of Carl's slugpox: Lil' Mello Haze has burst from his back as well, a level above her. At the parade the sluggalos rained from the airship onto the masked crowd in the stands, and Bigs has never been so proud.

Bigs and the sluggalos took the chicken truck's wheel from Tipid and made it the Sluggalo Chick-Chick Express, deep fryer on against orders. About ten of them are still in it when the killing stops, and they have lost Hedy.
Burcu is new to the top ten: a level-59 Porsuk swashbuckler with the head of a badger. She fought Osvaldo and Prepotente after Imogen's death at the close of the last floor.

Burcu is Turkish and very serious, and she was one of the three who fought over the memorial crystal. Tonight her drunk, jealous teammate punched Carl and promised that his Burcu is going to kill him.
Burcu's whole team seems to have been taken in by the Madness, and nobody can reach them. That most likely means conscription.
Architect Houston cut out Burcu's tongue and voice box, and he murdered her mother in front of her. She died in his theatre when the traps fired, looking at Carl with accusation in her eyes.

entities.name: Pater Coal
entities.role: High Cleric Supreme of Emberus · Club Vanquisher

taglines.text: Pater Coal is a level-101 Hobbledehoy, the High Cleric Supreme of Emberus at Club Vanquisher and one of the few mortals in constant contact with the god. He washes Carl's feet in boiling water, because Carl is a martyr of Emberus, and he does not always do his own talking.
Pater Coal arranged a loan from the church for Carl's new ring: 990,000 gold, interest-free for martyrs, with an asterisk. While he owes it, Carl may not renounce his religion.
Pater Coal was the first body Carl watched the AI wear. Now it is wearing Growler Gary.

Raul is a level-70 red Maníseros land crab and a Sun-Kissed Cloud Rank warrior, meditating on top of a crashed box truck on the eve of the Chowder War. After years of cultivation, he is on the verge of a breakthrough.
Raul the crab is a totem card in Princess Donut's deck. He fights well, chants his slow spells and grovels to everybody, and he and Geraldo come to blows on sight.
Raul has been summoned onto a beach full of corpses and told that his people are dead, that he is the last of them, and that he must fertilise the eggs right now, in front of everyone.
Raul has ascended to level 110, and his card is mythic now: ten minutes per summoning, and a much deeper voice. He still calls Carl Daddy.
Jola is a mythic totem card from Iceland, one of Katia's spares, and Princess Donut was delighted to put him in her deck.

Jola the Yule Cat is a fat, dirty-brown Persian the size of a house, with a candle as big as a garbage can burning on his head that reveals anything hidden. He speaks only Icelandic, which nobody present understands.
Jola's Fashion Critic blew every stitch of clothing off Quan Ch, and the cat meant to eat the lot. When Carl took Quan's cloak, Jola hissed at him and crouched to pounce.

People call him Paulie, but his real name is Goff. He is a Residual living in a homeless man's body at a shelter, and he gives the same speech over breakfast every day, in case a crawler is ever standing there to hear it.

In frozen time, Paulie told Carl the rest: when crawlers die, what is inside them is harvested to feed the centre system, and a drink of his coffee installs a menu that can blow the star. Then the Paulie part of him asked Carl to be sure.

entities.name: War Leader Arief
entities.role: Semeru war leader · Larracos Defense Force

taglines.text: War Leader Arief is a young, level-80 Semeru dwarf with a long thin moustache, wearing his great-great-grandfather's hat. He is the first NPC Carl has heard call himself an NPC out loud.

War Leader Arief guides the party down the rings of Larracos, which are numbered from the bottom. He means to take revenge on Architect Houston, who caught his brother sabotaging the Madness fortifications.
War Leader Arief stands guard at Juice Box's door, relays messages to the NPC spies, and runs the dwarven diggers whenever she is away.

entities.name: Dante
entities.role: Former crawler · Trap Master guild instructor

taglines.text: Dante was a crocodilian former crawler, a guild instructor fourteen seasons short of freedom, who wrote a single entry in the cookbook's third edition. He was reassigned to guard an ice castle, refused to follow orders, and is dead.
Dante was ordered twice to kill the ice elves he guarded, and he refused twice. There was no third warning: a beam came from the sky and erased him.
Volteeg's only note in the seventh edition of the cookbook says he misses her so much, and asks whether surviving this place is worth it with her gone. He does not think it is.

Volteeg was a pet songbird who became a gargoyle crawler, and then a Weeper commander for the Operatic Collective. He filled his tank with humming energy balls, put on Mozart, and drove it into his own warlord's caravan.
Rectrix is a sponsor whom Baroness Victory has reminded, along with the Maestro, that making a deity act outside its nature is against the rules.
Rectrix is the Open Intellect's agent and is driving the goddess Theia this season, which is why Samantha found a male skyfowl in her mother's temple.
Nami is a model and influencer who outbid the Priory to drive the goddess Eris. She had surgery to look and sound just like Hekla, and now she wants out.
Someone stripped Eris's soul armour and threw Nami out of the goddess. She landed in the grass outside the ball of flesh, and the fleshers took her.

entities.name: Fopsy
entities.role: Adjutant for the Dream · former Prime Minister

taglines.text: Former Prime Minister Fopsy is the Dream's adjutant: a tripod, a round body covered in black dots on three long, jointed legs. He observes, and keeps his theories to himself.
Fopsy says he had no idea that his own client was a robot, and if the vote goes a certain way, he may be Prime Minister again.
Fopsy was passed over for the vacant office of Prime Minister, because nobody was certain of his relationship to the Dream. Victory has the job instead, for now.
Quemada is a level-96 fire fairy, the protection in team Helix, a three-for-one mercenary squad. She speaks with a thick Spanish accent, and she has just tripled her price.
Since the elf mage spoke, Quemada no longer knows what is real, and her panic heats the cab by the moment. Finley has had to put her to sleep.
Quemada never woke. Finley was carrying her to a temple, so that she would not wake alone, when an APV hit him in the street, and Olga and Quemada died with him.

entities.name: Minus
entities.role: Syndicate security soldier · the tourist who was not Linus

taglines.text: Minus is a soother and a soldier of Syndicate security, sent into the crawl under the name of his dead brother, Linus. He has a primary target, a secondary target, and orders to act the pervert for a while.
Minus, the tourist who was not really Linus, was outed at the crawlers' farewell gathering by the fan club he had been imitating. His first target was Imani, and his second was Louis.
The AI has told the whole dungeon that Linus was replaced by his brother, a soldier sent to kill two crawlers and break what the rest have built. Princess Donut's only question: his name was Minus?

Tempest is Quasar's niece, a young Nullian with a school report due on the crawl, and she has been assigned Carl and Donut. Her uncle makes her pay for his recap by fixing a sink she knows nothing about.
When Taurins came to the house on a contract and hurt her father, Tempest fired the very illegal blaster her uncle had given her, and she was the one left standing.

entities.name: The Gate of the Feral Gods

taglines.text: The Gate of the Feral Gods is said to be buried in the long-lost Necropolis of Anser. A bugbear submarine captain spent close to twenty years looking for it, and an artifact of this grade has no business turning up this early.

descriptions.text: New Quest. The Gate of the Feral Gods. Henrik the Changeling. Commandant Kane. The Mad Dune Mage. They all have pieces of the artifact. Take it from them. Collect all three. Put them together. What happens next is pretty damn neat. Reward: Oh boy-oh-boy.

taglines.text: Carl's Doomsday Scenario is a soul crystal going off inside a Sheol Glass Reaper Case, big enough to flatten forty-five square kilometres. It can no longer be stabilized, and it will explode the instant it leaves his inventory.

descriptions.text: Carl's Doomsday Scenario. Type: Unstable custom explosive. Effect: An explosion large enough to rattle the teeth of a god. Status: Explosion Imminent. Created by a man who murders babies and steals rare collectibles from his elders, this device is powerful enough to level an entire city and all the suburbs around it. It is created by combining a massively overloaded soul crystal and a Sheol Glass Reaper Case. Warning: This item can no longer be stabilized.

entities.name: Enchanted Crown of the Sepsis Whore

taglines.text: The Enchanted Crown of the Sepsis Whore is a tiara with a clouded purple stone at its centre. Putting it on places the wearer permanently in the line of succession for the Blood Sultanate on the ninth floor, and Donut put it on before Mordecai could finish warning her.

descriptions.text: Enchanted Crown of the Sepsis Whore. Who's a dirty girl? You're a dirty girl! This is a Fleeting item! This is a Unique* item! Imbues wearer with +5 Intelligence, grants the user +5 to the Good First Impression Skill. All attacks, including magical attacks, now have a 15% chance to inflict the Sepsis Debuff. Warning! (Seriously though. I'm going to say this again. WARNING! Read this shit before you put it on.) Placing this crown upon your head permanently places you within the royal line of succession for the Blood Sultanate on the ninth floor of the world dungeon. Removing this item will not remove this status. Royal members of the Blood Sultanate will be required to slay the Sultan and all other members of the royal family before descending to the tenth floor. You'll only want to wear this if you're a blood-thirsty, raging psychopath.

taglines.text: The Dungeon Anarchist's Cookbook came off a prize carousel looking like a joke book of chicken and goblin recipes, each with a story from its anonymous author.
The Cookbook has been passed from crawl to crawl since the fifteenth season. Carl holds the twenty-fourth edition, and whatever he writes in it goes into the twenty-fifth.

descriptions.text: Book. The Dungeon Anarchist's Cookbook by Anonymous. This is a unique item. Chicken and Goblin recipes galore! But it's more than that, too. Each recipe is accompanied by a hilarious tale by the anonymous author, recounting some of the zany and madcap misadventures they experienced gathering these mouth-watering recipes. Fun for the whole family! This book is a real hoot.

taglines.text: An Enhanced Pet Biscuit has over a hundred possible effects, half of them good and the rest neutral or worse. The cat snatched this one out of Carl's hand, melted into a heap of furry goo, and got up talking.

descriptions.text: Enhanced Pet Biscuit. So, it looks like a regular pet biscuit. It's not. Feed to your pet at your own risk. What's the worst that can happen?

entities.name: Night Wyrm's Ring of Divine Suffering

taglines.text: Frank Q gave Carl this ring as a curse: while one of its marks lives, the wearer cannot be healed. Carl wears it anyway, for the five percent it adds to every stat.
The ring marks a target, and when the target dies, the wearer keeps a point of its best stat. Mordecai says it is addictive, and Donut does not want Carl picking up a new habit.

descriptions.text: Enchanted Night Wyrm's Ring of Divine Suffering. Oooh, that's scary sounding. For the discerning Crawler Killer, this magical ring can be one of the most formidable items in the dungeon. If utilized properly, this ring's wielder can grow exponentially in strength, especially on the deeper floors. But beware. If poorly wielded, this ring will kill you quicker than an exploding rage elemental. Either way, this ring imparts one of the dungeon's most highly sought-after skills. The wearer of this ring receives the following benefits: +5% to all stats. The Marked For Death skill.

taglines.text: Eat the Orchid of Eileithyia's Grace and you spend an hour unconscious at one percent health, with healing blocked. Survive it, and the goddess decides which of her boons you receive.

descriptions.text: Warning: This item can only be used by a female. Or a male, if you're a seahorse. It's a flower. You're supposed to eat it, though it might be a good decoration instead. […] Anyway, if you eat this flower, it renders you unconscious for one hour with your health at 1% of your max. You cannot heal during this time. If you survive this ordeal, you will be given one of three permanent boons from the goddess Eileithyia. The given boon is at the discretion of the goddess, and it cannot be predicted. If you choose to worship Eileithyia before you consume this flower, the descriptions of the boons will be expanded. She will also ask you which of the three you'd prefer. Her cooperation is not guaranteed, especially if she doesn't like you. But Eileithyia is known to be a generous goddess.

taglines.text: According to Mordecai, the Guild of Suffering keeps something called a memorial crystal, which is like a soul crystal, except that nobody has ever established what it does.

A memorial crystal is what a fallen god or demigod leaves behind. This one is the most expensive prize on Chaco's counter, at a hundred hunter hands: the queen usually wears it around her neck, and nobody knows which dead god made it.

descriptions.text: Memorial Crystal. Apito. This item is 0% charged.
Memorial Crystal. Emberus.

taglines.text: The Tiara of a Thousand Lights came out of a celestial box from a waste-management company, on the eve of a war. Donut wears it with Quan Ch's cloak, though nothing has been charged into it yet.

descriptions.text: The Tiara of a Thousand Lights and Accompanying Charge Pillow. This is a unique item. This item was made especially for Crawler Princess Donut by her sponsor, Long Haul Biological Waste Management Solutions. […] This particular tiara is imbued with 99 Absorption Jewels. The tiara itself has no inherent magical properties, and in its base state it gives no additional benefits or buffs except plus 10 to Charisma. However, it has the ability to be permanently charged with up to 99 different buff items. […] With some careful planning, one can turn this tiara into one of the most powerful items in the history of Dungeon Crawler World. Okay, here come the warnings.

taglines.text: The Scavenger's Daughter is a divine back patch for Carl's jacket: a pile of skulls, stacked nice and neat. What it does depends on which gods, and certain demons, happen to be nearby.
The Scavenger's Daughter is also a person. The war mages came to the castle looking for her, found her, and have left with her.

descriptions.text: The Scavenger's Daughter. Upgrade Patch. Back Patch. This is a divine item. This is a unique item. This is a fleeting item. You may only affix one back patch at a time. This patch depicts a pile of scary skulls, all stacked up nice and neat. I wonder if there's a story there? If this upgrade patch is affixed to an eligible garment, it will imbue the following upgrades: (Hidden until it is affixed and then worn.) […] Warning #2! This is a divine item. This means it gains differing abilities, buffs, and possibly debuffs depending on your proximity to certain deities and demons. It makes for new and exciting combinations!

taglines.text: Nothing! is a double-width space on the Desperado Club's wheel of fortune. At the roulette table, a player who lands on its twin falls through the floor, and a ghostly clawed arm rises out of the dark after him.
The Nothing is where gods are banished, as Samantha's own father banished her. Her first escape split her in two, and every time a Gate portal closes, one of those inside gets through.
The fans voted Carl a xistera: a scoop that looks like wicker, strapped to his forearm and reaching two and a half feet past his hand, which hurls whatever he pulls from his inventory into it.
An emergency box has sent Carl an extension slot for his xistera, made for throwing Samantha's head. With the slot on, the scoop will not retract.
A Skill Potion from a gold box raises one named skill by a single level.

Not every skill potion is worth a single level. On his show, the Maestro gave Frank and Maggie a legendary one that takes Find Crawler to level fifteen, and there is exactly one crawler Maggie wants found.

descriptions.text: Skill Potion. Drinking this adds a single level to the Determine Value skill. Hopefully now you'll realize all those Magic: The Gathering cards are nothing more than just meaningless pieces of paper, and you should have spent your money on something with actual value, like a treadmill. Or shampoo.

entities.name: The Filthy Little Crawler's Book of Voodoo

taglines.text: The Filthy Little Crawler's Book of Voodoo came out of a Gold Prepotente Box, and Carl cannot trade it, destroy it or throw it away. It is named after the message boards at old conventions, and the System goes out of its way to say that this is the only reason.
The System has dropped Carl a heavy hint, in the name of a box, that the Voodoo book can be used together with his ability tattoo, and then declined to say how.

descriptions.text: When you meet a crawler who owns this same item, their name will permanently appear in this enchanted book. You may use the book to exchange messages. You may write your message under their name, and only they will receive it. If you write under your own name, everyone who has your entry will see the message. You may write your message manually or using the messaging interface while turned to the page. One must open the book to read the message, but you will have the option to copy the words. Message will erase on demand, allowing one to write a new note. This book is not retroactively filled with the entries of people you have already met. You must be within close-ish vicinity of them for their name to be added. Works only with crawlers who also own this book.

taglines.text: A Fan Box holds items voted for by the crawler's followers. Once you receive one, you cannot open it for thirty hours while the fans vote.
A Fan Box is the prize for being watched: the audience votes on what goes inside, and the crawler carries it around for thirty hours, knowing that strangers are arguing about what they deserve.
Only a patron can send a Benefactor Box, and they hold the rarest items. According to Mordecai, even a bronze Benefactor Box is better than a plain gold Adventurer Box.
A Benefactor Box is bought for you by somebody out there who wants you to keep going, and it may hold things from the patron's home world that the dungeon itself would never give you.

The Royal Chariot is a tracked contraption that Carl and Katia built by hand around a magical train-cart engine. Donut named it before it was finished, and the System's description of it is mostly abuse.

descriptions.text: Tracked All-Terrain Suicide Machine. The Royal Chariot – Contraption. If a snowmobile got drunk on moonshine and had a sweaty, ill-advised night with a hillbilly’s coon-hunting ATV, this oversized birth defect of a vehicle would be the result.

taglines.text: A Cleaner Bot is one of the cheapest personal-space upgrades, at twenty-five thousand gold. Katia bought one without a word, because the room was swimming in ghoul blood.
Party Planner is a silver tilt-rotor airship that came out of the celestial box Louis earned by outliving a goddess's mark for death. He gave it the name Firas once suggested for another vehicle.

descriptions.text: Casket in the Sky. Party Planner. Tilt Rotor Stealth Light Bomber. Vehicle. This vehicle is classed as tier three Armor.

taglines.text: The Goblin Copper Chopper is a steam-driven goblin motorcycle with a sidecar: a single wheel on a huge spring and a fur-lined orc skull for a seat, which Donut began demanding changes to the moment she sat in it.

descriptions.text: Goblin Copper Chopper with attached sidecar. Human-sized. Contraption. Take a junkyard bicycle, add an unreliable steam engine, remove all the bolts holding it together.

taglines.text: Carl's Jug O' Boom is a clay jug of Rev-Up moonshine with a splash of goblin oil and a short torch jammed in like a cork. It throws blue flames up to the ceiling, and the dungeon has named it after him.
The Jug O' Boom is now in the Dungeon Codex under Carl's name, and he earns a gold coin for every kill another crawler makes with it, for the rest of his life.
The moonshine the Jug O' Boom needs is no longer being made, and Carl's royalties stopped after the first few coins.

descriptions.text: Created by an unstable, pantsless man who talks to a cat, Carl's Jug O' Boom takes the bigger-is-better approach when it comes to hobgoblin fire bottles. Burns hotter, bigger, and faster than your normal Molotov Cocktail. The use of a standard torch instead of a cloth wick makes these devices much more stable. Just don't drop it once it's lit, lest you find yourself doing a Joan of Arc impersonation.

taglines.text: The Bolt of Ophiotaurus is a single crossbow bolt from Princess Formidable. It is an ordinary bolt unless it goes straight into a god's eye, and then the god's invulnerability pauses for fifteen seconds.
The Bolt of Ophiotaurus opened a goddess to a killing blow. Magical bolts can be used again as long as they don't break, and Katia still has this one.
Princess Donut fired Katia's bolt straight into Emberus's eye, and for fifteen seconds the god had no invulnerability. Taranis used them.

descriptions.text: The Bolt of Ophiotaurus. This is 1 of 100. This item acts as a regular crossbow bolt unless it is shot directly into the eye of a deity. Upon a successful strike to the god's eye, the deity's invulnerability pauses for fifteen seconds.

taglines.text: A Celestial Grenade summons its thrower's god for sixty seconds. This one was Maggie My's, bought by the Skull Empire to bring the god of pain down on Carl, and Carl dived for it and has it now.
Carl took Emberus as his god in mid-air and threw Maggie's grenade at Quan Ch. Emberus arrived, and for sixty seconds of Divine Intervention nothing could hurt Carl.

descriptions.text: These little balls of fun were developed by the nuns of Enyo during the first enlightenment, back when the gods had to compete for worshippers. The nuns would descend upon a village and proselytize to the people about why their goddess was the best. If the villagers didn't immediately fall to their knees in veneration, the nuns would be forced to invoke a more aggressive campaign. A nun would drop a celestial grenade, which would summon Enyo directly into town for a period of sixty seconds. That was usually enough to change the minds of the survivors. Celestial grenades grant the following effects: If the wielder of the grenade has pledged themselves to a specific deity, this grenade will summon their god for sixty seconds. In addition, the wielder will receive a 60-second Divine Intervention aura. If the wielder does not worship a deity, this grenade will summon a random god. They will not receive the Divine Intervention buff.

entities.name: Enchanted War Gauntlet of the Exalted Grull

taglines.text: The Enchanted War Gauntlet of the Exalted Grull is a wrist bracer that becomes a spiked gauntlet of orcish steel when Carl makes a fist. It warns that striking Grull's adherents may transform them into the god himself, and according to Mordecai, those adherents include horses.
Every punch Carl lands on one of Grull's adherents has a 1.5 percent chance of summoning the god. The description never said the chance was cumulative. It is.
A platinum sharpening stone has given Carl's gauntlet longer spikes, a point more strength and dexterity when he makes a fist, and a slightly oilier, meaner look.

descriptions.text: Item is a wrist bracer that transforms into a spiked war gauntlet made of orcish steel when the hand is shaped into a fist or wields a hilted weapon for more than two seconds at a time. This item on its own does not negate the bare knuckle skill bonus. Warning: if you use this weapon to strike adherents of the war god Grull, you have a 1.5% chance to transfigure your target into the deity himself. Trust me on this. You don't want to do that.

taglines.text: Hob-lobbers are round hobgoblin bombs with an eighth of the yield of a hobgoblin stick, in fused and impact-detonated versions. Pustule has only one case of the fused ones tonight.
A fused hob-lobber is the perfect size for Carl's xistera, which sends it out like a cannonball. The fuse runs six or seven seconds, so he pre-lights them to cut it short.
Hob-lobbers are Carl's staple ammunition, fused or impact-detonated, and he cuts them down at the bench to half, quarter and eighth strength for close work.
Carl makes sticky hob-lobbers as well now, but the dungeon has learned to fight back: in one room, heat lamps threaten to set a bomb off while it is still in his hand.

descriptions.text: Hobgoblin Hob-Lobber – Fused. Type: Fragmenting Tossable. Effect: It blows shit up. A mainstay of the Hobgoblin Hob-Lobbing Lobbers, the Hob-Lobber is a stable, mostly-predictable, more practical and tactical solution to dynamite. All right? But if you toss it, make sure its wick is lit. While not guaranteed to do a premature blast, it's better than nothing, innit?

entities.name: Spunky Jefferson
aka: Spunky Jefferson the Enchanted Nickel Sock of the Elderly Miser
entities.role: Sapient nickel-sock flail · Dong Quixote's weapon

taglines.text: Spunky Jefferson is a crusty tube sock full of nickels, cursed to hold the life force of an elderly miser. It is sapient, it grows stronger as it kills, and Dong Quixote has taken it as his flail.
Dong's sock grows bigger every day, and it seems to be keeping him alive just by being near him. Imani does not like the look of that.
The sock was torn in a bar fight, shrank back to its original size, and stopped talking to Dong. Then it left him, cursed with Negative ROI, and told him he was a bad investment.

descriptions.text: Jefferson is the life force of such a miser who pissed off the spirit who'd come to show him the errors of his ways. He was cursed to inhabit a sock once owned by a kid named Tanner. The sock itself holds several USD worth of nickels. You swing it and bonk people with it.

taglines.text: The pink Crocs belong to Bea, Carl's ex-girlfriend, and they are too small for him. He squeezed into them to fetch her cat out of a tree on a freezing night, because his boots were in the dryer in the basement.
Both of the pink Crocs went flying when Carl turned and ran from a goblin murder dozer down the main tunnel.

The Goblin Murder Dozer is a goblin-built, steam-powered machine the size of a tractor, on treads like a tank, with a spinning, spike-covered wheel across its front. It waits in a dark alley, three goblins aboard, for a crawler to walk into an obvious trap.
Carl kills all three of the dozer's goblins and gets behind the guild door before its boiler breaches. Mordecai has never seen anything shake that door so hard.

descriptions.text: Goblin Murder Dozer. Contraption. A goblin-built, steam-powered machine designed to mow down and slaughter unsuspecting dungeon crawlers. I hope you’re up to date with your tetanus shots.

taglines.text: The Enchanted Nightgaunt Cloak of Stoutness came out of a gold apparel box together with a trollskin shirt, and Mordecai gasped at the sight of the pair.

Carl's nightgaunt cloak is black, leathery and hooded, the wing of some demon creature: four Constitution, resistance to poison and ice, and anti-piercing for all his worn armour. A Nightgaunt that sees him in it will not be happy.

Carl's black, hooded cloak, worth four Constitution and resistance to poison and ice, is made from the flesh of a Nightgaunt, a semi-intelligent species the dungeon dresses up as a demon. The sight of it drove one so mad it never played a single card.

descriptions.text: Enchanted Nightgaunt Cloak of Stoutness. The wearer of this cloak gains +4 to Constitution and becomes resistant to poison and ice-based attacks. In addition, the cloak adds Anti-Piercing resistance to all worn armor. It also makes you look like a dollar store Batman. Warning: if a Nightgaunt spies you wearing this, they probably won't be too happy with you.

entities.name: Enchanted Toe Ring of the Splatter Skunk
aka: Toe Ring of the Splatter Skunk

taglines.text: A toe ring is what the gold shoe box gives Carl, at a time when what he needs is shoes.

The Enchanted Toe Ring of the Splatter Skunk gives Carl three Strength and three levels of Powerful Strike, which multiplies his damage when he fights without a weapon. It sits on the index toe of his right foot, and it is uncomfortable, as promised.
Upgraded once by a scroll, Carl's toe ring now gives ten Strength and five levels of Powerful Strike.

descriptions.text: Enchanted Toe Ring of the Splatter Skunk. Imbues wearer with +3 Strength and gives +3 to the skill Powerful Strike. Also, it’s a toe ring. It’s probably uncomfortable and it makes you look like one of those hippie assholes who sit around in a field juggling and hula-hooping all day.

Enchanted Toe Ring of the Splatter Skunk. (Upgraded) The item has been upgraded once. Imbues wearer with +10 Strength and gives +5 to the skill Powerful Strike. Also, it’s a toe ring. It’s probably uncomfortable and it makes you look like one of those hippie assholes who sit around in a field juggling and hula-hooping all day.

taglines.text: The Enchanted Trollskin Shirt of Pummeling comes out of a gold apparel box beside a nightgaunt cloak, and Mordecai gasps the moment the two appear.

The trollskin shirt gives Carl seven levels of Regeneration and negates melee debuffs such as Stun, Knockback, Disarm and Out-of-Breath. Mordecai calls it one of the best under-armour garments for tanking, the sort of thing found in a Platinum or Legendary box.
A Scroll of Upgrade has added three Dexterity to Carl's trollskin shirt, a decent upgrade if not a great one.

descriptions.text: Enchanted Trollskin Shirt of Pummeling. The wearer of this shirt gains +7 to the Regeneration skill. In addition, all melee-based damage debuffs such as Stun, Knockback, Disarm, and Out-of-Breath are negated. The shirt is also quite stylish. Maybe a little too stylish. Unlike most monster-skin apparel items, this shirt will not grant a negative reaction amongst trolls. In fact, lady trolls might just want to haul you away for some one-on-one time if they see you in this.

taglines.text: The Goblin Pass comes out of a silver goblin box as a goblin-shaped skull that flies at Carl's left inner forearm and brands itself there, showing through his jacket as well.

The Goblin Pass is a tattoo that removes goblin hostility and grants free passage through goblin territory. The catch is that fairy-class creatures, the goblins' natural enemies, deal twenty percent more damage to whoever carries it.

descriptions.text: Goblin Pass. It’s a tattoo! On your forearm! Now you’ll never get a good job! Note: Pass tattoos cannot be hidden unless you purchase a coverup sleeve. Will show through any armor you may wear. Removes automatic goblin hostility. Allows for free passage through goblin-controlled territory in the dungeon. Warning: holding a Goblin Pass will cause natural goblin enemies, such as fairy-class creatures, to deal 20% more damage against you. Still, it looks kinda badass.

taglines.text: A Standard Healing Potion comes in a small red glass bottle with a cork and raises the drinker's health by at least half. Put on the hotlist, it is drunk without actually drinking.
A healing potion comes with a timer: drink a second before the first one's fifteen seconds are up, and the drinker is poisoned.
Healing potions hurt the dead: a note in the Cookbook says a smoke curtain soaked in one and left to dry mass-kills undead.
Healing potions come in grades, standard, fine and gold standard among them, and Carl keeps a gold-standard one loaded in his new toe ring, set to trigger on its own at two percent health.

descriptions.text: Standard Healing Potion. Increases your health by at least 50%. Doesn’t cure poison or other health-seeping conditions such as succubus-inflicted gonorrhea. So remember to wrap it up, bucko.

taglines.text: A Pet Biscuit is dry pet food that feeds a pet-based class for a full day. Pets find them delicious and will gobble them on smell, so they come out of an inventory one at a time.
A pet biscuit tossed into a cage turns a beaten danger dingo's dot from red to white. Donut, who still eats them, calls feeding hers to a dingo a betrayal most foul.
Pet biscuits are how Mongo is trained, because he is very food motivated.
The Poker is the second weapon the dungeon hands Carl, out of a Bronze Weapon Box. It is literally a fireplace poker, a wrought-iron stick with a screw-on point at the end.
Tried against a level-four cockroach, the Poker is knocked out of Carl's hand at the first stab, and he shoves the useless thing into his inventory.

entities.name: Scroll of Heal Critter
entities.role: A pet heal, good for one reading

taglines.text: A Scroll of Heal Critter came out of Carl's very first box, a bronze pet box, with ten pet biscuits: a single rolled-up piece of paper.
Read on Donut, a Scroll of Heal Critter does nothing and evaporates with an error message: No Valid Target Available.
A Heal Critter scroll fizzles out where something blocks magic, and Mongo, bleeding, has to heal on his own.
The Toad Cudgel is the first weapon out of Carl's boxes, from a Bronze Weapon Box: a stick shaped like a three-quarter-length baseball bat by someone with only a vague idea of what baseball is.
Carl likes the Toad Cudgel better than the poker, but its rounded end bounces off a giant cockroach without doing much damage, and he has to bend awkwardly to use it.

descriptions.text: Toad Cudgel. Big stick for bonking. Bonk toad. Bonk mob. Bonk girlfriend and drag back to cave by hair.

taglines.text: The Tome of Magic Missile came out of Donut's silver adventurer box with a pile of pet biscuits, and she had taught herself the spell by the time Mordecai noticed. A tome teaches a spell for good; a scroll casts it once.
In the first safe room, a silver Adventurer Box gives Carl a silver ring worth a point of Constitution, which brings the stat up to ten.
A boss box has added a second ring of constitution, worth two points, which Carl wears on his left ring finger. His Constitution score comes up to twelve.

The Talisman of the Slate Butterfly is a little silver butterfly that jingles on Donut's collar. It makes her a better jumper and a little smarter, and winged fairies are no longer automatically hostile to her.

Donut has worn the butterfly charm since the first floor, but to order the guards of Point Mongo around she has to wear a settlement charm on her collar instead; the butterfly can go back on if fairy-class mobs turn up.

descriptions.text: Talisman of the Slate Butterfly. Those who remember and commemorate the sad tale of the Slate Butterfly are given a boon by the fairies of the world. That story even made me cry. Adds +4 to the Light on Your Feet skill. Adds +1 to Intelligence. Winged fairies will no longer be automatically hostile toward you.

taglines.text: Goblin Dynamite is a red stick that sweats, so volatile that a loud noise might set it off without the wick. The System advises keeping it in inventory until it is wanted.
Goblin dynamite wears down as it is handled: every stick in Carl's pile reads out of fifty, and all of them are already at Detonation Imminent or Danger.
Pustule sells goblin dynamite by the case, twenty-five sticks for five hundred gold, beside hobgoblin sticks at twenty for two thousand.

descriptions.text: Goblin Dynamite. This stuff is especially volatile. It’s so volatile, you probably don’t even need to light the wick to set it off. It’s so volatile, even loud noises might set it off. Keep it in your inventory until you’re ready to use it. Be gentle and don’t squeeze too hard or else you might get the… BOOM!

entities.name: Enchanted Spiked Kneepads of the Shade Gnoll Riot Forces
aka: Spiked Kneepads of the Shade Gnoll Riot Forces

taglines.text: Carl's kneepads slip on like knee bracers, made of skin and fur, with needle-thin spikes about eight inches long that pop out only when they are needed. They add ten percent Damage Reflect to all his equipped armour and cancel momentum-based attacks.

descriptions.text: Enchanted Spiked Kneepads of the Shade Gnoll Riot Forces. Adds 10% Damage Reflect to all equipped armor. Cancels all Momentum-based attacks. Made of skin and fur and the spiky things from the back of Thorn Cadavers, these kneepads are both good protection and they’re stylish. Stylish, that is, if your knees are cosplaying as hedgehogs.

taglines.text: A Neighborhood Map is the scrap of paper a neighborhood boss drops, persistent loot any crawler can take. Touched, it fills in about a square mile of the minimap, red dots and all.
A neighborhood map fills in the minimap round where it was dropped, and the one Carl looted from a dead goose shows him where a living boss sits as well.
A Potion of Iron Skin raises the drinker's physical armour by a hundred percent for five minutes. Carl has five, from a gold crowd control box.
A Scroll of Confusing Fog fills a room with a mist that only the mobs can see. Carl has three, out of a gold crowd control box.
How long Confusing Fog lasts depends on the reader's intelligence. With Carl's intelligence of three it gave fifteen seconds; Donut reading the same scroll would get a hundred and twenty.

The Tome of Wisp Armor comes out of Carl's boss box, a magic protection spell he cannot cast yet on three mana. Mordecai calls it quite valuable and says to hold onto it, or give it to the princess, who wants it before she knows what it is.
Carl has read the Tome of Wisp Armor rather than sell it. The spell wraps him in tendrils of light that turn aside most magic damage and, for a few minutes, anything trying to take over his mind.

descriptions.text: Wisp Armor. Cost: 5 Mana. Target: Self Only. Duration: 5 minutes + 1 minute per level of spell. Requires 5 minute cooldown. Surrounds your body with tendrils of light. While ineffective against physical attacks, this spell negates 75% of incoming damage from magic-based attacks. Provides temporary immunity to mind-control effects. Higher skill levels increase both effectiveness and duration. It also makes you look all wispy and ethereal and druid-like. A great spell to have if you're a club kid or trying to bang a vegan.

taglines.text: The Torch tome is a spell book out of Donut's Bronze Boss Box, and she applies it before Carl has time to read the description. It teaches her Torch, a curl of light that follows her around and grows stronger with use, and she thinks it is a stupid spell.

entities.name: Desperado Pass
entities.role: The tattoo that opens the Desperado Club

taglines.text: The Desperado Pass is a tattoo out of an Asshole's Box that brands itself on: a gold splotch glowing through the fur over Donut's right shoulder blade, and a dagger dripping blood on Carl's neck. It grants access to the Desperado Club and rules out a Vanquisher pass.
The Desperado Pass also precludes several classes for Carl and Donut, among them the Cleric and Paladin classes.
The Desperado Pass is what gets Carl and Donut past Clarabelle and into the members-only room of the Desperado Club.
Katia has a Desperado Pass now as well, a dagger tattoo that formed on her neck out of a loot box.

descriptions.text: Desperado Pass. Great. Now you’re running with the type of kids who sit in the back of the bus. What would your mother say? This pass allows access to the Desperado Club. Warning: Holding a Desperado Pass negates the ability to obtain a Vanquisher pass.

entities.name: Enchanted Fae Scale Quadruped Crupper of the Fleet
aka: Fae Scale Quadruped Crupper of the Fleet

taglines.text: The Enchanted Fae Scale Quadruped Crupper of the Fleet is Donut's first armour: silver fae-steel scale draped over her back half like a skirt, with a slot for her tail and two points of Dexterity. Not the best protection, its description admits, but it makes her backside look oh so pretty.
Donut's old crupper has made way for a chain mail one, the Crupper of the Benevolent Champion. Its two points of Dexterity were great on the first floor and are laughably weak now.

descriptions.text: Enchanted Fae Scale Quadruped Crupper of the Fleet. Boy is that a fucking mouthful. By the gods. +2 to Dexterity. Light and flexible, this scale armor is made from Fae Steel. While not as strong as Elven mail or even good Orcish steel, it's the strongest alloy that fairy folk can wear. It's not the best protection, but it'll make your ass look oh so pretty.

taglines.text: A Sapper's Table is a workbench sold in safe room stores, and Carl's new Demolitions Workshop menu will not open unless he is standing in front of one.

Carl has a Sapper's Table of his own now, out of a Gold Sapper's Box: a crafting table like his engineering and alchemy tables, where the explosives and traps he makes don't lose stability or go off early.
Carl's Sapper's Table stands in his crafting space, where he expects to spend most of his time, and he spends two upgrade coupons to take it to level three.
At level five, Carl's sapper's table is still better for building explosives from scratch than the bench in his new bomber's studio.
The Tome of Minion Army comes to Donut in a Beguiler Box. Its spell makes hostile enemies fight for her, but it costs fifty spell points, she has twenty-four, and the book will not let her read it.

Donut has read the Tome of Minion Army. The spell takes five minutes to cast and roots her in place while it does, and at level one each intelligent mob in its circle has a two percent chance to turn on its friends.
Donut has cast Minion Army at last, rooted for four minutes, and the demon birds caught low in its circle turned on each other.

Agatha leans on a shopping cart heaped with blankets and odds and ends, a plastic pink flamingo with an arrow in its head among them. Her spray paint lives in it, in a blue IKEA bag, and she insists the paint is hers.

Carl's inventory history still lists everything that was in Agatha's cart while he held it: blankets, clothes, IKEA bags, spray paint, and three pieces of Valtay Corporation technology that sort to the very top by value.

Agatha already had this cart on Earth before the collapse. With the countdown running, she took her supplies out of her dimensional space, put them in the IKEA bag and shoved it to the bottom of the cart. Carl's inventory history still lists the three Valtay devices it carried.
A bracelet out of a silver Adventurer box adds two points to Donut's Dexterity, bringing it to twelve. It wraps snugly round her front leg.
Donut wears bracelets on all four legs now, and the plus-two Dexterity one is on a back leg.

The Enchanted Shuriken of Bloodlust are a hundred small, low-damage black throwing stars. Every monster hurt by one makes the set hit that monster type eight percent harder, compounded, but the stars are very fragile.
A star that takes a single chip loses its red enchantment. Fifty of Carl's shuriken became the spikes on the front of the redoubt for the borough boss, and only about twenty of those stayed unbroken.

descriptions.text: Enchanted Shuriken of Bloodlust (x100) Small, low-damage throwing stars. These bad boys aren't anything special upon first glance. They're the same black stars you wannabe ninjas purchased at the knife shop and the swap meet when you were kids. The same throwing stars you'd drill into the drywall of your room until your mom caught you and took them away. And while these shuriken don't have the ability to turn you into a ninja, nor do they have the capacity to make your mom stop drinking, they are enchanted with a Bloodlust enhancement. For every monster you damage with a shuriken from this set, the damage against that monster type rises by 8%.

entities.name: Heal scroll
entities.role: A heal for whoever it is read on

taglines.text: A Heal scroll heals whoever it is read on, and there is no countdown between one scroll and the next, as there is with potions. Donut won a dozen from a Silver Survivor's Box, and Carl's bronze one brought five more.
A Heal scroll works on Donut, but read on Mongo it does nothing.

The Puddle Jumper tome is a spell book out of Donut's Bronze Boss Box, and she reads it before Carl can ask what it is. It teaches her Puddle Jumper, which teleports her and up to three others anywhere in her line of sight, for 20 mana, on a ten-second delay and a five-hour cooldown.

The Speedbump is Brandon's name for the portable fortress he, his brother and Carl built from goblin tables and gym equipment: angled, four feet high, drilled to go up in less than twenty seconds and come together in twenty more, and meant to wedge a rolling boss against the ceiling.
What survives of the Speedbump travels in pieces in Carl's inventory, and an angled section that is still intact serves him as a shield in a boss fight.

A Borough Field Guide is looted from a dead borough boss, and Donut gets one of her own. It outlines the quadrants of the map round it, and hovering over one gives the levels and types of the mobs inside, though only for a limited area.
The field guide from the bowl's borough boss shows the level and description of every mob in the area, and it covers the entire bowl.

descriptions.text: Borough Field Guide. Ahh, look at you. The intrepid explorer. Alone. Lost. Afraid. But there is no reason to be frightened. Not today, not now. Not when the trusty field guide has added monster types to this area of the map. Now when you gaze upon the unknown, that fear is somewhat lessened. Instead of delving into the strange, mysterious dark, being devoured by an unseen horror, you will now know exactly what it is as it chews upon your tasty innards.

entities.name: Cheat Code Potion
entities.role: A skill boost that will not keep

taglines.text: A Cheat Code Potion raises one recently-used combat or magic skill by three, chosen at random and permanent. It expires shortly after it is generated, so it has to be drunk on the spot.

descriptions.text: Cheat Code Potion Warning: This item has a short shelf life. This item will expire shortly after it was generated. In other words, this isn't something you can hoard. Don't be a wuss. Drink it now. Causes one, recently-used combat or magic-themed skill to increase by three. Choice is random and permanent.

entities.name: Enchanted Pedicure Kit of the Sylph

taglines.text: The Enchanted Pedicure Kit of the Sylph is a little zippered folder of twelve tools. Used nightly in a safe room, it gives Carl's bare feet extra damage, three levels of Smush, bones that will not break and a five-second warning before any trap set off by a footfall, all for thirty hours.

descriptions.text: Enchanted Pedicure Kit of the Sylph. This kit contains 12 essential items for proper foot care. The magical enhancements of this item may only be imbued within a Safe or Personal Space. Warning: All of these enhancements require you to remain barefoot. Why? Because you know why. From a pumice stone to a cuticle pusher, this personal hygiene kit will keep your feet both luscious and in perfect fighting shape. Nightly care of your feet and toenails will result in the following bonuses: +15% Damage to bare-foot attacks for 30 hours. +3 to the Smush skill for 30 hours. +Unbreakable buff (feet only) for 30 hours. This buff keeps your pretty little metatarsals nice and unbroken. …

taglines.text: The Goo-Inator 3000 is a shaping tool from a silver mechanics box, an oversized silver lollipop with a button on the handle. It only works at a workbench, so for now it waits in Carl's inventory.
At his engineering table, the Goo-Inator lets Carl work metal like dough: flatten it into a sheet, or bend it freehand.

descriptions.text: The Goo-Inator 3000. This is a shaping tool. May only be used at a workbench. Assists in shaping materials into something else. You might want to keep the business end away from your face.

taglines.text: The Second Chance tome arrives by mail: a boss box has made Donut a member of the Dungeon Book of the Floor Club, one spellbook a level. It teaches Second Chance, which raises a lower-level dead monster to fight for the party for as many minutes as the spell's level.

Rev-Up Toilet-Grade Moonshine is a 180-proof accelerant made by Krakaren's operation from grub slime and a secret source, and carried by her clurichaun consultants in clay jugs. Carl and Donut take twenty-five of them, and Carl wants torches.
No more Rev-Up Moonshine is being made this season, and Mordecai tells a shopkeeper that Carl and Donut are the reason. Three of the bottles they kept buy a pharmaceutical starter kit.

descriptions.text: Rev-Up Toilet-Grade Moonshine. Type: Accelerant. Effect: Highly flammable liquid. Explosive fumes. Status: Will not activate until introduced to flame. At 180 proof, this moonshine will take the hair off your chest and then put it back on. The Rev-Up version is distilled using two types of sugars: the slime trails left behind by the passage of the Brindle Grub, and a secretive, proprietary source. Created exclusively on the dungeon's second floor by the Rev-Up company, jugs of this concoction are highly sought after by the drinking establishments that populate the third, sixth, ninth, twelfth, fifteenth, and eighteenth floors. …

taglines.text: The Rev-Up Immunity Smoothie is a recipe left in a dusty box beside a bicycle-powered blender. It takes two ingredients, and Carl reckons it is how a crawler is meant to get immunity from the Taint before fighting the boss.

The Rev-Up Immunity Smoothie is one part moonshine and one part fairy, blended pink on a child-sized bike. It gives ten doses of temporary immunity to health-seeping debuffs and disease, with the Buzzed debuff thrown in.
What is left of the smoothie from the second floor goes into Carl's infusion experiments, and mixed with a smoke curtain it is a dud.

descriptions.text: Rev-Up Immunity Smoothie. One part moonshine, and one part fairy, this smoothie offers 10 doses for the price of one! Each sip of this delicious concoction imbues the following effects: Temporary immunity to all health-seeping conditions and debuffs. Temporary protection against all communicable diseases. Inflicts the Buzzed debuff. …

taglines.text: The Enchanted BigBoi Boxers are white, covered in little red hearts and self-sizing, because a were-creature's underwear has to survive the transformation. They give two Constitution and let the wearer cast a level-fifteen Protective Shell once every thirty hours.

An upgrade has made Carl's boxers probably his most valuable item, Mordecai reckons: five more Dexterity, five more Intelligence, three more Constitution, and the Freeballing benefit. It adds a hundred percent damage bonus to every attack from below the waist and allows only a single layer over the crotch, so with the boxers on, no trousers.

descriptions.text: Enchanted BigBoi Boxers. Have you ever read an Incredible Hulk comic and thought to yourself, everything rips off of his body except his pants? No way. Well, spoiler alert. You're not wrong. Size-altering and were-creatures, such as the BigBoi are required to wear enchanted, self-sizing items lest they wish to turn the dungeon into a nudist colony when they transform. That means everything they wear requires an enchantment. Everything, including their naughty little undies. + 2 to Constitution Wearer may cast a level 15 Protective Shell once every 30 hours.

Enchanted BigBoi Boxers. This item has been Upgraded once. All right, you already know the description of this item. Something something Incredible Hulk, blah, blah, blah. Now you want to know how this item has been upgraded. Right? So here are the original benefits of these naughty little undies: + 2 to Constitution Wearer may cast a level 15 Protective Shell once every 30 hours. That's some good shit right there. But we can do better than that. Here's a few additional benefits. + 5 to Dexterity + 5 to Intelligence + 3 more (for a total of + 5) to Constitution + The Freeballing Benefit

entities.name: Enchanted Fur Brush of the Ecclesiastic

taglines.text: The Enchanted Fur Brush of the Ecclesiastic gives Donut two extra points of Constitution for thirty hours, as long as someone brushes her with it for ten minutes every night. It works much as Carl's pedicure kit does.
An upgrade out of a Scab box has the brush adding a further ten percent to Donut's Constitution, on top of its two points for a brushing.

entities.name: Residents' wheelchair train
entities.role: Meadow Lark's ride through the hallways

taglines.text: The residents' train is ten wooden cars on wheels from wheelchairs whose owners are gone, four riders to a car, linked by one glowing magic chain and pulled by Imani and Chris in pig harnesses. It was Imani's idea, and Brandon designed it.
Out in the scorched hallway there is no sign of the wheelchair train's cars, or of the wheelchairs and walkers left behind. Only its chain, which Carl grabbed earlier, has survived.

Yog's Special Chain is a scroll out of a Gold box that makes a magic chain, any length up to something like a thousand feet, light as a feather and gone in thirty hours. Imani's runs about three hundred feet through ten cars of residents.
Imani's chain outlasts the train it pulled, and dropped from a bomb launcher with weights at either end, it snares a rage elemental by the leg.
Imani uses the few chain scrolls she still has, and the chain they make hangs a whole interdiction cart from a crane without breaking.

Dungeon Gold Rush is a scratch-off lottery ticket with six spots. One spot can be scratched each hour, and the symbol revealed decides what happens to Donut's next attack on a mob: five thousand coins, say, or double damage, or a mob that splits in two.

descriptions.text: Dungeon Gold Rush! Scratch off one spot, and depending on the symbol revealed, your next attack against a mob will have varying effects! Guaranteed laughs! One hour cooldown between scratches.

taglines.text: Fireball or Custard is a scratch-off lottery ticket with five spots. Each scratch in battle casts a spell at the nearest red-tagged mob, an even chance of a level-15 fireball or a glob of healing strawberry custard, with thirty minutes between scratches.
Carl's first scratch comes up custard. It heals the bear he is fighting, and the healing kills the worms that have been controlling her.
Carl has scratched two of the ticket's five spots: custard first, then a fireball that half collapsed the room it hit.

descriptions.text: Fireball or Custard? Scratch off a spot in the midst of battle, and this zany ticket casts a spell at the closest red-tagged mob! Each spot has a 50/50 chance. Will it cast a level-15 Fireball? Will it cast a glob of delicious, healing Strawberry Custard? Who knows! Either way, the results will be a hoot! Thirty minute cooldown between scratches.

taglines.text: The Mother of All Bombs is not a bomb but a launcher Carl built on the chopper's trailer, a ski-jump ramp down which Donut rolls wheeled bombs, its babies, out behind them. Brandon says the name is wrong and calls it the Bomb Chicken, and Donut agrees with him.
The Gorgon Marital Aid is a spatula-shaped workbench tool that hardens and softens rigid materials, and the System says intergalactic porn stars are fond of it.
Carl has built the plungers of his first landmines with the Gorgon Marital Aid.

descriptions.text: Gorgon Marital Aid. A favorite amongst intergalactic porn stars, this is a hardening and de-hardening tool. May only be used at a workbench. Assists in fusing joints or creating varying degrees of plasticity in otherwise rigid materials without affecting material strength.

taglines.text: Mana Toast comes out of a plain metal toaster in a safe room, one burned triangle per crawler. It refills mana, and the System says that is all it does.
Donut keeps two slices of mana toast for an emergency, because they top off her spell points without counting as a potion.

descriptions.text: Mana Toast. This is toast. It refills your mana. That’s it. Nothing more. Fuck you.

taglines.text: A Proximity Trigger is a trap part, a black box the size of a dime on a long wire, that sets the conditions for a trap to go off. Carl gets ten in a Gold Sapper's Box, and his inventory ranks them near the top for value.

descriptions.text: Proximity Trigger. Trigger Warning! Traumatizing content! Using a Sapper's Table, the highly-valuable Proximity Trigger may be attached to any non-static trap. Allows for the establishment of activation conditions, including countdowns, mob-type triggers, etc.

taglines.text: On his show, the Maestro gives Carl a brand-new pair of Bates zip-up tactical boots in his size, identical to the service boots he wore on active duty, with socks in the box. It is a troll: Carl's barefoot buffs and skills stop working in shoes, and the orc knows it.
An Alarm Module is a ready-to-go trap, no tinkering required. Donut's gold sapper's box gives her one, along with a Spike Module.
An Alarm Module blasts a very loud song when something sets it off, or adds an alarm to a trap someone builds. On the train its first song tells the party the babies are through the door.
At his sapper's table Carl now seals alarm traps inside hollow banger spheres so they can be thrown, and because he puts them together there, he picks the songs, from memory.

descriptions.text: Alarm Module. Two items for the price of one! A favorite of the paranoid and the rich, you can use this module to either add an alarm element to a trap you're building, or it can be used as a ready-to-go trap for those who can't be assed to sit down and make their own. When triggered, it will play a Very Loud song. And by Very Loud, I mean Norwegian Black Metal loud. You may program the song at a Sapper's Table. If you do not or are unable to pick an alarm tone, a random, culturally-important song from the past US Billboard Hot 100 will be chosen. …

taglines.text: A Spike Module is one of two ready-to-go trap modules out of Donut's gold sapper's box, no tinkering required. Changing one needs a sapper's table.

A Spike Module is a cube the size of a pair of dice that pushes fifty-centimetre spikes out of a one-metre square every two seconds, forever once something hostile triggers it. Carl has found that it will stand on a door.
The Master Pen Key opens the cages of the fighters and the bait animals in the kobold fighting pits. It is attuned to kobolds, and in anyone else's hand it works once and breaks.

descriptions.text: Master Pen Key. Opens the individual cages of both the fighters and the bait animals within the kobold fighting pits. This key is magically attuned to the kobold race. If you are not a kobold and attempt to use this key, it will only work once before breaking. Choose wisely.

taglines.text: Donut 'coincidentally' receives a spell book of Heal Critter from the boss boxes in the kobold pits, just after she and Carl have won a baby dinosaur.
Heal Critter is on Donut's spell list now, at level one.
Donut's Heal Critter is level fifteen, though like every pet spell it will not work on a special mount.

The Valtay Perso-Shield Platinum Edition is a tech-based personal shield made by the Valtay Corporation. One was in Agatha's shopping cart, and Carl only learns it from his inventory's history, after he has given the cart back.

Carl has a Perso-Shield of his own now, a pinback button like the planet Saturn, unlocked from the hunters' tech loot. Switched on, it wraps him in an inch-thick buffer against physical blows, and somewhat against corporeal spells, for about two minutes, then takes about an hour to charge.

descriptions.text: Valtay Perso-Shield Platinum Edition. – Tech-based Personal Shield.

taglines.text: A magical pet carrier is the dungeon's equivalent of a pokeball: supposedly expensive, Odette says, and a way to put a bonded pet into inventory without harming it.
Mongo's carrier cost 15,000 gold: a square brown box the size of a Rubik's Cube with a fire hydrant etched on it. He sleeps and recovers inside it, and comes back out at the press of a button.
A pet carrier is how Ren hands Carl her pet, unconscious and level one now.
Carl carries Ren's pet in a pet carrier in his inventory, and as long as he stays boxed up, Mordecai says, he will be fine.
A Big Top Ticket is one of the things a dead clown was carrying, along with a hunk of Clown Meat and 35 gold. Carl loots all of it with a mass of red dots fifteen seconds away.

A Big Top Ticket admits one adult into Grimaldi's Traveling Circus Big Top Show, with Safe Passage through the public areas only. Signet says that means anywhere in the tent except the three rings, which is exactly where the three poles are.

descriptions.text: Big Top Ticket. Lucky you! This ticket admits one adult into the Grimaldi's Traveling Circus Big Top Show. The holder of this ticket is guaranteed Safe Passage through the public areas only. Grimaldi reserves the right to rescind this safe passage guarantee to drunks and purveyors of violence. Guaranteed good time or your money back!

entities.name: Carl's cactus
entities.role: A gift from the Earth box

taglines.text: Carl's Silver Earth box held a small cactus in a clay pot, three inches tall and covered in yellow spikes, with a $3.99 Home Depot price tag still on it. He cannot think why they chose it for him.

Li Na has cast a dread trap on Carl's cactus and then gone into a cleaner bot that is meant to carry her out of the dungeon. Its glow, its blooms and its dust will say whether she is alive, gone or dead, and a single flower will mean the way is safe.
A single flower has bloomed on Carl's cactus. Li Na reached the Pineapple Cabaret, and it is safe to send the others after her.

An Earth Hobby Potion is a reward the Syndicate Government requires for every crawler with a domestic class: drink it for level three in a random Earth hobby. Donut's is Scutelliphily, which nobody can explain, and Carl's is Cesta Punta, which he wonders might be a martial art.

What an Earth Hobby Potion teaches arrives all at once. Carl's Cesta Punta is jai-alai, the sport of the scoop his fans have just voted him, and Katia's has made her a gear head who has never actually fixed an engine.
Donut's Scutelliphily, Britney explains, is the love of small shields. Her hobby is patches.

descriptions.text: Earth Hobby Potion. Per subsection 1256-C of the Indigenous Species Protection Act, this particular reward is required by the Syndicate Government to be awarded to all Crawlers who have chosen a domestic class. Taking this potion is optional, however it may not be sold or transferred to other Crawlers or entities. Upon drinking this, you will immediately obtain a Level Three skill ability in a unique, Earth-based hobby. The benefit is chosen at random, however you will not receive a skill that you currently have. Gods, I hate it when the lawyers make me put their crap into the descriptions. Don't you? …

taglines.text: Mongo's collar is black and magical, out of Donut's gold pet box, and it puts his orange dot on the map wherever he is. He does not care for it.

entities.name: Enchanted Anklet of the Fallen Oak

taglines.text: The Enchanted Anklet of the Fallen Oak is a simple wooden anklet off a dead crawler, with three little beads that click like seed pods. Its description calls anklets garish, so Carl gives it to Donut for the constitution, and she wears it on a back leg where nobody will see it.
To the city elves, the anklet on Donut's back leg is the forbidden oak, and they take its bearer for the Oak Fell, Apito's version of the antichrist.

descriptions.text: Enchanted Anklet of the Fallen Oak. Imbues wearer with +1 Dexterity, +1 Constitution, and gives +3 to the skill Double Tap. It's also an anklet. One would think anklets enhance the beauty of feet like toe rings do, but they are excessive, jangly distractions that make you look too garish.

taglines.text: Nica's strength rings are two rings, each +2 to strength, that Carl takes off a dead crawler named Nica. They bring his strength back to an acceptable level.

Mordecai mixed a double healing potion that he insisted would cure a parasitic infestation. Carl drinks it in Grimaldi's big top with a mouthful of worms, and throws up a never-ending stream of them, dead and dying.
The double healing potion also works on a brain parasite, Mordecai says, if it is drunk before the parasite reaches the brain.

Carl's Lucky Bastard box, for surviving Signet's attack, holds a single comp chip worth 100,000 gold at the Desperado Club casino. It cannot be sold, traded or cashed in for gold, only played at the High Roller's Roulette Table or the Wheel of Fortune.
Carl played the chip on the Wheel of Fortune, where a comp chip leaves only two bad spots, and it won him a Scroll of Upgrade.

descriptions.text: 100,000 Gold Coin Casino Chip. This is a comp chip, and it may not be sold or transferred. You may not redeem this chip directly for gold. This chip must be played at the High Roller's Roulette Table or the Wheel of Fortune game at the Desperado Club Casino. Good luck.

entities.name: Enchanted Fang Caps of the Expectorating Tizheruk
aka: Fang Caps of the Expectorating Tizheruk
