taglines.text: The Enchanted Fang Caps of the Expectorating Tizheruk are a pair of metal caps like loose vampire teeth, out of Donut's Platinum Quest Box. They add half again to a bite, with a chance to poison or paralyze, and Donut decides at once that Mongo is getting them.
Mongo wears the fang caps now, and every time he snaps his teeth, little tendrils of electricity burst from his mouth.

descriptions.text: Enchanted Fang Caps of the Expectorating Tizheruk. This is a Fleeting item! Fun fact. There is not a single dentist from your world left in the dungeon. A few made it to the first floor, but every single one of those fuckers is now tits up. There're a few hygienists left, but I wouldn't want to rely on those chuckleheads. What I'm getting at is that you need to install these yourself. Make sure they're facing the right direction. You can always take them off, but this is a fleeting item. That means they disappear once they're off. So don't fuck it up. …

taglines.text: Hobgoblin dynamite comes in white sticks instead of goblin red, with a larger yield and far more stability. Carl's first whole box of it came with three globs of hobgoblin pus, remote-controlled detonators.
A stick of hobgoblin dynamite is practically a mini nuke: thrown half a block, it knocks Carl off his feet and brings down a building's front. It is utterly impractical in a regular fight.
Hobgoblin dynamite is much more stable than the goblin kind and should survive several impacts, so Carl builds it into his bigger bombs.
Carl cuts hobgoblin sticks down at need, carefully slicing one into twenty pieces.

A Scroll of Upgrade improves one random item a crawler has equipped, a little or a lot, and its short shelf life means it must be read at once. Carl's first makes his BigBoi Boxers probably his most valuable item, with the catch that he can no longer wear trousers.
Scrolls of Upgrade have been good to Carl. One won on the Wheel of Fortune takes his toe ring from +3 Strength to +10.
Not every Scroll of Upgrade is a great one: the third Carl reads only adds three Dexterity to his Trollskin Shirt.

descriptions.text: Scroll of Upgrade! Warning: This item has a short shelf life. Maybe it's not as good as getting something new, but sometimes it's better to just take something you're already comfortable with and improve upon it. Kind of like buying your girl new tits. Once you read this scroll, one random, currently-equipped item will receive an upgrade. That upgrade could be small. It could be huge. But since this item has a short shelf life, you gotta do it now or forever hold your peace.

taglines.text: Blitz sticks are what the Desperado Club's pharmacists sell in place of earth tobacco: eat one for five points of Intelligence for a while, or smoke it for a fifteen percent chance at a permanent point, with a side effect or two. Mordecai says they are magically addictive.
Katia smokes blitz sticks she found on one of Eva's victims, and they show her what she asks them to. Only Daniel knows.
A blitz stick is like weed plus a hallucinogen that shows you memories that do not exist, which is why it is so damn addictive. The cure is a patch worn on the skin.

descriptions.text: Blitz Stick. It's like candy, but for your mind. If you eat this, your Intelligence temporarily rises by five points. If you smoke it, there's a 15% chance your Intelligence will permanently rise by 1. There might be a side effect or two. Or three.

taglines.text: Quint's starter kit is a suitcase that is really a large chest, filled to the brim with chemicals and herbs: everything you need for a pharmaceutical empire, he says. Mordecai got it for three bottles of Rev-Up Moonshine, a potion for Donut thrown in.
The starter kit's supplies sit on the alchemy table in the crafting room now, for Mordecai to work with.

entities.name: Framed photograph of Bea and Brad

taglines.text: Donut's first gold fan box holds a small, framed photograph of Miss Beatrice, lifted from her Instagram: Bea in a bikini, laughing, on her ex-boyfriend Brad's lap. It is the photo that made Carl break up with her, and Donut loves it.
Donut keeps the framed photograph of Bea on a small table beside the bed, which is where she makes Carl put it.

The Gate Pass is a slip of paper from GumGum's inventory, signed by Magistrate Featherfall: the holder is doing this on his orders. It keeps the Over City's swordsmen off a crawler carrying a corpse, inside the township that issued it.

descriptions.text: Gate Pass. When one walks about the streets of any town within the Over City, the mindless Swordsman guards tend to get a bit squirrely if you're carrying a corpse with you. When it comes to their black and white view of justice, the rule of law is absolute. Unless you have a gate pass. This letter gets the city guard off your back as long you're not being too overt with your current criminal enterprise. Pass only works within the township in which it was issued.

taglines.text: The Mysterious Letter is a folded, blood-soaked paper from GumGum's inventory, written in squiggles and triangles nobody can read. Mordecai recognises necroscript, something an undead magic user would write, and suspects a lich.
The letter is a used Suppurating Eye scroll, and Mordecai thinks the blood on it is the caster's own. Whenever it is out of Carl's inventory, whoever cast it can see and hear what happens around it.

descriptions.text: Mysterious Letter. GumGum the orc had this blood-soaked letter in her possession. It's in an odd language. Is it a clue? Is it a grocery list? You can't fucking read it, so who knows?

taglines.text: The Scroll of Meat Hooks came off a dead city elf who used the spell to lure Mongo away into an alley. Cast, it draws every nearby carnivorous pet-class monster to the source of a burning stench.

Read from a plane, with Donut's charisma giving it a range of almost three kilometres, the Scroll of Meat Hooks trails a stench behind them like a blown engine, and draws a giant two-headed puppy out of the water after it.

descriptions.text: Scroll of Meat Hooks. Let's be real. Every pet owner already has this spell, at least when it comes to their own pets. Sometimes it's the sound of a can opener. Or a command, such as "chow time, Fido!" Sometimes it's the wisp of a jar of peanut butter being cracked open. No matter what the trigger is, the effect is the same. You do something, and your pets come running. Meat Hooks works on the same principle. You cast, and pets come to you. …

taglines.text: Hundreds of swordsmen guards stand in stasis in a warehouse, their yellow aura all leading to one point in the ceiling, and Carl reckons a soul crystal is up there somewhere.

A soul crystal is elf technology, a charger that runs on the souls of everything killed nearby. The one over the swordsmen's warehouse is overloading, and the map puts it at the epicentre of an explosion with a blast radius of forty-five square kilometres.
The guard depot's soul crystal went off inside a Sheol Glass Reaper Case, and the two together are Carl's Doomsday Scenario now.
Soul crystals power the fourth floor's ghoul generators too, and the generators do not take kindly to being blown up.

The soul crystals elves use are mined from Scolopendra's lair, made when certain kinds of people die and their souls are filtered through the centipede. Once installed as a power source they are worth nothing, except as an explosive.

descriptions.text: Soul Crystal. C-Grade. Elf technology. It's like a wireless charger. Instead of electricity, it runs on the soul power of everything killed within the area. And instead of charging your iPhone, this particular gem tops off the town's Swordsmen guards each night. Some of that power is also leeching into something else. If this crystal is physically touched by living flesh, it will shatter and cease to work.

taglines.text: A Sheol Glass Reaper Case is a small, expensive protective case forged in the fires of Sheol and sold by travelling Spider Reaper Minions. Carl's is one of Miss Quill's, pulled from the debris of her building with Kimaris inside, and every time it opens there is a 1.5 percent chance of Sheol Fire.
The case Carl closed round an overloading soul crystal is half of Carl's Doomsday Scenario now, a caged explosion sitting in his inventory.

descriptions.text: Sheol Glass Reaper Case. Forged in the fires of Sheol, the mysterious 15th level of the World Dungeon, these protective, expensive artifacts are built and sold by traveling Spider Reaper Minions. They also sell lollipops, which are said to be out of this world. When you absolutely, positively want to keep something safe, put it in this box. It will protect against most—but not all—forms of abuse. Warning: Every time you open this case, there is a 1.5% chance you will be blasted with the Sheol Fire spell. That's not a good thing. The item within the case will remain protected.

taglines.text: A Red Line Engineer's Key is what the magically locked service plate under a red line car's gangway floor asks for, and the System is happy to point out that Carl does not have one.
The keys are colour coded, Carl says, so each one works only on its own line's trains, and it takes one to get into the engine car at the front.
Carl holds two now: the Ochre Line Engineer's Key from a dead engineer, and a large bronze Steam Engineer's Key from the Nightmare's cab, good for all four hundred of the Tangle's steam trains.
An engineer's key is a pass as well. Equipped or held outside inventory, it lets a crawler through the gated portals over the abyss, which lead to a trainyard.

Keys are rescue gear now: crawlers trapped at the abyss need a hat or a key to get through the portals, and at station 75 Carl collects fifteen coloured-line keys from his fellow crawlers along with more than seven hundred hats.

descriptions.text: Steam Engineer's Key. Allows access to Iron Tangle employee-only areas and actions on all 400 steam-type trains of the Tangle.

taglines.text: The moment the floor begins, the System hands out one each for an achievement: a blue and white toddler's hat embroidered with I rode the Iron Tangle. Carl examines his. It is not magical. It is junk.
The souvenir hat is a key. Equipped, it carries a crawler through the gated portals over the abyss, and some crawlers have already sold theirs, for five thousand gold apiece.
With the Kravyad's portal closed and the trains stopped, a crawler without a hat may have no way off the line, and more than a hundred and fifty of Bautista's group have none.
Carl is carrying more than seven hundred of them, given up by crawlers who heard what they were for, to hand out to the people trapped at the abyss.
The hats have done their work. The crawlers Carl brought through give theirs to Donut, one by one, in tribute, and she gathers every one into her inventory.
Nobody is buying the hats any more, not even for a single gold, and Carl has not had the heart to tell Donut.

The Bang Bro tome comes out of the bronze boss box Carl earned for killing Miss Quill. Read, it teaches a five-mana spell that adds fire and electrical damage to whatever he has equipped, and Mordecai says it will work on his gauntlet.

descriptions.text: Bang Bro Cost: 5 Mana Target: Temporarily Enchant Equipped Item Duration: 5 minutes + 1 minute per level of spell. Requires 5 minute cooldown. Adds both fire and electrical damage to any currently-equipped item. May not be cast on flesh. Well, actually it can be cast on (your own) flesh, but I really wouldn't recommend it. May inflict Burn and Shock on targets. Can also be used to cook hotdogs and other items.

taglines.text: Mordecai says the personal space's second tier will offer something called a Bomber's Studio, which would let Carl practise blowing things up.

Carl's Advanced Bomber's Studio is a room ten feet wide and as long as a bowling lane. It holds a virtual range where any explosive he copies can be set off and paused mid-blast, and at the back a bench for taking real bombs apart.
When Carl leaves Donut's party, the bomber's studio stays on her side with most of his crafting tables, so that if he dies she does not lose it all.

entities.name: Enchanted Necklace of the Haute Bourgeoisie

taglines.text: The Enchanted Necklace of the Haute Bourgeoisie is the second smallest of the chains of leadership, and Carl has it for becoming magistrate of a Skyfowl town. Its one gem, a poor sapphire, gives him dexterity, the Talon Strike skill and 432 gold in taxes every ten days.

descriptions.text: Enchanted Necklace of the Haute Bourgeoisie. The second smallest of the chains of leadership, it is still considered a great honor to be the custodian of this burden. Each jewel encrusted upon this charm represents a settlement owned and controlled by the bearer. If one still maintains a settlement's jewel upon the collapse of the level, the holder of this necklace will permanently receive a tax stipend every ten days from that settlement based on size and population. […] One Attached Gem: Poor Sapphire. Medium Skyfowl Settlement (Third Floor). +5 to Dexterity. +Talon Strike (Level 5) Taxes received: 432 Gold every 10 days. May you be a kind and just leader.

taglines.text: The Enchanted Tiara of Mana Genita is a crystal tiara like the one Donut lost, with white jewels instead of purple. It adds intelligence, helps her spot mobs on the map, and keeps the worshippers of an obscure goddess from attacking on sight.
Donut wears the Tiara of the Inebriated Dragonfly now. The Tiara of Mana Genita is kept, in case it is useful one day.

descriptions.text: Enchanted Tiara of Mana Genita. A crystal tiara fit for royalty. Made in honor of all the lost children of the world. Because nothing helps sooth the tears of grieving parents like watching someone else dress up all fancy. +3 Intelligence Increased ability to detect mobs on the map. Removes automatic hostility by worshippers of Mana Genita.

taglines.text: The Hole spellbook is Donut's Book of the Floor Club prize, waiting in a saferoom mailbox, and reading it teaches her Hole: a temporary hole in any surface she chooses. At level one it is not deep enough to get through most doors.

entities.name: Upgrade coupon
entities.role: Slips of paper worth an upgrade

taglines.text: The AI's special box paid out seven slips of paper each: a coupon for a free level-three personal space, two for tier-one environmental upgrades, two for free tier-one crafting tables and two for table upgrades. Each is worth up to 250,000 gold, and two cannot be combined on one item.
Mordecai wanted everyone's table upgrade coupons for his alchemy table, but Carl spent his on the sapper's table and Katia hers on a makeup table.
Coupons keep coming in boxes: Carl now has three third-tier personal space upgrade coupons and a town upgrade for a castle, on top of the lower-tier town upgrade from the Tina quest.

The Battery Fabricator sits in a dusty corner of Limp Richard's general store at 75,000 gold, price not negotiable. Pour in mana potions, add a brick-sized metal block, and a charged battery is supposed to come out the other side.

Carl owns the Battery Fabricator now, traded for the rest of his westerns and a jug of moonshine. Four full mana potions and five minutes charge one dwarven battery, and the powered railway carts at this station can run on them.

The Gangway Chock is Carl's own name for a sheet of metal, a swordsman's breastplate thinned and stretched, that wedges into the gangway between two train cars. With wedge-shaped door blocks on the outer doors, it lets the party keep a cleared car to itself.
One leftover door block from the Iron Tangle has been coated by Mordecai with a holy protection oil, which makes it a repellent against the undead.
An Invisibility Potion does what it says. Carl's first is in the pocket of somebody's suitcase on a train, next to two mana potions.
Invisibility potions keep turning up in Carl's boxes, and he makes sure Donut always has a few. Smashed against someone, one works on them too.

descriptions.text: Invisibility Potion. Guess what this does.

entities.name: 1965 Harley Davidson FLH Panhead Electra Glide

taglines.text: Prize four on Chaco's carousel is a red and beige 1965 Harley Davidson with a small dent in the gas tank, and Carl knows that dent: he made it as a boy, knocking his father's motorcycle over. He does not pick it.

The Harley stands in the yard of Carl's father's trailer, which the dungeon has spliced into the floor from an earlier time, maybe a summer. Carl takes it into his inventory, and it files itself with his vehicles, not the temporary loot, so he thinks it is his to keep.
Carl's father's Harley starts at the first try, its gas tank full, and Carl rides off on it.
Carl rides his father's Harley across the arena at Scolopendra with Donut on his shoulder, and lays it down to make the throw.

The Enchanted Mongoliensis Saddle comes from Donut's fans: a garish blue-and-red seat with a pommel and a great many tassels, no straps and no reins, that clicks onto Mongo's back by itself. It boosts the rider's spells and the dinosaur's constitution, and his melee damage while someone is in it.
Mongo's saddle has an upgrade called Legendary Steed, which lets Donut hitch a cart to him without adding weight, and he can still jump.

descriptions.text: Enchanted Mongoliensis Saddle. Adjusted to fit Cat species. Magically affixes itself to the dreaded Mongoliensis, turning everyone's favorite murder chicken into a mount. Riders in the saddle are afforded the following bonuses: +15% to all offensive spell damage. Anti-Piercing Resistance. In addition, the saddle gives the following bonus to the attached Mongoliensis: +20% Constitution. +20% melee damage while saddle is occupied.

taglines.text: A Fragmenting Potion Ball is a hard rubber ball that holds one full potion vial, made at Mordecai's alchemy table to be thrown. A potion works on a mob that is hit with one, and as far as Mordecai can tell, mobs do not get potion sickness.

descriptions.text: Fragmenting Potion Ball. A full potion vial may be transferred to this ball.

taglines.text: Mordecai's Special Brew is his own potion: thirty seconds of nonstop healing and rapid regeneration that keeps a crawler's health topped up, though nothing in it saves anyone from an instant death. The price is about ten more hours of potion sickness, and no one can take more than two before they stop working.
Carl has drunk one under Grull's axe, and spent thirty seconds being broken and healed over and over.
The brew works thrown, too. Loaded into a potion ball and fired from Carl's xistera, it heals a giant puppy in one hit.
Thirty seconds of the brew is the window Edgar's surgery on Louis is built around.

descriptions.text: Mordecai's Special Brew. A potion designed by a shifty Changeling who has a tendency to kill those who count on him the most, this special potion combines the effects of a Gold Standard Healing Potion and the Troll's Second Wind to create a de facto immortality for a period of thirty seconds. It has a few unfortunate side effects.

taglines.text: The Superb Constitution Buff Potion is a stat potion of Mordecai's making, orange and bubbly, that permanently adds one to four points of Constitution. No one may drink more than two, whatever their quality, so Mordecai says to drink nothing like it they find unless it is labelled Superb.

descriptions.text: Superb Constitution Buff Potion. Drinking this mixture will permanently increase your Constitution by a random number between one and four. You may only drink two of these during your time in the dungeon. Why? Because drinking more would be cheating. And if anyone is going to cheat, it's going to be me.

taglines.text: A Jelly Bomb is Carl's landmine for taking a train off its rails: a tire-shaped, oblong metal tube stuffed with hob-lobbers and a stick of hobgoblin dynamite, set off when a train presses one of its spikes. The System named it, presumably after a jelly donut, and gave him no credit for inventing it.
Two Jelly Bombs on the ochre line are enough. The train comes off the track, and Carl gets an achievement for manufacturing a derailment.

Katia's Makeup Table is a crafting table Mordecai told her about. At level three, paid for with her table upgrade coupons, it lays the face of anyone she has met onto its glass to sculpt from, sitting at it does not hurt, and it stores three designs to call up on demand.
Katia can shape nearly anything on the fly now, but faces still come out best at her Makeup Table.
A bottle of Rev-Up Magic Hair Restoration comes off the corpse of Gore-Gore, along with an engineer's key and a neighborhood map.
Carl's hair has burned off, eyebrows and all, and he means to grow it back with the Rev-up hair tonic, though he has heard the results are a little overenthusiastic.
The tonic adds length for as long as it stays on, and Carl's head went wrong at the last step: his hair now reaches his waist, grows back when cut, and will keep doing so for about two weeks.
Carl had meant to cut his hair once the tonic wore off, but a hairbrush too good to give up means it stays long.

The Armorer's Table is the crafting table Carl buys with a free table coupon at station 281. Metal shaped at the engineering table is only metal, but picked through the Armorer's Workshop tab it becomes armour the system lets someone equip, Katia included.

entities.name: Ugly Ass Backpack With a Completely Useless Design that Only an Idiot Would Wear

taglines.text: Carl built Katia a way to carry her own mass: an open-topped metal basket on dingo-hide straps, which the System calls an Ugly Ass Backpack. Loaded with metal poles and equipped, it vanishes into her, and she grows by what is inside it.
Katia has widened the backpack herself on Carl's engineering table, packed more metal into it, and added rubber to layer between the metal and her flesh.

Katia has a better one now, out of a boss box: the same idea, but adjustable, so she can carry even more, and it will not break. It gives her a stability enhancement while she wears it, and retractable stilts make loading much easier.

Valtay Corporation Neural Enhancer #544 is a blue and yellow capsule from a bronze benefactor box stamped with the Valtay Corporation's symbol, and it permanently installs one upgrade in a crawler's interface: Identify and Analyze Subspace Portals. Carl has swallowed it. A doorway that is a portal now glows purple for him, and he can read it and see a still picture of the other side.
Portal sight is how Carl reads the gated portals over the abyss: who may pass, which keys count, and a picture of the trainyard waiting on the other side.
Carl's implant still reads portals, but in incompatibility mode since the changes to his body, with limited details and no picture.

descriptions.text: Valtay Corporation Neural Enhancer #544. Variant 32.c This item is compatible with your Morphology and Interface. Warning: This pill will cause a permanent change to your brain. This item cannot be unequipped or undone once installed. Warning: You do not have a Valtay Corporation Neural Interface installed. While your current wetware system is compatible with this Neural Enhancer, it is recommended you visit a Valtay Corporate Outreach Center to discuss upgrade options. Payment and Legacy plans available. Keeping the Best of You alive. Current wetware: Syndicate Crawl Version 47.002.Human. Taking this pill will install the following upgrade to your interface: Identify and Analyze Subspace Portals.

taglines.text: A Sheol Brick is what a Lesser Demon's young become: of the thousands born in a litter almost none live, and the rest shrivel and harden into black chunks that burn far hotter and longer than coal. The Nightmare Express runs on them, and Carl has taken a box of about fifty out of its cab.
Mordecai wants as many Sheol Bricks as Carl can get, and Fire Brandy has let him take several hundred, most of them still burning.

descriptions.text: Sheol Brick. If Santa gives coal to the regular naughty kids, he'd probably give this stuff to history's greatest villains, like Hans Gruber and the guy who invented those shoes with the individual toes built in. It burns a lot hotter and a lot longer than regular coal. And when I say "a lot longer," I mean until the end of your lifetime. So like a week or more. To save you distress, I'm not going to tell you where this came from. That was a lie! It's a baby corpse!

entities.name: Prism Industries Capacitating and Focusing Goggles

taglines.text: The Prism Industries Capacitating and Focusing Goggles are big round sunglasses, a signed gift to Donut from Princess D'Nadia, that seem to be magically fixed to her face. They see in the dark and by heat, guard her eyes, and turn her Magic Missile into a laser she can split four ways.
An empty benefactor box has upgraded Donut's sunglasses instead: they now read the surface and subsurface temperature of anything she looks at, in precise detail.
Donut's sunglasses are locked to her, as Louis found when he tried them on. A rare scroll called Cracker Jack could free them, and nobody they know has one.

descriptions.text: Prism Industries Capacitating and Focusing Goggles. Special High-Fashion Edition. "The Princess Donut." This is a Unique Item. This one-of-a-kind item was a gift from Princess D'Nadia of the Prism Kingdom to Princess Donut of the Blood Sultanate. It was personally signed by Princess D'Nadia. Protects the eyes from a variety of environmental hazards, including magic-based attacks that render the user blind. Enhances all dark vision effects. Allows for heat vision and other visible-light viewing options. In addition, any energy-based spell that originates from the ocular region is caught and focused by these goggles, which allows for multiple combat and targeting options.

taglines.text: Seize the Day Toothpaste is a tiny travel tube of cherry-flavored toothpaste, five applications, from a Platinum Big Daddy Box. Brushed with in a safe room, it gives thirty hours of three times damage to bosses, four times against province, country and floor bosses. Carl is keeping it for a day he knows he will meet one.
Its bonus is part of what puts Donut's effective charm over three hundred when she goes to work on Ferdinand.

descriptions.text: Seize the Day Toothpaste – Five Applications. You know that feeling you get when you walk out into the world with minty-fresh breath? It's like you can take on any challenge that is thrown your way. It gives you confidence. It boosts your self-esteem. It makes you feel like you're on top of the damn world. Well, this stuff does none of that. However, if you brush your teeth using this enchanted, cherry-flavored toothpaste, you are imbued with the following buffs for 30 hours: +Three Times Damage to all Boss Monsters. or +Four Times Damage to all Boss Monsters if the Boss is a Province, Country, or Floor Boss. This buff may only be applied in a safe room.

taglines.text: Banger Spheres are Carl's xistera ammunition: baseball-sized balls of dwarven robot scrap he made by the few hundred at his engineering table. The system gives the name only to the ones made at that size.
Banger Spheres are still Carl's everyday ammunition, plain or spiked, and he has made hollow ones too, with an alarm trap sealed inside.

A PVP Coupon is a black ticket with a gold-leaf skull that pays out a stack of boxes and a player level for killing the crawler named on its back. According to Hekla, a crawler in a party who earns a player-killer skull gets them in a Savage box, one for every member, and Katia has found the one with Carl's name on it where Donut hid it under a train track.
Donut says she got rid of both of hers, Carl's under a train track and Katia's in the garbage at a Hotdog on a Stick. The one with Carl's name on it is in Carl's inventory.

descriptions.text: PVP Coupon. Ah, betrayal. Sweet, delicious betrayal. If you have this coupon in your inventory, and you kill the crawler whose name appears on the backside of this coupon, you will receive the following rewards: Gold Savage Box Gold Weapons Box Gold Apparel Box Platinum Adventurer Box (This benefit may only be redeemed a max of 3 times) +1 Player Level (This benefit may only be redeemed a max of 3 times)

taglines.text: A Dirty Little Phased Bolt is ammunition for a crossbow assassin: invisible, hiding its own wound, it drains its victim to a tenth of their health with amnesia and a bleed, and a second takes them to one percent. A death that follows is put down to something else, so the shooter gets no credit and no skull. Two of them were in Katia, and Donut says she saw Hekla shoot them.
Carl keeps a broken one in his inventory. Dipped in blood it shows its shape for a moment, and it is his proof of what Hekla did.

descriptions.text: Dirty Little Phased Bolt. This item is broken. It must be repaired before you may use it. This is a Phased item. It is invisible. It will hide its entry point and will only be discovered if it is physically touched. The perfect ammunition for the discerning crossbow assassin. This item will cast both Temporary Amnesia and Suffering Bleed onto its victim, draining them of health until they are at 10%. A second bolt will lower the victim's health to 1%. Victims who subsequently perish will be listed as dying from an alternate source. You will not get credit or experience for the kill. …

entities.name: Enchanted Repeating Crossbow of the Scavenger Mother of Mothers
aka: Repeating Crossbow of the Scavenger Mother of Mothers

taglines.text: The Enchanted Repeating Crossbow of the Scavenger Mother of Mothers was Hekla's, and Katia, who killed her, looted it. It never runs out of basic bolts, only a woman may wield it, and its damage and speed climb with every woman in the party.
Katia's crossbow rides on Donut's back now, clipped to the Scorpion's Bite weapon mount and bigger than the cat herself. Donut admits it is weaker than it could be, with no women in her party.

descriptions.text: Enchanted Repeating Crossbow of the Scavenger Mother of Mothers. This is a unique item. This is a repeating, ranged weapon. It has the buffet enchantment, meaning it will not run out of basic ammunition. […] This crossbow is rumored to have been given to Nekhebit's last warrior guardian as a gift for remaining true to her faith. This item may only be wielded by a female. For every female in your party, up to thirty, this item's damage and firing speed is increased by 25 percent. […] +15 Dexterity when wielded +10 Strength when wielded Casts Birth Defect on monster types who generate or birth additional monsters.

entities.name: Enchanted Wrestling Belt of the Great Gorgo
aka: Wrestling Belt of the Great Gorgo

taglines.text: The Enchanted Wrestling Belt of the Great Gorgo is a gold champion's belt from Katia's Platinum Slam Master box. It adds strength and constitution, and when her whole body is moving, whatever she hits takes the force of twice the mass.

descriptions.text: Enchanted Wrestling Belt of the Great Gorgo. While you'll never be as amazing as the greatest, most beautiful wrestler of all time—Christopher Alan Pallies—you will look pretty snazzy when you wrap this bad boy around your waist. This enchanted belt offers the following benefits: +5% Strength +5% Constitution +The Avalanche benefit.

entities.name: Growler Gary's left hands
entities.role: The keys to the rapid-response carts

taglines.text: The rapid-response carts start only with a gnoll's left hand on each of two key consoles, so Carl collects fourteen left hands from Growler Gary, who regenerates every time. Take a hand off, and the cart shuts down.
Carl took one spare pair of Gary's hands, and he is still a pair short.

entities.name: Interdiction Rapid-Response Railway Repair Cart
entities.role: Railway cart with a mobile portal

taglines.text: The Interdiction Rapid-Response Railway Repair Cart is the hobgoblins' wreck-clearing vehicle, with a mobile portal across its front that sends everything on the track to a trainyard or into the abyss. It runs on batteries, and only a pair of gnolls can start it.
One interdiction cart hangs nose-down from a crane over the hole in the station, its portal facing the floor and tuned to the abyss, swallowing whatever comes up.

descriptions.text: Interdiction Rapid-Response Railway Repair Cart. Contraption. Main Passenger-Line Gauged. The main workhorse vehicle of the Hobgoblin Interdiction Team. Includes battery power or powered track selection option. Includes portal track selector. Includes dual-destination, selectable debris scoop. […] The debris scoop will safely transport any active and running trains and their passengers back to the railyard. Once the wreck is reached, the debris scoop is switched to abyss mode, clearing the line of the damage. […] Unfortunately, the corporation running the Iron Tangle has little trust for the hobgoblins and requires security to escort these vehicles at all times. As such, this cart may only be started by a pair of gnolls.

entities.name: Teleport Trap
entities.role: Two-part trap and a way to travel

taglines.text: In a note by Crawler Milk in the Cookbook's chapter on portals, teleport traps are simply the worst.

A teleport trap can be set inside a saferoom, because the real trap module sits outside, at the destination. Lucia Mar has set at least two, one just inside a saferoom door and one just outside the guildhall's.

A two-part teleport trap needs both halves set by the same trapper, but nothing says the anchor has to stay put. Carl mounts anchors on the backs of little spider automatons and sends them where he wants to go.

entities.name: The Left Fang of the Green Sultan

taglines.text: The Left Fang of the Green Sultan is one of Eva's two sabers, dropped in a train's engine car and picked out of the gore by Carl. It is half of a set and only magical with its brother, so on its own it gives nothing, and Eva has lost her main weapon.
Carl has given the saber to Katia as she prepares to go her own way, and told her to return it to its rightful owner.
Katia has returned the saber to Eva. She cut off Eva's escape-ring hand with it, then drove it through her breastplate.

entities.name: Enchanted Auto Buckler of the Peach Pit
aka: Auto Buckler of the Peach Pit

taglines.text: The Enchanted Auto Buckler of the Peach Pit is a wrist bracer that pops a small metal shield into place with a twist. Katia gives it to Carl once her new riot shield will not let her wear both, and a hit on it has a small chance to disarm the attacker.
Carl has swapped the Auto Buckler of the Peach Pit for a better shield bracer, and it has gone onto the pile of gear for the Faction Wars team.

descriptions.text: Enchanted Auto Buckler of the Peach Pit. Forms a metallic buckler on command. May be triggered via hotlist or by shaking your wrist like you're thinking of your hot Aunt Lydia. This item is enchanted with Shatter. Any attack that lands upon this shield has a 1.5% chance to disarm the opponent. If the opponent is disarmed, there is a 90% chance the item will drop to the ground, a 5% chance the weapon will break, and a 5% chance the weapon will be immediately transferred to your own inventory.

entities.name: Enchanted Shade Gnoll Riot Forces Crowd Control Shield

taglines.text: Katia's fan box gave her a riot shield of the Shade Gnoll Riot Forces: tall, curved and absurdly light, with Get Back on the front. It adds constitution and Rooted in Place, and it upgrades her Rush to Crowd Blast, which hits a whole cone in front of her and can be used every five minutes instead of once a day.

descriptions.text: Enchanted Shade Gnoll Riot Forces Crowd Control Shield. Sometimes the galaxy isn't a happy place. Sometimes the unwashed masses forget their place in the machine. And sometimes these dregs bubble up to the surface, causing a phenomenon widely known as "Civil Unrest." And when that happens, the powers that be don't want to become the powers that were. So they hire backup. An outside force to come down and kick everything back into order, and maybe commit a few war crimes in the process just so the filth knows their place. One such outfit, trained specifically for this sort of situation, is the Shade Gnoll Riot Forces. …

entities.name: Enchanted Shade Gnoll Riot Forces Telescoping Crowd Control Baton

taglines.text: The baseball bat in Katia's fan box is a police baton, faintly glowing with enchantment, that telescopes from twenty-five centimetres to three metres and casts a Cone of Knockback when swung at a group of ten or more.

descriptions.text: Enchanted Shade Gnoll Riot Forces Telescoping Crowd Control Baton. This enchanted truncheon is designed to crack skulls and to teach those ungrateful bastards to show some got-damned respect. This item's length is adjustable, from 25 centimeters to 3 meters. Automatically casts Level-five Cone of Knockback if swung at a group of 10 or more like mobs. This triggers only once every five minutes.

taglines.text: The Stuffed Grulke Infantry Figure is a beanbag toad in a spiked helmet, the commonest of its line, one of more than a thousand stuffed monsters from Miss Quill's apartment. Pull the tag and throw it, and a real grulke fights for fifteen to thirty seconds.

descriptions.text: Stuffed Grulke Infantry Figure. (With tags) This is the most common variation of the Grulke line of collectible figures. In terms of rarity, these things clock in just below frat boys with early-onset liver disease. It's literally not possible to enter a waystation kinder shop and not find one of these for sale on the shelf. You'll be hard-pressed to find a collector who will buy this off you. It sure is cute, though.

taglines.text: Astral Paw is the spellbook Donut pulls from the mailbox as her spellbook-of-the-floor club prize, and she reads it before anyone can talk her out of it. Mordecai calls it a good utility spell: a paw that handles things at a distance as if she were touching them, with more force than Astral Hand and claws to come at level five.
Donut picks Astral Paw as one of the two spells her War Crime combines, and over the hole of Larracos it becomes a glowing paw big enough to pin an army under it.
A gift from the gods has pushed Donut's Claw skill to 17, and Mordecai tells her that her Astral Paw spell can now cut through almost anything. She stiffens at the name.

The Enchanted Gnome FarSeerer is a dirigible gnome bomb sight, a white telescope covered in pipes and gears, that lets its user inspect things at a distance. Skarn keeps one to watch the patrols, and every gnome it targets is told they are being watched.
Donut has stolen the FarSeerer off Skarn's roof in ten seconds flat, and she says she forgot the thirty gold she was told to leave for it.

descriptions.text: Enchanted Gnome FarSeerer. Used to sight long-range targets for their bomb runs, the FarSeerer is credited as one of the key inventions that allowed the Dirigible Gnomes to obtain air superiority. When properly installed on a Gnomish Dreadnaught, this device increases the accuracy of gravity-based bombs by 75%. Allows for inspection and information on objects at a distance. It's pretty good for spying on your neighbors, too. You don't need porn when you got this thing hanging off the edge of your airship. Warning: All gnomes targeted with this device are given a notice that they are being watched.

entities.name: Enchanted Toe Ring of the Leprous Bandit
aka: Toe Ring of the Leprous Bandit

taglines.text: The Toe Ring of the Leprous Bandit, on Carl's left foot, carries two benefits. Sticky Feet lets him walk on walls and ceilings barefoot once every six hours, and Super Spreader passes his active debuffs to a target once an hour.

descriptions.text: Enchanted Toe Ring of the Leprous Bandit. This is a unique item. Most children in the universe know the exciting tale of the Leprous Bandit, the infamous human thief whose people were starving to death because of a planet-wide quarantine. … To this day, the Leprous Bandit remains an inspiration. This toe ring imbues the following: The Sticky Feet Benefit. The Super Spreader Benefit.

taglines.text: The Gnomish Knock-Knock is a refrigerator-sized fuel-air bomb, barely stable, slung under the gnomes' patrol ships. Only a few are left, and they are kept now as a standoff weapon.

The last few Knock-Knocks hang under the Wasteland itself on the morning it comes to bomb Hump Town. Carl's second volley of missiles goes at its gun battery and three bombs on its underside, and the sky to the north goes up in white fire.
Carl counts the Knock-Knocks under the Wasteland as one quadrant's "cheat", a quick way to kill everything, like the drain hidden in the side of the sandcastle.

descriptions.text: Gnomish Knock-Knock. Type: Fuel-air bomb. Effect: Thermobaric Explosion. Status: 40. Barely stable. I wouldn't be tapping on the thing. Ever seen a hundred Dromedarians die because their lungs imploded, followed by their skin getting melted off their body just before they all shatter into mist? Well now's your chance! Fun for the whole family, this was the main weapon of the Gnomish Bombardier Squads. There are only a few of these things left, and they're usually strapped to the failing air force's most reliable patrol ships. The fuel-air Knock-Knocks were once used to devastating effect in the early days of the last conflict. The remaining munitions are instead used as a mutual-standoff weapon. …

taglines.text: Pawna's Tears is the potion in Carl's Legendary Deity's Box, named for Pawna, the goddess of peace and Grull's sister and arch enemy. It adds five to any spell or skill its drinker chooses and can be saved, and Mordecai calls it the single best item of loot Carl has had.
Carl has spent Pawna's Tears on Donut, to bring her Laundry Day to fifteen against Circe Took. His sponsor says he will replace it.

descriptions.text: Pawna's Tears. This potion adds plus five to any spell or skill of your choosing.

entities.name: Scroll of Water Breathing
entities.role: Breathing underwater, a scroll at a time

taglines.text: A Scroll of Water Breathing lets a crawler breathe underwater for three seconds per point of intelligence. They turn up in box after box on this floor, which Mordecai reads as a hint about what the floor holds, and Donut announces that cats do not swim.
Water-breathing scrolls have to be chained one after another, and when one runs out, the water in a crawler's lungs comes back up.
A Water Breathing scroll grows gills, and in surgery Mordecai uses one to give Louis gills that stay.

descriptions.text: Scroll of Water Breathing. Allows you to breathe underwater. Lasts as many seconds as your intelligence stat times three. It does not protect you from swimmer’s ear or being eaten by an undead barracuda. I hope you know how to swim.

taglines.text: A Surefire is a crafting part the size of a bottle cap that gives any projectile the Guided status: an arrow, a bolt or a rocket seeks the target it is given. Carl has a case of twenty-five.
Surefires are what turn Carl's rockets into guided missiles. He had used ten when Ruckus's boss box sent a case of twenty-five more.
A launcher of twenty-five surefire missiles brings down a fleeing hunter, and Carl has used the last of the parts.
Out of the seeking-missile attachments for some time, Carl gets a group of surefires from a gold box and can build more missiles.

descriptions.text: Surefire. Crafting item. A Surefire adds the “Guided” status to any projectile, powered or not. It may be utilized on a vast array of crafting tables. If added to an arrow or bolt, you must choose a target prior to unleashing the weapon, and the projectile will seek that target. If added to a trap, additional options become available. Such as “Target any healers within range” or “Target anyone who thinks it’s okay to put mayonnaise on hotdogs.” If added to a powered weapon, such as an explosive-based rocket, targets may be assigned during the crafting process or upon firing, but not both. Note: this upgrade alone does not add range to the projectile.

taglines.text: The Wall of Fire tome, from Donut's platinum box, teaches a fifteen-mana escape spell: a wall of flame ten metres wide and two high, for fifteen seconds at first level. Mordecai warns that fire spreads. Donut wanted Fireball.
Donut's Wall of Fire crackles bigger than ever, thanks to her new nipple ring.
Wall of Fire is one of the spells Donut's new cloak is raising to level 15 over the coming week, and Mordecai expects her to be a terror on the battlefield.
Powered up to level 16, Donut's Wall of Fire runs a mile along the road and a hundred feet into the air.

The Gnomish Drop Bear is one of the dirigible gnomes' earliest fast-attack planes, an open-air, twin-engine biplane with famously underpowered engines and a quick-escape balloon. It does not drop bombs; its payload is something the System calls much more entertaining.
Carl now has a Drop Bear of his own, an abandoned biplane named Death Trap, which he sprays over and renames Nightmare II.

descriptions.text: Gnomish Drop Bear. Contraption. This is one of the Dirigible Gnome's earliest fast-attack planes. There are only a handful of these still in service. While able to quickly reach most targets when drop-launched from home base, the twin engines of these early models were famously underpowered. Damaged Drop Bears oftentimes had difficulty obtaining enough altitude to reach home, even after ditching their payload. This is why most of these planes carry rapid-deploying, quick-escape balloons, making them sitting targets for enemy aircraft and flak. … Don't worry, these guys don't drop bombs. Their standard payload is something much more entertaining.

taglines.text: Rapid Detox clears its drinker of alcohol and most drugs, and for a single floor makes them violently ill if they drink. Mordecai gives it to Louis and Firas disguised, so neither can read what it is.

aka.name: Veriluxx RealPet Dungeon Crawl Special Edition Exclusive

taglines.text: Veriluxx RealPet Companions is Donut's new sponsor, and its first benefactor box is a product sample she is to play with on camera before she, Carl and Mongo go on a program about it.
The product is a toy robot Donut, three-quarters her size, with fur like rat hair, bootleg Garfield lines and a creepy streak. Donut is thrilled to have merch. Mongo bites its head off.
The newest robot Donut is three times heavier and survives Mongo, but a cheap tab holds shut a panel at the back of its head, and opening it starts a five-second self-destruct warning.
Loita is dead, blown up by the last robot Donut, and Carl had made sure its panel would fall off.

descriptions.text: Veriluxx RealPet Dungeon Crawl Special Edition Exclusive. “Princess Donut the Queen Anne Chonk.” Dungeon Crawler World: Earth. The ultimate play toy, Veriluxx RealPet Companions are budget-friendly, nearly indestructible collectibles that will give your child hours and hours of fun. Because these interactive toys do not require an implant certificate to play with and enjoy, parents needn’t worry about how many hours their children are spending with their new best friends! Mix and match! They fight! They love! They will share your deepest, darkest secrets! Each Veriluxx RealPet Companion is a fully licensed depiction of your favorite personality or creature. …

entities.name: Mairmei Mushroom
entities.role: An alchemy material, and a drug

taglines.text: Mairmei Mushroom is an alchemy material, and all its description says is that these little guys are quite the trip. Carl took a batch from the town hall in Hump Town, and Mordecai has never seen the strain before.
The camels have been feeding a mushroom to their gnome prisoner to keep him compliant, and eaten raw, Mordecai says, the mushrooms help get people to do what you want, if not reliably.

descriptions.text: Mairmei Mushroom – Alchemy Material. These little guys are quite the trip.

taglines.text: The Toraline Root Vegetable is a rare tuber that grows only in dirt once covered by lava, and by the System's account it tastes like dogshit. It came in a silver benefactor box from the Open Intellect Pacifist Action Network, and nobody, Mordecai included, knows what it is for.

Mordecai, with Samantha's help, has worked out the toraline's uses: a special ink for scrolls, or lava-themed potions at about an eighth of the yam each. One of them, a phase potion, has got Maggie out of Chris's head.
More than half of the toraline is gone, and the sponsors who sent it have sent a note: Save the toraline.
A sliver of the toraline, brewed in a beaker by Shi Maria with Carl's own hands, has become the black ink of a tattoo on his chest. Mordecai still has the biggest piece.
Toraline ink mixed with Carl's blood makes a permanent tattoo that lends a spell to someone else, and the yam potion renews it. There is barely any of the vegetable left.
With some ink tips from Milk, Rosetta says, they no longer need the toraline to do what they need.

descriptions.text: Toraline Root Vegetable. Alchemy Material. This rare tuber only grows in dirt that has been covered by lava. They are very rare. Nobody ever goes digging them up, either. You know why? Because they taste like dogshit, that's why. They're pretty much useless. In fact, fuck you for wasting my time with this.

taglines.text: The Valtay Corporation's Neural Enhancer #275 is the second pill the brain-parasite corporation has sent Carl. Swallowed, it adds his current elevation and airspeed to his interface, permanently.

descriptions.text: Valtay Corporation Neural Enhancer #275. Variant 35.j This item is compatible with your Morphology and Interface. Warning: This pill will cause a permanent change to your brain. This item cannot be unequipped or undone once installed. Warning: You do not have a Valtay Corporation Neural Interface installed. While your current wetware system is compatible with this Neural Enhancer, it is recommended you visit a Valtay Corporate Outreach Center to discuss upgrade options. Payment and Legacy plans available. Keeping the Best of You alive. Current wetware: Syndicate Crawl Version 47.002b.Human. Taking this pill will install the following upgrade to your interface: Current elevation and airspeed.

taglines.text: Ruckus, the giant cyborg buzz-ard, carries a twenty-five-foot stick of ten spinning buzzsaws, each blade the size of a truck tire, hung under her on a pair of thick cables.
Ruckus is dead and her buzzsaw is in Katia's inventory. It runs on the same dwarfish battery as the Chariot, seems to work without the bird, and is lighter than it looks.
The buzzsaw is gone, broken apart on the ocean floor after it cut through Lusca's head.
Carl wants a parachute in a hurry, and Feather Fall is a potion for it, but Mordecai has none of the materials: the seed pods it needs, he says, are scarce until the sixth floor.
Carl buys a case of twenty-four Feather Fall potions at the Masquerade's prize counter, because Eva's thievery has left the group seven fall-protection potions short.
Carl hands out Feather Fall potions once the escape plan is live, and when the last five seconds come he drinks one himself rather than trust his nipple ring.

entities.name: Enchanted Roll of Never-ending Duct Tape

taglines.text: Carl asked the viewers for duct tape, and a silver fan box has sent him the universe's greatest: fifty metres of extra-durable fabric tape that grows back at a metre an hour until the roll is full again.
The duct tape has bound a gnome prisoner, sealed a bomb into a submarine's minifridge and patched a flying house's net of ropes, and Louis has just used up the whole roll.

descriptions.text: Enchanted Roll of Never-ending Duct Tape. Fifty meters. Odds are good you know who Ted Bundy is. Odds are even better you don't know who Vesta Stoudt is. And while this problem is not exclusive to you hairless monkeys and your pollution-ridden world, those first two statements are part of the reason why you have received this prize. Will you use it to tie people up? Will you use it to save the lives of those you love? Will you wrap your ankles together and sensuously rub your supple feet up and down a dungeon wall while you run your hands through your hair? Who knows! …

entities.name: Jellyfish Salve
entities.role: For a Pain Amplifier Jelly's sting

taglines.text: Jellyfish Salve comes in what Donut calls a lotion bottle, five applications, and takes the pain out of a Pain Amplifier Jelly's sting, though not the minute of blocked healing. It came out of Carl's silver boss box for killing Ruckus.
Carl has given Katia some of the Jellyfish Salve, and he tells her to keep it in her hotlist outside the Akula.

descriptions.text: Jellyfish Salve (5 applications) If you can’t talk someone into peeing on you after you get stung by a Pain Amplifier Jelly, then this will do the trick. Effect: removes the pain portion of the Kill Me Now It Hurts debuff. Warning: It does not remove the one-minute healing block effect associated with the Jelly’s sting.

taglines.text: The Vahana is a Gnomish Legate Balloon, perhaps the oldest vehicle left aboard the Wasteland, black and gold striped from the days when such balloons meant ambassadors and perhaps peace. It brings the gnomes' negotiator down to the sand.
Carl hijacks the Vahana with Donut and Katia and fires his missiles at the Wasteland from its basket. All three jump as the airship's gun battery smashes into it.

descriptions.text: Gnomish Legate Balloon. The Vahana. Contraption. Of all the vehicles left aboard the dreadnaught Wasteland, the Vahana is perhaps the oldest. Once, long ago, the gnomes believed they could avoid war. And while they could not leave this conflict-infested world, they could take to the skies, out of reach of everyone else. They hoped they could set themselves up as neutral peacekeepers. Everyone knew that the black and gold-striped balloons were off limits. The balloons were a symbol of hope. The sight of a Gnomish Legate on the horizon heralded the arrival of ambassadors, and perhaps peace. But when new visitors came to their world, coming via a mysterious portal, everything changed. …

taglines.text: Dolores Doesn't Splat is a potion for anyone falling faster than two hundred kilometers an hour. It speeds the fall, softens the ground at impact, and slams the drinker into it five times in a row.
Dolores Doesn't Splat is no pleasure, but Mordecai calls it genius: Carl's health was still at a hundred percent when he landed.

The Coffee Shop Author Kit is a magical sheet of paper with a quill and a jar of ink. Whatever Carl writes in a new tab of his scratchpad appears on the paper, and whatever is written on the paper appears in the scratchpad.
Clipped to the wall of the bathroom stall in the personal space, the Coffee Shop Author Kit is how Carl and Katia trade messages nobody else can see.

descriptions.text: Coffee Shop Author Kit. Alcoholism and crippling self-doubt not included. So you want to be a writer. It started with sappy poetry in middle school. You soon graduated to Naruto fanfiction. … Anyway, this is a magical sheet of paper. You will find you now have a second tab on your scratchpad in your interface. You can write something on this paper, and it will appear in the scratchpad and vice versa. If the proper spell and glyphs are accurately copied onto this paper, you can present the sheet at a market kiosk, and a scroll will appear for sale. …

taglines.text: Half Splat is a potion against falling: with it the ground cannot kill you, but you land at five percent of your health. Carl, Donut and Katia each have three, from the same Silver Skydiver's box.
At the Butcher's Masquerade Carl has half-splat potions to spare, and he leaves a bathroom counter covered with them, and a note, for the crawlers who come in after him.

A Live Ammo Ball is a dirigible gnome grenade: a fist-sized clamshell sphere holding a living creature in stasis, which bursts out when the ball hits. The five on a dead sniper's bandolier each hold a level-11 frenzied gerbil, and the many more that fell with the Wasteland loose thousands of gerbils on Hump Town.

A big, broken live ammo ball is the casing of the largest bomb Carl has built on purpose: filled with explosives and Nitro Sludge, welded shut, and named by the System Just Wait Until Your Daddy Gets Home.

descriptions.text: Live Ammo Ball. Live ammo balls are a common and versatile ranged weapon of the Dirigible Gnomes. These round, clamshell spheres are designed to be fired great distances using a gnomish Tickle Stick, or they may be manually lobbed like a grenade. They are also fired in large clusters from anti-aircraft point defense batteries. Just be glad you're not in charge of cleaning up that mess. A living, usually angry, creature is placed inside the ball, and the ball opens upon impact with the target. The stasis field keeps the creature within safe from injury until the ball is opened. These balls are similar in technology to pet carriers. …

entities.name: Mongo's speed and strength fang caps

taglines.text: Mongo's second pair of fang caps came out of Donut's platinum quest box, like the first, and adds fifteen percent to the dinosaur's movement speed and fifteen percent to his strength.

The Platinum Sharpening Stone is a little black rock from the quest box for saving Hump Town, made for any spiked weapon and too short-lived to keep. Carl rubs it along his gauntlet's spikes at once, and they grow a little longer.

descriptions.text: Platinum Sharpening Stone. Warning: This item has a short shelf life. Apply this to any spiked offensive weapon to receive the following buffs. Plus (2 x current level)% damage to all attacks. Plus 1 to all current stat buffs. Does not add new buffs if they do not exist. It also makes the weapon look extra oily and mean looking. In other words, the weapon’s appearance may change. But only a little.

taglines.text: Princess Formidable's emergency box gives Katia a set of ten crossbow bolts of Petrify Rock Class. Each one leaves its target Petrified, conscious but unable to move, for sixty seconds, and Mordecai says they cost more than regular bolts.

The Nightmare II is a gnomish Drop Bear biplane the other crawlers found intact, renamed by Carl over its stencilled Death Trap. It runs on gasoline, has a rear-facing gun, and carries an emergency balloon that lifts it to the top of the bubble.
The Nightmare II came down slowly on its emergency balloon after the boss fight, and it lives in the flying house's garage.
Carl has flown the Nightmare II once, against Quan Ch over Orthrus, and it went spiralling into the nose of Emberus and exploded.

Bonnie's necklace looks like a walnut and holds a little purple soul crystal, the power for the balloon that keeps her house afloat. How far its clamshell is open decides how much power the balloon gets, and Carl keeps it open just a fraction.
Katia says that if Carl had not left the controller with Louis, they never could have flown the house to the land quadrant. Louis and Firas have turned into quite the pilots.

descriptions.text: Soul Crystal. F-Quality. Used to power the balloon that keeps this house afloat. Nothing too exciting. You probably want to avoid breaking it, though. Charge: 89% Kill something to charge it up.

taglines.text: A Hobgoblin Disco Ball is a hobgoblin smoke curtain soaked in an invisibility potion. Its rainbow smoke hides everything inside it, bounces to the beat and blinds whoever threw it as well, and Carl's first one goes off on his crafting-room floor.

Orren credits the dust a disco ball leaves behind with Administrator Loita's death, and calls it one of the most brilliant assassinations he has seen a crawler execute. Carl had only wanted the toy too filthy to take into the studio.
Carl throws disco balls in fights now: from the wing of a biplane at Quan Ch, and by hand at Queen Imogen, whose goop-covered face, by Donut's account, never saw Prepotente coming.

descriptions.text: Hobgoblin Disco Ball. Type: Magically-infused Deflagrating Tossable. Effect: It's a real trip. Status: 25. Unstable. Molly not included. Take a Hobgoblin smoke curtain, soak it in an invisibility potion, and what do you get? You get a party, that's what you get! Produces heavy, multi-hued billows of smoke that are both photosensitive and frequency responsive. And in case you don't know what that means, just set one off and find out. The smoke will conceal all movement within, and the plumes will bounce to the beat. Warning: Unlike a regular smoke curtain, the caster of this tossable is not immune to its effects. In other words, you'll be just as blind as the monsters. …

taglines.text: The Belt of Buoyancy is a simple belt that wraps around Donut's stomach and keeps her from sinking, though it only works in the water. She spends a good three minutes complaining about it.

A Potion of Bloodlust doubles its drinker's strength and speed for as many seconds as their constitution, and leaves them not knowing where they are or why they are fighting. Carl has two, and Mordecai tells him not to use them.
Carl does not drink his Potions of Bloodlust. One, taped to a hob-lobber and set off on the flooding bridge of a submarine, spreads through the water and drives Lusca's babies into a feeding frenzy.
Carl's last Potion of Bloodlust goes into a potion ball. Beamed at a flying mantis warrior, it enrages her, and she pulls the head off her own sister.

descriptions.text: Potion of Bloodlust It’s like giving yourself a PCP enema after spending the day riding the Night Train Express. Drinking this potion gives the following effects for (Constitution) seconds. Strength times two. Movement speed times two. Dexterity times .5 The Where the Fuck Am I? Who the Fuck Are You? Debuff Constitution times .5 For every crawler, NPC, or mob killed by you while this potion is active, your movement speed increases by an additional 25%.

taglines.text: Drakea's Enchanted Kerchief of Disorder looks like an ordinary black bandana with a white paisley pattern. It gives Carl +5 to Detect Traps, a level-15 Tripper spell once every five hours, and the Remote Detonator benefit.

Carl's black paisley bandana still gives him a level-15 Tripper. Neither Imani nor Elle can wear it, so Imani carries its Tripper spell as a tattoo from Katia, and Carl feels a jolt in his chest when she casts it.

descriptions.text: Drakea's Enchanted Kerchief of Disorder. This handy-dandy, versatile garment can be worn around the neck, in the hair, or on your face if you want to cosplay as a cowboy robbing a bank. Can also be tied around your arms or legs, but only if you want to look like a moron. Don't tie it around your leg. This simple, square piece of fabric is a reminder that looks can be deceiving. The wearer of this item receives the following benefits: +5 to the Detect Traps skill. Wearer may cast a level-15 Tripper spell once every five hours. The Remote Detonator benefit.

taglines.text: The earth patch is a tiny round patch, the size of a half-dollar, depicting the planet Earth. Sewn onto an eligible garment it gives +5% Strength and immunity from cloud-based attacks, and Donut dismisses it as a screen print.
The earth patch was the first patch on Carl's jacket, sewn on by Katia, and a patch of flaming arrows now sits beside it on his shoulder.

descriptions.text: Upgrade Patch. Small. This patch depicts the planet Earth, which is currently under the regency of the Borant System. Ahh, the planet earth. A whole lot of culture. A whole lot of spunk. So many dumbasses. If this upgrade patch is affixed to an eligible garment, it will imbue the following upgrades: +5% to Strength. Immunity from cloud-based attacks. Warning: Upgrade patches are fleeting items. You may remove them, but they will be destroyed in the process.

taglines.text: The Enchanted Anarchist's Battle Rattle is a black, sleeveless canvas jacket that gives +1 to all Carl's base stats, a point more for every patch sewn onto it, double that with a back patch. It also adds half again to the range and accuracy of every explosive he throws.
Carl's Battle Rattle now carries three patches, the planet earth, a fistful of flaming arrows and a hand-stitched bomb, and each one adds a point to all his stats.
Carl's Battle Rattle carries five patches now, and on its back the Scavenger's Daughter, a divine back patch that doubles the stat boost they give him.

descriptions.text: Enchanted Anarchist's Battle Rattle. This sleeveless jacket in its current form only offers meager protections compared to some other items of this caliber. However, its ability to host as many upgrade patches as you can fit makes this one of the best, most upgradeable protection items in the game. The plain, unadorned version of this jacket imbues the following effects: +1 to all base stats. This base stat upgrade increases by +1 for every compatible patch that is added to this jacket. If an eligible Back Patch is added, this benefit is doubled. Access to the Desperado Club (already obtained) Access to the Naughty Boys Employment Agency (already obtained) +50% range and accuracy for all thrown explosives.

taglines.text: A Potion of Dinosaur Repellent promises that a pack of dinosaurs will eat its drinker last, for a full thirty hours. Mordecai's "uh-oh" when Carl draws one does not help.
Carl has received ten of these potions and drunk one, though the description is vague about what it actually does. Donut refuses hers, afraid it will make Mongo shy away from her.
Carl leaves a counter covered in these potions for the crawlers on their way into the ballroom, so that loose dinosaurs will go for the hunters and not for them.

descriptions.text: Potion of Dinosaur Repellent. Drink this if your party is attacked by a pack of dinosaurs, and they’ll eat you last. Effect lasts a full 30 hours.

taglines.text: A Ring of Water Breathing is a glowing blue ring that lets its wearer breathe underwater as well as on land, for a point of charisma. Carl, Katia and Tran each get one, and Mordecai warns that it grows gills and makes the skin slimy.
Carl slips the ring on to go into the water after Samantha, and the gills form on his neck at once. Donut is appalled that it costs him only one point of charisma.

descriptions.text: Ring of Water Breathing. If you wear this ring, you can breathe underwater. You can still breathe on land, too. That makes you an amphibian. Did you know that all amphibians swallow their prey whole? That’s such an interesting fact. -1 Charisma

taglines.text: Each of Carl's seven silver Summary Judgement boxes holds a gold piece, a photograph and a Stock Certificate for one share in a company from the home system of one of the plaintiffs who sued him. They are worth about ten credits each, and Mordecai says crawlers should not be getting anything with credit value at all.

King Rust tells Carl that the stock certificate he owns is losing significant value by the moment, now that his daughter has told the whole galaxy the Skull Empire builds backdoors into everything it makes.

descriptions.text: Stock Certificate. The bearer of this instrument now holds one share of common stock in the Sigmund Textiles Foundry, a publicly-traded company based in the Gun-ya system within the Skull Empire and traded via the I.R.F. Last recorded value per share: 10.422 credits.

taglines.text: The Twister is the flying house: a beige suburban house from Texas, cut down to its ground floor, hanging in a net under a huge glowing balloon. Louis and Firas fly it on the air currents and named it; Louis wanted Tiddy Twister II, after his van.
The Twister has gone through the portal to the sixth floor with the changeling refugees. Louis and Firas cannot pass that way, and mean to recover it once they have taken the stairs.
Louis and Firas have the Twister back, with a ballista Bonnie built on the side of its yard. The ceiling on this floor is too low for the balloon to clear the trees.
The Twister is gone. With the mantises aboard, the Sledge, who still has its controller, crashes it into the last two guard turrets still firing.

The Enchanted Handcuffs are novelty cuffs in red, fuzzy velvet, magically reinforced so that only a strength of 200 can break them. There is no key: Carl locks and unlocks them himself, and can set a safe word.

descriptions.text: Enchanted Handcuffs. My safe word is, "Harder, Daddy." You know what these are. Your mom had a pair in her drawer, and your dad was probably no stranger to these things, either. Used to lock a person's arms together at the wrist. This set of novelty handcuffs is magically reinforced. Requires a strength of at least 200 to break. There's no key. These are locked and unlocked magically by you. You may also institute an optional safe word or phrase that disengages.

entities.name: Ping tome
entities.role: Carl's spell book from a quest box

taglines.text: The platinum quest box for saving a puppy held a magical tome, a black leather hardback warm to the touch with a skull on the cover. Opened, it taught Carl Ping.

Rockard's Ring of Sniping is an amber-stoned ring that marks on the map every creature under half health and every one wearing magical gear, which makes stealing kills simple. Carl pulls it off the arm he tore from Quan Ch and puts it on.

descriptions.text: Rockard’s Ring of Sniping. This amber-stoned ring is named after Rockard, one of the dungeon’s most infamous crawlers. This orcish warrior was known for his uncanny ability to swoop in at the last moment and steal glory from other crawlers, gaining the best loot and experience. Everybody hated him. It was great! Fun fact. This guy led his season’s top 10 list until he was knifed in his sleep by his own mother. Luckily for you, crawlers can’t be killed by other crawlers in saferooms anymore. A shame, really. Wearing this ring imbues the following benefits: The Ripe benefit. The Loaded benefit.

taglines.text: The Tome of Twinkle Toes, from Donut's platinum quest box, teaches a cheap spell that makes Mongo, or any other minion, run really fast for as many seconds as her intelligence.
Twinkle Toes lets Mongo outrun the dune buggy, and Donut practices it to level it up. Mongo screeches with joy whenever she casts it.
Hedy the gremlin says pet spells do not work on special mounts, so Twinkle Toes will be no help to a biological vehicle on this floor.

The Enchanted Xistera Extension Slot is a head-throwing attachment made for Carl by the Open Intellect Pacifist Action Network and sent in an emergency platinum benefactor box. On the end of his xistera it throws Samantha five hundred metres for every point of his strength, and taking it off brings her back.
The extension recalls Samantha the moment it comes off Carl's hand, so he does not wear it all day, and she roams free instead.
Dropping the extension brings Samantha back, and what she holds can come with her: once it brought Sister Ines, the sea snake she rode and thousands of seals, crabs and fish, living and undead.

descriptions.text: Enchanted Xistera Extension Slot. Head-throwing attachment. This is a unique item! This item was created especially for Crawler Carl by The Open Intellect Pacifist Action Network, Intergalactic NFC. Attaches to the end of a xistera. Allows for the tossing of a head. This special edition head tosser is custom made to fit decapitated love doll heads. When tossing a head of a withering spirit, the distance traveled will be greatly enhanced. (500 meters x Strength.) Tossed head will be magically returned once the extension slot is removed from xistera.

taglines.text: The Phase Lava Rock potion is one of Mordecai's brews from the toraline yam. For one minute its drinker can move through lava and lava rock, and a creature made of lava rock cannot touch him.

A gold Hunter-Killer Box is the reward for The Hand that Claws the Master, an achievement for permanently killing a non-crawler biological. The achievement may be awarded more than once, but the boxes come only on the sixth floor, and Carl's first batch is thirty-four.
Each Hunter-Killer Box holds gold and the severed hand of a hunter; Carl's thirty-four open one after another, every one with a thousand gold more than the last.
A Hunting Trophy is a hunter's severed hand, and one comes in every Hunter Killer box Carl earns for a kill. The hand is a prize ticket for a counter that opens at the Butcher's Masquerade.
At Chaco's prize counter, hunters' hands are the currency. One buys a 25-pack of potions, thirty buy a future floor boon, and Carl arrives with sixty-six.

descriptions.text: Hunting Trophy. It's the hand of a hunter. Gross. You own 34 of these items. You ever go to one of those arcade pizza joints as a child? You're usually there because it's some other kid's birthday, or worse, because your parent hates raising you so much they'd do anything just to keep you distracted for ten minutes in exchange for a pitcher of watered-down beer. The whole place is chaos. …

entities.name: Just Wait Until Your Daddy Gets Home

taglines.text: Carl's biggest bomb yet: a broken live ammo ball about five feet tall, filled with explosive and Mordecai's Nitro Sludge, welded shut, imbued with Fear and set in a cart for Bomo to pull. The simulator says it flattens everything within a third of a mile.
Kicked out of a saferoom door at Vrah's mantises, the wheeled bomb kills the last three of her mantis warriors, explosion protection and all. Vrah gets away.

descriptions.text: Just Wait Until Your Daddy Gets Home – Wheeled Bomb. Type: High Yield Thermobaric Explosive. Also imbues Fear within blast radius. Effect: I hope you're paid up on your homeowner's insurance. Status: 250. Fortified. Boom.

entities.name: Enchanted Collar Charm of the Effete Bourgeoisie
aka: Collar Charm of the Effete Bourgeoisie

taglines.text: With the ursine town she renames Point Mongo comes a collar charm Donut must wear to order its guards: one tiny turquoise gem for the town, plus eight dexterity, plus four intelligence, the Snitch skill and 3,592 gold every ten days. She hates it, because it replaces her butterfly charm.
A second, red gem hangs on Donut's leadership charm now, for a small settlement: a little intelligence and dexterity, a spear skill she can never use, and only 403 gold every ten days.

descriptions.text: Enchanted Collar Charm of the Effete Bourgeoisie The middle size of the chains of leadership, this pendant signifies you as a member of the elite. Each jewel encrusted upon this charm represents a settlement owned and controlled by the bearer. If one still maintains a settlement's jewel upon the collapse of the level, the holder of this necklace will permanently receive a tax stipend every ten days from that settlement based on size and population. In addition, each gem will impart additional benefits based on the town. In order to upgrade this necklace, one must first conquer an Extra-Large-sized Settlement. Upgraded necklaces will also upgrade all existing gems. …

taglines.text: A pack of twenty trap add-ons called Fail Safes, the prize in a Trapmaster box Carl earns when one of his roadside traps kills a hunter. Each one tells him if its trap is ever disabled or set off.

Carl takes nine potions of Levitation off a dead hunter. They raise the drinker into the air for twice their intelligence in seconds, though nobody says how high one can go or what happens if it runs out on the way down.

A Levitation potion moves its drinker up and down on a slider and nothing more. Mordecai calls them dangerous: they will not stop a fall that already has momentum, so treat it like standing on thin ice.
Carl drinks his last Levitation potion at a railing in Larracos and goes straight up out of Larracos.

Carl's fan box holds a postcard-sized plastic badge on a red lanyard, SPECIAL GUEST flashing round its edge. His fans have put him on the CrawlCon roster for three events, attending virtually, and Zev advises him to cooperate.
Worn round his neck at the production facility, the badge lets Carl see the names over people's heads while his menus are switched off.

descriptions.text: Congratulations, Crawler! You've received a free fan booth at CrawlCon! With thousands of physical attendees and billions of virtual visitors, Dungeon Crawler World fans from all corners of the galaxy gather once every other season to geek out together over all things Crawl! With special guests, panels, vendors, cosplay, and so much more, CrawlCon is the event of the galaxy! Thanks to your fans, you've been added to the CrawlCon roster! You will attend three events! Your presence at the con will be virtual. Please see your outreach associate for details on your schedule.

taglines.text: Major Charlie is a potion Mordecai brews for Carl, usually called Brain Juice, though not even Mordecai can explain the name. It adds ten points of intelligence for thirty seconds, then takes ten away for five minutes.

entities.name: Enchanted Obsidian Bracelet of the Raggle Rouser
aka: Obsidian Bracelet of the Raggle Rouser

taglines.text: The black bracelet Carl took off the moon elf Akland is the Enchanted Obsidian Bracelet of the Raggle Rouser: ten constitution, five dexterity, fifteen percent fire resistance and a level-10 Fireball once every twenty minutes. Donut wears it on a front leg.
Donut has cast her bracelet's Fireball indoors now, into Lucia Mar in a wooden pub, and set its back wall alight.

descriptions.text: Enchanted Obsidian Bracelet of the Raggle Rouser. This item has been upgraded three times. Warning: this item has a 50% chance to permanently break if it's upgraded again. This murky bracelet is light and kinda stylish if you're one of those sad sacks who always wears black and complains about how nobody ever understands you. It's made of obsidian glass, which is actually a type of rock that only forms under extreme, lava-based circumstances. And interestingly enough, this is what you'll turn into if you don't treat this item with the respect it deserves. This bracelet imbues the following effects. +10 to Constitution. +5 to Dexterity. +15% Fire Resistance. Wearer may cast a level-10 Fireball spell once every twenty minutes.

taglines.text: A light-duty trebuchet the size of a windsurfing board, built from glowing, poisonous bamboo by the Dream's raiders and left spiked to the ground in a clearing. It hurls three hundred kilos and infuses whatever it throws with Poison Cloud. Carl takes it.

A little cup on the sling changes the poison: pour a potion in and the rock carries that instead. Loaded with Mordecai's weedkiller, Carl's rock chucker kills an Odious Creeper, and Donut, as spotter, gets the credit.

descriptions.text: Enchanted Venomous Elven Rock Chucker – Contraption. The mounted, fast-attack artillery specialists of the Dream don't bring siege engines with them when they go raiding. That's why they're so annoyingly deadly. Using a combination of knowledge, druid magic, and a little something-something extra—wink—they're able to rapidly construct their war machines on the fly. These can't-take-a-joke beanpoles can conjure up a whole regiment of wall-breaching contraptions in a matter of hours. Translation: you don't want these pale fuckers on your doorstep. This particular light-duty rock thrower is made by casting Bamboozeled on a patch of land and then assembling the device from the resulting poisonous bamboo stalks. …

taglines.text: A card Donut finds on a dead Skull Empire hunter when she loots everything at once. It has no description and looks like a credit card, and she wants to spend it before they cancel it.
