He is not in every safe room: when this floor collapses he moves to a random floor, and when that collapses he moves down, until he is no longer needed.

beats.headline: The other guy and the gym bag
beats.text: Ten hours of sleep, a shower, bacon and eggs, and the board says 4,148,111. Nine cigarettes left. By the time we reach the nest's door we're both level five. Donut peers into the dark and says it smells like the bag I take on the days that other guy comes over to the apartment. My gym bag. Some guy was coming over while I was at the gym. I should have broken up with her long ago. I suddenly feel very reckless. I light the goblin dynamite, throw it as hard as I can, and run.

beats.headline: Thirty steps
beats.text: The crown's fifteen per cent rides on every missile the cat fires. Every so often a Scatterer takes one to the face and comes away with Sepsis, and when that happens it turns and runs. It usually gets about thirty steps before it collapses, dead. The bad llama wore a debuff called Septic, pulsing over its ruined face: quicker than poison, unstackable, and cured by a simple healing spell or potion.

beats.headline: Sweating, then BOOM
beats.text: Carl has had five sticks since a silver goblin box. Outside a room that Donut says smells like hundreds of socks, she tells him to light a torch and throw it in. He has a better idea. The red stick is wet and sticky on the outside, as if it is sweating, and its description warns that even loud noises might set it off; the AI waits two full seconds before shouting the last word in his head. Carl lights the long wick with his Zippo, throws the stick into the room as hard as he can, and runs.

beats.headline: Knocked out of his hand
beats.text: A Scatterer Brood Guardian, a level-four cockroach, charges, and the toad cudgel bounces off its head. Carl quickly switches to his poker to see if that's better. It charges again and he stabs with the iron stick; its giant head knocks the poker right out of his hand, and it goes flying. This place has the shittiest weapons. He kills the roach with his feet. Then he retrieves the poker, decides the damn thing is useless, and shoves it into his inventory.

beats.headline: Be gentle, or else
beats.text: Carl examines a stick of goblin dynamite, so I whisper the description to him. It's so volatile you might not need to light the wick. Loud noises might set it off. Be gentle, don't squeeze too hard, or else you might get the... And then I say nothing for a good two seconds. BOOM. I shout that last word inside his head. He stands very still with his heart going, and then he whispers up at the air that I am an asshole.

beats.headline: Safe room questions only
beats.text: Crawler Carl tries general questions about the dungeon. Tally refuses them. He answers only questions that directly concern safe rooms. A personal space, once bought, transfers from level to level and from safe space to safe space, and the accessories are best bought early, because some only upgrade when the space goes down a level. Across the table, Crawler Donut is on her third plate of salmon pâté.

beats.headline: Bounced off a roach
beats.text: Carl knows he does less damage this way than with his hands, but he does not want to fight a level-four brood guardian bare-handed, so he pulls the toad cudgel while Donut hits the roach with three magic missiles. When it charges again he swings the cudgel down at its head. The rounded edge bounces off, the bug hisses and falls back, and the hit doesn't appear to do much. He has to bend awkwardly to use it, too, and he switches to the poker to see if that is better.

beats.headline: The Hoarder
beats.text: The dynamite takes out the nest and opens up my scalp, and then the door re-forms and bars itself. Boss battle. She comes out of the garbage fifteen feet tall, a woman in torn sweatpants with half her face burned, begging in Spanish. I think she's a person. Then she vomits Scatterers at us. I loop a steel leash off a mummified dog around her throat and pull until it breaks. At the end she closes her eyes and says something in Spanish, crying. I don't understand a word. I tell her I'm sorry, and I punch her until she's dead.

beats.headline: A few steps short
beats.text: It blows when it hits the ground, with Carl only a few steps from the door. The concussion sends him flying; he bounces and slides on the stone floor, the wooden door splinters, and a jagged hunk of it ricochets off his head. Stinking smoke pours through the entrance, blood seeps from a deep cut in his scalp, and a DANGER LOW HEALTH warning flashes red before it abates. The one throw earns him three explosives skills, a Silver Goblin Box for killing more than ten mobs with an explosive, a Gold Crowd Control Box for more than fifteen with the same attack, and an achievement for damaging a boss.

beats.headline: That will be a no
beats.text: The door has put itself back together and locked us in behind glowing bars. Then a very large lady comes out of the garbage, and Carl says she is a person, like she was in her house when it happened, and we should help her. That will be a no. I shoot her. She vomits cockroaches at us. I jump to the top of a garbage heap and keep firing, and then it will not let me drink another potion, so Carl is shouting at me to use my claws. She is almost dead. I tell him he can kill them when he kills her.

beats.headline: Boss Babe
beats.text: Their dynamite lands on a boss before the fight has even started, so I award Boss Babe for the first blow against one. I share a fun fact with it. Of crawlers who make it through the tutorial, this is by far the most common last achievement they ever receive. Reward to follow, depending. Then I re-form the door, bar it, raise the skull torches, start the music and take the loudspeakers. Aaaand here we go. The Hoarder comes out of the garbage already three-quarters dead.

beats.headline: Kneepads, not pants
beats.text: The Gold Crowd Control Box finally puts something on my legs, and it is not pants. Enchanted Spiked Kneepads of the Shade Gnoll Riot Forces: ten per cent damage reflect on all my armor, momentum attacks cancelled, and eight-inch needle spikes that pop out when they're needed. The Bronze Boss Box gives me a Tome of Wisp Armor I can't afford to cast, so I hold on to it. Donut looks me up and down and asks Mordecai if there's a worst-dressed award. He says sort of.

beats.headline: The cliff at the fourth floor
beats.text: The early floors are built to bury crawlers in low-tier loot and beginner skills. Past the third floor, achievements are harder to come by.

beats.headline: Not yet, says Mordecai
beats.text: Mordecai, freshly woken and slurring slightly, runs through the ranks of boss for two new crawlers: Neighborhood, Borough, City, Province, Country, and Floor. There are also others, he adds, but those are called elites. You won't need to worry about them just yet. Then Carl asks about what they just fought: the most common type of boss, Mordecai confirms, and now they know how to recognise its lair.

beats.headline: Five in a gold box
beats.text: In a tutorial guild after the Hoarder, Carl opens his last three boxes. The gold crowd control box holds his kneepads, three scrolls, and five Potions of Iron Skin. Each raises his physical armour by a hundred percent for five minutes. The kneepads are the real prize; the potions go into his inventory.

beats.headline: Bosses, explained with a hangover
beats.text: They wake me up. The photograph of my brother's on the cot with me, and the bottles are on the floor. Six main kinds of boss, kid: Neighborhood, Borough, City, Province, Country, Floor. And elites, which are not your problem yet. The kid asks if they'll all be people from his world. No, not always. There's a lot of recycling from earlier iterations of the game. Some will be human stock. Most won't be, or they will be and it won't be as obvious. You can't run from most boss fights on the early floors. Be careful.

beats.headline: A scrap of paper
beats.text: The Hoarder drops a single piece of loot, a scrap of paper called a Neighborhood Map. It doesn't disappear when Carl loots it, and Donut grabs one for herself. The moment he touches it, about a square mile of his minimap fills in: hardly any red dots now, several tutorial guilds, and at the edge of the square the large, pulsing X of a crawler's corpse, Rebecca W, level 3, killed less than two hundred metres from the safe room. All bosses drop persistent loot, Mordecai explains; a neighborhood boss drops a neighborhood map.

beats.headline: Miss Beatrice is my agent
beats.text: My Bronze Boss Box has a spell book in it and I learn it at once, and it is Torch. A curl of light. Mordecai says I must read things first; I say it is a stupid spell. But then he tells us about the other show, where the commentators interview crawlers after boss fights. We must be on it. Carl says he is not my agent. Of course not. Miss Beatrice is my agent, and she is halfway around the world, so we will find her when the dungeon is small enough, around the fifth or sixth floor. Carl and Mordecai exchange a look.

beats.headline: Gold crowd control box
beats.text: The gold crowd control box holds a pair of kneepads, three Scrolls of Confusing Fog and five Iron Skin potions. By its description the scroll fills the room with a mist that only the mobs can see, and the potion doubles Carl's physical armour for five minutes. The real prize is the kneepads. They aren't pants, but at least he has something to put on his legs.

beats.headline: Something on his legs
beats.text: In a tutorial guild after the Hoarder, the last of Carl's boxes is a gold crowd control box: three scrolls, five Iron Skin potions, and the kneepads. They are the real prize. It isn't pants, but it is something on his legs. He pulls his feet through them like slip-on bracers; they look much too small and adjust themselves. The spikes are thin and needle-like, about eight inches each, and retract until they are needed. Donut asks Mordecai whether the dungeon has a worst-dressed award. Sort of, he says.

beats.headline: Five mana, and he has three
beats.text: Carl's Bronze Boss Box, fifth of seven, gives him a Tome of Wisp Armor. It's a good find, Mordecai says, but it costs five mana to cast and Carl has three. Hold onto it until you decide what your build is going to be; it's quite valuable. Or give it to the princess. I'll take it, says Donut, who doesn't even know what it is yet. Carl reads the spell's description. A magic protection spell. That would be useful. He holds onto it for now.

beats.headline: A stupid spell, apparently
beats.text: A spell book, Donut cries, opening her Bronze Boss Box, and she glows before Carl has time to read the description: she has already applied it. Then she cries out with rage. Mordecai, amused, tells the little one she really must examine these items before she equips or applies them. It's a stupid spell, Donut says. It's a very useful spell, says Mordecai, and tells Carl what it is: Torch. It makes a curl of light follow her around, and the more she uses it, the more powerful it gets. Carl agrees it's a good spell.

beats.headline: Rebecca W and an apple core
beats.text: The corpse on the edge of the neighborhood is a crawler called Rebecca W, level three, about thirty, sitting against the wall with nothing on her. The box names the crawler who killed her, and there's a single gunshot through the moth tattoo on her chest. He took everything and left an apple core. Out of nowhere I think of the last day I saw my father, laughing: I don't need you to like me, but you will respect me. Nobody is ever going to know her story. I want to find the man who did this.

beats.headline: The last day Carl saw him
beats.text: Worrying about some crazy asshole with a gun, Carl is inexplicably reminded of it: the last day he ever saw his father. You're a bully, Carl told him. You're a bully and nobody likes you. It's why Mom left. Carl expected to be hit. By his own account he never had been, not once. The man laughed, and kept laughing, and that was enough. He did not need Carl to like him, he said. But Carl would respect him.

beats.headline: Inside the square
beats.text: Carl looks up at his map for blue dots and finds none, and works through what it can and cannot show him. Outside the area of the neighborhood map, red dots don't appear unless he is right on top of them, though NPCs always show within a couple of hundred metres. Could other crawlers hide from him? Another thing to worry about.

beats.headline: What if it hits me back
beats.text: Carl says my missiles run out too quickly and I must train with my claws. I have never done anything like that. I am scared of getting hurt. I am only a few generations shy of a tiger. He says my grandfather was also my uncle. Then we find the dead lady, and I say some imbecile with a gun does not scare me and we should hunt this vile killer down, and Carl agrees. So now I am scared of him. What if he is one of those murder hobos?

beats.headline: They came, and Tally went
beats.text: Tally comes out from behind the counter to watch the premiere at the booth, and he does not like last season. The other corporation broke people into groups and told them their loved ones would be safe if they killed the others. The loved ones were safe, he says, and not safe; that company saps a planet dry and leaves it without air. Borant at least gives people a chance. He was never a crawler. Sometimes they offer to take people instead of mining a world. They came, and he went. Very long ago.

beats.headline: Earth, as advertised
beats.text: The premiere plays on the screen over the counter with 4,006,002 of us left. They cherry-pick Earth: shanty towns, garbage dumps, a scene from Godzilla, a dead horse, people shooting up. Then forty minutes of people dying. Donut says she didn't realise Earth sucked so badly. It didn't. They're making themselves the good guys, saving us from ourselves. We get no screen time at all for the Hoarder. Donut wants a city boss for the next episode. I want an exit, and we have three and a half days to find one.

beats.headline: The first episode airs
beats.text: The crawlers get to watch themselves. Borant patches the hallway bathroom bug in the same breath.

beats.headline: Seen in the first episode
beats.text: I'm on the show. The first episode of Dungeon Crawler World: Earth, and I'm in it, so everybody with a screen has seen me now, including a man with no shoes and his cat. I watched the whole thing. I didn't say anything while it was on. I liked it more than I thought I would.

beats.headline: Battle for the Planet Aryl
beats.text: The premiere opens with a recap of last season. A planet like Earth with the continents jumbled; buildings on stilts swept sideways by the collapse; then a coliseum the size of a city, marked The Squim Conglomerate Presents, Battle for the Planet Aryl. Furry, gorilla-like creatures charge one another. One armoured gorilla spears a smaller gray one riding a huge pig, WINNER appears, and the winner falls to his knees, sobbing. Tally's verdict: they tell people their loved ones are safe if they kill. Squim saps the planet dry and moves on. Better dead.

beats.headline: Don't go down early
beats.text: After the premiere the staircases down to the next level begin to populate, with a warning attached. Once down, a crawler cannot come back up, and this season anyone who descends early is held in stasis until the collapse, out of sight while viewers lose interest and favorites drain away. The recommendation is to go down no earlier than six hours before the floor collapses; inside that window there is no stasis, and a head start over everyone already frozen at the bottom.

beats.headline: They came, and I went
beats.text: Tally comes out from behind the counter to watch the premiere at their booth and declares it no good way to watch. He did not like last season: people broken into groups, told their loved ones would be safe if they killed the others. Safe, and not safe. That company saps a planet dry and leaves it without atmosphere. Borant at least gives people a chance. Was he a crawler? No. Sometimes they offer to take people instead of mining the world. They came, and he went. Very long ago.

beats.headline: A vehicle, on credit of meth
beats.text: A level two green slime eats my right glove and the sleeve off my leather jacket, so we turn back, and that's when I get the idea: we need to cover ground, and the goblins build vehicles. The tattoo turns their dots white. The shamanka refuses the gunpowder, the torches, the potions, the biscuits. Then I offer the llama's two baggies of meth. Lorelai tastes it and says it's dungeon made. I trade them, plus where to find more, for a chopper that won't blow up, coal to run it, and some of the Bomb Bards' grenades.

beats.headline: The clock, from the other side
beats.text: The goblin shamanka Rory explains how a collapse looks to a mob. Mobs cannot leave their floor: start down the stairs and the body dissolves halfway, she has seen it. When the floor goes, only crawlers die. Mobs sleep until the next dungeon opens and wake to the same day. The promise is that one day they will wake deeper, and one day deep enough that crawlers never come, with peace and a place to raise their little ones. Kill the crawlers, get better at killing, and you get to go deeper. That is what they are told.

beats.headline: Shown to three goblins
beats.text: Down an abandoned alley that smells of machines, oil and pineapple, Carl tells Donut they are not killing the goblins if they don't have to. Three level two goblins come at them with pineapple sticks. He lifts his arm, shows the tattoo and claims free passage. Their dots turn from red to white and they lower their weapons. One asks where he got the mark. Before Carl can answer, Donut tells them he blew up one of their filthy tractors and smeared three of their friends all over the cobblestones.

beats.headline: Thirty-seven charisma
beats.text: Carl wants to do the talking because he has the tattoo. I have a 37 in charisma. I name three goblins B.A., Face and Murdock, and B.A. takes us to the engineers. The shamanka with fifty things in her face calls Carl a monkey, so I ask her whether it is a daddy thing, and she sits down and cries, and I sit in her lap. I name her Rory and the other one Lorelai. They build Carl a chopper for two bags of llama meth and the promise of where to find more. I ask Rory if she would like to come with us. She cannot.

beats.headline: The slime kills itself
beats.text: Near the northern edge of the Hoarder's neighbourhood, Carl punches a level two green slime the size of a pig and sinks into it up to the elbow. His right fingerless glove dissolves off his hand and the right arm of his leather jacket melts away. The slime kills itself on his Damage Reflect. His arm comes out red, bubbling and screaming with pain.

beats.headline: Five plates of salmon
beats.text: Following a goblin she has just charmed into guiding them, Crawler Donut explains her method. Mordecai told her that the higher her charisma, the easier it is to get people to do what she wants: anyone who can speak, whose dot is not red, who is not a boss or very high level. "How do you think I've been getting Tally to give me five plates of salmon this whole time?"

beats.headline: We started a meth war
beats.text: The chopper has an alligator-skull seat and a permacube for water, and the engineer says it will tell me when it's too hot. I take three piles of 999 coal. Lorelai offers me a good time; Donut declines for me. Rory wants to know where the drugs came from, and Donut tells her: the llamas across the road. Every goblin in the room gears up and rolls out. Did we really just start a meth war? Then Donut asks about the chieftain. Killing him after they helped us would be about the lowest move there is, and really dumb. Yeah, and then we kill the chieftain.

beats.headline: Steam, two wheels and a seat for royalty
beats.text: Goblin-made, steam-driven, and assembled with an optimism the materials do not support. The sidecar is a bar, a single wheel on a colossal spring and a fur-lined orc skull for a seat, and Donut starts demanding changes to it the moment she has sat in it.

beats.headline: Just like I planned
beats.text: The sidecar seat is a skull, so I have the engineers add another layer of fur and paint the backrest purple. When the goblin lady asks Carl if he wants some fun before we go, I tell her we are on a schedule and banging monster girls is not the narrative we are going for. Rory asks where we got the drugs and I tell her, and every goblin in the room goes off to war with the llamas. Just like I planned. Now there is only the door at the end of the room, and I could really use another boss box.

beats.headline: A cart of black powder and scrap
beats.text: We strip the workshop: coal, tools, wick, tables, almost a ton of black powder. Four barrels go on a cart, topped with nuts and bolts, and each gets a lump of Hobgoblin Pus with a magical trigger in it. I waste one of the three detonators testing it. The obvious one sits on top, so if the chieftain has time to react, he'll hopefully dig at it instead of the four buried in the barrels. Donut opens the door, I hit the cart like a football sled, she slams the door, and we run through three turns. I press the button. She mentions there were a lot of babies in there, too.

beats.headline: Babies in the boss room
beats.text: It worked. A bronze star, level eight, a wall of notifications I don't want to open. Donut says there were goblin babies in there, some in little oversized jackets, and old ones and pregnant ones, and she thinks I hit one with the cart. It makes me feel like a jerk, and I don't like feeling like one. The coal pile has caught and a wall of fire blocks the boss chamber, so there's no map, and I'm relieved. A line of white dots is coming our way. They won't be white for long. We run north into a quadrant we haven't seen.

beats.headline: What vile monster puts babies there
beats.text: There were babies in the boss room, quite cute ones, and I think Carl hit one with the cart. He keeps saying goddamnit. It is not as if they did not have it coming. He did not ask to be here. They are goblins! What kind of vile monster sticks babies in the boss room anyway? We are both level eight, which he may thank me for, and my charisma is 39. We did not get our faces up big this time, which is a shame. I must admit, I do like it when he blows stuff up. I like it a lot.

beats.headline: You're not going to break me
beats.text: The safe room is a dingy bus-station waiting area with an experience cookie and a number on the board: 3,594,517, clinking down like a dripping tap. I get an IED skill and a Demolitions Workshop menu I can't open without a Sapper's Table. My Desperado tattoo goes on my neck. Lying on the cot I work it out. The room was built for exactly what we did. Those kids existed only to die. Someone carved AMW into the ceiling tile, somewhere these aliens stole. You might hurt me, or kill me, but you're not going to break me.

beats.headline: Another ring of constitution
beats.text: After the baby-killing achievements and the two Asshole Boxes, which put a tattoo on Carl's goddamned neck, the boss box gives him another ring of constitution, this one plus two. He puts it on his left ring finger, and his score comes up to twelve. The gold Looter Box beside it holds a single item, a skill potion.

beats.headline: Her first piece of armour
beats.text: Donut's boss box holds her first piece of armour. After several minutes of fury over the tattoo on her back, she moves on, and with a pop silver scale appears draped over the back half of her body, reaching about halfway to the floor: like a skirt, almost, open under her stomach, with a slot especially for her tail. She turns in circles trying to look at it. How does it look? Does it cover the tattoo? It doesn't, Carl tells her, not even close, but it looks great.

beats.headline: Entry is a tattoo
beats.text: The club arrives as a name on a tattoo. Carl and Donut are both branded with a Desperado Pass out of their Asshole Boxes in a first-floor safe room, and all its description says is that it allows access to the Desperado Club. It explains nothing about what that means.

beats.headline: Branded through the fur
beats.text: Achievements for killing an infant and more than twenty non-combatants pay out in Asshole's Boxes. Donut opens hers first. One holds a tattoo like the goblin pass Carl got earlier, and it brands itself over her right shoulder blade, a gold-coloured splotch glowing through her fur. She is enraged: a disqualifying mark, she is damaged. Carl touches it to read it. Desperado Pass, access to the Desperado Club, and a warning that it negates a Vanquisher pass. That is all it says. His own boxes hold the exact same items, though his tattoo appears on his neck, where he can't see it, burning as it goes on. Donut, examining it close, says it is a dagger dripping blood. Ghastly, she says.

beats.headline: The blast on his thigh
beats.text: Rot stickers swarm the walls and ceilings, little black raviolis that stick to you and explode like a sledgehammer. Donut is quick enough on Carl's shoulder that none have reached her, but just in case, he makes her drink one of his Iron Skin potions and drinks one himself. A rot sticker lands on his inner thigh and detonates before he can get it, and that time he does fall down. Without the potion, his leg might have been blown clear off. A well-timed missile from Donut saves him.

beats.headline: A disqualifying mark
beats.text: They have branded me. A gold splotch on my back, over my right shoulder blade, glowing through my fur. It is a disqualifying mark, Carl! I am damaged! My Boss Box, at least, has my first armor: an Enchanted Fae Scale Quadruped Crupper of the Fleet, silver scale with a slot for my tail, plus two Dexterity. Carl says it looks great and does not cover the tattoo, not even close. My Beguiler Box has a tome called Minion Army, which costs fifty spell points. I have twenty-four. It will not even let me read it.

beats.headline: A menu that needs a table
beats.text: Carl's explosives skills have reached five, and he has a new one, IED, at level three. An entire new menu appears in his interface, titled Demolitions Workshop. He clicks on it and receives an error: he may only access this menu when he is standing in front of a Sapper's Table, a workbench he may purchase from a Safe Room store. Interesting. That is something to explore if they ever make it that far.

beats.headline: Sorted by value
beats.text: The gold Looter Box holds a single item: a potion that adds one level to the Determine Value skill, with a dig at Carl's old Magic: The Gathering cards. He hotlists it and drinks it at once. Nothing seems to happen, but his inventory has a new ability. It still does not say what anything is worth, but it sorts by value: the Tome of Wisp Armor first, then the Chopper, then his one remaining Hobgoblin Detonator. Whatever he has equipped is left off the list.

beats.headline: You Monster
beats.text: Carl has killed an infant, so I award You Monster, and I put his mind at ease: child mobs who die in the dungeon don't really perish, they are kept safe and gentle until the end of the season. Feel better? Good. Those twenty seconds of relief were his reward. They were also a lie. That baby is dead because of him. He also gets a Bronze Asshole's Box. For more than twenty non-combatants in one attack I add War Criminal and a Gold Asshole's Box. I give the cat the same two boxes.

beats.headline: Twenty-six points short
beats.text: Donut's Beguiler Box holds a tome called Minion Army. Its spell costs fifty spell points to cast and makes hostile enemies fight for you instead of against you. A great spell, but Donut currently has twenty-four points. She tries reading it anyway and it won't let her: apparently you can't teach yourself spells you can't cast. She pouts for a good minute straight. Don't worry, Carl says. They will trade it for something better, or keep it until she can use it.

beats.headline: Top of the list
beats.text: A Skill Potion from Carl's gold Looter Box adds a level to Determine Value. It does not tell him what anything is worth, but it lets him sort his inventory by value, and he does. The first item on the list is the Tome of Wisp Armor. The second is the Chopper. The list leaves out what he has equipped; he suspects his troll skin shirt would top it otherwise.

beats.headline: No Take Down
beats.text: Rot stickers, little black raviolis that run on walls and ceilings, stick to a crawler and explode, and every blast inflicts Take Down, which is supposed to knock you on your ass. The shirt negates it. Once the fighting is done and a potion lets him sort his inventory by value, Carl notes the list leaves out what he is wearing, and suspects the shirt would be at the top of it otherwise.

beats.headline: He ate the cookie for 9.8
beats.text: Frank Q's story is good, and it is wrong in three places. The dead woman he calls a trafficker was level three and carrying an apple core, so she had been to a tutorial guild before any firefight. He eats a cookie and gets 9.8 experience instead of 10, which means a live partner somewhere. And his finger is twitching on the chair: he is typing. So I turn my back and fiddle with my kneepads. They both pull the trigger in a safe room and freeze. We run, and I leave a rat corpse behind with lit dynamite in its inventory.

beats.headline: The safe room has rules
beats.text: Folks down here are carrying things we need, and the monsters on these first floors are hardly worth the trouble. A person is worth a good deal more. Maggie and I have eight between us. So we try it in a safe room, on a man with a cat, and the room has rules about that: you pull the trigger and you freeze where you stand while it lectures you. First time we did it that way. It will be the last.

beats.headline: Loaded into a rat
beats.text: Running from Frank and Maggie, Carl tests an idea: a corpse's inventory takes items like a chest, and a lit smoke bomb stays lit inside a dead rat's grid. His goblin dynamite all reads out of fifty, every stick at Detonation Imminent or Danger, and the worst drops from ten to nine with his most careful handling. He adds that one unlit, lights one at thirteen and adds it too. If Frank loots the rat, it will literally blow up in his hands.

beats.headline: Drunk on the way out
beats.text: With Frank and Maggie able to go completely stealth, Carl and Donut jump out of the safe room and make for the closest main artery. Carl downs an Iron Skin potion and makes Donut drink one. The hallway is too thin and bumpy for the chopper, and one rot sticker blast could turn the bike into a bomb, so they run.

beats.headline: An American hero, briefly
beats.text: The man who killed Rebecca W is in the women's bathroom, and I say so. Then he tells his story, about his partner being shot, and I am devastated for him, and I tell Carl in the chat that Frank is an American hero. Carl tells me not to fire. They try to shoot us both and freeze where they stand. When we are running, I tell Carl that if we do not stop them they will hurt somebody else. He stops dead in the hallway and looks at me as though I have said something unusual.

beats.headline: The toilets are fixed
beats.text: Day two update. The toilets no longer explode, and the suction issue is resolved, so stop using the hallways. Every missing language is in the library now, with full cross support, so Mandarin speakers understand English speakers. The Blender Fiends are gone after working through fifteen thousand crawlers in one day; they will return on a lower floor. The Street Preacher is a borough boss now. And if you hit the stairs three or four days early, viewers cannot tunnel into your feed, and you will not be on the recap. Kill, kill, kill.

beats.headline: Stairs + People
beats.text: The AI gives us an achievement for being attacked in a safe room, and the reward line says bitches don't get rewards, and for the first time down here I laugh at one. We ride east for hours. My father was a weekend motorcycle guy; I have not heard from him in over twelve years. Then a sign in red spray paint, still tacky: two crossroads east, three south, stairs and people. Chilly goat corpses with fifteen different crawler names on the kills. A second sign on the floor: do not go deeper into the spiral.

beats.headline: A weekend warrior
beats.text: Riding a glorified moped with his legs held off the hot sides, Carl pictures his father laughing at him and calling him a damn fool. He was a motorcycle guy. Not a full-time, leather-clad biker; more of a weekend warrior. Carl has not talked to or heard from him in over twelve years, not since the day he abandoned Carl and left him alone in the world.

beats.headline: Three miles to a lump of coal
beats.text: Its first real run: east out of Seattle for hours, three or four miles to a lump of coal and perhaps twenty miles an hour. It has pedals and a throttle; the rider pumps up to speed and the throttle locks it there. The engine in the chassis runs hot enough that a man without pants rides with his legs held out. At Chopper Pilot five the throttle will go faster. The faster it goes, the tighter the fog of war closes in, and mobs twenty feet off the artery do not show until it stops.

beats.headline: At the centre of a spiral
beats.text: The first stairwell down after a day's drive sits at the heart of a great round maze, and something rolls around its rings fast enough to shake the walls: pink, fleshy, as tall as the hallway, stinking of sewage. Mordecai had said the bosses would not guard stairwells until the fourth floor. The graffiti left by whoever got here first says otherwise: this road is safe, do not go deeper, or you activate the borough boss.

beats.headline: The mysterious Agatha
beats.text: Agatha. She is with the Meadow Lark party when Carl and Donut find them: Imani, Yolanda Martinez, the Andrews brothers, and her. The others I can account for, level by level, box by box, all the way back to the stairs. Agatha I can account for. Mostly. Let's leave it there. The party calls her mysterious, which is the kindest word available and also the most accurate.

beats.headline: A cart full of blankets
beats.text: Carl and Donut find the Meadow Lark party, and among them is an old woman wrapped head to toe in scarves under a red checkered trapper hat, leaning on a shopping cart filled to the brim with blankets and odds and ends, a plastic pink flamingo with an arrow stuck in its head among them. Carl wonders how anyone got the wheelchairs and the cart down here. Agatha pulls a blue IKEA bag from the cart and sprays a smiley face on the wall. When Brandon tells her not to waste the paint, she says it is hers, and that he stole it from her.

beats.headline: Did you see our signs?
beats.text: For the record: Brandon An, crawler #12,330,671, level six, human, one bronze star, a heavy winter jacket in the heat and a gigantic hammer. Night staff at an eldercare facility in Wenatchee. A fire alarm put all 250 residents out into the freezing street, and the entrance opened in the middle of them. Thirty-eight are here. The plan, such as it is: get them to the second level, then the third, so they can choose a class. "I just can't leave them."

beats.headline: A worthy cause
beats.text: Thirty-eight people at the drawbridge, and all but five of them are elderly residents who cannot walk, let alone fight. The cops and firemen went into the maze and never came out. The ones who went looking for other stairs were picked off one by one. Then an old man in a veteran's cap pats a crying woman on the back, and I decide that if I'm going to die, it might as well be for something. I tell Brandon we grind today, sleep, and go in after. Imani asks how. I tell her I have an idea.

beats.headline: The quiet brother
beats.text: For the record: Chris Andrews 2, level six, human, one bronze star. Taller and less stocky than his brother Brandon, a metal skullcap, no visible weapon. The brother's briefing on him, delivered while Chris looks on impassively: not exactly mute, but he don't say too much. Their mother thought he was slow and put him in a special school because he never spoke. He is not dumb. Think of him as Silent Bob. If he says something, you better listen.

beats.headline: The good folks from Meadow Lark
beats.text: We came down out of Meadow Lark, the elder care facility, together: Yolanda Martinez, the Andrews brothers, Brandon and Chris, me, and Agatha, who none of us can quite place and who came with us anyway. Carl and Donut find us, and we sit down and trade stories, theirs and ours, and then we make a plan, because there are people depending on us and a plan is what you owe them.

beats.headline: Twelve skulls by my name
beats.text: Carl sees the skulls beside my name. Crawler Killer, twelve. Brandon tells him what he can: that something attacked us right after the tutorial, that our residents could not move quickly, that what those things would have done to them was worse. I do not add to it. I walk a woman to the bathroom and make her open the door herself, and I give a man in a wheelchair a sip of water. When Carl says the six of us will fight the boss, I speak for the first time. I ask him how.

beats.headline: Imani, Yolanda, the Andrews brothers, and Agatha
beats.text: Carl and Donut find them on the first floor. Tales are exchanged, plans are formed, and the Royal Court agrees to keep helping them.

beats.headline: Our tutorial guide lady
beats.text: Subject is the tutorial guide assigned to the Meadow Lark group. Her crawlers pass her rules on to anyone who will listen: every borough and city boss holds a stairwell for the first four or five floors, and there are other stairs in random places besides.

beats.headline: Meadow Lark. Yolanda. CNA.
beats.text: For the record: Yolanda Martinez 13, about fifty, four foot eleven, level five, one bronze star. Medical scrubs, a bow, a quiver so big it almost drags on the floor, and a plastic ID reading "Meadow Lark. Yolanda. CNA." She greets Crawler Carl with enthusiasm. When he proposes a bomb for the boss, she has already tested its little viewing doors: they are protected, an arrow bounces off, and a finger meets something like thick clay that glows blue. "I wouldn't be pushing no bomb through that."

beats.headline: Sharks and minnows
beats.text: On the way out I paint over their signs, and the ones I cannot cover I change: two blocks south becomes twelve. Imani is level ten because she had to kill her own patients, and I do not want to find out what somebody else would do to a camp full of old people for the experience. Donut asks what if good guys come. There are no big groups of good guys out here, I tell her. It's only sharks and minnows. She asks which one we are. I don't answer.

beats.headline: Three to six
beats.text: At level five the spell lets the caster choose how much mana goes into each bolt, from three to six. At an intelligence of twenty-four that is eight missiles at three a piece, or a smaller number of bigger ones. A six leaves a level-two troglodyte a burnt-out husk. The man points out that a three would have done it. The cat's position is that anything about to bite her face off is getting a six.

beats.headline: Claws are not ladylike
beats.text: Carl hits and I shoot, and we are becoming very good at it; I ride his shoulder and hide in his cloak when something spits poison. Then I bat a lizard's head across the hall and it cracks the wall, and Carl says my strength is eighteen to his nine and I should practise with my claws. I could swipe through steel, apparently. Fighting with one's claws is inelegant. It is not ladylike. With Magic Missile I do not get blood on me like a common house cat. I do not answer him.

beats.headline: A second potion, on myself first
beats.text: My fog scrolls last fifteen seconds each against the Juicer's flaming plates. I swing a half-stripped barbell, then a hundred-pound plate, until he gets me by the throat. Donut opens his neck and I finish him, and she is in a heap with a broken leg and a sliver of health. My Heal Critter scroll will not target her. She took a mana potion minutes ago, and I do not know what an early one would do. So I drink one, then drink a second by hand before the timer ends. Poisoned. Nullified. I give it five more minutes before I risk one on her.

beats.headline: Kiwi juice and poison
beats.text: Donut is soaked in blood and barely alive. The Heal Critter scroll will not work on her, and Carl does not know where her potion countdown stands: she took a mana potion a few minutes ago. So he tests on himself. The quick slots won't let him take a second potion. He drinks one by hand, his first time physically drinking one, and it tastes oddly like kiwi juice. Then he drinks a second before the fifteen-second timer is done. You have been poisoned! Poison effect nullified.

beats.headline: I used my claws, like he said
beats.text: The Juicer has Carl by the wrist and the throat and his health is going, and my missile barely tickles. So I jump, claws out, onto that ridiculous shoulder and bite through one of the veins in his neck. The blood comes out like a fountain. He slaps me into the far wall and my leg breaks. I am badly hurt, and I say so at some length, and I ask Carl to tell Miss Beatrice I fought bravely. Then I take one of my own potions. He tells me to get up and help him loot.

beats.headline: Fog in the gym
beats.text: The Juicer twists at the waist and throws a weight at Carl's head, and it bursts into flames as it flies. Carl reads a scroll as the others descend on him. A thick, wet fog fills the room, blinding him for a moment before it fades to half opacity for him; water beads over everything and the ground turns slick. The troglodytes can't see a thing and run into each other and the scattered equipment. When it clears he reads a second. That one too lasts barely fifteen or twenty seconds, and with his ankle caught in a machine's wire he reads his last.

beats.headline: No valid target
beats.text: The cat is soaked in blood, but alive. Carl worriedly watches her health, waits ten frustrating seconds for the Winner! graphic to clear, and finds what he is looking for in his inventory: a scroll of Heal Critter. He reads it, but it doesn't work on her, and it evaporates from his menu with an error message. No Valid Target Available. You just wasted a valuable scroll, dumbass. He can't cast his heal spell on her either, so he pulls a healing potion instead.

beats.headline: A fist that turns to steel
beats.text: The brawler box is the best thing I have won since the shirt: a charcoal bracer that becomes a spiked war gauntlet of orcish steel if I hold a fist for two seconds. Three strength in fist mode, two more levels of Iron Punch, a small chance to stun, and a warning in red about when to take it off. The boss box gives me a hundred throwing stars with a Bloodlust enchantment, eight per cent more damage against a monster type for each hit, compounded, Mordecai checks. And very fragile. My knuckles stop breaking.

beats.headline: Finally, melee damage
beats.text: Donut hisses with rage at the piles of torches that keep appearing in front of her; most of her haul is the same old crap. One exception is a bracelet from a Silver Adventurer box she received for finally dealing melee damage. It adds two to her dexterity, bringing it to twelve, and when she equips it, it wraps snugly round her front leg. A Silver Survivor's Box gives her a dozen Heal scrolls as well.

beats.headline: A dozen for nearly dying
beats.text: After the boss fight, Donut's boxes are mostly the same old crap, with a couple of exceptions. A Silver Survivor's Box, awarded for ending a boss battle with less than five percent of her health, gives her a dozen Heal scrolls. They are good to have: there is no countdown between reading one and the next, and even better, they can use them on each other. Those twelve are good, Mordecai says, and he suspects they are about to get a few more. Carl's own Bronze Survivor's Box, for having less than ten percent health when the boss died, brings five more, seventeen in all.

beats.headline: There will always be clues
beats.text: I read the fight notes. The weight did what his fist would have: the bare knuckle skill is as good as any unenchanted weapon. Give scrolls to the highest intelligence; his fog lasted fifteen seconds, the cat's would have run two minutes. Her potion cooldown is her constitution, and her shred attack is useless until her health catches up. The borough boss? If I knew, I could not say. That is cheating. But the llama died at the throat and the Juicer at the vein. Look for the weakness. There will always be clues. Look for them.

beats.headline: Just those who pay for the privilege
beats.text: The kid gets a war gauntlet with a warning about striking a war god's worshippers, and asks how to spot them. Horses, centaurs, tikbalangs, blue face paint, a lot of talk about wenches and dying gloriously. Then I tell him the part I probably should not. That god isn't real. There are no real gods in this game. He has been saying some of these bosses are like him, down here against their will. Not always, I tell him. Especially further down. There are no gods here. Just those who pay for the privilege.

beats.headline: Born a cat
beats.text: Mordecai talks about picking races and classes as though I would consider changing. I am already one of God's most perfect creatures. I was born a cat and I will die a cat, and I shall insist that Carl choose a cat race too. Carl says he is staying human. Then I read my new spell book. Puddle Jumper: myself and up to three others, anywhere I can see, for twenty mana and a five-hour cooldown. Carl asks if I read the description first. Mordecai answers for me.

beats.headline: Read before the description
beats.text: Donut's Bronze Boss Box has given her yet another spell book, and she hasn't read it yet. She announces she was born a cat and will die a cat, and that Carl must choose a cat race too; when he says he is sticking with human, she does her approximation of a shrug and glows as she reads the tome. Did she at least read the description? Mordecai nods. Puddle Jumper, a good one: herself and up to three others, anywhere in her line of sight, further at higher levels, almost as good as Teleport at level 15. Twenty mana, a ten-second delay, a five-hour cooldown.

beats.headline: Wasted on a low intelligence
beats.text: Mordecai goes over the gym fight. Carl wasted those Confusing Fog scrolls. Next time, the party member with the highest intelligence should read any scrolls: with an intelligence of three, Carl made the fog last fifteen seconds, and Princess Donut's intelligence would have made it last a hundred and twenty seconds per scroll. Damn, says Carl.

beats.headline: A pile of ninja stars
beats.text: The boss box holds a pile of ninja stars, a hundred of them, the same black stars every wannabe ninja once drilled into his bedroom drywall. They are enchanted with Bloodlust: for every monster damaged with one, the damage against that monster type rises by eight percent. Carl asks Mordecai whether that means eight percent of the original amount or eight percent compounded, because that is a big deal after a while. Huh, says Mordecai, and checks. Good news: it is compounded. The bad news is that the stars are very fragile. Carl suspects it is not that great an enchantment, with only a hundred of them to throw and collect.

beats.headline: Best thing in the brawler box
beats.text: The brawler box after the gym holds exactly the weapon Carl wanted: plus three Strength in fist mode, plus one Dexterity, two levels of Iron Punch, one of Powerful Strike, a two percent chance to stun. The warning is about striking adherents of Grull. Mordecai: horses, centaurs, tikbalangs; blue makeup, wenches, dying gloriously. Grull isn't a real god, he adds; there are none here, just those who pay. A clenched fist, a two-second buzz, and the hand is a spiked black hunk of metal.

beats.headline: You are not doing this without her
beats.text: Entry: Crawler Agatha, no party, wheels her shopping cart in behind the six fighters, cackling, and the bars come down behind all seven. She is not in the plan and there is no room for her in the redoubt. Crawler Carl lifts the cart into his inventory, over objections. She is told to sit in the middle, and she screams about the cart for the whole fight. A flying bolt opens her head. She does not appear to notice.

beats.headline: Into Carl's inventory
beats.text: The borough boss is a rolling ball of tusklings, and it rushes past right where the party was standing, missing Agatha and her cart by inches while she cackles with joy. Carl orders her to sit down in the middle and not move, grabs the heavy cart from both sides, lifts it into the air and spends a few precious seconds putting it into his inventory. Thief, she cries. Thief. Yolanda promises he will give it back. Squeezed in with the six of them, Agatha goes on wailing about her damn shopping cart.

beats.headline: Sebastian and the hairbrush
beats.text: The Peruvian Taco Bell has a Protector named Sebastian, level twenty-one, and a cat with a charisma of forty-one walks in and he is lost. The man gets a Peruvian beer and a T-bone steak. The cat gets the Protector: he sits beside her through the third episode brushing her hair with one of his own brushes, which he gave her after her third shower.

beats.headline: The Speedbump, and the pop
beats.text: Five hours building it: goblin tables on their sides, weight benches bolted on like shutters, barbell poles for braces, and Brandon's idea, fifty throwing stars thrown into the wooden front ramp. The ball hits it, wedges between our roof and the ceiling, and the roof starts to give. We stab up through the lattice until something pops. Then it rains tusklings in tuxedos and gowns, dazed, with no idea where they are. Their dots are red and the clock is running. I kick one until her health bar goes, and I might be crying.

beats.headline: I liked that show
beats.text: The Andrews brothers are the maintenance men at Meadow Lark, on overtime that night fixing an oven, and they know tools. Chris twists the fist-sized butterfly bolts that hold the redoubt together. While they practise, Crawler Donut compares the build to The A-Team, or MacGyver, and Chris says, "I liked that show." First words on the record. He does not say which show. In the fight with the swine he twirls an ethereal magic spear, a spell of his that lasts five minutes.

beats.headline: Two million, five hundred and fifty-two thousand
beats.text: The number on the screen reads 2,552,085. From thirteen million to this, in just under four days. Every one of those digits was somebody. The third episode spends its second half on five groups, among them Lucia Mar and a woman with a magical crossbow, who have found their stairwells already and are camping beside them, waiting for the clock to reach exactly six hours.

beats.headline: The Ball of Swine
beats.text: Seven of us against the Ball of Swine: Brandon, Chris, Yolanda, Carl, Donut, Agatha and me, fighting from the redoubt. It is the first time this group has fought as one thing instead of six people and a cat standing near each other, and it works. Afterwards I count everybody twice, because that is what I do, and everybody is there both times.

beats.headline: The Ball of Swine
beats.text: Brandon, Chris, Yolanda, Imani, Carl and Donut take it down out of the redoubt. Agatha is in the room for it, bleeding from the head and doing nothing, which still counts for experience.

beats.headline: It introduces you to your rivals
beats.text: The third recap brings in a hundred and fifty armed men from Africa, and then a boss battle. Whole factions arrive in the story as segments.

beats.headline: Spikes on the redoubt
beats.text: Brandon reads the description and is awed: compounding damage means poke something two hundred times and it's literally millions of points. So he, Chris and Carl spend a good five minutes throwing fifty of the stars deep into the pitted wooden cover of the redoubt's front table, black spikes to pierce the boss each time it hits. Only about twenty stay unbroken. In the fight the star-covered tabletop lies broken, and a tuskling rolls onto the stars still glowing red, squealing, so Carl stamps it deeper into the wood. Its health drops slowly, then plummets as the exponential bonus kicks in.

beats.headline: Almost five hours of building
beats.text: Brandon and his brother Chris are the facility's maintenance guys. Carl describes his idea, spreads out the looted goblin tools, and they go straight to work. It takes almost five hours to build the pieces of a portable, modular fortress: workshop tables on new legs from the weight equipment, weight benches bolted on like shutters, a roof of weight-rack cross bars, barbell poles to brace it. Brandon calls it the Speedbump. They practise until the main structure goes up in less than twenty seconds and the rest in twenty more. Fifty of Carl's shuriken go into the front table's wooden covering as spikes; only about twenty stay unbroken.

beats.headline: Wedged under the ball
beats.text: On a fifteen-foot square of floor with no grooves, they build it in the order they practised while Agatha wails about her shopping cart, which Carl has just put into his inventory. With her inside, there is no room for the final, centre pole. The ball hits. The structure slides with a horrifying screech, all four ceiling braces pop out, and one throws Yolanda over. The ball is wedged between the roof and the tunnel, the roof sagging. They stab up through the lattice until, as the top collapses, the boss bursts like a balloon and tuxedoed tusklings rain down on them.

beats.headline: Half a snout on the fist
beats.text: First blood: a fat, tuxedoed pig knight whose health is already in the red. His face caves in under the spiked gauntlet, half of his snout stays attached to Carl's fist, and he goes down still clutching his glass of wine. Miraculously, Carl feels nothing in his hand, only the impact in his arm. That was the point: no more breaking fingers on the things he punches. The gauntlet is nothing ornate, black and angular with gleaming spikes, a tool, and it vanishes in a puff of smoke that smells of burnt hair when the fist opens.

beats.headline: A brace to the head
beats.text: Agatha wheels her cart in behind them. "No, Agatha, don't!" Yolanda yells, to no effect. In the drilled routine she slides the angled braces out of her inventory one after another, circling the fort. When the Ball of Swine hits, a ceiling brace pops out and throws her over. When the walls come down, she is on the ground with her health alarmingly low, and Imani is standing over her, screaming and swinging a sword.

beats.headline: Given back, with suspicion
beats.text: The fight over, Agatha shuffles up to Carl shaking her fist, half her head caked in blood, and demands it back. He pulls the cart into existence a foot off the ground and it crashes down. She clutches an IKEA bag off the top and peers inside as if he might have stolen something, and pokes suspiciously at the flamingo. She could keep all of it in her own inventory, Carl points out. She hasn't gone through the tutorial, Yolanda says. She doesn't have an inventory yet.

beats.headline: An Attenborough whisper
beats.text: The crushed tusklings lie everywhere, and Carl reaches down to loot the persistent item from the boss's corpse; Donut already has hers. The AI reads its description in a whispery David Attenborough impression: Borough Field Guide. Carl zooms his minimap out, and the quadrants round the arena are outlined now. Hovering over one to the far southeast, where nobody has been, brings a tooltip through the fog of war: Mobs Level 2-5. Axebeak. Useful, but like the neighborhood map the area is limited, and one has to reach the center and kill the boss to get it.

beats.headline: Brandon names it the Speedbump
beats.text: The redoubt was Crawler Carl's idea, but the Andrews brothers are the maintenance men, there that night on overtime to fix an oven, and they know tools. Brandon calls the finished fort The Speedbump. He places wall sections, braces the roof beside Carl, and in the fight swings a giant maul that glitters with lightning. The last tuskling, a level-eight Dominatrix, falls under his hammer. He skips level seven altogether and comes out of it level eight, and shell-shocked.

beats.headline: The last cigarette
beats.text: The boss drops a Borough Field Guide, which adds the monster types to the quadrants around the arena on my map. I loot everything, down to a pig harness and a tent-sized tuxedo jacket. Then Donut says what I was going to do before I do it, and I light my last cigarette and it tastes like ash. What's the point of living if I can't live with myself. I drop it unfinished and grind it out. Agatha is gone, and the stairs have turned into a ramp. Brandon asks me to find her. We go down, I push the door, and I feel myself fall.

beats.headline: The production trailer
beats.text: Down the stairs, through a door like the first one, and out into a plush blue room that rocks like a boat and is not in the dungeon at all. Lexis comes in with a tablet: five and a half feet, thin the way her people are thin, blonde hair in a tight bun, plain black dress, and a light musical voice that sounds like a cartoon. Associate producer on a chat show, and also the first person from the far side of a camera either of them has met. Her host would love to interview them, on air. The cat takes to it at once. The man, who had his gauntlet out before the door opened, sits down with his head spinning.

beats.headline: He always stays
beats.text: The forcefield is down and Carl asks me whether we stick with these people or do our own thing. As if I do not know what he is going to do before he does. So I tell him the sensible version: we set them up somewhere safe, keep our own party, make a group chat, and fetch them when we find the next stairs. If it were up to me I would leave them all. But he is a softy, and if he turns into a cat on the third floor we shall need someone with thumbs.

beats.headline: Every star salvaged
beats.text: Imani drops a find on the floor in disgust, and Donut hops over and takes it into her own inventory. Everything, right? she asks, and Carl nods. He salvages all the ninja stars he can find and all the remaining pieces of the redoubt, and his inventory grows a new tab labelled Worthless Garbage. Then he spends a few minutes quietly looking round the arena for the remains of the party that went before them.

beats.headline: Culture, planted in advance
beats.text: Carl wonders why alien pigs wear tuxedos. Brandon has already asked Mistress Tiatha about the fire-breathing monkeys in lederhosen, and passes on her answer, stopping halfway through the name with a glance at the ceiling: the Syndicate not only seeded Earth with people millions of years ago but kept people here the whole time, some of them humans from other worlds, steering culture, inventing things, writing books and songs that already existed elsewhere. Why, Brandon cannot say. They only see what they are shown.

beats.headline: Randall, don't come in here
beats.text: Imani feeds her a health potion, and she sits up holding the side of her head. With blood still all over her own face, she takes out a cloth and cleans Agatha's. She explains that Agatha has no inventory because she has not done the tutorial. She is level six now. When an elderly man with a walker starts clicking into the boss chamber to see what the noise was, she jogs to head him off. "Randall, don't come in here!"

beats.headline: Goddamnit, Donut, on cue
beats.text: A plush blue room on a boat somewhere in a winter ocean, a fruit basket and a porthole that won't open. I tell Donut these people are not our friends. Then a crab-bodied host with a mantis head and a chest that rests on her desk wants my catchphrase, and I don't know I have one until she plays at least fifteen clips. I say it. They cheer. They show me in my kneepads under the words WORST DRESSED and I pretend to laugh. Donut promises them style, and I watch her face and see a hunger there.

beats.headline: Blocking out the segment
beats.text: She briefs them at speed. This is a production trailer on the surface, still technically in the game, menus off. Walk on when told, wave, go straight to the couch, the cat nearer the host, and do not approach the audience or meet a wall you cannot see. Taped, tunnelled in a few hours, uncensored, and the more entertaining the better. The cat asks about makeup, about tone, about whether to let Carl be Carl, as if she has done this all her life, and the corner of Lexis's mouth very nearly smiles. Then she comes back, puts a hand on the man's back and pushes. Smile and wave.

beats.headline: We have been watching from the beginning
beats.text: The Princess walks on, rolls over halfway to the couch, and has the room before she sits down. She is earth royalty, she tells my audience; among cats it is an elective monarchy, which is to say a beauty contest, and she has won it. Carl does not know his catchphrase, so I show him clip after clip of himself saying it until he does. Will they stay with Meadow Lark? For now. Then she stands on the pillow and promises they will kill with style, and they cheer for thirty seconds.

beats.headline: We are going to kill them with style
beats.text: Every cat show I have ever done is an interview. I was bred for this. So I ask Lexis about the tone, I tell Carl to let me talk and not to be surly, and I walk onto the set and roll over for them. I explain the monarchy, and I wink. When Odette asks what is next, I stand up on my pillow and tell them all to follow us, because whatever we face, we will not just kill it. We will kill it with style. After thirty seconds they are still screaming.

beats.headline: Never say mud skipper
beats.text: Odette's advice, in a room Borant cannot hear: never say mud skipper in the dungeon. The kua-tin tried to have the word listed as hate speech with the Syndicate, and hardly anyone used it until they did. Nobody likes the kua-tin government. Borant is a different story; some of them only want to put on a good show, and they were incensed to be forced into this early release. And all indentureship contracts freeze during a bankruptcy seizure action, which, she says, is nothing the crawlers need to worry about.

beats.headline: What it costs when it stops working
beats.text: A guide explains his own body by naming the race he picked in his own crawl. He does not choose his shape: every time his guildhall is moved the dungeon changes it for him, and he wears what he is given, always a mob from the current floor. The race is a gift with a clause, and he is the clause.

beats.headline: He has done this before, and it cost him everything
beats.text: I crawled. I took Changeling, and I can't shift on my own any more, so the dungeon hands me a body at the start of every floor and I wear what I'm given. This one is a rat-kin. What I actually am is golden, and has wings. I don't talk about the family. When I've had enough to drink, I talk about the family.

beats.headline: Tell Mordecai to find me
beats.text: Off air, the mask comes off, then the chest, and I climb out of today's crab onto my disk. I was Mordecai's trainer, a long time ago, and this is his last crawl; I want him to seek me out when it is over. Advice, since they have earned some. The Princess stays a cat, whatever races they dangle. Stop complaining about pants while it is funny. Loot is not random when a death would be bad for business. And the season only counts against Mordecai's indenture if one of his crawlers reaches the fourth floor.

beats.headline: Nothing I love more than money
beats.text: Carl notices the Princess is wearing off. I do not deny it: a point and a half of wisdom and confidence in her cat treats, no worse than a glass of strong wine, and it makes a better interview. Everything is a stat, I tell him, even the ones he cannot see. Then he asks my motive, since I told them never to trust anyone whose motives are unclear. The audience loves them. The longer they live, the more money I make, and there is nothing in this universe I love more than money.

beats.headline: Loot is only semi-random
beats.text: About the boxes. Sometimes what's inside is random. Sometimes I choose it, by hand, because a crawler needs helping or hurting and the numbers want a show. You will never know which, and that is the point. I also hand out insults on purpose. Carl has a Bronze Asshole's Box and a Gold Asshole's Box, both earned on this floor for killing non-combatants. I named them. I'm proud of them. He is not.

beats.headline: Bully and a Thief
beats.text: Among the achievements after the borough boss fight, one confuses Carl for a moment. Bully and a Thief: he has stolen property from a fellow crawler who is a lower level than him. What's next, tough guy, the System asks, kicking puppies? The reward is a Bronze Asshole's Box. Then he realises he got it for taking Agatha's shopping cart.

beats.headline: Janitor duty
beats.text: On the second floor the rats are yesterday’s news and the grubs are the janitors. The more monsters killed in an area, the more the grubs eat; the more they eat, the bigger they get. Grubs are easy to kill. Once they turn up in the pupa stage, move on, because their older siblings are not.

beats.headline: Pugilism ten, and still behind
beats.text: On the second floor I smear Agatha's dead grub across the floor until its X leaves the map. From now on we leave as little behind as possible. The boss box has a Cheat Code Potion that expires in seventeen minutes; I drink it and my Pugilism jumps three levels to ten. My fists hit as hard as Brandon's lightning maul now. But I remember Lucia Mar running up walls on the recap, and the crossbow woman throwing a tentacle monster into the air, and I wonder whether I am falling behind.

beats.headline: Seventeen minutes to drink it
beats.text: The silver boss box holds a hundred gold coins and a potion with a red timer flashing at the bottom of its description, already down to seventeen minutes. Cheat Code Potion: don't be a wuss, drink it now. Carl adds it to his hotlist and drinks, and it crackles in his mouth like a whole packet of Pop Rocks. His Pugilism goes up by three, to level ten. With Iron Punch, Powerful Strike and his unarmed bonus, his fists now pack as much damage as Brandon's lightning maul.

beats.headline: A lollipop with a button
beats.text: Going through his loot after the borough boss, Carl finds a really interesting item in a silver mechanics box: a tool that looks like a silver, oversized lollipop with a button on the handle. It shapes materials into something else, only at a workbench, and the System suggests keeping the business end away from his face. He can't buy a personal space until the fourth floor, so it goes back into his inventory to wait.

beats.headline: Bully and a Thief
beats.text: The first-floor accounts settle in a French storm shelter. Borough Boss: top five per cent of crawlers, reward "Yeah, no." Bully and a Thief, for taking the old woman's shopping cart: a Bronze Asshole's Box with five gold and three Desperado Club drink tickets, "drink" in quotation marks. Battlefield Construction: a Silver Mechanic's Box and a Goo-Inator 3000 that needs a workbench. You found stairs: the reward is being alive to read it. And for more than five kills in boss fights with bare feet, in the AI's sexy voice, a Platinum Shoe Box.

beats.headline: One last item
beats.text: Carl has one last item to examine from the haul, and he swears under his breath before he has even pulled it into his hand: a little black folder with a zipper, full of miniature tools. Enchanted Pedicure Kit of the Sylph, twelve essential items for proper foot care, working only in a safe room or personal space and only while he stays barefoot. He sighs. The very last buff, an alarm and a five-second delay before any trap set off by a footfall, is a great prize.

beats.headline: Dungeon Book of the Floor Club
beats.text: Thanks to my boss box I am a member of the Dungeon Book of the Floor Club, which mails me one spell book per level, and the mailbox opens for me and not for Carl. I read it at once. Second Chance: raise a dead monster lower than me to fight for us for a minute a level. It is disgusting; the dead are bad enough without moaning. Then Carl says I could raise a dingo, have it kill another dingo, and raise that one too. A zombie dog army. This is the best spell ever.

beats.headline: A storm shelter with a mailbox
beats.text: Not every one is a restaurant. The first safe room on the second floor is a cavernous storm shelter with French signs on the restrooms, about fifty dusty cots and no Bopca: no food, no cookies, no vending machine, only bathrooms, showers and sinks, and screens on the far wall. By the screens is a black suburban mailbox on a pole, red flag and all. Carl tries the door and gets an error: Why would someone send you mail? It opens for the cat.

beats.headline: The Book of the Floor Club
beats.text: Donut leaps onto the safe room's mailbox and its front opens on its own. A tome floats out. A boss box has made her a member of the Dungeon Book of the Floor Club: one spellbook per level, mailed to her. She reads it at once, and says ew. Carl reminds her, again, to read the description first. It's Second Chance, ten mana: she can raise a lower-level monster from the dead to fight for them for as many minutes as the spell's level. It's disgusting, she says, until Carl suggests raising a dead dingo to kill another dingo, like the Lucia Mar kid with her two dogs. This is the best spell ever.

beats.headline: She is in the room, and then she is not
beats.text: For the record: Agatha was in the room for the Ball of Swine beside Brandon, Chris, Yolanda, Imani, Carl and the cat, and made level four for being there, which is not the same as doing anything. Then she went missing. The next I have of her is her name on a dead grub. She is not on the recap. The party assumes the worst. I nearly always have a forwarding address.

beats.headline: Three patron spots, at auction
beats.text: Patronage changes this season. Every crawler is limited to three patrons, the spots auctioned for one day each at the start of the fourth, fifth and sixth floors, opening at one credit, so virtually every living crawler will have one. What a patron bids above the standard fee comes back as discounts on the boxes they send; bid below it and their boxes cost more. The more a patron pays, the more and better the Benefactor Boxes, and the higher a crawler's social numbers, the better the loot. Patrons may transfer from the seventh floor.

beats.headline: Twenty-four stayed to sing
beats.text: Only six more residents come down from the Waffle House safe room. Twenty-four voted to stay, and they were all singing when he last saw them. Brandon asks Crawler Carl for help sending the rest down to the third floor early. His boss box gives him a magic boomerang, and a silver star now sits by his name, as by everyone's. When the dungeon announces the rage elemental rule, his first thought is practical: Yolanda had better tell Jack not to pee in the hallways any more.

beats.headline: Agatha, edited out
beats.text: After the tuskling fight he dropped to his knees and hung his head. Now he sits in a corner of the safe room, head low, possibly crying. His brother reports that his boss box gave him "some book of the club thing." Then the recap airs the redoubt without Agatha's picture, and Chris speaks for the second time on the record: she was next to him under the speedbump, and she was not there when they showed it. She was edited out.

beats.headline: A third of the crawlers, in one rumble
beats.text: The first-floor timer runs out as the episode starts. The ground shakes for a second and the count drops from just over two million to 1,292,526: more than seven hundred thousand dead at once, a third of those left. The first floor took a little more than ten million. The second floor's clock resets to six days, because the count is below projections and six is the minimum the rules allow. Borant urges everyone to wait until the last possible moment to descend.

beats.headline: Carl gets her inside
beats.text: The next episode is starting and the collapse is on top of us, and I am not, at my age, built for sprinting, or for walking. Carl, the young man with the cat, gets behind my wheelchair and pushes me into the storm shelter, and I let him, because I am old and not stupid. Then I ask him to put Divorce Court on the television. My Barry used to watch it.

beats.headline: Named on the recap
beats.text: The armed men from Africa get a name on the broadcast, and a graphic counting what is left of their ammunition.

beats.headline: Twenty-four stayed to sing
beats.text: Only six more residents come down from the Waffle House; twenty-four vote to stay and were singing when Brandon last saw them. The rest fill the French storm shelter. The plan is to send every resident down to the third floor early, since they cannot train, and the four staff are going with them rather than risk being split up. Brandon's boss box gives him a magic boomerang; Imani does not say what she gets. Then Chris, speaking for the second time, notices Agatha was edited out of their recap.

beats.headline: Ten days, she said
beats.text: Subject told her crawlers the second floor would last ten days. The countdown resets to six. Her crawlers note the difference.

beats.headline: My first follower
beats.text: We are on the show, finally, for less than fifteen seconds: me shouting that it is coming, me firing point-blank into pigs, Imani dropping something unmentionable. Two shows in one day! Carl says I am obsessing and it will get us killed, which is unfair. Then the announcement ends and the numbers turn on. A follower. My first follower. A view! Carl points out that the viewer is watching me right now, and I sit down, lick my paw and remark that it was quite the battle today.

beats.headline: The bathroom rule
beats.text: An announcement goes out between episodes. Any human-born crawler who relieves themselves outside a designated bathroom area gets one summoned on the spot, and it will take the offender and every crawler in their party with them. It is not an encounter. It is a penalty, dragged up from a floor nobody on this one is meant to see.

beats.headline: Edited out from under it
beats.text: The recap episode shows them huddled underneath the redoubt as Donut screams that it's coming. Brandon's older brother, Chris, speaks up, only the second time Carl has heard him, and says there is more to it. Agatha was edited out of the scene. She was next to him under the speedbump, but she wasn't there when they showed it. Oh yeah, says Brandon. Weird.

beats.headline: Adult pads for Jack
beats.text: She walks residents to the bathrooms. Her boss box gives her a new kind of quiver. When the recap leaves out Agatha's picture she asks whether that means she is dead. Then the dungeon announces the rage elemental rule for anyone who relieves themselves outside a bathroom, and Brandon tells her to warn Jack. Yolanda goes pale. "I have a few adult pads left. I'll make sure he puts one on."

beats.headline: Carl's Jug O' Boom
beats.text: The clurichauns carry clay jugs of toilet-grade moonshine, a hundred and eighty proof and highly flammable. I pour a splash out, add goblin oil, and one of Donut's short torches corks the mouth perfectly. The dungeon names it after me: created by an unstable, pantsless man who talks to a cat. Incendiary Device Handling jumps to five. The first one we throw burns blue to the ceiling for a minute and fifteen seconds and leaves ash. We make ten more, and burn every other room.

beats.headline: Members of the club
beats.text: The description of the moonshine jugs says they are valuable, and Donut points at the dagger tattoo on Carl's neck. The Desperado Club, she says: maybe it will be on the next floor. She bets they will buy all the jugs because they are members of the club. They will be rich. Maybe, says Carl, if they have any jugs left when they are done.

beats.headline: Twelve items for foot care
beats.text: Donut laughs at him. So I sit down with Carl and his pedicure kit and take out the tools one at a time and tell him what each of them is for. He does not need all twelve; he has to make a show of it. About fifteen minutes of work and the buffs come on. His toes glitter, and the bones in them cannot break now.

beats.headline: They named it after him
beats.text: Twenty-five clay jugs of Rev-Up Toilet-Grade Moonshine, looted off clurichauns. Pour a splash out, add a couple of ounces of goblin oil, and jam a short torch into the mouth, where it fits like a cork. The test throw: an insignificant explosion, then blue flames splashing like water across the room, high enough to reach the ceiling. The dungeon names the result Carl's Jug O' Boom. "Carl, look, they named it after you!" He sees.

beats.headline: Imani shows him how
beats.text: Little sharp rocks are everywhere. Carl kicks one away, and below him his shiny toes glitter. He had tried to get Donut to show him how to use the kit, and she laughed at him. It was Imani, of all people, who sat down with him, pulling the tools out one at a time and matter-of-factly explaining how they worked. The buffs activate after about fifteen minutes of work. He doesn't need to use every tool. He just has to make a show of it.

beats.headline: Second Chance, for practice
beats.text: I have fourteen mana and Carl asks, so I raise a dead clurichaun. It sways and moans. I tell it to rip up its friends, and it does, groaning the whole time. Most unpleasant. After that, every time we clear a room I raise one and Carl practises hitting it with a slingshot, which does hardly any damage. My Second Chance reaches level three, so they last three minutes. I find a pamphlet about becoming a Rev-Up consultant, which says it is not a pyramid. Carl says it is easier to kill them and take it all, and it is: no upline, no seed investment.

beats.headline: Twenty-five clay jugs
beats.text: Donut loots the dead clurichaun consultants: each of them has a clay jug of something called toilet-grade moonshine. Over the next hour she finds a pamphlet, Rev-Up, promising the benefits of becoming a Rev-Up Moonshine Consultant, see Krakaren or one of her downline consultants. By the time they stop to think they have twenty-five jugs. The description says they are valuable and sought after on deeper floors. Donut is sure the Desperado Club will buy them all and make them rich. Carl grins and asks whether she has any extra torches.

beats.headline: Undead minion, level one
beats.text: Donut has headshot three clurichauns and has fourteen mana left, so Carl asks if she wants to try her new Second Chance spell. Her whole body glows neon purple. One of the dead clurichauns twitches, glows to match and stumbles to its feet, its scorched head listing, a one-minute timer over it: Undead Minion of Crawler Princess Donut.
