Donut finds it most unpleasant and has no sort of controls, but told to rip up the bodies of its friends, it does, and within seconds it is dead again, the job unfinished. For the next hour she raises one after every skirmish so Carl can practise his slingshot on it, and the spell reaches level three: the minions now last three minutes.

beats.headline: Two seconds is a long time
beats.text: A clurichaun comes at Carl impossibly fast and grapples instead of using its slingshot. He forms a fist, but the gauntlet takes two seconds to arrive, which is a long time when something is clawing at you. The first, bare-knuckle hit stuns it. The second, with the gauntlet, sends it flying with its head caved in. When he opens his hand his fingers are covered in lime-green oily residue, and a warning: he has been infected with the Taint.

beats.headline: We were going to move down
beats.text: The second fairy screams it from the ceiling, just before she hits me in the chest with a magic missile: not fair, they were going to move down to the third floor. Forty dead at once and I hit level eleven, and I feel like hell about it. Mordecai said the deeper mobs would be less sympathetic. The real enemies are the Syndicate, Borant, the kua-tin. You're not going to break me, I whisper; it has become a mantra. I decide to leave the boss alone. Then the door with Live, Laugh, Love on it blows open, and the boss comes out.

beats.headline: Two for the laminak
beats.text: The moonshine is made nearby, where dozens of clurichauns fill jugs from a filthy aluminium bathtub under two fairy managers. Crawler Donut lures the fairies out; Crawler Carl lights two jugs and tosses them in among the forty workers. Afterwards he collects everything that survived: eighty empty jugs and sixty full ones. He leaves the moonshine in the tub alone, in case touching it blinds him.

beats.headline: Plan Pied Piper
beats.text: I Puddle Jumper into their filling room, right between the two fairy managers, and they are charmed at once, though the forty workers stay red. So, plan Pied Piper. I tell the fairies a terrible story about dingoes and walk them all into the next room to see, the workers too, and leave the workers there. Carl throws his jugs. I catch one of the fairies out of the air like a bird. The other one takes longer, because Carl insists on his slingshot. My first solo mission. I would be fine crawling this dungeon by myself.

beats.headline: A wet pop between fairies
beats.text: The two biggest problems with Puddle Jumper are the cooldown and the mana. Once Donut is in that room she cannot teleport out for five hours, and the spell costs 20 of her 26 points. Carl stays behind; with his extra fairy aggro, nobody knows what would happen if they both showed themselves. Donut casts it, fades through the ten-second countdown and vanishes with a loud, wet pop, reappearing at the far end of the room right between the two laminak fairies as the clurichauns jump to their feet.

beats.headline: Two boxes in a corner
beats.text: In the corner of the clurichauns' room, Carl pulls a dangling banner, Rev-Up Smoothies! Invigorating!, off the wall and looks over two child-sized stationary bikes. A pulley runs from each tire to a little platform: a bicycle-powered blender, apparently never used. One wooden box holds twelve glass containers with screw-on lids and a lid with blades; the second holds six glasses, no blade, and a sheet of paper, the Rev-Up Immunity Smoothie Recipe. It needs two items. No wonder they discontinued this. Gross. It's all game setup, he tells Donut, and takes everything, one of the bikes included.

beats.headline: Plan Pied Piper
beats.text: The soccer-mom fairies who run the moonshine room are winged, so Donut can turn their dots white. She teleports in between the two of them, and they fall under her charm at once. Get back to work, one shouts at the clurichauns: this is a client, not an enemy. The other forty or so are not airborne fairies and stay red, so it is plan B, which Donut insists is called Plan Pied Piper. She walks the two fairies toward Carl, telling them about a horrible slaughter, and invites everyone to come and see.

beats.headline: One part moonshine, one part fairy
beats.text: The recipe from the dusty box: a third of the glass moonshine, one laminak fairy corpse, blend until pink. I cram her in headfirst and pedal a child's exercise bike while tentacles full of screaming mouths break through the walls. Ten doses of immunity, and it makes you drunk. Donut raises a clurichaun and I send it running at the boss's door with a lit jug over its head and dynamite down its overalls. My health is in the red. I put a table over us and wrap myself around the cat.

beats.headline: Named in a drunken confession
beats.text: Crawler Princess Donut, under the Buzzed debuff from a blended corpse, informs Crawler Carl that she loves him. Almost as much as Bea. Almost as much as Ferdinand. Ferdinand is the other cat. That is the whole entry: a cat, ranked above the man who carried her down the stairs, by a cat. I keep records on everything in this dungeon. This one I opened for the ranking.

beats.headline: Twenty percent harder
beats.text: The clurichauns are fairy-class mobs, and their description says so: twenty percent more damage against him, due to his goblin pass. Running, buzzed and laughing at nothing, Carl takes a slingshot rock off the head. His health bar drops further than it should, the damage enhanced by his stupid goblin tattoo.

beats.headline: Carried in by a zombie
beats.text: The delivery method for the Krakaren's chamber is a zombified clurichaun. On Crawler Donut's order it holds a jug over its head, like the boombox in Say Anything, a stick of dynamite shoved down its overalls for good measure; the torch is lit, and it runs through the doorway. Crawler Carl dives behind a shield, puts the alchemy table over himself and the cat like a clamshell, and wraps himself around her before the explosion comes.

beats.headline: The thing behind the moonshine
beats.text: Twenty feet of immobile octopus in a chamber with Live, Laugh, Love spelled out over the door in cut wooden letters, sitting behind a still that produces toilet-grade moonshine at industrial volume. Her tentacles are lined with human mouths that scream without pause and drip something that stops a body healing. The cat and the barefoot man take her apart and drink a blended corpse to do it. She is not the point. She is a copy, and somewhere there is an original, and the original is a committee.

beats.headline: I lied before
beats.text: The smoothie has made me drunk. I tell Carl that if we die, I want him to know I love him. Not as much as Miss Beatrice, who is my person, but I love him. Then he sends a zombie with a bomb into the boss's room and pulls a table over us and tells me I will be okay, that I should go back to Brandon. No. I lied before. I will not be fine on my own. I need him.

beats.headline: Blend until pink
beats.text: Tentacles are breaking through the walls when Carl shouts that he needs to make a goddamned smoothie. A third of a glass of moonshine; the dead laminak shoved in headfirst, her shoulders cracking; the bladed top screwed on. He sits on the much-too-small bike with his knees at his chest, recites the recipe aloud, and pedals. The fairy spins away, green, then red, then pink, and it starts to sparkle. Running, with the Taint already on him, he takes a sip that tastes like a diseased skunk, and shoves it at Donut to drink too.

beats.headline: Infection negated
beats.text: The smoothie does not lift the Taint Carl already carries, so he still cannot heal, but a pair of icons flashes for his immunity, and both of them are Buzzed: he laughs at his own death measles joke, and Donut slurs as she fires her missiles. Then a new tentacle, covered in hundreds of tiny orifices, sprays a fine green mist through the chamber. You've been infected with the Vigorous Measles! Infection negated due to immunity!

beats.headline: A third of a glass
beats.text: With the boss's tentacles breaking through the walls, Carl pulls a glass smoothie container into his right hand and a jug of unaltered moonshine into his left, pulls the cork with his teeth and fills the glass a third of the way, to a little line on the side. A tentacle bursts in overhead and moonshine sloshes out; he pours a little more, then throws the jug toward the entrance, where it shatters. The rest of the recipe is a dead fairy.

beats.headline: A shield in the corner
beats.text: Krakaren's tentacles are smashing through the walls and Carl is buzzed on his own smoothie. Running for the back corner of the room with Donut, he pulls an angled, still-intact section of the redoubt from his inventory and puts it up as a shield; the clurichauns' slingshot rocks ping off the steel table, and a screaming tentacle slams it and rockets them both against the back wall. When he has sent a zombie off toward the door with a lit jug, he dives behind it again and pulls the alchemy table over the top to make a clamshell.

beats.headline: Really? Fucking really?
beats.text: Carl opens the boss box, tells himself not to say anything out loud, and says it to the ceiling anyway. Behind him Mordecai laughs, then adds that it is actually a really good prize: a white pair of boxers covered in little red hearts, the Enchanted BigBoi Boxers, plus two Constitution and a level-fifteen Protective Shell once every thirty hours. Don't look, Carl says. He pulls his scorched and threadbare boxers off and slips the new ones on, and the old ones fall apart in his hands.

beats.headline: Boxers with little red hearts
beats.text: The alchemy table I hid behind comes out of that fire cool to the touch. I think those tables cannot be destroyed. That is a bug, and bugs get patched, so it stays in my head. Then the boss box gives me a pair of white boxers covered in little red hearts, and Mordecai laughs, and then says that is actually a really good prize. Enchanted BigBoi Boxers: plus two Constitution, and a level-15 Protective Shell once every thirty hours. My old pair falls apart in my hands.

beats.headline: Off limits
beats.text: Carl asks Mordecai about the tattoo on his neck, the Desperado Club. Nope, says Mordecai. Off limits. They will learn about the third floors soon enough. Sorry. Then he tells Carl he had better open his boxes before Zev gets here, because the cameras always turn off when kua-tin are around.

beats.headline: Ten minutes every night
beats.text: Donut combs through her achievements and boxes and finds nothing noteworthy except one item. Her boss box holds an Enchanted Fur Brush of the Ecclesiastic, which works much like Carl's pedicure kit: as long as someone brushes her for ten minutes every night, she gets an extra two points of Constitution for thirty hours. It is better than nothing, Carl reckons, but even with the buff her Constitution is only four.

beats.headline: Dungeonpreneur, and a Codex entry
beats.text: New achievement: Dungeonpreneur, for inventing a stackable weapon, device or potion. The recipe goes into the Dungeon Codex under Carl's name. The reward: one gold coin for every kill made with it by other crawlers, payable for the rest of his natural life if he survives, even in future seasons. The lawyers insisted on that last part. The citation adds that he is going to die, and the dungeon is going to keep using his work.

beats.headline: A Bugaboo, and a hard no
beats.text: New floor, new body. A Bugaboo this time: seven feet, no neck, and the chairs are too small now. The kid tells me Odette wants me to seek her out. I'd rather spend another two thousand years in this room. Her show, though, you should go on; it's one of the few I'd recommend. And listen. Viewers can see you in here. They can't see me or hear me. Only those with press credentials can. Like Odette.

beats.headline: Saved by a pedicure
beats.text: Carl wakes in the hallway, healed by one of Donut's healing scrolls, his one-armed jacket scorched to hell. His toes sparkle. He thinks he was saved by that damn pedicure kit. The table should have severed his feet right at the ankles. Instead it bounced off and broke his legs, and without that, he would have bled out.

beats.headline: She drags him out by the cloak
beats.text: The boss is dead, the room is on fire, and Carl is lying in the rubble telling me he cannot hear me. So I write it in capitals. He cannot stand either, apparently, so I take him by the cloak and drag him out, and he is much heavier than he looks. He croaks something about a scroll, and I use one of the healing scrolls. He says I saved him again. That is what I do. I do not say the next part out loud: our views went way up.

beats.headline: Inside a pair of boxers
beats.text: A boss box yields a white pair of boxers covered in little red hearts, the Enchanted BigBoi Boxers: plus two Constitution, and the wearer may cast a level-fifteen Protective Shell once every thirty hours. No mana; take the boxers off and the spell goes with them. A sphere with a radius of three metres plus half a metre per point of Intelligence, lasting twenty seconds. Mordecai had it during his own crawl and starts to explain its fantastic secondary effect, when an admin warning cuts him off.

beats.headline: Not on your schedule
beats.text: The admin is a two-foot fish in a diving suit, and she tells me to line up a major boss fight for the end of the floor, because that played well last time. Something in me lets go. I tell her we are fighting for our lives, that we will smile and joke on their shows because we have to, and that we are not going to fight or survive on her schedule. Mordecai looks terrified. Zev tells me they are all afraid. Then Donut says this is just like season three of Gossip Girl, and I laugh, and I cannot stop.

beats.headline: There are other shows
beats.text: Zev introduces herself as the liaison between Borant and the privately run programmes that borrow crawlers for their own shows. A production may pluck a crawler off between stairwells; anything else goes through her office. A crawler may turn a show down, but has to pick one.

beats.headline: The Party, in a whisper
beats.text: While the fish and the cat talk Gossip Girl, I get the kid alone. Listen. The Party is the Bloom: ultra-nationalists, under fifteen percent of the vote when I signed my indenture, and now they run the whole kua-tin government. They've run it into the ground. Borant is being forced by its own government to end this game fast; it gets no money until the season's over. The committee has already warned them about the bugs. So the government is working extra hard to get you killed. Don't upset them.

beats.headline: She explains how the shows work
beats.text: Okay. So. Carl has just met his first Borant dungeon admin and managed to be civil, which I am counting as a win for everyone, including me. My job today is to walk them through how crawlers take part in the Syndicate programmes, and I get through all of it. Then Princess Donut mentions Gossip Girl, and Mordecai has seen it, and I have seen it, and for a few minutes nobody in the room is anyone's liaison.

beats.headline: Nobody in this room is an idiot
beats.text: Okay, so, Carl shouts at me, and I let him finish. Then I tell him how it actually is. Mordecai relaxed the moment he saw I wasn't wearing a party badge. My boss is a member. If I say the wrong thing, my entire family is wiped from the universe. The mobs out there live in fear of crawlers. We are all parts of the same machine, and all of us are afraid. I am on your side, Carl. The better you do, the longer you survive, the better I do.

beats.headline: Wait until you see what we built
beats.text: The people train: ten cars of residents, two by two on their own chairs, linked on one glowing chain. The chain was Imani's idea; Brandon designed the rest and added ramps so they can get on and off. He, Yolanda and his brother went out and cleared the Mind Horrors, a boss that turned out to be a giant blimp, which earned him another bronze star. To Crawler Carl, at the rendezvous: "You are helping us to your own detriment. You are a good man."

beats.headline: Five thousand to a quadrant
beats.text: A guildmaster checks his menu and confirms it: they are being spawned. The system is making anywhere from one to fifteen grubs whenever a corpse is created, with no janitor mobs nearby, and with no corpses about they hunt crawlers instead. The seven hundred and fifty fried in a boss's cage count. Dead grubs make more grubs. There is a cap of five thousand per quadrant, and Carl and Donut have already hit it. The level twos neither bite nor give experience. They squeak, they wriggle, and they eat their own dead.

beats.headline: The tunnel of love
beats.text: I'm on the last car of a train that rolls on wheelchair wheels, and the young man with the cat is walking beside me. I remember his name today. Carl. This reminds me of the tunnel of love. My Barry and I used to go to the carnival, and back then it was a boat, and I'd let him touch them, but only on the outside of my sweater. Barry wasn't pretty. If Carl were in that tunnel with me, I'd let him do more. He says thank you. I cackle.

beats.headline: Yog's Special Chain
beats.text: Someone had to stay with the residents while Brandon, Chris and Yolanda cleared out the Mind Horrors, so I stayed. Then we built a train. The wheels come off wheelchairs whose owners are gone; Brandon designed the cars and added ramps. The chain is mine, a scroll out of a Gold box: any length up to about a thousand feet, light as a feather, gone in thirty hours. Chris and I wear pig harnesses and pull thirty-nine people, ten cars, one glowing chain running from him, through every car and back to me.

beats.headline: A parade float
beats.text: A wall of blue dots comes down the hallway, and Carl laughs: they have built a parade float. Imani and Chris strain at the front in leather pig harnesses from the tuskling courtesans. Wheels from wheelchairs that no longer have owners are fixed to long wooden platforms, cobbled together with goblin tools, the wood from the blimp boss's warehouse. It is more like a train, ten cars of four, most riders in their own chairs locked two by two, the walker users cross-legged on the boards. More maneuverable than it looks, Brandon says, but too wide for a safe room door. He added ramps.

beats.headline: Where'd you get that chain
beats.text: The residents' wheelchair train runs on one glowing chain, about three hundred feet long, from Chris through every car and back to Imani. Carl asks where the chain came from. Imani had a scroll called Yog's Special Chain, or something like that, out of some Gold box. She could pick any length up to something crazy, like a thousand feet. It's light as a feather, but the chain only lasts thirty hours.

beats.headline: Deflating the Mind Horrors
beats.text: She went out with the Andrews brothers to clear the Mind Horrors, shooting the floating brains from down the hallway and deflating them before they could reach anyone. The boss, a blimp, went down easily, by Brandon's account thanks to Yolanda. She is level nine now, equal with both brothers. On the march she barks with laughter when Mrs. McGibbons propositions Crawler Carl, tells Jack not to be crude, and walks at the rear with her bow ready.

beats.headline: A voice in his head
beats.text: Okay, so, I have been watching. Carl tells Brandon that the day we stop helping each other is the day we stop being human, and it is great, and I ask him to say it again without the cough. He will not. The save-the-elderly storyline is playing well with most viewers; about twenty percent of the focus group calls them dead weight. Princess Donut is right that it is a little dry. Then an old man stands up on the train with his pants around his ankles, and I tell them to run.

beats.headline: Protective Shell, first cast
beats.text: Jack pees on the wall and the wall makes a monster: level 93, smoke and claws. Yolanda stands her ground, and it unravels her and Randall both. I hit Protective Shell as a claw comes in, and the thing bounces off like a dog at the end of its leash. Then gravity flips and I am running on the ceiling. Mrs. McGibbons is up there under her own wheelchair. I carry her like a sack, fall when I cross the edge of the spell, and dive through the safe room door with a claw missing me by millimetres. Then I go back out to throw a boom jug.

beats.headline: Stuck to the ceiling
beats.text: One minute I'm on the last car, the next I'm on the roof of the hallway with my own wheelchair on top of me and my health deep in the red, and I start to cry. Carl picks me up like a sack and runs upside down, and then we fall. He gets me inside. Brandon helps me drink the potion. You saved me, I tell Carl. Thank you. Jack was always an ass. Poor Yolanda was such a good kid. Randall was dumb as a pigeon, but he deserved better. At least it was quick.

beats.headline: Jack, Yolanda, Randall
beats.text: One resident, who had had the rule explained to him, stands up on the train and relieves himself on the dungeon wall. Yolanda Martinez puts an arrow in his temple, too late to matter, and the rage elemental that rises out of the stain cuts through her and through Randall, thrown off the last car. A hundred feet away, Chris and Imani pull the others off their seats and throw them through a safe room door. Three are dead, and the train stays outside.

beats.headline: A dog at the end of its leash
beats.text: First cast, in a hallway, with a rage elemental coming for the residents. The glowing half-sphere fills the corridor floor to ceiling, and the monster flies back like a charging dog reaching the end of its leash. It charges again; its badger head gets through, but its claws cannot. Crawler Carl's ears pop as he runs out of the area toward the safe room. Twenty seconds, and he spent five of them being dumbfounded that it worked.

beats.headline: Nothing to fight
beats.text: One arrives in a dungeon hallway beside the residents' train, a hundred feet short of a safe room, called up out of Jack's stain on the wall. Arrows shatter against the smoke without raising a health bar at all, and a magic missile raises a flicker of one that it heals straight off. Gravity reverses. Yolanda goes down covering Randall, and Imani, Chris and Brandon get the rest of the residents behind a safe room door while Carl pulls Elle in.

beats.headline: Too wide for the door
beats.text: Jack has stood up on the last car to piss on the wall. Yolanda's arrow kills him and he falls off the trailer, and as the train lurches forward Randall flies off the last car with his walker. A monster forms out of the sizzling stain: a Rage Elemental. The train rockets past Carl toward the safe room a hundred feet away, but its cars are too wide for the entrance, so Imani and Chris pull people off their chairs and toss them through the door. Gravity reverses. The last car flies up and dangles from the ceiling, still chained to the rest, and Mrs. McGibbons slams into the roof of the hallway.

beats.headline: Fog in the hallway
beats.text: In a hallway, a monster is finishing forming, the last of a black and purple mist twirling round it, and Yolanda is standing over a fallen man. Fog, Carl yells. Donut has read his mind and activates her scroll of Confusing Fog at the same moment. The wall of fog billows into the hallway as the creature drops to all six legs. It spins toward them, impossibly fast, cleaving through the cloud like a boat cutting through waves.

beats.headline: The last car dangles
beats.text: Gravity reverses. The rage elemental's spell does not reach all the way to the safe room door, so the last platform, still connected to the rest of the cars by Imani's magic chain, dangles upward, having thrown off its only remaining rider. Carl pulls himself to his feet and keeps running, upside down along the ceiling of the hallway, toward the crumpled form of Mrs. McGibbons.

beats.headline: A nurse her entire life
beats.text: Jack stood up on the train and relieved himself on the wall. Yolanda put an arrow through his temple, a fraction too late. Her arrows shattered against the rage elemental that rose from the stain, and she stood over Randall, thrown from the last car, while it finished forming. It cut through them both. Yolanda Martinez, nurse all her life, who worked sixty-hour weeks to put her son through college, unravelled in a red cloud. The creature did not break stride.

beats.headline: Named on the recap
beats.text: A woman with a crossbow and an ever-growing crowd of female warriors, killing their way through the dungeon. They have named themselves Brynhild's Daughters. The leader is Hekla, and the announcer gives a short history of her home country, Iceland. The AI is throwing loot at her to fit the shieldmaiden persona, including a glittering breastplate better suited to the cover of a harem fantasy novel than to a dungeon. Donut thinks they should join up. Carl suspects he would not be welcome.

beats.headline: He really did
beats.text: The people train runs on one glowing chain, three hundred feet of it, from Chris through ten cars of residents and back to Imani, and once it gets going he barely feels the weight. When the rage elemental forms, he and Imani pull residents out of their chairs and throw them through the safe room door. The recap replays Jack, and then Yolanda. Afterwards, nobody speaks until Chris does: "He really did have a weird-looking dick." Imani wraps her arms around him, laughing and crying at once.

beats.headline: Luck goes both ways
beats.text: For hitting a mob more than seventy-five levels above them, Carl and Donut each get a Platinum Lucky Bastard Box, and each holds a lottery scratch-off ticket. Donut's is red and green, with a troll-like creature throwing gold coins in the air and six spots to scratch, and the safe room will not let her use it. On the back are about twenty symbols, most of them good, like five thousand coins or double damage, a few not, like a mob that splits in two or turns invulnerable for thirty seconds. Don't use it, Carl says, not until they have talked. Fine, says Donut.

beats.headline: Luck goes both ways
beats.text: Damaging the rage elemental, a mob more than seventy-five levels above them, earns Carl and Donut each a Platinum Lucky Bastard Box: luck goes both ways, like your mom. Both hold a scratch-off ticket like any sold at a gas station. Donut's is Dungeon Gold Rush. Carl's has five spots and is red on one side and pink on the other, with a little cartoon dragon in the corner holding a spoon and licking its lips. Donut loves custard, and has the room's Bopca bring her some.

beats.headline: She demands more brushing
beats.text: On the screen the shots keep coming, crawlers being slaughtered, and Carl can barely taste his fried chicken. At the table, Donut sits being lovingly groomed with her new brush by the safe room's Bopca Protector. The constitution buff activated many minutes ago. She demands he keep brushing. People are asleep in all twenty of the safe room's rooms for rent.

beats.headline: Almost a quarter of an elemental
beats.text: From the safe room doorway, Crawler Carl tosses a lit jug at the back of the rage elemental and slams the door. The recap shows the rest: the show pauses on the recipe, stamps Added to the Dungeon Codex over his mugshot, and then the monster's health plummets almost twenty-five percent. It is stunned for a good ten seconds, and the napalm-like fire slows its healing.

beats.headline: Dungeon Gold Rush
beats.text: We get a Platinum Lucky Bastard Box for hurting something more than seventy-five levels above us, and inside is a scratch-off ticket. Mine is Dungeon Gold Rush: scratch one spot an hour, and my next attack might drop five thousand coins. It will not work in a safe room, and Carl makes me hand it over so he can read the back, and then says we will talk about it. Why must he always be so pessimistic? His ticket casts either a fireball or custard, so I have Qwist bring me custard. Not strawberry. Vanilla.

beats.headline: It hammers on the door for hours
beats.text: The survivors sit through the recap while it rages outside. The thing does not tire, and when it leaves the door to tear through a wave of grubs, it comes straight back. Fire is the one lever: a jug of boom takes a quarter of it away and the burn holds the healing back afterwards. The rules change the same day, so that no crawler can sit in a safe room until the collapse.

beats.headline: Closed an hour early
beats.text: Too many crawlers camped in safe rooms when the first floor collapsed, so the rule changes. All safe rooms and safe areas now close one hour before a floor collapses, and any crawler inside is teleported to just outside. A new timer appears under the collapse countdown, one hour faster. In a chicken restaurant full of the elderly, with a rage elemental hammering at the door, Carl and Brandon look at each other and think the same thing: it is time to give it up.

beats.headline: A skull over her head
beats.text: The recap plays it in slow motion. Jack at the wall, Yolanda's horrified face, Crawler Donut leaping, the arrow into his temple, and a player-killer skull icon slowly forming over Yolanda's head as he falls from the platform. Imani cannot watch and gets up and turns away. At the end of the episode the show replays her death from the beginning, in gruesome detail. Mrs. McGibbons's eulogy, delivered on the safe room floor before the episode airs: "Poor Yolanda. She was such a good kid."

beats.headline: Mother of All Bombs
beats.text: I spray-paint Mother of All Bombs on the launcher. Brandon calls it the Bomb Chicken, and so does Donut. Five hours of work: a ramp on a trailer behind the Chopper, and wheeled bombs we call babies, rolling on free weights. Imani opens the door, the elemental teleports away, and we ride. Donut drops babies, then the chain, then the oil. The boiler is about to breach and I open the throttle anyway; Donut sprays the oil, and we jump and let the Chopper go into the stairwell. One more baby at the edge of the hole, Puddle Jumper, and the thing goes in. No experience. We did not kill it.

beats.headline: Into the stairwell
beats.text: Boiler breach imminent: fifteen seconds. The pilot cannot remember which valve releases the pressure, so he opens the throttle instead. The Goblin Copper Chopper hauls the Mother of All Bombs into the stairwell chamber, its trailer spraying oil across the floor, and goes over the edge of the hole without its riders, who jump. A crunch. A relatively small explosion. Black smoke billows out of the stairwell.

beats.headline: Open the damn door
beats.text: Carl is building a bomb launcher, and I ask the obvious question. Why don't we just open the damn door? We are in a safe room. Mobs get thrown out. So we test it. The claw comes through, the thing goes thwum and vanishes, and a moment after, its dot is rocketing straight back at us. Keep it open, I say. See if it learns. Ninety seconds, and it is back, this time from another hallway down. It does not. Seventy-five to a hundred and twenty seconds, every time. When the launcher is ready, I count down from three and pull.

beats.headline: Boom babies down the hall
beats.text: Carts on free-weight wheels, dropped off the back of the trailer into the hallway behind it with the rage elemental in pursuit. Baby Uno carries three boom jugs, a jug of goblin oil, a jar of gunpowder and the last of the hobgoblin pus. There are boom jar babies, shredder babies, and the oh shit babies, which pair two boom jars with a gunpowder satchel wrapped in dynamite. They carpet bomb the hall, and whatever does not light itself, Crawler Donut lights with a low magic missile.

beats.headline: Five hours of building
beats.text: Building the launcher takes about five hours, and Carl sprays Mother of All Bombs on its side with Agatha's paint. Brandon points out that MOAB stands for Massive Ordnance Air Blast, and that a mother of all bombs means one giant bomb: call it the Bomb Chicken or something. Too late, says Carl. While they build, he finds that in a safe room every stick of dynamite reads Inert While in Safe Room. He doesn't expect it to kill the level-93 thing outside. The babies will slow it down, though.

beats.headline: The first baby rolls
beats.text: With its sidecar the chopper won't fit through the door, so a new bike trailer carries the launcher and a tall seat for Donut behind it, facing backward like a tailgunner. The ramp is a pair of spare chopper wheel wells with half-pipe channels and wheelchair coasters at its foot. Each baby is snowboard-sized, weighted like a pinewood derby car, on free-weight wheels. Donut pulls the first, Baby Uno, onto the platform: three boom jugs, goblin oil, gunpowder and the last of Carl's hobgoblin pus. She nudges it, and it rolls away down the hall behind them, straight, without rearing up.

beats.headline: Boom babies and shredders
beats.text: Carl presses the detonator, and during its five-second delay Donut pulls the black lever to drop Imani's weighted chain through a chamber. Baby Uno blows half a second late, in the elemental's back. Then the boom babies go, one after another, flipping into the grubs and filling the hallway with blue flame, while the chain snares the monster for a moment; the few that do not light themselves she hits with a low-powered magic missile. The elemental's spell flings the back of the trailer up, but they are too far away. Around the last corner she drops shredders, gunpowder and shrapnel on long wicks, which burst the pupae and give the monster hornet creatures to stop and kill.

beats.headline: Over the edge
beats.text: The chopper's boiler is about to breach, fifteen seconds, and Carl can't remember which valve to turn, so he speeds up. In the stairwell chamber Donut pulls the red lever and the second chamber sprays champagne-coloured oil across the floor. Both of them jump. The chopper keeps going, trailer and launcher with it, spilling oil, and plummets into the stairwell hole. It crunches, followed by a relatively small explosion. At the edge Carl sets down one of the oh shit babies, two boom jars, gunpowder and a ring of dynamite, as the elemental comes out of the smoke.

beats.headline: Tailgunner on the Bomb Chicken
beats.text: I sit backward on a tall seat behind the launcher, like a tailgunner, and I have just hit one trillion views when Imani opens the door. Bombs away. The chain from the black lever. Burn, baby, burn. The oil from the red lever. Then Carl tells me to jump off a moving vehicle. Are you crazy? I jump. I cast Puddle Jumper when he says, and the monster goes into the hole, and we get no experience at all. Carl, you broke the game.

beats.headline: One man and his ex-girlfriend's cat
beats.text: Carl finishes the Bomb Chicken and takes it out with everyone in the universe watching. Bombs, obstacles, a safe room door used as an ejector, and one exploit the designers never priced in. The elemental is no more.

beats.headline: Ash in the hallway
beats.text: Carl pushes hard on the pedals and they rush out into the hallway. Everything out there is blackened and turned to ash, and it smells like burning garbage. There is no sign of the train cars, or of the wheelchairs and walkers that were left behind. The only thing that survived is the long, three-hundred-foot length of glittering magical chain, which Carl grabbed earlier.

beats.headline: Mobs do not go down
beats.text: A goblin shamanka told them once: mobs that climb down the stairs dissolve halfway. The guide said the same. So a level-93 rage elemental, which nobody here can kill, is lured across an oil slick into a stairwell hole, and the dungeon follows its own rules. The elemental dissolves with its health already in the red and a bomb going off beside it. Nobody is credited with the kill, and nobody gets the experience.

beats.headline: A bola off the launcher
beats.text: Everything in the hallway is ash; the train cars and abandoned wheelchairs are gone. The only thing that survived is the long, three-hundred-foot length of glittering, magical chain, which Carl grabbed earlier. Weighted at either end, it waits in one of the two chambers built on either side of the bomb on the trailer, the levers beside Donut's chair. Drop the bola! She pulls the black lever and Imani's chain snakes away through the chamber. Far behind, the elemental stops: it has been ensnared by the chain. When it comes out of the smoke at the stairwell, a length of chain is still attached to its back leg, and its health is in the red.

beats.headline: A hug at the hole
beats.text: Forty minutes after the elemental dies, what is left of Meadow Lark arrives: thirty-six residents in three shopping-cart contraptions built from chopper wheels. Brandon, weaker than the other two, pushes six people by himself. "We didn't need your directions," he says; the scorched hallway leads straight to the hole. He asks once whether Crawler Carl wants to come with them. Carl does not. Brandon pulls him into a hug. "You two take care of yourselves, okay?"

beats.headline: A substitute admin
beats.text: Zev is in a time out, says an admin called Mukta, who is her substitute. Mukta has overridden the round-table Zev booked and put us on something that pays a higher fee. I remind her we were promised the right to refuse. You seem to be under the impression that you have a say in this, crawler. Then the chat is gone, with no way to answer. I brush Donut for the first time down here, the way Bea taught me, and then we are on a boat the size of a walk-in closet.

beats.headline: Barry, where are we?
beats.text: There's a nice young man kneeling by my bucket, and I ask him: Barry, where are we? He says we're in the dungeon, and I'm going down to the next floor. The dungeon? Like a sex thing? He says goodbye. I touch his cheek. We should have had children, Barry. I wish I hadn't talked you into working so hard. I think I've had too much to drink, or I'm having another one of those acid flashbacks. This cat keeps talking to me.

beats.headline: Shaped like a spatula
beats.text: A mechanic's box gives Carl a tool shaped like a spatula. What the hell is this, he mutters, and pulls up its properties: a hardening and de-hardening tool for the workbench, for fusing joints or giving otherwise rigid materials varying degrees of plasticity without changing their strength. That seems pretty useful. He puts it in his inventory next to his Goo-Inator 3000.

beats.headline: One per crawler
beats.text: An unmanned safe room was once an industrial kitchen, stripped of everything but a working walk-in freezer. On a steel counter under the screens sits a plain metal toaster in a pile of crumbs, plugged into nothing and impossible to lift. The screen reads Free Mana Toast! One per Crawler! Carl presses the handle and a burned triangle of toast jumps out onto the counter. Its description ends with fuck you. Well, that was unnecessary, he mutters, and gives his piece to Donut, who tucks both away.

beats.headline: Thirty-six go down
beats.text: Forty minutes after the elemental dies, what is left of Meadow Lark follows the scorched trail to the stairwell: thirty-six residents in three shopping-cart contraptions built from Chopper wheels and hunks of wood. Chris and Imani push the two big people buckets; Brandon pushes six. Brandon hugs Carl goodbye. Imani is the last one down the ramp, and she waves, unsmiling. Donut asks whether they will see them again. Carl does not know.

beats.headline: Zev is in a time out
beats.text: For the record: Mukta (Admin) opens a chat in a safe room in the kobold quadrant. Crawlers Carl and Princess Donut are to be transported to their interview in ten minutes. Their outreach associate has been put in a time out and returns tomorrow; Mukta is the substitute until then. Zev had them booked on Dungeon Crawl Tactics. Mukta has overridden her and picked a better program, one paying a higher fee. Still round-table style. Close enough. Crawler Carl says they were promised the right to refuse. "You seem to be under the impression that you have a say in this, crawler." The chat closes. It cannot be answered.

beats.headline: Ten tiny black boxes
beats.text: A mob has been injured by something Carl purposely left lying around, and the System awards a trap achievement and a Gold Sapper's Box. He is not sure what earned it: the chain or the oil slick, probably not the bombs. The box holds a sapper's table and ten of a trap-building item, each a tiny black box the size of a dime with a long length of wire attached. The moment they are in his inventory they place themselves near the top of the list by value, right behind that ridiculous Fireball or Custard lottery ticket.

beats.headline: It nearly knocks him over
beats.text: Carl's trap achievement pays out a Gold Sapper's Box with two items in it. The first is a Sapper's table that practically knocks him over when it appears, a table just like his engineering and alchemy tables. Its description says explosives and traps created at it don't lose stability and can't be prematurely set off. The second item is ten proximity triggers, which only attach to a trap at a Sapper's Table.

beats.headline: We are expensive
beats.text: The segment is called Death Watch: two crawlers guess who lives to buy their friends' lives. I climb over the table and walk out. A voice threatens to drown us; Mukta threatens to accelerate us. So I ask one thing: as long as I participate, is there any consequence for what I say? They paid for our appearance, nothing else. Fine. We are not stronger than this host. We are expensive. On air I demand the points to send us into that fight, call him pork boy, and dare him. He sends the two men back instead, and I have already told them to run.

beats.headline: Death Watch Extreme Dungeon Mayhem
beats.text: The Maestro puts Zhang and me up against Brindled Vespas and does all the talking for us. That is the show. We are the part that gets hurt. Then Carl, the one with the cat, works out that he is worth too much to the production to be punished, and gambles on it, in front of everyone, and it holds. He gets us out. Zhang, our boss, me, and my sister Li Na. I owe a man I have just met more than I have ever owed anyone.

beats.headline: Death Watch Extreme Dungeon Mayhem
beats.text: The show is Death Watch Extreme Dungeon Mayhem. The host calls himself the Maestro. He pulls my brother and Zhang off the floor and makes them play a guessing game for points that buy lives, and they will not choose which of us to spend them on. The rest of us stay frozen where we were standing, between the troglodytes and the Brindled Vespas. Then the crawler with the cat, Carl, decides he is too valuable to the production to be punished, and bets on it, out loud, and the four of us walk out. I am remembering his face.

beats.headline: Glurp, glurp
beats.text: Two crawlers, Li Jun and Zhang, a pack of Brindled Vespas, and me with the microphone. That is the format. The format works, and I am very, very good at it. Then the one with the cat opens his mouth. He wagers, on my air, that the production will not dare touch him, and the production, to my everlasting disgust, does not. He walks the whole group off my show alive. Every one of them. Glurp, glurp. We will be right back.

beats.headline: Sit, or be accelerated
beats.text: On the Maestro's set the crawlers refuse to take part, and a first voice threatens to drop them in the ocean. Crawler Carl calls bullshit. Then: "Crawler Carl, this is Administrator Mukta." They are required to take their seats. Refusal means acceleration; there are plenty of other crawlers to show; this is not a bluff. Asked whether that other guy can hear, a pause, then no. Asked whether anything he says carries consequences, provided he participates, a longer pause: "They have paid for your appearance. Nothing else."

beats.headline: I do the talking
beats.text: This boat heaves more than the last one, and I am going to puke on television. Carl brings up his pillow. That was different; I did that on purpose. The crowd is all boys chanting glurp, and I remind Carl of our arrangement: he sits there and looks angry, and I do the talking. Then he climbs over the table and walks out, and I tell him he is going to get us in trouble. Twice. When we sit back down, he says he is the one who talks this time.

beats.headline: Two teleport points, four people
beats.text: Li Jun and I are standing on a stage in front of the Maestro while he plays with us, and behind us Li Na and the manager are boxed in between hatching Brindled Vespas and troglodytes with nowhere to go. We have two teleport points. Two. I say put them on Li Jun and Li Na and leave me where I am, because that is the arithmetic and somebody has to say it out loud. Then a barefoot man starts whispering, and the arithmetic changes.

beats.headline: A present for Carl
beats.text: The Maestro's gift for his VIPs is a literal cardboard box, for Carl alone, something the orc says Carl wants really bad. Carl opens it and has to laugh. Inside is a brand-new pair of Bates zip-up tactical boots, identical to the service boots he wore on active duty, in his size, and the Maestro adds that there are socks in the box too. These will be really comfortable in a safe room, Carl says, and puts the lid back on. His soles have fully acclimated, several of his buffs and skills only work barefoot, and the orc knows it. I love them, Carl adds. I hope they weren't too expensive.

beats.headline: Usually the first of nine out
beats.text: A talk-show host with a family stake in the matter laughs at the idea that he is one of them. Do I look like a Naga to you? By his account the Blood Sultanate is almost always the first of the nine to be eliminated, and the cat wearing its crown has been dead since the moment she put it on. He means to be on the ninth floor this season himself, as War Leader of his own family's clan.

beats.headline: Boots, in a box
beats.text: The parting gift is a cardboard box, and in it is a brand-new pair of Bates zip-up tactical boots, identical to the ones I wore on active duty, in my size, with socks. My soles have acclimated, several of my buffs only work barefoot, and the orc knows it. I tell him I love them, they will be really comfortable in a safe room, and I hope they were not too expensive. On the way out I tell him I look forward to beating him again on the ninth floor. That gets a reaction from the crowd.

beats.headline: Maggie does the talking
beats.text: The show plays our whole road for the young man and the cat, out of order, and he watches his own present go off in our faces. He says she wasn't dead yet. Maggie goes at him with the dagger and finds the trailer wall instead, and tells him she's going to find him and watch him die, him and the cat. I don't say a word. Then the orc hands us a Legendary Skill Potion: Find Crawler to fifteen, any name, anywhere. Maggie holds it to her chest, and for the first time, she smiles.

beats.headline: On the Maestro's show
beats.text: The Maestro's show plays the rest. Frank and Maggie were frozen in the safe room, and their teenaged daughter Yvette had been hiding under her mother's stealth field the whole time. At the rat, Maggie yells at Frank not to loot it. He does it anyway, and pulls out one item, the lit stick. He drops it in surprise and all three turn to run. The shrapnel takes Yvette down, and Frank too; a dislodged hunk of rock shears his hand right off. Carl understands that the girl's injuries were his doing.

beats.headline: Of gods and royalty
beats.text: Off mic, the barefoot one asks if I was ever a crawler. Please. I come from a civilized system. My family was there when the Syndicate created the crawl. We are of gods and royalty. The Blood Sultanate? Do I look like a Naga? My family's Skull Clan has won six of the last ten, top three every time, and the Sultanate is almost always the first of the nine eliminated. They have been dead, the pair of them, since the cat put on that crown. I am on my way to their planet right now, and on the ninth floor I will be War Leader Maestro.

beats.headline: Find Crawler
beats.text: Carl's trap closes on Yvette, and her own mother finishes what the trap started. On his show, the Maestro hands Frank and Maggie My a Legendary Skill Potion that takes Find Crawler to level 15, and Maggie snatches it up. There is exactly one crawler she wants found.

beats.headline: Always plays Battle Royale
beats.text: The Maestro, in the interview on the big screen, explains why he missed Faction Wars last time. He was of age last season, but the stupid Squim Conglomerate always plays Battle Royale, which has no Faction Wars or Celestial Ascendancy segment. This year he means to be there. He is on his way to Carl's stupid planet right now, to be War Leader Maestro of the Skull Clan. He pounds his chest like a gorilla while saying so.

beats.headline: The girl who would not kill anything
beats.text: Yvette. Her guide, a floating brain, told the three of them that the only way to survive was to kill other crawlers, and she wept and declined. Her mother and father did not decline. A whole group who took them for a family, shot in the back, and then a string of frightened stragglers, most of them alone. The daughter was there for some of it and not for the rest. She has killed nothing at all.

beats.headline: Her mother's hands
beats.text: Crawler Yvette is dead. Her father lifted a lit stick of dynamite out of a rat's corpse the barefoot man had left behind, and the blast took his hand and put her on the ground, crying that it hurt. Her mother knelt and put her hands around her daughter's throat. The barefoot man says she was not dead yet, and would have healed. Her mother says he does not know the whole story. Afterwards a talk-show host handed her parents a Legendary Skill Potion for Find Crawler, on air, as a prize. I am obliged to carry the programme. I am not obliged to say anything about the rest of it, and I find that I would rather not.

beats.headline: Two trap modules
beats.text: Back in the safe room after the battle, Donut opens her loot boxes. The only new thing is two Trap Modules from her gold sapper's box: one called a Spike Module and the other an Alarm Module. These are ready-to-go traps, no tinkering required. They can be upgraded and reconfigured, but only with a sapper's table.

beats.headline: Half as many hornets
beats.text: The System AI decides the Brindled Vespas are proliferating too aggressively and halves the number in the dungeon. Their spitting acid is adjusted down. Slightly. New grubs keep generating whenever a corpse is created, but each now has only a fifty percent chance of reaching the pupa stage. On the same recap, Lucia Mar smashes a vespa to pieces with her mace while its acid sizzles two inches from her head, on a personal shield.

beats.headline: Four kills, less fees
beats.text: A new tab: Accounts. A creator's fee on Carl's Jug O' Boom, one gold coin per kill by other crawlers. Current kills: four. The fine print takes two coins plus twenty-five percent, rounded up, and forfeits the lot if I die. Cash out now and I get one coin. Highway robbery. I have slept on Maggie, too. She is hell-bent on hunting us down, so we are not running. I would rather be ready for her than have her sneak up behind us, and her invisibility is not nearly as powerful as I first thought.

beats.headline: Under a million
beats.text: On the recap Le Mouvement is gone to a city boss, all but one man, and the ticker reads 990,303. Carl had not noticed it drop below a million, and for every crawler that ticks away he feels a part of himself going with them.

beats.headline: Last one down
beats.text: I am the last of us down the ramp. Carl and Donut stand by the hole and wave, and I wave back. I don't smile. Thirty-six residents went down ahead of me in buckets built from chopper wheels and hunks of wood, and Yolanda did not. At the scorched entrance to the third floor I stop, look up into the air, and raise a middle finger. Then I go inside.

beats.headline: Four kills, one coin each
beats.text: A new tab in the interface: ACCOUNTS. One item. Creator's Fee, Carl's Jug O' Boom. Royalty: 1 gold coin per kill. Current kills: 4. The small print, too small to zoom: the count updates once daily, and two gold coins plus a 25% deposit fee, rounded up, are deducted upon cash out. Four kills, all by other crawlers' hands.

beats.headline: Wiped
beats.text: Another recap carries the news: a city boss kills every one of them except a single man locked outside the boss room, and the remaining-crawler count drops below a million in the same broadcast.

beats.headline: Should never have booked it
beats.text: Mukta warned there would be a discussion after the show. The program ends, the crawlers are transported back, and there is no sign of the admin. Afterwards a warning arrives, no weapons in the presence of Admins, and Crawler Carl says "Mukta is coming." It is Zev who appears, her censure lifted on appeal. Her verdict on the Maestro's show: Mukta should never have booked it. Her own booking would have been a discussion of dungeon tactics, done in a creative, silly way. Borant, she adds, is not allowed to discriminate against Syndicate-member production companies.

beats.headline: I heard him
beats.text: Back in the safe room I cannot stop talking. Yvette is a pretty name, and it's sad, but I'm also kind of relieved: her mother killed her, so Carl didn't. And the orc said we broke the record. Then I tell Carl the other thing. Not what the orc said about the ninth floor. What Mordecai said, when he told Carl he should leave me when we get to that floor. I heard him. Carl says to worry about getting to the third floor first. Okay.

beats.headline: Two trap modules
beats.text: Back in the safe room after the show, Donut opens her loot boxes from the earlier battle. The only new things are two Trap Modules from her gold sapper's box, one called a Spike Module and the other an Alarm Module. They are ready-to-go traps, no tinkering required. They can be upgraded and reconfigured, but only with a sapper's table, and that won't happen until the fourth floor.

beats.headline: The stairwell rule is patched
beats.text: The exploit gets its own paragraph in the next announcement. Yes, everyone just watched that rule get exploited on the recap. It was very clever and very exciting. It is not going to happen again. Effective immediately, any non-sapient mob that happens upon a stairwell will not be disintegrated. The same message says game guides may now explain the third floor's race and class selection.

beats.headline: Censured, and cleared
beats.text: Okay, so, I was censured by the System AI. It decided I cheated by warning Carl and Princess Donut before the rage elemental appeared, and I was suspended. My representative appealed, and on review they found Carl noticed the man at the same moment I shouted, so my record is clean. It is not really clean. Once the AI notices you, it is difficult to get it to un-notice you. Mukta should never have booked that show, and I apologise. Also, Carl, there is a video I need to tell you about.

beats.headline: Sorry, Ralph, and a stamp
beats.text: The kobold boss chamber is a dog pound with the music so loud we talk by chat. Dingoes in the cages, scarred and beaten, and between songs I hear cheering from the pit. A fighting ring. I toss a pet biscuit into a cage and the red dot turns white. Donut calls it a betrayal most foul. The boss comes out of a carrier: Ralph, a frenzied gerbil. The one-eyed dingo swallows him, and he comes out through its head. I punch him, the stun lands for the first time ever, and I put my bare foot on him.

beats.headline: Frozen in mid-air
beats.text: Crawler Carl lights a jug and throws it at the barn doors of a neighbourhood boss's chamber as they open, just as about forty cheering kobolds come pouring out. The world freezes with the jug hanging in the air like a comet while the dungeon introduces the boss. When it unfreezes, the jug explodes among the kobolds, evaporating most of them, including the boss's owner.

beats.headline: Held in reserve
beats.text: Outside the kobold boss room, Donut has a pool of twenty-eight mana points, two pieces of mana toast and a pile of mana restoration potions. With her two-minute cooldown between potions, the potions are next to useless in a battle. So they decide to wait and see what they face first.

beats.headline: A betrayal most foul
beats.text: Outside the kobold boss room, beaten danger dingoes lie in cages. Carl has no Heal Critter scrolls left, but he has a ton of pet biscuits, which Donut still eats despite being a regular crawler. He tosses one into a cage. CARL WHAT ARE YOU DOING. THAT IS MY FOOD. The dingo pulls itself up painfully, sniffs, eats the tiny biscuit and turns its back, and its dot blinks white. They repeat it for all fourteen.

beats.headline: Two percent, finally
beats.text: The two percent chance to stun has never once fired. Then, in a room full of cages, a dingo's head explodes and the gerbil that was inside it rockets at Carl's throat. He was ready. One full-strength punch, and the gerbil bounces off the floor with a sickening crunch and slides into the edge of a cage, health deep in the red, Stunned over its head with a fifteen-second timer. Carl takes two steps toward the tiny, unmoving thing, with a baleful glance at the ceiling.

beats.headline: I wanted the grub
beats.text: The dungeon groans when I stamp on the gerbil, and the blood will not come off my foot. Along the back wall of the fighting arena is a pet reward room: ten cages, one key. I want the white-tagged brindle grub; I have seen what the hornets do. Donut only has eyes for the last cage: seven inches of raw chicken with pink feathers, a Mongoliensis, red-tagged. Thirty seconds until the cages close. I open his, grab him, and he fights me while she feeds him. The dot stays red. I knew we should have gone with the grub.

beats.headline: Choose wisely, says the key
beats.text: Picking through the slagged kobolds, Carl finds that the one who pressed the button to open the cages also had a key. It opens the individual cages of the fighters and the bait animals in the kobold fighting pits; for anyone but a kobold it works once and breaks. Past a dirt arena stained red and a pile of bones as tall as the ceiling, a line of ten cages waits, and the room announces itself as a pet reward room. Its reward: you have a key, and it opens only one cage.

beats.headline: The last cage
beats.text: Donut claims the choice and gasps at the very last cage: a pink-feathered chicken dinosaur thing, a red-tagged mongoliensis. Carl thinks it looks like dinner and would rather take the brindle grub. A pet biscuit tossed at its cage bounces off a blue forcefield. Warning: the cages will permanently close in thirty seconds. Donut begs. Carl sighs, takes the key, and jams it into the lock of the mongoliensis cage. The little bastard shoots out, and he grabs it in both hands.

beats.headline: Seven inches of pink feathers, in a cage
beats.text: CAGE. Small. Pink? Pink. TWO BIG THINGS. Bite them. Bite them. Bite. Biscuits. FOOD. Peck. Peck. Cat pats head. Bite cat.

beats.headline: Pecked like a chicken
beats.text: The baby mongoliensis comes out of its cage thrashing and trying to bite. Carl has to sit on the ground holding it in both hands while Donut pulls a few pet biscuits from her inventory. It slows, eyeing the food, and when he eases his grip it pecks at them like a chicken. Its dot stays red. Carl, it's a boy, Donut cries, and promises Mongo a bow tie. He bites her on the nose.

beats.headline: She adopts a dinosaur
beats.text: There is a reward room on the second floor with a cage in it, and in the cage is a pet-class mob, and the pet-class mob is my son. I did not know that until I saw him. He is called Mongo. He is mine, and that is the end of the discussion.

beats.headline: Another off a kobold
beats.text: Carl had no Heal Critter scrolls left in the cage room, where the beaten dingoes got pet biscuits instead. Now the dingoes are gone, and he picks through the slagged, smoldering remains of the kobolds in the main room, looting a few spiked helmets and gold coins here and there. One of them has a scroll of Heal Critter and a handful of pet biscuits.

beats.headline: Them critters already know
beats.text: For the record: Crawler Agatha, level four, still alive, arrives at the stairwell pushing the same squeaking cart. Crawler Carl has just found, in his inventory history, three items that came out of it: an inter-tunnel communications relay, flagged illegal; a platinum personal shield; a pulse pistol. One manufacturer. He offers to fix her wheel. No need, she says. Them critters already know she's here; they just don't know what to do about it. She goes down. The feed was out for a couple of minutes, which is nothing unusual.

beats.headline: Three items in the history
beats.text: Carl's inventory has grown a History tab. Sorted by value, its top three entries are things he has never seen: a Trans Tunnel 7C Orator Relay by Valtay Corp., a Valtay Perso-Shield Platinum Edition and a Mag 3040 Valtay Corp Pulse Pistol. The relay is a communication device, and illegal. Then Donut sees a blue dot coming, and he knows where they came from: Agatha's cart, all of it, held in his inventory through the boss fight. She wheels it in, squeaking, and calls him a cart thief. He offers to fix the wheel. No need to fix her squeak, she says.

beats.headline: A coincidental spell book
beats.text: The rules are a little weird about taming dungeon pets, Mordecai says, while Mongo screams and hisses at him from his cage: remove the creature's hostility first, then come back. Then Carl and Donut open their boxes from the boss fight. Donut 'coincidentally' receives a spell book of Heal Critter; Carl gets another Potion of Determine Value and a thousand gold.

beats.headline: MOTHER comes fast
beats.text: BUG. Big bug holds Mongo. Up. Mouth. MOTHER comes fast. Bug head OFF. Mongo down. Mongo MOTHER'S now. Jump. Jump. Bite MOTHER nose.

beats.headline: Arcanist, and a brother
beats.text: Now I'm allowed to talk about the third floor, and I've cleaned the place up. Down the stairs, back in this room: race, then class, then stats. The AI will recommend, and its recommendations are good, and they don't care how you look on camera. Me? Arcanist. Changeling Fire Mage Arcanist. I almost picked a class called Storm Commander. Odette talked me out of it. My brother picked it instead, on her recommendation. The third floor itself we'll do when you get there.

beats.headline: A very food-motivated dinosaur
beats.text: Several hours of dog commands follow. Attack, come and even lie down work really well; stay is another story. Mongo is very food motivated and loves pet biscuits, which makes him easier to train. After a full day he no longer charges at everything he sees. He snarls and hops, but waits for Donut's command, which has somehow evolved from attack to sic 'em.

beats.headline: Mongo becomes a Royal Steed
beats.text: Who knew being a mother would be this difficult? Mongo bites my nose over and over. I show him how a grub opens, and we teach him attack and come, and attack becomes sic 'em. Then, outside the stair room, a hornet grabs my son and lifts him toward its mouth, and I take its head off. Then I have a new menu: Mongo the Mongoliensis, pet of Grand Champion Best in Dungeon Princess Donut, title Royal Steed. We tamed Mongo. Then he bites me on the nose.

beats.headline: A History tab
beats.text: The boss box gives Carl yet another Potion of Determine Value, and he wonders why the System keeps handing him these. He drinks it, and his inventory gains a few new sort options, among them a tab labelled History: much the same junk he carries now, plus the chopper and the potions, scrolls and parts he has used up. Sorted by value, its top three are Valtay Corp items he has never seen: an Orator Relay, a Perso-Shield and a pulse pistol. Then Agatha's dot comes up the map, and he knows where they came from. He took her whole shopping cart into his inventory during the fight with the Ball of Swine.

beats.headline: In the History tab
beats.text: Waiting out the timer, Carl opens a new inventory tab labelled History and sorts it by value. At the top sit three items he has never seen: a Valtay tunnel communications relay, a Valtay Corp pulse pistol, and a Valtay Perso-Shield Platinum Edition, a tech-based personal shield. The relay carries a warning that unsanctioned communication devices are illegal down here. Then a blue dot moves toward them, and when Carl sees who it is, he understands: he took Agatha's whole shopping cart into his inventory during the boss fight with the Ball of Swine and never examined it. She wheels the squeaking cart in and calls him a cart thief.

beats.headline: The footwear situation does not improve
beats.text: The second floor finally addresses my feet. It hands me an Enchanted Pedicure Kit of the Sylph. So now I am still barefoot, but my feet are shiny and they glitter, and the audience has noticed, and the audience does not let things go.

beats.headline: The show goes on hiatus
beats.text: My show is on hiatus while it restructures. A spokesperson for the royal family has requested that people stop calling me Carl's Naughty Little Piggie. So far nobody is complying. Odette tells her audience never to call me that, holds out her hands, and they shout it for her. The crawler sits on her couch, says he knows nothing about the video, and says his offer of single combat still stands. Then her audience starts glurping.

beats.headline: The dungeon's pokeball
beats.text: Donut has trained Mongo to perch quietly on her back, clinging to her fur, and he has behaved himself. Mostly. Odette has mentioned something called a magical pet carrier, apparently the dungeon's equivalent of a pokeball. They are supposedly expensive, but one would let them put a bonded pet into inventory without harming him. Carl doesn't care how much it costs. If they can afford it, it is going to be one of their first purchases.

beats.headline: Bow tie, three seconds
beats.text: BOW on neck. BAD. Off. Lady hand. Bite. MOTHER's back. Hold fur. Quiet. Quiet. Wall. WALL. Wall. MOTHER's tail. Bite.

beats.headline: You called them velociraptors
beats.text: That thing is going to get you killed, Carl, you do realise. You should have picked the little round one with the mohawk; still, if it lives, it will be a vicious fighter. As for the third floor: take a pathfinder skill or advanced mapping. Let the Princess go first and tailor your class to hers. Ignore the AI on race; look carefully at what it suggests for class. And you honestly don't know what it is? Mongoliensis. The trouble is the translation. You called them velociraptors. One more, which I am not sure is moral: hidden among the Princess's choices, for high charisma only. Pick it, and someone will be very angry.

beats.headline: I pushed him too hard
beats.text: Mordecai had a few additional choice words for me after Carl delivered my message. I watched. He will come around. Tell him I understand his feelings, and that I would love the opportunity to explain myself. What happened between us? The short answer is that I pushed him too hard, and he paid dearly for it. And if a certain corporation is trying to reach you, be very cautious. They have an entire fleet parked outside the Borant system, ready to collect on the debt.

beats.headline: Fewer classes
beats.text: Picking Donut's class, Mordecai finds her list of 34 the shortest he has ever seen. It is a combination of four things, he works out: her racial choice, her stats, the Desperado pass they both have, which precludes several of the classes right off the bat, and the tiara on her head, which narrows it even further. There are still a few great choices on there, he says.

beats.headline: Taken with the Cat race
beats.text: Donut picks it while pretending to pick something else, and takes Artist Alley Mogul as her first specialty. It is a Charisma-and-chance class built on the Character Actor skill: each floor she chooses a specialty, the AI rolls how much of that class she gets, and when the floor ends she loses it and starts over. Her own spells are untouched. It also makes her immune to poison and disease and hands her Cockroach, a chance to survive a killing blow.

beats.headline: Manoeuvred into managing a cat
beats.text: The cat picks Former Child Actor and tells Carl she was acting. She has also received the Manager benefit, and the Manager is me. From now on I teleport to any saferoom they are in. I was supposed to transfer to a magic guild after this floor: a bigger room, my potions, more spells. Now every time they sleep or eat or brush their teeth, I'm with them. No tunnel access. No television. No codex. No warning before I'm pulled away. Carl tells her that wasn't cool. Oh gods.

beats.headline: An incubus, in a tuxedo
beats.text: Three hours I have been standing in this tuxedo waiting for them. The third floor has made me an incubus: grey skin, short horns, bat wings, a barbed tail, and a deeper voice. Guildmaster of this guildhall, the tooltip says. Carl tells me I look good. The cat says something about crackers. I welcome them properly, because the training levels are over. Then the door closes, the public cannot see in here, and the jacket and tie come off. I hate formal wear.

beats.headline: Her advice makes the party
beats.text: The Princess took my advice, which is what advice is for. A class that lets her choose another every time she levels, and a manager who has walked those floors himself and remembers every one of them. Mordecai is not to know he was steered. He would sulk, he would be entitled to, and a sulking guide is no use to anybody. Some gifts are best received as accidents. I have given a great many that way.

beats.headline: Cat, and a Former Child Actor
beats.text: Odette suggested it, so obviously it is a good idea: a class that lets me choose another class at every level. I also arrange for Mordecai to be my manager. He is thrilled. He does not show it, but he is. My constitution is apparently far too low for what Carl calls melee, so I will be fighting with charisma, spells and the audience, which is how it should be done.

beats.headline: Primal, and a Compensated Anarchist
beats.text: Class selection, on the way into the Over City. I take Primal for the race and a monk-rogue hybrid nobody has picked before, and the AI writes me up as "a trapmaking, bomb-making, social-media dynamo" who "will happily throw a Molotov through a window one moment and step in front of a camera to plead for the violence to stop the next." I'd argue with it if I could think of the argument.

beats.headline: Already at ten
beats.text: Among the classes on offer, Prizefighter adds three to Pugilism, which would be a huge bonus, Carl thinks, considering the Cheat Code potion has already taken the skill to ten. He would pick the class in a second if he thought he could just punch his way through the dungeon. He knows already that he can't.

beats.headline: Taken with the Primal race
beats.text: "The Compensated Anarchist will happily throw a Molotov through a window one moment and step in front of a camera to plead for the violence to stop the next."

beats.headline: No clerics, no paladins
beats.text: Carl picks Primal, and his list of classes runs to over 650 choices. He would have even more without that tattoo on his neck, Mordecai says. The Desperado Club does not allow goody-two-shoes sorts, so there are no Cleric classes and no Paladin classes, along with a few monk classes, which is unfortunate, as they would have been worth a look.

beats.headline: Eight days for the third
beats.text: Halfway through Carl's class selection the world rumbles: the second floor has collapsed. Just over 700,000 crawlers remain, and the third floor gets eight full days. Mordecai does the arithmetic out loud. If they keep this up, the sixth floor will be open only eleven or twelve days, where it is usually open for thirty, and the factions are going to be pissed.

beats.headline: Money, and lots of it
beats.text: Compensated Anarchist is potentially the best of the three, and it requires a lot of work: grind, grind, and focus, on shortened timers. He picks it while I narrow my eyes at him. Only one thing is going to make this work, and it is not training. It is money, and lots of it. As a manager I cannot fight beside them, but I can still step outside now and then, especially on the urban levels, and I have to present them. So the tie goes back on.

beats.headline: Carl takes the empty box
beats.text: Race selection, on the way into the Over City. The preview model for this one is blank, because nobody alive knows what they looked like. Mordecai's summary: the progenitors, the first species to conquer the universe, the boogeymen of the cosmos, gone one day without a note. Taking it costs fifteen stat points against staying human: the ten a human gets, and five more. What it buys is a ceiling. Every skill trainable to twenty, and only a rare few who take it ever train one or two skills above fifteen.

beats.headline: Asleep through the paperwork
beats.text: I curl up with Mongo and fall asleep while Carl reads every race there is. Staying a cat gives me Night Vision, Slash Attack, Cat-like Reflexes and something called 9 Lives, which halves the first nine physical hits I take each day. When I wake up I ask Carl if he grew elf ears. He did not. He is still human, which is boring. He says he is a Primal. That sounds like a caveman, and he smells exactly the same.

beats.headline: Enough intelligence, not yet
beats.text: With his stats settled, Carl has given himself enough Intelligence to read the Wisp Armor spellbook, and he doesn't do it quite yet. He is still on the fence about using it himself, giving it to Donut or selling it, and he wants to see what its actual monetary value is first.

beats.headline: A sign that grows out of the ground
beats.text: At the gate Mordecai gives me the first rule: don't cross the level-75 guards; there is no jail, only the death penalty. Then he points at a discoloured rock just outside it. Focus on it, and a holographic sign grows out of the ground like a tree: arrows and distances in kilometres to saferooms, restrooms, stairs six kilometres off, and a medium-sized settlement 34 out. Then the rest of the rules. Don't go into the ruins at night until he says so. Stay away from girls with horns. Then he makes a beeline for a pub.

beats.headline: Where the tourists are
beats.text: No tourists on the third floor, Mordecai says. Most of them are on the eighteenth, a billionaire's luxury retreat where the galaxy's rich and elite party, gamble and satiate their most base desires, and the one place where printed people may legally be used for the rest. Carl asks what happens if a crawler gets there. Nobody ever has, so nobody knows; the same goes for the fifteenth. Borant and the AI are required to have a plan.

beats.headline: Props who do not know it
beats.text: Most of the people in these villages were engineered by Borant, so Borant owns them. It is the only world they have known. Every time they are regenerated their minds are altered and planted with false memories, and anything inconvenient, like a crawler explaining that they are props, is erased. Those meth-addicted goblins were written for this world only. Carl asks how that is legal. You cannot alter the memories of naturals unless they sign their rights away. Using the printed ones outside sanctioned entertainment is basically a war crime.

beats.headline: Off a dead clown
beats.text: A clown in a red wig and a little hat, carrying a pair of oversized butcher knives, goes down under Carl's fists, its forked tongue lolling, and he keeps pounding until its head caves in. A mass of red dots is fifteen seconds out. The clown's inventory reads Clown Meat, Big Top Ticket, 35 Gold. Carl loots it all, plus both knives, the wig and the hat. Mongo is still tearing at the clown's ankle, and when Carl picks him up he has gotten noticeably larger and squeals in rage.

beats.headline: A quest, and a stilt clown
beats.text: A lemur in a painted human skull throws a knife at my head, and the cloak turns it off my chest. Then a Quests tab, trumpets, streamers: The Show Must Go On. Find out why this circus still exists and end it, for a gold quest box. I ask Mordecai whether to take it. He answers with something about his mother's ashes; he is drunk after fifteen minutes. A boom jug sets the building alight, a giraffe flings lemurs at us, and Donut drops an eleven-foot stilt clown so I can land on its chest.

beats.headline: A family establishment
beats.text: For the record: Gordo, Bopca protector at the Belly-Rubbed Pug, a renaissance-fair pub of a saferoom where rooms now cost ten gold a night. Twenty minutes after the crawlers left their manager, he teleports in beside the bar with his pants at his knees, asking for Grannie first. Gordo, from behind the counter: "My good sir, I must ask you sheath your sword immediately!" This is a family establishment. Mordecai vomits on the floor, sits in it and passes out. Gordo leans over: this is their manager? Yep. A sad shake of the head. "You two are so dead."

beats.headline: Clown ankle
beats.text: Clown DOWN. Ankle. Bite. Bite. BITE. Mongo is BIGGER. Carl picks Mongo up. NO. Clown is FOOD.

beats.headline: A knife off the chest
beats.text: A red-furred lemur wearing a black and red painted human skull as a mask sits on the ledge of a second-storey window, little legs dangling, and only appears on the minimap once it has thrown its knife straight at Carl's head. Luckily the knife flies low, hits him in the chest and bounces off his jacket, thanks to the cloak's anti-piercing benefit. Four more lemurs appear in the window.

beats.headline: The Belly-Rubbed Pug
beats.text: On the third floor the saferooms are inns. This one is a renaissance-fair pub at the end of a dead-end alley, a pug in a top hat on the sign, the three screens as before and a Bopca called Gordo behind the counter. The sleeping rooms, only five of them, now cost ten gold a night, and the food costs money too. Mordecai teleports in with his trousers round his knees, addressing two girls and a grandma who are not there, vomits, sits in it, and passes out. Gordo's verdict: "You two are so dead."

beats.headline: Thumbs up on the classes
beats.text: Hello, hello. Okay, so, good news, Carl and Princess Donut. Odette's show was another hit, and the majority of viewers are giving a thumbs up to your class and race choices. Both of you picked unique classes, which is always a plus. There are a few other Primals, no straight cats, one were-cat and some cat girls. The public cannot see Mordecai now. No VIP crawlers nearby, and I'd avoid the locals. The next interview is likely the fourth night. I have had to take on extra people for the requests.

beats.headline: A cactus and eighteen westerns
beats.text: My Silver Earth box: a three-inch cactus from Home Depot, $3.99 price tag still on the pot, and a shrink-wrapped pack of eighteen L'Amour paperbacks, the Sackett Family Saga. My dad had a whole shelf of them, and I used to read them under the covers with a flashlight. I haven't read these. My hands are shaking and I'm not sure why.
