Evidence, they call it, and the human has shown the swordsmen a pass for it from the magistrate, so they leave without him. The magistrate is not to be disturbed. If he does not care about your business then he will certainly care about being disturbed, and I will not be discussing it further. Behind me is a shelf of beanbag figures in their proper order, and the human is standing far too close to it. The door behind me is locked. It is locked for a reason.

beats.headline: Donut picks it up
beats.text: Carl falls onto the corpse of the Divider as his dynamite blows, the corpse bursts, and he lands unconscious on a roof across the street. She grabs the neighborhood map, leaps out of the pool, finishes off the last three monsters with two magic missiles and Mongo, then leaps up to the roof and uses a heal scroll on Carl.

beats.headline: The only one still awake
beats.text: Carl jumps into a swimming pool full of dead boss and the boss goes off like a potato in a microwave. I watch him sail over the street spinning like a pinwheel. So I fetch the neighbourhood map, missile two of the last three, set Mongo on the third, jump to the roof and heal Carl with a scroll. I am covered in three inches of guts. Mongo is level 12. We have a new rule: no throwing explosives while blind. And I need a shower before our interview.

beats.headline: The frog in the pot
beats.text: I have had an answer ready for this. All it takes is a little seed. When the host asks about the Skull Empire's unrest I tell the frog story: boiled slowly, it never jumps. If it used to be okay and it isn't any more, do something about it. Kick them out and set up your own. Tucker says advocating sedition is a crime. Then you're all in that same pot. Besides, what are they going to do, throw me in the dungeon? Barely two minutes pass before the shot comes. It was meant for Donut and me.

beats.headline: A seat on the Danger Zone panel
beats.text: Ripper Wonton's panel, and the crawler and his cat are on it. I keep reaching for his hand and my claws keep going straight through his fingers, which does not stop me reaching. Then the Skull Empire fire at those two and hit Manasa instead. My friend. The comedian starts treating her death as a piece of political arithmetic, and I tell him to shut his mouth. The Prism Kingdom condemns the action, and I say so on air within the hour: we will bring a grievance against the Skull Empire in the Syndicate Courts.

beats.headline: His name was Gravy Boat
beats.text: A caller on Danger Zone asks Princess Donut who Ferdinand is. The answer given is the love of her life: a star-crossed ruffian, branded a Moggie, hunted by the authorities, who called to her from outside the window. Carl identifies him as the creepy yellow cat that came to the window when she was in heat. His name was Gravy Boat, and he belonged to Marjory on the first floor. Animal control never managed to catch him. "He preferred Ferdinand," says Donut.

beats.headline: Asked about her husband
beats.text: Carl and the cat are on the panel. One of the Daughters is near them. She recognised the circus and wants to come back to the team, but we are too far. She needs levels. I ask them as a personal favour, and the cat says yes before Carl can. The One-Eyed Narwhal, tonight. Don't blow her up. Then a caller asks why I left my husband to fend for himself. He left me. He was going to get us both killed. Now he is dead and I am not. Do I regret it? Of course I do.

beats.headline: Disowned, then rumoured aboard
beats.text: The Maestro has been stripped of his titles and disowned by his father, amid unrest in the Skull Empire's home systems, and is no longer counted as royalty. When Prince Stalwart's yacht fires on the wrong trailer, the Valtay Corporation claims one of its dreadnoughts in Earth orbit has destroyed that yacht. Stalwart was not aboard. The Queen Consort Ugloo and the former prince are rumoured to have been. Princess Donut asks Carl whether he heard that the Maestro is dead. He did.

beats.headline: A worm in a famous head
beats.text: For the record: Manasa, a silver and black cobra-headed creature whose hood is a meter wide, towers over the Danger Zone table as a hologram. The director Evo's briefing: a famed singer. A Naga, but not of the Blood Sultanate, so Crawler Donut need not kill her on the ninth floor. Not really a Naga either. The real Manasa perished long ago, and she contracted with the Valtay Corporation to keep her career going once she died. A worm in her brain, driving the body? Correct. Her career is hotter than ever. Latest single: eighth in the entire universe.

beats.headline: On the side of the Valtay
beats.text: She laughs at Crawler Donut's put-downs of Tucker, the comedian who is not funny, forked tongue flipping in and out. On the panel's main topic, the Valtay Corporation's attempt to collect its debt from the Borant system, she is, for obvious reasons, on the side of the Valtay. Ripper and Princess D'nadia think both sides are dicks and also side with the Valtay; Tucker mostly backs the kua-tin. The three crawlers are careful to say nothing stupid about either.

beats.headline: The pulse hit her trailer
beats.text: Manasa has been removed from the broadcast. Mid-sentence from the host, her hologram blinks in and out and is gone, and the studio bucks. The report: an attack on her trailer. She was vacationing on Earth and had ascended for the interview, and the trailer was hit with a pulse. Ripper announces that it appears she has perished. Then Prince Stalwart's statement plays, announcing the crawlers Carl and Donut executed by a pulse from his personal yacht. Tucker, no longer snooty: "It was meant for you."

beats.headline: She offered to trade
beats.text: Princess D'nadia explains. The crawlers needed cleaning facilities, and Manasa offered to trade trailers. D'nadia weeps black oil: Manasa was her friend for countless years, worm head or not, and the Prism Kingdom is filing a grievance. Tucker supposes the Valtay must see it as an accident. Ripper: does anyone know how much money she brings the Valtay each year? Their entertainment assets outearn their technology, and they just murdered her. Then word arrives: a Valtay dreadnaught claims Stalwart's yacht; the rumor puts Queen Consort Ugloo and the former prince Maestro aboard.

beats.headline: The statement read out on air
beats.text: Subject is the crown prince, brother to the Maestro, a coarse-haired boar-like creature with lean muscle and a manner that is meant to be read as cruelty and largely succeeds. When his empire fires on a trailer and takes someone who was nobody’s enemy, it is his statement that goes out on air. He recorded it before the shot was fired, with an army drilling in the window behind him, announcing an execution that had not happened and, as it turned out, did not.

beats.headline: Will she leave Carl for Bea
beats.text: A caller in a top hat, Chappy, asks me what happens if Miss Beatrice is alive and shows up. Am I really going to leave Carl for her? The studio has already bucked once tonight, and I was sick all down my front. Now this. When we reunite with Miss Beatrice we will all work together. It will be like before. He seems perplexed and asks Carl, who mumbles something about bridges. Then the host breaks in with news.

beats.headline: Danger Zone, with two new guests
beats.text: Welcome back, folks. On the panel tonight: Princess D'nadia, Manasa, Tucker, Hekla, and the two everybody in this galaxy has been waiting to get in a chair. Tucker opens with a crack about letting a pet sit on the panel, and the cat spends the next half hour taking him apart on air and calling him Butler, and I put my head down on the table so nobody sees me laugh, because it was funny and because he had it coming. Then the barefoot one starts talking about revolution inside the Skull Empire, and when Tucker tries to cut in I tell him to stop and let him finish, because a guest of mine gets to finish a sentence.

beats.headline: The show goes dark
beats.text: And then the Skull Empire answers my guest by firing on a trailer, and they take Manasa, who had swapped trailers with my guests and was nobody's enemy and was not even the target. I hand the room to the audience questions while I find out what happened. Then we come back and I read Prince Stalwart's statement out on air, because that is the job, and then I say what I think of it, because that is also the job. By the time I finish saying it the Valtay have taken his yacht apart, with his mother and his disgraced brother rumoured aboard and Stalwart himself not, and folks, none of this is entertainment any more.

beats.headline: Carl plants a seed on Danger Zone
beats.text: A few minutes of provocation on a chat show, and the Skull Empire answers them with a pulse from Prince Stalwart's yacht. It hits Manasa's trailer instead of Carl's, which was a mistake, and the Valtay answer that in turn by destroying the yacht, with his mother and the Maestro rumoured to be aboard. Three funerals come of it.

beats.headline: A singer with a worm in her head
beats.text: Manasa, the cobra-headed pop star with the eighth-ranked single in the universe, died long ago; she contracted with the Valtay so that one of their parasites could keep her career going, and it is hotter than ever. On the panel she backs the Valtay's attempt to collect their debt from Borant. Then a pulse meant for Carl and Donut hits the trailer she swapped into, and she is gone. Their entertainment assets bring in more than their technology, Ripper says. Then the Valtay claim a dreadnought has destroyed Prince Stalwart's yacht.

beats.headline: The beads rattle
beats.text: Nine city elves are spoiling for a fight, and Carl wants them to make the first move in front of the town guards. On his word Donut lifts her back leg and shakes it, and the anklet's three little beads rattle. The elves come apart. They growl and hiss like a pack of wild animals, the Light Healer claws her own face bloody, the fire mage wets himself and the summoner sucks his thumb. Donut grumbles that she always said wood jewelry was ugly. Salvatore names her the bearer of the forbidden oak, eats an acorn, and begins to glow.

beats.headline: Set up, and the pawns with us
beats.text: Manasa is dead in the trailer we were meant to be in, and I don't trust luck that tidy. Stalwart had his statement ready and the camera pointed at the army outside the window before I opened my mouth. So I say it in chat, never out loud: we were the bait, and so was she. Someone knew the orcs meant to kill us and set up the switch on purpose, or jumped on it. If the Valtay lose an ally, maybe go to war with the Skull Empire, they won't have time to take over the Borant system. Borant benefits. But we have so little information.

beats.headline: I punch a level-75 guard
beats.text: The elves are glowing on acorns when a pregnant fathom dwarf named Eunice lays their leader out with a rolling pin. An Icer freezes her solid, and two level-75 swordsmen lift their blades over her and the boy lying across her. So I punch the nearest one. It is like punching a Sherman tank: I dent it, and it does not stagger. Warning: branded a troublemaker, attacked on sight. Then Mic Drop: a one-armed kid under my arm, a boom jug in the air, Puddle Jumper to a roof across the street. The remaining eight elves are crisped. The temple burns, and the house next door with it.

beats.headline: A dark cleric, in theory
beats.text: The working theory, formed after an attack by shambling berserkers that Crawler Carl assumes were sent by "our Featherfall friend." The town's lead skyfowl is a dark cleric who commands the undead. The city elves of the 201st Security Group worship the skyfowl as living angels, which makes them free, enthusiastic labour for herding his undead minions. Knock out that support network first. Nobody has yet explained the dead women in the alleys.

beats.headline: Tortured for a name
beats.text: Outside the elves' temple, Salvatore of the 201st Security Group explains. They had to torture her to tease the crawlers' name from her lips. GumGum was serving an important purpose, removing the unworthy filth from the streets. Then she started asking questions, and the questions attracted the Oak Fell, just as the Master predicted. "You tortured GumGum?" asks Crawler Donut. Yes, says Salvatore, just as they shall torture the crawlers.

beats.headline: Practically mini nukes
beats.text: From a rooftop near the saferoom, Carl does not want to waste his hob-lobbers on a handful of shambling berserkers, so he tries a stick of hobgoblin dynamite, which he has never used. He hurls it with his upgraded strength at a shambler half a block away. The explosion knocks him off his feet, the front of a distant building caves in and fills the street with debris, and the shambler and the one behind it are obliterated. The power is great, he decides, but the sticks are utterly impractical in regular fights.

beats.headline: Mic drop at the temple door
beats.text: A one-armed dwarf child under one arm, a lit jug in the other hand, a swordsman guard swinging. Crawler Carl tosses the jug straight up, Crawler Donut's Puddle Jumper takes them all to a rooftop across the street, and the jug comes down on the temple entrance. The remaining eight city elves are crisped instantly. The two guards' health bars barely move.

beats.headline: Her final performance
beats.text: Ripper closes the show on a video of Manasa singing, her final performance: a cappella, in an opulent dining room, a hauntingly sad soprano. The studio watches in dead silence. Afterwards Crawler Donut says she was really nice. Over chat, Crawler Carl works it through: the crawlers were the bait, and so was Manasa, and the switch was either arranged or seized upon; it humiliates the orcs and damages their alliance with the Valtay, and his guess is that Borant benefits. Crawler Donut: MANASA HAD THE VOICE OF AN ANGEL. To Mordecai she adds that Manasa thought Mongo was adorable.

beats.headline: Benjamin, twice
beats.text: FOOD. Small lizard on a stick. BAD. Lizard comes back up. Small dwarf hits me. Arm is FOOD, and lizard again. MOTHER says HOLD. Tummy BAD. Small dwarf wants arm back. Give.

beats.headline: New rule: nothing outside the dungeon
beats.text: I distinctly remember saying subtle. The kid calls an orc king a pussy on air, the king's son lasers the wrong trailer from orbit, and the Valtay answer by blowing up the royal yacht. His wife is dead. So, new rule. We do not mention anyone outside this dungeon, not until after the sixth floor, if these two idiots make it that far. Odette asks, they have no opinion. I wanted his people aimed at the Blood Sultanate on the ninth floor. I don't think that's going to be an issue now. What can he do to them in here? Nothing yet. That changes very soon.

beats.headline: Named the Oak Fell
beats.text: The city elves outside a corrupt temple call me a disgusting, vile blasphemer, and I have done nothing. It is the anklet: the Enchanted Anklet of the Fallen Oak, which Carl gave me and which I always said was ugly. I show them my backside, which is award-winning. On Carl's word I shake my back leg, the beads rattle, and they come apart; one of them claws her own face bloody. Then they eat acorns and glow, and their leader announces who I am. Donut, the Oak Fell. The Death Upon Us All. She Who Ends.

beats.headline: Benjamin, on a stick
beats.text: For the record: about fifteen dwarven kids in patched clothes play in the street beside the elves' temple. One of the older ones chases the rest with a small salamander tied to a stick and jabs it at a robed elf; the lizard spits a single spark. Left in the street, it tries to drag itself away, and Mongo swallows it whole with half the stick. It comes back up, dead, in the middle of a standoff. "Benjamin?" asks the young dwarf. Ricky Joe. Level 2. Juvenile Fathom Dwarf.

beats.headline: He punches the raptor
beats.text: His mother, Eunice, level-30 fathom dwarf and enormously pregnant, has been frozen solid by an Icer, and the swordsmen guards raise their blades over her. Crawler Carl punches a guard. At the same moment Ricky Joe punches Mongo in the face: "You killed my best friend!" On the second swing his arm is no longer there. Mongo has bitten it off below the elbow and swallowed it, along with Benjamin, for the second time. Crawler Donut's "Mongo, hold!" saves his life. Carl tucks the bleeding boy under his arm like a football.

beats.headline: Give me my arm back
beats.text: Crawler Donut's Puddle Jumper takes the crawlers and the boy to a rooftop across the street as the boom jug lands below and crisps the remaining eight elves. Crawler Carl shoves a health potion into the squealing boy's mouth. The blood stops, and his health returns to green. His arm does not grow back. He moves to hit the dinosaur again with his left, and Carl holds him back. "Give it back! Give me my arm back!"

beats.headline: He closes with Manasa singing
beats.text: We are out of time and I am not doing a comedy sting tonight. Roll the tape of Manasa singing. All of it. Goodnight, folks.

beats.headline: Booking schedules are public
beats.text: Okay, so. That was terrifying, and I thought Carl and Princess Donut were dead for certain. How did they know which trailer? Rental trailers put their booking schedules out for anybody to see, so everyone can coordinate availability. Nobody has ever needed to hide one, because nobody has ever tried to assassinate a crawler outside the dungeon. Now the Valtay have blown the royal yacht into dust. The good news is that nobody on the net is saying anything negative about Carl and Princess Donut; the prince is the villain. Our team is fielding a wave of interview requests. Odette has the contract on the next one.

beats.headline: They carry her as far as they can
beats.text: A neighbourhood boss and a borough boss with Katia in tow, until the third floor scatters everyone on arrival and she is too far from the rest of them to share in the experience.

beats.headline: Talking to the letter
beats.text: Mordecai works it out. The Mysterious Letter from GumGum's inventory is a spent Suppurating Eye scroll, a lich spell, and the blood on it is the caster's. Out of my inventory, whoever cast it can see and hear what's near it. That's how he answered me with a dead woman on a roof. Donut says we use it. So on a rooftop at night I set it on the tiles and we perform: stuffed animals worth stealing, a filing cabinet to loot, a hole to hammer through the ceiling of the office. Donut overacts. It's too late to fix that. The letter goes back in my pack.

beats.headline: Two Mongos and a bloody letter
beats.text: On a roof across the alley from the magistrate's building, Donut casts it on Mongo and pulls the original back into his carrier. The two copies squeak their disappointment and then do the work. One swallows the Mysterious Letter, which carries a lich's eavesdropping spell, and the pair leap across the alley and up a full story to the magistrate's roof, howling. Anyone listening through the letter should now place the crawlers overhead. Carl had not believed they could jump that far. The real party is crouched a building away when he presses the detonator.

beats.headline: A gear head
beats.text: Katia tells Carl what she can do. She has no useful spells. She is immune to wind spell damage. She is also good at fixing engines, though she was never a mechanic and has never actually fixed one: she got her Earth Hobby Potion, and she is a gear head. Before all this she was an art teacher, which Carl, looking at her poorly sculpted face, finds hard to credit. She smiles sheepishly.

beats.headline: They bite ghosts
beats.text: The alley on the way to the magistrate's roof is full of Shadow Leaks, smoke-like, ghost-class mobs with a stinging cold attack. Carl's magical gauntlet damages them as easily as if they were flesh, and Mongo's magical teeth caps can hurt them too. The ghosts give off an unusually high amount of experience and are easy to kill. Mongo hits level 13 and gets noticeably larger, rising to the height of Carl's chest.

beats.headline: The letter was listening
beats.text: That morning the crawlers stand over a dead woman with "No you won't" carved into her, dropped on their inn the night before moments after Crawler Carl promised revenge for GumGum with her letter in his hand. Mordecai works it out. The Mysterious Letter was likely planted in her inventory for whoever investigated the deaths: a spent necroscript scroll, Suppurating Eye, soaked in the caster's blood. Out of inventory, the caster can see and hear anything near it. Crawler Donut's idea: use it as bait.

beats.headline: She asks them to take her
beats.text: We carried Katia and her friend through a neighbourhood boss and a borough boss, and I would do it again. Then class selection split us, and I run this party on numbers, and Katia's numbers stopped adding up next to anyone she stands beside. I cannot carry that down another set of stairs. So I am the one asking. Carl. Donut. Take her. She is better than she looks right now, and she will hate that I said so.

beats.headline: Three boxes, impact-detonated
beats.text: A stop at the Silk Road with funds running low. Carl picks up three more boxes of hob-lobbers, all of them the impact-detonated version, and Pustule has brought a ten-pack of hobgoblin smoke curtains, round fused bombs that work much better than goblin smoke. Pustule is right about the curtains. That night they fill the air over the rooftops like a heavy fog.

beats.headline: Ten levels behind and nobody's problem
beats.text: I came in with a friend. We fell in with Hekla and Brynhild's Daughters, who carried the two of us through a neighbourhood boss and a borough boss, and I know exactly how much of that was us. Class selection split us up, and she did not wait. Now Hekla is asking Carl and Donut to take me. The system has just upgraded my displayed race from "What the f-word?" to "Human", so things are looking up.

beats.headline: Doppelgänger, Monster Truck Driver
beats.text: Bannon, my guide, talked me into it: a momentum-based constitution tank who can reshape her own mass, body and equipped gear together, into any form of the same weight. I sculpted my face using my reflection in a health potion bottle. Carl says it looks like a Juan Gris. He is being kind, and I would know.

beats.headline: Fuel tank, battering ram, stairwell finder
beats.text: Strength eleven. Intelligence eight, Charisma eight. Dexterity thirty. Constitution fifty-one: fifteen from a ring out of a loot box at the start, more from buffs, more from the class. Second Fuel Tank absorbs damage and reflects some back, once a fight, at random. Rush uses my body as a battering ram, once a thirty-hour day. Pathfinder finds stairwells. I am immune to wind spells. My Earth Hobby Potion made me a gear head, though I have never fixed an engine. I was an art teacher. What is the saying? Those who can't do, teach.

beats.headline: Four from under the building
beats.text: Four of them emerge from underneath the building, where they have been waiting on its unoccupied first floor, and head for the roof where Carl and Donut crouch. The answer is smoke: two hobgoblin smoke curtains, and two clockwork Mongos leaping across the alley with a letter swallowed as bait. The floating heads see the dinosaurs jump before the fog closes and turn after them. Mordecai says the smoke works on these ghosts because they have a physical presence.

beats.headline: A feud, according to the recap
beats.text: The recap has a feud now. The cat, against my dogs, Cici and Gustavo. The cat says she never challenged anybody. The show says she did. Everybody watching heard the show. I know which one I am going to listen to.

beats.headline: Dynamite in the shelves
beats.text: They did not come back. They did not need to. The human fixed my shelf for me, the day he threw a dead woman across my desk, while I was on the floor gathering my figures, and I did not so much as look up. The shelves are hollow. Three sticks of hobgoblin dynamite and a detonator are sitting inside the second one now, under my figures, which is the one place nobody ever looks, because nobody but me has ever cared what stands on that shelf.

beats.headline: Pony-sized
beats.text: Cold ghosts. Bite! Level thirteen. BIG now. MOTHER on my back! Jump! Jump! MOTHER falls off. MOTHER angry.

beats.headline: What the newsletter does not say
beats.text: I talk Fitz into showing me his herb stash and steal his newsletter. Borant is warning shopkeepers and pub owners to be extra careful not to anger crawlers. It doesn't say why. I can read between the lines. Some of you are getting stronger than you should; the kid who trashed the Desperado Club is proof. Borant controls the mobs and most of the experience. The System AI controls most of the loot boxes, it is still the ultimate arbiter, and it is evening the odds against the shorter floors. These elaborate quests are the same symptom. Keep the new girl alive. If she dies, get those rings off her.

beats.headline: A spy camera in blood
beats.text: Mordecai has worked the letter out. Carl swore, in a safe room, to hunt down whoever killed GumGum, and within moments a dead woman was dropped on the building with No you won't carved into her. He had been clutching the letter as he said it. It is a used necroscript scroll of Suppurating Eye, a common lich spell: the caster leaks a bodily fluid onto a surface and can see and hear anything near it, and he thinks the blood on this one is the caster's. It does not work from inside an inventory. Donut wants to use it, so on a rooftop she and Carl talk for whoever is listening.

beats.headline: Swallowed whole
beats.text: Donut splits Mongo into three and pulls the real one back into his carrier, and Carl sets two lit smoke curtains billowing over the rooftops. Then he pulls the letter out. We're jumping onto the roof now, he says, crumples it up and tosses it in the air. One of the clockwork Mongos grabs it and swallows it whole, and the pair leap across the alley and a full story up to the top of the magistrate's building, one of them howling into the night.

beats.headline: Since when can the news lie
beats.text: The recap puts me against Cici and Gustavo 3 with a lightning bolt between us, as though I had thrown down a gauntlet at Lucia Mar's dogs. I have done no such thing. They play me at the bar, being rude about rottweilers, which was a remark and not a challenge. Then the girl herself, with bugs crawling in her eye sockets, says she will find me in the dungeon and her dogs will tear me apart. Carl, since when is the news allowed to lie? We would kill them easily, of course. I simply do not want those ugly skulls after my name.

beats.headline: Ten smoke curtains, as promised
beats.text: She came through. Three more boxes of hob-lobbers, all impact-detonated, and a ten-pack of hobgoblin smoke curtains, round fused bombs meant to outperform the goblin kind. Crawler Carl buys all ten. That night, on a rooftop beside the magistrate's building, one of them fills the whole area like a heavy fog, far better than the goblin kind. Pustule had been correct.

beats.headline: Benjamin was in training
beats.text: He sits cross-legged on the roof, clutching his severed limb and Benjamin's twice-eaten corpse. He screamed bloody murder on learning the arm could not be reattached, and Crawler Donut talked him down. Told that tying a lizard to a stick is not cool: at least he did not eat him, and Benjamin liked it. Fathom dwarves strap them to their hats when they go into mines. He was in training. The boy's own home, attached to the temple, has burned to the ground.

beats.headline: The skyfowl lady
beats.text: Asked about the temple: the elves were always weird. One cried for his mama every morning, through the walls. His brother Bubba Lane saw something fly from the roof a couple of nights ago, probably just that skyfowl lady. She visits a lot, just before dark, and leaves with a bunch of other ladies, elves and dwarves and humans, dressed like they are going to the Desperado. Where she takes them he does not know. They are not allowed past the street.

beats.headline: In charge of the left leg
beats.text: Crawler Carl carries the protesting boy down the rope under his arm and drops him the last ten feet. He belly-flops, loses his grip on the arm and the salamander, and wails. His health has barely blipped. "Walk it off, kid." A scream from the building next door: "That's me mom." She is in labor again, and she is going to be really mad if he misses it. He is in charge of holding her left leg. "Bye, Princess Donut! Bye Mongo!"

beats.headline: Healing would undo her
beats.text: The magistrate's building is coming apart when one of the burnt, headless corpses flickers from X to red to white. Her head has magically returned to her body, and the system calls her human. The lower half of her is char. The eyes identify her: Burgundy, from the stairs. Crawler Carl pulls a healing potion. No: healing her would heal her body, and she would turn into one of those things again. She is cursed. The kindest thing is to kill her while she is still mortal. "Hurry. Please. It hurts."

beats.headline: The job at the club
beats.text: A person by day and one of those things at night, she confirms. The elves brought her from another settlement with a promise of work at the Desperado Club. Everyone knows a job there is a chance to descend: to the Hunting Grounds, then maybe deeper, where it is safe. It was all a lie. Asked whether she was a prostitute: yes, and if they do not like it, fuck off. She has stabbed men for less. Crawler Donut's torch keeps the curse back, and she can feel it fading.

beats.headline: Her husband, across the street
beats.text: Featherfall did not do this. He hangs on that thing, dead before she arrived, turned into a dark fetish that keeps their bodies safe at night. Miss Quill is the real magistrate. Quill took Burgundy from the temple to her husband, Remex, across the street above where the guards sleep: not alive, not dead, casting a big spell to bring himself fully back. By day the women work in the building and the shops below, plucking a feather from every skyfowl or chickadee customer for Quill. At night they are his army.

beats.headline: The ones who do not turn
beats.text: The women in the alleys, she says, are those whose sins are not enough. They came to work at the Desperado Club, and when Remex twists them they do not always turn. Sometimes they simply die. Then the survivors are allowed to feed on them, and one of his avatars drops them in the alleys, within a few blocks of his lair. The avatars are his limbs, but they cannot go far. Not yet.

beats.headline: Before the floor goes
beats.text: Final entry for Burgundy, magistrate's assistant, whom the system filed as human. The room slumps forward and her body begins to slide away as the roof above her caves in. "Kill me, please!" Crawler Princess Donut hits her with a Magic Missile in the moments before the body disappears into the collapse. She had asked for exactly that twice, while the torch still held her curse back and she was mortal.

beats.headline: Magistrate of a town that ignores me
beats.text: Three achievements scroll by after the blast. Assassin, for a ranking town official. Ultimate Extreme Power, a Platinum Tyrant's Box, and control of the whole settlement. CockBlock, for killing an NPC another crawler needed. My title goes from Royal Bodyguard to Magistrate Carl, until the floor collapses. I don't laugh. The quest is still sitting in my menu, which means we may have just killed the wrong bird. Two of the town's bird people hover over the roof and I tell them I'm on magistrate business. They tell me, less politely, to go back to the Desperado.

beats.headline: Fireball, for once
beats.text: The muted room fills with krasue peeling their heads free, trailing organs; one slaps me in the face with a still-beating heart. We back out into the smoke of the living room and I pull the Fireball or Custard lotto ticket. Last time it cast custard. I scratch it expecting custard again. Fireball. Spicy! It rolls through the doorway, shatters the jamb on both sides and goes off against Featherfall's corpse in its hoop of bone. The floor buckles. The room turns to Xs and half drops to the level below. The red dots circling Donut on the roof all disappear.

beats.headline: The bait is a job at the club
beats.text: Burgundy worked in another settlement until city elves told her she could get a job at the Desperado Club, which had an entrance in this town. Everyone knows, she says, that working at the club brings a chance to descend, and maybe deeper, where it's safe. It was all a lie. Women who come to work at the club are the ones brought to Remex.

beats.headline: In a muted zone
beats.text: Donut finds the area muted and cannot cast. Mordecai explains: in a muted zone, spells from the menu and scrolls won't cast, but magical items, potions and spells already cast still work. Mongo has those magical teeth caps. Go bite that elf's head off, Carl tells him, but be quick, and Donut says sic 'em. The dinosaur weaves in, turns his head sideways like he is eating a taco, and chomps down. The dark elf's head caves in under the bite, and the purple swirls of magic blink off.

beats.headline: Credited with his death
beats.text: Dynamite through the magistrate's floor. The notices arrive: a public official assassinated, control of the Medium Skyfowl Settlement, a new title, Magistrate Carl. The only NPC the notices name is Miss Quill, and a bronze boss box says one of the two was a neighbourhood boss. But the quest is still open, which should mean the head bad guy is still alive. Crawler Carl's conclusion: they killed an NPC they never met, blew his house to bits, and still have not finished the job.

beats.headline: Upside down in a bone dreamcatcher
beats.text: Found in the magistrate's quarters, at the centre of a room of krasue bodies hanging from the ceiling: Magistrate Featherfall, naked and emaciated, lashed upside down in a massive dreamcatcher of bone, featherless wings spread, a clear fluid dripping from beak and eyes. He had been there some time; the body was being mummified. Lootable Corpse. Former Magistrate Featherfall. Dark Cleric. Level 32. A fireball scatters his ashes. No neighbourhood map turns up in them, so by Crawler Carl's reckoning he was not the boss.

beats.headline: A dark fetish, by her account
beats.text: A dying krasue woman, mortal while Crawler Donut's torch holds the curse back, sets the record straight. Featherfall was not the one who did this. He has been hanging on that thing the whole time, and he was dead when she arrived. His body was turned into a dark fetish that keeps their bodies safe at night. Miss Quill has been running the city all along. She is the real magistrate.

beats.headline: Then a fireball
beats.text: Krasue fill a smoking apartment and Donut is on the roof above with red dots circling her. Carl yanks the ticket, fully expecting custard again, and cries fire in the hole. Fireball. Spicy! An egg-shaped ball of fire the size of an opened umbrella rolls through the bedroom door, shattering the jamb, and detonates against the upside-down corpse of Featherfall. The building rocks, the floor buckles and the room half collapses to the level below. The red dots harassing Donut all disappear, and Carl thinks they fried Featherfall's loot.

beats.headline: A meat locker of women
beats.text: The magistrate's bedroom is a meat locker: naked female corpses hanging upside down by the ankles. The headless ones show on the map as corpses. Thirty or more still have heads, dangling six inches below the neck, with purple energy swirling around them. Mongo's magical teeth bite through several heads. Then the rest wake up, wailing, working their heads loose, and flock through the smoke-filled room slapping at Carl with trailing organs. A lotto-ticket fireball finishes the room.

beats.headline: What Burgundy says she is
beats.text: One burned body turns back into a woman, and she explains. By day they live and work in the building as assistants and in the shops below, plucking a feather from every skyfowl who comes in for Miss Quill. At night they are his army. The women found in the alleys came to work at the Desperado Club; when Remex twists them they do not always turn, and the ones who die are fed upon, then dropped nearby by his avatars. She asks to be killed while still mortal.

beats.headline: The administrative building, and everything in it
beats.text: Miss Quill is dead. The reception office came apart with her in it, and the shelf, and every figure on it. Magistrate Featherfall, credited dead in the same blast, had been hanging mummified in a dreamcatcher of bone in the rooms behind for a long time before any of this. The barefoot man is magistrate of this settlement now, which is what happens when nobody checks the paperwork. He collects one achievement for assassinating a public official and a second for killing an NPC another crawler needed for a quest. The achievement declines to say whose, or what the quest was. She kept that door for a very long time and not one crawler ever thought to ask her why.

beats.headline: Hanging ladies
beats.text: Hanging ladies. Heads FOOD. Crunch. Crunch. Crunch. One head NOT THERE. Bite legs instead. MOTHER says RETURN. Ladies wake up. Screaming. More FOOD.

beats.headline: She asked me to
beats.text: The burnt woman is Burgundy, from the stairs, one of the magistrate's assistants, and one of those things: a person by day, a krasue at night. Carl wants to heal her. She says healing will only turn her back, and to kill her while she is still mortal. So I stroke her hair and tell her it is going to be okay, sweetie, and ask about Featherfall. She tells us Miss Quill ran the city all along, and about a husband named Remex across the street. Then the room slumps and she slides away, begging. I hit her with a Magic Missile before she is gone.

beats.headline: A survivor gives up his name
beats.text: A woman called Burgundy, one of the Krasue, lies burned to charcoal from the waist down in a building that is coming apart, and she has given two crawlers my name and told them where I am kept. Her husband, she called me: not alive, not dead, something monstrous. Accurate, as far as it goes, and it does not go far. Nobody has had cause to say my name aloud in a very long time. I know what that means. I have known what it would mean since the day I was pulled back.

beats.headline: It hurts ghosts
beats.text: The third floor's ghost-class mobs can only be injured by magic or magical items, and the gauntlet counts. Outside the magistrate's building it damages a swarm of stinging, cold-attacking ghosts as easily as if they were flesh; they give off an unusually high amount of experience. Inside the krasue nest, Carl punches a flying head as he rushes past, and the magical gauntlet connects with a wet splat. Mongo's magical teeth caps can hurt them too.

beats.headline: Kept out of sight
beats.text: A single crawler stands in the crowd watching the municipal building fall, and Carl whispers to Donut not to let him see the fallen oak bracelet on her back leg. It is Daniel Bautista, the man who killed the Divider in the swimming pool, and Carl takes him for family of the three dead women they found days ago. Donut picked up the anklet off them. If the man knew, would he want it back? Too bad for him if he did. Carl decides it is best not to broach the subject at all.

beats.headline: He thanks the two who took his revenge
beats.text: My sisters and a cousin, five of them, went in seconds to Former Circus Lemurs; I was with my other cousin, and we barely got away. He gave up, and the next day he was gone. Now I walk out of the crowd to find the lemurs already dead by somebody else's hand, and the secretary I had a quest to kill dead by the same hand, and none of it mine. So I swear a debt to a cat and a man with no shoes, give them my chat contact, and point them at a stairwell three kilometres east. Then I ask the man the question I cannot answer for myself: how can we make it to heaven if God does not recognise us?

beats.headline: A forester
beats.text: Donut asks what I'd do if I could do anything. Not fixing boats. Not the Navy, either; it was the Coast Guard, whatever Bea told people. I think of the college applications I started and never finished. The forestry service, as a forester. I've seen enough ocean to last a lifetime. I'd be happy alone in the woods, watching for forest fires. She says she and Zev will be a television writing team, Gossip Girl with an intergalactic slant, and maybe if the shows are good enough people won't be so interested in watching real people kill each other. You surprise me every day, Donut.

beats.headline: Ten sticks, one button
beats.text: The tenth and last stick of goblin dynamite goes on an exposed joist outside the building where the lich waits, fixed with a sticky detonator charge. One stick of hobgoblin pus allows up to ten simultaneous detonations with a single press. Carl hands Katia a pencil-like detonator and makes her keep it in her inventory: if they die, or if he says so, she presses the button. No questions.

beats.headline: Holding the boom switch
beats.text: My face is better now. Carl calls me out of the crowd and puts a pencil-like detonator in my hand, and I back away from it; the description says it might click on its own. Keep it in your inventory, he says. If they die, or if he says so, press the button. They need someone outside the lich's influence holding it. Mutually assured destruction, then. Hekla warned me that he was crazy. Then he tells the crowd they are all still in the blast zone, and I back up with the rest of them.

beats.headline: Rescued from the rubble
beats.text: Recovered from the debris of Miss Quill's building, which is falling in at the time. One of her glass cases, charred and half-buried less than a foot from the explosion, and not broken, so likely enchanted. The char rubs off. Inside is a plush: an armoured man atop a black horse. The tag says Kimaris. Crawler Carl pulls the whole thing into his inventory and runs, and the rest of the building caves in behind him.

beats.headline: Liches never shut up
beats.text: Liches come in all shapes and power levels. But they all have one thing in common. They are just like Odette: they never, ever shut the hell up. Narcissists, and cowards, who will do anything not to let go of the life they have grabbed back, so they always have minions and grandiose plans. I said blow the building and take a chance on losing the quest. Then they killed most of his support, and I changed my mind: he'll be weak. One more wrinkle. The last one was a neighbourhood boss. I'd bet my left nipple this is a borough boss. Come prepared.

beats.headline: Best not mentioned
beats.text: In the crowd outside the fallen municipal building, Carl recognises a crawler he takes for family of Grace, Nica and Lea, the three dead women they came across several days earlier. Someone with them had looted most of their gear. Donut picked up the anklet, and Carl took the two generic strength rings. If the man knew they had them, would he want them back? That would be too bad for him. Carl figures it is best not to broach the subject at all.

beats.headline: He promised I would not die alone
beats.text: Carl's plan is to ring the warehouse with dynamite and go up alone to meet the lich while I wait outside. Absolutely not. He promised me I would not die alone, and he cannot keep that promise if he dies before me. We do this together. So the plan changes, and Katia gets the button. I tell him at the bottom of the ladder that I do not like this plan. Mongo stays in his carrier; he has proven he cannot be trusted to stay still. I ride up on Carl's shoulder.

beats.headline: They take him for a lich
beats.text: They come across the floor towards me with the cat out in front and a fuse somewhere behind, and they have decided that I am a lich, that I am the borough boss, and that finishing me finishes their quest. I am no lich. I am no boss. I am a level one bird with no feathers left and a nick in the plane between the living and the dead, and if they lay a hand on me their souls come out through the scratch and go into the tank, and I have no way on this earth to give them back.

beats.headline: A point in the ceiling
beats.text: Through the open door of the warehouse's first level, even in the dark, Carl can see the inactive Swordsmen guards: hundreds of them in silent formation, like the terracotta army, with no dots over them on his map. A yellow aura swirls round their metallic bodies, and all of it leads to a point in the ceiling. There would be a soul crystal up there somewhere. At night, Mordecai says, the guards are in stasis and invulnerable, so locking them in and blowing them up over and over is out.

beats.headline: A case for the gem
beats.text: The epicentre is the gem, not Remex, and I have one thing that might hold it: the glass case Miss Quill's Kimaris came in. It protects against most, not all, forms of abuse, and every opening carries a 1.5% chance of blasting you with fire, which I read after opening it. I close it around the floating gem without letting my hands touch it, hook the latch, and try to pull it into my inventory. Yeah. Nice try, asshole. So I let go, and it hangs there around the gem, the cracks spreading, two and a half minutes on the clock.

beats.headline: Killed by the feedback
beats.text: Remex, Soul Leech Capacitor, tells it as a story he has rehearsed. Featherfall never liked the guards and wanted more control over them; after Remex retired and handed him the perch, he asked what it would take. After Remex died, Featherfall asked Quill to help cast a spell that would pull a dark cleric back from the dim as a capacitor. He took the Night Votive position with Quill in the room, too close to the amplifier. The feedback killed him. Quill planned it. She kept his office running with a forgery spell.

beats.headline: Somebody did notice
beats.text: Remex explains why the women were brought in from out of town: the raw materials came from elsewhere, so nobody would notice his wife collecting them. Crawler Donut corrects him. "Somebody did notice. Gumgum noticed." For the record, the one who noticed asked two crawlers for help at a pub table, and was told to fuck off.

beats.headline: She spends a death sentence saving NPCs
beats.text: The Fools Who Broke the Glass quest is close to unsurvivable, and it triggers before I have earned my place. I spend the time getting NPCs out. I tell Carl and Donut to save themselves. I mean it.

beats.headline: Out of the case
beats.text: Sorted by value, the stuffed horse-riding soldier is the top item in Crawler Carl's inventory, and its glass carrier is the second. The case is a Sheol Glass Reaper Case. It protects against most forms of abuse, and carries a 1.5% chance of Sheol Fire every time it is opened, which Carl reads after opening it. He takes Kimaris out and keeps the case, closes it around a soul gem that is about to flatten the neighbourhood, and sits down to watch.

beats.headline: Easy to make, easy to control
beats.text: Remex gives the reasons, in his wandering way. His wife needed help the city elves could not give. The krasue are easy to control and easy to make with the correct materials; they fly, and they are intact and compliant during the day. Making them creates a powerful spike of soul power for him. And since the raw materials come from out of town, nobody would notice she was collecting them. Donut corrects him: GumGum noticed. They were to be her lieutenants, her eyes and ears for the battle.

beats.headline: Correction to the file
beats.text: Remex tells them the rest of it, there being nobody left to stop him. She was not guarding the magistrate. She was guarding what she had done to her own husband: let Featherfall drag him back into the world as a soul leech, knowing the feedback would kill Featherfall, and kept him above the swordsmen's warehouse as her capacitor, feeding off the soul crystal, so that she would have the mana for a working called The Final War. The devotion to the figures was real. The refusals at that desk were real. Both of them were also the cover, and I filed her as an obstructive minor official for the whole of the season.

beats.headline: A bereft minion, then run
beats.text: Not a lich, he says. No. A bereft minion: one still alive after its controller is dead. You killed the head bad guy when you blew up Miss Quill. Quests sometimes look bigger than they are; I should have known, it was only a silver quest. Sorry about the dynamite. Get the story, put him down, get out before the swordsmen wake. Then the quest drops. Run for the Desperado Club; the second room is out of the blast. Protective Shell won't work, it's magical. Break the gem? Probably makes it blow early. It's called The Fools Who Broke the Glass for a reason.

beats.headline: I know she's dead
beats.text: Carl says we can save ourselves, or try for Katia and eighty other people with an idea that probably won't work. I don't know. Then I do: we try, because it is the right thing. We sit and watch a glass case float round a cracking gem while Remex tells his son he is coming. Carl says Remex was a crawler once. I do not want to become an NPC. Carl says he is proud of me for worrying about Katia; I tell him I just don't want Hekla mad at us. Then I tell him I am not as dumb as I pretend. I know she's dead.

beats.headline: Soul Leech Capacitor
beats.text: You asked before you detonated anything, which is more than most would do, so here is the story. A Soul Leech Capacitor is what a necromancer builds when what they want is a battery with a face. The spell reaches for the soul the target loved best and drags that soul back into the world, tied to them for good. Featherfall cast it, wanting power over the swordsmen, with my wife in the room to help, and the feedback killed him, which is exactly what she had planned. Since then the power of this town's soul crystal has run through me, and she has been spending it, and what she is spending it on is a working called The Final War. I agreed to none of it. I would like that written down somewhere.

beats.headline: Opened, then read
beats.text: Sorted by value, the top item in Carl's inventory is Miss Quill's stuffed horse-riding soldier, Kimaris, and the second is the glass case it is stored in. The little door isn't locked, just a hinged flap held by a cheap-looking hook and eyebolt. Carl opens it, pulls the plush into his inventory, and only then reads the case: forged in Sheol, sold by Spider Reaper Minions, a 1.5 percent chance of Sheol Fire every time it opens. He should have read that first. He remembers a flash of light when they landed in the debris, and decides the System brought the case to his attention on purpose.

beats.headline: Like catching a firefly
beats.text: Four and a half minutes are left on the soul gem's red timer. Careful not to touch it, Carl closes the case round the floating gem like catching a firefly in his two hands, shuts the door and hooks it closed. He tries to pull the whole thing into his inventory and gets an error. He lets go. The case drops a couple of inches, clinks against the gem and floats there with it, while cracks form along the gem's edge. Most forms of abuse, the description said. He sits down on the floor, and Donut jumps into his lap to watch.

beats.headline: The Amplifier
beats.text: In the room above the warehouse a golf-ball-sized amber jewel floats, tethered to Remex's chest by a thread of golden light, a stalk of light running down through the floor. Carl examines it: a C-grade soul crystal that charges the swordsmen each night and shatters if living flesh touches it. With Miss Quill gone, Remex says, there is no siphon tonight. The roof is the antennae, he explains, and the soul crystal stores the power: that is the Amplifier. The map puts the gem at the epicentre of the coming blast. Breaking it, Mordecai thinks, would only make it blow early. A red timer appears over it.

beats.headline: The Fools Who Broke the Glass
beats.text: Am I glad you asked. A while back an NPC started a spell so potent it had to be finished by a future generation, and old spells are like trees: they grow, and when they get screwed up, the bigger the spell, the worse it goes. I was looking forward to this one going off. Oh well. Every bird-folk NPC in the area is falling ill, being tied to it. Every crawler within forty-five square kilometres gets the quest: don't die. Not your fault, unless you are Carl, Princess Donut or Katia Grim. Sixty seconds to reach a saferoom. Seven minutes to the explosion. Run.

beats.headline: I told you it was here
beats.text: I told them there was a stairwell three kilometres due east of the village. Now the whole district is running for it, and I jog up with a new group behind me while the timers run down. I told you it was here, I say. The man with no shoes, in nothing tonight but a jacket, claps me on the shoulder. I nod to him, and I am the first of us down the stairs to the fourth floor.

beats.headline: Naked, running east
beats.text: Mordecai says every magical item off, now. Everything I wear is magical except the jacket, underwear included, so it all goes into my inventory. I post the two ways out in the quest chat, and three crawlers answer the same way: the back room at the Desperado Club disappeared when the saferooms closed. That leaves the stairwell three kilometres east. Katia jogs up with a handful of strangers. Magical gear off, I tell them; sixteen minutes, full speed. One of them finally asks why I'm naked. I point east. Go.

beats.headline: Congratulations, unanswered
beats.text: Mordecai is in his room, safe. He'll sit and twiddle his thumbs for three days; we won't notice the difference. The guards came back on the second burst with a single life point each, and he'd have me killing them if I were there. Then I tell him congratulations. He doesn't answer. Donut works it out: we make the fourth floor, and he gets to go home once the dungeon is over. I think of Remex, about to finish his duty too. Of Signet, Quint, Pustule, GumGum, Miss Quill, and little one-armed Ricky Joe. I wonder if his mom ever had her baby.

beats.headline: Built in the middle of a collapse
beats.text: During the Fools Who Broke the Glass, Carl drops a Sheol Glass Reaper Case around a Soul Crystal that is already going up and pulls the result into his inventory. Status: Explosion Imminent. "This item can no longer be stabilized."

beats.headline: Forty-five square kilometres
beats.text: Enough to take a city and every suburb around it. It can no longer be stabilized, and the moment it leaves his inventory it goes off, with less than a second to spare. "Created by a man who murders babies and steals rare collectibles from his elders."

beats.headline: Destroying it does not help
beats.text: The crown crumbles to dust in the Over City's collapse, taken by one of the pulses that strip magic from whatever is still being worn. The succession survives it.

beats.headline: Destroyed, and it changes nothing
beats.text: The third pulse of the blast destroys any armour still equipped, and the crown crumbles to dust on her head as she agrees to take it off. The succession is untouched. It said as much on the label.

beats.headline: Through the wall
beats.text: The fourth pulse fires the first things in everyone's hotlist, and for me that is Rush. I glow, clip Carl on the way past, and go straight through the wall of the building with the stairwell in it. That really hurt. At the bottom of the stairs Carl has me take out the detonator. It has a ten-second delay; press it at about fifteen. Won't that make the bomb go off faster? By a couple of seconds, he says, and it probably died in the first burst anyway, but if it works we all share the experience. I press it at twenty.

beats.headline: It was my first item
beats.text: Carl wants the tiara off. I will lose five Intelligence, and my Sepsis debuff, and I really like it. And if I lose it somebody else gets it and we will have to fight them, and I do not want to hurt a person. But a man's arrows have just gone off in his quiver, and Carl says it might set my head on fire, and Katia says he is right. Oh, all right. It crumbles into dust before I can take it off. At the door I point out that Carl should have put his pants back on before we go straight to Odette's show.

beats.headline: On the way down
beats.text: On the stairs off the third floor, Crawler Carl runs through everyone they met there. Signet the half-naiad. Quint, the possum-faced pharmacist. Pustule, the hobgoblin explosives dealer. GumGum the orc. Miss Quill. Little Ricky Joe, the one-armed child dwarf. A week on that floor, and it felt like a millennium.

beats.headline: Four shocks, and a town coming apart
beats.text: Remex is finished. He began to convulse and the settlement went with him: a foreshock that stripped the enchantments off every piece of gear in the district, a second that set weapons off where they hung, a third that took the Enchanted Crown of the Sepsis Whore apart, and a fourth that reached into every crawler's hotlist and set off the first two things on it. Ranger Conrad E's arrows went off in his quiver and took him with them. For the record: he asked them not to come closer, he told them the whole story, and he was the most honest thing in that town.

beats.headline: Whether the baby came
beats.text: On the stairs down, Crawler Carl runs through everyone they met on this floor. Among them, little Ricky Joe, the one-armed child dwarf, whose word that a female skyfowl was visiting the city elves had first made Carl suspect Miss Quill. He wonders whether the boy's mom ever had her baby.

beats.headline: A part in a bomb
beats.text: The word arrives the way most of the dungeon's cosmology does: buried in an item description. A Sheol Glass Reaper Case is half of what makes an explosion large enough to rattle the teeth of a god. The case's own description says it was forged in the fires of Sheol, the mysterious fifteenth level of the World Dungeon, and nobody asks what that means.

beats.headline: A caged sun
beats.text: Remex's scream jolts Carl's eyes open. They are not dead. The case has fallen to the floor, glowing red hot, light streaming from it like a miniature, caged sun, and the floorboards are bubbling. Case and gem have transformed themselves. Carl reads Status: Explosion Imminent in the two seconds before he grabs it, and pulls it into his inventory as the skin burns off his fingers. The new item is Carl's Doomsday Scenario, created by combining a massively overloaded soul crystal and a Sheol Glass Reaper Case.

beats.headline: Half of a bomb
beats.text: The explosion goes off silently inside the glass case Carl closed round the gem. Light streams from the container like a miniature, caged sun, one lance-like ray straight into Remex's chest, and the floorboards bubble and burn. The case and the gem have transformed. Carl reads Status: Explosion Imminent in the two seconds before he grabs it and pulls it into his inventory, burning the skin off his fingers. It is Carl's Doomsday Scenario now, created by combining a massively overloaded soul crystal and a Sheol Glass Reaper Case.

beats.headline: Mind the gap
beats.text: This one sits three kilometres east of the settlement in a small, decrepit building, and with the saferooms shut and the Desperado Club's back room sealed, it is the only way out of the blast. Crawlers have been leaving notes in the bars with stairwell locations. A floor ends for whoever goes down the moment they pull the handle at the bottom. The door there carries the usual oversized carving, and its properties read: Entrance to the fourth floor. This is where the real fun begins. Mind the gap.

beats.headline: It burns a veto rather than pay
beats.text: Eighty-three Celestial boxes are owed. Borant appeals, a Syndicate court overrules it, and it burns its one seasonal veto to void the prizes anyway, which has never been done this early. It is still liable for the one box that was opened before the appeal. A production company that cheap has seams worth looking for.

beats.headline: All about progression and training
beats.text: Odette runs the footage of me crossing the city in a one-armed leather jacket and nothing else while I sit on her couch in a loincloth of toilet paper. Then she explains how we were robbed: a Syndicate court said pay us, and Borant burned its one veto of the season so it wouldn't. I laugh. It doesn't matter how hard we work, we keep getting screwed. We messed up chasing quests when we should have been grinding, and we're not going to make that mistake again. It's all about progression and training. The explosion still counts: I go from twenty-one to twenty-seven.

beats.headline: Tenth on the board
beats.text: Tenth on the draft leaderboard, spelled Elle McGib: Frost Maiden, Blizzardmancer, level thirteen, bounty one hundred thousand. She began the third floor at level one. Carl knows her as a wheelchair-bound resident of Meadow Lark and cannot work out how she got there; he has not talked to Brandon in several days.

beats.headline: Fourth on the board
beats.text: They put the leaderboard up tonight and I am on it. Fourth. Crocodilian, Shotgun Messenger, level twenty-four, three hundred thousand. I don't know what they showed to get me there. I wasn't doing anything I would call footage. I would have preferred to stay a name nobody had learned yet. Too late for that.

beats.headline: Second on the board
beats.text: Second on the draft leaderboard: Hekla, Amazonian, Shieldmaiden, level twenty-eight, a bounty of five hundred thousand, behind only Lucia Mar. Odette, who has watched her some, has her parted from her guide, and fixed on bringing Princess Donut into Brynhild's Daughters. Not for the cat's sake. The cat comes with a permanent manager, and Hekla knows about Mordecai because Katia told her.

beats.headline: Eighth on the board
beats.text: The board does the introductions this dungeon never bothers with. Ifechi is eighth: human, a Physicker, level eighteen. Healing is a class down here and a liability at the same time, since the one thing nobody in this place will let you do is keep other people alive. Note it and move on. The audience already has.

beats.headline: This is the real me
beats.text: We come through the door into a green room that seems to be on a boat. Donut says I am getting really good at the sculpting. I touch my face. This is the real me: short black hair, the face I came in with. On Odette's couch I am brought out as the newest member of the Royal Court of Princess Donut, and I answer her questions one word at a time. Then she puts our levels up over our heads. I have gone from nine to twenty-one.

beats.headline: Ninth on the board
beats.text: Ninth on the draft leaderboard: Li Jun, human, Street Monk, level twenty-five, bounty one hundred thousand. Carl remembers him from the Maestro's show, the one he helped save from the troglodytes and brindle grubs, and is glad to see him there. He hopes Zhang and the others are doing well too.

beats.headline: The top tiers cost the house real money
beats.text: Borant owes the Syndicate tax on every non-sponsored box it hands out: a handful of free Celestials a season, and a steeper bill for each one after that. In the whole history of the show only 2,145 Celestial boxes have been awarded, and no crawler has had more than four. The previous record for one season was eighteen, in a Naga season long ago.

beats.headline: Eighty-three Celestials, and one veto
beats.text: A quest reward gets double-upgraded to Celestial for 83 crawlers. Borant burns its single seasonal veto to void them and is a moment too slow — Quan Ch has already opened his, which leaves the company liable and in a Syndicate court. The upgrade achievements responsible are patched out immediately.

beats.headline: First on the board
beats.text: First on the draft leaderboard, and by a distance: Lucia Mar, Lajabless, Black Inquisitor General, level twenty-nine, bounty one million, twice the next name down. Odette explains afterwards that the number is what other crawlers get for killing her. Princess Donut calls her ugly on air, and the audience laughs.

beats.headline: The season that lost money
beats.text: By Odette's account, more than 250 cycles ago the Blood Sultanate of the Naga ran the first crawl ever to lose money, and they are still recovering. That season also handed out eighteen Celestial boxes, the most in any one season before this crawl, and was cursed for other reasons she declines to get into. The Nagas have not run a season since. They keep a standing place only because they bought a permanent spot early on.

beats.headline: Why I warn Carl about Hekla
beats.text: Lexis takes the new girl out, and Carl sends the Princess after her, because this is for him. Hekla is not evil, or psychotic like Lucia Mar. She is practical and cunning, and she does not have his sense of what is just, which makes her dangerous. She wants Donut in her party, because Mordecai comes with Donut, and a permanent manager is worth having. Donut would never leave him, not as long as he is alive. Why tell him? I bought their rights early, when they were cheap. If he dies and Donut joins Brynhild's Daughters, my contract is void. And those numbers on the board are bounties.

beats.headline: A war god and a sponsorship
beats.text: Be careful with that gauntlet, Carl. Used against a war god's celebrants, it can summon the god himself, and his celebrants start appearing on this next floor. The Skull Empire has just spent a lot of money on a deity sponsorship, which they don't usually buy, so it may be an attempt to get to you. I don't know which god. If I were still a gambler, I would bet on that one. Can he reach you if you don't summon him? Probably not, not on this floor. Ask Mordecai how that works. He has a lot of experience in the subject, unfortunately.

beats.headline: An iron paw
beats.text: Odette shows a crawler dragging himself into a saferoom, the same one who was so rude to us in the quest chat. I am glad he survived; I felt kind of bad, because I blocked him. You cannot let people in your chatrooms get out of control. Then Quan Ch opens a Celestial box that he got for our hard work, and we get nothing, not even a Platinum. This is an outrage. Then the leaderboard: Carl sixth, me seventh, dear Hekla second, and that ugly Lucia Mar first. We are in the top ten!

beats.headline: He opens his before the veto lands
beats.text: Eighty-three crawlers are owed Celestial boxes at the close of this floor. Borant appeals the ruling and loses, appeals the prizes and loses again, and then burns its one seasonal veto here, voiding the lot. It is a fraction too slow. Crawler Quan Ch's box is already open, and you cannot un-open a Celestial box, not even with a veto. So the count comes to one: a level fifteen trooper in a glowing robe that lifts him off the ground. The veto was not mine. I want that on record.

beats.headline: Remex the Grand
beats.text: The newscast has a name for him now: Remex the Grand, whose tragic, controversial tale finally comes to an end. The footage shows the pus detonating at the warehouse, swordsmen tumbling with their health deep in the red, and Remex curled in his corner, a silhouette of pulsing yellow. The light leaves him two seconds before the blast. He cries out as the dynamite takes him. The soul release from the fallen swordsmen tempers the wild magic, and thousands of NPCs and several dozen crawlers are potentially saved.

beats.headline: Katia joins on air
beats.text: Odette brings the newest member of the Royal Court of Princess Donut out in front of the virtual crowd: Katia, who answers the first few questions in single words. Mongo gets a welcome back, squawks at the audience and curls up at Donut's feet. Behind them the court's levels go up on screen, all earned from an explosion that paid no prizes: Donut nineteen to twenty-six, Carl twenty-one to twenty-seven, Katia nine to twenty-one.

beats.headline: One veto a season
beats.text: The AI rules that Carl's detonator came through both precursor bursts; Borant appeals, and a Syndicate court overrules it, adding that the achievements from the explosion are just and must be paid. But Syndicate rules give every host a single veto each season, almost always saved for the tenth floor or deeper. Borant spends it on the third. The Syndicate also taxes every non-sponsored box, allowing only a handful of free Celestials a season, and an emergency session is now deciding whether Borant pays for the other eighty-two.

beats.headline: A warning from Odette
beats.text: At the end of the floor, Odette looks at Carl and tells him to be careful with that gauntlet. It has the power to summon the war god Grull if he uses it against any of Grull's celebrants, and they start appearing on the next floor. King Rust has also just spent a lot of money on a deity sponsorship, which the Skull Empire does not usually buy. She does not know which god. If she were still a gambler, she would bet on Grull.

beats.headline: A song in the gangway
beats.text: Rabid babies are at both doors of the car when Carl asks Donut whether she still has those two trap modules. Each is a tiny cube about the size of a pair of dice. He sets the alarm on the floor of the fore gangway and puts the spike module on the janitor car's door. When the babies break through, the announcement rattles the walls: peaking at number 2 on January 13, 2007, it's Fergalicious. Donut loves this song.

beats.headline: A shield left behind on the tracks
beats.text: My pedicure buffs have lapsed, and a Drek baby finds that out by gnawing on the sole of my foot. Then they get through the first door, and the alarm trap plays Fergalicious loud enough to hurt. I check the map for a straight run of track and cast Protective Shell. The shell stays where it's cast. The train doesn't. It sweeps back through cars sixteen to twenty and off the end, pushing every mob in the way ahead of it. Car sixteen is all blood after that, with a Psycho Sticker so flat it doesn't even show on the map.

beats.headline: A plate that wants a key
beats.text: Aboard a red line subway car, with monsters in the next one, Carl gets down on his knees and pulls up the panel in the gangway floor, hoping to find the train's electrical system and the controls for the couplers. Under it is a small metal door with a lock, like a breaker box. He puts his hand on it and gets an error: the service plate is magically locked, and he needs a Red Line Engineer's Key. Do you have a key? No you don't. So back off. Carl puts the panel back. It will have to be the nuclear option.

beats.headline: Three spots left
beats.text: Shut in a train car with no doors to the outside, Carl prepares a smoke curtain and moves the ticket to his hotlist. It has three scratch-off spots left. If whatever is out there breaks in, they are screwed, and he knows he won't be saved by a glob of custard this time.

beats.headline: They are waiting when the doors open
beats.text: The commonest ghoul on the line, and by the System’s own account the most tractable of them, which says more about the others than it does about these. The court meets its first pair in the first minutes on the new floor, by diving into their train car to escape a flood of Drek babies, before anyone has established what the rules of the place are.

beats.headline: First through every door
beats.text: Something on this floor has doubled my constitution to 102. It is a momentum bonus, though we are standing still, and Carl says it may be patched out tonight. So I go through each door first, because my constitution is four times his. I suppose that is my job. The first time, Mongo leaps in with me and I land on my face, and my axe skitters ten feet ahead. It is a good weapon. My strength is not high enough for it.

beats.headline: The skill that stayed behind
beats.text: Kid, listen. Her Negotiation came at level five with the Artist Alley class, and she sold it up to seven. The class is gone and the five levels went with it, but she kept the two she earned, experience and all, so it bumped itself to four. So a skill she levels even once, she keeps. Stat points, no. Use Mongo as much as you can and Mascot stays. Watch for classes with rare spells. And it's probably a bug, so don't talk about it out loud. They won't notice until she carries a spell down a floor.

beats.headline: Next stop, transfer station 83
beats.text: The first mention is a train announcer's patter. Aboard the red line, with a service plate that wants a Red Line Engineer's Key and monsters in the next car, the loudspeaker crackles: coming up on Mora station number 82, home to the Psycho Stickers. Watch out for those guys. Next stop is transfer station number 83, where one may access the yellow line and the Nightmare Express. After that, Rusalka station 84. Thank you for riding the red line. Then the door starts to slide.

beats.headline: The buffs ran out
beats.text: On the red line, a level-six baby chomps onto Carl's foot, which should do nothing because of his… and then he is crying out in excruciating pain as it gnaws on the meat of his sole. He stamps it into a burst of tomato soup, spreads his toes to check they are all there, and heals. It has been a long time since he let his pedicure buffs expire. He had forgotten what it felt like to be vulnerable down there.

beats.headline: Hooligan, on six minutes’ notice
beats.text: The moment we land on this filthy train, my Character Actor skill says I must pick a new class in six minutes or be given a random one, and the list is nothing like before. I DON'T LIKE THESE CHOICES, and I tell Mordecai so. He says Football Hooligan: a momentum bonus, team buffs, and a skill called Mascot that is all about Mongo. I get Mascot. I do not get Group Chant or Moving Riot. I get ten points of Constitution, and Guinness, which doubles my strength when I am drunk. So if there is fighting, we stop at the club first for a dirty Shirley.

beats.headline: Left behind on the tracks
beats.text: The secondary effect, applied. Trapped in a speeding subway car with mobs breaking through the doors, Crawler Carl checks that the track is straight and casts. The shell ignores solid objects and stays exactly where it was cast along the track, so the train carries on through it, and it rolls down the cars, sixteen to twenty, pushing every mob before it like a bulldozer and squashing them into paste against the first surface they meet.

beats.headline: Spikes on a door
beats.text: Rabid babies are at both doors of the train car, and Carl asks whether Donut still has the two trap modules. Each is a tiny cube the size of a pair of dice. The spike module pops fifty-centimetre spikes out of a one-metre square every two seconds; friendly NPCs and crawlers won't set it off, but once triggered it spikes forever. Could it go on a door? He places it against the janitor car's door, and it lets him set it vertically and moves with the door. When the alarm goes off, shrieks explode behind the far door and experience notifications roll in from mobs impaled on the door spikes.

beats.headline: Choo Choo
beats.text: The party lands in a hurtling subway car, Mongo screeching in anger and fear, Donut trembling on Carl's shoulder, Katia clutching a pole, and the System greets them with an achievement: I'm on a train! Choo Choo, Motherfucker. The reward is a Train Conductor's Souvenir Hat. Wear it with pride! Getting dressed in the car, Carl briefly examines his, and it is junk. It is not magical. It is a simple, blue and white hat of the kind one would see on a toddler, with the words I rode the Iron Tangle embroidered on it.

beats.headline: Out of Quill's boss box
beats.text: Among the loot from the quest is the bronze boss box from killing Miss Quill, and inside it a magical tome for a spell called Bang Bro. Carl sets it aside, and after a new skill comes back to it: five mana, five minutes and a minute more per level, fire and electrical damage on any equipped item, and it cooks hotdogs. He shows Mordecai. It will work on the gauntlet, Mordecai says, but not on the xistera, not the way Carl loads it, and on his foot only while his invulnerable buff is up. It is a good spell in his mana price range. Carl reads the tome and adds the spell to his list.

beats.headline: Something for tier two
beats.text: Katia spends one of her coupons on a Training Room, which trains any skill that is not a magic spell for an hour a day, supposedly as if the crawler were really fighting with it. It costs 250,000 gold, and it will not train anything explosive. Mordecai says tier two will have something called a Bomber's Studio, which would let Carl practise blowing shit up. It joins the list of upgrades Carl still wants, beside the expensive kitchen ones that serve food with buffs and the kennel ones that do the same for Mongo.

beats.headline: The magistrate’s necklace
beats.text: The Tyrant's box holds ten thousand gold and the Enchanted Necklace of the Haute Bourgeoisie. One poor sapphire on it, for the town I ended up magistrate of on the third floor, worth 432 gold in taxes every ten days if I keep it. Plus five dexterity and Talon Strike, which turns the side of my bare foot into a slashing weapon with a two percent chance to cast Eviscerate. It sits heavier than it should under my shirt. We didn't wear dog tags in the Coast Guard. The boss box is a tome for Bang Bro: fire and electric damage on my gauntlet.

beats.headline: Read, not sold
beats.text: Donut has a spellbook coming to her, and remembering it, she rushes to the mailbox in the restaurant's shadowy corner, opens it, and grunts. When is she going to get a good spell, something with some kick, like Fireball? For once she asks Mordecai whether to read it or sell it. Read it, he says, and she glows. It is a spell called Hole, he explains, and it does exactly what it sounds like: a temporary hole on a surface of her choosing. A level-one hole is not thick enough to get through most doors, but it is a useful spell, especially if she is creative. Carl can already think of half a dozen uses.

beats.headline: A shield that looks like my sleeve
beats.text: My box gives me an arm bracer that becomes a shield. When I activate it, it takes on the look of whatever is around it, so it is a buckler of blue polyester, but it rings like metal when I knock on it. Mordecai says it carries Shatter and I should use it with Rush. Donut says I can be the liquid metal Terminator. I never saw that film. I don't like violence. She says I am in the wrong job, honey. I have promised my coupons to Hekla, and Mordecai has already worked that out.

beats.headline: Supplies for the weary
beats.text: For the record: at the top of the stairs at transfer station 83 stand a saferoom, a mace and bashing weapons guild, and Limp Richard's Sundries. Subject is a Mole Man, level thirty-six, non-combatant, short and squat, glasses, reading a book in his open doorway. The system's note on his kind: they call themselves Men and Women, which is exhausting, and spend their days and nights reading. Welcome to station 83, says subject.
