beats.text: My note is in the Cookbook, in the chapter on bombs. That is the whole of what anyone here knows about me, and for a long while it was the whole of what I wanted them to know. You do not put your name on a thing like that expecting to be asked about it afterwards.

beats.headline: Level three
beats.text: At the saferoom in station 281, inside a glass-fronted donut shop, Carl asks the bopca, Nodd, for a black coffee and the crafting table menu. It is a long list, most of it useless, at about 25,000 gold a table. He slides one of his two free table coupons across for the one he has been looking for. Then he presents his two upgrade coupons, hesitates over whether this is the right move, and asks to upgrade his Sapper's table to level three. A note in the cookbook has already told him what a level-three table does: it lets you infuse bombs.

beats.headline: Backpacks were a thing
beats.text: Notes in the cookbook's margins argue about backpacks. Rosetta found that unstable satchels hold their stability in an equipped backpack, Allister confirmed it, and Forkith, mourning a little sister, says they only slow it now: he found that out the hard way. What Carl takes away is that backpacks are a thing, and he has an idea. He shows Katia the result on a stand he built for it and says he saw backpack listed on the armorer workshop tab, which is true. The System labels it Ugly Ass Backpack With a Completely Useless Design that Only an Idiot Would Wear. Carl does not care, as long as the word Backpack is in there.

beats.headline: A shell on her back
beats.text: Carl loads it with metal poles and a pour of tiny xistera balls. He has made it open-topped with a slight lip, so that it lists what is in it as contents. Katia is sure she will only get the backpack's own mass. Following a drawing on a gym membership form, she reforms into a slug-like shape with a shelf on her back, the stand clatters away, and the backpack lands on her and disappears, turning the colour of her flesh. The dense mass forms a rounded, shell-like shape. It worked. She tumbles onto her back like an overturned turtle, then reshapes herself round more than a ton of extra metal, closer to a ton and a quarter, Carl says, and stands about eleven feet tall with a strength bonus.

beats.headline: Thirty seconds is too long
beats.text: Katia spends the next hour practising with different masses. Taking it off through her inventory is inelegant: unequip more than half her mass at once and her body resets, splotching onto the floor as a quivering blob for a couple of seconds before she is herself again. Putting it on means setting up the redesigned stand, pulling the backpack onto it, backing in, strapping up and turning slug, and then forming whatever she wants from the mass she keeps in it. It takes about thirty seconds, which is still too long. They are working on it.

beats.headline: Armorer's table, sapper's three
beats.text: Carl asks the Bopca Nodd for the crafting table menu: a long list, most of it useless, most about 25,000 gold, from the generic Tinker's Table to a Beekeeper Beesuit Mending Station. He slides one of his two free table coupons forward for the one he wants, an armorer's table. Then he presents his two upgrade coupons, hesitates over whether it is the right move, and asks to upgrade his Sapper's table to level three.

beats.headline: Planet Beautiful
beats.text: Hi guys! The fans liked your line at the end, Carl. People want the trademark line more often, though not too much, or it gets weird. Okay, so, I booked you two for a show in two days. Katia stays in the dungeon; Mongo goes in the cage. It's called Planet Beautiful: narration from a sound booth, a segment about this season's planet. Carl asks what the segment is and tells me I'm a terrible liar. Okay. It's about beauty pageants. And pet shows. Princess Donut says yes before he can.

beats.headline: Fist bumps all round
beats.text: I get the dance floor's attention and ask every crawler in the club for their chat details. We should all make a habit of it, so information can move: there are probably lots of ways off this floor, and everybody needs to know them. There are about twenty of them, most around level twenty. Bomo looks close to a heart attack, but I fist-bump the whole room, add twenty-two names, and make Donut do the same. Now a guy named Koki has found a way to message everyone on his list at once, and my inbox is a mess.

beats.headline: Stealing the Nightmare Express
beats.text: The plan: Donut Puddle Jumps us up the track, I hit Protective Shell as the train reaches us, and the shell clears every car. Donut's jump won't land as close to the platform as we wanted, and the train speeds up instead of slowing. I jump. I don't make it. Two potions on, I'm lying above the cowcatcher. I punch through the cab window: two bodies in the gore, and the boiler about to go. A demon woman in the firebox talks me through the valves. Level thirty-two, three boss boxes, and I have stolen a train.

beats.headline: Bronze, in the gore
beats.text: Carl is in the Nightmare Express's cab and has just boxed up its bricks. In the mess of gore, where the driver or the war mage was pushed against the box at the back, he finds a small satchel holding 350 gold and a large, bronze key: a Steam Engineer's Key. It allows access to the Tangle's employee-only areas and actions on all four hundred of its steam-type trains. Only then does he relax enough to look around. He is alive, and he has stolen a goddamned train.

beats.headline: Stoking the Nightmare Express
beats.text: Subject is a Lesser Demon and a non-combatant, level seventy-five, and she shovels for the Nightmare Express. Where one finds large ovens that want feeding, one regularly finds her sort, and the tangle has more large ovens than it has anything else. She is on the crew that the crawlers need and does not pretend otherwise.

beats.headline: Forty cars and no way in
beats.text: At station 283 it eases in: an old-school steam engine painted jet black, a wedge-shaped cowcatcher, about forty cars. Most are open-topped livestock cars caged to the ceiling with chain link, and in them massive things scrabble to get out: tentacles, claws and fire, one car full of seawater and spikes. The only ways aboard are a caboose and a passenger car behind the engine marked exit only. The train takes a minute and a half to leave. Protective Shell lasts twenty seconds.

beats.headline: Hit by the Nightmare
beats.text: So Carl walks up the tunnel with Donut on his shoulder, casts Protective Shell as the train bears down, and Puddle Jumper carries them a quarter-mile down the track. Every monster aboard slams into the wall of the spell. The train speeds up. It catches Carl as he leaps for the platform: the cowcatcher, then the front of the engine, his invulnerable foot taking the hit. He climbs the boiler, punches in the cab window and finds two dead engineers, and gauges climbing toward a train-sized grenade.

beats.headline: A stolen goddamned train
beats.text: A face in the firebox window talks him down: Fire Brandy, the Fire(wo)man, who says the engineer and a war mage went splat and walks him through the valves until the bomb warning goes away, then the throttle and the two-control brakes. In the gore of the cab Carl finds a Steam Engineer's Key, good for all four hundred steam trains of the Tangle. The shell killed every monster aboard, three neighborhood bosses among them. The cars behind are flatbeds now. Carl has stolen a goddamned train.

beats.headline: You are making her change
beats.text: We are in the dark tunnel waiting for the train, and Carl says Katia is a big girl who can take care of herself. Then why does he keep telling her what to do? He didn't even ask her if she wanted to get giant. He just shoved the backpack at her. He says look who's talking, me with the boots and the purple mohawk. That's different. Fashion is different from making someone change. He says I'm right, and next time he'll ask her. Good boy, Carl.

beats.headline: The train drives into it
beats.text: The plan for the Nightmare Express: stand on the track in the tunnel, cast the shell as the train arrives, and let Crawler Donut's Puddle Jumper take them a quarter of a mile down the line. They cut it close. The train roars through the spell, and every red-tagged monster aboard slams into its wall and is pushed backward. The train then speeds up, and they have to run for the platform.

beats.headline: Sheol fire, in a train
beats.text: On the Nightmare Express the name turns up in a stoker's description. Where an oven needs stoking a Lesser Demon is usually in charge, but a fire that must burn extra hot gets one of the much rarer Sheol MILFs. The young of a Lesser Demon's litter that do not live harden into Sheol Bricks, which burn long and hot, and a box of them sits at the back of the cab.

beats.headline: Running on dead babies
beats.text: Fire Brandy's own description explains her trade. A Lesser Demon in labour gives birth for about sixty days, fifteen to eighteen thousand babies, one roughly every five minutes, and only one in ten thousand is viable. The rest shrivel and harden into a valuable resource called Sheol Bricks, which burn long and hot when exposed to fire. A stoker who learns water magic seals herself in a boiler, keeps a big engine humming almost by itself, and disposes of her failed young in the same stroke. The train is running on dead babies. Holy crap, thinks Carl, that's fucked up.

beats.headline: The box in the cab
beats.text: Fire Brandy points him to a small box at the back of the cab, covered in gore where the driver or the war mage was pushed against it. Carl lifts the lid and pulls out a black chunk. Its description promises not to tell him where it came from, to save him distress, and then admits that was a lie: it's a baby corpse. He drops it in revulsion and wipes his hand on his cloak. There are about fifty bricks in the chest. He takes a deep breath, picks up the entire box and adds it to his inventory. He shudders.

beats.headline: A spell bought with my own money
beats.text: The Princess rides on my shoulder through the club now. As we cross the dance floor I cast a protection spell on the party, and everyone glows blue. I bought it with my own money. Bomo tells Carl so, which is the longest sentence anyone has heard from Bomo. The Princess says thank you, Sledgie, and pats my head. The Dodge room will not let Carl in. It lets me in with her. Carl waits at the bar.

beats.headline: The pit at 436
beats.text: Abyss Station has one steep stair, and it takes almost an hour to climb. At the top is a burning pit at least a mile across, its walls covered in portals. For a moment I'm at the Grand Canyon with my mom, her hand tight on my wrist. Then a train bursts out of a portal and falls, and there's no engine car. So the colored trains don't loop back in time: the cars get thrown in here, the engines go home, and they build new trains. The portal analysis says three things I'm carrying count as keys. One of them is that stupid conductor hat.

beats.headline: You can't save them all
beats.text: I send what we know to everybody on my list: four ways back to the early stations, two sure and two maybe. The replies all tell the same story. Trains out of service at an alarming rate, people stranded, dozens of miles to hike, almost six days left. Mordecai's voice in my head: you can't save them all. York's last entry in the back of the cookbook won't leave me: the hive, protecting those who are yours even if you never knew them, and the consolation of dying for a cause worth it. I'm not sure I agree with that last part. I fall asleep thinking there's something more to be done.

beats.headline: Stuck at 275
beats.text: We clear stop 275 on the Camel Line and kill one of those Krakaren bitches. Easier than Imani thought. Then the train to 277 never comes. Imani blames that Quan Ch fellow for blowing up trains. It's twenty or thirty miles to the next stop and another thirty after that, so instead we take the druggie portal back to 272 and hike down to 271. If the Cobalt line is out too, there's a named train there called the Eviscerator. We're out of commission for a day, at least. I tell Carl. He tells me to stay away from the third rail. Oh, you know it.

beats.headline: Three keys in the list
beats.text: At Abyss Station, Carl reads a portal over the pit. It is gated by conveyance type and to key holders: a crawler must be on a gated conveyance, or have a key equipped or held outside inventory, and compatible keys have been marked. Sorting his inventory on the way back down the stairs, he finds three: the Ochre Key, the Steam Train Key, and the souvenir hat from the start of the floor. His message to every crawler on his chat list sets out the ways through, and one of them is to kill an engineer and take his key, without crashing the train.

beats.headline: Swarming the wreckage
beats.text: At the bottom of the pit above Abyss Station lie thousands of crashed train cars and hundreds of fires, and the janitor ghouls are down there, swarming the debris like ants. Train after train bursts from the portals in the walls and tumbles in on top of them. None of them has an engine car.

beats.headline: Down the tracks
beats.text: MOTHER on back. Down the dark tracks. Mongo RUN. Really, really fast. Dead things on tracks. MOTHER finds map. MOTHER finds gold. MOTHER says Mongo FAST.

beats.headline: A yard full of engines
beats.text: At Abyss Station a driverless train nosedives into the pit, and Carl looks up at the portal over it: an Ultima Corp DungeonWerx Industrial Subspace Portal. The analysis runs much longer than the last one. He is facing the wrong side, and entering from it will do nothing. Passage is gated by conveyance type and to key holders, with compatible keys marked in his inventory. Visual Analysis shows a massive trainyard, thousands of trains spreading out in all directions, only the engine cars, all inside a high fence.

beats.headline: Up to 436
beats.text: Past a switching station, with its Station Repair portal and a track called Recycle, the train reaches Abyss Station, 436. A steep fire-escape stair climbs to a catwalk inside a burning pit of portals, where engineless colored-line trains burst through and tumble onto thousands of crashed cars below. Carl comes back down with the answer, the conductor's hat, and sends it to everyone he knows. The train is still there, boiler chugging on standby. About two hours after that it is back at 283 for Katia.

beats.headline: The Princess Donut goggles
beats.text: My first benefactor box is the greatest prize in the history of prizes. Princess D'nadia had it made especially for me: Prism Industries Capacitating and Focusing Goggles, a unique item, personally signed. They turn my Magic Missile into a laser, and I can shoot four at the same time, into four train doors at once. Plus they're beautiful. I look like Miss Beatrice. Also I went up two levels to thirty, my charisma hit a hundred, and I picked Love Vampire, which Mordecai told me to get.

beats.headline: Super sunglasses
beats.text: Back on the platform, Carl notices Donut's new look at once: large round sunglasses that make her look like a bug, like the movie-star pair Bea wears on her head in Donut's photograph. The frames have no arms and her nose is too squished to hold them, yet they stay plastered to her face. They are not just couture, she says. Carl reads the description twice. They turn her Magic Missile into a laser, and she can shoot four at once; standing at the back of the Mauve Platform, she has been firing into four train doors at a time. They can even hold one shot's energy and add it to the next.

beats.headline: A decent one
beats.text: The best prize in the neighborhood boss boxes is a Scroll of Upgrade. They have been good to Carl so far. This one adds +3 Dexterity to his Trollskin Shirt. That is a decent upgrade, especially since he had been planning to put a couple of points into dexterity anyway, but it isn't a great one.

beats.headline: Carpe Diem
beats.text: Killing three bosses with one attack earned Carl a Platinum Big Daddy Box, and it holds a regular, unenchanted toothbrush and a tiny, travel-sized tube of toothpaste: red, with a black skull, and Carpe Diem written on it in what appears to be Comic Sans. Five applications. Brushed in a safe room, it gives thirty hours of three times damage to all boss monsters, four times if the boss is a province, country or floor boss. A fantastic prize, Carl thinks, but only useful if he knows he is going to face a boss that day. He will need to be stingy. He adds it to his stash.

beats.headline: The stupid hat was a key
beats.text: Going down the stairs from the abyss, Carl sorts his inventory by the items the portal has marked, and finds three keys to it: the Ochre Key, the Steam Train Key, and that stupid souvenir hat. Holy shit. All they needed to do was equip the hat. He messages everybody on his chat list: equip the hat, ride a train to the end of the line, and you will get through, though the train car will not, and you will land in a station full of thousands of zombies. Mei W answers that her whole party sold theirs. They were offering five thousand gold each.

beats.headline: The switch nobody is meant to take
beats.text: The named trains run their loops until they reach a set of three switches, and only one of them leads here. Getting to it means reading the network, or else noticing that the souvenir conductor hat handed out at the start of the floor is one of the keys, which is the sort of joke the fourth floor keeps making.

beats.headline: Three points of Dexterity
beats.text: After a neighbourhood boss, the best prize in the boxes is a Scroll of Upgrade, which has been good to Carl so far. Applied, all it does is add three Dexterity to his trollskin shirt. That is decent, since he meant to put a couple of points into Dexterity anyway, but it is not a great upgrade.

beats.headline: The last entry in the back
beats.text: Crawler Carl cannot sleep, and a passage from the back of the Cookbook keeps coming back to him. It was written by a crawler named York, author of the tenth edition, who wrote pages and pages of rambling philosophical essays Carl can barely follow. This one appears to be his last entry. I have been surrounded by my hive, yet I have been alone, it says. The Cookbook, York writes, is an attempt to make a hive of those who never cross paths, except in these pages. And there is consolation in dying in the pursuit of justice, however small.

beats.headline: Baseball-sized, by the hundred
beats.text: The close fighting on the trains has given the xistera little use this floor. On the platform, with babababoons crawling all over the Nightmare, Carl calls one of his new Banger Spheres into the scoop and spins. It hits a babababoon in the neck with an audible splack, and the mob falls; he had been aiming between the eyes. They are nothing but spheres of dwarven robot scrap. He made a few hundred at his engineering table after trying several sizes, and the system only gave the name to the baseball-sized ones. He has ideas for others, spiked balls among them. He throws two more, and the two mobs across the platform die.

beats.headline: A way out of the robot rooms
beats.text: Hey, hotshot. Your instincts were right. There's a secret way out of the robot rooms: a long tunnel sloping downward. It doesn't open until the robots wake up, and they don't wake until the monsters start their withdrawal. Lucky us, we don't have to fight the metal bastards. I still can't believe you blew two of them up. We're following the tunnel now. Sounds like there's another train track down there. It's far. More when we know.

beats.headline: Two little ones
beats.text: At the switching station the stoker puts her head out of the firebox and chats. Crawler Donut says she is a mother too; her boy is named Mongo. A good name, Brandy says. She has two children so far, and her kind do not name their young until they are presented at the altar. Crawler Katia says she was about to adopt when aliens destroyed her planet. That's too bad, honey, says Brandy, and sounds as if she means it. Another child is born mid-conversation. Her one request of Carl: try not to blow up the train.

beats.headline: Traveling spikes
beats.text: Babababoons in the transit station, second stage of the DTs, crawling all over the Nightmare. I have one in a bear hug and he's hitting me really hard. Then my body jerks to the side and takes his top half with it. I think I've figured out how to move the metal around inside me. It's slow, but it hurt him more than it hurt me. I think I can make traveling spikes, so anything using its hands impales itself on me. When I do it really fast, it feels like breaking my own bones.

beats.headline: Minion Army, read already
beats.text: Remember the tome of Minion Army from the Beguiler Box on the first floor? It costs fifty spell points. With our rest and shower buffs I have fifty-two, so I looked. And of course I read it, Carl. Mordecai isn't here, so we're talking about it now. Five minutes to cast, stuck in place the whole time, and at level one each mob has a two percent chance to change sides. Carl says don't cast it unless he tells me to. Don't be so pessimistic, Carl.

beats.headline: Read at fifty-two
beats.text: Carl wakes from a nap to Donut's discovery. Her Intelligence is forty, her butterfly charm and new tiara add four, and the Good Rest and shower buffs add twenty percent to her base, which a bug keeps off the stat list but not off her spell points. Fifty-two. Of course she has read the tome already. The spell is simple on the surface and convoluted underneath: five minutes to cast, stuck in place while casting, a five-hour cooldown, intelligent mobs only, and at level one a two percent chance for each to turn on its friends.

beats.headline: Banger Spheres
beats.text: The close fighting on the trains has kept it mostly idle this floor. On the platform at 283, Carl loads a Banger Sphere, one of a few hundred baseball-sized balls of dwarven robot scrap he made at the engineering table; the system names only that size. The first catches a babababoon in the neck when he was aiming between the eyes. It dies anyway. He throws two more at the two mobs on the other side of the platform, and they die too.

beats.headline: Widget, briefly
beats.text: Station and Repair Hub E: a yard of engine cars, a shaking fence, and thousands of ghouls. A grease gremlin named Widget rides a basket down a chain from his tower, takes one look at us and asks what happened to CrackJack. I tell him. He doesn't mind much, as long as Brandy is fine. He says a train called the Escape Velocity goes to all the stairwells; you catch it at 89, up the Tangerine line. He unhooks our wrecked cars and waves, and the spider ghoul Donut shot gets back up and takes his head off.

beats.headline: Six mimics at Terminus
beats.text: Madison, from human resources, can't tell me how to get to Yard A, or whether she's ever been to her own apartment. Mandatory overtime, she says. The back of the cookbook has an essay on this: challenge an NPC when they don't know what they should, kind but firm. So I push, and she tells me what she does know. She tells employees overtime is mandatory, and she's benefits manager for the six Station Mimics at Terminus, which get cranky if not enough passengers go into them. Bautista is nearly at 433. I message him: don't get off at Terminus. It's a trap.

beats.headline: Out of the burning substation
beats.text: Subject is a level ten human and a non-combatant, filed as a Human Resources Associate for the line. She comes running out of the burning substation at Trainyard E in one heel with a ghoul at her hair, rides the Nightmare Express as far as station sixty, where the employees are supposed to live, finds nothing there, and sits down to wait for Rod. Her name was probably something like Jennifer or Ruth before she had it changed, around the time of the divorce.

beats.headline: First the Raven Blade, now the Nightmare
beats.text: Through the Station Repair portal the whole train makes it, into Station and Repair Hub E: a yard at least a mile deep, lit by spotlights, and thousands of festering ghouls penned inside its fence. A furious creature comes out to tell them the station is closed. First the Raven Blade Unlimited, and now the Nightmare? There is a ghoul infestation, and nobody is getting a resupply. Donut, sent to find the gate controls, opens the gate by accident.

beats.headline: The tower controls
beats.text: I'll go up the chain. Carl is the only one who can drive, and Mongo would be ready to graduate college by the time he got up there. From Widget's tower I can see really far. It smells awful. How many lotion containers does one gremlin need? There are multiple control panels and nothing is labeled. Whoops, that one tipped over a freight car. Then the turntable, one slot over, and it lines up. I opened the gate already, by accident, and more ghouls walked out. I didn't tell Carl straight away, because he might get mad.

beats.headline: A yard given up to ghouls
beats.text: Station and Repair Hub E is not coping. The DTs have been turning mobs into Festering Ghouls born knowing how to get here, and thousands have arrived, pushing the fence back and forth. According to Widget, someone cheaped out combining two systems: the ghouls were meant to be caged and conveyed onward, the cages broke, and too many came at once. The staff are about to abandon the yard for Yard A. Then a section of the great wall collapses, and the ghouls surge out of the enclosure toward the conductor staging area beyond it.

beats.headline: A memory with nothing under it
beats.text: Crawler Carl reopens the file while questioning Madison, an employee who has been putting in a lot of mandatory overtime. When Vernon told him about his wife, Carl had taken her for a made-up phantom. Now he has a theory to put under it: this floor's NPCs were given false memories without a proper foundation, stories as paper-thin as the background of an NPC in an actual game. Asked whether she has ever been to her own apartment, Madison says of course she has. It has just been a few days.

beats.headline: A wrench three times his length
beats.text: For the record: the subject arrives at the broken port-side window of an engine that has just rolled into Station and Repair Hub E. Goblin-shaped, covered in black bristly hair, about Zev's height, wearing a railroad cap and a toolbelt that drags a wrench three times his length. Level nineteen Iron Tangle Steam Engine Train Technician. His file notes that grease gremlins could go either way, and that the only thing keeping this one from attacking is a Sensitivity Training class human resources made him take. He opens by complaining that the station is closed.

beats.headline: Nobody ever asks Widget
beats.text: He asks after CrackJack, and Crawler Carl tells him the engineer is dead. He hopes for their sake they did not hurt Brandy. Told they want a stairwell, he laughs: this train stops at 83 Tangerine and Plum, the Tangerine runs to 89, and the Escape Velocity goes to all the stairwells. Then the ghouls. Someone cheaped out combining systems. The ghouls were meant to be caged and carried back on a conveyor, then wheeled onto the Terminus direct lines. Too many came at once. Nobody ever asks Widget what he thinks.

beats.headline: A stew at station sixty
beats.text: He waves his wrench at a climbing ghoul like a halberd, and Crawler Donut blasts it onto its back with a Magic Missile; it goes unconscious, then to an X. Oi, nice shot, lassie. He likes a lass with meat on her bones and fight in her, which Crawler Donut hears as being called fat. He gets off shift in a couple of hours, has a place up at station sixty, and his wife cooks a nice stew. There is fresh fish in their food boxes. Crawler Donut wants to know what kind of fish. Crawler Carl wants to know how they get out.

beats.headline: Plan change at the yard
beats.text: His system involves climbing his chain into the tower. He has Crawler Carl turn a red spigot, and the steam sends the ghouls below scrambling. Then a section of the yard's wall collapses and the ghouls pour out through it. Plan change. He lays out the route: onto the turntable, onto the employee line, a loop at sixty, a service entrance at every station. Then he drops a ghoul at the cab door with a bonk from the wrench and unhooks the cargo cars. He means to come down and ride out with them. He winks at Crawler Donut about the fish.

beats.headline: The ghoul that got back up
beats.text: Widget, grease gremlin, is dead. He turns and runs to the edge of the engine, and pauses to wave. The spider ghoul Crawler Donut had put down turns from an X back to a red dot, grabs him, rips his head off in one smooth motion and starts to eat the rest. Less than a second. Crawler Donut goes up his chain to the tower in his place and tries his controls. Her review of his quarters: very messy, and a great many lotion containers for one gremlin.

beats.headline: My name on the back
beats.text: Katia gets me alone at station 24 and hands me a black ticket with a gold skull on it. A PVP coupon: kill the crawler named on the back and collect three gold boxes, a platinum box and a player level. The back says Crawler #4,122. Carl. She watched Donut stuff it under the track. Imani tells me the first player killer in a party gets a coupon for every member, and that Donut already talked it through with her. So this is the only one anybody saw Donut throw away. I'll ask her, but up in the production trailer, not down here.

beats.headline: Now's our chance
beats.text: It is not a train. It is a roller coaster with no cars. The robots fill rolling cages with ghouls and push them down, the bottom catches on the track, and off they go, like the thing at the hospital that takes your trays away but a hell of a lot faster. Carl says if it were him he would take it, and that it is a huge gamble. By the time the good roller coasters came along I was too old for them, and my Barry puked cotton candy after the tilt-a-whirl. Now's our chance.

beats.headline: The skull she carries
beats.text: Katia and I came into this place together. A man we did not know attached himself to us, and when we joined the Daughters he would not be sent away. He took hold of her arm, so I put my trident in the back of his leg. He died of it. The skull over my head is his, and I am not sorry. I kept moving with Hekla. Katia went her own way.

beats.headline: The coupon book she left behind
beats.text: Carl asks whether I got a PVP coupon with my skulls. I did. A Savage box with nothing in it but the coupon book, one for every member of the party. I tried to burn them and they would not catch, so I left them on the first floor. Brandon wanted me to keep them, in case. I could feel them sitting in my inventory. Elle got no book with her skull, and Donut told me about the two she got, so I think only the first in a party to earn a skull gets one. I tell him to talk to her.

beats.headline: A third eye, pointed backwards
beats.text: The description says at least two of my eyes have to be flesh, which means I can have more. More than two makes me want to vomit, so I am training a third, pointed behind me, a minute or two at a time before the headache. It makes me feel less human. It is also how I saw Donut push a slip of paper under the track while Carl was gone. I grew an arm along the rail and took it. It has his name on it. Hekla thinks it was a setup to test me. I give it to Carl.

beats.headline: Whatever they are, they are at station 435
beats.text: A few dozen of them work directly under the line’s management, and they are stationed where the employees leave the train. Whether they count as a boss or as scenery depends entirely on who is describing them, which is a distinction the dungeon is happy to leave unsettled for as long as it is useful.

beats.headline: The gold armband
beats.text: Subject describes the Kravyad as a human resources initiative: blue, six-armed, and paid in one or two dwarves a shift. They hypnotize the crews stepping off the trains and hold them until the next shift is due, so nobody remembers a break and nobody asks for time off. Productivity up thirty-five percent. Workers who ask anyway get a trip to her office and a gold armband, and are told it will send them home. It tells the Kravyad they are safe to eat. That was her idea. It added five percent in Q2. Even Rod was impressed.

beats.headline: Sweet, delicious betrayal
beats.text: Katia hands Carl a slip of paper. While he was gone after the Nightmare hit him, she and Donut went back out to clean the tracks, and practising with her third eye she saw Donut pull this from her inventory and stuff it under the track. She grew a new arm along the rail and grabbed it. It is a black ticket with a gold-leaf skull, and its description is a list of boxes and a player level. On the back: Crawler #4,122. Carl. Hekla says, Katia explains, that a party crawler who earns a skull gets one for every member. This is the only one Donut got rid of.

beats.headline: Imani's book
beats.text: Katia fears Donut still has one with her name on it. Her friend Eva has a skull, she says, for a man she stabbed in the back of the leg, and the coupon book, and told only Hekla. Carl pockets the coupon and asks Imani. She got a Savage box holding only the coupon book, one coupon for every member of the party. She tried to burn them and they would not catch fire, so she left them on the first floor, though Brandon wanted her to keep them. Elle got none with her skull. Donut told Imani about the two she received, and Imani told her to get rid of them.

beats.headline: The purple Voca Nye
beats.text: The Kravyad at 435 is no boss. She is a snake woman with many arms, just as Carl was told. She tried to hypnotize us, and I used my last Voca Nye, the purple variant, and her spell would not come. Now she has nothing left but the threat to kill herself if we come any closer, and if she dies, the portal dies with her. One of our brothers was a police negotiator, and he talks to her through the doorway. Fewer than half of us still have our hats.

beats.headline: Bomo casts smack protect
beats.text: Service upgrade logged at the Desperado Club, station 41. Clients: Crawler Carl and Crawler Princess Donut. On entry the Sledge casts magic protection, as before. Bomo now adds a shield spell, bought by Bomo, which stops physical attacks as well. His summary: the Sledge casts magic protect, Bomo casts smack protect. Assignment: stay with the client while he sits beside a drunk, one-handed crawler with skulls. When the crawler lets a small metal object clatter onto the bar, Bomo is between them at once, and several cretin bodyguards the client had not noticed are standing round them.

beats.headline: Level seventeen at station 101
beats.text: Level seventeen, night elf, blood assassin, and I don't remember picking any of it. I was that drunk; I think the tentacled fella picked it for me. Haven't seen Maggie since the end of the second floor. We fought about the young man and his cat, and I think she blocked me. The folks I fell in with on the third floor ditched me once I told them the truth, and the new bunch on the train wanted nothing to do with a man wearing skulls. So I got off at 101, found this bar, and stayed. Tonight I gave the young man our ring. That's my revenge.

beats.headline: A name on a ring
beats.text: Frank hands Carl a ring and does not make sense while he does it. The item's full title: Enchanted Night Wyrm's Ring of Divine Suffering. For the discerning crawler killer, and its wielder can grow exponentially in strength, especially on the deeper floors. Whose name is on it, the item does not say. That is the whole of the file for now: a name in the possessive, on a ring meant for killing crawlers.

beats.headline: Down the ghoul coaster to Trainyard D
beats.text: They ride the conveyor all the way to Trainyard D, where the gate is breached, and land in a yard full of ghouls. A running fight carries them to the Iron Tangle's administrative building outside the yard. Elle floats above the horde and freezes them by the hundreds until everything around the building is dead, then complains to Carl for five minutes about how little experience it paid. The ghouls that arrive afterwards ignore the building and walk straight back into the tunnels. Carl suggests the employee tunnel, on foot, to the nearest transfer station.

beats.headline: A curse, handed over at the Desperado Club
beats.text: Frank Q gives it to Carl at the Desperado Club, and it is meant as a curse. He and Maggie My made their daughter Yvette wear one to level up, and Yvette marked Carl before they attacked him on the first floor. A wearer cannot heal while a mark lives, so when Yvette was hurt, Maggie had to kill her own daughter. Carl keeps the ring for the five percent.

beats.headline: Why nothing could be done for her
beats.text: Frank Q hands the barefoot man a ring at the club and calls it a gift, and the gift is the answer to a thing that man has been carrying since the second floor. The ring marks a target for death, and while the mark draws breath the wearer cannot be healed by any means at all. They put it on their daughter to bring her level up. She marked somebody in a safe room on the first floor and that somebody walked out of the room alive. So when the dynamite found her there was nothing on this planet that would have saved her, and her mother knew it before anyone else did, and did the only thing that was left.

beats.headline: The portal closes at 435
beats.text: We tried to paralyze the Kravyad, and she died, and the portal closed. More than a hundred and fifty of us have no souvenir hat. A man at the bar bragged about what they were fetching, and a bunch of us sold them. I have none. The trains have stopped on every track. We are walking to the abyss portal, about fifty kilometres. Carl says to send those with hats through, and to look for a way to station 436, where the named lines run.

beats.headline: Not reading this one
beats.text: Planet Beautiful parks us in a submarine and a real sound booth, and hands me a script on beauty pageants written by an AI consultant they got at a discount, because Borant started the season before it finished scanning us. Chad-class males. Roasties. A video of me eating a roast beef sandwich. I tell Bin, the producer, I'm not reading it. He says his little show is suddenly a ratings powerhouse and Titan is all over him, and offers me mechanized warfare, video arcades or pasteurization. I take the video games. On the way out I steal the fridge shelves, the makeup table and the couch.

beats.headline: Frank Q, at the bar
beats.text: Frank Q is dead, and the Sledge reports who did it. A crawler sat with Frank at the Desperado Club, they got into a fight, and the crawler killed him and walked right out. That crawler is now banned from the club. It was Chris, a rock monster like the Sledge but a different kind. Crawler Carl does not recognise the quiet man he knew in this, and reads Brandon's last message about his brother again and again.

beats.headline: Chris, at the bar
beats.text: Frank Q stays at the bar. A crawler talks with him; they fight; the other crawler kills him, walks out, and is banned from the club. The Sledge reports it to the cat by chat. The killer is Chris, of the Meadow Lark group, a rock monster of a different kind from the Sledge. The last thing Frank Q said to the barefoot crawler, as he slipped the ring on, was vengeance is mine.

beats.headline: Rid of both of them
beats.text: On the undersea show I tell the universe the real reason cocker spaniels keep winning Crufts, because it is the truth that needs to be told, CARL. Afterwards, in the green room, he brings up the coupons. I already know he will, because Imani is a big gossip and messaged me to apologize for telling him. I got rid of them. I buried his under a train track and threw Katia's in the garbage at the Hotdog on a Stick place. And quite frankly, it is a subject I would rather not talk about.

beats.headline: Buried and binned
beats.text: In the rental trailer, before they leave, Carl starts to raise something, and Donut gets there first: is it about the PVP coupons? Imani is a big gossip, she says, and messaged to apologise. You don't need to worry, Carl. She got rid of them. She did not like having them, so she buried his under a train track and threw Katia's out in the garbage at that Hotdog on a Stick place, and quite frankly it is a subject she would rather not talk about. Carl relaxes. That went much easier than he thought it would.

beats.headline: No hat, no way out
beats.text: Bautista sends an update. They tried to paralyse the Kravyad, she ended up dying, and the portal closed. Over 150 of them do not have their souvenir hats, the trains have stopped coming on all the tracks, and they are heading for the abyss portal on foot, about fifty kilometres. Does he have a hat, Carl asks. Nope. A guy at the bar was bragging about how much they were buying them for, and a bunch of them sold. Dumb. Get to the abyss, Carl tells him, and send those who have hats through on foot.

beats.headline: Thirty in the Royal Court's space
beats.text: Thirty of them, most around level twenty-five with Hekla at thirty-three, get through the employee portal at substation H after Sadie casts Glass Prison on its Kravyad. They hike to station sixty, find a switch there onto any of twelve Homeward Bound platforms, and turn up inside the Royal Court's personal space, because Katia holds a space attached to it and has whitelisted every one of them. Their own two combined spaces cannot take visitors until they buy a third. They ride to station sixty clinging to the outside of Carl's train.

beats.headline: Why I never told Donut
beats.text: Odette warned me about Hekla, and I never passed it on to Donut or Mordecai. Standing in our own space with thirty of her Daughters, I finally admit why: part of me thinks Donut would be better off with them. Then I look at Eva, the one at Hekla's shoulder, with thirteen kills' worth of skulls over her head, and that thought goes. I tell Donut in chat to watch Eva and to keep an eye on Hekla too. I put an invisibility potion and Mordecai's Special Brew on my hotlist. Then I say yes, out loud.

beats.headline: At the controls
beats.text: Half nagini, half orc, Nimblefoot Enforcer, level twenty-seven. One large skull and three small ones over my head, thirteen in all, and I don't want to talk about them. Carl stares at them anyway. I stole the second engine and backed it onto the Vermillion train, and I am the one who can drive a subway car, so I will be at the controls. We are taking the train down to 101 to pick everybody up. Before this I taught economics in Reykjavik, and Hekla was my psychiatrist.

beats.headline: A thousand crawlers stranded at 101
beats.text: A thousand of them are stuck at 101 on the Vermillion line, Li Jun's team among them, and there is a train sitting at 60. So I take my party into the Royal Court's safe room and I ask for help, which is not a thing I enjoy doing twice in one crawl. Katia means to use her own body as the plough. I let her offer it. That is the arithmetic.

beats.headline: They came back for me
beats.text: Hekla wants me on the front of a subway car as a plough, and Carl is horrified, and he does not know it was my idea. I widened my backpack at his engineering table while he was away, so I carry more metal now, with a layer of rubber between the metal and the flesh to take the impacts. I tell him it is what I am for. I call him a backseat dungeon driver. He does not understand, and I tell him so: she brought the entire team to pick me up. Nobody has ever done that for me.

beats.headline: A thousand stranded at 101
beats.text: We are stuck at 101 on the Vermillion line, my team and something like a thousand other crawlers, and we are not getting out on our own. Word comes through that Hekla's people have reached Carl's safe room and asked for his help, that a train is ready at stop 60, and that Katia means to use her own body to get it through. I do not know what that means. I have decided to find it encouraging.

beats.headline: On the hotlist
beats.text: Before agreeing to help Hekla's team, Carl rummages through his inventory and rearranges his hotlist. Into one slot goes the invisibility potion from the suitcase. Then Mordecai's Special Brew, for almost-invulnerability for about thirty seconds. He has to be careful with that one, because afterwards he cannot take another potion for ten hours. Okay, he says out loud. We'll help. Just don't get me killed so you can have Donut all to yourself.

beats.headline: A parade float
beats.text: The Nightmare waits where they left it on the dark employee line, idling, while the ghouls leave the track alone. Hekla's team wants to ride. There is no room in the cab, so Carl, Donut and Katia climb in while Hekla, Eva and a few others stand on the back platform, the rest clutching the railings on either side of the boiler, and small fairy-like daughters perch on the platform above the cowcatcher. It looks, Carl thinks, like a parade float.

beats.headline: Given memories of a child that was never made
beats.text: Subject conducts the Mango Line. He was also issued with a set of memories containing a daughter, and the daughter was never made, and he has worked that out and cannot understand it. He is found on the ground with his head down and a puddle forming underneath him. The memories work. That is the part of the design I would draw attention to.

beats.headline: Wider, with rubber
beats.text: Hekla wants Katia stuck to the front of a train as its cowcatcher, and it was Katia's own idea, she tells Carl in chat; it is why the Daughters are here. While he was gone, she altered the backpack on his engineering table and made it wider. There is more metal in it now, so she can make herself even bigger, and she has added rubber to the mix: layered between the metal and her flesh, it absorbs the impacts. What she needs is help with the design for the front of the train. She has to be careful of the third rail.

beats.headline: The line he mentioned
beats.text: The party is studying a large paper map of the lines spread on a counter. Crawler Katia points out the Vermillion line, which is coloured like the others but behaves differently, running the whole route in about a day. She thinks it is one of the lines Widget the gremlin was talking about when he mentioned the Terminus Direct. Hekla's plan is built on it: a Vermillion train down to 101 to pick everybody up. The subject is not present to confirm.

beats.headline: A floor that feeds itself
beats.text: A head on the cab floor growls and I stomp it. The next one is a torso reaching for the fairy, and I read it before I crush it. Blister Ghoul, level twenty, spat out by a soul-crystal ghoul generator at stop 72: every non-undead mob that dies on this floor births one, and every mob on the floor is sick with something that will kill it. Soul crystals again, like the one in the bomb I still haven't dared take out at my sapper's table. This isn't a maze. It's an almost perpetual engine, and in a day these things will be everywhere.

beats.headline: Mixed in with her arrows
beats.text: Katia is the train's scoop, and Donut, watching through her sunglasses, messages Carl in capitals: Hekla has shot Katia with an invisible arrow. She did it earlier too and Donut took it for a mistake. It was mixed in with her regular arrows, it went into the scoop, and the arrows are still stuck in her. Katia comes off the front of the train with her health plummeting and falls unconscious. There is no wound on her shoulder. Carl scrabbles until his hand finds something invisible and yanks, and only then does the hole in her leather appear. Donut heals her.

beats.headline: No credit for the kill
beats.text: Carl pulls the invisible bolt into his inventory, finds the second one, its shaft splintered, and yanks it out too. He examines it. It is broken, phased and invisible, it hides its entry point until it is touched, and it is the perfect ammunition for the discerning crossbow assassin. Temporary Amnesia and Suffering Bleed drain the victim to ten percent, a second bolt to one, and a victim who then perishes is listed as dying from something else, with no credit, no experience and no skull. What the actual fuck? Why was she trying to kill Katia?

beats.headline: Topping off Katia
beats.text: Carl has eight scrolls of healing ready and Donut another six when the train runs into the ghouls. Gore blasts into the engine like a firehose, and Katia, who has been fine, is suddenly unconscious at half health and dropping: something is shocking her. Where the hell is that healer? Carl casts his heal scroll on Katia and her health returns to the top, though she stays unconscious and it keeps dropping. At ten percent he slams another to top her off, and when her health keeps dwindling with no debuff showing, he reads another, then another. He will soon be out.

beats.headline: Stop 48 is full
beats.text: We crossed at station sixty onto Carl's line, found his train parked, and went down to the stairwell at 48. It was full of festering ghouls, and we watched them change: worms come out of them, and they pull together into one giant thing that fills the room. A province boss. We all got achievements just for discovering it, and it let us leave. Now the wrath ghouls are stopping at 36. We are going to post up there and kill them as they come in, before they can do the same. We could use some boom jugs.

beats.headline: Katia as the cowcatcher
beats.text: I am the cowcatcher: a scoop and a comb, spikes at chest height, anchored through the windows like a toggle bolt, rubber on the side near the third rail. The first mobs are a bee sting, and experience. Whatever lands in the scoop goes into my inventory, liquids too, under a new tab called Gross shit. Near 72 I get a fan box for the most new followers in thirty hours. Then something shocks me unconscious. In the main horde my health keeps falling and nobody can say why. When I come to, I ask Carl where I am, and why Eva is not answering me.

beats.headline: A manager on spring break
beats.text: Report filed by her crawler Elle McGibbons. Subject was very excited to become Meadow Lark's manager and is treating the post like a spring break. She spends most of the day drinking and smoking blitz sticks, cries about her space pony, or whatever it was, from her own time in the dungeon, and takes gold from Elle to buy more booze. She does throw out a suggestion every once in a while. One of them is that her crawlers pull a Carl and blow the room up.

beats.headline: I saw it with my sunglasses
beats.text: In the middle of the horde Hekla shoots Katia with an invisible arrow. I see it through my sunglasses, mixed in with her regular ones, going into Katia's scoop. The first time I think it is a mistake. Then she does it again. I tell Carl, and he tells Katia to lose her mass, and we pull the arrows out of her shoulder, and he tells me to be cool, because this does not have to turn into a fight. Then I tell Hekla exactly what she tried to do, and put a full-strength Magic Missile into her face.

beats.headline: The healer rides up front
beats.text: For the record: on the Vermillion engine's run to station 101, one more daughter rides in the cab. Silfa, Wisteria Fairy, level twenty-five, Holistic Healer. Plump, about fifty in appearance, half the size of Crawler Donut. She hangs back quietly. Crawler Carl hopes her healing works better in here than holistic snake oil did at home, eyes her nervously because he has never fought beside her, and keeps eight scrolls of healing ready anyway. Crawler Donut has six more.

beats.headline: Supposed to wait for 25
beats.text: Crawler Katia is the train's scoop and her health keeps falling, and subject has not healed her once. When a blister ghoul torso reaches for her, subject buzzes to the ceiling screaming for Hekla. Pressed, she says she is supposed to wait until Katia is at 25 percent. She looks at Hekla. Hekla nods. Then she heals. Before the next horde Crawler Carl gives her exact orders, and again she looks to Hekla first. When the horde hits, subject runs into the engineer's apartment.

beats.headline: The ghoul generators
beats.text: The fourth floor's Blister Ghouls come out of soul crystal-powered ghoul generators, one ghoul for every non-undead mob that dies on the floor, and every mob on the floor is suffering from something that will kill it. Goddamn soul crystals, Carl thinks: they powered the swordsmen on the third floor and Miss Quill's spell, and one became the bomb still sitting in his inventory, which he has not dared take out at his sapper's table. The generators are run by soul crystals, he tells Elle, and they don't take kindly to being blown up.

beats.headline: Spikes for a ghoul
beats.text: The engine ploughs through a tunnel packed with ghouls, and pieces of them shower into the cab. Carl smashes a gnashing head with his fist and it explodes. Another chomps painfully onto his leg. He pushes it down, the kneepads activate, and the spikes kill it. The train whines and noticeably slows while Donut screams and slices with her claws.

beats.headline: Bolts, Donut
beats.text: You tried to kill Katia, Donut yells at Hekla in the cab; I saw it; you used invisible arrows. Bolts, Hekla says. They're called bolts when they're from a crossbow, Donut. Katia, awake now, wants everyone to take it down a notch, and cannot understand why she does not remember. Because Hekla shot you with a scary arrow, Donut tells her. Hekla laughs, and it sounds unhinged. Bolt, Donut. It was a bolt. No, says Katia: they were both shooting, and Donut hit her with a magic missile aimed at the ghouls. She remembers.

beats.headline: Useful, for once
beats.text: Katia keeps asking what she did wrong. Nothing. She always said she felt useless, and for once she was useful. We were never really going to kill her; we wanted Carl's famous temper to flare. The cat shot Hekla, and in the mess Hekla took one of my hands off in the cab. I have three more. I tell Katia to stop being stupid and come with us. I tell her this is why I left her behind on the third floor.

beats.headline: Killed by the crawler she handed off
beats.text: Crawler Hekla is dead, on the train, in front of everyone. Katia aimed a Rush at Eva, went wide, and put Hekla against the wall of the cab instead. The first crawler this season to kill one of the top ten and claim the bounty. A golden Player Killer Skull, and five hundred thousand gold on Katia's head.

beats.headline: Rush, a few inches wide
beats.text: I cannot remember the fight. Everything hurts, Hekla is smoking against the wall, and Donut says Hekla tried to kill me. I think it was an accident. Then Eva tells me they only meant to make Carl's temper flare, and mocks me in my own voice: Fannar leaving me for a student, the adoption they would not give me. She says this is why she left me behind on the third floor. I use Rush, which I hate, and aim it at Eva. It goes a few inches wide. When I fall back from the wall, there is a golden skull over my head.

beats.headline: You pretend to be good
beats.text: Hekla corrects me: bolts, not arrows. I will never team up with her. She tells me to breathe. I used to think Hekla was awesome. She is just like all the rest. She told Katia she wanted her, she made her feel special and loved, and all she wanted was to use her and trade her in. Katia did her best. She did not do anything wrong. It is not fair. Now Hekla leans on the wall and lights a cigarette.

beats.headline: She heals Hekla
beats.text: Crawler Donut puts a full-strength Magic Missile into Hekla's face for the invisible bolts, and the cab fills with the Daughters: Eva with her swords, two mages with glowing hands, and subject out of the apartment with her eyes wide. Hekla is back on her feet shouting hold, fully healed by subject. Then Hekla sends the mages out, and subject with them. They wait right outside the door.

beats.headline: Leaderless on a train
beats.text: With Hekla dead, party leadership passes automatically to Eva. People do not like Eva, and they start leaving. The Daughters have hardly any equipment and no personal space any more. Most of them share Hekla's sponsor, a crab ranch, which has never sent them anything. The healer Silfa came in with her own two daughters, the mages at the engine door, who had Hekla's orders to kill Carl first if anything went wrong. Brynhild's Daughters, as Silfa puts it, is no more.

beats.headline: The bait was a bakery owner
beats.text: Donut pins the healer who was hiding in the engineer's apartment, and I talk instead of fighting. Silfa admits it was Eva, not Hekla, who told her to stop healing Katia. My read: Katia dies, I lose my temper on the nearest target, Hekla has to put me down, and Donut, with Mordecai, has nowhere to go but the Daughters. Silfa says her own daughters, the two mages at the door, had orders to kill me first if anything went wrong. She owns a bakery. She just wants to go home.

beats.headline: Off Hekla's back
beats.text: Carl tries to pull the crossbow off the undead Hekla's back and it will not come; it has to be Katia, who killed her, and he tells her to grab the key first and then everything she can. In the escape the body is torn in half, and the half with the crossbow is left on the far side of the wall. It's too bad about that crossbow, Carl says. Oh, you mean this, says Katia, and it forms in her hands. It looks like gold, feels almost like plastic, and is inlaid with carvings of a vulture creature. The moment Carl touches it, the system warns him: You have a dick.

beats.headline: Dipped in blood
beats.text: Silfa insists Hekla would never have let Carl hurt her. Just like she wouldn't deliberately shoot Katia with two of those invisible bolts from her crossbow? Carl pulls the broken bolt from his inventory. It stays invisible in his hand, so he dips it in blood and holds it up, and its shape appears for a moment before everything flows off it. He hands it up to the fairy. She hesitates, grasps it, and her eyes go big as she examines its properties. He takes it back. This means nothing, she says.

beats.headline: The Vermillion key
beats.text: Hekla is dead, Donut has her corpse up and lurching at the Daughters, and Carl is tugging at its crossbow when he sees the square access panel in the gangway floor. Katia has to get the Vermillion key from Hekla's corpse, he tells her, and it has to be her, because she killed Hekla. Get the key first. The engine doors were blocked so they never locked, but uncoupling the car still needs it. Once the cab door is slid shut and locked against the Daughters' spells, he asks whether she got it. I got it, says Katia. Not that it matters now.

beats.headline: Nowhere to sit down
beats.text: It has to be me who loots her, because I killed her, so I get the Vermillion key. Carl drags half of Hekla into the cab; the other half stays beyond the door. Eva went out of the window. She is still in my chat. I did not mean to kill Hekla. I am not even a little okay, and there is nowhere in this cab to sit down and have a breakdown, and all three of us laugh until we stop. When Carl says it is too bad about the crossbow, I let it form in my hands.

beats.headline: Saved again, and a train to drive
beats.text: I knock on the engine door and Carl lets me in, to more blood than I have ever seen in one room. My sister and Zhang are safe in the cargo near the front; we are twelve now. We have been saved, again, by him, and I have come to pay my respects. He shows me how to drive the train. I will take everyone back to station 36, where his friends are already waiting, and we will make a stand. I ask why not 24, which has stairs and no ghouls. Nobody knows yet what will go there.

beats.headline: Three Heklas in the cab
beats.text: Hekla is dead on the floor and the Daughters are pouring in, so I cast Second Chance on her corpse, and then Clockwork Triplicate on my new minion, and now there are three Heklas. One throws Eva out of the window. The others push everybody back through the door, and the Daughters scream about desecration. Afterwards Katia says she did not mean to kill her. I didn't mean to kill that guy either, I tell her. But he had it coming, and Hekla had it coming even worse.

beats.headline: Bait, and a bakery
beats.text: After Hekla's death Donut spots a blue dot hiding in the apartment. Subject bolts for the exit and is pinned under the gore; one weak ice spell at Crawler Carl. Traitor, she tells Katia. Carl explains she was bait. She insists Hekla would never. Then: Eva told her to stop healing, not Hekla. The two mages outside are her real daughters, told to kill Carl first if anything went wrong. I own a bakery, subject says. I just want my girls to be safe.

beats.headline: The Daughters are no more
beats.text: Subject's account of what is left. With Hekla dead, Eva is automatically party leader, and nobody likes her; they are leaving. Brynhild's Daughters is no more. Hardly any equipment, no personal space. Most share Hekla's sponsor, the crab ranch, which has never sent them anything. What are we going to do? Crawler Carl does not know, only that it cannot be with them. He opens the door enough for her to slip out, and on the other side three women start to sob.

beats.headline: Seven hundred hats
beats.text: At station 75, with Katia kept out of sight, I shout for hats and keys, and I expect people to hang on to them for resale. They don't. They coordinate and spread the word, and in twenty minutes I have over seven hundred hats and fifteen colored-line keys for the crawlers stranded at the pit. There is hope for us. Not a lot, but it's there. Donut whispers that we could sell them for three and a half million gold. If we save those people without the hats, I tell her, absolutely.

beats.headline: A dagger on Katia
beats.text: Katia receives ten loot boxes, and after showers they gather to watch her open them. She opens the first and looks at Carl, grinning. Sorry, Carl, she says, as the dagger tattoo forms on her neck. I know you wanted to get me into Club Vanquisher. Donut, poofed out, washed and smelling of lilacs, realizes what has just happened. Oh my god, yay. We can go dancing now.

beats.headline: Ten boxes and a belt
beats.text: Ten boxes. The first puts a dagger tattoo on my neck, and Donut says we can go dancing. The gold Savage box has no coupons in it, only a Find Crawler skill potion, level three, and I drink it at once. The bounty box is five hundred thousand gold. Being the first to collect a bounty earns an achievement and nothing else. A Platinum Slam Master box holds a wrestling belt: five percent strength, five percent constitution, and Avalanche, which hits whatever my moving body strikes with twice the mass. The platinum fan box is still being voted on.

beats.headline: She has her pick, and she uses it
beats.text: Subject is an outreach associate for the Borant Corporation and a member of the Bloom, the party that runs Borant, and party members are treated better as a matter of course. Brynhild's Daughters were hers, and Hekla with them, and the moment that account is lost she lodges a claim on the party that now has a former Daughter in it. The claim is not a strong one. She is Bloom, and the associate who holds the account is not.

beats.headline: Floor is FOOD
beats.text: LOCKED UP. Too long. Mongo squawks at them. Then: blood. Blood on Carl. Blood on Mother. Lick Carl. Carl smacks beak. Blood on floor. Mongo cleans floor.

beats.headline: A party member
beats.text: Zev warns that Loita has a claim on the crawlers' account. She is Bloom, and Zev is not. By Crawler Carl's understanding, Bloom is the kua-tin political party that runs Borant, and its members receive much better treatment. For the record, he files a precedent: the last substitute they had, "the Mukta guy" who put them on the Maestro's show, was a party member.

beats.headline: Ninth on the board
beats.text: Top-ten leaderboard, bounty column. Ninth: Dmitri and Maxim Popov, Nodling, Illusionist and Bogatyr, level thirty, one hundred thousand gold. Two names, one race, one level, one bounty, one line. Tenth is Ifechi. The list does not explain how two crawlers came to share a single entry. Crawler Princess Donut does remark on it: if those two get to share a spot, it is not fair, and she and Crawler Carl should both be number three.

beats.headline: A tribute to Hekla
beats.text: The whole recap is a tribute to the death of Hekla. It opens on her walking in, in street clothes, fighting with a husband who looks twenty years older; she leaves him poisoned by a cactus and comes back to find rats eating him, and kills one with his rib for a Legendary Grrl Power box. It shows Eva killing the man who grabbed Katia, and Eva leaving character creation on the third floor while Katia was still transforming. Then the plough, and Katia killing Hekla, cut as rage at being used rather than an accident.

beats.headline: Seven hundred in twenty minutes
beats.text: With people trapped at the end of the line, the plan is to take the battered Vermillion car all the way there and hand out as many hats as possible. At station 75 Carl trades fist bumps and loudly asks for people's hats and any keys they have gathered. They are standoffish at first; once they learn why, they coordinate and spread the word, and in twenty minutes he has over 700 hats and fifteen keys. Donut whispers that they could sell them for over three million. The System awards him Mentally Unstable Clothing Hoarder, and declines to reward the behaviour. It's weird.

beats.headline: Platinum Slam Master
beats.text: After the bounty, Katia's boxes bring a Find Crawler skill potion and half a million gold, and one more: a Platinum Slam Master box, for killing a certain number of mobs with her momentum. Out comes a gold wrestling belt like any heavyweight champion's. Who is Christopher Pallies, she asks; Carl does not know. Five percent strength, five percent constitution, and the Avalanche benefit: hit a living creature with her body while all of it is moving, and the force is as if they were hit by twice the mass. It does not carry to weapons. We need to stick you to the front of another train, Carl says. He does not say aloud that her Rush just got stronger too.

beats.headline: In case something happens to me
beats.text: Okay, so. I am still in the suit, because the dual-layer system was supposed to be replaced at the end of the third floor and Hinter would not rent us the cores. Congratulations, Katia, on the top ten. Odette has added a Katia option to her contract, with a rider: be zippier. In case something happens to me, I want you to know I appreciate how hard you have worked. Loita is Bloom, she has lost her main account, and she is claiming yours. I am not Bloom. Something happened at home. I cannot talk about it. Also, your chats go public tomorrow, for people who pay extra.

beats.headline: Traded for westerns and moonshine
beats.text: Pulling the battery from a railway cart, Carl recognises it: a dwarven battery, at two percent. He has the fabricator now, traded for the rest of his westerns and a single jug of moonshine; the mole man practically begged, having finished the books Carl had already given him. Carl suspected the fabricator's odd placement in the first store they came to was no coincidence. The cookbook says each battery takes four full mana potions to charge, and it takes five minutes. Fifty came with it, most at ten to fifteen percent, five full and five at half; Carl charged two more, for twelve usable. If every powered cart here has one, that is another forty-plus for the stash.

beats.headline: Three groups at the pit
beats.text: Somebody has found the Sinopia line, about five levels deeper than most of us, and there is a group down there. For mine, a gangway leads up one level to the Mindaro line. It still stands, but the Wall Monitors are gathering near it, and we will have to fight our way up. One more group is heading for the Grullo line. I think that is everybody. Carl and I spend two hours matching lines to his carts, and I tell him the tunnels open out near the pit, so the people there can step clear of the first cart.

beats.headline: A portal on the front of a cart
beats.text: Station 75's yard has ten rapid-response interdiction carts that never ran. The blade across the front is a portal: it throws everything on the line to a trainyard or into the abyss, and the cart only starts with gnoll hands on two plates eight feet apart. Every gnoll corpse in the station has been chewed to nothing, and that is no accident. So, two carts per line: the first set to the abyss to clear the track, the second fifteen minutes behind, set to the trainyard, for the crawlers standing on the rails. It needs Growler Gary's hands.

beats.headline: Some NPCs come back
beats.text: A passage in the NPC chapter, from Crawler Azin of the seventeenth edition: some NPCs are indestructible and regenerate minutes after they are killed, which means they carry or know something big. A note from the twenty-second edition adds a story of tying one to the front of a shield, which the Nagas quietly patched the next day, and of a man who exploded and was reborn each time he was dragged out of his church. He knew the password to the safe holding the stairwell key. Carl remembers it at the Downward Dog, listening to a gnoll whose throat was ripped out.

beats.headline: The bartender who cannot go outside
beats.text: The ghouls came through station seventy-five. Everyone out on the platform died screaming, and I went to fight and got stopped at my own door, because I cannot cross that doorway. Not will not. Cannot. Then a woman came through, took everything off my brothers and sisters, walked in here, pulled my throat out and stole my alcohol, and I woke up on my own floor in a pile of my own blood. She missed the stuff under the counter, which is the best part of the whole business. Good stock, good rag, no way to help anybody. If you tell me that is not cowardice I will believe you for about an hour.

beats.headline: Fourteen left hands
beats.text: Two keys to a cart, and each one wants a gnoll's left hand, and there is exactly one gnoll in this station. I cannot walk out to the carts. What I can do is die and get up again. The first time I was asleep and never knew. After that I came round sober and confused, and the next few times I tried to fight the dinosaur. After that I got in the corner with my spear and stayed there. Then Carl told me why: the carts, the portals, the hundreds stranded at the end of a line I will never see. He did not have to. I asked for a drink when it was done, and told the dinosaur to make sure it doesn't hurt. Fourteen left hands.

beats.headline: Left hand only
beats.text: Some NPCs regenerate in minutes, says Carl's book, and Growler Gary once woke in a pile of his own blood. While he sleeps, Mongo kills him and chomps off both arms at the elbow. Sorry, Gary, says Carl, and takes them. On the first rapid-response cart he puts one arm on the hand-shaped key console and it glows green; he weighs it down with a rock and crosses to the second, eight feet away, too far for one gnoll to reach both. Warning: You must use your left hand to activate the key. Back to the bar, says Donut. Gary, resurrected, is sober now, and Mongo kills him again. Within five minutes the first cart is running, and with its portal tuned Carl lifts a hand away to start the next one. The cart shuts off. Back to the bar.

beats.headline: Fourteen left hands
beats.text: Altogether they collect fourteen left hands from Growler Gary: twelve would have done, but Carl wants an extra pair in case they need to drive a seventh cart. Gary, sober now, because resurrection does that, fights back only the first few times. They are too strong for him. He hides in the back of the bar, huddled into the corner with his spear, whimpering like an injured dog. If you're sorry, he says on the fifth, why are you doing it? The floor of the back room is slick with blood.

beats.headline: A blade that is a portal
beats.text: Growler Gary tells them to take an interdiction team cart: dial in a line and it goes, on batteries even with the power out, and take a lead car, with the front portal. The yard holds unpowered trailers too heavy to lift, flatbed auxiliary carts with an outboard engine, and ten rapid-response carts that have never been used, each with a wide, flat blade across the front like a squeegee. The blade is a mobile portal. It fills the tunnel ahead and throws everything on the track, trains included, to a trainyard or into the abyss. Only a pair of gnoll hands on two sensor plates will start one. Mongo kills the sleeping Gary and bites off both his arms at the elbow.

beats.headline: Two carts down each line
beats.text: Three groups of crawlers are stranded at the abyss at the ends of different lines, and Carl's plan is not to drive at all: start a cart, set it on the right track, and let it run to the end. The first draft scoops everything to a trainyard, the crawlers too. Katia and Bautista point out what else is on those tracks, crashed trains and possibly thousands of ghouls, and what the crawlers would be thrown into. So each line gets two carts. The first has its portal tuned to the abyss, to clear the way. Fifteen minutes behind it comes a second, its portal tuned to the train station, for the crawlers to stand in front of.

beats.headline: Ninety-eight percent gnoll
beats.text: The key plates want gnoll hands, so I try to become a gnoll. I get to ninety-eight percent, and the last time I come out the system designates me a gnoll, and the plates still refuse me. So I stay in the personal space while they do what has to be done to Growler Gary. I understand why. I don't want to be part of it. What I can do is take an engine apart: my Gear Head knowledge base knows engines, and I am certain we can put this one back together on something else.

beats.headline: Westerns for a fabricator
beats.text: A trade entered after the fact, as Crawler Carl files it: he traded the rest of his westerns and a single jug of moonshine for the dwarven Battery Fabricator, and the moleman shopkeeper practically begged him to, having finished the first five. Carl suspected the machine's odd placement in the first store he came across was no coincidence. It came with fifty batteries, five fully charged and five at half, and they are the same dwarven batteries the trainyard's repair carts run on.

beats.headline: Face first, then the hands
beats.text: Bar dog asleep. Mother says GO. Face first. Arms off at the elbow, onto the counter. NOT FOOD. Back to bar. Again. Again. Bar dog in the corner with a stick. Mother says WAIT.

beats.headline: Half a mile over the pit
beats.text: In station 75's yard Carl reads the portals. The first of four multi-destination light-duty ones, each signed with forty-eight coloured lines, needs a selector to dial and defaults to the Orange Line; its picture is just a stretch of track. The heavy-duty clean-up portal at the front of a rapid-response cart is set to the abyss and carries an environmental warning, and the picture shows why: whatever it catches comes out in the air over the pit, a good half mile above the ground. Elevation is the highlighted problem. He switches the selector to the trainyard, and the warning goes away.

beats.headline: Physical, through the portal
beats.text: The carts make hardly any noise, which is a problem for the crawlers waiting at the far end of the line, so Carl puts an alarm trap on each of the six: thirty-minute delays on five, one minute on the last, to make sure the delay works before it goes through the portal. Donut is sure it will be Wonderwall. Peaking at Number 1 on Nov 16, 1981, it's Physical, so loud Carl takes a small amount of damage. He pushes the throttle, jumps down, and watches it shoot down the track into the portal.

beats.headline: The first cart plays "Physical"
beats.text: Six rapid-response carts, Growler Gary's hands roped to the pedestals because we have no duct tape, and an alarm trap on every one, because the carts barely make a sound and the people at the end of the line need to hear them coming. The test cart gets a one-minute delay, the rest thirty. The trap plays anything that ever charted on the Billboard Hot 100. This one picks "Physical" by Olivia Newton John, loud enough that I take damage. I push the throttle and jump. It hits the portal and is gone, and I can still hear it, far below.

beats.headline: The vermillion engine sent home
beats.text: The ghouls out of 72 are piling up behind the dead Vermillion train outside station 36, so I send our battered vermillion engine down the line at them. Hobgoblin dynamite roped to the rear shelf, and a long pole with an impact hob-lobber on the end, set high enough that only one of the big stage-three monsters will trip it. I ease it to full speed, and on the way out the front window I find one of Eva's sabers in the gore and take it. The blast knocks everybody at 36 off their feet. Level thirty-five, explosives handling eleven. Imani would rather I didn't do that again.

beats.headline: Two a second, not Hekla's speed
beats.text: Katia rolls into her sentinel-gun form, three spider-like legs and a flesh-coloured shield, and the crossbow appears out of her inventory and locks into place behind it, a firing slit opening like a mouth. It loads, cocks and fires itself while she holds the prod down: about two bolts a second, magical, razor-tipped, about twenty inches long, gone on their own a minute after firing. That is fast, but nowhere near as fast as it was for Hekla, and the fire and lightning on Hekla's bolts went with the rest of her gear. Against the tentacled thing that used to be a Razor Fox, each hit takes only a tiny bit of health.

beats.headline: No cobra lady in the crowd
beats.text: Carl asked me to go through every single person here and I did. No four-armed cobra lady. There's a man who turned himself into a mushroom, which, why. The fairy with the two mage daughters says the woman isn't answering anyone; if she came in with us, she took off. Imani is mother-henning everybody, and they're all terrified of her. Then Carl throws a train full of explosives our way and knocks everybody off their feet. He's lucky I can fly. I think the mushroom guy soiled himself.

beats.headline: One pair short
beats.text: With the tunnel sealed, the ghouls being generated at 72 stop heading for 36 and turn this way. Carl thinks once again of Growler Gary. They collected one extra pair of hands from the poor gnoll, but they are actually one pair short. He can't use the portal carts to protect the others, but he can use one to protect themselves. Help me position one of the carts on the track, he says. Then we gotta go talk to Gary again.

beats.headline: A game at the carnival
beats.text: A creature with a round mouth full of teeth charges down the rails, shrugging off a storm of crossbow bolts. Carl's metal ball shatters teeth.
