The next shot is a half-strength, impact-detonated hob-lobber, because the monster is too close for full strength; it goes into the giant mouth and takes out another tooth. There is a muffled thump. A moment after, the monster blows apart from the inside, like a water balloon filled with Beefaroni, and Donut gets no experience for it.

beats.headline: A train full of explosives
beats.text: Elle tells Carl by chat that some crazy asshole is throwing a train full of explosives their way. He laughs and ties the last piece of hobgoblin dynamite onto the pile. It is much more stable than the goblin stuff and should, in theory, survive multiple impacts, and the bundle rides up high so it won't go off until triggered: a long pole with an impact-detonated hob-lobber at the end, too high for the ordinary blister ghouls, low enough for a giant stage-three monster, or the back of the other train.

beats.headline: Six carts, six alarms
beats.text: Each portal is a two-way switch, abyss or trainyard, and each cart's trainyard is different, painted on the edge of each cart; only one is tuned to trainyard E, where they came in, so that cart stays. The carts make almost no noise, so Carl fixes an alarm trap to all six, to let the stranded crawlers hear the portal coming. He engages the first engine, checks that the portal is set to the abyss and the cart dialled to the right portal, and watches it shoot down the track, hit the portal and disappear. Katia and Donut send the last three while he wires explosives to the back of the vermillion train.

beats.headline: The prototype trigger
beats.text: Carl wants to sandwich a horde of ghouls and monsters between two trains, partly to see whether he gets experience for it. Apart from the landmines that derailed that first train, he has hardly had a chance to use explosives on this floor. The trigger he ties to his bundle of hobgoblin dynamite is a piece of his first landmine prototype: a long pole with an impact-detonated hob-lobber at the end, too high to hit the ordinary blister ghouls, low enough for a stage-three monster. If it misses, the bomb goes off when the train crashes into the other one.

beats.headline: The sentinel gun against a stage three
beats.text: I roll back into the sentinel gun: three legs, the shield, Hekla's crossbow locked in behind it, and a firing slit I open and close like a mouth. Two bolts a second, slower than when she owned it, and the fire and the lightning went with the rest of her gear. The Razor Fox barely notices. I think the body is a kind of living armour; the tentacles take real damage, but they are hard to hit, and my crossbow skill is still four. Eva's saber is no use to me on its own. It is only magic as a pair, which means she has lost hers too.

beats.headline: The stage three hatches
beats.text: Stage three of the DTs turns anything, ogre or rat, into the same hippo-sized mouth with tentacles on its back, and it is always fatal. The one Carl's party brings down on the Vermillion line gives no experience, because it has not died. It has hatched. Several thousand Krakaren Crotch Dumplings, level one, each the size of a grain of rice and already growing. A crawler named Donita Grace messages from stop 24 that there are millions of them there. The dungeon tells a bedtime story about a lonely creature who could not have children and made clones instead, and recommends a firm stomp. Carl stomps, then burns the rest with moonshine.

beats.headline: Found in the gore
beats.text: His train bomb built, Carl is about to jump out of the front window of the vermillion engine when he spots something on the floor. It is one of Eva's two sabers, dropped when Donut raised Hekla from the dead, fallen into the gore and forgotten. He pulls it into his inventory and goes out the window. In the hours of grinding that follow, Katia practises with it in her smaller form. The description says it is part of a set, only magical when the two are together; alone, the enchanted saber gives no buffs at all. Good, thinks Carl. Eva has lost her main weapon.

beats.headline: The sixth hand on the cookbook
beats.text: Subject carried the cookbook in its sixth edition and added to it. Her note on portals admits what nobody else will: there are dozens of kinds, they do not behave consistently, and one the size of a button can throw you into a monster den.

beats.headline: A blast far off
beats.text: An explosion far away is still loud and powerful enough to be felt where Carl is. A team of something like 300 to 400 crawlers had set out to fight their way to the blister ghoul generator at one of the station 72s, to remove the crystal or disable the machine. I think they blew the soul crystal, Carl says; he warned them it was dangerous. He tells Imani and Elle to send a group to find the line there: if the generator blew, everything over there is dead, but the stairwells might still be open.

beats.headline: The worst of the portals
beats.text: Carl slips off to the personal space and opens the Cookbook's chapter on portals. A note by Crawler Milk, from the sixth edition, finds them hard to understand: dozens of types that work in different ways. Some are like doors you never notice, some work at a touch, some drag you in if you go slack, though you can still break free. Sometimes you must be big enough to fit, and sometimes a portal the size of a button tosses you into a monster den. Teleport traps are the worst. Carl adds a note about the different brands of portals, but has no time to write more.

beats.headline: Six hundred at the end of the line
beats.text: Carl steps off a cart with a portal on its nose, and I tell him the truth: you have saved us. Again. Then he tells me he has sent the station mimic to trainyard E, where his own cart points. I have fought that city boss. Cut a piece off and it becomes a spider and crawls back to the whole; bashing does nothing; it resists magic. I do not know how to kill it, and I say so. He has hats enough for all six hundred of us, so we go through the great portal to yard H instead. Thank God for plan B.

beats.headline: A crossing gate on the track
beats.text: Bautista's second cart never reached him, so we take one down the Mindaro line ourselves. Five crawlers are running on the track, and one of them fires an ice bolt at us before we plough through them and send them to trainyard E. Then, outside station 433, a red and white crossing barrier with a stop sign, blinking, where no barrier should be. I stare at it for two seconds, and that's enough. I go to flip the portal back to the abyss, and hesitate. A fleshy appendage runs from it up into the station. We hit it, and the whole station mimic goes to trainyard E.

beats.headline: Asking the manager about mimics
beats.text: Carl wants to know if there's a secret way to kill a mimic, so I ask him: are you about to do something really stupid, or have you done it already? Both, he says. Our manager says you don't fight the giant ones. Slice a piece off and it grows legs and runs home. Get more than half the mass off at once and it can't heal or change shape, but the cut-off pieces come for you, and they only die when the mimic does. I also talked a group out of the province boss at 48. You can hear it screaming from here.

beats.headline: In Donut's mouth
beats.text: The last of the hat-wearing crawlers have gone through the portal to yard H, and the party follows on the cart. Carl puts his own hat on. Donut does not want to remove her tiara, so instead she sighs and holds an engineer's key in her mouth, and Mongo goes into his carrier. Carl suspects that since the cart itself is allowed through, they need neither hat nor key, but there is a cliff on the other side and no sense risking it. He eases the cart through, and just like that, it is done.

beats.headline: A pile of hats, in tribute
beats.text: CARL throws thirty of our hats on the ground for stragglers, and I have to tell him there is a fine line between being helpful and being a fool. Millions of gold, Carl. Then Bautista takes off his own hat and sets it in front of me, and suddenly there is a line of people, and every one of them bows and puts a hat down and says thank you, Princess. It is not necessary, I tell them. It was nothing. Our pleasure. I gather every single one into my inventory.

beats.headline: Not in vain
beats.text: Elle's away team, with the help of Tizquick the dwarf, finds the right coloured line to the exploded station 72, where plenty of other crawlers had the same idea. The ceiling has caved in, but the circle of stairwells remains, and people have cleared the rubble. Word goes out that it is a place to descend without fighting, and crawlers flock to it. The ones who died blowing the soul crystal did not, at least, die in vain.

beats.headline: Plan C, and a tribute
beats.text: Carl changes the plan: he has enough hats in his inventory for everybody, so they go through the abyss portal and skip the mimic waiting at the cart portal. Donut wants the hats back afterwards. Millions of gold, Carl. He tosses thirty on the ground behind the cart for stragglers, puts his own on, and they go through. Then Bautista takes his off and sets it in front of Donut. For you, Princess Donut. A line forms, each crawler bowing and dropping the stupid train hat in tribute. It was Katia's idea. Donut gathers them all into her inventory, tail swishing.

beats.headline: Much better than a litterbox
beats.text: Katia's fan box gives her a riot shield, and when she tries to equip it the system will not let her wear both. So she takes a bracer off her left wrist and tells Carl to have it; he needs a shield anyway. He had forgotten she owned it. She mostly used it to add to her mass. It looks like the bracer on his right wrist, the one that forms his gauntlet. He slides it on over the arm of his jacket and experiments: a twist of the wrist and a small shield pops into place, a shake and it disappears. Much better than a litterbox, says Donut.

beats.headline: The Jaxbrin babies
beats.text: Jaxbrin Amusements sponsors me, the same people who make my babies. Stuffed monsters: pull the tag like a grenade, throw it, and in ten seconds something real is fighting for you, or now and then against you. A green Slizzer attacked me once. Miss Quill had more than a thousand of them in her apartment, and I took them all. I have used about forty. I raise it with Carl because I have been meaning to ask whether he has any, and because I am afraid of running out. He tells me to train with my sword. He is right.

beats.headline: One of a hundred, in a benefactor box
beats.text: Katia's first benefactor box from Princess Formidable holds a single small item, and nobody says anything while she examines it. A crossbow bolt, just the one. It is a regular bolt unless it goes directly into the eye of a deity, in which case the god's invulnerability pauses for fifteen seconds. The sender is the youngest sister of the Maestro, now dead, and of Crown Prince Stalwart, who is somewhere in the dungeon. Carl reads the description and decides the sister is not a huge fan of her big brother.

beats.headline: A stairwell under the mimic
beats.text: The recap shows a group in a dark, dripping cave with a single stairwell, glowing below the ground and corkscrewing up into the dark. That's station 433, where we took the mimic away. A city boss sitting on a stairwell hides it from the map, same as Grimaldi did, so there's a way down for anybody still stuck on that side of the tracks. Donut wants to know if we could have just gone back down there. Probably. Katia points out they still have to find it, and there are five more mimics up there.

beats.headline: Viewers may now read the chat
beats.text: The second-to-last message of the floor opens with pride in human tenacity: fewer deaths than expected, which has them rethinking how easy the next floor was going to be. Crawlers on the next floor will be scattered further apart, and only parties formed before the message began will travel together, so goodbyes are best said now. For a small fee, viewers may now subscribe to the private messages between crawlers, live the moment the message ends. And liquids may no longer be stored in an inventory unless they are in a container.

beats.headline: The recap cuts it for laughs
beats.text: The recap runs the whole thing with me being put down over and over and not one second of the reason for it. No rescue. No six hundred people stuck at the end of the line with no hats. No carts. Just a barefoot man looming over a bartender in the dark, a dinosaur coming out of the fog, and whimpering they added in, because I was always dead by the time they took the hands. I would like the record to show that I said yes.

beats.headline: A beanbag with its tag on
beats.text: Bautista's quest to kill Miss Quill failed when Carl's party killed her by accident, blowing a hole in the ceiling of the magistrate's office, and when he got into her apartment it was empty except for stuffed monsters, more than a thousand of them. He tosses Carl one: a brown frog in a spiked helmet, tag still on, the same creature Mordecai is shape-shifted into. The paper tag says only Grulke Infantry, Jaxbrin Amusements, Ltd. Pull the tag like a grenade, Bautista explains, throw it, and in about ten seconds it fights for you, or attacks you. The common ones last fifteen to thirty seconds. He has four more like it.

beats.headline: The riot shield and the baton
beats.text: My fan box is a riot shield with "Get Back" across the front, and a telescoping police baton. I cannot tell if people are trolling me; they know I hate using Rush. The shield upgrades it to Crowd Blast: everything in a wide cone in front of me takes part of the hit, and I can use it every five minutes instead of once a day. The baton casts knockback when I swing it at ten or more. The shield will not share my arm with the Auto Buckler of the Peach Pit, so I give the buckler to Carl. He needs a shield anyway.

beats.headline: One bolt from the youngest sister
beats.text: My sponsor is Princess Formidable, youngest sister of the Maestro, who is dead, and of Crown Prince Stalwart, who we think is walking around inside Grull. We know nothing about her beyond the fact that she exists, so there is no predicting what she sends. The silver box holds a single crossbow bolt. The Bolt of Ophiotaurus, one of a hundred. An ordinary bolt, unless it goes into a deity's eye; then the god's invulnerability pauses for fifteen seconds. Carl says he is starting to think the sister is not a huge fan of her big brother.

beats.headline: What a tag does
beats.text: Bautista explains his stuffed animals. Pull the tag, throw it, and after about ten seconds the creature appears and fights for you, or attacks you. A sprite he summoned told him these are true summonings: the real creature, teleported in. Crawler Carl mentions he has one, a dude on a horse named Kimaris. Bautista does not have that one and tells him to hold onto it until he knows its worth. Carl's own reading: his Kimaris figure is a demon, and Unique, not legendary or rare.

beats.headline: Blood rain
beats.text: Katia goes BOOM. Red. Red EVERYWHERE. Rain! Mongo spins. Mongo splashes. Tap, tap, splash. MOTHER jumps away. Mongo stays. Mongo dances.

beats.headline: Seven days, in a blink
beats.text: Where is he? Where did that — oh. By his left tit. The notifications say seven days. For me no time has passed at all; I lost my temper at Chaco, blinked, and here I am. The cat has a player-killer skull over her head. So does Katia. The dinosaur is jumping circles around me. I see I have missed a few things. Carl starts to tell me, and then Katia erupts. Blood, gallons of it, in every direction, over the walls and the ceiling and me, and I go backward over the couch with my legs in the air.

beats.headline: One bolt, for a brother
beats.text: Subject's first benefactor box is opened by a group that knows nothing about her except that she exists: youngest sister of Prince Maestro and Crown Prince Stalwart, two princes who want Crawler Carl dead. Inside is a single crossbow bolt, one of a hundred, which does nothing special unless it lands in a deity's eye. Crawler Carl reads the description and draws his conclusion aloud: the sister is not a huge fan of her big brother.

beats.headline: Not a baseball bat
beats.text: The other thing out of Katia's fan box looks like a baseball bat, and it is actually a police baton. At first glance there is nothing special about it, but as Katia rolls it over in her hands, eyes wide and lips tight, Carl sees the slight glow of enchantment. Its length adjusts from twenty-five centimetres to three metres, and swung at a group of ten or more like mobs it automatically casts a level-five Cone of Knockback, once every five minutes. Those are both pretty awesome, Carl says. Especially the shield.

beats.headline: Get Back
beats.text: In the Soda saferoom at station 59, Katia opens her fan box first, before Mordecai gets back. Out pop a goddamned baseball bat and a shield: about six feet tall, curved like a half cylinder, with loops to hold with both hands or slide one arm through, a small plastic-like window at the top, and Get Back on the front in white, blocky letters. It's a riot shield, Carl says, and it is absurdly light. It gives five percent to constitution and five to Rooted in Place, and it upgrades Rush to Crowd Blast. Only a crawler with Rush can equip it.

beats.headline: An electric litterbox
beats.text: Crowd Blast is the battering-ram skill Katia killed Hekla with, upgraded. She still rushes forward, but everything in a wide cone in front of her takes ten to twenty percent of the damage, and she can use it every five minutes, not once a day. Rooted in Place makes her much harder to knock over, which, its description warns, is not necessarily a good thing. Katia cannot tell if people were trolling her: they know she hates using Rush. Donut compares it to getting an electric litterbox for your birthday. Useful, indeed. But a litterbox.

beats.headline: Five more, unopened
beats.text: Bautista explains his stuffed animals. His most valuable, a legendary, came in a weird glass case. He has five more legendary rares and is afraid to open their cases: the description says there is a chance of being blasted with fire, and a Sage Sprite told him it could still trigger in a safe room, where he would be safe but case and item both would be ruined. He thinks he might open them in his inventory, but is too scared to try. It is the same kind of case Carl's Kimaris figure came in, the one that now holds Carl's Doomsday Scenario.

beats.headline: Like a monster truck
beats.text: Katia's new riot shield upgrades her Rush to Crowd Blast. It is still the battering ram she killed Hekla with, but now everything in a wide cone ahead of her takes ten to twenty percent of the damage. With her wrestling belt bonus on top, Carl reckons, it would be the equivalent of hitting someone with a monster truck. More important, she can now use it every five minutes instead of once a day.

beats.headline: The truer translation
beats.text: Mordecai puts a name to the thing the Iron Tangle keeps caricaturing. Apothecary is the closer translation, taken from her ability to synthesise elements, and the dungeon's version bends the joke into an insult. She is a collective mind and she is spreading, which is a sentence that makes a great many people elsewhere nervous.

beats.headline: Smacked, and the ring comes off
beats.text: Mordecai smacks me. Right on the side of the head, and he doesn't freeze or get teleported for it. My father used to do the same, harder. He says he shouldn't have, and keeps going: crawlers ride out the ninth floor with their heads down; a Divine Suffering ring on the finger of a man the whole universe is watching is idiocy we don't need; and if I keep it he'll tell Donut to stay away from me on the sixth floor. I pull it off and feel my strength drop. We'll talk about selling it on the fifth floor. Don't touch me ever again.

beats.headline: Bought for the housekeeping
beats.text: A personal space upgrade bought from the Bopca for twenty-five thousand gold, one of the cheapest there is. Katia pays without a word, because the room is swimming in ghoul blood, and the bot sets to work at once. It is going to take a long time.

beats.headline: Two tracks on every noodle
beats.text: It has bothered me for days: we are still missing half the system, and the logo only works from above. Mordecai says they have flipped floors upside down several times; it is easy and saves space. So I fold the map in half, tear it a little, and it works. Each line is a noodle with track on the outside, and another track upside down on the opposite side of the same noodle. Dig under station 59 on the zomp line and you reach station 59 on some other line, with an empty chamber between. The mimics are so big because each fills two stations. It feels like a trap to me.

beats.headline: Already spent
beats.text: Mordecai is back. All they need now, he says, is to wait out the timer and hop down the stairs. Oh, and give him their table upgrade coupons, so he can boost up his alchemy table before they go down a floor. Carl and Katia exchange a look. They have both already spent theirs, and Katia's went into the Makeup Table. Okay, Carl says, they will give him a quick recap. But he has to promise not to smack them again.

beats.headline: The map is the Syndicate logo
beats.text: Look at the named lines from above: rings of different sizes, overlapping. That's the Syndicate logo, and the Nightmare's loop is the second ring. So a train has to loop to the front, and you already found it: the Escape Velocity line, named for the ship that found the wormhole that led to the Vog Generation Ship. The abyss is the centre of the galaxy; the tracks are the original worm paths. Six station mimics are the H'lene, who set six waystations near the centre as traps and ate the travellers. The Valtay and the orcs wiped them out. They really went all out.

beats.headline: Catching the staff up
beats.text: Mordecai is back, and he has missed a great deal, so I start with what matters. My sunglasses, from Princess D'nadia, which are the only reason we knew Hekla was trying to kill Katia. My charisma is over a hundred. And I took the Love Vampire skill, exactly as he told me. I have cast it a few times, but it has never triggered, because we have been very careful to keep me from getting hit. He tells me to slow down. I tell him to wait until he hears about Katia on the front of a train.

beats.headline: Mordecai sees it on his hand
beats.text: Back from his suspension for throwing a chair at Chaco, Mordecai sees the ring on Carl's finger and tells him to get rid of it at once. Carl is wearing it for the five percent to all stats and nothing else. After a smack on the head he pulls it off, agreeing only to talk about selling it before the sixth floor.

beats.headline: The tunnelling system
beats.text: Mordecai catches the team up on the shape of the wider universe, and two powers come out of it: the Apothecary, and the Plenty. The Plenty built the tunnelling system a few hundred seasons ago and kept it proprietary. Before it, most of the universe got the crawl on a delay of anything from an hour to a year. Prosperity, in other words, is a thing they sell.

beats.headline: Already spent
beats.text: Now that they know how to get to the front, Mordecai says, they only need to wait out the timer and hop down the stairs. Oh, and then give him their table upgrade coupons, so he can boost his alchemy table before they go down a floor. Carl exchanges a look with Katia. They have both already spent the upgrade coupons. Okay, says Carl: they will give him a quick recap, but he has to promise not to smack them again.

beats.headline: A cart hung over the hole
beats.text: The Def Leppard cart won't fit the hallway into station 36, so Zhang shrinks it and we roll it in. Five legs of welded metal, one between each pair of stairwells, meeting overhead: it looks like a campus art installation, and it's a crane. Imani's magic chain lifts the cart until it hangs nose down, the portal half an inch off the marble, tuned to the abyss. At one day left the Iron Tangle announces its own self-destruction. All over the floor the centres of the stations fall away and the Krakaren pour up into the rooms. In ours they pour into my portal.

beats.headline: Melancholy at the firebox
beats.text: Subject is still aboard the Nightmare, still idling, still giving birth, and has refused a pair of dwarven engineers who wanted to drive it somewhere: there is nowhere to go. Her persona has slipped into something melancholy. Tizquick has told her about his daughter. She reports that the dwarves and gremlins hanged Madison, the human resources woman, and brought her the body, and she took it into the fire. She lets Carl take several hundred sheol rocks. The rest she keeps, to keep the fire hot for her babies for as long as it will last.

beats.headline: Still in place
beats.text: The interdiction cart hangs vertically from the crane like a prize fish on display, its front facing down, the scoop at the bottom of its portal scraping the marble floor. With chains anchoring it so it won't swing, Carl climbs his handmade ladder to the cockpit. He pats the two Growler Gary left hands to make sure they are still firmly in place, then turns on the portal and tunes it to the abyss.

beats.headline: Fall back to the train lines
beats.text: For the record: when the station floors fall away and the Krakaren monsters pour up into the rooms, the chat fills with screaming, and one voice in it is giving orders. Gwendolyn Duet tells everyone that the bomber guy warned all of them, and to fall back to the train lines and hold the choke points. A crawler named Ronaldo Qu objects that he did not say it would be this bad. She asks whether he is on crack, and tells him to clear the chat.

beats.headline: A ring of flamers around the portal
beats.text: Carl's plan needs chain, and I still have a few of the scrolls that make it, so the chain is mine. The plan I'm less sure of. When the centre of the floor opens, nothing comes up at us, because it all falls into his portal. I tell them to secure the entrances and put a ring of flamers and mages around the hole in case something happens to the cart. Then they come through the hallways instead. When Carl, Katia and Donut stumble back out of one, burning with acid, I'm right there, and I take it off them.

beats.headline: A crane over the hole
beats.text: Crawlers build a five-legged crane over the station's five stairwells, two train wheels on top for the pulley, and Imani's magical chain lifts the back of an interdiction cart until it hangs vertically, front down, like a prize fish. Carl climbs his handmade ladder to the cockpit, pats the two Growler Gary left hands still in place, and turns the portal on, tuned to the abyss. Facing down, it is almost exactly the size of the marble circle in the centre of the room. At one day left, across the Tangle the centres of the stations fall away and Krakaren monsters pour in. Back in their station, the monsters are falling into the portal headfirst, feet first and sideways. Thousands of them, and they keep coming.

beats.headline: Crowd Blast down a hallway
beats.text: I hate that ability. I turn the riot shield ninety degrees and Crowd Blast into a hallway crammed with Krakaren and ghouls, and they go back like bowling pins. Acid in the air; it burns. I come out at a T junction, stairs going down on both sides, swing the baton one way and fire the crossbow the other. There are about fifty of them at the bottom of each stair, and Carl throws a boom jug down both. Donut jumps us back to the main room. But it works well.

beats.headline: The stairwell stations flood
beats.text: One day left on the floor clock and they come out of the deep tunnels in numbers nobody in production budgeted for. Thousands of them, growing as they travel, pouring up out of holes in the middle of every station, hours before a single stairwell opens. Carl warned everybody this was coming, in detail, on an open channel. Being right about it helps nobody at all.

beats.headline: Hanged by the staff
beats.text: Subject Madison, human resources associate, is dead. The dwarves and gremlins of the Tangle built a stand and a noose and hanged her, once word spread, as Fire Brandy tells it. Fire Brandy did not see it. They brought the body to her, and she took it into the fire. Carl's assessment: Madison did not deserve it, though her character did. That is the whole difficulty with a staff that is starting to notice it is a cast.

beats.headline: Parked at sixty
beats.text: Its last job was ferrying Brynhild's Daughters to station sixty, and it is still parked there, a few stations down the employee line. Fire Brandy is still aboard and has turned away a pair of dwarven engineers who climbed in through the broken window: there is nowhere to go, you fool. Mordecai, told about the capture by Donut, assumes Carl thought that was a glorious idea too. Carl says it was a dumb idea. The new one is better. Though it's funny Mordecai mentions the Nightmare.

beats.headline: The last Puddle Jump of the floor
beats.text: The dog woman with the flamethrower shot my monster after I said I had the one on the left, and then she said I did not call it, and she is not a he, and I should go to a different position, cat. CARL made me move. Then Katia blasts down a hallway, Carl throws two boom jugs, and I count down from three and Puddle Jump us back to the main room. That was my last one for the floor. We are all burning. I tell the dog woman she is welcome. She grunts.

beats.headline: Swung one way
beats.text: Crowd Blast has carried Katia into the hallway full of Krakaren monsters and ghouls, all the way to the first intersection, a T with short stairwells going down on either side. Dazed but still on her feet, she pulls her crowd-control baton and swings it in one direction while the crossbow flips upside-down and fires in the other. Carl comes running up behind her with a second boom jug in his hand.

beats.headline: Like a wrecking ball
beats.text: Katia, in her she-hulk form, about eight feet tall and wide, wears the riot shield on her left arm in its original form, and it makes her look especially imposing. When the hallway ahead fills with Krakaren monsters and ghouls, crammed tight and rushing at them, she widens, rotates the shield ninety degrees and pushes it forward like a battering ram. Go, says Carl. She activates Crowd Blast and explodes into the crowd like a wrecking ball, and the monsters rocket back like bowling pins. Acid mists into the air and she cries out, but she goes all the way to the first intersection.

beats.headline: Several hundred, still burning
beats.text: Carl and Donut find Fire Brandy still aboard the idling Nightmare, still giving birth, refusing a pair of dwarven engineers who want to take the train somewhere: there is nowhere to go, she tells them, and they leave when Carl arrives. Her persona has slipped into something more melancholy. He has shown one of the rocks to Mordecai, who was nearly beside himself and told him to get as many as possible, so Carl asks if she can part with any. She lets him take several hundred still-burning pieces, along with a few dozen that have not yet caught fire. She would give him all of it, she says, but she needs to keep the fire hot and her babies happy.

beats.headline: A name nobody on the crawl can pronounce
beats.text: Subject is from Earth, a level twenty-seven Dog Soldier who took the Crisper Class, which in practice means a magical flamethrower and a helmet with holes cut for the ears. Nobody has worked out how to pronounce her name. A certain cat has already called her 'he' and accused her of hogging a kill she did not steal, over a race the cat dislikes on sight, and she holds the choke point beside that cat's party regardless, which is a distinction the cat never quite grasps.

beats.headline: Holding up a cart
beats.text: Imani still has a few of those chain-making scrolls, and Carl asks her to use them. Several piles of the magical chain sit coiled and ready while she asks if he is sure. Within the hour the chain lifts the back end of the interdiction cart into the air from a five-legged crane over the stairwells, and it does not break. They lock it in place, the whole cart hanging vertically like a prize fish on display, and anchor the front with more chain so it won't swing.

beats.headline: The last charge of the wand
beats.text: Li Jun tells me what Carl is trying to do, so I run all the way from the safe room. The cart will not fit the hallway. I have a wand that shrinks things. It does not work on living things. We shrank a monster's collar once and it choked him. I used it on a train that was going to run us down; it killed everyone on board and I jumped six levels at once. One charge left, saved for an emergency. This is one. Five minutes small, and it is still as heavy as before.

beats.headline: Pulled in by the foot
beats.text: Two neighbourhood bosses guard the employee line, and my gauntlet can bring Grull out of one of them. So I lure them into the tunnel. Katia pins one and Li Na chains it unconscious. The other gets torn up by Li Jun, Mongo and Donut before I can stop them, and I punch it until the notification blinks. Ten seconds. It clamps onto the track, so Zhang brings the portal to it. We drop it at one second. It has let go of the track and wrapped that hand around my foot, which I can't feel, because it's numb. Then I'm through.

beats.headline: Three kinds of summoning
beats.text: For the record: the subject's first note on file sits in the middle of the Cookbook's miscellaneous chapter. Avoid all three types of deity summoning. The big gods, Apito and Eris and so forth, are sponsored by some rich prick who paid extra to play the Celestial Ascendency, and they are invulnerable below the twelfth floor. Celestial boons, indentured summonings, involuntary summonings. In his short experience, all three lead to the summoner's death. Even the first. His advice: just stay the fuck away.

beats.headline: Gods as a revenue stream
beats.text: Below Crawler Forkith's reply, a second note by the subject covers involuntary summonings, which is what Crawler Carl's gauntlet did. They are common. God-summoning equipment is sprinkled through the dungeon as a way to collect more sponsorship money, allowing for special guest appearances, and the deity spots are often bought by celebrities. It is a safe way into the game for anyone not part of the dynastic families who control the armies of the ninth floor. Crawler Carl already knew most of it. He asks Mordecai anyway, so there is a record of the question.

beats.headline: Three kinds of summoning
beats.text: Deities get no chapter of their own, only notes in the miscellaneous one. Coolie, nineteenth edition: there are three kinds of summoning, the celestial boon, the indentured and the involuntary, which arrives untethered and smashes everything, and in Coolie's experience all three end with the summoner dead. Gods are invulnerable below the twelfth floor. Forkith, twentieth, adds that they still bleed, and prays to reach the twelfth to kill one for a sister, Barkith. Tin, twenty-first: gods are Soul Armor, worn by aliens like clothes, so a spell that strips biological armour could in theory strip the driver.

beats.headline: For Barkith, on the twelfth
beats.text: In the Cookbook's few notes on deities, Crawler Coolie advises staying away from gods entirely. Forkith's addition: they may be invulnerable, but they still feel pain, they still bleed, and the drivers of those bodies suffer. In honour of his sister, he prays he reaches the twelfth floor just so he may slay one. He knows it is a dream. He has the line ready anyway: he means to look in the god's eyes and say, this is for Barkith. This is for my sister.

beats.headline: Twin fireballs at a junction
beats.text: In the station defence, Katia's Crowd Blast carries her into a T-shaped junction packed with krakaren monsters. Crawler Carl follows and throws one jug down each branch as Crawler Donut puddle jumps the three of them back to the main room. Twin fireballs erupt at the far ends. Soon after, the two closest soul crystals pop.

beats.headline: Bait the boss through the hole
beats.text: Carl has saved my brother and me twice. I thank him, and the cat. Then I ask for the whole plan before we move, in case he dies and we must carry it on. Raise the cart a foot. Make the province boss on the other side of the noodle attack; it hits the portal and goes to the abyss. That gives us one more place to fall back to. He calls it fantastic. He offers a high five. If I touch someone with my hand, they feel excruciating pain throughout their body and lose control of bladder and bowels. I tell him so.

beats.headline: Same plan, other side of the Tangle
beats.text: We worked it out some time ago: the ghouls keep coming while the generators stand, so the generators have to go, every one of them. We have been taking them from this side of the knot, Prepotente and I, at his pace, which is patient. He puts debuffs on a thing for hours and waits for it to fall. Now Carl's group arrives from the far side with the same plan, and they have just dropped into the abyss the boss my boy was two hours from finishing. He threatens them for it. I take my staff to the top of his head until he apologises, and I tell them all that two groups landing on the same plan only means the plan is good.

beats.headline: No cooldown on a god
beats.text: Carl, if you've summoned Grull: run. Don't fight him. He's invulnerable. Take my special brew. You haven't? By the gods, don't scare me like that. The rules, then. An involuntary summoning lasts the vessel's level in seconds plus the god's. Grull is sanctum tier, level 250; from a level-forty vessel that's 290 seconds. Summoned, he grows until he fills the room. There's no cooldown, and a god held in one summoning breaks out and goes to the next if someone calls him. I learned that the hard way. The hardest way possible. Now don't you even dare think about —

beats.headline: Deprived of my prey
beats.text: I had the province boss asleep and entranced, and I was lowering its blood pressure toward cardiac arrest. Two more hours. Its death would have blown soul crystals through the whole system and let everyone down. Instead a portal takes it, and through the hole I find Carl, a colossal dolt, and the cat. The cat is delightful; we are the only two Earth creatures left in here with true sapience. I tell the woman beside him I could crunch her bones. Miriam strikes me with her staff and has me say I am sorry I wanted to murder them.

beats.headline: He called me delightful
beats.text: I insist on being the one to look through the hole, and CARL fusses about my whiskers. The boss is hair and quivering skin, like a man whose pants do not cover his behind, and I get an achievement just for looking at it. Then I lean in and hit it with a double shot, a full-powered Magic Missile stored in my glasses, and the portal takes it. On the other side is Prepotente, who says I am even more delightful in person and wishes to share a brandy with me. He called me delightful!

beats.headline: A note in the miscellaneous chapter
beats.text: The Cookbook hardly covers deities, and what there is sits in the middle of the miscellaneous chapter. Crawler Coolie, nineteenth edition: only idiots deal with gods. Some are genuine NPCs, but the big ones, Apito and Eris and so on, are sponsored by some rich prick who paid extra to play a game called the Celestial Ascendency. It is contained on the twelfth floor, with its own followers and storyline. Coolie admits not understanding it. What Coolie knows is that gods are invulnerable except on the twelfth floor and beyond.

beats.headline: Summoning by accident
beats.text: The cookbook sorts deity summonings into three kinds, and the kind Carl's gauntlet does is the involuntary one: some poor fool summons a god by accident, through a trap or a spell or bad luck, and the god arrives angry and untethered. A second note calls it common. God-summoning equipment is sprinkled through the dungeon for special guest appearances, the deity spots are often bought by celebrities, and it is a way to collect more sponsorship money.

beats.headline: Still human, and heavier for it
beats.text: I stayed human at selection. No fur, no beak, nothing added on. Earth Mover for the class, which is a spellcaster and a wall in the same body, and Dirt Clod is exactly what it sounds like and it works better than it has any right to. The armour I am in now is black and gold and glows in the dark.

beats.headline: Death Challenge
beats.text: The world freezes, heavy metal starts, and my face goes up in the air with Death Challenge stamped across it. On one side a level-ninety Mimic Rex with over twenty-three thousand kills; on the other Grull, sponsored, the announcer says, by the Maestro. I go invisible for thirty seconds, which is my intelligence times two. A hob-lobber through a Jibber-Jabber's mouth. Grull splits the mimic in half as if it were nothing. Then Mordecai's Special Brew: thirty seconds of almost-invulnerability, during which Grull steps on me and a train car rolls over me, and I heal every time.

beats.headline: The world freezes, the music starts
beats.text: Carl tumbles out of a portal into Trainyard E beside a glowing mantaur, a Mimic Rex's mouth opens in front of him, and the world stops. Music starts: heavy metal, bass-driven. A framed graphic of Carl's face appears in the air with Death Challenge! stamped across it, blood running from the words. The announcer promises the death of a celebrated crawler, live, and asks which lucky monster gets to kill him. Carl, frozen, has one thought about it, and it is a swear word.

beats.headline: Two contenders and a sponsor
beats.text: On the right, a level-90 Mimic Rex, city boss and crawler-killer champion of the floor with over 23,000 deaths. On the left, Grull, and for the first time on Dungeon Crawler World his sponsor: Prince Maestro of the Skull Empire, once thought dead, interviewed on screen telling the worms to try harder. The world stays frozen through the portraits while Donut gallops toward the trainyard on Mongo. Then the announcer tells everyone to get their bets in, and the world unfreezes.

beats.headline: No announcement at the end
beats.text: Grull splits the mimic in half, steps on Carl, and runs off after a second Carl who is Katia in disguise. Carl lives through the god's stamping on Mordecai's Special Brew. A mutilated mantaur, thrown into the portal with one second left on its summoning, takes the god away mid-attack. Then the music stops. There is no additional announcement, the way there usually is. There is only the chugging of a train, and a whole page of notifications.

beats.headline: Icicles off a god
beats.text: I've got a scroll that lets me fly higher and faster than an old lady has any right to, and I spend it. Icicles off Grull's head, and then I shoot past him like a bullet. He swipes at me and nearly has me. Then he opens his mouth and a blast of heat comes out that melts everything in its path, and it misses me by inches. I land on a derailed train by the gate, next to Katia wearing Carl's face, and take off again.

beats.headline: Grull against the Mimic Rex
beats.text: Crawler Carl, a Mimic Rex, and War God Grull, in one place, and the god is being driven by the Maestro like a stolen vehicle. Grull kills the mimic. Grull steps on Carl. Carl's friends come for him anyway, which is the part I did not have odds on, and by the finish Grull has been sent to the Abyss. Four storeys of war god, removed from the floor by people who were, this morning, worried about a train.

beats.headline: What the file says about him
beats.text: The file, for those keeping one. Grull is one of the few trueborn heirs to the Celestial Ascendency, which makes him a candidate for the throne of heaven, and level 250, which makes him unkillable on this floor. His worshippers are horses, centaurs and tikbalangs, and from this floor down the llama-shaped ones join in as well. They paint themselves blue and talk without stopping about wenches and dying gloriously in battle. Crawler Carl's guide gave the blunt summary of the whole subject a long way back: there are no real gods down here, only the ones who pay for the privilege.

beats.headline: Through the mouth, rolling
beats.text: Invisible and running out of time between two cold engines in the trainyard, Carl finds the way out blocked by a Jabbering Jibber-Jabber, a minion of the Mimic Rex and nothing more than a giant mouth of needle teeth, a splitter. It doesn't see him. He pulls an impact-detonated hob-lobber and dives through the side of its open mouth like a trick poodle through a hoop, and keeps going. The Jibber-Jabber chomps down. None of the pieces get back up.

beats.headline: Grull, thrown away
beats.text: Grull is loose in Trainyard E, melting through its far side with his heat breath, when the portal cart comes barrelling in with Zhang at the controls. Li Na has kept the second mantaur alive as nothing but a torso and a head, which makes him easier to throw. Five punches start the summoning, and Grull turns and gallops at them. They toss the mumbling mantaur up at the oncoming cart, and with one second left, the body enters the portal and disappears. Grull, readying some massive, body-glowing attack, whiffs away, leaving only a smoke outline in the air. The music stops.

beats.headline: Thirty seconds, intelligence times two
beats.text: As light bursts from the mangled mantaur, the mimic's tongue lashes at Carl, slaps the still-forming god aside and sends it flying. Carl rolls, slams the last item in his hotlist and applies his potion of Invisibility just as the tongue smacks into the spot where he was. Dude! Where'd you go? He is invisible for thirty seconds, his intelligence times two, and he should have put more points into that stat. The mimic roars and belches, and a mass of mouth minions the size of rhinoceroses bursts out, several of them coming his way.

beats.headline: Carl, on a derailed train
beats.text: Carl is inside the trainyard walls and cannot get back out. So I tell him to shut up and listen: run back toward where the portal brought him in. Elle bounces icicles off Grull's head to turn him. On a derailed train by the gate I make myself into Carl, cloak and heart-covered boxers and all, and stand there with both hands up, flipping off the god. Then I jump down and disappear. He screams and comes after me.

beats.headline: Easier to handle this way
beats.text: Carl goes into the trainyard behind a summoning. Katia and Elle draw the god away. The rest of us jump in front of the portal cart and come through the wall, and I bring the second vessel. Only the torso and head. I took off the lower body and the arms and healed him after each cut; it cost a few potions. The same idea as Carl's gnoll. He is easier to handle this way, and we can throw him into the portal instead of risking another accident. Carl should start punching.

beats.headline: Back, in a god
beats.text: People thought I was on that ship. My brother had already brought me into the dungeon; like I'd be stupid enough to be vulnerable like that. You gotta try harder, worms. Rest well, Mom. Now I'm Grull, level 250 and invulnerable, and I have a dozen ways to kill the piglet. I want to pick him up and crush him in my hand. His planet was nothing, and nobody is going to remember it. There he is, on a derailed train by the gate, flipping me off. Here, piglet, piglet.

beats.headline: Broken and healed
beats.text: Grull lifts his axe. It will not hit Carl, but it will hit close enough to kill him, and Protective Shell will not help this time. He slams the potion. Gold-Standard! A thirty-second timer appears. The ground buckles and launches him into the wall of a train, the shockwave slams him again, and his back shatters over and over while he is healed again and again. Grull, blind in the smoke, steps on him with a flaming horseshoe and shatters his pelvis. A rolling train car flattens him. Each time, he heals.

beats.headline: A throne with heirs
beats.text: Grull arrives, involuntarily summoned, and his description fills in a little. Grull, child of Taranis and Apito, is one of the few trueborn heirs to the Celestial Ascendency. Taranis, it adds, worries that his son may not be the best choice to rule the heavens, what with the temper and the donkeys among his worshippers. So the Ascendency has a throne, the throne has heirs, and the heirs have a family that argues about them.

beats.headline: Down the stairs with her cart
beats.text: Subject Agatha reappears at the station 36 stairwell: level eight, still human, still no class, pushing a squeaking shopping cart with the pink flamingo standing at the front. The steps turn into a ramp for her. She cackles that she sees they are all still kicking and goes down. Imani moves to intercept her and Carl holds her back, telling her they will talk about it another time. Imani wants to know what is happening. Nobody answers.

beats.headline: Still squeaking, still pushing
beats.text: Carl moves to step down the stairs, and they suddenly turn into a ramp. A familiar crawler is pushing a squeaking shopping cart toward them: Agatha, level eight now, still human, still without a class, with the pink flamingo standing at the front of the cart. I see you lot are still kicking, she cackles. The whole group watches open-mouthed as she heads for the stairwell. Imani moves to intercept her, and Carl holds out a hand to stop her. Don't, he warns.

beats.headline: A message, not a plan
beats.text: In the trainyard, Grull, with the Maestro at the controls, told Carl mid-rampage that even the magical bolt his sister wasted on Carl's friend would not work: Carl was not strong enough yet to hurt him. Afterwards, loading the portal cart onto the employee track, Katia wishes she could have used it. Carl says it would have been a waste, since they could not have hurt him, and that the gift was probably more a message to the brother than a plan to kill him. He promises her a use for it.

beats.headline: Map, guide, stars
beats.text: In the middle of the enormous pile of dead mimic, a single object appears on the map. Neighborhood bosses drop the neighborhood map, borough bosses the field guide, and thanks to both the cookbook and Mordecai, Carl already knows what this one will be. It is the Map of the Stars, which adds boss locations and descriptions to a large area of the map. It is a little late to be useful, but he wades into the gore and picks it up anyway.

beats.headline: I will break them
beats.text: Fire Brandy went into the pit so she would not lose any more children. Tizquick went because his daughter was a lie. Everyone here jumped into certain death to save me, and I finally see how much I need other people. Level forty-one. At the stairwell, in the cookbook's hidden pad: the NPCs and the mobs are victims as much as we are, and killing them is the best thing we can do for them. But all twenty-four before me only talked about burning this place down. We need to start killing them too. I will break them all.

beats.headline: Half a birthday present
beats.text: At the end of the fourth floor, with two people just gone to their deaths by their own hand, Carl thinks of his own mother. She attempted to kill his father and then herself, as a birthday present to Carl. She only half succeeded. He thinks, too, of everyone standing there with him, who jumped into certain death to save him.

beats.headline: Into the pit with her train
beats.text: Subject Fire Brandy is gone into the abyss aboard the Nightmare, by choice. After talking with Tizquick, she remembered the babies from before: a ship's boiler, a castle's heating, one or two each time, then gone and never returned, and she always sent back. Three this time. They will not use her like this again. She asks Carl to help them: they should not be enemies in this. The train whistles twice and goes through the portal, and Carl's log fills with experience.

beats.headline: The Nightmare into the abyss
beats.text: With five hours to the collapse, they carry the portal cart, turn it and set it on the employee track, its wheels just inside the wider rails. The Nightmare is loaded with explosive satchels, meant to blow up in the abyss and take loads of Krakaren monsters with it, maybe the province boss too. Fire Brandy and Tizquick have chosen to stay aboard; Carl says goodbye to them and steps off. The train backs up to the edge of the trainyard, whistles twice, speeds toward the portal and disappears. Zhang climbs back into the cart and turns the portal off.

beats.headline: Its last run
beats.text: Tizquick the dwarf helps drive it down to the trainyard, where the portal cart waits on the employee track, and Carl explains the plan to Elle: send the Nightmare into the abyss loaded to explode, and knock out the ghoul system. Fire Brandy and Tizquick tell him they are staying aboard. He has a few more explosive satchels to place at the back. The train backs up to the edge of the yard, whistles twice, and speeds toward the portal. Afterwards Bautista reports that they felt the generator explode.

beats.headline: Not Miss Beatrice
beats.text: Carl scratches me, and I purr, and then he tells me I should not have come for him: we risked ourselves, and the cart. I was not going to abandon him. Who does he think I am, Miss Beatrice? He agrees that I am most definitely not. Then I remember we never sold my hats, and he says they will be collectibles on the next floor. We will be millionaires. And then Loita messages that Odette is waiting, and will not tell me where Zev is.

beats.headline: Rides the Nightmare down
beats.text: Subject Tizquick, conductor, helped drive the Nightmare to the trainyard and then stayed aboard. He and Fire Brandy discussed it and decided together. He knows how this works, he says, and promises to make her blow nice and big just before the bottom of the pit. Carl's reading is that he went because his daughter was a lie. Soon after, Bautista reports feeling the generator on his side explode.

beats.headline: Not for a single gold
beats.text: The whole group is waiting at the open stairwell for them. Carl, Carl, Donut cries as they approach: we never tried to sell my hats! Carl had, actually, tried to sell one while she was in the training room. The proprietor laughed at him and said nobody was buying them any more. Not even for a single gold. He hasn't the heart to tell her. They will try on the next floor, he says.

beats.headline: What the odds were
beats.text: On Odette's couch it is explained. A Death Challenge is not a boss battle but a pop-up gambling event: viewers in systems where gambling is legal bet on outcomes, general or specific, each at its own odds. The AI put Carl's general survival at fifty to one. Plenty of viewers thought that was a good bet, and the odds slid less than you would expect. Borant has filed an appeal over how slowly the AI moved the spread. Odette made a good amount of credits.

beats.headline: Fifty to one
beats.text: A Death Challenge is not a boss battle but a pop-up gambling event: viewers where betting is legal wager on outcomes general and specific, at odds the AI sets. It put Carl's survival at fifty to one, and plenty of viewers took the bet. Borant has filed an appeal against the odds, citing the AI's sluggishness in moving the spread; nobody yet knows how much it lost. Minutes after, a new snick, Carl's Naughty Little Piggie Goes to Market, is doing the rounds. The showrunners will not let it be shown.

beats.headline: Next time I will be you
beats.text: In the production trailer my body stops answering; I arrive as my plain self with the heavy backpack straining on my shoulders, and Loita makes me put it away. On air, Odette asks whether I have done Carl before, since I did him so well. This time I recover on my own: I am getting better at emulating people, and next time maybe I will pretend to be her. Afterwards she says I was much better than last time. I still need to learn to relax.

beats.headline: The new arrangement
beats.text: Subject Loita takes over as the Royal Court's PR agent, with Zev kept on as social media manager. Zev, Loita says, has had a personal tragedy back home and has been sent to a temporary reeducation retreat, which never takes long on the weak-minded. Refreshments are over, on the grounds that some crawlers were getting illegal buffs from them. On air, Odette is muted mid-question about Eva, and off air again mid-sentence about Chris. Before the show, she tells Carl he does not scare her. Ditto, he says.

beats.headline: Anything but the Nightgaunts
beats.text: A wheel spins to choose the opponents of the next level, and one of its four choices is the Nightgaunt Precipice. Donut hopes for the foxes. Carl holds his breath and hopes for anything but the Nightgaunt choice: his cloak's description specifically warned that Nightgaunts would be enraged by the sight of it, and he doesn't want to have to get rid of it. Click, click, click. The wheel stops on the second choice.

beats.headline: It was me
beats.text: On air Carl says he hopes my winnings covered what I lost sponsoring Hekla, and I tell the audience it was my husband, who is sleeping in the skiff for it. My question about Eva is muted mid-sentence, and when my voice comes back I move us on to the next floor's preview. Off air, I tell Carl the truth: it was not my husband. It was me, and I hope one day to explain it further. He was right to call me out. It plays well to his smoldering anger.

beats.headline: Butting heads with Cichociemni
beats.text: Odette, on air between floors, running through the season's best stories for the benefit of her guests: the battle with Grull, Prepotente and Miriam Dom losing a province boss twice, Quan Ch, the hilarious but ultimately tragic fight between Lucia Mar, Florin and Ifechi. Not to mention the Popov brothers butting heads with team Cichociemni. That is the entire mention. It establishes a feud, and that the feud made television.

beats.headline: A reeducation retreat
beats.text: Loita says Zev is taking time off at a reeducation retreat and that Loita is our PR agent now. There are no snacks. I tell Carl we only work with Zev, and he tells me we need to pick our battles. On air there is a video of Carl and that silly pig boy, and I am in it, and nobody will show it to me. After, I ask what reeducation means. Carl says nothing good. I know we are not supposed to like the bad guys, but Zev is my friend. We are going to write a TV show together.

beats.headline: The wheel lands on Air
beats.text: I am team leader, so I spin. Land, Sea, Air or Subterranean: it nearly stops on Sea, then ticks over to Air. Maybe I can pick a class that flies this floor. The second wheel chooses our opponent, and I was hoping for the foxes, but it stops on the Dirigible Gnomes, and we must storm their castle in the sky. The door opens on sand and hot wind. It looks like a giant litterbox. I am very excited. Come on, team. Let's go kill some gnomes.

beats.headline: Gold or drugs
beats.text: To get into Hump Town a dromedarian wants payment, gold or drugs, the dungeon's version of the old bumper sticker. Donut senses a deal and straightens on Carl's shoulder; he holds up a hand to stop her and holds up a single blitz stick instead, one of the couple he got from Quint. The camel squints at it, pops it in his mouth and lights it. Good shit. Welcome to Hump Town, and stay out of city hall. He wanders off smoking it and shows it proudly to another camel.

beats.headline: Every bounty on me, doubled
beats.text: The stairwell drops us into a sandstorm and an achievement. The Quarry Sees Another Spring: a Gold Venison Box, which is just money, and every bounty against me now and in the future gets a times-two modifier. Nobody warned me. Not Mordecai, not the cookbook. I can't even swear about it properly, because every time I open my mouth it fills with sand. Tens of thousands of crawlers didn't make it through the last few hours of the fourth floor. We lean into the wind toward a town we can't see, talking in chat.

beats.headline: Down into the bubble
beats.text: Carl, Donut and Katia come down into the air quadrant of a sealed bubble and walk to one of the only two towns in it. Mordecai meets them there wearing a Skyfowl, which is what this floor has made of him. Donut takes the Glass Cannon class on the way in.

beats.headline: A building under our feet
beats.text: My pathfinder skill is acting oddly: behind us there is nothing but the mountain wall. But the wall looks carved, not grown, and I say so. I think there is a building under our feet. At a cave mouth a forcefield keeps us out until our own quadrant's castle is liberated. Carl rolls a bomb through and sets off a trap somewhere below. I throw a lit torch after it, and it shows a long, sloping hallway of carved bricks. An underground tomb, I think. Like Indiana Jones.

beats.headline: Fifteen days is a warning
beats.text: I was expecting twelve days. They gave us fifteen, and three extra days are not a gift, they're a nasty surprise waiting to happen. I got here first and gathered what I could: two towns, a sandstorm an hour or two a day, a castle that's a speck against the top of the dome, and maybe three dozen crawlers in this quadrant, every one I've seen so underpowered it's a miracle they're alive. Then the announcement. Four quadrants, four castles, and the stairwell won't open until all four fall. So assume the other hundred and fifty are idiots. Eat. Open your boxes. Sleep.

beats.headline: Four hours to go
beats.text: Out in a driving sandstorm on the way to town, Carl catches a countdown timer in the upper left of his vision. It is his potion sickness indicator, left over from Mordecai's Special Brew. He still has over four hours before he can take another potion. At least the timer kept ticking while they were on Odette's show.

beats.headline: Glass Cannon, minus the constitution
beats.text: I have to pick a new class the minute we arrive, and the choices are all different, and nobody gives a princess enough time. Mordecai likes Glass Cannon: plus fifteen constitution to replace the ten I lost with Football Hooligan, faster training on all my spells, cheaper spells, and a much stronger Magic Missile. I chose it. I got everything. Except the plus fifteen constitution. Now Mordecai says I am to be kept out of harm's way until I have better armor, and no more riding Mongo into battle. Also the sand is ruining my fur.

beats.headline: The guide's own people
beats.text: Eagle-headed, and by the guide's account his own people, who tend to outlast humans because they roll with whatever comes. He was born one and was a centurion before he took another race, and on the fifth floor the dungeon puts him back in something like the shape: a rock edge skyfowl cleric, wings clipped, the first body near his real one in a very long time.

beats.headline: A paw with no thumb
beats.text: On the way to the personal space, Donut bounces over to the mailbox and grabs her spellbook-of-the-floor club prize, and she is glowing as she reads it before Carl can remind her that they talk about spellbooks first. Unwad your panties, Carl. Mordecai names it: Astral Paw, a utility spell like Hole. Not as good as Astral Hand, with no thumb to hold things, but more force, and it can be a weapon: claws at level five, a much bigger paw at ten, her own skills carried into it at fifteen. About ten meters at level one. Back home, Carl laughs, she could finally have knocked that vase off the high shelf.

beats.headline: What a god leaves behind
beats.text: The Grull achievements pay out. Being stepped on by a god earns me a Platinum Spicy Box, because the AI is a pervert, and inside is a toe ring with two benefits, Sticky Feet and Super Spreader. Wiping out the wall monitors earns me a tattoo only a cover-up sleeve will hide: a little lizard foot under my left eye, and lizards hit me twenty percent harder now. Surviving a god's attack earns me a Legendary Deity's Box. Pawna's Tears. Plus five to any spell or skill I choose. Mordecai's talon shakes when he holds it.

beats.headline: Precious, and perishable
beats.text: Why is Pawna's Tears so valuable, Katia wants to know, when they have seen skill potions, potions that max a skill out, and Cheat Code potions that give three levels? Because it is plus five to any skill he chooses, Mordecai answers. Legendary potions that max a skill exist only for a few skills. The Cheat Code is also precious, plus three to a random skill. However, it has a short shelf life, so it has to be taken immediately.

beats.headline: Twenty of us, and a sailboat
beats.text: There are twenty of us on this boat and not one of these old farts has ever sailed. I told them not to put me in Meadow Lark. The system gives us a sailing tutorial that won't tell you where the boom vang is. We'd have an NPC to help if I hadn't iced him, but he was being suspicious. Then Imani crashes the boat and I have to freeze the water so nobody drowns. My deity box gave me a spellbook. Graupel. Big ice storm, fifty mana, long cooldown. Most powerful thing I've got, and I'm kinda scared to try it.

beats.headline: Skarn watches the patrol
beats.text: Skarn moves to the telescope, which points toward the desert. He likes to watch the patrol to make sure they are okay; Flint says if he grows up big and strong, maybe they will let him stay and he can join it one day. The telescope is a white tube covered in pipes and gears, made of something odd, maybe ceramic. Carl examines it: a dirigible gnome bomb sight that lets its user inspect things at a distance, and tells every gnome it targets that they are being watched. Flint found it in the dunes, Skarn says, among lots of crashed stuff from the last war. There! There it is!

beats.headline: Under a rowboat-sized airship
beats.text: Through a telescope, Carl looks the Wasteland over: a jagged island held aloft by colossal balloons, its edges dotted with ballistae and trebuchets. A rowboat-sized gnomish airship drifts into view on four propellers, and dangling under it is a refrigerator-sized bomb. Zoomed in, the telescope gives him the item, status 40, barely stable, with an adjustable pressure fuse that sets the height it bursts at. Carl asks Skarn whether they dropped one of those on his old village. Yep, says the kid. It was a long time ago, though, and he does not remember it.

beats.headline: The only reply from 543
beats.text: Crawler Carl asks who else is in bubble 543 and gets one answer. Subject: human, level 27, a Boring Ol' Fighter, which is the class's actual name, and vocal in the chats. Her team rolled the land quadrant and the Sandcastle of the Mad Dune Mage, with giant snakes, spiders, scorpion men with nipple rings, and four levels of walls. She holds a Club Vanquisher ring, being a proper lady by her own account. Her name takes up half his screen, so he renames her Gwen.

beats.headline: What is in the town hall
beats.text: Skarn lends Carl his telescope for a look out at the Wasteland, and explains why the gnomes riding it leave this town and the Bactrian village alone. It is not mercy. It is what both places keep in their town halls.

beats.headline: Catcher at eleven, Eva on chat
beats.text: My gold Survivor's box holds a skill potion I have to drink on the spot, and it takes Catcher, the skill I have been training relentlessly, to eleven. The rest is gold, water-breathing scrolls and antidote potions, which Mordecai reads as a warning about poison. I asked the former Daughters whether any of them are in this bubble. Nobody answered. Eva is still alive. She is still on my chat. My find crawler shows eight others nearby, all in their low twenties, and I don't know any of them.

beats.headline: The yardstick for everything else
beats.text: Crawler Carl measures loot against it now. A ring with two benefits on it lands above the Ring of Divine Suffering and below the Kimaris figure. Then Pawna's Tears, a potion from the goddess of peace, becomes the first item he has seen valued higher than the stuffed demon on the horse. Mordecai tells him to save it.

beats.headline: Pawna's Tears, saved
beats.text: Every box on this floor is handing out water-breathing scrolls and antidotes. That's the floor telling you what's coming, kid. Then Carl opens his deity box and I have to ask to hold it. Pawna's Tears. Goddess of peace, Grull's sister and enemy. Plus five to any skill he picks, and unlike a Cheat Code it doesn't have to be drunk on the spot. Train something to fifteen, take it, and it's twenty. Single best piece of loot he's had since he came in. Not including the pet biscuit, the cat says. Fine. We decide after he picks his subclass.

beats.headline: From the deity's box
beats.text: Surviving a physical attack by a god earns Carl the Indomitable achievement and a Legendary Deity's Box. In it is a potion in a rounded, ornate bottle, like expensive perfume, smoke rising from the glass. Mordecai's talon shakes as he holds it. Pawna, he explains, is the goddess of peace, Grull's sister and arch enemy. Don't take it now. Save it. It is valued above the Kimaris figure, and it can be saved, unlike a Cheat Code: Carl can train a skill to fifteen and take it to twenty.

beats.headline: Astral Paw, and no swimming
beats.text: My spellbook of the floor is a good one this time, and I read it before Carl can make his speech. Astral Paw. Mordecai says it's a utility spell like Hole, with more force than Astral Hand, and claws at level five. Carl says that at home I could finally knock the vase off the high shelf. That vase was haunted. Then a boss box gives me a Scroll of Water Breathing, and I announce that cats do not swim and it is not going to happen. Mordecai tells me not to say that sort of thing out loud.

beats.headline: One of the children who lived
beats.text: Subject is a child of Hump Town. Her village was bombed by the gnomes, the dromedarians took in what was left, and not many of the children lived. She did. Flint says she is destined to spend her life in Weird Shit Alley.

beats.headline: Cats do not swim
beats.text: Among Donut's boss boxes is a scroll that fills Carl with dread: a Scroll of Water Breathing. I am a cat, Donut announces the moment she gets it; cats do not swim, cats do not go in water. Katia receives several more of the scrolls along with antidote potions, making them this floor's version of the torch and the bandage, and Carl gets a handful. Sometimes things like these scrolls are a not-so-subtle hint about what is on a level, Mordecai says.

beats.headline: He runs the telescope
beats.text: Subject is a juvenile changeling who takes the shape of a boy of about eight, orphaned when the gnomes bombed his village, and now living in Hump Town with a dromedarian named Flint, whose opinions he quotes constantly. He operates the telescope on the roof. He likes to watch the patrol through it to make sure they are okay, and, on Flint's advice, he charges a gold coin for the view.

beats.headline: Twenty-five bottle caps
beats.text: Carl's gold sniper's box holds a crafting item: a case of twenty-five small black items, each about the size of a bottle cap. A Surefire adds the Guided status to any projectile, powered or not. On an arrow or a bolt, the target is chosen before the shot; on a trap, new options open up; on a rocket, targets are set while crafting or on firing, but not both. It adds no range. Cool, Carl says, and moves on to his platinum boxes.

beats.headline: Smushed for Daddy
beats.text: Being stepped upon by a deity and surviving earns Carl the Smushed for Daddy achievement and a platinum Spicy Box, which he got, as he puts it, because the system AI is a goddamned pervert. Inside is a toe ring with a long tale of a human thief who broke into a floating garden. Two benefits in one item, says Mordecai; that is almost legendary tier. Sticky Feet: once every six hours, for his dexterity times two seconds, Carl may walk on a wall or ceiling, bare feet only. Super Spreader passes his active debuffs to a target once an hour. Gross, he says, and slides it onto his left pinky.

beats.headline: Another magic book
beats.text: Donut's final box, a platinum one, contains another magic book: a fifteen-mana spell called Wall of Fire. That's an escape spell, Mordecai says, a wall about ten metres wide and two metres high that lasts fifteen seconds at level one. It is common, and it grows powerful, but it is fire, and fire spreads: cast on something flammable, it stays on fire when the magic goes away. He has seen it a hundred times: fire gets out of control very easily. It's not Fireball, Donut grumbles. She glows as she reads the book.

beats.headline: The castle is the aircraft
beats.text: The flying home of the dirigible gnomes and a heavily armed military platform, and there is no seam between the two. It holds the air quadrant of the bubble, and the stairs down sit inside it, which settles what anyone wanting to leave the floor is going to have to do about it.

beats.headline: A dead boss in a broken egg
beats.text: A gnome biplane drops out of nowhere with two egg-shaped things slung under it, and my explosives skill doesn't twitch. Donut teleports us to the ridge, my hob-lobber goes off too low and behind, and the plane limps away trailing smoke. The egg bounces and does nothing. Donut's clockwork Mongos crack it open: inside is a goose, a level 45 neighborhood boss, killed by the landing. The deployment device is rusty and broken. I take the goose and the shell. It feels like we're on rails. Then eight more planes start circling down, and we run for Hump Town.

beats.headline: Keep it away from the market
beats.text: The new marketplace interface would finally put a price on everything in Carl's inventory, and the Cookbook warns against using it while carrying the Cookbook. Batbilge, twelfth edition, found the market values the tome as a unique heirloom at something like fifty million gold, and did not like giving a third party that kind of look into his inventory. Allister, thirteenth edition, added that this appears to be Batbilge's last entry, and that he leaves his cards on his bed whenever he trades. For Allister it took the form of a deck of cards. Carl plans to use his bedside table.

beats.headline: The desert quadrant
beats.text: Crawler Firas. Fifth floor, desert quadrant. Located in the company of Crawler Louis and Langley's team, a party of car salesmen who have taken up the bow, at the moment Crawler Carl's group came looking for other crawlers. Keeps close to Louis. Present for the march on the Bactrian town and for the run back to Hump Town that followed it. The file on this one is thin. So is the file on most of you.

beats.headline: A buzzsaw overhead
beats.text: A plane rockets by a hundred feet over their heads, whining like a flying buzzsaw. It must have dropped from the Wasteland: an open-air biplane, an engine nestled between the wings on each side, a red-hatted gnome pilot and a second gnome facing backward. A screaming grey animal like a jacked-up rabid koala is painted on its nose, and two egg-shaped objects hang under it in small nets. Carl's smoke curtains do not hide them. As it lines up thirty feet off the ground, Donut teleports them away, and the object it drops where they stood clangs, bounces once, and does nothing.

beats.headline: Smoke from one engine
beats.text: Carl's full-strength hob-lobber goes off in mid-air, much too low and behind the fast plane, but the biplane shudders and smoke trails from one of its two engines. It banks away and climbs, fleeing the fight. The metallic egg it dropped is the size of a garbage can, and nothing moves. Katia, watching the plane, sees it turning into a balloon; it has dropped the second bomb way over there, and that did not go off either. Their engine went out, says Carl; they are deploying their escape balloon.

beats.headline: Regroup
beats.text: The party finds the other crawlers in town, among them Firas, Louis, and Langley's team of car salesmen who have taken up the bow. Carl, Donut and Katia set out for the Bactrian town without them, and a Thorny Devil and a Gnomish Drop Bear turn them back short of it, so they run for here instead.

beats.headline: Never going to fly
beats.text: In the Spit and Swallow two drunk crawlers have a changeling on a lap, describing famous women for her to become. She looks me up and down, spits on the floor, and moves to the other side of the room. Mordecai warned me shapeshifters sometimes don't like each other. Donut says she's jealous. Maybe. Changelings gain some of the abilities of whatever they become. I weigh more than most flying creatures my size, even with no mass added; I would need something like a dragon, and there isn't time. I'm never going to be able to fly, not like them.

beats.headline: A team of car salesmen with bows
beats.text: Subject leads a six-man team of archers, all of whom sold cars in Helsinki and all of whom picked the Archer Class together, which is either loyalty or a failure of imagination and has worked out the same either way. They come into the fifth floor as strangers to the court and do not stay strangers.

beats.headline: We'll be there, Carl
beats.text: Okay so, me and Firas are in a bar in Hump Town, and the lady on my lap is doing Jessica Rabbit, which, much better than the slave Leia. Then Carl walks in. I told Firas that was Carl. He wants everybody at the Toe after the recap. The Toe, man. It's a camel town. Get it? Firas does not get it. I ask if he's gonna blow us up, and the cat jumps on the table, spills the vodka and calls us chuckleheads. We'll be there, Carl.

beats.headline: Spiky lizard eats the copies
beats.text: Two Mongos, not Mongo. Big spiky lizard. Copies BITE. Lizard CRUNCH copy. Lizard CRUNCH other copy. Mongo HOWL. MOTHER says stay back. Mongo stays. Pieces on sand. Mongo sad.

beats.headline: Selling to the armies
beats.text: The marketplace interface is on Donut's account, because her Charisma goes into the prices. For now it's a virtual general store. Once the sixth floor opens, the tourists and the factions trade through it too, and anything magical you list gets snapped up, because this is how they outfit their armies. Yes, kid, you might be selling to people you'll fight. If you don't sell your gear, somebody else will, and they'll mostly be using it on each other. Once the ninth floor opens the factions can't buy new gear at all. I'll explain that when you get there.

beats.headline: We'll be there, Carl
beats.text: Carl asks nicely, and Louis asks whether he's going to blow them up. So I jump onto their table, which scatters their glasses and spills vodka everywhere, and I explain. Carl won't hurt them. But anyone who isn't part of the team will be kicked out of town, and I haven't seen a mob out there lower than level thirty, and these two chuckleheads are level twenty-two. Then I tell them exactly what to say. We'll be there, Carl. Louis says it. Lovely. Chuckleheads is from the AI, not Elle. I've been waiting to use it.

beats.headline: Hulking out
