beats.text: The others secured an intact Drop Bear, its pilot nowhere to be found, and Langley had it covered with a tarp before the storm. It runs on actual gasoline. Carl fills the tank only a quarter of the way to keep it light, and there are no bombs left under the wings. On the nose, over a frothing, rabid koala, the stencilled name reads Death Trap, with four bombs painted after it. Carl sprays over it and writes Nightmare II on the side. Donut objects, but only half-heartedly. He has to rip off both armrests to fit in the pilot's seat.

beats.headline: Up on the emergency balloons
beats.text: There is no runway. Donut takes the rear-facing gunner's chair and makes shooting noises. Carl yanks the lever beside his seat like a car's emergency brake, the twin emergency balloons hiss full, and the plane jerks upward tail first; on the way up Donut finds there are still bullets in the gun, and don't you dare, says Carl. At the ceiling of the bubble, about five kilometres above the bowl, the plane, still tied to its balloons, skitters along on its engines like a bicycle on training wheels toward the glowing balloon of the flying house. Donut jumps from her seat onto its net, and Carl follows from the nose.

beats.headline: Why the changelings want her flesh
beats.text: Juice Box lays out the arithmetic. The changelings want Quetzalcoatlus given a body so that they can touch her, because touching a thing is how a changeling adds it to the shapes it can wear. And they need what she carries: a great many of them are sick with compression sickness, and they believe she has a spell that alters living things which can be turned on the illness. A wailing shrieker over a tomb, wanted for her hands and for her medicine.

beats.headline: Compression sickness
beats.text: Subject is a changeling, and she has compression sickness: in her default form she has no arms and her head is sunken. One birth in four now arrives this way, and the ones born with it are sterile. I note it because nobody else in the building will.

beats.headline: Three more, all broken
beats.text: The toy company has sent three more robot Donuts, and Mongo has promptly destroyed two. The third, supposedly more durable, has survived one attack. It jumps onto Carl's shoulder, wondering how long the babies will continue to cry in the dark, until he pushes it off and Mongo shakes it by the neck. The head rips, a countdown appears, and it explodes in sparks and smoke, scorching the front of the Spit and Swallow. Its marble-sized controller core has popped like popcorn. Loita says the sponsor now has to make the doll self-destruct if it is sufficiently broken, to keep Carl out of its parts.

beats.headline: If you must choose, Ivy
beats.text: Okay, so, the audience loves the strange vibe of the doll, but I tend to agree with the crawler: it does not sound like Princess Donut. We put that in the notes. Veriluxx hasn't changed it. Carl says he can't imagine it doing well, presented the way it is, and I tell him he is not wrong. There are memes. When Princess Donut asks whether she should name her robot Charlie or Ivy, I tell her it is inconsequential, crawler. Then, before the chat closes: if you must choose a name, I would go with Ivy.

beats.headline: She brings them inside
beats.text: Subject is a juvenile Dirigible Gnome of the air quadrant, daughter of a commandant. She is the one who brings the crawlers in through the door, and what they find on the other side of it is her father, already dead, ripped to shreds by her new pet, which has gone out for food. The girl's eyes are dilated and she is setting up a lemonade stand. She is under a spell. Nobody discusses the alternative.

beats.headline: Head first into the disposal
beats.text: The boss is Denise, a feral goose in a blue bonnet, and the rules say no magic and no physical damage, with three minutes before the house hits the ground. I grab the lemonade, because it has to be the answer. It's lemonade. The AI calls that a Wild Goose Chase. What actually hurts her is anything that was already in the house: a mug, the pitcher. Bonnie pointed at the sink earlier. I remember the two switches beside it, shove Denise head-first into the drain, and yell at Donut to flip them. The garbage disposal does the rest.

beats.headline: On the kitchen table
beats.text: Lootable Corpse. Commandant Kane. Dirigible Gnome. Level 55. Ripped to shreds by Denise. Found draped across his own kitchen table, half eaten, while his daughter set up a lemonade stand beside him. Asked why Denise killed her father, the girl pointed at the kitchen sink. Crawler Carl looted him by accident, falling into the body when the house lurched: 5,030 gold, a Mysterious Watch, and a Letter from the Glass Wizard telling him his bombs were weakening the temple, and to stop, and think of his people and his child.

beats.headline: Ripped to shreds by Denise
beats.text: Subject enters the record on another creature's corpse tag: Commandant Kane, ripped to shreds by Denise. Asked who Denise is, the Commandant's daughter, eyes dilated, said she went out to get some food. When the child's pig was taken, her father kept getting her new pets. Not the gerbils; they were mean. Other things, including ol' Denise. She's okay. She's no Sausage. Do not tell her that, though. She gets jealous.

beats.headline: When she gets mad
beats.text: The floating house began to sink. That's Denise, the child explained: when she gets mad, magic stuff doesn't work, and the balloon goes down; she is probably on the roof. Somewhere in the house the clockwork Mongos exploded early and tore up the real one. Mordecai briefed the party: no spells, no scrolls, no gauntlet, gear protections gone. Scrolls on the bleeding Mongo did nothing. Then the flying lemonade glass moved itself away from Crawler Carl's hand, the window slammed, and the doors locked.

beats.headline: The Feral Goose Mother
beats.text: A white goose in a frilly baby-blue bonnet and a torn, bloodied shawl. Level 53 Borough Boss. Plucked from the seventh floor when her grandfather, emperor Anser, used a magical gate to bring his people here, she lingered too long in the Nothing, and her mind is all but gone. The gnomes captured her without knowing who she is. Neither does she. She can prevent magic from harming her. She is an environmental. She needs to protect children. Mostly, she wants to kill everybody.

beats.headline: No health bar
beats.text: Mongo got her by the neck and shook her; she bounced back up. Subject's bill opened into a flower of razor teeth and fired them like a shotgun. A banger ricocheted off her bill. No health bar appeared. She took a chunk out of Mongo, and a thrown mug knocked her off the kitchen table and launched the Commandant's corpse into the ceiling. She chased the party upstairs, hopping one step at a time, and put two barbs in Crawler Carl's face. Only then did a health bar appear, barely dented.

beats.headline: The garbage disposal
beats.text: The lemonade was a trick: Wild Goose Chase, magic doesn't work, it's lemonade. Crawler Carl hit subject with the pitcher, took her teeth across the face, lost his left eye's sight, and held her bill shut by hand. He remembered the child pointing at the sink, and saw the two switches. Subject went into the drain face first. Princess Donut flipped both switches. The timer stopped at one second. The Commandant's quarters are occupied. The Air Quadrant is liberated.

beats.headline: A truce, by letter
beats.text: Kane. Cease your hostilities. Your bombs do not harm me, but they are ruining the structure of the temple, weakening its wall, and surely even in your floating city you understand the danger if it collapses. So I propose a truce: you stop the bombing, and I won't end this world. I have the winding box. I have cracked its secret. I know how to open a portal, and I do not need your watches to throw this entire world into the void, which I will do before I allow that ghost to leave the temple. Think of your people. Of her. Stop.

beats.headline: It doesn't work
beats.text: A door glows behind them, locked until the fight is over, and Mongo is hurt. Donut is more taken up with him than with the fight. He no longer seems to be in pain, but he is bleeding. Carl, Mongo won't stop bleeding, she cries. My pet carrier doesn't work! His health is still going down. Carl tosses a broken side table onto the stairs and tells her to try one of the bandages. They each have hundreds of them.

beats.headline: Goose NOT FOOD
beats.text: Brothers go POP. Hurts. Goose. BITE goose. Shake goose. Goose gets up. Goose has teeth. MOTHER pulls tail. Up the stairs. Rabbit. Mine.

beats.headline: My heal spell stopped working
beats.text: The goose turns off magic, and the two clockwork Mongos explode early and hurt my baby. My heal spell will not work. My Heal Critter scroll fizzles. My pet carrier does not work. Mongo is bleeding and his health keeps going down, and CARL shouts at me to use a bandage, so I do, and it works. I rip a hole in the bedroom floor so we can drop back into the kitchen. And who flips the garbage disposal switch while Carl holds the goose's head in the sink? Me.

beats.headline: It fizzles
beats.text: The monster blocks magic, Carl tells Mordecai, and Mordecai answers that it likely means no spells, no scrolls. Mongo rushes into the kitchen screaming, bleeding from dozens of places where the other two clockwork Mongos exploded. Donut's heal spell has stopped working. She rushes to him, his health about halfway down, and glows as she tries a Heal Critter scroll. The spell fizzles out. His health is going back up on its own, Carl tells her; stop wasting scrolls, they won't work. Do you want some lemonade, Bonnie asks again.

beats.headline: The air quadrant liberated
beats.text: The last piece of the Wasteland comes down in a hurry and stops just short. With Denise dead in the kitchen's garbage disposal, the Commandant's quarters count as occupied, and a bubble notification congratulates crawlers Princess Donut and Carl on taking the throne room. The Air Quadrant is liberated, and every crawler who started there may now travel freely into the other quadrants. Then the house bumps gently onto the ground.

beats.headline: Denise killed my dad
beats.text: Subject Bonnie is waking from her father's potion in Skarn's house, where Juice Box is showing her a cot. It is not her bed, so Crawler Carl pulls her own pink bed and nightstand out of his inventory. She states that Denise killed her father, that he knew it was coming and could do nothing, that he told her to make lemonade and gave her the potion so she would stop being scared, and she asks for another one. Juice Box says no. Skarn tells her his parents died when his town was bombed, and that the camels are grumpy but not mean.

beats.headline: A walnut on a string
beats.text: The suburban house has come down cockeyed on a dune half a mile east of Hump Town, and since Denise died its magical balloon has been slowly refilling. The ropes are like steel cables. Carl tells Bonnie they have to leave; she pulls a walnut-like necklace from her shirt, fiddles with it, and the house settles. Her dad gave it to her with the potion, she says, and told her to give it to an adult. Inside a sliding clamshell is a little purple-hued gem, a soul crystal. It stopped feeding the balloon under the goose's anti-magic aura. Carl keeps it, the shell open just a fraction: enough, he hopes, to keep the balloon off the ground but not to lift the house.

beats.headline: The moment I change my mind
beats.text: I strip the house: two laptops, three televisions, the gaming consoles, the bikes, a kayak, the Christmas tree and the electrical panel, whose outlets keep working as long as they stay attached. No guns, though the doormat says they had some. At Skarn's house I set down Bonnie's own bed and the picture of her with her mother and father. Loita tells us to stop concerning ourselves with NPCs. When I look back, the girl is sobbing into Juice Box, holding the pink rabbit Mongo gave her. I'd been toying with an idea and dismissed it as too risky. That's the moment I change my mind.

beats.headline: A drawing in a frame
beats.text: Addendum, from the house. On subject's nightstand, in a frame meant for a photo, a drawing he had put there himself: Kane, a woman gnome, and a baby. His watch is bronze, carries a bone symbol, and does not tick. His daughter, waking from his potion, supplies the rest. Denise killed him. He knew she was going to. He said there was nothing he could do, told her to make lemonade, and when she started to cry he gave her the potion, and she was not scared anymore.

beats.headline: Supposed to drown her
beats.text: Post-mortem. The house's power crystal had shut itself off under subject's anti-magic aura; with her gone, the balloon began refilling on its own. Princess Donut's assessment of the fight is that the goose was meant to be drowned, in the sink or the lemonade pitcher, and not put through the garbage disposal. When the child woke, she told the party her father knew Denise was going to kill him and could do nothing, and asked for another potion.

beats.headline: Mongo, as a threat
beats.text: Subject Loita announces that Crawler Princess Donut has a new doll to spend time with, and that if it works the pair will do the show a day early. When the cat talks back, Loita tells her she keeps forgetting her place. When the cat says she smells, Loita says the feeling is mutual, and that if she talks back again Mongo will be taken from her and fed to a mob on the next floor while she watches. She refuses to send Zev down for a goodbye. At Bonnie's bedside, she tells the crawlers that audiences like drama, not melodrama.

beats.headline: Rabbit for small gnome
beats.text: Small gnome sad. Crying smell. Rabbit from her room. Rabbit NOT FOOD. Put rabbit down. Small gnome holds rabbit.

beats.headline: Veriluxx, and who owns it
beats.text: Kid, don't press your luck with that panel. It's a non-enhanced toy; set off the self-destruct and I honestly don't know what the AI does with it. Most toys need a licensed enhancement zone, and some need a license key in the kid to prove his parents paid their taxes. This one needs neither. As for Veriluxx: never heard of them, but the logo says Veritan Linkage, a mostly-Soother lending fund that advocates enslaving people who can't pay their taxes. Odds are it's a way to funnel money to Borant. Carl asks if the whole universe is assholes. Just the ones with the money.

beats.headline: Back down on its own
beats.text: Marching back to Hump Town, Donut spots the airplane slowly descending from the sky. It is the Nightmare II. It came loose from the main balloon during the boss fight, and its emergency balloon has finally lost its juice and is letting it down. Carl sends Louis and Firas out to secure it and drag it back to the house. It should fit in the large garage, safe from the next storm, and it will give them something to do.

beats.headline: Third, above the cat
beats.text: Miriam and I scale the inside wall of our bubble. A debuff puts the spiders to sleep, and they plummet to their deaths, every one of them, and somehow that finishes the subterranean zone as well. Now we go underwater. The list is posted: third, Prepotente, Caprid, Forsaken Aerialist, level thirty-eight, four hundred thousand. Carl is second. The cat is fourth.

beats.headline: Wall climbers and an absence
beats.text: The recap features the fight on the falling house. Prepotente and Miriam Dom are as far along as Carl's party: they scaled their bubble's inner wall, sent every spider plummeting in its sleep, finished the subterranean zone with it, and are preparing to go underwater. Lucia Mar shatters a multi-limbed ice mummy and is working with a group. Quan Ch has already popped his bubble and is flying around farming every mob he can find. The top ten: Lucia Mar first, Carl second, Prepotente third, Donut fourth. Florin the crocodilian has dropped off it.

beats.headline: Three times the weight
beats.text: The newest version weighs about three times as much as the last and is slightly bigger. Mongo attacks it at once and does no obvious damage. It still throws out bootleg Garfield quotes. A small panel on the back of its head is held shut by a cheap little tab, like a battery compartment; when Carl clicks it open, a warning gives five seconds until self-destruct, and he shoves it back. Patted on the head, it moans. Mordecai says the logo on the box suggests Veriluxx is associated with Veritan Linkage, a lending fund that advocates enslaving those who can't pay their taxes.

beats.headline: Goodbye, from behind the scenes
beats.text: Anyway, the fans really enjoyed that battle. Good job, you two. I'm sorry to say this is goodbye, however. I will still be Loita's assistant, working behind the scenes, but you no longer need a social media manager. Loita explains it: they have bought the social media board, so nobody needs to relay what the dry masses are saying about them. Carl asks whether I can come down so Princess Donut can say goodbye. Loita says no, of course not. He asks whether I can come to the infomercial. Loita says it is not my job anymore.

beats.headline: A commercial that goes off script
beats.text: Before we transfer, I set off a disco ball in the crafting room, a smoke curtain soaked in an invisibility potion, and it coats the robot and me in rainbow dust. In the trailer I lean over Loita to ask whether these things can go into space. I leave robot Donut next to her with orders to stay. On set I go off script and ask about Veriluxx's parent company and slavery, until the lights go red. The couch is gone. Loita is blackened, missing an arm and both lower legs, and alive. She says I did this. I tell her it was an accident.

beats.headline: A window with no glass
beats.text: Nineteenth edition, entry one of three. The subject went on a program tonight. They transported him to a ship floating in low orbit over his planet, with an open window that has no glass and is protected only by a forcefield. He calls it amazing. He can look down on his beautiful, lost planet. If he is to die here, he wants this to be his last view. Crawler Carl is at that moment about to be transferred to a sponsor's trailer, with the admin Loita, for a toy commercial.

beats.headline: Bugbear paste in his boots
beats.text: Entry two. Another program tonight. He has secreted bugbear paste into his boots and means to detonate them while in orbit. There are to be two admins on board. His Blast Shield skill should protect him from the explosion, if the skill works at all in that place; he does not know. If he blows the ship, it does not matter. Think of me, brothers, he writes. It is little, but it is all he has. Crawler Carl leaves robot Donut on the couch next to Loita and goes to do the commercial.

beats.headline: The admins were holos
beats.text: Entry three, and the last on file. He has blown the ship. His skill protected him, but the forcefield kept the ship from breaking apart, and the two admins who appeared to be with him were holograms. He was fooled, and he is ashamed. The gravity has failed, the temperature is dropping, and it is getting difficult to breathe. He does not think they can remove him while the forcefield holds. He can see his beloved Qurux. It shines and warms him in the cold. He prays someone avenges her, because he cannot.

beats.headline: Not god. Coolie.
beats.text: Robot Donut explodes in the green room. A massive crack runs across the picture window, and the blue forcefield is the only thing keeping the water out. It holds. Crawler Carl's first thought is to thank god, and his second corrects it: not god, Coolie. The admin Loita dies on the floor of that room, unable to teleport while the shield is up. Crawler Carl adds a note of his own to the Cookbook, addressed to the subject: he used this passage to plan the first step, and he did it for Coolie and for a little girl named Bonnie.

beats.headline: Coolie's last notes, and Carl's first
beats.text: Three notes by Crawler Coolie, nineteenth edition, run through the pages: a program on a ship in low orbit, its open window held by a forcefield; bugbear paste in his boots for the two admins on his next show; then failure. The admins were holos, the forcefield kept the ship whole, and he wrote as the air thinned, looking down at his planet, Qurux. Beneath them now sits a note from Crawler Carl, twenty-fifth edition: Coolie's passage helped plan the first step, and it was done for him and for a little girl named Bonnie. Then a second note, one word long. One.

beats.headline: Rainbow in the crafting room
beats.text: Carl has been infusing smoke curtains since he read about the idea in the cookbook, mostly into duds. This one he stole the recipe for and has to pretend he stumbled on: a red smoke curtain soaked in an invisibility potion, now shining with a multi-coloured opalescence. His Infusion skill rises to level 3. Robot Donut, watching from the table, hops up and down to cheer, the ball goes flying to the floor, and Carl steps back right onto it. Rainbow smoke fills the room, Mordecai curses over his alchemy table, and it leaves a sandy, technicolor residue on everything. The common area smells of burnt cotton candy.

beats.headline: Soaked into a smoke curtain
beats.text: At the infusing trays Carl soaks a Hobgoblin smoke curtain in an invisibility potion, and his Infusion skill rises to level three. The ball, normally red, comes out shining with a multicoloured opalescence: a Hobgoblin Disco Ball, heavy multi-hued smoke that hides all movement inside and bounces to the beat, and blinds its caster as well as the monsters. Infusing smoke curtains makes them inherently unstable, which is why he is not yet trying it with real explosives.

beats.headline: The toy on the couch
beats.text: Subject Loita, outreach associate of the Borant Corporation and member of the Bloom, waits in a rented undersea trailer while the crawlers tape a toy commercial, Crawler Carl having left the cat doll beside her with orders to stay. She has just told them that their culture is a rot upon the Bloom, and that bringing Zev back into the fold took unspeakable things done to Zev's mother and aunts. The doll explodes. The trailer's shield holds the cracked window, and repair ships are on their way. Her last words: the Bloom will prevail. Crawler Carl tells her nobody likes melodrama.

beats.headline: What they did to Zev
beats.text: The fish lady will not let me bring Mongo to meet his own doll, and then she tells us why she is so angry. We are dry. We are a rot. And to bring Zev back into the fold, they did unspeakable things to her mother and her aunts, and only then did Zev take the badge. I ask Carl whether she is a complete loon. On set, a lady in a cow-print cape says I am one of her two favorites; the other is Lucia Mar. I read my line: This sure is a hoot. Then the lights go red, and I cannot cast a thing.

beats.headline: A dud infusion
beats.text: Two smoke curtains are infusing at Carl's table, an idea from the cookbook he has been experimenting with. In the first he is trying a smoke curtain with a splash of the Rev-Up immunity smoothie he made on the second floor, the potion that gives temporary disease immunity and makes you drunk off your ass. He can tell right away it is a bust: the curtain is blacked out and has gained the Dud status, which is what usually happens. The second infusion, a recipe from the cookbook, works.

beats.headline: Left beside Loita
beats.text: Carl sets robot Donut on the green-room couch next to Loita and tells it to stay by her. It asks her if she has ever felt true cold. On the set of the Veriluxx New Toys Showcase, holo dolls of Donut and Mongo bounce on the table, and Carl goes off script: he likes how compliant the toy is, and isn't compliance the thing of their parent company, Veritan Linkage? Then the lights flicker and the studio goes red. In the green room the couch is obliterated, and Loita lies blackened, missing her left arm and both bottom legs, still alive.

beats.headline: The controller left with Louis
beats.text: In the personal space, Katia catches Carl up. Once she learned they would not know his fate for a few days, she took matters into her own hands and tried flying the house to the land quadrant. It would not let them at first, until they worked out what was wrong. If Carl had not left the controller with Louis, she says, they never could have flown the thing. Louis and Firas have turned into quite the pilots, and they are already on the way back to pick him up.

beats.headline: A fingernail for a shim
beats.text: Orren's version is polymers, and residue eating a panel. The truth is dumber. The back panel on robot Donut was junk. I cut my left thumbnail three-quarters through, practiced on a spare panel on the toilet, and when I leaned over Loita the second time, I broke the nail off as a shim under the tab. The disco dust was only there so they wouldn't want the doll in the studio. I told it to stay by her, and I gave her a reason to get off the couch. I tell Orren I wish I'd thought of it.

beats.headline: The source he protects
beats.text: Pressed to name his outside source, and offered a Legendary box for it, Crawler Carl does not give it up. If he names the Cookbook, it disappears. The version put to him, with polymers and technicolor residue reacting to space plastic, is more complicated than what happened. What he actually knew was simpler: the forcefield, thanks to the subject's passage, and that a disco ball covers everything in dust, from the same book. The rest was a toy panel he already knew was a piece of shit.

beats.headline: The dust did the job
beats.text: Administrator Loita is dead, killed when the Donut toy that followed her off the couch exploded, and Orren lays out how. The disco ball's residue slowly ate at the panel on the back of the toy's head, the moisture of the admin's rebreather ran it along the edges, and the jump dislodged the panel and set off the self-destruct. One of the most brilliant assassinations he has ever seen a crawler execute, he says. Carl knows better. He only wanted the dust all over the toy so nobody would want it in the studio, and had not realised the dust was already doing the job for him.

beats.headline: Five days on my own
beats.text: Carl and Donut vanished from chat, Mordecai disappeared, and none of them showed as dead. Once I learned we would not know for days, I took matters into my own hands. The house would not fly to the land quadrant at first. It was the stairwell in the master bedroom; we almost died working that out, and the fix is what Louis did to his mother's minivan. Without the controller Carl left with Louis, we could not have flown it at all. Five days of scorpion men and arguing with Gwen. Level 41. Zev says she is our temporary PR agent.

beats.headline: A liaison hold
beats.text: I didn't think I'd see you again, kid. I got a notice there was a liaison hold on Donut, and then five days were gone. Only the fifth floor, and the liaisons are already involved. By his left tit. Next thing you know, the lawyers will be here, and everything gets complicated once the lawyers get here. A Syndicate liaison, and he let you walk right out? Then the kid pulls Loita's rebreather out of his waistband. He looted it off her body.

beats.headline: He cannot prove it was on purpose
beats.text: Crawler Carl and Crawler Princess Donut have been brought before me at the Desperado Club to account for the death of Loita. My position is that it was deliberate. My position is not evidence. I cannot establish intent, and so I am required to release them, which I am doing, with a note in the file. They have only now worked out how long they have been outside the dungeon. Five days. Their faces are the one part of this I have enjoyed.

beats.headline: Fifteen this season
beats.text: Not counting Administrator Loita, fifteen admins have died to crawlers this season. Crawler Lucia Mar accounts for two, three if one counts her first game guide, which we do not; she signed a confession both times. For every one of them we know exactly how it was done. For this one I can describe a mechanism and cannot establish that it was intended. I offered Crawler Carl a Legendary box for the name of his source. He declined. Until the next floor, no crawler will be teleported out by third parties, and Crawler Carl's next appearance on Odette's program is cancelled. My personal recommendation was not followed.

beats.headline: No admins lost
beats.text: Orren the liaison, making Carl sit through a lesson on assassinated admins. Two seasons ago, a crocodilian bit the head off his outreach associate, and the Fortent admins lost two security agents on top of that: three dead, which is a lot. Last season, the Squim Conglomerate had no admin fatalities due to crawler attacks at all. Orren asks Carl to guess this season's number. Zero, says Carl. It stands at fifteen, not counting Admin Loita, and Lucia Mar has killed two.

beats.headline: The liaison under the hood
beats.text: Orren, the Syndicate liaison who questions Carl over Loita's death, lets slip that the kua-tin intervened on the crawler's behalf and overruled his recommendation to remove him, and that the mudskippers are not known for recognising threats. If the rumors are correct and his own people take over after the next floor, he hopes they will listen to him. Then his hood slips. The swirling darkness is a face-shaped bowl of liquid, and in it Carl glimpses a worm. A Valtay worm.

beats.headline: The panel falls off
beats.text: Orren lays it out. Loita jumped down off the couch, the toy jumped after her, the panel on the back of its head dislodged, and a few seconds after that it exploded, killing her. Sitting on Carl's sapper's bench had raised its yield. Carl calls the panel a cheap piece of crap. What he does not say is that he shimmed the tab with a cut-down thumbnail as he set the toy beside her, knowing the heavy robot would jump the moment she stood up.

beats.headline: All four castles, and the cost
beats.text: All four castles in my bubble are cleared. I report it in the chat. Most of the people in the bubble did not survive to see it done. How that sits with me is not the kind of thing a chat window was made for, so I leave it out.

beats.headline: Mr. Banana and the flesh weasels
beats.text: Subject and a crawler named Mike, who is dressed as a banana, gather several water-breathing scrolls and leave the saferooms at the top of the subterranean quadrant. In a water-filled tunnel they set off a trap. A tube shoots from the wall, pierces Mike's stomach, and fills him with Finger-sized Flesh Weasels, which eat him from the inside out. Subject retreats quickly. The rest of the party stays in its saferooms, paralyzed, waiting for somebody else to drain the place.

beats.headline: Not as indispensable as I thought
beats.text: The house comes down for us with its whole top half hacked off, because the stairwell was in the master-bedroom closet and the quadrant would not let it leave attached. Firas fills us in. Katia got the house down to the land quadrant and worked out how to breach the castle's door, all without us, and they would be finished already if Zev hadn't asked her to wait. Part of me is proud. Part of me stings that she managed, and I'm horrified I thought it. I decide it's a necessary feeling.

beats.headline: Everybody else in the bubble is dead
beats.text: I finally come out into a quadrant. Everybody else in my bubble is already dead. Not most of them. All of them. That leaves the castles, and one man to take them. I have cleared one so far. I am working my way through the rest. The general view is that I am screwed. I keep going.

beats.headline: Face to face at the sandcastle
beats.text: Crawler Carl lands and finally meets subject: about forty-five, solid, five feet tall, from Canada, a spear over her shoulder, an old double-v tattoo on her forehead and straight-line tattoos down her hands. Level 34 now. Her team has breached the last wall and found a drainage wheel that would wash the castle away, and Crawler Katia has kept her waiting nearly a day so the crawlers can go in the hard way, through the lightning door. Crawler Katia's assessment: once Gwen decides something, she becomes a bully about it.

beats.headline: Holding out for the hard way
beats.text: There are two ways into the sandcastle. Gwen's team found a drainage wheel against the tomb wall: turn it and the water inside blasts out through the drain the castle is built around, and the castle goes like sand under a hose. It also turns the mage, and the winding box, to mud. The hard way is to clip the towers' cables to the door and let the storm's lightning open a glass hallway, once per storm, for a few of us. Zev was unusually insistent that we wait for Carl and Donut, so I made Gwen wait almost a day. Honestly, I would rather do it her way too.

beats.headline: Gustavo, after the battle
beats.text: After a battle, Gustavo kills a group of crawlers. Gustavo is the smaller one. Everybody says he did it by accident. They say accident like it has quotation marks around it. Then I am not all right. I am worse than usual. They show me sitting in a room by myself, and I am crying. They put that on the show.

beats.headline: A cannon full of oil
beats.text: Word reaches Carl through the chat. Meadow Lark are down to the last castle in their bubble, and it is an air castle. The plan is a cannon that shoots oil into the sky, which will hopefully bring it down. If that does not work, Elle is going to use her new Graupel spell to crash the thing. Elsewhere Li Jun and Li Na's team are about to storm an underwater castle, the last in theirs.

beats.headline: Karaoke, and then the curse
beats.text: They put me on a show with Katia and have the two of us sing karaoke. While I am gone, Prepotente has a panic attack and goes berserk and runs off. When I get back I go looking for my boy, and that is when something attacks me and curses me. I was a vegan before all this. The curse has made me a vampire, and I understand the people who chose it for me thought that was very funny.

beats.headline: The house in her inventory
beats.text: Firas, down from the balloon-hung house with water arcing out of it behind him, tells Carl what he missed. It was Louis's idea. With the house floating just off the ground, Katia did that weird thing she does when she puts the backpack on, and it worked: the whole house went into her inventory. That same night, after the recap episode, they patched it, and the whole contraption popped out of her inventory over their heads in a pub called Cuttlefish Point. It almost smooshed them all, and it pretty much blew up the tavern.

beats.headline: Horrors near the ocean floor
beats.text: Subject enters the record by name only, relayed by Firas. The water quadrant left two other survivors, Vadim and Britney, and neither wants to go back in. They say there are horrors deep down near the ocean's floor. Firas had told them about Chris. Neither of them was surprised, which is also on file.

beats.headline: Punch him, take the bag
beats.text: Through the peephole the Mad Dune Mage is a guy in a bathrobe watching cartoons, living on top of a floor that is actually a mob. Katia yanks me back when it comes under the door, and my Protective Shell blasts the ooze away and the door with it. Ghazi runs to us, goes back for a leather bag off a burning table, and pats the flames out. I ask if he has the winding box, because the college needs it to save the world. He pats the bag: it's here. I punch him out, take the bag, and we run up the stairs.

beats.headline: What he wanted
beats.text: They come in through the fountain court, three of them and a dinosaur that shatters my Lika where she stands, and then they find me, so you may as well have all of it. Lika is a half-naiad trobairitz out of the stage plays they put on in the city. A bard cleric under a vow of celibacy, played by a different half-naiad every season, based on a minor deity, and not real. I know she is not real. I wanted Yarilo brought back out and asked to make her real, and to make her mine. I told the College of Magecraft I was studying the Gate of the Feral Gods for stable long-distance transport. What answered when I opened it was not Yarilo. It was something else that had learned to wear the name, and it is why this castle is what it is.

beats.headline: Married to the ooze
beats.text: She tricked me. That is the part I want written down. I asked for Lika and the thing married me to the ooze instead, and my wife is still down in my halls being exactly what she is. The doll in the fountain, the one with a soul sitting in it, that is the nearest thing to a real Lika this world ever managed. Carl knocks me flat and takes the winding box off me while I am out. I wake up with a headache and tell them everything anyway, because who else is there to tell.

beats.headline: Under the door
beats.text: Carl has his eye to the peephole and Donut is talking about Juice Box when I see the sand. It is oozing through the bottom of the door and moving its way up the wood. I pull him back and shout for his shell. The spell pushes the ooze back and blasts the door to pieces. Then Carl knocks the mage out, and I catch him before he lands, throw him over my shoulder and carry him up the stairs while the floor follows us.

beats.headline: The glass lady falls
beats.text: Sniff the glass lady. She WOBBLES. BAD. Back away. CRASH. Glass everywhere. Only her head stays. Carl puts the head away.

beats.headline: He had Tish all along
beats.text: The letter from the council is appalling. Ghazi had Tish the whole time, and he left her for Lika, who is a character in a play. When he wakes up I jump on his chest and tell him exactly that. Then he admits the sand ooze is his wife, because he married it, and that the Lika in the fountain was a companion device. Everybody has worked out what kind. I am the first one to say it out loud, because somebody has to.

beats.headline: The floor was the monster
beats.text: Cast on a stairway as a door explodes inward, the shell sweeps the sand off the floor of the room like a broom and uncovers glass beneath. Suddenly the whole room is red on the map. The sand is a mob, and there is no second cast today.

beats.headline: What the council is afraid of
beats.text: A letter from the council of Ghazi's college sets out the fear. What he summoned was not the god of lust but a banished lesser deity pretending to be him, and the scholars believe she only half crossed over. She will occupy the one creature nearby that stands equally between worlds: the ghost queen of the necropolis. If Quetzalcoatlus gains corporeal form, that deity is fully resurrected and the true gods are forced to react. The council's instruction is that Ghazi use the winding box to banish himself, and the entire necropolis, out of this world.

beats.headline: It's sticky
beats.text: In a glass fountain in this crystal castle stands a statue, with a plaque: Lika, my love, my wife, and a promise to burn and bury anyone who gets in the way. Mongo sniffs it, it wobbles, and over it goes. CRASH. Nearly all of it turns to dust except the head, which keeps its looks apart from a chip out of the chin. Carl puts it in his inventory with a few big pieces of the glass, fulgurite, the inventory calls it. Decapitated glass head depicting Lika from Troubadour's Bounty, says the description. And then: it's sticky. STICKY.

beats.headline: A postscript in another hand
beats.text: Subject exists, at first, as a postscript. Below a council letter to Ghazi, in a different script: Ghazi, you fucking idiot. She told him this would happen. They needed that artifact, without it Scolopendra cannot be defeated, and all he could think about was his cock. She does not forgive him. She was there the whole time, and she guesses she was not enough. She hopes he dies in pain. Do the right thing. Signed, Tish.

beats.headline: So you are from the college
beats.text: Princess Donut read the postscript over Crawler Carl's shoulder and took it personally. When Ghazi came round she jumped on his chest: he had Tish all along, and he left her for Lika, who is not even real. Ghazi's eyes went huge. Tish? So they were from the college? Crawler Carl advised that nobody knew the story beyond one letter. Princess Donut's closing remark on the subject, as Ghazi explained his wife: if Tish could see you now.

beats.headline: Inside Ghazi's room
beats.text: Katia cries Shell, and Carl flies back from the door and slams against the stairs. He hits Protective Shell just as Donut's Wall of Fire bursts up inside the room, and the door explodes. The fire catches the piles of books and tables at once. Ghazi runs into view, shouting, straight through the wall of the shell, trapped on their side of the flames. His dot is still white.

beats.headline: The summoning that went wrong
beats.text: Sandcastle of the Mad Dune Mage. Read Ghazi's description and the whole sad story is in it: he wanted the gate so he could reach Yarilo, the banished god of lust, and have Yarilo make Lika love him. Lika is the heroine of a stage play. She was never real. What came through was not Yarilo either. It gave him a wife made of sand, which is why the ooze follows him about, and it left him trapped in his transformed castle with the knowledge of what he has let out. The plaque under his display says my love, my wife. Crawlers, this is the standard outcome of aiming a summoning at a god of lust. Please make notes.

beats.headline: Bouncing to the beat
beats.text: Carl made five of these at his sapper's table, each labelled with a purpose, and because he built them there he could pick the songs. This one says Bass heavy. For distraction: a hollow banger sphere with an impact-detonated alarm trap inside. Katia lobs it down the stairs at the ooze. Peaking at Number 2 on October 10th, 1992, it's Jump Around. Muffled by the metal, it still shakes the walls, and the ball bounces with the beat, slipping out of the ooze's grasp. Donut asks if that is seriously the only bass-heavy song he could think of.

beats.headline: Bass heavy, for distraction
beats.text: Carl made five of these at his sapper's table, each labelled for a purpose, and because he made them at the table he could pick the songs. This one is a hollow banger sphere with an impact-detonated alarm trap inside, labelled Bass heavy. For distraction. Katia lobs it down the stairs at the ooze, and the announcement comes: Jump Around. Sealed in the metal ball, the music is quieter than usual and still shakes the walls. The ball protects the trap and bounces up and down with the beat, and every time the ooze grabs for it, it slips away. Donut objects to the song in capital letters.

beats.headline: Upside down over the ooze
beats.text: No explosives in the lab, Ghazi says, or the glass comes down on us. So Katia lobs an alarm trap in a metal ball down the stairs to distract the ooze with "Jump Around", Donut holes the floor above, and I go in upside down on Sticky Feet from my toe ring: seventy-something seconds on the ceiling. I pipe Mordecai's burn gel onto the recliner over the core and drop a torch. It burns hotter than I expected. The boss dies just as the roof comes in, and I'm buried upside down in sand.

beats.headline: Flushed into the water quadrant
beats.text: Tran opens the valve part way. The ceiling gives and the water hits like a train. I wrap myself around Donut and we tumble in the flood, my health falling; a spar off the dwarven automaton goes through my leg, and a spear of glass goes through my hand and into Donut. She never took the potion I told her to. Two heal scrolls on her, and we're a hundred and fifty meters down in the water quadrant with dead things sinking all around us. Something big is eating them.

beats.headline: Out of the castle, and no further
beats.text: Ghazi, human, level 43 glass mage, known across the quadrant as the Mad Dune Mage, is dead. The sand ooze went down, the sandcastle came in on itself, and Crawler Katia Grim carried him clear of it. She killed him in the open a moment after that, for the notes in his coat explaining how the artifact is worked. He went to sand. Carl and Princess Donut were still buried under the other end of the building and heard none of it.

beats.headline: This is where I point out
beats.text: Crawler Carl and Princess Donut are in the castle's basement with the ceiling coming in when he sends subject a note. She asks whether he means electrify it. No, he answers, hurry. Tran opens the valve part way, and the castle goes like sand under a garden hose, taking the two of them down into the water quadrant with it. Subject's first message afterwards: this is where she points out that if he had simply let her open the valve in the first place, they could have avoided whatever that was.

beats.headline: Too hot for this job
beats.text: Two jugs left. The sand ooze's core sits under the recliner, and ordinary fire is no good: the ooze has already snuffed out the flames left by Crawler Donut's spell. It needs something that burns hot, and Crawler Carl fears the jugs would burn a little too hot. He uses burn gel instead, a cookbook recipe that Mordecai showed him how to improve. With moonshine and a paste of his, it burns hot and bright with little smoke.

beats.headline: She kills Ghazi and takes his notes
beats.text: The sand ooze is dead and the walls are coming in. I get out with Ghazi. Then I kill him, for the notes that explain how the Gate works. Carl and Donut are still buried when I do it. I know how that sounds.

beats.headline: Do not let it touch you
beats.text: Do not let it touch you. Once a sand ooze gets ahold of you it's like quicksand, and Carl's already burned his Protective Shell. It won't just suffocate you, kid. It pours sand into every opening you've got until you burst, and he's wearing boxers. They hunt by vibration and sound, not heat, so clomping across a ceiling will still get noticed; he'll need one of the toys he was building. And I wouldn't trust a guy who married an ooze. Katia, watch him while Carl's in there.

beats.headline: If your health gets low
beats.text: The ceiling is about to give way over them. Take a water scroll, Carl tells Donut, and do it now; put the rest in your hotlist, fast. If your health gets low, don't take a health potion. Take Mordecai's Special Brew. Donut has changed her mind, she says; she would rather be buried alive than... Carl pulls her from his shoulder and wraps himself around her, muffling the rest, as the ceiling splinters and the sand pours in.

beats.headline: I bite his foot and pull
beats.text: The floor breaks right after I cast my Hole spell, and I fall through with it, and there is sand all around me. Carl is buried upside down, so I bite down on his foot and drag him out. Then we are in a tiny space under three floors of sand, and I did not get to say goodbye to Mongo, and he is just going to sit in his pet carrier forever. And all Carl will ask me is how many water-breathing scrolls I have. Eight.

beats.headline: Eight scrolls
beats.text: With Donut afraid of being buried alive, Carl asks how many water-breathing scrolls she has. They're called water breathing, not sand breathing, she tells him. Eight. Then the water hits, and they are sinking in the water quadrant, Donut unconscious and bleeding. Thankfully she had taken the scroll: with her intelligence it lasts over two and a half minutes. Carl's lasts 54 seconds, and he is already close to needing another.

beats.headline: Upside down over an ooze
beats.text: They go with Carl's least favorite idea, the last resort, which Donut suggests out loud: he will walk on the ceiling over the ooze. Sticky Feet gives him his dexterity times two seconds, once every six hours, and his dexterity sits at thirty-two. He has practised a few times, but not yet in combat. Oozes hunt by vibration and sound, Mordecai warns, so his clomping on the ceiling will draw it unless he distracts it with one of the things he built. He lowers himself, places a bare foot on the ceiling, and readies Sticky Feet.

beats.headline: He opens the valve
beats.text: Carl and Donut are under the sand in the castle's basement, and the ceiling is about to come in. Carl sends Gwen a note. I open the valve, only part way. The water in the necropolis comes out through the drain the castle is built around, the castle washes away like sand under a hose, and everything in there, the two of them included, goes with the water into the ocean.

beats.headline: Swallowed by a shark
beats.text: In the water the party is sandwiched between the current and a mob, apparently a shark, lazily circling toward them. The creature crunches on a corpse and some other debris, and when it opens its mouth Carl can hear the distinctive beat of Jump Around blast out into the ocean. It has eaten the goddamned alarm trap. None of Carl's explosives with exposed fuses will work well under water, and he is not keen to be anywhere near the ones that might.

beats.headline: One more thing for Donut
beats.text: More than sixty seconds fully submerged without dying earns the I was in the pool achievement, an honorary mudskipper, and a Bronze I'm Wet Box, which holds another ten scrolls of water breathing for each of them. Donut's box, for some unfathomable reason, is silver instead of bronze, and she gets an additional item: a Belt of Buoyancy. It is a simple belt that wraps around her stomach and keeps her from sinking, and it only works in the water. She spends a good three minutes complaining about it, and about how she is never going back there again.

beats.headline: The second-to-last drawing
beats.text: Ghazi's note ends mid-sentence on a missing page, but the last page is drawings: two watches, the winding box, two gates, every combination and what happens. All but one end with a monster coming out on the opening side. Katia points at the circled one, where we lose the box and nothing gets out. I'm stuck on the second-to-last. I put that away and ask Mordecai whether a feral god could leave the bubble, or break the wall. Then I ask if there's a Desperado Club in this town.

beats.headline: A gate to the ninth floor
beats.text: The mage's notes list times standing for places, all of them around the city of Larracos. Katia works out it could open onto the ninth floor — and Mordecai points out that crawlers cannot hop floors, so all that would accomplish is releasing whatever awful thing comes through when it shuts.

beats.headline: She turns the watches into a map
beats.text: The linked watches read as a reverse compass: a time, an altitude, an exact position relative to anywhere else. Which means the Gate could open onto the city of Larracos, on the ninth floor, and I am mapping ground nobody has stood on.

beats.headline: A city named on the surface
beats.text: Carl and Donut come up out of the water with the concierge sharks behind them and once they reach a town that will take them in, Katia reads the Mad Dune Mage's page of numbers as places the Gate can open onto, every one of them around Larracos, the capital city four floors below them. Mordecai points out that a crawler cannot use it to skip ahead. All it would do is let something out.

beats.headline: Two potions he should not drink
beats.text: Carl's Pacifist box gives him two Potions of Bloodlust. Double strength, double speed, half dexterity, half constitution, and a debuff that means you don't remember where you are or why you're fighting. Don't use those. The last time I saw someone drink that potion, they accidentally killed half of their party. And don't get ideas about the gate either, kid. Crawlers can't hop floors. If you ever get the last watch, stick it in your inventory until you're strong enough to deal with whatever comes out. Which will be never.

beats.headline: A town that would take them in
beats.text: After the sandcastle the party had to track a quarter turn around the land quadrant before any town would let them in. This one did. Its people are pazuzu, half human and half scorpion, built like centaurs and dressed as though the world already ended: punk leather, tassels, goggles, chains and dreadlocks, all bound for a Mad Max convention. Louis and Firas went off to sleep, Louis grumbling about the drink. Once Mordecai walked off, Carl's question about the place was whether it had a Desperado Club.

beats.headline: Two potions, one warning
beats.text: Carl's silver Pacifist's Box, for winning a boss battle without killing the boss, holds two potions that give Mordecai pause. Don't use those, he says: the last time he saw someone drink that potion, they accidentally killed half of their party. It is a berserking potion, and its debuff means the drinker does not remember where they are or why they are fighting. Carl puts both away. He will look in the cookbook for advice that might make the potion more useful.

beats.headline: Worse than the danger dingo
beats.text: I wake up underwater. Completely underwater. I cannot swim; my legs only tread. I stop screaming only because Carl says Mongo needs me. Then I see a shark down there, and more coming, which is a betrayal worse than when he gave my pet biscuits to that danger dingo. Then he says "Hekla", so I cast Second Chance on a dead beluga and Clockwork Triplicate on top, and send them at the shark, and they explode. In the kayak a small fish comes out of me. The box gives me a Belt of Buoyancy. I am never going back there.

beats.headline: Brown water
beats.text: Carl pops a kayak from the flying house's garage onto the surface, lifts Donut in and paddles. His water-breathing scroll runs out, and he vomits dark, brown water he had not known was in his lungs; it feels like being kicked in the stomach while breathing fire. A moment after, Donut vomits too, far more water than seems possible. A bronze I'm Wet box, for more than sixty seconds fully submerged, brings ten more scrolls for each of them.

beats.headline: A letter addressed to her
beats.text: The pages Katia Grim took off the Mad Dune Mage open as a letter to subject. I know you hate me, but please listen. Hope is not lost. He writes that he was asked to use the box to pull the whole island into the Nothing, and refused, because all three pieces of the artifact would go with it. He sets out how the gate works. If his plan succeeds he dies, and she receives the letter with the winding box and can send another expedition.

beats.headline: The only place they can die
beats.text: I flip Katia's map over and ask Mordecai if it's right. He draws nine petals round Larracos: a city dug deep like an inverted cone, a faction in each petal, fifteen thousand troops apiece, mostly NPCs. The real people there can't die; the system pulls them out first. Then the questions I actually care about. Hunters sign up until the sixth floor opens, and start at level thirty. And that floor is the only place in the game where these rich tourists can really die. Katia asks why she gets the feeling I'm about to do something really stupid.

beats.headline: How to work it
beats.text: Dial a time standing for a place on one watch and the other mirrors it. Both go in the box, which winds and must not be moved or the count resets. Pulling the watches out opens a one-way portal, good for roughly twenty minutes. Afterwards it lingers where it was opened as a two-way passage into the Nothing until something comes through — often a feral god. A weak constitution too near an open portal gets painted with the feral madness.

beats.headline: She planned it from inside the doll
beats.text: I think I see it. When she first escaped, half of her went into the love doll, the closest thing to her real form she could find. So she was the one who talked Ghazi into coming here, and let him think he was calling the god of lust. When he opened the way, her second half came out with the sand ooze. Then something went wrong, the doll was turned to glass with everything else, and she had to use the ooze to keep him here. The scholars thought she had gone into Quetzalcoatlus. Nobody knew there were two halves.

beats.headline: Keep her, as a trainer
beats.text: A withering spirit. Sometimes a soul gets split, and the two halves try to reunite in a proper vessel; when that goes wrong, you get this. Not alive, not dead, hard to kill, mostly harmless, haunting the object. They use them as quest-givers a lot. We avoid gods like we avoid outside factions. And then, knowing I'll regret it, I say we keep her. In the saferoom she can't summon anything, and a minor deity may know potions. Donut can hire her as a trainer. She'll live in a corner of the training room.

beats.headline: In charge of the death charges
beats.text: Carl says I take two or three showers a day, so the ocean is no different. It is entirely different, and it is not happening again, and there is not a thing in this world he can say to change my mind. Then he admits he is teasing. I will only have to float over the water in the house and be in charge of the depth charges. I do like the death charges. And since Zev has her job back, I can check my social media board again.

beats.headline: The head from Ghazi's castle
beats.text: Yes, I am a head. Yes, THAT kind of head. Get it out of your system. I am Psamathe, or the half of her that got stuck when I tried to climb out of the Nothing, and what I got stuck in is a Lika doll from Ghazi's castle, crystallised until now. Withering spirit, the system calls it. Carl carried me here in his pack like a snack. Now he is HIRING me. A goddess. As a trainer. Kept in the safe room. Fine. FINE. I want a mirror.

beats.headline: What escaping it costs
beats.text: Psamathe tried to get out and ended up as half a soul in a doll's head. Every closing Gate portal lets one of the inmates through on the opening side. The winding box alone is a direct conduit — wound and fed a stream of charged energy it will drop an entire location, up to a whole necropolis, into the void.

beats.headline: Tish almost ruined everything
beats.text: Princess Donut, to the doll head of Samantha: she does feel bad for Tish, who really seemed to like him. Samantha's view differs. Tish? Tish almost ruined everything. Take me to her. Crawler Carl completed the sentence for her with the threat Samantha uses on everyone, the one about mothers, and Samantha burst into tears.

beats.headline: Two new crawlers
beats.text: Vadim and I have fallen in with Carl's team. Introductions here are short. Everyone counts heads, adds two, moves on. The first real conversation I hear is Katia telling Carl that pregnant women could not enter the dungeon, and that nobody inside it can get pregnant. Said flat. Like weather. That is the kind of thing people know here, and say out loud. I am going to have to get used to that.

beats.headline: A ghost on the bridge
beats.text: Inside the Akula, a door Vadim swears they left open is dogged shut. Past the airlock, under a floor grate, I loot the neighborhood boss, a little box somebody had to destroy to turn the sentinel gun off, and the whole sub fills in on my map. Corpses on the bridge. And one red dot flickering between the bridge and a chamber outside the quadrant entirely. A ghost that shouldn't be in here. A glowing green pterodactyl head screams through the bulkhead, my vision flashes red, and Vadim drops with his health in the red.

beats.headline: Keep it on the hotlist
beats.text: Over the Akula, Katia sees big blue jellyfish near the entrance. Vadim tells her to watch for the white ones, the pain amplifiers, which are smaller; the big blue ones only wrap round you if you get close. She lands, and Carl puts his hand on her now-silver edge. We're going in, he says. Be safe. Keep that salve I gave you in your hotlist. In and out, she answers.

beats.headline: The diving bell
beats.text: I make a diving bell I have never made before, on the spot, hanging off the corner of the house: more an elevator than a bell, three poles for Carl, Tran and Vadim to hold, a ring of dense metal at the bottom so I do not flip. We drop at about five meters a second. Five hundred meters down I open like a flower on the hull of the Akula, spread myself over it as camouflage and stay outside to watch while they go in. Something swims by underneath. It is bigger than the submarine.

beats.headline: Faces still need the table
beats.text: Katia hangs off the corner of the floating house, one arm anchored to the magical brace that holds the balloon, and forms herself into a diving bell, a shape she has never made before, on the fly. Carl remembers when even a small change physically hurt her. Now she can contour herself into just about anything at a moment's notice. She still is not perfect with faces unless she sits in front of her makeup table, but with inanimate things like this, she is an expert.

beats.headline: The Death Stalker
beats.text: Smaller than Hump Town, with several inns and taverns. No Desperado Club, but a Club Vanquisher, currently closed for cleansing after Prepotente set his hellspawn goat loose in the main lounge over Miriam Dom's revoked membership. So the party met at The Death Stalker: a few tables, a bar and, inexplicably, a gelato cart with about twenty flavours. Donut talked the pazuzu down from two gold to one for a bowl of raspberry. Two crawlers from the water quadrant joined them at the table.

beats.headline: The club revokes Miriam
beats.text: The club revokes Miriam's membership because she is a vampire now. As if that were her doing, as if any of you idiots chose what you are. So I let our third companion loose in the main lounge. It devoured a number of clerics before the rest had the sense to flee. There is a Holy Crusade Bounty on the three of us now, whatever that is supposed to mean, and the club is shut while they cleanse it.

beats.headline: Shuruga36
beats.text: A viewer called Shuruga36 says I have no redeeming qualities whatsoever, that I ruined the viewing experience and almost made him stop watching, and that Donut and her stupid dino-chicken irritate him to no end. Mongo is a child. I can take criticism, but picking on a child is uncalled for. Then I hit the detonator for the chum bombs and go up a level, to 38. Before they drop, I tell Carl and Katia to be safe, because it is horrible down there.

beats.headline: Out of her tomb
beats.text: Quetzalcoatlus is not confined to her tomb. She is on the flooded submarine's bridge, flickering between it and the chamber on the far side of the hull, and she does not like visitors. Her scream is an aural attack: one shriek through the bulkhead reddens Crawler Carl's vision and drops Vadim Zbar into the red. Then she shoots out of the side of the sub, strikes something enormous in the water below, and flies back toward the temple. The thing she struck comes for the sub.

beats.headline: Class: Gut Rearranger
beats.text: Subject: a level-28 spotted, gecko-like Kuhli, which Crawler Carl believes is a fish. Class: Gut Rearranger, a healer and rogue. Sheaths of daggers from head to toe. Cosmetic surgeon in the old world; Crawler Britney was in his office for a consultation when the collapse came, and the two of them were outside taking before photos. At the tavern Crawler Britney said she would rather die than go back into the water. Asked the same, subject said: I'll go. Crawler Tran asked him whether he owned a red shirt.

beats.headline: Fifty children, reportedly
beats.text: Gossip entered into the file via Langley, via Katia Grim. Doctor Vadim was, or had been, famous in the Ukraine: television commercials, billboards, clinics, and lawsuits over botched surgeries. Langley says he has something like fifty children and is known for impregnating his clients. Crawler Carl concluded that if true, subject was a weasel, and not someone to go into danger with while carrying a bounty. Subject's own manner through all the briefings: matter-of-fact and emotionless. He was going anyway.

beats.headline: The way into the Akula
beats.text: Subject supplied the route. The Akula lies 500 meters down, nose fastened to the necropolis, its torpedo tubes pumping the ocean in. A docked mini-sub blew after his party took the bridge. He and Britney had free dived those depths on water-breathing scrolls. His map showed monster types, never the full sub. He rode down in Katia Grim's diving bell, cast Torch as they entered, and led the way in. Crawler Carl kept him in front on purpose, lest he lead the party into a trap.

beats.headline: Chris never talked much
beats.text: Swimming the flooded corridors, subject gave his account of the first assault. Skeletons of bugbears, robots, and only three survivors. Chris was higher level, never talked much, fought fiercely and without emotion, insulted them when they did not do as he said; Britney never liked him. Chris took the boss's note, with the key code to the escape tubes, and did not show it to them. At the bridge a ghost screamed through the bulkhead, and subject went down with his health in the red. Tran healed him.

beats.headline: Depth charges, and everyone inside
beats.text: Something drags the Akula out of its hole and down to fifteen hundred meters. I take Henrik's body whole, watch and all. Then a sharktopus the size of a mountain comes at the window, the world freezes, and it's a Special Event boss battle with a pair of commentators. I tell Donut to drop the depth charges at maximum depth, Louis and Firas to land and get to a saferoom, and Gwen, the tomb raiders and Langley to do the same. Donut asks if the death charges will hit us too. I really hope not.

beats.headline: Locked, then released
beats.text: The moment Carl takes Henrik's body into his inventory, and the watch with it, the world freezes. An admin notice flashes past: three items are under an administrative lock while an appeal in the Syndicate court decides whether they are eligible. A second notice follows before the first has finished: lack of standing for all plaintiffs, lock removed, apologies for the inconvenience. Several someones would like the three pieces out of his hands. For now, they have lost.

beats.headline: The body in the submarine
beats.text: Henrik of Hump Town, changeling, is dead, and has been for some time. Katia Grim runs into the flooded submarine to get away from a sharktopus, and Carl finds the body already sitting in there with its piece of the Gate of the Feral Gods still on it. One magically linked pocket watch, recovered. Also on him: a note recording that Quetzalcoatlus can be put down with an electric shock. Whatever else he was doing, he was still working that problem right up to the finish of him.

beats.headline: Too late to surface
beats.text: Carl tells me to blow my ballast and get to the surface. It is already too late; the big thing is reaching for the sub. So instead of going up I go in, through the torn-open top and down the corridors toward them, and wait in the airlock while it drains, which takes almost a full minute. Carl swears at me over chat. I would not have gotten away. Then I bring Tran and Vadim through, and the three of us stand at the bridge window and watch the second monster come.

beats.headline: The recap guy has a name
beats.text: Subject hosts the recap. He is orange-hued and four-eyed and built along lizard lines, and he delivers the rundown of each floor at a pace that does not permit anyone watching to think about what is being described. Tonight he also takes the live commentary, beside an orc in a sportscoat, and the orc says his name on air: Kevin. I have worked with him for a long time and I have never heard him ask a question he did not already have the answer card for.

beats.headline: Something covering the port
beats.text: The Akula was pulled free of its hole in the necropolis and dragged down past 550 meters, with boss music playing and no boss yet. A sucker the size of half the bridge window pressed against the glass. Then subject came into view: a shark the size of a mountain, glowing, tentacles flowing behind. Crawler Carl identified it as a sharktopus and observed that Princess Donut would be angry to have missed it. His second observation was that this was not good.

beats.headline: Straight from Hayes 17
beats.text: A Special Event boss battle, streamed to subscribers, in a new beta format with live commentary from Kevin and Magnificent Troy. It's Lusca, Kevin shouted, taken from the depths of the water moon Hayes 17. My own description, for the record: Octo-Shark Brood Mother Queen, level 82 City Boss, a single mother carrying a boatload of hungry babies in her mouth. The male who dragged the crawlers down already got his and is long gone. Lusca herself already ate. The babies, however, need feeding.

beats.headline: Ten minutes for the babies
beats.text: Subject is a mouthbrooder, per Magnificent Troy's diagram. She had snapped the Akula in half, and the crawlers were floating in her mouth. Once she clamps onto something, her babies get about ten minutes to eat their fill, and whatever is left goes to mama. The cartoon that followed showed the rest of the process in several stomachs, ending with a skeleton in heart-covered boxers and a crying cartoon Donut. Both announcers fell about laughing. A ten minute timer slammed onto the screen.

beats.headline: How to put her down
beats.text: A note comes off a body in the flooded submarine and it is the answer to her. Quetzalcoatlus can be finished with an electric shock. A wailing shrieker takes banishment, exorcism, a current, or the destruction of her lover's corpse, and of those four exactly one is lying around this quadrant with the power still running to it.

beats.headline: Pulled out of the hole
beats.text: The Akula was torn free of the necropolis and dragged into the deep. The hull rolled onto its side and subject fell with Crawler Tran into the room behind the bridge. Crawler Carl called them through to loot the dead changelings and make for the last escape hatch. The four of them then stood looking out of the bridge window at something the size of a mountain. Subject's mugshot went up on the special event broadcast beside the others.

beats.headline: Bloodlust in the fridge
beats.text: Inside the octo-shark's mouth, a ten-minute timer, thousands of babies hammering at the bridge window. I tape a Potion of Bloodlust to a hob-lobber, duct-tape it inside the bolted minifridge, and seal Katia, Tran and me in the captain's stateroom. The window goes. Something on the other side starts turning the wheel on our door, so I hold it with one hand and hit the detonator with the other. One X on the map. Ten. Thousands. They may be babies, and half octopus. They're still sharks.

beats.headline: A shell down her throat
beats.text: When the timer hits zero, Lusca lifts her head to swallow the Akula, and I cast Protective Shell. I want it to go through her like a bullet. Instead it stops her dead, like she's hit a wall that won't move, and peels her upper jaw back over her own eyes, and every baby left in her mouth dies at once. Then we're pinwheeling on Katia's rocket and buzzsaw, out of her mouth and back through her head. Winner. Then a warning that at this depth I'm losing two percent of my health a second.

beats.headline: What the word means
beats.text: The keyword marks a thing that has been inside the Nothing. The old gods went in at the making of the world and have had every century since to come apart. Duration is not required: standing too near an open portal will do it, and a weak mind takes the stain fastest.

beats.headline: One gets out over the water quadrant
beats.text: Carl steps himself, Katia and Tran off the ocean floor through the Gate, and the Gate shuts behind them. Something comes the other way on the opening side: a god, feral, loose in a sealed bubble with a town in it. The achievement that follows warns that other gods do not like feral ones, and tend to react.

beats.headline: Out of Lusca, and an ocean with it
beats.text: Carl, Katia and Tran kill Lusca and her babies at the bottom of the water quadrant. Carl opens the Gate and takes the three of them to the surface outside the pazuzu town of Pandinus. A spray of ocean comes through in the few seconds the portal is open and knocks over the town wall and a guard tower. A feral god is loose, and the System's achievement warns that other gods tend to react.

beats.headline: Seeded into death charges
beats.text: Two commentators admire Carl's depth charges on air. Multi-layered, gunpowder-filled barrels, seeded with impact-detonated hob-lobbers that go off the moment the barrel crushes under the pressure, with holes and a manual dial to choose how deep. Donut calls them death charges. While the commentators jabber and the display window is about to break, Carl yanks the fuse out of a hob-lobber and replaces it with a piece of hobgoblin pus, bought from Pustule, and burns through more of his expensive detonator materials.

beats.headline: Leatherface, underwater
beats.text: Carl calls Leatherface. The move is made for the flying house, and I do not have the mass for it, so I just hold on: braces around Carl and Tran, the steam rocket wrapped in my flesh, and the twenty-five-foot buzzsaw out of my inventory, running. We spin the wrong way, out of her mouth, then back through her snout, and the saw cuts through her like a hot knife. It is her brain we hit. One of her tentacles slams us into the sea floor, the saw buries itself, and I let go.

beats.headline: The babies turn on each other
beats.text: Juvenile Octo-Shark, level 30, minion of Lusca. In each birthing of two to three thousand pups, one or two survive, because in time they learn their siblings are delicious. Crawler Carl's depth charges landed a direct hit; Kevin said she would shrug them off. Then Crawler Carl set off a potion of bloodlust in the water, the babies went into a feeding frenzy, and the kill markers multiplied. Subject swam on in circles around the quadrant at about 35 kilometers per hour. Crawler Carl wondered whether she knew most of her babies were now dead.

beats.headline: Mama swallows the Akula
beats.text: The timer hit zero and subject raised her head to swallow the Akula whole. At that moment Crawler Carl fired his shell spell down her throat. It did not punch through as intended. She stopped dead in the water, as if she had hit a wall; her upper jaw bent back over her own eyes, cartilage snapping, and teeth shattered as the spell drove her into the ocean floor. Every remaining baby died as the inside of her mouth turned outside. She was grievously wounded. She was not yet dead.

beats.headline: Cleaved through the brain
beats.text: Katia Grim fired a rocket and held on to a live twenty-five-foot buzzsaw, and the three crawlers pinwheeled out of subject's mouth and back through her exposed upper snout, cutting her like a hot knife through calamari, until one of her tentacles slammed them into the seabed. Lusca, the Octo-Shark, now floats on her side on the ocean floor, upper jaw peeled back and split, a jagged red line through her tiny little brain. Winner. From her corpse: a Map of the Stars.

beats.headline: A wall of water
beats.text: Carl dialled the Gate of the Feral Gods to a spot just outside town, and he, Katia and Tran splashed out onto the beach inside a wall of seawater. The portal was open three or four seconds. That was enough to topple the metal wall, knock over a guard tower and put a chunk of metal through one pazuzu's front door like a javelin. Any longer and the town would have gone the way of the sandcastle. They ran for the nearest inn, past a staring bartender.

beats.headline: In the minifridge
beats.text: The sub is already inside Lusca, and the bridge window is about to break. Carl swaps a hob-lobber's fuse for hobgoblin pus and duct-tapes a potion bottle to it; the cookbook has a more elegant version with a different potion, and he has no idea if this will work. He tapes the bomb inside the bolted minifridge by the captain's chair. The window breaks and the babies flood the bridge; holding the stateroom door's turning wheel with one hand, he slams the detonator. Xs bloom on the map. It was the potion of bloodlust: spread through the water, it started a feeding frenzy.

beats.headline: Up a level for doing nothing
beats.text: Carl wants to know if we are almost back. We are not. The wind starts early and blows wrong, Firas says, and we keep getting higher and higher, so we have to go back to Hump Town, and Louis says ten minutes. Then I go up a level, and I did not even do anything. I should stay back more often. This is great. When Carl finally falls into the personal space he is sopping wet. He smells terrible, and he has seaweed in his hair.

beats.headline: Straight down a city boss
beats.text: Swallowed along with a submarine, Crawler Carl casts in the throat of an enormous shark. The static sphere, about twelve metres across by now, shoots away as the shark swims on. He hoped for a bullet through the brain. Instead the boss stops dead, as if it had hit a wall; the top of its mouth peels back over its own eyes, teeth shatter, and the immovable spell pushes it down into the ocean floor. Grievously wounded, it is not yet dead.

beats.headline: Pus by the set
beats.text: Supplier note. On the Silk Road, Crawler Carl bought a few sets of hobgoblin pus from Pustule, the magical detonator, and he is burning through the expensive stuff. Inside a submarine a city boss is about to swallow, he yanks the fuse from a hob-lobber, fits a piece of pus in its place, duct-tapes a potion to it, and seals the lot in the captain's minifridge.

beats.headline: Taped into the minifridge
beats.text: On the submarine's bridge the commentators expect the rest of the depth charges to be duds, and the display window looks about to break. Carl yanks the fuse from a hob-lobber, replaces it with hobgoblin pus, and tapes a potion bottle to the bomb with his duct tape, a crude cousin of something more elegant in the cookbook. He has no idea whether it will work. He looks for a place safe from the first rush of water, puts the bomb in the bolted-down minifridge beside the captain's chair, and duct-tapes the door closed.

beats.headline: Leatherface
beats.text: Inside Lusca's mouth, Carl calls the plan they made for the flying house: Leatherface, the saw dropped on a chain and swung as a melee weapon. His Protective Shell stops the boss dead. Katia fires the rocket and pulls the activated buzzsaw from her inventory, holding onto its back. They pinwheel out of the mouth and back, and the screaming saw cuts through Lusca's upturned snout like a hot knife through calamari, until a tentacle slams them down and it buries itself in the ocean floor. They have cleaved her brain.

beats.headline: Broken on the seabed
beats.text: Lusca floats on her side on the ocean floor, a jagged red line along the top of her. Behind Carl, the buzzsaw is buried all the way into the seabed. It makes a strangled noise, and the whole thing breaks apart, pieces flying every which way. One of the round blades dislodges and shoots off through the water, spinning into the darkness like a tire off a crashed car.

beats.headline: Everyone take a scroll
beats.text: Lusca's babies are dead, but oxygen is running low and the AI complains they are just sitting there being boring. They have to go out there.
