beats.text: For Sadir, a null with two strikes on his trespass record, the season's Walk-On List is work: he marched to the closest port and signed onto a bounty crew that hires his kind. Everybody knows about the list. The Syndicate knows. There was a holo drama about it. Rights organisations write bills demanding it be condemned, and nothing ever happens: Syndicate security still hunts trespassers, and the corporations who are the real culprits face no accountability at all. He has children in a null commune to keep.

beats.headline: Collected, Crawlers, Natives
beats.text: How it works. A planetwide collection sorts everyone into the Collected, caught in the collapse; the Crawlers, who went in; and the Natives, everybody else. Producers may pull collected people into the show for drama. Natives are untouchable under the rules. So, the list: trackers hired to sneak onto the planet and kidnap survivors a production wants. Not remotely legal; as old as the crawl. Earth's natives had their implants scrambled when the crawl began, and Borant's early start left the records two days stale.

beats.headline: A cat called Gravy Boat
beats.text: This season's list is shorter than usual, and competition is fierce. Dozens of hunters search a tropical zone a tsunami washed clean for one high-value woman; as many hunt a little girl's father in the southern hemisphere. Sometimes a list has 5,000 names and one or two are found. Sadir and his sac partner Gennrik are after a cat named Gravy Boat, an A-tier target, with a bonus for the first capture, in a survivors' camp in what was once Seattle.

beats.headline: Lexis gets there first
beats.text: The raid goes wrong once the tent is open. Gennrik's chest explodes; Sadir, hands up, stares at the woman on the mattress and asks, Beatrice? Lexis takes her. Odette's orders for the scene: make it look like a fight over the cat, buy out the null's warrant to keep him quiet, let the wounded human expire, and have a security man sneak the cat over to Borant so the walk-on bounty gets collected. Beatrice is to be reassured: no selling her to Borant. They have a better use for her.

beats.headline: A class with a room
beats.text: At the filthy screen where he picks his class specialty, Carl has three choices. Mordecai insists on the melee one. The Guerilla gets the Advanced Trap Maker's Workshop, which is only a table. The Agent Provocateur gets plus one intelligence a level, a skill level for his Sapper's table, plus two to Explosives Handling, faster explosives training and access to the advanced Bomb Maker's Workshop: an entire room, where he could precisely tune his explosives, and which a few recipes in his cookbook need. With a minute left and the coin slot's orange light blinking, he clicks the third choice. Sorry, Mordecai.

beats.headline: Agent Provocateur
beats.text: The Hunting Grounds are opening and I take the bomb-focused specialisation. Agent Provocateur. I would like to be very, very good at exactly one thing, and I have picked the thing.

beats.headline: Agent Provocateur
beats.text: The bomb-focused specialisation, taken on the Hunting Grounds.

beats.headline: Immune by patch already
beats.text: On the sixth floor the specialties for Carl's class play out on his screen, and he cannot click anything; he just has to watch. Revolutionary means the front of the line, a tear gas canister to the chest, the first to start swinging. It gives an extra point of strength at every level, two to Unarmed Combat, faster melee training, the Blend into the Crowd benefit, and immunity to cloud-based attacks, which the menu marks as already obtained via upgrade patch.

beats.headline: The stray the circus kept
beats.text: Background, for the file. Grimaldi's circus took in a half-Naiad child that no throne would keep, and put her on a poster: Tsarina Signet and Her Amazing Battle Squad. The child grew up. The child fell in love with him. Ringmasters take in strays. It is most of the job.

beats.headline: The HAZMAT endorsement
beats.text: They brought me into the liaison's office first, because the Gate was in my inventory. They asked whether I considered myself its owner. I said Carl is its true owner, and then I was sent back to the staging area with a headache, and they kept the Gate. I think I accidentally got him into trouble. I didn't know what to say. The little room gave me three endorsements to choose from, ten minutes to choose, no chat. My class is still Monster Truck Driver. I took HAZMAT.

beats.headline: The attendant who was a crawler
beats.text: The bush elf dragging a cart for the rolled-up carpets in the registration arena tells Carl he was a human once, a crawler, a very long time ago. Everybody working the arena was, he thinks, though sometimes it is hard to tell. He usually works at Club Vanquisher. His advice is to stay on the trail and away from the city in the north, where the aliens are. Last season one of them ripped his brother's head off at a food stand, and since the guards did not see it, they did nothing. Then he jerks as if shocked and pushes his cart away.

beats.headline: Borant would like the Gate back
beats.text: The Hunting Grounds. I have been sent to Crawler Carl with a request from Borant, which I am instructed to describe as a request. They would like the Gate of the Feral Gods surrendered, voluntarily, to be held until the ninth floor and not a floor longer. I put it to him exactly as written. He asked for a lawyer. I have passed that back exactly as spoken. I expect to be sent again.

beats.headline: Legendary Diva
beats.text: I have the world's greatest class for this floor, and I will tell CARL only if he promises not to get mad. Katia says he is going to be mad. I am a bard. A Legendary Diva. I sing songs and they cast spells, and I got a bunch of them. They said I could permanently pick any class I already had, and Mordecai told me not to, so I did not. The tree man at the pub says I can have a gig for the lunch shift. Katia says after the lunch shift. Don't ruin it, Katia.

beats.headline: Tish's note
beats.text: According to the note Tish left for Ghazi, the Gate of the Feral Gods was the artifact needed to defeat Scolopendra.

beats.headline: Night weasels at the gate
beats.text: I walk out of a port-a-potty into the jungle, and at the village gate both mushroom guards fall over, paralysed. Something invisible is hitting my shell. I throw a sack of gunpowder at it and it gets a shape, smaller than Donut and fast. Then its partner bites my neck from behind and I'm paralysed for five minutes. Donut's missiles make them visible: six-legged black weasels with too many teeth, pets of a hunter I've never met. Chris steps on the one dragging itself toward my face and carries me into the saferoom over his shoulder.

beats.headline: A Pocket Kuma
beats.text: You had to go and challenge all the hunters, and now look. And that doesn't look like a melee class to me. Laugh it up, Carl. Get it out of your system. This floor I'm a Pocket Kuma: knee-high, buck teeth, elf ears, a monkey tail and eyes like a baby's. Half-fairy, bred as a pet for the High Elf court, until King Finian learned they were intelligent and had them executed. They can't fight and they can barely walk. I jump for my doorknob, hang off it, and the door opens on its own.

beats.headline: Small, adorable, and a rescuer
beats.text: Carl called for help at the village entrance and I came on Mongo. Low-powered magic missiles make the invisible weasels show themselves; one of them caught fire from the gunpowder on its fur. When one died I raised it and cast Clockwork Triplicate on it and told it to get them. Then a guard spewed a poison cloud and we had to run. And now Carl is on the floor laughing at Mordecai. You shouldn't make fun of someone just because they're small and adorable. I'm small and adorable, and I just saved your life.

beats.headline: Tootsie, and the rest of them
beats.text: Night Weasel Scout, level twenty-five, name Tootsie, dragging itself on one leg across the ground toward Crawler Carl's paralysed face. This a pet of Hunter Zabit. A gang runs to about twenty, invisible, with scouts that smell prey across hundreds of kilometres and disable it for the rest. A lava-rock crawler stamps Tootsie flat, Mongo eats the second one, and Crawler Princess Donut raises a dead weasel against its own pack. Carl is carried into a pub like luggage, and a guard's poison cloud clears the street outside.

beats.headline: Part of the price of the Gate
beats.text: Contract amendment, filed by Quasar, Carl's new lawyer. Carl surrenders the Gate, on a temporary basis. In exchange: four mercenaries, free of charge. Bomo. The Sledge. Clay-ton. Very Sullen. Plus two spells, issued to Bomo and the Sledge, that copy two of the Gate's tricks: a jump to the stairwell, and Zerzura. So the client keeps the tricks, loses the object, and gets four bodies thrown in. Lawyers, crawler. Get one.

beats.headline: The shrine takes its cut
beats.text: There is a small shrine in the corner of the room now, a disk and a cup, and the cup boils over whenever I'm near it. Every day it takes a drop of my blood. Thanks to my new religion it also takes five percent of my looted gold, and a number floats over it to say exactly how much I owe. The shrine's idea of looted includes what I got for surviving the last floor in the top ten. I paid it when Donut wasn't looking. She noticed anyway and complained for five minutes straight.

beats.headline: A foot on the weasel
beats.text: First day of the sixth floor. A weasel pet crawls toward the paralysed Crawler Carl's face, and a dark, rocky leg crushes it. Chris picks Carl up, burning his skin, and carries him into the personal space over his shoulder. When the Royal Court receives four cretin mercenaries, Chris and Clay-ton, almost exactly the same size, trade one grunt each. Clay-ton is assigned to stay with Chris.

beats.headline: Level fifty-two
beats.text: Carl finally notices my level. I was forty-four when I opened the Gate onto Larracos, and apparently it paid. Fifty-two. My base constitution is over a hundred now, which brought something called Steely Skin. The lower my health, the thicker my flesh. A Platinum Asshole's Box gave me a gambling chip and an upgrade to Find Crawler, and there's one more thing I almost tell him about and then don't. Louis and Firas have the Twister back from the changeling refugees. Meadow Lark, Bautista's team and others are gathering at a big settlement a few hours south, and Chris and I mean to reach them before the hunters are released.

beats.headline: The deal for the Gate
beats.text: I arrive, I introduce myself as my client's counsel, and we proceed to terms. The Gate goes back. Temporarily. In consideration: four mercenaries at no charge to my client, Bomo, the Sledge, Clay-ton and Very Sullen, and two spells for Bomo and the Sledge that reproduce two of the Gate's abilities, teleport to stairwell and zerzura. My client wanted to keep it. Everyone wants to keep it. A negotiation is what you get instead.

beats.headline: Say nothing, touch nothing
beats.text: First instruction to my client. Any time he gets hauled in front of one of these liaisons, he says nothing except that he wants to talk to his lawyer, and he doesn't touch anything until I get there. They were trying to get him to pick up the artifact while it was under administrative hold, which would have deleted the item. I am his attorney. Nobody else's. Not the cat, not the lady who turned into a shovel. What I get out of it is credits. Not a lot. Not too many outfits hire a Null.

beats.headline: Part of the price of the Gate
beats.text: Carl's lawyer trades the Gate of the Feral Gods back, and I am part of what he gets for it. Four of us, free of charge: me, Bomo, Clay-ton, Very Sullen. Two spells on top, one for Bomo and one for me, copies of what the artifact could do. Bomo gets the jump to the stairwell. I get Zerzura. Nobody explains Zerzura to me. Nobody has to.

beats.headline: The lawyer's idea
beats.text: Carl explains the deal for the gate. Four cretin bodyguards, and two of them got extra spells. Bomo's is Teleport to Stairwell. The Sledge's is also teleportation, and even more impressive: it was the lawyer's idea, and it is called Zerzura. Donut wants to sing the Sledge one of her new spells. Katia wants to know what it does, and does not get an answer. Carl fingers the charm on his necklace and remembers Quasar: it was glorious, shame how it ended for Remex. Everybody likes carnage when it's not them.

beats.headline: A private bowling alley
beats.text: Carl has bought the advanced bomber's studio alongside a magic workshop, which leaves them only 100K gold. The room is only about ten feet wide but long, like a private bowling alley. Nothing in its testing area really explodes: he can copy a design or a bomb, build a virtual village, set it off, pause it and see which way it blows, though the system sometimes gives only a range, and the cookbook stresses it is no guarantee. Being advanced, it can also test virtual bombs he does not have, though for now only with items in his inventory. At the very back is a level-one bench for examining and dissecting explosives. On it he sets Carl's Doomsday Scenario, out of his inventory for the first time since he grabbed it, copies it into the simulator and puts it back, his hands trembling.

beats.headline: He moves them to the stairwell
beats.text: Service rendered. The hunters are about to be released and the clients want to be somewhere else, specifically the stairwell in Zockau. Bomo casts the spell he was issued, and Carl and Princess Donut are there. No fuss, no speech, no ceremony. Some mercenaries want to be thanked; this one has already been paid for, in Gate. Enjoy Zockau, crawler.

beats.headline: On the bench
beats.text: The Advanced Bomber's Studio has a workbench built for examining and dissecting explosives, and Carl sets the Doomsday Scenario on it: the first time he has taken it out of his inventory since he grabbed it. The bench reshapes itself around the glass reaper case, which glows like a miniature sun. It is a microsecond from exploding and there is nothing he can do to stop that. He can copy it into the studio's simulator, where it can be played with safely, and he does. Then it goes back into his inventory, his hands still trembling.

beats.headline: A singer who must be in key
beats.text: My bard spells don't use mana. I only have to sing them, in key, and the spell is only as strong as the singing. Standing Ovation, Entourage and Encore I can manage if I sing the words in a steady monotone, so they are weak. The two attack songs I cannot manage at all. Katia and Chris left on the caravan, and Katia kissed me on the head. What if something happens to her and we can't protect her? Mongo would never forgive me. Then Mordecai and I went shopping for a Golden Throat enchantment, and there was none.

beats.headline: The hunters' door
beats.text: The stairwell down stands in a quaint little park in the town square of the city every hunter on this floor has been gathered into. Bomo casts his teleport and puts Carl and Donut on its steps in the hours before the release.

beats.headline: Zockau burns
beats.text: Zockau burns. I mark hunters with the Ring of Divine Suffering, I kill them, and I take their stats, and enough of them are inside the Desperado Club when it goes that the survivors have to be dug out. I get hurt on the way out. That part is fair.

beats.headline: Full of hunters when the roof comes in
beats.text: Carl's explosives bring Zockau down and trap whoever is inside it.

beats.headline: Every trap at once
beats.text: Carl sets a launcher box of twenty-five surefire missiles against a hedge and marks its timed trigger with Remote Detonator, then marks a bomb with a second one. One mental click on the first trigger in his hotlist, and the rockets corkscrew into the air one by one. Then, on the run, he steps on two traps at once: a cheap spike trap and an alarm that starts blasting Kickstart My Heart. He casts Tripper, and every trap in a wide radius goes off around them, songs and small explosions. He pulls the alarm into his inventory to shut it up.

beats.headline: The map stays; the monsters change
beats.text: On the Hunting Grounds, Forkith has set earlier editions against what he saw himself. Herot wrote of tall creatures bellowing into the sky each night, Azin of kite birds overhead, Ikicha of ice and cold. None of those were there in his iteration. The jungle is constant; the monsters change, so earlier advice on this floor needs care. The map, though, is the same every time, and so is the political landscape: a round world with a single named metropolis and dozens of unnamed cities.

beats.headline: A block per barrel
beats.text: They jump into burning, smoky chaos. The whole block is on fire and blown apart, a thick fog fills the air and bodies are everywhere. Carl's barrel explosives were crammed with gunpowder, hobgoblin dynamite and delay-detonated smoke curtains, packed for the most destruction: unstable as anything, but a single one can take out an entire block. They lived only because they hid inside a real saferoom.

beats.headline: Predator
beats.text: Carl has been collecting invisibility potions, and he makes sure Donut always has a few, because of Predator, one of their newer moves: on his call they both go invisible, Donut switches her sunglasses to infrared, and she rides his shoulder calling out by chat anything she sees. Sorry about this, Bomo, Carl says, and smashes an invisibility potion against the side of the rock monster's head. Bomo disappears. Carl drinks his own just as the timer hits zero, Donut does the same, and they are in Zockau.

beats.headline: Not a potion
beats.text: Planting barrel bombs from alley to alley, Carl and Donut chain invisibility potions. Donut's potion countdown is much better than it used to be, but at a minute forty-five it still means she cannot keep her mana topped off and stay invisible. She has two slices of mana toast saved for an emergency. The toast would top off her spell points and would not count as a potion, and Carl does not want her using it unless it is absolutely necessary.

beats.headline: He ruined my spell. Again.
beats.text: Again. He has done it again. Mother and I have been at work on a spell over that city, and now this idiot is lying at the edge of the jungle with bolts through his leg and his shoulder and a stack of debuffs. Level fifty-four. How did this idiot get so high? And what are those knife symbols over his head? Mother, you should feed on him before he dies. She will not. I say we let him die. He ruined my spell. Again. You need blood.

beats.headline: A move, not a plan
beats.text: Predator, Carl says, two seconds before we land in the hunters' city. That is not a plan, Carl. That is a move. We go invisible, I call out what my sunglasses see, I puddle jump us past a park full of traps, and then a barrel goes off outside the saferoom and blows us across the bar. I think I want to go to Katia's team now. Instead we run, and I try to sing Entourage on his shoulder, which is like karaoke on a rollercoaster, and an invisible hunter on a roof fills him with crossbow bolts.

beats.headline: Zockau
beats.text: Carl goes at the hunters with it — marking one, killing him, taking the stat — while his explosives bring the town down around them and trap whoever is inside the Desperado Club. He is badly hurt getting out.

beats.headline: Five by five
beats.text: Carl sets a multi-launcher the size of a poker table against a hedge: twenty-five single-stage surefire missiles in a five-by-five grid, targets already programmed, on a remote trigger. When he clicks it, the first five streak after the fleeing hunter Xindy. The fourth is shot down early; the fifth hits as her shield fails, and she explodes. The rest spread off in different directions. His second rocket box holds only ten rockets, because he ran out of surefires, and is pre-set to kill the closest hunter-class mobs.

beats.headline: Left to Fester, shared
beats.text: Carl has used Sticky Feet a lot; the ring's second ability he has never tried. Super Spreader reaches anyone close enough for him to see their name, and Ping has made that range far greater. He scrolls the list to Hunter Xindy, a level 61 mantis of the Dark Hive, and clicks Activate. She stops dead in the air, then retreats fast as she realises she has a debuff: she now has his Left to Fester too, and it will not go away until Chin'Dua is dead.

beats.headline: The roof comes down
beats.text: Carl marks a drunk hunter with the Night Wyrm's ring, uses him as bait, kills him for his stat, and lines the street of pubs with barrel bombs. When they go, the Desperado Club's façade comes down on its entrance bar, and whoever was inside the club stays trapped there. He is shot to pieces getting clear of the town, and Miriam Dom and Prepotente carry him the rest of the way.

beats.headline: The goat pulling the cart
beats.text: Subject was a goat once. Specifically a Boer goat, one of the Shepherd's. She is now a Hellspawn Familiar the size of a draft horse, with black flames coming off her back and a stubby pair of wings coming out of it, and at present she is pulling the cart that carries Carl, whom she helped to save. Her own description calls her kind scary as shit. The cat reports that she liked being petted on the rump and loved grapes.

beats.headline: Thirty-four hands
beats.text: I come round in the back of a cart with Miriam Dom stroking my hair. Level fifty-four now. Thirty-five of the Hand that Claws the Master achievements, which is the AI padding the count, and thirty-four Gold Hunter-Killer boxes, which is the real number. Mass Casualty Event, too: more than two hundred and fifty non-mob casualties. And it doesn't bother me nearly as much as it should. I want to be more efficient about the innocent ones. This isn't on me. They started this. Their rules. Their game.

beats.headline: Five mercenaries, one disaster
beats.text: For the record: a note in the Cookbook, signed Crawler Everly, fifth edition. Her party hired five mercenaries: four from the Merc guild in the Desperado Club, a healer from Club Vanquisher who charges per spell. It was, and continues to be, a disaster. 1,500 gold a day each, payable for the rest of the floor even after they die. Lose one through a personal space and he turns up three saferooms away. One wandered off and cannot be fired. Her level-50 dwarf died when a chair hit him. The whole thing is a scam.

beats.headline: A red dagger, then thirty-four
beats.text: Donut has a new symbol after her name, a single red dagger with its point up, like the Desperado Club's logo: Hunter Killer X 1, for a magic missile fired while they were running away. Carl dives into his notifications. The Hand that Claws the Master (x35): he has permanently killed a non-crawler biological, and the AI admits it may have slipped an extra one in. The reward is a Gold Hunter-Killer Box (x34), with a note that the achievement may be awarded more than once, but the boxes only on the sixth floor. He has killed thirty-four.

beats.headline: A vampire now
beats.text: I am a vampire now, and the leaderboard says so. It changes a great many things. It has not changed how I feel about my boy, which is the part I was afraid of. We bring Carl out of the city in the back of a cart, with Bianca hauling it, and while he comes round the cat tells him what Mordecai has said: the Ring of Divine Suffering is addictive. I hope Carl listens. Men with a tool that works rarely do.

beats.headline: Tripper, tears and a hug
beats.text: There is a line of traps at the town entrance built to decapitate anyone who comes near, and they require a special touch. I am explaining this to Carl, who cannot manage his own basic hygiene, when he casts something and sets off every trap at once. That was an attack. Negligence most serious. I prepare Bianca for battle, and he calls me by my special name, which only Mother may use. I weep into her robes. Mother says we must apologise. I apologise for calling him malodorous. Then we hug, and I scream in his ear.

beats.headline: Hunter Killer, once
beats.text: There is a red dagger spinning after my name now: Hunter Killer times one. It was nothing, a magic missile while we were running away, and I think Carl's explosion really killed him, but they gave me the credit. Carl was in a coma for half an hour. Miriam, Prepotente and Bianca saved him, so he must say thank you, and he must be nice to Prepotente, who does not like him. From now on I am not participating in a Carl plan unless I know what I am getting myself into. Mongo is quite upset with him.

beats.headline: Mordecai's warning
beats.text: Donut passes it on: Mordecai says it is addictive.

beats.headline: The contract outlives the floor
beats.text: Before the transfer to Odette's show, Zev passes on a message: the programme is still active, so Carl's contract regarding participation in any other programme is still in effect. If some other elite approaches, he is required to extract himself as best he can. The showrunners of other programmes generally honour the contract with Sensation Entertainment, and try to intervene on their end. A good-faith effort should be enough, though that is a question for his new attorney.

beats.headline: The contract does not lapse
beats.text: Zev reminds Carl that his agreement with the programme is still in effect. Nothing signed on a floor above stops mattering because he has walked down a flight of stairs.

beats.headline: She reminds him the contract stands
beats.text: Carl. I know you have a lot going on. I know the Hunting Grounds are the Hunting Grounds. I still have to say this, because saying it is my job: your agreement with the Vengeance of the Daughter programme is still in effect. Nothing you signed on an earlier floor stops mattering because you have gone down a set of stairs. It doesn't work like that. Please don't make me be the one who has to remind you twice.

beats.headline: Room for explosions
beats.text: Mordecai says I only killed a handful of them. With Donut's kill it was thirty-five hunters. And I didn't blow the town up. It was one or two square blocks, and those barrels were only about a fourth the strength I could have made them. I have a plan for another one that's really big. Like huge. That's the best part about this floor: lots of room for explosions. Mordecai supposes I have a plan for that one, too. The hunters are released in just over thirteen hours. Oh, it's going to be spectacular.

beats.headline: Mordecai's verdict
beats.text: The team says goodbye to Miriam and Prepotente at a small bugbear settlement. Mordecai is waiting to take Carl apart for what he did to the city, and Donut gets in first: yes, it was idiotic and suicidal, and no, she is not leaving him. Mordecai shuts his mouth and settles for pointing out that for all the noise, only a handful of hunters died.

beats.headline: Mongo's spot
beats.text: I'm in Mongo's spot on the floor. I push him away a few times. He puts his head in my lap anyway, and now I am petting him like a dog. I was a Pit Fighter. I'm a Pit Champion now. Carl doesn't know what's different and I don't tell him. I am not Firas's girlfriend. Then Donut says pet beauty contest and the dinosaur jumps up and starts hopping, and I shriek and get out from under him.

beats.headline: A stream at the back of my mind
beats.text: Something at the back of my mind has always been there, like a stream hidden in the weeds, so quiet I never noticed it. Now it's getting louder. It isn't a sound, not really, or a physical feeling. A sense of flow, rising. I've only found one way to mute it, which is to be completely at rest. Running from Zockau, it was right there. By the end of the recap it's rushing, tumbling, crashing, getting faster and louder, and it's starting to hurt. Just a little. That's okay. Rest can wait.

beats.headline: Tundra Princess
beats.text: There I am on the recap, for everyone: Blizzardmancer to Tundra Princess. Some sort of earth class, combined with the ice. And I get to pick yet another class on the ninth floor. Seventh on the top ten, Frost Maiden, level forty-seven. Carl and I have managed one quick check-in this floor and he didn't ask how I'd changed, so this is how the young man finds out.

beats.headline: Announced after the recap
beats.text: The announcement after the recap carries the news that the guild system is going live. Crawlers can build alliances larger than a party without having to sit inside one together.

beats.headline: What a charter costs
beats.text: A guild charter runs upward of five hundred thousand gold from a bopca protector. A level-one guild holds five parties or individuals, provided each has one member with a personal space of their own, and each of those spaces opens onto a shared common area. Private and party rooms stay shut. Environmental upgrades can be licensed across the membership for a small fee, and shared experience can be bought outright.

beats.headline: A demigod with a cult
beats.text: Carl touches the spiderweb on his elbow: the Night Wyrm's Nasty Little Web of Suffering, access to the Guild of Suffering. Mordecai frowns. It is a cult, he says, not a real guild and not a real church. They have outreach centres. They worship a demigod, the Night Wyrm, who is not a regular member of the pantheon; similar to Samantha. There is a memorial crystal involved, whose purpose has never been established, and all of it ties back to that ring.

beats.headline: A row down to the wall
beats.text: Donut has a Hunter-Killer box of her own but wants Carl to open his first, because thirty-four will be more dramatic. They line up in a row floating all the way to the wall, and everybody stops to watch. The first holds 1,000 gold and the mangled claw of Xindy, the mantis he blew out of the sky; the second, 2,000 and the hand of Chin'dua; the third, 3,000 and an orc's hand. Each adds a thousand, 595,000 gold in all, and the Emberus fountain chimes: Carl owes it 29,750. Donut's own box gives her a gray hand and, to her outrage, only 1,000 gold.

beats.headline: Thirty-four boxes of hands
beats.text: Thirty-four Hunter Killer boxes line up in a row that floats all the way to the wall, and each holds gold and a hand. The first is the mangled claw of Xindy, the mantis Carl blew out of the sky with his rockets. The second is the hand of Chin'dua, the drunk draconian. The third is an orc's. None of them wear rings. All that, Donut says, and it's a bunch of horrible hands. At least it's not tongues: Lucia Mar collects tongues.

beats.headline: A prize ticket
beats.text: Carl pulls the mantis claw from his inventory and examines it while Donut opens her own box, and a gray hand pops out. The description wanders through arcade pizza joints and a prize counter where forty dollars of tickets buy five cents of bubble gum, then gets to the point: the hand is the ticket. The prize counter where it may be exchanged opens at the Butcher's Masquerade, near the end of this floor. The cheapest award costs a single hand. Transfer or sell one, and it reverts to some dude's appendage.

beats.headline: She won't be on there much longer
beats.text: The top ten hasn't changed since the end of the last floor. Donut thinks I should be back on it after what happened at the end of the last floor. I am perfectly content to hover outside the list. But Eva is ranked, ninth, and Donut says that isn't fair. Don't worry about that. She won't be on there for much longer. Carl looks at Mordecai. He opens his mouth to ask me something, and then shuts it again.

beats.headline: A box for every hunter
beats.text: Carl's thirty-four Gold Hunter-Killer boxes line up across the room, and each one holds gold, a thousand more than the last, and a severed hand: Xindy's claw first, then the drunk draconian's, then an orc's. Five hundred and ninety-five thousand gold, and not a ring on any of them. The hands are Hunting Trophies. The prize counter that takes them opens at a party called the Butcher's Masquerade near the end of the floor, where the cheapest prize costs a single hand. Sell or transfer one and it reverts to being some dude's appendage.

beats.headline: Juice Box told you, huh
beats.text: Okay so, Donut sits down next to me and wants to know when the nuptials are. She'll be maid of honor, Mongo's the ring bearer, Carl can officiate because he found religion, and she'll sing. For a fee, obviously. My face is on fire, man. Juice Box told you, huh? She didn't have to, Donut says. Love makes a person glow. Also, I'm level thirty-five and I'm an Extermination Professional now instead of a Pest Exterminator, which gets me half a percent insta-kill on mobs my level or lower. That's it. That's the upgrade.

beats.headline: A giant foot on the replay
beats.text: Recap footage from the last moments of the previous floor. One of the two heads screams "Murderer!" The two-headed nodling is fighting a big, leather-clad man with a shaved head and a war gauntlet, and their magical meteor hammer is about to brain him when a giant foot crashes into the scene and everyone goes flying. It belongs to Slit. The target runs for a stairwell. In the specialisation rundown, Dmitri goes from Illusionist to Visionary; the other half remains a Bogatyr.

beats.headline: A pet beauty contest
beats.text: The party at the end of this floor has a pet beauty contest, and Mongo is going to follow in Mommy's pawsteps. We will need an extra hour of training a day, a seamstress, a walk coach, the upgraded pet shower to get the blood out, and the standards manual immediately. Carl should message his attorney. And he may not say we are not doing this. I have very little, and this is something we are going to do. Very well, Carl. But we are going to need more hands, and the guild immediately.

beats.headline: Sergeant-at-Arms
beats.text: Crawler Quan Ch, one-armed, pale and sick-looking on the recap, specialises from Imperial Security Trooper to Sergeant-at-Arms and keeps his place on the top ten: tenth, level forty-eight, a hundred thousand on his head. Crawler Princess Donut, watching from a personal space, objects to the plural. It should be Sergeant-at-Arm. She would like Crawler Carl to remove the other arm at their next meeting, after which he will simply be a Sergeant.

beats.headline: A web on the elbow
beats.text: The Gold Junkie's box Carl earned for using the ring the first time opens with nothing in it. A spiderweb pattern appears in the air instead and settles onto his left elbow as a tattoo, faded, green-tinted and poorly drawn: the Night Wyrm's Nasty Little Web of Suffering, which gives its bearer access to a guild. Mordecai says it is a cult, not a real guild and not a real church, worshipping the Night Wyrm, a demigod outside the regular pantheon. Everybody who uses a divine suffering artifact is marked this way.

beats.headline: A foot in someone else's fight
beats.text: Recap footage from the last minutes of the previous floor. The Popov brothers are about to brain a man with their meteor hammer when a giant foot crashes into their world, knocking everyone off their feet, and jumps away. Crawler Carl recognises it as Slit, on her way back toward the party's bubble after Samantha. The man the brothers were fighting uses the distraction to escape into a stairwell.

beats.headline: A ballista in the yard
beats.text: Louis and Firas have recovered the Twister from the changeling refugees, and Bonnie went with the refugees. Before she did, Firas says, she built a giant crossbow, a ballista, out of the mechanism for the garage door opener and fixed it to the side of the yard. Katia test-fired it, and it blew up a tree. But the ceiling on this floor is low: the balloon is too big to get over the trees, so the house is not very useful.

beats.headline: Just Wait Until Your Daddy Gets Home
beats.text: Mordecai left some blocks of Nitro Sludge on my table, a by-product of a shield potion. Inert, but vaporised hot enough they release an insane amount of oxygen. Too little does nothing and too much mutes the blast, so it took trial and error to find the mix. Egg-shaped casing off a broken live ammo ball, welded shut, Fear imbued because why not, on a little cart Bomo can pull. The simulator says it flattens everything for a third of a mile. The system names it itself: Just Wait Until Your Daddy Gets Home.

beats.headline: A bomb for Bomo
beats.text: The plan: send Bomo out of the personal space into the Zockau saferoom with a very large bomb, step outside, and level the town with half an hour on the timer. The bomb starts from blocks of Nitro Sludge Mordecai left on the sapper's table, a by-product of a shield potion that look like squares of uncooked ramen: inert, but each the equivalent of several hundred pounds of ammonium nitrate when vaporized hot enough. Carl finds the mix by trial and error and packs it into a broken live ammo ball, an egg-shaped clamshell, welded shut. It stands about five feet tall, so he builds a cart Bomo can pull, and adds Fear, because why not.

beats.headline: A map the size of Iceland
beats.text: I made the map from the gate coordinates Gwen's team looted off Quetzalcoatlus. If I'm translating them correctly, it's about a hundred thousand square kilometres. Really similar to Iceland, even the shape. Four hundred-something kilometres north to south, three hundred-something east to west, and a river about five hundred long because it isn't straight. Imani mostly coordinates the reports as people call things in; I copy everything down. Some of the bridges are estimates. Carl wants one thing organised. I'll do anything he asks. To a point. He wants all the bridges knocked down except one.

beats.headline: Welded into a bomb
beats.text: Carl has a large, egg-shaped, clamshell bomb casing from the previous floor, a live ammo ball too broken to hold a living creature again. He fills it with explosives and a few blocks of Mordecai's Nitro Sludge, welds it closed, builds a little cart for Bomo to pull it on and, for good measure, imbues it with Fear. If it works properly, the simulator says, it will flatten everything within a third of a mile. The System names it on its own: Just Wait Until Your Daddy Gets Home.

beats.headline: The caravan road is clear
beats.text: We are on the main road south, sweetie, following the path of the caravans, and there are very few mobs about. The bodyguards on the caravans cast anti-trap spells as they travel, so even the traps made for crawlers are disarmed. We plan to cross the river soon and disappear into the jungle. Yes, there is a town near the bridge, a very big one, a large Ursine settlement on the far side, forty kilometres from Carl. It is where we started. Be careful there. They are very peculiar. We have to put Bianca away when we enter.

beats.headline: A clockwork Bomo
beats.text: Carl wants to send Bomo out as a suicide bomber. Bomo is our friend. We don't blow up our friends, Carl. It isn't a suicide bombing if he comes back next floor, he says, and Bomo seemed excited. It won't work. They'll be waiting for him. So what if I made a clockwork Bomo? He'd have to be switched to a minion of me and not the party, like Clay-ton and Very Sullen, and then I can make copies. Really, Carl. Pay attention to how the party system works. I just have to be in the saferoom.

beats.headline: Elmer goes down the slope
beats.text: Elmer the mayor charges a customary execution fee of a hundred gold, and offers both at once for a hundred and fifty. Let's do it, says Carl, and pulls out a few more coins. The moment Elmer steps closer to take the money, Donut casts Astral Paw and pushes him from behind toward the slope. He tumbles off the edge of town and rolls down, flipping like a ragdoll and bouncing off a rock. Carl whirls with a banger sphere and never gets the chance to throw it.

beats.headline: A line that won't paste
beats.text: I copy every new description into my scratchpad now. The one for the Ursine mayor has an odd line in the middle, about other new, shiny AI iterations with their clean lines and error-replacement nets, and a curse at the lot of them. When I paste the text, that line isn't there. I retype it from memory while it's still fresh. Earlier, on the road, a notification said my god, Emberus, had made an appearance in this realm. About a minute after that he'd returned to the Halls of the Ascendency. Nothing else changed.

beats.headline: The Hive is hunting you
beats.text: A hunting party on the Hunting Grounds, and the message it sends Carl is a note knifed to the saferoom door and signed by Vrah: the Hive is hunting him, there will be nowhere to hide, and his death will not be quick.

beats.headline: A temple in the Ursine town
beats.text: Temple of Hellik: a red diamond at the edge of Crawler Carl's map, in the large Ursine settlement across the bridge. Hellik is the brother and the enemy of Emberus, whom Carl worships. Carl holds a quest to kill this god, and is told he earns a bonus for every worshipper of Hellik he kills. There is no temple of Emberus in the town. He has declined to wade into that particular pool today. He has way too much else to deal with.

beats.headline: A knife in the door
beats.text: Minutes before the hunters are loosed, Carl pulls the cart from the bomber's studio to the door. Bomo will open it, Donut will cast Clockwork Triplicate so a clockwork Bomo appears in the space outside, and the clockwork one will roll the bomb out. Bomo opens the door, and a note is stuck to the outside with a knife. Vrah: every hunter is now protected from further explosions, so he would only be killing his precious NPCs, and she has ordered the town guards to worship Emberus. Sorry, Bomo, Carl says. They will save him and the bomb for another time. He writes come and get it on the note and tosses it out.

beats.headline: No dinosaurs
beats.text: Mushroom points stick at Mongo. Mongo SCREECH. Mushrooms GROWL. Paper says NO DINOSAURS. Bear falls down hill. River eats bear. Carl slaps. Mongo RUN.

beats.headline: I have my own town
beats.text: The town rules say no dinosaurs of any kind, no exceptions. They specifically called out Mongo. I demand the person in charge, and the mushroom actually goes and gets him. The mayor thinks I am a monkey. Carl agrees to pay him a hundred and fifty gold to have us both executed, the mayor steps closer to take it, and I cast Astral Paw. He rolls down the slope and finds every rock on it. Something from the river takes the body. I got the credit. My own town! I'm going to make dancing mandatory.

beats.headline: Faster than the buggy
beats.text: Carl drives the chariot down the main road while Donut rides Mongo alongside. Her Twinkle Toes spell lets Mongo run faster even than the dune buggy, and she has been practicing it, trying to level it up. Mongo loves going fast and screeches with joy whenever she casts the spell. Carl stops a few times to plant claymore-like mines that only hunters will trigger.

beats.headline: Signed, Vrah
beats.text: Hunter Vrah. Mantis. One of the regulars who come every season, with a death count in the thousands by one attendant's reckoning, and she wears the heads of her kills. She is the Grand of Zockau. Her little sister was Xindy of the Dark Hive, the flier Crawler Carl blew out of the sky on the first night. Her note, knifed to his door: the hunters are protected from explosions now, the guards all worship Emberus, and his head is going home to her sister's grave. He writes a reply on it in pen and throws it back out the door.

beats.headline: A note on the door
beats.text: A second bomb is ready to walk back in when Carl finds a note pinned to a door: the hunters inside are proofed against explosives now, and the Hive is hunting him. It is signed. Vrah does that.

beats.headline: JayGee's hand
beats.text: A trap I left beside the road after the bugbear town kills a hunter. Gold Hunter-Killer box, a new achievement called Insurgent, and a Trapmaster box of twenty Fail Safes. The hunter-killer box holds thirty-five thousand gold and the fat, mottled gray hand of a hunter named JayGee. I hold it up to the ceiling and tell his family and friends where they can go, and to mention him to anyone who wants to hunt innocent people for fun. Mordecai says people out there have long memories. Good. I don't want them to ever forget.

beats.headline: The gem is turquoise
beats.text: Donut likes her butterfly charm. It makes fairies like her, it is part of her fit, and stupid Angel the cocker spaniel had four or five tags on her collar. The system only lets a crawler wear so many magical items, Carl says, and the new one is better. It's ugly, says Donut, and the gem is turquoise: does she look like an elderly woman in a bingo hall? She does not need it to rename the Large Ursine Settlement Point Mongo, but to order the guards about she must wear it. One gem, Plain Turquoise, Point Mongo: plus eight dexterity, plus four intelligence, Snitch at level ten, and 3,592 gold in taxes every ten days.

beats.headline: Nobody likes a snitch
beats.text: The charm's gem comes with Snitch, a skill rather than a spell. Inside any settlement it alerts all the town's guards, who start moving to her. At level five one guard is teleported to her at once, at level ten it is five, and at ten they can also be summoned up to a kilometer outside a town she owns. There is no cooldown, but the System warns her not to abuse it: these guard guys get really cranky. Donut huffs, mumbles, and changes out the charms.

beats.headline: A trap-leaving reward
beats.text: A sudden group of notifications: a trap Carl left has killed a hunter, a gold Hunter Killer Box, and the achievement Insurgent, for an explosive device left along a well-travelled path that killed its intended target. Too bad he didn't get to see it, because he is a trap-leaving bitch. The reward is a Gold Trapmaster Box. He cannot believe it worked; he placed that one after the bugbear settlement. The hunter-killer box holds 35,000 gold and a hand. The Trapmaster box holds a very useful mod, a pack of twenty trap add-ons called Fail Safes, which will send him a notification if a trap is ever disabled or set off.

beats.headline: Katia has it worked out
beats.text: Over chat, while Carl hands out weapons to the town guards, she lays out how it would work: whoever starts it leads it, neither Carl nor Donut wants the job, and Imani might if they ask. They would have to pool money to share the upgrades.

beats.headline: Wants to murder Louis and Firas
beats.text: Crawler Katia's report on her party: big personalities, and they do not all get along. Florin broods like Crawler Carl. Britney has given up on everything. Subject constantly wants to murder Louis and Firas. When Crawler Carl suggests subject for a job Imani may not want, Crawler Katia refuses; she is not going to let Gwen do it either. The party heads southwest the next day, away from elf territory and deeper into the wild.

beats.headline: JayGee's hand, held high
beats.text: A trap Carl left kills a hunter, and the gold Hunter Killer box holds 35,000 gold and the fat, mottled gray hand of a hunter named JayGee. Carl holds the trophy up to the ceiling and waves it: if JayGee's family or friends are watching, they can go fuck themselves. You shouldn't do that, Mordecai says. People out there have long memories. Good, Carl says. He doesn't want them to ever forget.

beats.headline: Big personalities
beats.text: We're okay. There are some big personalities in this group, and they don't all get along. Florin is doing a good Carl impersonation with how broody he's being. Gwen constantly wants to murder Louis and Firas. Britney has given up on everything, and I don't know what to do with her. We'll make it work. Southwest tomorrow, away from elf territory and deeper into the wild, grinding quests and collecting the former Daughters. Then the notifications arrive. Point Mongo? Really? And why did I just get a quest to hunt dinosaurs?

beats.headline: Mongo runs off
beats.text: Mongo bolts with Princess Donut still on his back and runs a pack of dinosaurs to ground. Kiwi is at the head of it. Level 60 mongoliensis, the fastest and cleverest predators anywhere in this jungle, and the whole pack is female, as is every dinosaur anyone has counted in the area. Which is odd. Odder still: dinosaur-class mobs did not exist on this ground before Scolopendra's nine-tier attack, and here they all are. Mongo and Kiwi settle the introductions between themselves, at length, with Princess Donut obliged to watch.

beats.headline: Kiwi
beats.text: Smell. Out there. Mongo RUN. MOTHER on back. Many Mongos. Big one. Pink feathers. One eye. Mongo GROWL. Big one says UNK UNK UNK. Mongo says UNK. Not fight.

beats.headline: That was an accident
beats.text: The cleric bear, Tam, is shouting down at me that the naiad and dinosaur rules have to come back. I ask him why it's necessary. The guards will keep the town safe regardless. Have there been naiad attacks recently? Always, he says, and the lizards are worse, and if the pagan monkey won't restore the rules, you'll have to go out there and do something about the dinosaur menace. Ah, hell. Sorry, guys. That was an accident. And no, I don't know what the town upgrade is. Everything on my manager menu has moved around.

beats.headline: A new mayor and a new name
beats.text: The settlement across the bridge keeps a long list of rules, and one of them is that Mongo does not come in. Donut kills the mayor, takes the office herself, and renames the place after the animal they would not admit.

beats.headline: The Recital quest
beats.text: Something has been coming out of the trees for the townspeople, and the job of looking into it lands on the party the same hour the new signage does. Mongo, for his part, runs off with Donut on his back, and Carl has to pull her out of the saddle in a clearing ringed by an all-female mongoliensis pack. Its leader does not want to fight him. Not exactly.

beats.headline: Forty pairs of eyes
beats.text: Mongo rushes out of the gate into the jungle with Donut on his back, and the shrieks that follow are not his. Carl has received ten dinosaur repellent potions since the end of the previous floor, and the description is vague about what the potion actually does. He took one earlier. Donut refused, afraid it would make her pet shy away from her, and he regrets not making her take it. In the clearing ahead, forty velociraptors surround Donut and Mongo, every one of them watching Mongo.

beats.headline: Mayor Donut, briefly
beats.text: The system made me Mayor Donut, and I changed it back to Princess immediately. To order the guards about I must wear a new collar charm, and the gem is turquoise. Turquoise! Do I look like a woman in a bingo hall? I have removed all of those idiotic rules except the bugbear one, until Carl said it was a trap. I have named the officers and sergeants: Dinallo, Miss Nance, Doctor El. I absolutely will not reintroduce a racist policy to make a bunch of overgrown teddy bears comfortable. The town is named after a dinosaur.

beats.headline: A town, newly named, with a dinosaur problem
beats.text: Donut renames the settlement Point Mongo and the quest arrives on the same day. Mongo takes her off into the jungle on his back and finds the pack: all female, all mongoliensis, headed by one called Kiwi. When Carl carries Donut back to town, Mongo stays behind.

beats.headline: One charm too many
beats.text: Donut likes her butterfly charm. Fairies like her, it is pretty, and it is part of her fit. She has had it since the first floor, it was instrumental against the first Krakaren, and it keeps her Light On Your Feet at ten. But the system only lets her wear so many magical items, and to order the guards of Point Mongo around she has to wear the new settlement charm with its tiny turquoise gem. Carl tells her she can always switch back if they come across some fairy-class mobs.

beats.headline: Double-Billed
beats.text: New achievement: Double-Billed. I'm one of the first five crawlers to receive double-billing, which is similar to switch-overs, except this time it's on purpose. The AI bets that didn't help at all. The reward is a Platinum Fan Box. My view counter has been buried to the right since Donut ran off after Mongo, so that tells me nothing. Donut didn't get one. Far behind us a missile shoots into the air and detonates. Time to get back to work.

beats.headline: We'll deal with it when we get there
beats.text: Donut asks about the ninth floor. The crown she no longer even wears put her permanently in the Blood Sultanate's line of succession, removing it removed nothing, and she cannot go down to the tenth until the Sultan and every other royal is dead. That means killing the nagas, which is harder than it sounds. They have had this conversation before, and it always stops at the same place: we'll deal with it when we get there. This time Carl says instead that he will not leave her behind.

beats.headline: White for the cat
beats.text: Kiwi and a few dozen of her pack stand at the edge of the woods outside Point Mongo, looking in. Their dots have turned white for Crawler Princess Donut. Kiwi's is still red for Crawler Carl. Deeper in the trees stands something much bigger that was not there before; it waits, then turns and moves away. Kiwi calls unk, unk, unk once more and the pack melts back into the jungle. Mongo has already stumbled back into town, collapsed in the street with his health full, and gone into his carrier without objection.

beats.headline: Everybody always leaves me
beats.text: I'm supposed to pretend like I don't know. And I was doing good. Then Mongo ran off, and it was Miss Beatrice's car accident on the way back from the cat show all over again, me slamming into the side of the carrier. Everybody always leaves me. Am I really that awful? Katia left us. Carl keeps doing more dangerous things. Mongo is going to leave for some hussy. And what about the ninth floor? Carl holds my face and says he will not leave me behind, on the ninth or any other floor. No matter what.

beats.headline: Bad timing, on purpose
beats.text: Hey guys! I just wanted to quickly touch base. We rearranged the schedule a little, so you'll be visiting with Odette today. Try not to schedule a boss battle or anything during that time. Yes, everything is okay, and yes, I will be there. Carl, I also want to remind you that you'll be receiving some extra scrutiny before you go to the trailer. So just be aware. But you'll be fine, because you're both really strong and brave. Especially you, Donut.

beats.headline: Two red crosses past the bridge
beats.text: A guard's missile knocks a flying hunter into a tree across the river, and the tree starts shaking when I light up the map. Seven white dots around him, one of them long, like a snake, wrapped around the hunter. And two white dots with red crosses. Elites, and not moving off. A trap, and not a hunter's. I'm starting to understand Double-Billed. Quasar never told me whether Sensation Entertainment took the deal, and his reply is automated. I give Donut the choice, like I promised. She climbs back onto my shoulder.

beats.headline: A coveted ninth-floor slot
beats.text: At the negotiating table, Quasar slips in an old emergency-use rule, and the kua-tin agree to keep it quiet. It guarantees Vengeance of the Daughter the equivalent of a third season. What makes that valuable is where it leads: not all secondary programs are allowed to send their elites to the ninth floor. It is a coveted reward, Quasar insists the producers are sure to leap at it, and it gives them one more reason to keep Carl alive.

beats.headline: Subsection 674
beats.text: Second request. The sixth floor is where secondary programs go to die, and a limited number get licences to continue. We want one for Sensation Entertainment's Vengeance of the Daughter. Not possible, says the liaison: licences are an AI decision, at the end of the floor, by lottery. Subsection 674, paragraph five or six of the secondary program amendment, buddy-boy. Showrunners running below expected profits may give emergency use to a single program. The price is an extra twenty percent to Borant. They've already agreed, I tell them, and wave my device. They haven't. I couldn't reach them.

beats.headline: A licence they never asked for
beats.text: In the negotiation with Borant, Quasar asks for one of the licences that let a secondary programme continue past the sixth floor, for Sensation Entertainment's Vengeance of the Daughter. It is an old rule: a showrunner running below expected profit may grant emergency use to a single programme, for an extra twenty percent to Borant. Borant agrees, provided it stays quiet. Quasar says the producers have already agreed. They have not; that is a bluff, and they have been unavailable. Carl's chaser gets an automated reply.

beats.headline: What she did to the cat
beats.text: I chose Carl for my blood sacrifice, and I did not ask him first. When he broke his promise, I put the cat to sleep under the Water Lily, with only her dinosaur to guard her, so that he would do as I said. She slept until the sun rose on the night Grimaldi set me free. I forgave Carl his lie, because my mother taught me grace, even in the face of betrayal. Now the two of them walk out onto the bridge, Carl calls me out of the bushes, and I come.

beats.headline: Blood magic, cast on a loser
beats.text: The tattoos move under my skin because they are not pictures. They are Blood and Ink Elementals, and I raise them. The craft is exact. I set two creatures against each other and cast on the one I judge will lose, before it has taken a single wound. I may not bleed the sacrifice myself; that is the law of it. The moment another cuts it open, all of its blood flows into me, and my lovelies take it and form. One summoning a night. Judge badly and the night is wasted.

beats.headline: She brings him a hunter
beats.text: Who said anything about hiding, old friend? We came seeking Carl, and found others are seeking him as well. My friends range north to keep the path clear; one invader slipped past. Some idiots have destroyed bridges, so this town is the only way into the Liana district. With me is Areson the Wise, and Clint and his brothers, were-kin, who share my enemy. The hunter lies bound across my caterpillar's saddles. I thought to use him for my blood sacrifice, but it is Carl's kill. Heal him, he says. Still soft. Not anymore, he says, and puts on a ring.

beats.headline: A third season, if they take it
beats.text: Quasar's second request in the negotiation for the Gate: an emergency licence for the programme to continue past the sixth floor. The kua-tin agree, on the condition that it is kept quiet; one mention out loud and it is negated. It is the equivalent of a third season, and not every secondary program is allowed to send its elites to the ninth floor. It would also give Sensation Entertainment an incentive to keep Carl alive. The producers have not actually agreed to anything. That was a bluff, and they have been unavailable.

beats.headline: The admin gives himself away
beats.text: The negotiation, as it went. The nameless kua-tin admin from Borant pretended to hem and haw about giving Carl the four bodyguards, but the moment Quasar mentioned the Zerzura spell, he practically creamed himself. The mudskippers do not have good poker faces. Behind him, Orren the liaison grunted with amusement from his chair and said nothing once the negotiations began. Quasar winked and moved on to the next item on the list.

beats.headline: One kill short of two points
beats.text: Bravvo's highest stat was dexterity, so the ring pays me a single point of it. Donut and I loot him with my new safe method while Signet and her people watch: boots against magical bolts, thirty health potions, thirty slow mana refills, a longsword for the sell pile, and nine potions of Levitation. Then I take his naked corpse. The rain keeps coming. The Ring of Divine Suffering is warm on my finger, warmer in the wet. One more kill and it starts giving me two points instead of one.

beats.headline: Like the bear
beats.text: Asked what became of the circus, Tsarina Signet uses Heather as the measure. Grimaldi killed the parasites and set their family free. It was like when Carl freed Heather the bear: all the clowns and lemurs and other performers simply crumbled away, finally free. All but Grimaldi himself, whom Signet took with her.

beats.headline: Nine off a dead hunter
beats.text: The hunter Bravvo was using one of these to scout Point Mongo when he caught a missile to the face. Hunters carry slots, not bottomless inventories, so his loot is thin: thirty good health potions, thirty good mana refills, a longsword for the sell pile, clothes, and his naked corpse. The only real prize is a set of nine potions of Levitation. Not as good as flying potions, they let the drinker rise into the air for intelligence times two seconds. It is not clear how high one can go, or what happens if the potion runs out before you have lowered yourself.

beats.headline: Two cancers in a sacred land
beats.text: The crawler has looted the dead hunter. My mother is long dead. My father is gone, and his daughter, my half-sister, rules the high elves. I am recruiting a team, and he and the cat are the last pieces. Grimaldi killed the parasites and set our family free, all but himself, whom I took with me; his story in this is mostly done. There are two great cancers in this once-beautiful land, and with every breath left in me I will cut both of them free. The Confederacy and the High Elves.

beats.headline: Part one of two
beats.text: The Vengeance of the Daughter, part one of two. Tsarina Signet, exiled half-daughter of the naiads, has come home to a kingdom marred by infighting and a sloppy revolution that cut off the head of the government and left the body flailing. The current leaders of the Naiad Confederacy are holed up in the former river palace, now dubbed Fort Freedom. Assault it, avenge her mother's assassination, and survivors follow your orders twenty percent more willingly. The name is doing a lot of work.

beats.headline: Circled until the pencil broke
beats.text: Okay so, the Dream have one name on their list. One. The very last one, which is mine. Their dead guy circled it so many times the pencil went through the paper, and then drew my face at the bottom with a big X over it. Carl puts the whole map in the group chat and tells Katia she has to watch my back. Man, all I did was grab a photo of their boss's mom and ask Juice Box to turn into her. It's not my fault they can't take a joke.

beats.headline: Circled on a dead man's map
beats.text: A map off a dead hunter. The hunters sat down and divided the floor between them: the Hive has the bottom left, the Dream holds Point Mongo, and the unaffiliated are relegated to the country around Zockau, among them groups called the Crafters and the Nebular Sin Patrol. Some groups have also claimed specific crawlers. The Nebular group's names are Prepotente and Miriam Dom. It is a hunting licence, drawn in pencil, and it ended up in the wrong hands.

beats.headline: A court order to write
beats.text: I now need a court order to send my client a message; he can still send me all he likes. His complaints about hunters getting outside information have caused a stir. Sensation has agreed to Borant's offer of a ninth-floor extension but wants a few days before signing. My read: make the program more exciting without the spotlight throwing the star into the shadow. Too bright, and they might pull his plug. The other matter is one hundred fifty million credits. His net worth out here is about 117, against a tax bill of maybe 50. I have an idea. I'm working on it.

beats.headline: Yes, but not yet
beats.text: Zev reports that she is talking to the Sensation people, and that they mean to steer the narrative so the crawlers are back in a saferoom in time for Odette's show. Then Quasar's message, good news and bad: Sensation has agreed to accept Borant's offer of a ninth-floor extension, but they are being little bitches about it and want to wait a few days before signing anything officially. His reading between the lines: make the programme more exciting without throwing the star into the shadow, or they might decide to pull his plug.

beats.headline: Daughter of King Finian, and of nobody
beats.text: I am the daughter of King Finian of the High Elves, who is no longer with us, and of a Naiad princess. Then came the revolution. My mother was assassinated, and the dukes of the confederacy sit in her river palace and call it Fort Freedom. I was cast out of the river and exiled from the Hunting Grounds by my father's people. I was still a child. The circus took me in when no throne would. Now I have come home to reclaim my mother's crown, or at the very least to put a proper government in its place.

beats.headline: A claim staked on the hunters' map
beats.text: The map off the dead hunter divides the hunting grounds between the outfits working them, and two of those outfits have put a claim on Carl and Donut. The Hive is one. The Skull Empire is the other.

beats.headline: A hunter of theirs, and the map on his body
beats.text: The group takes one of their hunters down and Carl loots him: an Arrow of Enthusiastic Double Gonorrhea, and a crude map of the hunting grounds with a territory marked for every outfit working them. That is the first honest look anyone gets at how the hunt is organised. The Hive and the Skull Empire have both put a claim on Carl and Donut. The Dream have their own reasons for being here.

beats.headline: Part one: Fort Freedom
beats.text: Signet gathers about seventy in a clearing around an old white tree: six were-warriors and their caterpillar, the ogre, forty bush elves, a talking tortoise, dryads, monkeys and forest creatures, plus Carl and Donut; the last to arrive are a pair of ursine. Then the quest drops. Part one of two. The leaders of the Naiad Confederacy are holed up in the former river palace of the Naiad, now called Fort Freedom. Help Signet assault it and avenge her mother's assassination. The reward is part two, and every survivor of the assault will be 20% more willing to follow Carl's orders.

beats.headline: The ratings are okay
beats.text: Okay, so, Princess Donut asks how the ratings are on Signet's show, and I say they're okay. Ratings were good on the third floor when Carl and Princess Donut were involved, and they lagged a little while they were on the fourth and fifth. People really like the six warriors and their caterpillar mount. Some of the hardcore fans think Carl and Princess Donut are going to make everything implode before there's a resolution, or take the show over. I am talking to the Sensation people so they're back in a saferoom in time for Odette's show.

beats.headline: The third and final sponsor
beats.text: Clint has the account of Scolopendra's attack, and says the high elves were protected by something they had stolen. On the way back to Point Mongo the last sponsorship slot fills. The Apothecary takes it.

beats.headline: Suggestions, not strings
beats.text: Two of Signet's were-castors insist on walking Carl and Donut back to a saferoom, and it takes Carl a minute to see why: Signet pushed them, and the showrunners pushed Signet, because Odette's show is in a few hours. Elites are not nearly as autonomous as regular NPCs. They are not controlled like robots, but showrunners may send them suggestions that make them act out of character. Carl wonders whether an elite could be made self-aware, like other NPCs, and what would happen then.

beats.headline: Signet has a writers' room
beats.text: Signet's were-castors hurry Carl back to a saferoom, and it takes him a minute to see why: the showrunners pushed Signet, and she pushed them. Elites are not nearly as autonomous as regular NPCs. The producers can send them suggestions that make them act out of character, and nobody knows how far that control goes.

beats.headline: Back into town
beats.text: The group returns here after Clint's account of Scolopendra and the stolen thing that kept the high elves standing. The third and final sponsor signs as they cross its bridge. The Apothecary.

beats.headline: Out of tune, apparently
beats.text: The murder weasels attack from three sides, and I start singing Standing Ovation, which would have given everyone a dexterity boost. It fails. Afterward Holger, whose face is swollen shut from fighting his own friend, informs me that I cannot sing in tune. He says there is no shame in it. The easy spells simply fail, but try something big off-key and it becomes dangerous, so I need lessons. It is very hard to sing properly with all that grunting and stabbing going on. Besides, Carl and Mongo think I am an excellent singer.

beats.headline: What the were-castors remember
beats.text: Holger's village came through the demon's cloud better than the city across the river, and he wonders if it was because one of the attacks in it was a transfiguration spell they had already been hit with. He got sick that day, and then was fine. Clint has it from the poem: the high elves cowered in their castle, protected by something they took. Rumour says they went down while she slept, collected their soul gems, and stole an item that shielded everyone in the castle. Holger thinks her nine-tier attack was a slow damage reflect. They settle it with their fists.

beats.headline: Where the idea came from
beats.text: Clint has a theory about the nine-tier attack that blames the high elves. Crawler Carl has heard a different one, from the Cookbook: the Semeru dwarves of the ninth floor dug their city too deep, a Tower of Babel run in reverse. It was that story that gave Carl the idea to fill it with water in the first place.

beats.headline: Earth, from the checkpoint
beats.text: Zev warns us about a security checkpoint. Nobody mentions it's in orbit. A glass floor, almost no gravity, and under it the whole planet: the Indian Ocean, the edge of Madagascar, almost no cloud. I think of Coolie, who wrote the 19th edition, and whose last view was his own world. Donut throws up her tuna lunch. Two shade gnoll mercenaries drop through a hatch, ask if I'm carrying explosives, and pat us both down. Then we're in Odette's trailer, with Odette herself waiting as a holo, to tell me Beatrice is alive.

beats.headline: Patted down by gnolls
beats.text: Two gnoll security guards with diver's flippers tied at their waists search Carl and Donut, then leave through a hatch in the ceiling. The one bent over Donut clutches her collar charm and examines it closely. It used to be a butterfly, Donut tells him, but now it's this ugly thing. Ghastly, she knows. He lets it go, declares them clear, and appears to scratch her under the chin on his way out.

beats.headline: His last view
beats.text: Crawler Carl and Crawler Donut are pulled onto a ship without warning, and the side wall is clear. Earth fills it: the Indian Ocean, the edge of Madagascar, mostly clear skies. Crawler Carl feels tears come, and thinks at once of the subject, who wrote the nineteenth edition. This was his last view, though of his own home planet. The file is now explicit: he died after a failed assassination attempt on a pair of admins. Crawler Donut vomits her tuna lunch.

beats.headline: She wants her body back
beats.text: SIGNET. Take me to Signet. Signet can put me back in a body, a real one, with all the parts, and I have been saying so since they walked in and nobody is LISTENING. Carl has the face he makes when he wants to put me back in the bag. He says they will bring me if I shut up. So I am shutting up. This is me. Shut up. Are we going or not?

beats.headline: Alive, and off the planet
beats.text: Beatrice survived the initial collection. Bounty hunters were after her, meaning to sell her illegally to Borant, who would have transformed her into a country boss. A very specific one. Odette had her removed from the planet before they found her, then used her to blackmail Borant: the official story will say Borant did something noble, and Odette gets a higher revenue share for the rest of the crawl. The contract was signed in a hurry. The former girlfriend of Crawler Carl is now on her way to the inner system, standing by for a guest appearance.

beats.headline: Protecting an investment
beats.text: I tell Carl that Beatrice is alive and that I took her off the planet. There were only four ways it could have gone, and in three of them they find her and use her against him, and it ends a crawl. For one of them, at least. He asks why I did not simply kill her. The thought entered my mind. I ask whether Mordecai ever told him what I did to him; get the story from him, and my actions may make sense. Another program means to ambush him with this. I want his permission to bring her on.

beats.headline: It is my decision
beats.text: Odette says Miss Beatrice is alive and wants her on the show, and Carl tells Odette where to go and that we are not going out there. I say we are. It is my decision. Carl wants to do it alone, to protect me, and I remind him what I told him before: we need to trust each other. It is going to happen one way or another, so at least now we have a moment to prepare. I thank Odette for saving her from becoming a dungeon boss, and for the warning. Then I find the treats in the pink bag under the counter.

beats.headline: Close that yap
beats.text: Okay, so, Odette dropped this on me as we started preparing, and I'm the one who tells Carl the part she didn't: she's using Bea to blackmail Borant. I also have to tell him about the fan box. The votes are in, and soon after he opens it he goes to an event with fans, alone, without Princess Donut. That's where they were going to confront him. When he asks why I'm so nervous, I whisper that Donut is going to need him, to focus on that, and that he needs to close that yap of his right now. Please.

beats.headline: On the couch, as a holo
beats.text: Beatrice, newest full-rights citizen of the Syndicate, appears in a red gown and very tall shoes, much thinner, pale, and by every sign drugged. Her story has holes: pirates came into her tent while she slept, her memory was wiped, and at some market a small alien recognised her and started shouting before she woke among men with hyena faces. She is surprised the cat talks. She asks Carl why he is not wearing pants, and whether he can come to her. He says nope. When he has said goodbye, Odette nods, and she disappears.

beats.headline: Not my person anymore
beats.text: On air I lick my paw. I tell her to have a good life, to buy only the wet food, and not to pretend to love a cat she means to sell. Then Odette says we are off the air, and I tell Miss Beatrice what she is. She danced with me and sang to me and was my whole world, and she was going to give me away. What she did to Carl was not okay either. I still love her, and I hate myself for it. She does not get to explain. You're not my person anymore. Carl is. He's always been.

beats.headline: Regency to the worms
beats.text: Two messages land the moment the interview ends. The first: a regency change has created a conflict of interest, so the Valtay Corporation is removed as one of Carl's sponsors, effective immediately, and an auction will fill the slot. The second goes to the whole planet. A Syndicate court has declared the Borant Corporation independent of the Borant System Government, which automatically executes an earlier ruling handing the Valtay 51% of the corporation. Borant still runs the crawl, and contracts stand, indentures included. Odette thanks the gods, then tells Carl: too bad it's the Valtay.

beats.headline: The version for broadcast
beats.text: Odette's show runs a segment Carl and Donut are not allowed to see: the rules for humans who stayed out of the dungeon, and the walk-on list, the illegal practice of bounty hunters finding survivors to sell to the production. Then Odette's story: a guest who survived the collapse, was kidnapped by bounty hunters and taken off world, until Borant, wanting no part of kidnapping, turned the pirates over to the Syndicate. A pirate died. She is now a full citizen. Carl knows it for utter horseshit. The guest is Beatrice.

beats.headline: Lexis, speaking for Odette
beats.text: There is talk. A woman called Lexis, speaking for a woman called Odette, tells the man and the cat that the Queen of the High Elves will most likely prove to be one of your repurposed humans, and that with the one called Bea accounted for, nobody can say which. She also says I am a country boss, placed to zero out the best of you at the Butcher's Masquerade. I am Imogen. I am giving a party. The rest is gossip.

beats.headline: A warning delivered on someone else's behalf
beats.text: Lexis speaks for Odette, because Odette cannot be the one saying it. What is waiting on this floor is a country boss dressed as a queen, and the queen is very likely a repurposed human. She does not know which human any more, now that Bea is off the board. She says the thing is built to zero out the crawlers at the top of the leaderboard, and when Carl says they will go down the stairs early, she says that would be Odette's advice as well. All of it comes at speed, in the minute the system is handing over control, with her eyes on a blinking cursor on her tablet and a vape pen that smells of burnt candy.

beats.headline: Reading the shop software
beats.text: The kid says they told him my contract's still being honored. We'll see. This sort of thing happens a lot, just not usually mid-season: contracts frozen, guides traded to other companies, lawyers and rule changes for cycles. I check whether the shop is still running kua-tin software or the Valtay's. It looks the same, which is good and bad. They'll keep the fantasy theme, hopefully. Meanwhile the Ursine finally understand they're in danger, we beat back two more Dream elves, and they've talked Imani into being guildmaster. Katia wants to borrow money for something called a manager's headquarters, which will let me keep my room when she disengages. Sort of.

beats.headline: What she smuggled
beats.text: In the green room Lexis tells us about the elf queen and the party, and says the Valtay will want to wipe out the top of the leaderboard and start fresh. That is most distressing. I certainly would never have smuggled all those Valtay secret agent guys to Zev and the Borant Emancipation Front if I had known this was going to happen. Lexis stares at me with her mouth open. Carl says 'What?' and then we are transferred. Back in the saferoom he tells me not to say a word. Relax, Carl. Everything will be okay.

beats.headline: Nothing has changed, says Borant
beats.text: The announcer is chipper. The Valtay news means nothing, she says: Borant is still a kua-tin organisation, severed from the civil war that has just erupted at home, and this crawl is her personal life project and she is going nowhere. Then the notes. Sponsors may sell their stakes starting next floor. Over 500 crawlers are claimed and over 50 hunters have fallen. Hunters may no longer communicate with anyone outside the dungeon. The southwestern hot springs were turned up, cooking the crawlers in them. Crawlers in the top 1,000 can now see their rankings.

beats.headline: Moderated by Circe Took
