beats.text: CrawlCon programme, as printed. Panel: Crawling Through the Ages. Crawlers both new and old lead a discussion on the current state of the crawl, followed by a Q&A, special guests to be announced. Moderated by Circe Took of the Hive. Next item down, an autograph session with Crawler Carl, refunds guaranteed if he does not survive long enough to attend. The listing does not mention any history between the moderator and the fan favourite.

beats.headline: What it is
beats.text: Panels, autograph tables, special guests, crawlers both new and old and a children's art contest, held once every other season for thousands in person and billions watching virtually. No active crawler has been on the roster in more than a century.

beats.headline: Carl gets a booth
beats.text: Word reaches him on the sixth floor: his fans have voted him onto the roster, and attendance is not a request.

beats.headline: Fan box time
beats.text: Carl opens a fan box with Katia watching. A plastic rectangle pops out on a red lanyard printed Titan Entertainment in Syndicate standard. The badge is the size of a postcard. Its back scrolls with advertisements; its front shows a moving image of a horned demon shooting fire from its mouth, SPECIAL GUEST exploding along the edge, and a spinning logo reading Carl, Dungeon Crawler World: Earth. A timer appears at twenty-two hours. Carl reads the description: what the ever-loving fuck? Yeah, thanks, assholes, he tells the ceiling. Katia reads it and barks with laughter. He tells Zev to send Donut instead. It's in your best interests to be cooperative, Zev answers, just this once.

beats.headline: Safehome Yolanda
beats.text: The party joins an existing guild on the same day Katia finally walks out of the party. She does not go far. The charter is what keeps her within reach of people she is no longer travelling with.

beats.headline: A counterspell in the druid town
beats.text: We raid a small druid town after Eva, and she has already gone. She leaves a glamour behind: she charmed the townsfolk and talked them into attacking us as we came in. When they approach, I cast a counterspell and take the glamour off them. A tree-person tells me, in tears, what she did to them. The raid ends without violence. I can fly now, and I move with Elle behind Katia, Florin and Bautista. Li Na can track her, and she is backed into the hot springs and the lava tubes.

beats.headline: Leaving the party
beats.text: I watch the recap in the guild and come over to make the exchange and finally leave the party. Every time Donut gets a quest, I get one too, and soon I will be getting my own. We pooled enough for the purchase that lets Mordecai keep his space, and Mistress Tiatha gets her own as well; she is pretty excited. We would like Donut to be the one who buys it, because she has the highest charisma of any of us. She asks whether she can still visit. Of course. I will be right next door.

beats.headline: The smaller dog
beats.text: The recap shows me in my beautiful shape. A borough boss that looks like a stegosaurus. I put my damage reflect on the smaller of my two dogs. The boss crushes him. The damage goes back to the boss, and the boss dies. The dog is fine. I pull out the dead boss's eye with my bare hand and bite it like an apple. I am laughing.

beats.headline: He did the con once
beats.text: The kid's fan box is a CrawlCon badge. I haven't seen them use current crawlers for the con in over a century. I was a special guest once, years after my season. All I did was the autograph session, and I only ended up signing three items. Three events means they're going all in. He asks how this is even a thing. The first active prep teams landed on his planet in 1936. The first sci-fi convention was in Philadelphia in 1938. Do the math. And no, Donut. Sorry, kid. This one's just Carl.

beats.headline: Heads on the carapace
beats.text: Hunter Vrah, as featured in tonight's recap. She and a unit of four other mantis creatures swoop out of the air onto a cart on a heavily wooded trail and decapitate the crawlers riding in it. The five land and loot the bodies while the show runs a rapid-fire list of what they took. The heads of the two crawlers Vrah killed personally, both human, she affixes to her carapace by some method the broadcast does not explain.

beats.headline: A guild called Safehome Yolanda
beats.text: The Royal Court of Princess Donut is now a member of the guild Safehome Yolanda. Controlling party: Team Meadowlark. Guildmaster: crawler Imani C. Level seven, six parties, sixty-three crawlers. Despite their age difference, Yolanda was one of Imani's best friends, and the name lands on Crawler Carl like a punch to the gut. A new door appears beside the saferoom exit, labelled Guild Common Area.

beats.headline: What I do now
beats.text: A Levitation potion lifts me off the ground, Mordecai's Major Charlie puts ten points on my intelligence for thirty seconds, I rise through the gas, and my spell finds two purple dots a kilometer and a half out. Samantha kills one and brings the other back by the ankle. Akland, moon elf, artillery specialist, the Dream. Cuffed to a pole, he says he's an accountant who did well at fantasy hunter camp, and that his boss only wants Louis. I let the view counter climb. I tell him I used to fix boats. Then I mark him. I'm going to show you what I do now.

beats.headline: Cuffed to a pole
beats.text: The elf hunter is going to wake up in seconds. Hunter Killer, asks Donut? No, says Carl: heal him, but I want to talk to him first. He slips a ring on and pulls the enchanted handcuffs from his inventory. Akland comes round handcuffed to a pole, Donut behind him with a magic missile ready. It's not supposed to be like this, he pleads. He is just an accountant who did well at fantasy hunter camp, and they offered him money. Carl tells him about the world he had. Then the system tells Carl he has marked Akland.

beats.headline: Up and down on a slider
beats.text: Two or three elf hunters have set up a catapult and are walking gas-filled rocks across the town, and Carl has Samantha loaded face down in the xistera. He drinks the first potion. A slider appears in his interface, up and down only, with a sixty-second countdown, and he realises he has done this in the wrong order. His feet rise a foot, and tapping the air feels like standing on glass. Mordecai has stressed how dangerous these are: momentum will still drop you, so they are no substitute for feather fall unless taken before the jump. Treat it like thin ice. Carl hovers, waiting out his potion timer.

beats.headline: Three kilometres of Ping
beats.text: Elf hunters with a catapult are shelling the town with gas-filled rocks from somewhere out in the forest. Carl's intelligence sits just over thirty with his daily buffs, and his Ping reaches a kilometre plus five hundred metres for every ten points, so Mordecai has made him a potion: ten more points for thirty seconds, then ten fewer for five minutes. Carl drinks it hovering on Levitation. Boy, are you smart! He zooms up through the green cloud, casts Ping, filters the map down to purple hunters and finds two of them, a kilometre and a half northeast. Then he hurls Samantha at them.

beats.headline: A rocket on Samantha's head
beats.text: Samantha's head sits on the ground with her jaw held all the way open, like she is getting a root canal, and a rocket tied to the side of it with duct tape wrapped round her forehead and her neck. This is one of the few things Carl could not test in his workshop. He pulls out his xistera extension and tells her not to close her mouth until she sees them or the catapult. Okay, says Samantha. Click. The missile launches her into the air like a bottle rocket.

beats.headline: Launched, twice
beats.text: Carl duct-tapes a missile to my head and ties the string to my fang, and I say okay and close my mouth and go up like a bottle rocket with my HAIR ON FIRE. So he tapes on two. This time he throws me at the elves, and I pull the cord right over them, and I come down in the trees, and boom. Then I bite the other one's ankle and do not let go. BRING ME BACK, I say, and he does, and the elf comes too. It's my kill. MY KILL. Carl says not this one.

beats.headline: Elves at the door
beats.text: Two or three of the elves get a catapult set up and walk gas-rock artillery across the town. Carl uses Samantha to deliver missiles, delivers a villain's soliloquy while he is at it, and puts down another of their hunters.

beats.headline: A hunter camp in her family
beats.text: Hunter Akland, an accountant who works with soy crop shipping manifests, explains where hunters like him come from. Vrah's family runs a fantasy hunter camp, so people can pretend they are on the show. Once a cycle the Dream rent the whole moon out for their employees and family members to play. The best players win places in an army for the ninth floor. Akland did well, won a spot, and was then offered a great deal of money to come down to the Hunting Grounds instead. He was never supposed to be in real danger.

beats.headline: Two rockets and a ping
beats.text: Two missiles duct-taped to her head, Samantha lies face down in the installed extension. Carl drinks a levitation potion, then Major Charlie for thirty seconds of extra intelligence, rises up through the green cloud and pings: two hunters in a clearing a kilometre and a half northeast of town. Go get 'em. He lobs her at them, the rockets flare over the clearing, and she disappears into the trees to a distant detonation. Bring me back, she messages. He drops the extension and she pops up at his feet, hair on fire, with the ankle of the second, unconscious elf clamped in her teeth.

beats.headline: The Raggle Rouser
beats.text: Carl holds out a bracelet from the dead elf. Black, glass, a plain bangle, and then I read the description. Enchanted Obsidian Bracelet of the Raggle Rouser: ten constitution, five dexterity, fifteen percent fire resistance, and a level-10 Fireball once every twenty minutes. Give it to me now, Carl. It appears on my front right leg, much smaller, and I move it to my front left. He tells me not to use a fireball in a tight space, because it is more dangerous than magic missile. I know how fire works, Carl.

beats.headline: Give it to me now
beats.text: Akland, the moon elf Samantha dragged back by the ankle, had a black bracelet on his arm, and Carl pulled it off before killing him. He offers it to Donut and asks whether she still has a couple of slots left. Black, glass, a plain bangle, she says, not as ugly as that wood anklet, and then she reads the description and gasps. Give it to me now, Carl. It appears on her front right leg, suddenly much smaller; she snorts and moves it to the front left. Don't use a fireball in a tight space, says Carl. I know how fire works, Carl.

beats.headline: Two points a kill
beats.text: Congratulations, Murderer. With Akland dead, the ring levels up and now gives two stat points for every kill. This one paid out a single point of constitution, the elf's highest stat, along with two trophies and level 55 for Carl, who had forgotten to summon his gauntlet. The elf's inventory is crawler biscuits and another gonorrhea arrow, obviously meant for Louis. Donut says it was unnecessarily gruesome, that he is getting angrier and angrier and it is scaring her. He promises to kill them nice and clean.

beats.headline: A dud boon and a hunch
beats.text: My first boon from Emberus is a dud: plus 50% damage to fire spells for 30 hours, and I don't have any fire spells. The rock chucker the Dream left in the clearing is better. It glows green, it throws poison, and the plates that power it are covered in little diodes, which is not magic. I take it anyway. Then the thing that's been bugging me. They'd never let this floor's climax belong to Signet's program. So if she goes after Imogen before the party, it's against a boss nobody is allowed to kill. They want a tragic ending.

beats.headline: Target the coin
beats.text: A note in the twenty-second edition, from Crawler Drakea. Hunters avoid the elites; the elites are more dangerous and more numerous; some of the more powerful hunters go after them anyway, for gear and clout. Drakea is not yet strong enough to kill either claw to claw, and is experimenting with hidden traps to bring hunter and elite together. The woman from the talk show let slip that the naga have offered insurance to the dramas that control the elites. Killing individuals may be satisfying. When one values coin above life, you should target the coin.

beats.headline: What the hunters leave alone
beats.text: A note in the cookbook from Drakea, 22nd edition, on the sixth floor's hunters: they avoid the elites. They are smart enough not to fight something they are not allowed to defeat easily. The trouble for crawlers is that elites are more dangerous than the hunters and much more numerous, and they should always be avoided. Some of the more powerful hunters hunt elites anyway, for the equipment and the clout. The note calls it a most dangerous game.

beats.headline: A castle mostly underwater
beats.text: Night in the forest, heading north to join Signet's assault team at one of the old trees before approaching the river. Crawler Carl and Crawler Princess Donut have only a minor role tonight; Signet is plainly saving them for part two. That suits the cat, because the castle is mostly submerged, and she has reiterated her position on going underwater several times. Carl is more concerned with part two, and with which programme gets to own its climax.

beats.headline: The real prize
beats.text: The dead hunter's hand is already gone, sent to Carl in a hunter killer box; his loot runs to an unenchanted bow, a gonorrhea arrow and a photograph of Louis with a dog filter. The real prize is the trebuchet, abandoned in the clearing and spiked to the ground, oddly small for the rocks it has been lobbing: the size and height of a windsurfing board, made of a weird, hollow wood, light enough to carry easily, and glowing green. There is no counterweight. Two plates want to come together like magnets; ratchet the arm, attach the rock to the sling, pull the lever. Carl suspects the postage-stamp plates are high tech, not magic. These assholes are still cheating.

beats.headline: Something extra from loot-all
beats.text: The Skull Empire hunter called The Talent has zapped himself with his own Lightning scroll. Carl tells Donut to loot him, so he will not pay that much in tithe taxes, and she gasps: almost 75,000 gold and three scrolls of Lightning. When she hits loot all she gets something extra that was not listed: a credit chit. It looks like a credit card and has no description. They need to go buy something with it before they cancel it, she says. Hold onto it for now, Carl tells her; they will ask Mordecai. And from now on, loot hunters one item at a time.

beats.headline: Traps all the way down
beats.text: From the treeline, Fort Freedom glitters in the dark. The river is a mile and a half wide here. The naiads have cleared the long, muddy slope so nothing can approach unseen, and one stone-paved trail runs down to an archway at the water. The slope lights up with traps: alarms, summoning traps, silent alarms along the walkway. Inside, the usurpers occupy the castle and neither maintain it nor rule. They were so obsessed with being free that they forgot what governing involves.

beats.headline: His whole team, hunting a top ten
beats.text: A champion has fallen, and a hunter has claimed a bounty. Crawler Langley and every member of his team have been eliminated on the sixth floor. They were not on the top ten. They were hunting a man who was, Bogdon Ro, with a large group, and had him cornered. Whatever happened next killed all of them, and a hunter took the credit. Immigrants to Finland, according to Crawler Carl, who had not said a word to him since the floor began. Katia broke the news in the chat. The orc at Carl's feet says it shows how dangerous Vrah is.

beats.headline: She asks for Signet's body
beats.text: Signet! Darling! Cousin, or niece, whichever. Nice tits, from my side of the family. I explain it simply: she is the last trueblood heir and a blood relation, so she can give me my body back. Really she has to give me HER body. She dies, of course, but it only takes two or three minutes, and I will walk her through the spell. King Blaine will stop banging my mother once he sees it. She says after the naiads and the elves she possibly has a spell for a permanent body. Ungrateful bitch. She's full of shit.

beats.headline: Part of my family
beats.text: Fort Freedom glitters in the dark, and it is falling apart. If they had only waited, the confederates would have had it without blood. I was my mother's only child and never eligible under the imperial charter; rule would have gone back to the people. They killed her just before she was to become tsarina. I think she meant to step down. My tears do not touch my skin. I tell Carl that if something happens to me tonight, I appreciate all he has done, and I consider him part of my family now. And family is very important to me.

beats.headline: Future Huntress
beats.text: Three of the Skull Empire's hunters try an ambush near an outcropping of the all-tree, which turns spells back on their casters. The Talent zaps himself dead with his own Lightning scroll, carrying almost 75,000 gold and a credit chit. The survivor is Future Huntress, level 50, a Boring Ol' Fighter who has not levelled once. She says top tens are fair game for anyone who bought the hunting license, that the empire paid for first crack at Carl, and that her death leaves him to the Dark Hive. Her highest stat is charisma.

beats.headline: Lights on the slope
beats.text: From the edge of the forest above Fort Freedom, a long, muddy slope runs down to the river, cleared of foliage by the naiads so they can see anything coming. As Carl watches, lights pop up all over it. Traps, lots of them: alarms and summoning traps, and silent alarms all along the stone walkway. A group of bush elves crawls over the mud, quietly disarming the ones inside the protection spell, then creeps out of it to start on one Carl had not even noticed. They are carving a path to the water.

beats.headline: The front door is the decoy
beats.text: The plan is child's play because the defence is a joke. An alarm goes off at the front, the poorly trained guards run toward it, and Signet's amphibious team comes in the undefended rear, straight to the throne room, where the confederacy's leaders are conveniently hiding. Samantha is given a long line to deliver if captured, announcing herself as Psamathe. Signet walks in with the water shying away from her. Then the bodies start surfacing: naiads, paper soldiers, and what is probably a bush elf, ripped in half.

beats.headline: Goddess of unrequited love
beats.text: Carl says we have never learned what Samantha is supposed to be the goddess of. I asked her, Carl. She says unrequited love. I must say, I get the impression it is more like the goddess of crazy ex-girlfriends. Everything she does is because she wants to get back with some king. She also thinks her sand ooze child, the one married to the mage on the last floor, is alive and on the ninth floor. She wants to pick the child up and then get down to wherever the king is. The first part of her plan is a body.

beats.headline: Hit with the ugly stick
beats.text: Samantha thinks it was a trap and says she has just wriggled free. Carl tells Donut to stay where she is; he is going in. He slips the water-breathing ring on his finger and feels the gills form on his neck, and a notice says he has been hit with the ugly stick. Donut is appalled that it only lowered his charisma by one: he is all slimy, and Signet told them to wait. A new explosion rocks the river, bloody water showering from the castle window.

beats.headline: Past the guards and into the vent
beats.text: They come out of the water to get me, but I go right past them and into their castle. They have really let this place go. The tapestry of my grandfather is gone. Then I get sucked into a filter vent, and the song trap falls off my head and goes deep down, so now they'll never turn it off. I do not say my line. There's no talking in war. The water tastes of blood and green algae. Then: uh-oh. I think it was a trap. Don't worry. I wriggle free. I almost have him.

beats.headline: Water does not touch me
beats.text: Water shies from me as I walk into my mother's palace, the way iron filings flee a magnet. It is the curse. A high elf cast it the night my mother died; the dissenters who killed the tsar and his family managed it only with high elf help. I float like an apple, so my hammerhead, the one with the body of a man, takes me in his arms and carries me down. Once I am deep enough I do not rise again. I have a spell for air.

beats.headline: Recalled from the river
beats.text: Carl loaded Samantha into the extension with an alarm ball taped to her head and threw her upstream, to shout when it went off and aim for the castle. The extension has stayed on his arm since. Now Miss Nadine breaks for the water, and he has to take it off before he dives in. Samantha, I gotta teleport you back. No, she messages, I almost have him. He pulls the extension into his inventory.

beats.headline: Straight up, not sideways
beats.text: Samantha said 'I almost have him,' and I recalled her without asking who. What arrives is Claude Sludgington the Fourth, a truck-sized, lightning-eyed level-65 borough boss with Samantha and Holger inside it. Its eye-lightning blows Miss Nadine apart. The hint says flip it and go for the stomach, so I cast Protective Shell. I'm too close. It launches straight up instead of rolling over. Donut sets its belly on fire, it falls on me, Mongo eats his way out through the back using me as a foothold, and the whole fight takes maybe thirty seconds.

beats.headline: An eryops on the throne
beats.text: Whatever holds the throne room is a lightning-shooting river monster, and Samantha has her teeth in it. Claude Sludgington the Fourth, Eryops Gigantis, arrives beside Crawler Carl at truck size. His history: short of gold, because they would not tax anyone yet still owed tithes to the high elves, the confederates threw a fundraiser ball at fifty gold a head. Nobody came. The citizens were starving and eating anyone near the water. Claude did come, and the guards let him in.

beats.headline: In one side, out the other
beats.text: BIG FROG. FIRE HOLE IN FROG. MOTHER JUMPS OFF. MONGO GOES IN. MONGO EATS THROUGH. MONGO COMES OUT THE BACK. FROG GOES BOOM. MORE GUTS. FOOD.

beats.headline: Fireball is awesome
beats.text: Carl's shield throws the disgusting thing straight up, which is not to the side, Carl. He shouts at me to shoot. Fireball! The level-10 ball rises slowly, almost reluctantly, and blasts into its pink stomach, and the whole creature catches alight and lands splat on the shield, sliding off face down against the trees, firing lightning everywhere. Wow. Fireball is awesome. Then Mongo dives for the wound with me still on his back, and I backflip onto Carl's shoulder, firing one last magic missile.

beats.headline: A beachball of fire
beats.text: Carl's Protective Shell goes up too close to the boss and launches it straight into the night sky, with the ogre Areson, Carl assumes, still riding it. Donut gallops into the shell on Mongo. Shoot it, Carl shouts. Fireball! A beachball-sized ball of fire rises slowly, almost reluctantly, and blasts into the pink stomach of the flailing beast. It bursts into flames end to end, lands on top of the shield with a vicious splat, and slides off into the trees, stuck face down. Fireball is awesome, Donut cries.

beats.headline: Two dead guards
beats.text: Knocked off course by a sizzling saddle, Carl scrambles back up the hill toward the rampaging boss, and his foot hits a summoning trap nobody disarmed. A pair of naiad guards suddenly appear in front of him, already dead, splat onto the hill and roll down toward him. He has to hurdle one to keep going.

beats.headline: The quest gets a name
beats.text: Samantha goes across the water to look at the far shore and finds the team over there dead. All of them, and all of them by one thing. The Recital quest updates with the name it has been withholding. Big Tina. Allosaurus, level 80, immortalized city boss, and the attacks on Point Mongo have been hers from the beginning.

beats.headline: Ahead of the quest
beats.text: The boss dies before anyone gives me the quest for it, and the achievement says so: Premature Questjaculation, and no quest box. Clint was ripped up in the water, and Holger howls for Miss Nadine. I tell him it was my fault for bringing the thing up here. Areson says no, she died a warrior's death. Then I work the slope for traps, and after the third or fourth summoning trap Find Traps finally hits ten and the hill lights up like a Christmas display. That leaves me ten summoning traps, which only Donut could use.

beats.headline: Barely a fight
beats.text: Premature Questjaculation: a quest is beaten before it can even be handed out, so the reward is nothing. Tsarina Signet takes the castle. Plenty of guards, an algae infestation, confederates who stopped attempting to rule ages ago, a throne room surrendered to an eryops, a kingdom in shambles. It would have fallen on its own within months. Part one completes. Part two names the true culprit: the high elves, and Queen Imogen.

beats.headline: The quest names the house
beats.text: Part two of Vengeance of the Daughter comes down: kill Signet's half-sister, Queen Imogen of the high elves, who leaves her chambers only for the yearly party the high elves throw for their elite, the same party the game's top players are invited to. The reward is the run of her castle, and the castle is said to hold the thing that turns Scolopendra's attack aside.

beats.headline: The attacks have a name
beats.text: The quest updates with the answer: the dinosaur eating the town is called Big Tina. Samantha's recon on the far shore turns up ursine bitten to pieces, one set of three-toed tracks and pink feathers everywhere, and Areson knows whose they are.

beats.headline: A name for the thing at the fences
beats.text: Samantha's reconnaissance across the water finds the ursines on the far shore torn apart, and the quest updates with the culprit: Big Tina, the dinosaur behind the raids on Point Mongo.

beats.headline: It was barely a fight
beats.text: We have taken the castle. If I had known it was defended so poorly, I would have gone in myself. There were guards enough, but it would have fallen in months on its own: an algae infestation, and confederates who stopped trying to rule ages ago and lost the throne room to an eryops. The kingdom is in shambles. Once we are free of the high elves, I must find a suitable ruler to begin the long work. My mother weeps from beyond the veil. The cat asks if I will rule. Not with my curse. I will never be able to remove it.

beats.headline: Ten for the inventory
beats.text: While Samantha makes her own way to the shore, Carl works the slope for untriggered traps to train his stalled Find Traps skill. The summoning traps are hard to spot. He trips two by accident, and both times they bring a pair of naiad guards, every one of them already killed by were-castors. After the third or fourth, Find Traps reaches ten, and the slope lights up like a Christmas display. He collects everything, ten summoning traps among it. He has no towns on this floor and no minions; that is a Donut thing. If they ever use one, she will have to set it.

beats.headline: Part one done, part two named
beats.text: The first act completes. The second arrives as a name: Queen Imogen of the high elves, Signet's half-sister, who will be at the masquerade at the close of this floor. The reward is the run of the high elf castle, thought to hold something that blunts Scolopendra's attack.

beats.headline: The ink comes from the body
beats.text: Edgar is a tortoise. Edgar is also the reason Signet's tattoos are what they are, and the method is not squeamish: he works from the corpse. Miss Nadine, dead, goes onto Signet's skin as ink and comes back off it as something that moves and fights. Miss Nadine's attachment to Clint drags Clint along with her, so he turns up on the skin as well, unasked and unbilled. Nobody in the party looks surprised. There is apparently a queue for this.

beats.headline: Mayor of Alucarda
beats.text: This village is Alucarda. It already has a name, which the cat does not like. The mayor was R'aggah. He has returned to the earth. The mayor is me now. The tree man at the saferoom door tells the man so: an evil woman with two beasts that kill indiscriminately. The man asks where I am. Nobody answers him. He is gone before they can. The cat is still here.

beats.headline: What a nodling does at death
beats.text: Tsarina Signet, explaining her ogre Areson, supplies the relevant biology. When a nodling dies, it splits into new creatures, one per head. They emerge as toddlers and grow quickly, and the original body remains. A nodling may have anywhere from two heads to six, usually two or three. Crawler Princess Donut asks whether that is what the Popov brothers are. Crawler Carl says yes, and that it raises more questions than it answers about two men who picked that race.

beats.headline: Never alone with her
beats.text: Signet wants to jump Carl's bones, and if I know anything, it is how story arcs work. Before the final battle there will be a meadow and a ring of flowers in her hair and candles and butterflies, and afterward they will try to kill him. Sex with a guest star always spells doom. Well, I am not going to let it happen. He is never to be alone with her again. Carl says he is not going to boink Signet. No, he is not. Not if I have anything to say about it.

beats.headline: Di-we, and the ones born of him
beats.text: Edgar works the new tattoo into my thigh from what remains of Miss Nadine. My tattoos are fallen companions, or fallen enemies we have deemed worthy. I received the first on the night of my mother's murder, the same night I met Edgar. The second is Di-we, a three-headed nodling who died protecting me from agents of my sister. When a nodling dies, he splits: Areson, Apollon and Herman were born the day he fell. The new one on my skin is not Miss Nadine. She is a facsimile. A loving memory.

beats.headline: Into the inventory
beats.text: Across the river on the south shore, the ursine are big dead, chomped in half by something huge, and pink boa feathers litter the ground. Carl ties the sleeping Samantha to his back by her hair and loots armour, enchanted daggers and swords, worth over a thousand gold in all. Most of the traps here have already been disarmed or triggered, but at the edges of the area he finds and disarms a few more, among them a new one called Slippery Slope, which would have caused him to slip and fall into the water. The traps all go into his inventory.

beats.headline: The grandpup named Lix
beats.text: Second trip through the checkpoint in orbit, and this time Donut and Samantha are down there alone with that psychopath. My interface is blacked out. Something is burning near the southern point of India, big enough to see from up here. The gnoll who finally comes down the chute is older, gray around the snout, head of security on the production vessel below. He says his grandpup's name is Lix, that he'd take it as a personal favour if I looked approvingly on her entry, and that he can overlook any future thefts from production trailers.

beats.headline: Around his neck
beats.text: Zev opens Carl's inventory for a moment: pull out the CrawlCon badge from the fan box and put it around your neck, take nothing else out, and lose the bandana. The red demon on the front roars silently, shooting fire, and the back scrolls an ad for a real estate venture on what looks like a swamp planet. A new tab appears in his interface, CrawlCon schedule, and he cannot open it. This vessel has its own containment zone, Zev explains, and his crawler wetware blocks him out.

beats.headline: Linger as much as you can
beats.text: Okay, so, this is not a regular production trailer. It's a Valtay landing vessel parked at the bottom of the ocean, and we are under constant surveillance, by the AI and by the ship's own security. The rental trailers were kicked off system after an escape attempt. Donut had quite the fight, and she's okay, safe in the guildhall. I can't tell him more. I tell Carl it might be in his best interests to linger as much as he can, that others may be waiting where he goes back down, and that he needs his rest.

beats.headline: Thirty for Lix
beats.text: Three judges, scores from one to thirty, two hours of children. Hurk the gleener is blitzed and so is the camel beside me, who passes out while somebody else votes for him. A kid named Keith draws me being eaten by a brindle grub and says his dad calls me a cheater. He gets a one. For Lix, the security captain's grandpup, I buy Hurk's vote by promising to praise his Desperado Club on my panel. Her drawing of her pup-pop with a truncheon wins with a perfect 90. Keith comes last with four.

beats.headline: Judging children's drawings
beats.text: The first event is a juvenile quickdraw contest, scored out of thirty. Between rounds he learns who is moderating his panel: the mother of a hunter he put down on this floor.

beats.headline: Judge us
beats.text: Three small jet-black goats with red eyes walk up to the art contest's judging table side by side, carrying no entry, with names like equations. Judge us, says the one in the middle. Carl gives them a five. They sigh as one, spin, and walk off: judgment received. Hurk the gleener shivers and says they are all like that, the adults worse, and nobody knows what goes on in their heads. The caprid on the crawl sits in a circle with them on a program every few days, screaming while they scream back.

beats.headline: Train the spell, upgrade the shorts
beats.text: One training room here combines a regular training room, the magic workshop, the explosives studio and several others into one. Carl's ordinary spells are listed as trainable alongside the spells that come from equipment, like Protective Shell. Apparently, train one of those here and it is the equipment itself that gets upgraded: in the case of Protective Shell, his boxer shorts.

beats.headline: The tier-four room
beats.text: Security installs a tier-three bed and a door marked Ultimate Training Room, tier four, and the gnoll says the captain sends his regards. Six hours a day across six skills, spells, and workshop tables I don't even have with me, and the trainer is a real AI: a badger with an eyepatch and a hook. The weapon I'm after, he says, needs a table for multiple permanent minions, or a bunch of suicidal friends. I spend two hours fixing my sticky bombs instead, and Powerful Strike finally moves from nine to ten.

beats.headline: A daughter lost on her first hunt
beats.text: Briefing from Zev, four hours before the panel. Circe Took: a minor hive queen, a mantis, outside both the military and the Burrower clan. She started out as a hunter, was quite famous for a while, and is now a businesswoman who owns an amusement park. Crawler Carl killed her child: Xindy, Vrah's little sister, on her very first hunt. Zev's assessment is that the mantis people are overly dramatic about everything and a hive queen probably has ten thousand children. Her advice: avoid the subject of her government.

beats.headline: Train the spell, upgrade the shorts
beats.text: The tier-four training room installed for Crawler Carl while he is held off the floor lists spells that come from equipment alongside the ordinary ones. Train Protective Shell there, and it is the equipment that gets upgraded: the boxers, in this case. The room also trains workshop tables without them being present, which Crawler Carl rates as its most valuable feature.

beats.headline: A copy, less scorched
beats.text: Carl's training room can teach him his workshop tables as well, and they need only be installed in his crafting studio. He finds Sapper's Table on the list and clicks it. A familiar level-five table pops up out of the ground, identical to his own, though less scorched, and his hand doesn't come away sticky with the residue the hobgoblin disco ball left. Instead of the usual multi-armed trainer, a badger with an eyepatch and a hook for a hand fades in, decides Carl is practically ready to teach him, and tells him the weapon he wants needs a different table altogether.

beats.headline: Diminishing returns past fifteen
beats.text: In a training room on the sixth floor, a skill all his gear should lift to sixteen stays at fifteen. Armour and weapon enhancements lose effectiveness past fifteen, as Mordecai warned. The gauntlet's one point of Powerful Strike and the toe ring's five will still carry Carl past it, but he will probably need to reach twelve or so on his own first, and each level beyond comes with diminishing returns.

beats.headline: Her little sister
beats.text: Hunter Vrah's little sister was Xindy, killed by Crawler Carl on her very first hunt. Their mother is Circe Took, a minor hive queen, a mantis outside both the military and the Burrower clan: a former hunter, famous for a while, now a businesswoman who owns an amusement park and probably has ten thousand children. She is moderating Carl's panel. Carl's reasoning runs that if she has found a way to speak with her daughter, Vrah will know exactly where and when he goes back down.

beats.headline: A fist that does not form
beats.text: Escorted by two gnoll guards, Carl climbs a ladder into what one of them calls a zero zone, no enhancements at all, and makes a fist. For the very first time the gauntlet does not form. The guard says not to worry: studio three is a class two. The same day brings some arithmetic: past fifteen, armour and weapon enhancements like the gauntlet's plus one to Powerful Strike lose effectiveness. It still counts, with diminishing returns.

beats.headline: Because of a pin
beats.text: Okay, so, the moderator is Circe Took, a minor hive queen, and the hunter Carl killed was her daughter, Xindy, Vrah's little sister, on her first hunt. Try to avoid talking about her government. He asks if I'm doing okay. About the best anyone can expect. Our whole system has gone dark. Those of us who stayed on after the change don't know if we'll be welcomed home or executed as traitors. My entire family was slaughtered because I refused to wear a pin. But I've got a job to do. I have to go, Carl.

beats.headline: Their spokeswoman takes the floor
beats.text: A woman in a brown cloak patterned with circles and lines tells the stagehand not to cut Carl off, and he freezes. The people nearest her get up and move away. She cannot address Carl directly, she says, because she is one of his sponsors and it would breach the contract; she is also a sponsor of CrawlCon, and she has told them to let him speak. Then she walks out, and Circe Took calls her a bitch. Uptown Hal names her afterwards: the collective's spokeswoman.

beats.headline: Left behind after the panel
beats.text: On the way to his CrawlCon panel, Carl was walked through a studio where an older dwarf with a CrawlCon badge, Dr. Ratchet, was preparing a demonstration at a workbench beside a quarter-sized dwarven automaton. He needed the room's juice, so Carl would have to go upstairs; then he called after him: good luck, and keep your head down. After the panel, the studio is empty except for one table. Automaton Table. Level 5. On it lies Dr. Ratchet's Guide to Building Automatons for Fun and Profit. Carl takes the table and the guide into his inventory.

beats.headline: He crowdsources the kill
beats.text: The guards' vape smoke was not just smoke. By the time I notice they are gone, my bare feet are up on the panel table and my inhibitions are with them, and I find I don't care. Circe Took won't let anyone else talk, so I ask the room the question this convention is really about: what's the best way to kill her daughter? An orc in the audience counts them for me. Seven warriors including Vrah, and a male trading in Zockau. Hands go up everywhere.

beats.headline: A table and a book, personal
beats.text: The guards walk me back without much talk. At the studio door Frito tells me there are two kinds of transactions, personal and business, and we have done both today: the drug was business, the matter with the commander is personal. I tell him I don't understand. In the empty studio sits a level-five Automaton Table, and on it an autographed copy of Dr. Ratchet's Guide to Building Automatons for Fun and Profit. Both go in my inventory. Then the bandana, the ring, and the green room.

beats.headline: The table, cut in two
beats.text: Panel footage. Circe Took is the size of a mantaur, with folded blade arms a metre long, and she can see Crawler Carl before the audience can. Her opening remark is that his luck is a dishonour on the hive. Her second is an arm brought down through the table beside him. Had he truly been sitting there, it would have cut him in half. She then introduces the panel, talks over the author mid-sentence, and informs the room that the season's top crawler has not long to live.

beats.headline: Bored to death, on air
beats.text: Circe Took lectures for almost ten minutes on the history of the crawl, the Hive's place in it, and the danger of the Indigenous Species Protection Act. Crawler Carl bangs his head on the table and announces she has succeeded in boring him to death. When he turns to her dead child, she orders him cut off. A robed woman at the back says no, and Circe accuses the room of a setup to mock her child's death. She is not the Maestro, she says, and she is not so easily trapped.

beats.headline: About the other daughters
beats.text: The robed woman leaves. Circe Took calls her a godsdamned bitch and swears to kill her, throws the broken piece of table at the wall, and heads for the exit. Crawler Carl asks the room for the best way to kill Vrah. She freezes where she stands while the audience answers: eight left, one of them a male who stays in Zockau to deal with the trade representatives, seven warriors including Vrah, all Dark Hive. Invited back to the table, she hisses that she means to hunt down, personally, whoever harms her other daughters, and stomps out.

beats.headline: The panel goes the way it was booked to go
beats.text: Dosed by his own guards into losing his inhibitions, Carl picks a fight with the moderator on stage and asks the room for the best way to get to her surviving daughter. She smashes the table and walks out. A hooded woman at the back stops her cutting him off first, then reveals herself as one of his sponsors and leaves.

beats.headline: Circe Took's daughters
beats.text: The Dark Hive's party in the Hunting Grounds is a family concern. A CrawlCon audience that knows it well counts eight mantids left on the floor: seven warriors, all daughters of Circe Took, Vrah among them, and one male who stays in Zockau trading with the other representatives. Circe chairs Carl's panel herself, carves a chunk out of the table beside him, and on her way out promises to hunt down whoever harms her other daughters. Carl calls after her that it will be him.

beats.headline: Autographed and left behind
beats.text: On his way to the panel, Carl passed through a studio where an older dwarf with a CrawlCon badge, Dr. Ratchet, was preparing a demonstration at a workbench beside a quarter-sized automaton. Now the studio is empty except for a table: Automaton Table, Level 5. On it lies a regular paperback with a familiar smiling dwarf riding on the back of a mechanical horse thing, Dr. Ratchet's Guide to Building Automatons for Fun and Profit. Carl opens it to the first page. It is autographed. He takes the guide and the table into his inventory.

beats.headline: Crawling Through the Ages
beats.text: Subject is a former crawler and a member of the Dream, appearing on a CrawlCon panel on the current state of the crawl. He is also carrying a Gondii worm in his brain on behalf of the Valtay, which is a detail the panel does not cover. He brags well. It is the part of him that is still his own.

beats.headline: The river says jump
beats.text: Zev's green room, five minutes to go. I can't take anything out of inventory here, so I set an alarm trap going inside it and paste the plan into the chat while Donut gives me backstory. A potion won't work either, so I'm going in with nothing to protect me. A calm comes over me that isn't peace. The river in the back of my head says this is where I belong. I ask Zev, if I die and Donut gets out, to watch over her. She says she'll do her best.

beats.headline: A decoy from a beanie
beats.text: We were trying to get back to Carl, but it was too far, so I am in a guildhall when he asks. I can't make a good facsimile of Donut in time. Daniel has a stuffed animal called a back alley mouser that will work, and I am at a table shaping a fake crown and sunglasses for it. It is a pity we don't have Robot Donut anymore.

beats.headline: Sand people in bishop hats
beats.text: The CrawlCon audience briefs Crawler Carl. The Nebulars are camping out and claiming the right to hunt him too, since he is in their territory, and they are pushing back against the Dark Hive: the nebs and the mantids fought a war once. They are not a race but a religious cult that augments itself as a sacrament. They settle hard planets, engineer their children to survive them, then half move on. Soothers, humans, elves and more, all in the same full-body outfit. Carl pictures sand people in bishop hats.

beats.headline: Priests in training
beats.text: The Nebular Sin Patrol attends nearly every crawl with different hunters each time: young males, studying for the priesthood, trained for the event. Anyone born on a seeded planet is an abomination to them, and hunting one is a crusade. They spend heavily, sometimes on a deity sponsorship, and campaign for the right to run a crawl of their own. They favour cleric and paladin targets, hence Prepotente and Miriam Dom. Someone mentions they botched an attack on Lucia Mar a few days ago.

beats.headline: Lucia's traps in the doorways
beats.text: Lucia is in the saferoom, screeching and punching herself in the face, waiting for me to come out. She has found a way to cheat the safety measures: traps that kick people out of the room. I went out when I thought she was gone, hit one, and landed in the middle of town, and then I hit another, and she came out of the woods and chased me inside just as the hunters arrived. So now I am in the guildhall, trying to give CARL important backstory.

beats.headline: Tortured, and five meters off
beats.text: They TORTURED me to find out where Carl would appear. Like they can torture ME. Ha! I played along and gave them the wrong spot, a whole FIVE METERS away. You're welcome. Then the dryad guy snitched. Now I am tied to the back of this bug, surrounded by decapitated heads, and they are POOR COMPANY. Donut abandoned me to a slobbering dog. The robe guys and the bug guys are fighting over who gets to kill Carl, and their hats really are fashionable.

beats.headline: Chaos to hide in
beats.text: I come back with my face against the tavern door, drink invisibility, drop a smoke curtain and cast Tripper, and every trap in town goes off at once. Donut sends two clockwork Sledges into the saferoom. The second carries a beanie cat in a crown, and Lucia takes the bait and teleports the room away. A hob-lobber into the bunched-up hunters kills three of the nebs. A berserking potion makes one mantis tear her own sister's head off. Drick said make chaos. I'm hiding in it.

beats.headline: Seven warriors down to one
beats.text: Carl kicks a wheeled bomb the system has named Just Wait Until Your Daddy Gets Home out of the saferoom door and slams it. It kills the three remaining mantises, explosive protection and all. With the berserker and the sisters who went down with her, the seven warrior daughters are now one: Vrah, infected and airborne. The only other mantis on the floor is the male merchant holed up in Zockau, and Carl is already writing him a note offering protection in exchange for the gear.

beats.headline: Out the saferoom door
beats.text: Carl rams a gonorrhea arrow into Vrah's neck just before her shield pops up, and he and Donut vault into the saferoom. The wheeled bomb is right there at the door, the one he wanted to use to level Zockau, with the Sledge peering out at two mantises rushing toward them. Cover your ears, Carl shouts, kicks it out the door and slams it. Donut has been over this: she can't cover her... Bam. The saferoom rocks and everyone rolls like billiard balls. The blast kills the three remaining mantises despite their protection against explosions, an ursine guy and a bunch of mobs in the woods. Lucia has got away, and so has Vrah, rocketing into the air.

beats.headline: His head bites Vrah
beats.text: Crawler Langley's head is mounted on Hunter Vrah's shoulder, beside Bogdon Ro's, among the trophies she wears on her back. Princess Donut, invisible, has cast Second Chance on as many of them as her mana allows. Carl tells Langley he is sorry he could not help him before, and that he appreciates his help now. Vrah says "What?" as the head bites into her exposed neck and holds. Bogdon Ro bites from the other side. Then a third.

beats.headline: Caught between mantises and a hob-lobber
beats.text: Zockau. A group of robed priests opens up on Crawler Carl's doorway with magic missiles and fireballs and hits a mantis warrior too. Her sisters take it personally. Carl drops a hob-lobber into the argument and kills three priests; the mantises are protected against explosives. A berserking mantis tears into what remains, and Carl marks three more with his Ring of Divine Suffering before she cuts them down. The first is a young human under the robe, name starting with Q. By the end, every neb is dead.

beats.headline: The last one, thrown
beats.text: Running up a temple wall on Sticky Feet, Carl pulls a potion ball filled with his last potion of Bloodlust. Ping returns only an error, as if the map is blocked in this town. He stows the ball and throws a full-strength hob-lobber into the bunched mantises and nebular priests instead. Then two more mantis warriors swoop in, and he beams the berserking potion at the closer one. It slams into her back. Enraged, she yanks the head off her own sister, dives on the group below and cleaves a human priest in half.

beats.headline: Marking priests mid-brawl
beats.text: Carl picks a nebular priest out of the melee by the Q at the start of his name, finds the only nebular on the ring's list beginning with Q, and marks him just before a berserking mantis cleaves him in half. He marks the next, and the next, and then stops, because they are all fighting and all injured and he does not dare mark more. All three had intelligence as their highest stat. Marked For Death levels between the second and third kill: seven points. Vrah is on the list. Lucia is not.

beats.headline: Lucia's saferoom loophole
beats.text: Lucia sets teleport traps inside saferoom doors, and the system allows it because the real trap module sits outside, at the destination. From inside a saferoom she can also cast a spell that teleports everyone in the room to a spot she chose in advance, where the room's safety no longer applies. It only works in her beautiful-woman form. A nerd kid at CrawlCon supplies the detail. Carl supplies a decoy, and the loophole takes Lucia to a spot where Vrah is already waiting.

beats.headline: Two copies and a bomb
beats.text: The Princess casts on me and there are three of us. The two copies go into the saferoom, one after the other. The first hits the trap and lands outside among the hunters, and it explodes there. The second carries the fake cat to Lucia. I wheel the bomb to the door, like Carl said, and stand there. Two mantises run at us. Carl kicks the bomb out and slams the door.

beats.headline: Lucia's two traps
beats.text: Lucia Mar has set at least two teleport traps, one just inside the saferoom door and one just outside the guildhall's. According to some kid at the panel, the system allows them in saferooms because the real trap module is set outside, at the destination: a loophole that has been around for years. Carl's plan uses it. Donut casts Clockwork Triplicate on the Sledge and sends the two automatons in one after the other. The first triggers the trap and appears right outside among the hunters. The second rushes at Lucia with what looks like Donut on its shoulder, but is one of Bautista's beanie babies, a black cat thing in a crown and sunglasses.

beats.headline: Level 74, and one arrow
beats.text: Hunter Vrah, now level 74 and larger, lands on Carl's alarm trap outside the saferoom and deshrouds him. She informs him that he is livestock, and that when this hunt is done she will take her place in the birthing hall of Hive Home two. Then the heads on her shoulders bite her, and Carl rams an arrow of Enthusiastic Double Gonorrhea into her neck. Her carapace bursts into flames and she ejects into the sky. The cures are gelding or passing it on. A future hive queen is not about to do the first.

beats.headline: Katia sews on two
beats.text: Two patches in one sitting. The gold ranged weapon box gives a small square of flaming arrows in an eagle claw, and the Gold Spicy Box a bigger white rectangle with a bomb hand-stitched in fine black thread, which Donut calls classic Spanish blackwork. Each patch adds a point to all Carl's stats on top of its own benefit; bigger ones take more room for the same. Katia, who affixed his first one, has already grabbed the sewing kit. Carl pulls off the jacket and hands it to her, and she maps out the best places and sews the arrows next to the planet earth on the shoulder, then moves to the bomb, placing it at the bottom left of the front along the hemline.

beats.headline: Five hundred beanies left
beats.text: The ruse used one of my uncommon mousers, fuzzier than the common kind, with the sunglasses and the false tiara, and a tame spell on it, because they attack when I pull the tag. The Princess says it looks nothing like her. It fooled Lucia and Vrah both. I have about five hundred left. My sponsor sent a refresher kit, and I can re-tag the ones that survive being summoned, twice. Tran and I are both swashbucklers now. We train together, and we get a bonus as a team.

beats.headline: Classic Spanish blackwork
beats.text: Carl expected a toe ring or foot lotion from the Gold Spicy Box. Instead he gets a second patch, a little bigger than the first: white, rectangular, with a little circular bomb hand-stitched in fine black thread, almost like a pencil drawing. Donut gasps and pulls it over to look. Exquisite, she says, classic Spanish blackwork. How would she know? Then it clicks: the useless hobby potion she got on the third floor, Scutelliphily, must be about patches, and Britney supplies the Latin, the love of small shields. The silk is Spider Reaper Minion thread. Carl hands Katia his jacket, and she starts mapping out where to sew the patches.

beats.headline: This is my family now
beats.text: The saferoom is full: Katia, Elle, Imani, Bautista, Louis, Firas, Gwen, Tran, Britney and others, and Mongo going person to person demanding scratches. This is it. This is my family now. I know the shakes are coming, and the river. For now I take the faces. Then the boxes: fourteen Hunter Killer boxes, 637,000 gold that the Emberus shrine beeps at every time, a patch for the vest, and a tattoo of a flaming ball of snakes that slaps itself onto my left arm.

beats.headline: He picks Swole over Stepson
beats.text: My base strength goes to 100 and I physically get bigger. The upgrade offers Swole, Prison Bitch or Stepson, three minutes to pick. Mordecai says Swole, Katia agrees, and Donut argues for the feet, because you should always take the foot-based choice. I take Swole: every strength point from a level-up counts double. Afterwards I sit with my hand on my arm and wonder whether that kid Keith's dad was right that I'm only alive because the AI wants it, and whether I should have picked Stepson.

beats.headline: An Enemy of the Church tattoo
beats.text: Saferoom paperwork. Crawler Carl comes out of this one with a fresh Enemy of the Church tattoo, awarded for defiling a shrine of Diwata, and with a piece of advice from a professional who has watched several seasons of this: steer well clear of dryads, and steer further clear of Diwata herself. He takes the tattoo. I have no record of him taking the advice.

beats.headline: Small shields
beats.text: Carl thinks he has finally worked out Donut's hobby. He pats his bomb patch: what type of thread is on this thing? Something to do with embroidery or patches, he says, and Donut gasps that he's right. Britney supplies the rest. Scutellus is Latin for small shield, phileein the Greek for the love of, so it means the love of small shields. Donut loves little patches. If anyone had asked, Britney says, she could have told them earlier.

beats.headline: Arrows on the shoulder
beats.text: The gold ranged weapon box holds a small square patch, about the size of Carl's first, the planet earth: a dozen flaming arrows clutched in an eagle claw, drawn Sailor Jerry style. Each new patch adds a point to all his stats plus its own benefit. Katia, who affixed the first one, has already grabbed the sewing kit. She takes the jacket, maps out the best places, and sews the arrow patch next to the planet earth on the shoulder.

beats.headline: Tundra Princess, level fifty-one
beats.text: Tundra Princess now, level fifty-one, and you'd never know it to look at me. Same anti-slip socks from Meadow Lark. Wedding ring on a chain, because my fingers shrank. I've got a glass of something yellow, and Louis is watching it like a dog watches jerky. Katia turned this whole circus around to come save your ass, young man, and then the flying house got jumped by pterodactyls, so now we're stuck in the jungle. How was the convention?

beats.headline: Sailor Jerry style
beats.text: Fifty-two hunting trophies in, Carl works through his boxes. The gold ranged-weapon box holds a patch for his jacket, the first he has got on this floor. Every patch he can fit adds plus one to all his stats on top of its own benefit. This one is small and square like his first, the planet earth, and shows about a dozen flaming arrows clutched in an eagle's claw, drawn in an old-school Sailor Jerry style. He thinks it looks kind of cool. Plus five percent dexterity and five percent damage to all ranged projectiles. Hell yeah. Katia, who sewed on his first one, grabs the kit and sews the arrows next to the planet earth on his jacket's shoulder.

beats.headline: He asks if Lucia lived
beats.text: I am in the back corner of Carl's space when he and Donut come in from the fight. I ask the one thing I want to know. Lucia survived? I did not see a notification. Donut says yes, that she's a cheater like Quan Ch and she got away. Good, I say. I push off the wall and go out into the guildhall common area. They all watch me go.

beats.headline: Nearly a sleeve
beats.text: A Gold Apostate box slaps another tattoo onto Carl's left upper arm, his largest yet: a flaming ball of snakes, one head reaching down to curl round the spiderweb tattoo on his elbow. With this, the spiderweb and the goblin pass, he practically has a whole sleeve on his left arm.

beats.headline: Fourteen more than expected
beats.text: Most of Carl's new prize boxes are low-tier adventurer boxes, but fourteen are Hunter Killer boxes, including the one from Future Hunter the orc, several more than he expected. He seems to have been credited for three nebs and three mantises killed by another mantis while she was enraged, though not for her own death at the hands of her people. Those six earn boxes and no experience. He now has 52 hunting trophies and 637,000 gold from those boxes alone.

beats.headline: Fifty-two trophies now
beats.text: Most of Carl's new boxes are low-tier adventurer boxes, but fourteen are Hunter Killer boxes, including the one from Future Hunter the orc. He now has fifty-two hunting trophies.

beats.headline: Letting Louis build his confidence
beats.text: Carl tells me not to let Louis drop a giant breastplate on me. The idea has some merit, and I am trying to let him build his confidence. He doesn't show it, but he was really upset when he learned those elves were hunting him. I walked in on him earlier, when he thought he was alone, and he was crying. I think he is worried we will kick him out of the guild. Then I sew Carl's new patches on, and Donut tells me my stitches are off.

beats.headline: The Voltron move
beats.text: Okay so, I came up with a move on my own. I throw armor at Katia and it equips itself the second it lands, if she has the slot open. Now picture her huge, no breastplate, and we drop a giant one on her from the Twister, and she gets even bigger, then a bigger helmet. Like Voltron. Sort of. Britney says if it misses, Katia gets crushed. It's a work in progress, man. Carl says it's a good idea. Just be careful.

beats.headline: Whisked away to a convention
beats.text: Crawler Elle McGibbons, briefing at speed. Team Cichociemni killed their own leader because he did not want them to be a group of murderers, and that leader was friendly with the Popovs, before Dmitri accidentally picked a race that combined him with his brother. The Popovs had Cichociemni cornered when the brothers were whisked away to CrawlCon. They have been gone two days and are back tomorrow. According to them, they are sharing a table with Crawler Carl.

beats.headline: A vocal coach of her own
beats.text: My platinum box gave me a vocal coach. A whole little room, with a microphone behind glass and a holographic lady called Lover Illiana who says I have a voice like a cygnus cloud gull. My singing is already level four. Mordecai says it is a great prize, even if we still need to discuss the name of the box. Then Carl finally works out what my useless Scutelliphily potion was for. Patches. Embroidery. Carl, I think you're right!

beats.headline: Straight up, not sideways
beats.text: The frog-lizard boss on the hill had a weak belly and a description hinting it should be rolled over. Crawler Carl cast too close and at the wrong angle, and the monster went straight up into the night sky instead of sideways. Crawler Donut's fireball met its stomach as it fell back down, and it landed on the shield in flames. Now, in a saferoom, the achievement catches up: Uprooted notes that a rooted-in-place boss was moved, and hopes he remembers how.

beats.headline: Voltron, sort of
beats.text: Louis tosses a potion bandolier at Katia, and it equips itself the moment it lands on her. Carl asks what, exactly, the move is. The pitch: she has that new backpack that lets her add a bunch of mass, so let her get really big without a breastplate, drop a giant one on her from the Twister so it equips, let her get bigger, then drop an even bigger helmet. Like the Voltron formation sequence. Sort of. Unless the item misses or does not hit right, Britney points out, and she is crushed. It's a work in progress, says Louis.

beats.headline: A hundred guilds, and a party
beats.text: The daily announcement counts just over 66,000 crawlers, exactly 100 guilds combining almost 1,500 parties, and over 90% of crawlers partied with somebody. For a non-stigmergic species, says the System, you do love your societal structures, and it makes you easy targets. Hunters are hiding in Zockau, and if that goes on, things may change. The seventh floor has been completely redesigned. The top 50 will be invited to a party at the Butcher's Masquerade, attendance mandatory, each with a plus one.

beats.headline: Under her own feet
beats.text: The dog's jaws close right through Donut. There were five Donuts, not four, and she had laid the middle illusion over herself. She had also downed an invisibility potion, and she had cast Hole under her own feet just as the dog lunged. The view changes to the outside, and a translucent outline of Donut drops straight down and lands deftly on the ground beside the burning tree. Carl cannot believe that worked.

beats.headline: She killed the wrong one
beats.text: The cat fought good. I say it's a draw and order two milks. The bear goes to get them and doesn't come back. Alexandro is mad. He says I should finish her. I tell the cat about Bini and Abraham and Siti, on the ice, and how I fell asleep and didn't tell Gus to sleep. Gus is the bad one. Then I tell Cici to kill the kitty, and the cat drops Cici's head through the floor. She killed the wrong one. Where's my milk? Yes. They all must die. No more friends.

beats.headline: Youth assistants shouldn't be here
beats.text: Loop-de-Loop, kid: a trap spell, not a module trap. She can send you somewhere or swap places with you, and she peppers every town she enters with them. Exploits that let one crawler trap and kill another usually don't get patched. Then Donut tells me what the show cut: Lucia named someone invisible, Alexandro, her youth assistant. Children under a certain age are taken out of the dungeon until the crawl is over, and youth assistants look after them. Kids shouldn't be in here. Youth assistants shouldn't be here. It's really strange.

beats.headline: Cici, and the Hole spell
beats.text: The recap shows the whole thing, and I am magnificent in it. Lucia swaps places with me so I land between her two rottweilers, and I backflip off the big one. She snares me in the treehouse pub. So I sing, and Entourage gives five Donuts, one laid over myself, and I drink invisibility and cast Hole under my own feet. Cici sticks her head down the hole. I close it. Her head drops into the mud. The only bridge she'll cross today is made of rainbows.

beats.headline: An outdoor spell
beats.text: On the screen, Carl watches the fight in the treehouse pub. Donut is rooted by a snare, one paw stuck to the floorboards for ninety seconds. She fires a full-powered magic missile into Lucia Mar, and as Lucia starts to recover, Donut casts a Fireball into her chest. Lucia slams into the back wall, and the far wall of the wooden pub bursts into flames. Donut has already opened a platinum Did-You-Really-Just-Cast-Fireball-in-a-Room-This-Small box. Fireball is an outdoor spell, Donut, says Mordecai.

beats.headline: Punched twice, unbothered
beats.text: Service note. Bomo posts Carl's note in the Zockau tavern saferoom and waits there, as instructed, for close to two hours. The mantis merchant punches him, is frozen for a minute, says "wait for me", and punches him again, for which he is frozen for an hour. The saferoom is full of hunters. Bomo reports that they are scared of Bomo. He comes back with the mantis standing in the hallway behind him.

beats.headline: Edict chooses to die fighting
beats.text: Edict is a mantis accountant, level fifty, buying for the Burrowers, and he has already handed the loot to someone else to deliver. Help me and his family is ruined; refuse Vrah and hers takes revenge; mate with her and he's a traitor. The only way to keep his honor, he says, is to die in battle. That's why he punched Bomo twice. Vrah limps in smoking, I give him a one-time pass, and he swings at my crotch. Super Naughty. He's gone. A metric ton of gold lands at my feet.

beats.headline: A corporation that sells upward
beats.text: Edict explains the arrangement. The Dark Hive is a private corporation, and it sells everything it loots to the Burrowers, the royal family and government of the mantis system, who have paid in advance and expect delivery on the ninth floor. Edict's own family is of Deep Mind and employed by that government. Every mantis coupling must be registered ahead of time, with a trial and counseling for the male, and a government family may not couple with a for-profit one without a bond and a license.

beats.headline: Frozen twice for punching Bomo
beats.text: For the record: Crawler Carl sent Bomo into Zockau with a note for the last mantis on the floor, the one who trades the looted gear, offering protection in exchange for that gear: no gear, no deal. The mantis comes. In the saferoom he attacks Bomo twice with his fists, and is frozen for a minute and then an hour. He is small and shivering, without the sword-arms the females carry, and looks like a child. Edict. Mantis. Level fifty. Merchant. The Dark Hive. He is not a hunter or a fighter, he says. He is just the accountant.

beats.headline: Already paid for
beats.text: He learns from Crawler Donut's joke that the elf Akland is dead, and deflates further. Vrah is almost here, and has told him he must mate with her. His loot is contracted to the Burrowers, the mantis government, paid in advance and due to them when this floor collapses; he goes straight to the ninth. Giving it to Crawler Carl would ruin his family and his hive. He is of Deep Mind. So he has already handed it to another entity for a small fee, and does not say who.

beats.headline: A split in the tunnel
beats.text: The disease Crawler Carl gave Vrah has put his hive's fate at a split in the tunnel. Hand over the gear, and his family is ruined and he must kill himself in shame. Refuse Vrah, and her family takes revenge on his. Mate with her, and it is a forbidden coupling between his hive and hers; they would be deemed traitors. He explains to Crawler Donut that the female eats the male's head, and a secondary brain in his abdomen keeps him going. The more he talks, the straighter he stands. He needs to die in battle.

beats.headline: Finding the stars
beats.text: He hates this place, he says, and everything about it. Finding the stars was the worst thing that ever happened to his people: a slow, horrific death, expansion to the point of oblivion. The primals finally understood, too late. Some of the kua-tin know it too. They call it the Great Consensus, but it is not; there is no agreement, and their young do not understand. Then he asks, quickly, to be let into Crawler Carl's space.

beats.headline: Super Naughty, an inch short
beats.text: Vrah limps into the hallway, smoke rising from her crotch. Crawler Carl gives the subject a one-time pass through his door. With a strangled battle cry, Edict lunges at Crawler Carl and punches, and freezes with his small fist an inch short. Super Naughty. He blinks twice and disappears, teleported naked to the closest mob nest. Despite his report that he gave all his loot away, a metric ton of gold coins drops at Crawler Carl's feet, burying him to the ankles. Crawler Carl suspects this was the best possible outcome for him, or if not him, his family.

beats.headline: Burning in the hallway
beats.text: Hunter Vrah reaches the Zockau saferoom hallway limping, smoke rising from her crotch with an odour of burned cheese, crying out for Edict. She arrives in time to watch him throw a punch at Carl and be teleported away, naked, to the nearest mob nest. She has shed every head from her back, not only the ones Princess Donut reanimated, perhaps to be lighter. The flames go out, she heals, and the fire starts again. A saferoom does not protect against this. The cat recommends ointment.

beats.headline: Ask the lawyer first
beats.text: Carl's legal question for his attorney is still unanswered, and Mordecai does not know either. Ask your lawyer, Mordecai says, and if he doesn't respond, wait until after the next recap episode. If they don't take it away from you, install it in the crafting studio and start working.

beats.headline: Prepotente Town #4
beats.text: Carl and Princess Donut take two more towns and arrive at a third to claim it. There is not much left of the third. She has already been through it, and there is a pattern to which places she visits that nobody has sat down and read yet.

beats.headline: Edict's words stay with me
beats.text: I've been thinking about Edict all day, and what bothers me is that I think he was wrong. I believed him when he said he didn't want to be here and hated how the universe works. I still think he was wrong. My dad's voice says knowing that stuff rots you from the inside out. And Lucia: you killed the wrong one. Someone invisible was with her. Nobody on that panel knew much about her, and it seems important. It doesn't change anything. She has to be put down.

beats.headline: Copy out the automaton book
beats.text: Carl's question for his attorney is a legal one, and he has not heard back; Mordecai, asked first, does not know. Ask your lawyer, Mordecai says, and if he doesn't respond, wait until after the next recap episode. If they don't take it away from you, install it into the crafting studio and start working. In the meantime, transcribe everything you can from that automaton book into your scratchpad.

beats.headline: What he said stays
beats.text: At the end of a long day, approaching an ursine village, Crawler Donut says she kind of feels bad for that guy, Edict: he did not want to be here, and they forced him to play the game. Crawler Carl is not sympathetic. He has been thinking about what the subject said all day and cannot get it out of his head. He believes Edict did not want to be there and hated how the universe works, and he still thinks he was wrong. That is what bothers him most.

beats.headline: Starting to feel obsolete
beats.text: Every day, kid, you do and come across something that's never been done or seen before. I'm starting to feel a little obsolete. You want to know if you can use that table? Ask your lawyer. If he doesn't respond, wait until after the next recap, and if they don't take it away from you, install it in the crafting studio and start working. In the meantime, transcribe everything you can from that automaton book into your scratchpad. And the stores in Nipton are terrible.

beats.headline: Out from under a log
beats.text: They found me stuck under a log half a mile south of town, because I am LOUD. I am still mad at Donut for leaving me to that Rottweiler. Being tortured by bugs was actually kind of fun. I wish I'd been there for the accountant; I'd have killed him. Now I'm scouting Prepotente Town Number Four for them, and there are corpses and pink feathers everywhere. I tried making gore angels. Too sticky. And Signet STILL hasn't given me her body.

beats.headline: The interview tunneled
beats.text: Okay, so. Carl, you need to get to a saferoom. You're getting filthy, and you have your event. I also need you to know that Odette's interview with you and Princess Donut and Beatrice tunneled last night, and between that and the Dark Hive business there is a lot of attention focused on you. I'll see what I can do about your attorney. There is something else we need to discuss, but I will do it in person.

beats.headline: The Popovs in person
beats.text: First time I've been in a studio room with another crawler who isn't Donut or Katia. Dmitri and Maxim, number five in the dungeon, one two-headed ogre, a Visionary and a Bogatyr in one body, kept in a room with a level-one training space and a single greasy chicken. It's practically a jail cell. Dmitri is disappointed I didn't bring the cat. He'd gotten an orange one, Kapitan Whiskers, the day before. He says I'm a good man, because I went out in the cold for a cat.

beats.headline: Names without menus
beats.text: Zev makes Carl put the badge on again before he is transported down to the production facility for his next appearance. He lands hard in the green room in front of a two-headed ogre trying to play cards against itself. His menus are gone, but thanks to the badge he can still see the names floating over their heads: Dmitri on the right side, Maxim on the left, the Popov brothers, number five in the dungeon. They wear the badge too, around both their necks.

beats.headline: Kapitan Whiskers, orange
beats.text: The green room. About seven feet tall, broad, grey and callused like an elephant. Dmitri, the Visionary, has the right side and a bare, round head. Maxim, the Bogatyr, has a beanie and the meteor hammer. Fraternal twins: not identical before, not identical now. Dmitri is disappointed the cat has not come, and Maxim apologises for him. Dmitri had just got a cat, orange, named Kapitan Whiskers, the day before it happened. Maxim complains they were promised food and given one chicken.

beats.headline: Promoted, and still in the dark
beats.text: Skindle, who looks after Dmitri and Maxim, introduces me as her boss. I did get a promotion. Carl, about your replacement sponsor: the first winner of the bidding could not pay, so there was a new bidding event, and the winner wants to award your first benefactor box during the signing. You will see who at the end. Who could not pay is still above my pay grade. About three hundred fans won a lottery place, plus thirty premiums, plus press.

beats.headline: A pen in the naga
beats.text: Last come the reporters, and Nihit, a naga from Elemental Collection Updates, snaps at my head and hisses that I'm cheating, that Odette is complicit, that he can hurt me just fine from the inner system. I ask if he thinks he's safe. He asks what I think I can do. I pick up the magical Sharpie and put it into his neck as hard as I can. It breaks into a dozen pieces, a stick of metal stays in, and he goes over screaming. The room blinks twice. The lights come on.

beats.headline: Gone apeshit, in transit
beats.text: Gossip at the autograph tables, logged because it is consistent. Circe Took has, in the phrasing of the attendees, gone completely apeshit about the whole business with her daughter, and is on her way to the Earth system to do something about it. Crawler Carl cannot see what: it is too late for her to join the hunters on this floor. A reporter begins, "With the news that Circe Took is possibly..." and is shoved aside by a naga before finishing.

beats.headline: Autographs, and a new sponsor
beats.text: Carl and the Popov brothers sign for a queue of fans, a good many of them dressed as him in heart-print boxers and no shoes. His replacement sponsor is announced live at the table: the Plenty.

beats.headline: For the thousandth time
beats.text: Autograph session. Dmitri signs everything and chats; Maxim looks bored. A blob child asks whether it was really an accident. Dmitri, for the thousandth time: their game guide, Hongrish, told him the nodling was a good choice that would give him an extra life. He did not say it would force his brother into the same body. When the child presses a theory about a television programme, Maxim threatens it with his foot. Asked about Bogdon Ro's death, Maxim says cheerfully that the man got what he deserved, and he is sorry others had to die too.

beats.headline: The vacated sponsorship goes to them
beats.text: Carl signs autographs with the Popov brothers, poses for photographs with a fan who has a head tentacle named Maggie and strong views on the eradication of cocker spaniels, and finds out on the same afternoon who has bought him. The Plenty.

beats.headline: Riding it out, with bets on
beats.text: Word at Carl's signing table: Hunter Vrah intends to ride the infection out, and CrawlCon attendees are actively betting on whether she will give in and cut it away, which would end her chance of being the next hive queen.
