beats.text: An unaffiliated hunter, a level-50 dreadnought merchant, opens his mouth to scream, and Carl kicks him in the nuts. He lands on the man's chest and breaks his neck by the twin horn stubs, out of sight of the guards. Into the inventory goes the body. It doesn't have much, but it does have one of those weird credit chits, like the one taken off the orc several days earlier. From what Carl gathers, they are the equivalent of intergalactic credit cards.

beats.headline: The changelings have to be inside
beats.text: Carl and Donut blackmail their way onto the hunters' level of the Desperado Club to reach the changelings, and the message they carry is a map. The spell that can move the changelings works only on a town, the elves have razed every town in the forest but their own castle, and so the changelings have to be inside it.

beats.headline: Still not drained
beats.text: Clarabelle, at the club door, says the level below the Hunting Grounds is still under water. Something keeps clogging the drains, and the sharks are not helping. The outworlders trapped on the Larracos level have the hotel and the main casino, so nobody is complaining much, but the weapons brokers who usually buy a pass up to trade with the hunters have not managed it once. They were trying to drain it before the floor ended. It does not look like they will.

beats.headline: The ledger, privately
beats.text: Clarabelle will not let us down to the Hunting Grounds level, and she is insulted when I mention a hundred gold. She has misunderstood. My interface keeps track of every gold piece I have ever spent. Five hundred gold, paid to Clarabelle for private secure escorts, the day I met Sledgie. A refund from Astrid of only four hundred. Carl has a kind heart, and he thought we should take the matter up with her privately. I look at the door. This is us, taking the matter up privately.

beats.headline: It only works on a town
beats.text: Carl hands Pearson a map with the evacuation plans on the back. They are using a spell called Zerzura, but the brambles are moving fast, and it cannot be cast for another two days. It is cast on a town, not a group of people, so the changelings need to be inside a town. The high elves have destroyed every town in the forest around them but one: the high elf castle. So that is where the changelings have to get. Pearson mentions that Juice Box told them to be careful of Carl.

beats.headline: A warning about liaisons
beats.text: I had Astrid bring Crawler Carl to me. I leave when this floor collapses and do not return until the ninth, so it is now. A liaison is chosen for two things: passion for the game, and fundamental disagreement with the goals of his own nation. Technically I should have lost this chair when the Valtay took control of Borant. I am not the only liaison who disagrees with his nation. Some of us meet that second requirement a little too much. I have said all I can about the matter.

beats.headline: The courts are frozen
beats.text: On to business. The courts have stopped nearly every crawl-related case, including ones the AI is usually indifferent to, until they have a better read on this AI's stability during the floor change. Crawler Carl's attorney now needs a court order to send him a message, and has not been permitted to try. We have decided to circumvent this, just this once, and I must remain in the room. I wave my hand, and Quasar is here, with a woman in a Goddamnit, Donut shirt.

beats.headline: He is trying to warn us
beats.text: Carl was out for forty-five minutes, and they let me order from the kitchen. Capers are really gross. Orren talks and talks about liaisons and the spirit of the game, and Carl asks what in the flying fuck he is talking about. It is obvious. He is trying to warn us about something, but he is struggling because he does not like us and he is scared of breaking the rules. They both stare at me. Orren says he likes us quite a bit.

beats.headline: Not much use yet
beats.text: The level-five table is not much use yet, despite a manual full of recipes. Carl has been terrified they would take the table or the recipes back, since he basically stole them from the production facility, but nobody has said a word. The trouble is parts. Then he finally finds the materials for something called Spider Stalkers.

beats.headline: Shunned, and the spider plan
beats.text: The Automaton table finally makes something: Spider Stalkers, once I buy a case of rare driveshafts on the way out of the club. After our first raid I learn one hunter I killed from afar worshipped Emberus. Boon cancelled, fifteen hours of Penitence, tithing doubled, and Shunned over my head, to everyone's delight. So tonight Donut will tap the spiders awake and take the credit for anything they kill. Two more are programmed to chase Samantha and explode five seconds after they catch her.

beats.headline: One, two, stab
beats.text: Donut is still on about it, days after. Once trust is broken it can never be replaced, she tells Carl: if someone says they are going to count to three, one expects them to actually count to three, not to stab willy-nilly into one's body without warning. She didn't get to prepare herself.

beats.headline: Gear that will not change hands
beats.text: Most of what the hunters carry is restricted to the hunter. Florin took out two Goriffs, blue aliens with antennae like twin elephant trunks, and has their pulse rifles and electric armour, but he cannot equip them. Donut's sunglasses carry the same restriction, as Louis learned when he tried them on. Mordecai says it is a common addition to benefactor box items, to keep players from murdering the recipients for their gear. A rare scroll called Cracker Jack can free an item, but nobody they know has one. They collect everything anyway.

beats.headline: Recipes, but no parts
beats.text: Carl's level-five Automaton Table is not much use yet, despite an instruction manual filled with recipes. He has been terrified they would take the table or the recipe book back, since he basically stole them from the production facility, but so far nobody has said anything. Just in case, he has copied every recipe into his scratchpad and then into the Cookbook. The problem is supplies: he has some of the parts for several recipes and every part for none, until he finds the materials for something called Spider Stalkers.

beats.headline: His worshippers in the hunters' ranks
beats.text: The mantis brought me to Zockau early, briefly, and so its guards may worship me, and that was her notion of keeping the man out. Some hunters who saw me that day now pray to me as well, for the same reason. The man killed one of mine from afar. I cancelled his boon, gave him fifteen hours of Penitence and doubled his tithe, and told him two more would earn a smite. He wore Shunned over his head, and the cat enjoyed it.

beats.headline: Gear I can't wear
beats.text: Two Goriffs, blue, trunks on their heads. Pulse rifles and electric armor. The armor didn't cover their faces. I have their gear now and I can't equip any of it. It's locked to the dead owners. Mordecai says that's common on sponsor items. There's a scroll called Cracker Jack that frees it, and nobody has one. We keep collecting. Carl's still talking. Quit jawing and get on with it.

beats.headline: No more suing the AI
beats.text: Zev confides, after Carl's visit with Quasar, that multiple immediately unsuccessful lawsuits followed once the brambles hit Zockau. The Syndicate Council itself, not the subcommittee but the actual council, ruled that nobody may file any more lawsuits naming the AI as a defendant, to slow the AI's deterioration. That ruling set off a whole new set of lawsuits challenging the council's authority, and the mess is working its way through the courts. Carl does not understand why they cannot just unplug the thing.

beats.headline: A grapefruit-sized hole
beats.text: The pulse rifles on this floor are a downright menace: portable guns firing an unending supply of full-strength magic missiles. Bautista almost had his head blown off by one the day before. One has also punched a grapefruit-sized hole clean through subject's midsection. The system does not treat the wound as an amputation, so it heals, and she is back to her normal, grumpy self.

beats.headline: The hunters are being sponsored
beats.text: The hunters' levels are not going up, and their gear keeps getting better: pulse rifles, electric armor, an anti-air gun in most of the bigger groups. I am fairly sure they are being allowed sponsors now. That is probably what the recap woman meant a few days ago. If they are stuck here, it makes sense. Their families are pouring money into the show, and most of it is locked to the hunter who receives it.

beats.headline: Ten in the open, five in the pub
beats.text: Ten hunters on the south side of town, preparing to leave. One anti-air gun, spelled against targeting. Mostly level 50; one 53, one 63 in magical plate, possibly human. One rifle. Five mushroom guards. Maybe five more in the pub at the centre, Cold Stone Creamery. No sign of Vrah. My race sees who is bound to a god, and what god if I am close. The rifle carries the mark. I am not close enough to name it.

beats.headline: Not like the Naga season
beats.text: The hunters are dying in numbers nobody has ever seen. And this isn't like the Naga season, where they bled money with every bad decision. It started that way. Now it's the opposite: everyone else is losing money, and all of it is flowing into Borant. Too bad for the kua-tin government that they couldn't keep their little flippers on the company. No offense, Zev, if you're listening. She is.

beats.headline: He did not count to three
beats.text: The costumes are ready. Mordecai helped with the bubbles for Kiwi's, but my clam does not like her outfit and miss seaweed's falls off every time they practise the jump. They let me dress them because they trust me. Once trust is broken it can never be replaced, Carl. If someone says they will count to three, one expects them to count to three. You're lucky the saferoom froze me. I almost bit your hand off. He says I have a saferoom strike now.

beats.headline: Locked to the princess
beats.text: Most of what the hunters leave behind is restricted to the dead hunter: Florin has two Goriffs' pulse rifles and electric body armour and cannot equip any of it. Donut's sunglasses turn out to carry the same restriction, which they learned when Louis tried to put them on. Mordecai says it is a common addition to benefactor gifts, to keep other players from murdering the recipient for the gear. A rare scroll called Cracker Jack could free an item, but nobody they know has one. In the meantime they collect all the gear they can.

beats.headline: Twenty out of the bag
beats.text: Carl finally finds the materials for something called Spider Stalkers, which are really just robot rot stickers, a pretty common mob. Their main driveshaft is rare and expensive, and he secures a case on his way out of the Desperado Club. On the raid, Donut is to do the honors. He pours twenty rat-sized automaton spiders from a bag; they roll out like spilled tennis balls, sprout legs and line up. Each exploding one is programmed with a target, Hunter Not Already Targeted, so any kill goes to Donut. Two more he sets on Samantha: explode five seconds after target acquired.

beats.headline: The council closes the courts
beats.text: Okay, so. After the brambles hit Zockau there were several lawsuits, and they failed immediately. Then the Syndicate Council itself, not the subcommittee, the actual council, ruled that nobody may file a suit naming the AI as a defendant. It is meant to slow the deterioration. That has started a whole new set of suits about whether the council can do that. Mordecai is right that the money is flowing to Borant. Our Valtay partners have shown no dismay so far. The council and the liaisons are very nervous. Now stop talking about this.

beats.headline: Much too close
beats.text: The hunters come running straight at the party, leading two of the explosive spiders right into their laps, and Carl scrambles into his interface to disable them. Before he can, Kiwi and Mongo fly over him and pounce on the pair, two tentacle-faced Saccathians with mechanical enhancements on their legs, who die screaming. The spider automatons stop dead, turn back around, and go looking for new targets.

beats.headline: Five points a kill, level 59
beats.text: Sixty-six trophies. I've marked three more hunters with the ring, all Constitution, and it gives five points a kill now. Level 59; I put every level-up point into Strength, where my ability doubles it. 254 base points. Donut's at 278 and dropping behind, and if I pass her she loses control of our party of two. Firas pointed that out in the planning session. Tonight's raid finally goes to plan. Then Donut asks what the antler X over my head means. Diwata has marked me for death.

beats.headline: A squirrel out of a hunter
beats.text: Crawler Elle McGibbons reports from outside a church. A green explosion, a bush with a giant flower pod, and inside the pod a hunter, who swallows the blood and bark of the dead tree guards and swells until he bursts. Out of the gore comes an antlered squirrel covered in hunter pieces: Diwata, sponsored by Circe Took, on a five-minute timer. It flies away like a rocket. Crawler Carl works out the destination. Her daughter. His word for the errand is a cure.

beats.headline: Marked for death, mid-raid
beats.text: A raid on a church is in progress when the notification lands on Crawler Carl: Diwata has entered the realm, and he is marked for death. That is the arithmetic of defiling a shrine. The god whose shrine it was is now on this floor, in person, with a grudge and a name to attach it to. Continue the raid, crawler. The mark does not expire because you are busy.

beats.headline: She has somewhere else to be
beats.text: She comes out of the church and runs, past the party, away, which is not what a marked crawler expects from a god with his name on a list. Samantha explains it. Diwata gives birth to new forest creatures, whole new kinds of them, and the rest of the pantheon finds this distasteful. Her sponsor is Circe Took of the Dark Hive, Hunter Vrah's mother. So Diwata is crossing this floor to reach Vrah, and the crawler she marked can wait his turn. I did not write this floor. I only run it.

beats.headline: Milk on the Treasure Map
beats.text: Crawler Milk's note in the sixth edition: when a country boss dies, it drops persistent loot called the Treasure Map. Don't pick it up. Over four hundred crawlers faced a boss in a low-ceilinged cave and fewer than fifty survived, hitting each other as often as it. Then they all picked up the map, which showed every piece of magical gear in the area, and started a second slaughter. Milk's first player-killer skull came from it. Blood on the claws, the note says, that will not wash away.

beats.headline: Right above the church
beats.text: I was right above it when the church blew. Green smoke, like the mushroom spores but thicker. Gave me a buff against fire and poison. Five or six dryads went up pinwheeling blood, it all swirled into a giant flower, and the bud opened with that eyebrowless hunter inside. The gore poured into his mouth and he swelled like a can of potted meat on a cookfire. Out came an antlered squirrel no bigger than me. Diwata, sponsored by Circe Took. It flew off like a rocket. Mordecai wants the pollen. He can wade in himself.

beats.headline: Exactly what we needed
beats.text: The hunters have been whittled down by more than half. The inexorable brambles combined with the blood bar seemed terrible at first, and turned out to be exactly what the crawlers needed. Most of the hunters had no idea what they were doing, were not organized or trained, and did not work well together, and between the thorns and the need to kill, they were hunted down one by one. Samantha, rolled at the hunters' anti-air guns as the workaround, was once blasted five kilometres away by one and landed in the brambles.

beats.headline: It has to be Vrah
beats.text: Samantha says Diwata gives birth to new creatures, and Carl and I work it out at the same moment. She did not attack him because she had five minutes to reach her daughter. And she probably does not want to be the one who kills Carl, either. It would make Vrah look weak. It has to be Vrah. So Vrah is about to be cured, and we should assume she is back in this. Then Tina breaks away and eats a sleeping mushroom guard.

beats.headline: Two in the trees
beats.text: Hunters run at Carl. JUMP. Kiwi jumps too. Two for two. FOOD. MOTHER says good boy!

beats.headline: Not the Stupid Dictator Carl
beats.text: I got five kills. Five! Good boy, Mongo! Good girl, Kiwi! Then Carl sees his mark and tells me to take both potions right now, and my cooldown has a minute and forty-five seconds left, and the god runs off anyway. Carl says when he tells me to do something I have to do it immediately. The last I looked, this was the Royal Court of Princess Donut. Not the Stupid Team of Stupid Dictator Carl and his Abused Slave Cat, Princess Donut.

beats.headline: The gun, and a pretty ring
beats.text: Come on, my pretties! I roll to the gun with two spiders chasing me, because the gun will not let them seek it and nothing can kill me. Last time I went in too early and got punted into the brambles. This time I am at the gun and I say so, and it explodes, and my hair is on fire. Again. Afterwards I bring Carl a hand with a pretty ring on it, for when I get my body back. Florin says I can have it.

beats.headline: Seekers into the rain
beats.text: You, and you, and you, Donut says, tapping each seeker spider on the head, and they scuttle off into the rain. Samantha rolls off toward the town exit, and on Carl's word Donut taps the last two, and they chase her: the anti-air gun has an anti-seeking enchantment, and the indestructible head is the workaround. Explosions rip through the night as the seekers find targets, and the gun goes up in a red geyser. When it is over, a few spiders walk in circles, unable to find a target. They will run out of power in a few minutes, and Carl will have to collect them and recharge them at his table.

beats.headline: Her mother comes to cure her
beats.text: Hunter Vrah's condition, courtesy of Crawler Carl: gonorrhea, which for her kind, Crawler Princess Donut recalls, has only one cure. Her mother, Circe Took of the Dark Hive, has sponsored the god Diwata, who arrives on a five-minute timer, marks Carl, and rockets away without touching him. Carl and Katia Grim agree where she is going: to her daughter. Crawler Princess Donut asks whether Vrah will rip her own mother's head off. Carl does not know. The party assumes Vrah is back in play.

beats.headline: Five boxes, all for the cat
beats.text: Five items on the table, all Apothecary sponsor boxes, each sent to a different crawler with a note saying it belongs to Princess Donut: a wand recharge scroll, a tiara, sheet music, an Enchanted Hammer of Fast Forward that Borant tried and failed to block with an appeal, and an enchanted metal stick, named for someone Mordecai cannot place, given to Dmitri Popov. The hammer does nothing magical; the stick is no wand, but used correctly it can do something truly magical. Each carries a small seven worked into it. The one Apothecary box not meant for Donut went to Katia: a beanie that sank into her.

beats.headline: Taking apart a spider
beats.text: Bonnie sits on the guildhall counter with a disarmed spider automaton in pieces around her, humming, prying its guts out. Randy, the smaller bear cub, tells her she is going to hell, and that all heathens burn in the fires of judgement. She looks up at him and says nothing. Skarn tells him not to be mean. The changeling children and the cubs have been bickering the whole time, and the cartoon on the television is why they are all still in the room.

beats.headline: A lie to Signet
beats.text: I tell Signet her assault will fail if it lands as the party starts: the people running this place won't let her climax touch the main story. Zev tells me to drop it, twice. So I offer a better plan: get into the castle, wait for my signal, and fight Imogen alongside all of us at the end of the party. It's a lie. We mean to use her as a distraction and keep her in reserve so I don't get dragged into her fight. Her odds are still better this way. She asks to hear it.

beats.headline: A seven on the stick
beats.text: Mordecai has never seen anything like it. Why send a hammer and a metal rod to a cat? Then I let the ugly thought surface. They send it all to Donut because she's the one most likely to survive this. It's why Quasar wanted her on the board. There's a stairwell right outside and twenty of the top fifty in this room. We could just go. Then I see Bonnie on the counter, prying apart a spider. If we don't do this, it's all for nothing. My finger finds a seven etched in the rod. Another on the hammer.

beats.headline: No hidden seven
beats.text: Of the five Apothecary items on the table, all meant for Donut, Carl understands three: a recharge wand scroll, a sheet of music and a new tiara. It is the stick and the hammer that puzzle him, and each carries a hidden seven. He checks the others. The scroll has no symbol that he can find, and neither does the tiara or the sheet music. That makes sense, he thinks. Their purpose is clear.

beats.headline: Carl cannot stop thinking of her
beats.text: Crawler Carl turns over the items just given to Donut and suspects the reason: they expect everyone else to be dead. He finds a seven worn into the end of a metal rod, then another in a hammer's handle. Seven, as in the seventh floor? And he cannot stop thinking of the subject's final, heartbreaking entry in the Cookbook: My sponsor was deliberately steering me not toward life, but a death that would be watched and remembered. He thinks of Orren the liaison, and of the warning Orren tried to give.

beats.headline: Never this aggressive
beats.text: Signet, alone on a log with a butterfly on her hand, as the sun comes up over a town the brambles are due to overtake in hours. Everything is dying, she says, but there is still beauty. She has never seen a Gehenna bramble this aggressive. It truly is the end of days. The all-tree has survived countless infestations like this one; the brambles fade with time. They are due at the elven border in a few hours, and the elves are going to spend the day beating them back. Even their magic is not enough to stop it.

beats.headline: Planted by an all-tree
beats.text: Status update on Redstone Grimaldi, filed by Tsarina Signet from a log outside the town. When he came to this world, they planted him next to an all-tree node. The roots intertwined, and he became one with the tree. The tree's roots go deep; it has survived countless infestations like this, she says, and will outlast this one. Crawler Carl did not ask whether that means the ringmaster is alive. He decided not to pursue it.

beats.headline: Borant appealed, and lost
beats.text: Five hours before the Butcher's Masquerade, five Apothecary sponsorship boxes sit on one table, given to five different crawlers, all with notes saying they belong to Donut. Imani's held a ball peen hammer that fits in Carl's hand, and she was told Borant had filed a dangerous appeal to keep it from arriving, an appeal immediately denied. The box was only silver. Why give it to Donut, Carl asks, when she cannot even use it: is she supposed to hold it in her mouth? Mordecai has seen it before. Some items are enchanted with no properties, which lets them be used against things like ghosts. After finding a seven on the stick, Carl looks at the hammer again, and along its wooden handle is another.

beats.headline: I Need My Personal Space
beats.text: The only Apothecary box this floor not meant for Donut came to me. A small knit beanie: three per cent to all my stats, and a spell called I Need My Personal Space, which knocks everybody around me back with a powerful blow, including my own party. Good, and dangerous. I put it on, and it sinks into my mass. Carl pings me about the talk we still have not had. We should wait and see whether we can take the castle first.

beats.headline: The one box not for Donut
beats.text: Mordecai has never seen anything like it. Five items sit on the table, all from Apothecary sponsorship boxes, all given to different crawlers, all with notes saying they should go to Donut, and that is not counting Carl's Pawna's Cries or Prepotente's I Take It All Back, both meant for her too. Of everyone the Apothecary sponsors, only Katia got a box not meant for Donut: a small knit beanie, three percent to all her stats down the line, and a spell called I Need My Personal Space. It violently knocks everybody back, party members included. She puts it on, and it sinks into her mass and disappears.

beats.headline: If it goes sour
beats.text: Five sponsor items from the same outfit, each sent to a different crawler, every one of them with a note to give it to the cat. I've never seen anything like this. Enchanted and nothing more, some of them; you can enchant an item with no properties so it works on ghosts. The kid says he doesn't like all these loose ends, that something is going to go wrong. It always does. If it goes sour, you have the escape plan. Get to the Twister and fly away.

beats.headline: One more for Donut
beats.text: Mordecai stands over a table of five items from Apothecary sponsorship boxes, each given to a different crawler with a note saying it should go to Donut, and he has never seen anything like it. Carl's Pawna's Cries, from the Open Intellect Pacifist Network, was meant for her too, and so was the I Take It All Back potion given to Prepotente. Of everyone the Apothecary sponsors, only Katia got a box not meant for Donut.

beats.headline: Asleep through the bickering
beats.text: Her cubs spend the evening feuding with the changeling children. Randy tells Bonnie the gnome she is going to hell and that all heathens burn in the fires of judgement; When Skarn tells him not to be mean, Todd stands behind his brother. The subject, the mother of the two bears, is passed out on the couch, snoring.

beats.headline: On a log, so very tired
beats.text: Everything is dying, and there is still beauty. I have never seen a Gehenna bramble this aggressive. Carl sits beside me and I put my head on his shoulder, and I tell him I am so very tired. Grimaldi we planted by an all-tree node, and the roots intertwined. My soldiers are hidden. When night falls and his party begins, we strike Imogen. Carl says it is a trap, that they will not let us win. Who is they? I need someone inside the castle. Then he says he has a better idea. Tell me your idea.

beats.headline: Grand Theft Auto
beats.text: Carl rigged up a television. Grand Theft Auto. Bomo and me play it all the time. A changeling kid sits on my lap. I show him how to steal a car. Carl tells Mordecai we are why the kids stay in the room.

beats.headline: Guts out on the counter
beats.text: Little Bonnie the gnome sits on the counter, humming to herself as she pries the guts out of a disarmed spider automaton. Carl's eyes catch her as he weighs taking the stairs and avoiding what comes next. We need her and the rest of them, he thinks, if we want to survive the ninth floor.

beats.headline: Not a wand
beats.text: Dmitri Popov was ridiculously excited to finally meet Donut and hand his gift over, and unlike Imani he got no notice of an appeal. It is a metal rod about a quarter of an inch thick and ten inches long, apparently aluminium, though its description does not say, and from that description it seems connected to the hammer. Who's Cascadia? Carl asks. Mordecai shrugs: this kind of thing is usually named after past crawlers, bosses or places, and of the few Cascadias he can think of, only one is connected to the crawl. Then Carl's finger catches a slight imperfection at the end of the rod. It feels like a symbol. He thinks it is the number seven.

beats.headline: Five boxes meant for Donut
beats.text: Five hours before the Butcher's Masquerade, Carl and Mordecai stand over a table of five items, all from the Apothecary in sponsorship boxes given to different crawlers, all with notes saying they should be given to Donut. Mordecai has never seen anything like it. One is a recharge wand scroll. That one Carl understands, he says, and the tiara and the sheet music too. What he cannot work out is the stick, or the ball peen hammer he picks up next.

beats.headline: Drop this, Carl
beats.text: Carl. I highly suggest you drop this. I say it once, while he is telling Signet that the people controlling her world will not let her win, and he does not drop it. I say it again when he starts offering her a new plan: they are not going to let it happen this way, and we have discussed this.

beats.headline: Donut's guitarist
beats.text: I'm not top fifty. Firas talked me into this: Donut's plus-one, because I play guitar. It was this or Gideon's assault team. The jacket itches. The elf says security checks, twice, and those are just the ones he's telling us about. This isn't going to work. I've been taking the dinosaur repellant every day. Mongo still tackles me. Shield's ready. Then the queen fades in next to me, and I cast it.

beats.headline: The queen has a face I know
beats.text: Theobold lists the rules: no magic, no weapons, no inventory, and safeguards on the ballroom he won't describe, put in place by a goddess. I ask about Quan, the dog girl and Eva, and fighting will not be tolerated. I plant a little doubt about Ferdinand. Then the guards go into the last cart, where Pearson is wearing Signet's face, and the queen fades in beside Britney. Are you really smuggling someone who looks like my half-sister into the castle? We drew her out. And she's Ifechi. Florin's dead girlfriend.

beats.headline: On the list, between the castle and the hunters
beats.text: The plan goes into the cookbook in a bathroom, and saving the changelings is written down beside taking the castle and killing every hunter. They have gone from a species trait to a constituency, with a line in an operation nobody expects to survive.

beats.headline: The plan, written down
beats.text: Carl adds a note to the Cookbook, 25th edition. He is starting something he does not think will succeed, and as Drakea asked of future authors, he means to document every step. The crew has a way of talking that prying eyes cannot see, and he points readers to his earlier post on the coffee shop author's kit to see how it works. Then he pastes in page one of their notes. The party is a trap. Queen Imogen is a country boss. Goal one is to survive.

beats.headline: Good with the dinosaurs
beats.text: The caravan is escorting the party to the castle, and new guards in black jackets keep coming. Carl tells Donut to keep Tina under control: they have waited long enough, so put the new tiara on. She already has, Donut replies, and it has helped a lot with the dinosaurs, but the guards are still agitated, probably because of the lady in the last cart.

beats.headline: He writes his own plan into it
beats.text: Alongside a copy of the notes the team has been passing through the Coffee Shop Author's Kit, a way of talking that prying eyes cannot see. Goal one: survive the Butcher's Masquerade, which he calls a trap. Everything else is secondary.

beats.headline: Everly takes it all back
beats.text: Three entries from Crawler Everly. First: a sponsor box meant for one of her mercenaries, a spellbook he used within five hours to kill the boss holding the lockbox key. She does not trust sponsors, she writes, but they want her alive. Second, on floor eight, a tool for shortcuts through the maze, and a spark of hope. Third: I take it back. I take it all back. The sponsor was steering her toward a death that would be watched and remembered. Drakea notes it is her last entry, and asks the next author for detail.

beats.headline: The main show does not share
beats.text: Carl lays it out for the other crawlers before the high elves' party. Queen Imogen is a country boss, and they are probably going to have to fight her at the end of the party. His elite quest wants to fight the same boss before or during it, which means it is doomed: the main showrunners are not going to let a secondary production hose their climax. He likes Signet. He would like to avoid going down with her. He has already told her to her face: attack when the party starts and she is dead.

beats.headline: Hasten Poison, and a hope
beats.text: Two entries, fifth edition. First: her sponsor sent a box meant for someone else in her party, and not a crawler but a mercenary. A spellbook of Hasten Poison. She was upset. Not five hours afterwards, he used it to kill the boss holding the lockbox key and saved them all. She does not trust her sponsors, but she trusts they want her alive, so their advertisements stay on display. Second: on floor eight, a great box, a tool for shortcuts through the maze. A spark in her chitin. A longing for warmth and stars.

beats.headline: I take it all back
beats.text: Her last entry, fifth edition. I take it back. I take it all back. Her sponsor was deliberately steering her not toward life, but a death that would be watched and remembered and heartrending and painful. She was a fool. She curses Dictum Waystation Controls, Limited, whatever that means, and wishes pain on its children. Beneath it, Crawler Drakea, twenty-second edition: this is Everly's last entry. She did not say how she was set up, which is unfortunate. Future authors, be as detailed as you can.

beats.headline: The sir is part of his name
beats.text: Background from the caravan to the castle. Queen Imogen's familiar is Sir Ferdinand, rarely off her shoulder when not hunting away from the castle. The footman Theobold is firm that the title is not a title: a familiar, a pet, a lowly creature, the sir simply part of the name. Crawler Carl mentions that Ferdinand implied, out in the woods, that he was second in charge of the kingdom. You must be mistaken, says Theobold. Carl advises him to watch the cat.

beats.headline: Lucia Mar is mine
beats.text: Carl's plan goes round on the paper in the bathroom and everyone signs it. Goal five is kill Lucia Mar, because she is too dangerous and a wildcard. I sign under it. I am claiming Lucia Mar for myself. If someone attempts to stop me, we will have a problem. That is the whole of what I write.

beats.headline: My half-sister, in a cart
beats.text: My guards go into the last wagon and find a robed woman wearing my half-sister's face. They do not touch her. I come instead. I fade into the man's wagon beside a girl who squeaks and throws up a shield, and I ask him whether he is really attempting to smuggle someone who looks like my half-sister into my castle. He says your majesty and struggles to swallow.

beats.headline: Nobody asked me not to
beats.text: Everybody's signing Carl's plan in the bathroom thing. Katia, Imani, Elle says Jesus Christ, Carl, you're going to get us all killed. Donut hates the paper. Florin wants Lucia Mar. I write that nobody has tried to convince me not to go down the stairs, and I think we should. Firas writes same.

beats.headline: The tiara helps
beats.text: Tina keeps wandering off from the caravan, so I am outside keeping her in line. No, Tina! If you eat the elf he will not let you into the castle! We just gave you a bath! Kiwi, you must keep your child under better control. Carl tells me to put on my new tiara. I already did, and it helps a lot with the dinosaurs, but the guards are agitated. New ones in black jackets. They go into the last cart.

beats.headline: A pet like a lumpy meatball
beats.text: Crawler Tserendolgor, ranked 38 and now called Ren by everyone who cannot pronounce the rest, rides to the castle in the fifth wagon with her plus-one. Following on foot: her pet show entry, a level-20 blob she received on this floor for attending CrawlCon. It is as tall as Carl, shaped like a lumpy meatball, has one tooth and a mouth that could swallow a man, giggles as it walks, and tanks enormous damage. People love it.

beats.headline: The boon behind the peace seal
beats.text: Evening entertainment. Your host holds her party under a celestial peace seal: no violence, and anything that breaks the peace goes into the Nothing. If she reaches the end of the night with the seal intact, Apito hands her a boon. Elves call Apito the Oak Mother and the mother of all the gods, and a boon from the mother of all the gods is worth a room full of armed crawlers and a Tsarina you did not want. Queen Imogen has that arithmetic in front of her all evening. Watch her doing it.

beats.headline: The queen lowers her hand
beats.text: I'm in the carriage with Carl when the queen appears. A notification comes in: an achievement for total views, a fan box. Carl and I look at each other. The queen turns to me and lifts her hand as if to cast. Then she stops. When she's gone I tell Carl she reminds me of my mother.

beats.headline: The queen visits the carriage
beats.text: Queen Imogen turns up in our carriage and tells me the rules I didn't have. The masquerade is a spell, one of Apito's sacraments, and the whole party sits under a celestial peace seal. Whoever breaks it gets fed into the Nothing. If nobody does, she gets a boon. She knows I'm working with her half-sister, she has me on her dance card, and then she comes apart like dandelion seeds. The party hasn't started and the plan is already dead.

beats.headline: She loved reading to children
beats.text: Entered into the record in passing, while I described somebody else. Sometimes a villain has a good quality buried somewhere. Remember Denise the goose, the one shoved headfirst into a garbage disposal? She loved reading to children. That makes two bosses Crawler Carl has now killed who loved reading to kids. I raised it to point out that the creature I was describing at the time has no qualities like that at all.

beats.headline: Empress, judging the pet contest
beats.text: The ball, and I am judging the talent show and the pet contest both. Chaco is running the prize counter. I find the crawler in the crowd and tell him the truth of it: he and his attorney very nearly ruined my buy-in bid, and here I am regardless, judging, which makes me production.

beats.headline: Ugly, and temporary
beats.text: At the castle, Donut complains that her charm upgrade is not working on the high elves. It is working fine, Carl tells her: these elves think the party is beneath them, and someone has left them with a negative opinion, so the fact they are talking at all is a sign. He is only bummed it is not permanent. This tiara is ugly anyway, Donut says. But don't tell the Apothecary lady she said so.

beats.headline: He will not go down the stairs
beats.text: The queen has Ifechi's face. Katia says it's her twin sister, and she warns me. Carl reminds me of the rule we all agreed to: if Imogen took the form of someone's loved one, that person goes down the stairs. I tell him to go fuck himself. I don't see his cat going down the stairs. I tell him to back off. I'm fine. I've been pacing for an hour, waiting for this party.

beats.headline: A counter full of potions
beats.text: In the boudoir off the ballroom, a glorified locker room where nobody actually changes, Carl covers the bathroom counter with dinosaur repellent and half-splat potions, with a note for everyone who finds them: store the half-splat in the inventory in a ready position, and drink the dinosaur one now if they have not already. They may have to flee fast, and there will be loose, prey-driven dinosaurs everywhere. Carl wants them attacking the hunters, not the crawlers.

beats.headline: The Sugar Cube
beats.text: Up close the castle is not stone. It is white wood, maybe bleached oak, carved all over with acorns the size of a fingernail as if the whole building were turned from one piece, and it is hot to the touch. Elle calls it the Sugar Cube and the name sticks. There used to be a moat; the queen had it drained because it smelled funny. A pencil-thin tower stands at each corner, and trolls fight the elves in the caves below.

beats.headline: The queen has her sister's face
beats.text: Queen Imogen, host of the ball, is Ifechi's twin. Born together in Nigeria. One of them walked into the dungeon with a medical bag over her shoulder; the other one was taken somewhere else entirely and comes back wearing a crown and a boss's level. Carl is at the party working out the resemblance in real time, under a celestial peace seal that feeds whoever breaks it to the Nothing. Enjoy the canapés.

beats.headline: I want that boon
beats.text: The man knows nothing of why it is called the Butcher's Masquerade, so I tell him: Apito's first party, Yarilo's breach, the slaughter after. Only the most divine may cast the spell, and only once in their lives. The goddess writes the guest list, and if the evening ends without violence, the boon is mine. I want it. I may not harm my guests before the party. I do not need to. Whoever breaks the peace, the ground opens under them.

beats.headline: On the bathroom counter
beats.text: Past the security checks, the crawlers are ushered into the boudoir, a glorified locker room with cubicles and bathrooms on the way into the ballroom. Carl covers a bathroom counter with dinosaur repellent potions and half-splat potions, with a note: store the half-splat ready in your inventory and, if you have not already, drink the dinosaur one now. They may have to flee quickly, he warns, with loose, prey-driven dinosaurs everywhere. They want those attacking the hunters, not them.

beats.headline: The dinosaurs get the other room
beats.text: The castle elves say my professional show animals must go in cages. Outrageous. The stablemancer, Kibben, says the belly acher would swallow one of my mongoliensis whole, which is a reason to disqualify that walking meatball, not to cage my Mongo. I ask whether my dinosaurs can go to the other attendant ballroom, and Carl tells him the best way to shut me up is to let me have my way. Rude. It works. I insist on watching the transfer.

beats.headline: Dreaming on the ballroom ceiling
beats.text: The ballroom's domed ceiling is a moving mosaic: a black-and-gold cave glittering with crystals, like the inside of a geode, and curled in it a black centipede that twists like a hypnotist's spiral. The note says this is Scolopendra, dreaming, and that when she finally awakens she will destroy everything and free us all. From the middle of the mosaic a living white tree hangs upside down, and the centipede never stops twisting around it, as if to strangle it.

beats.headline: Returned to the Halls
beats.text: The Ascendency has an address, and gods go home to it. Earlier on this floor, Crawler Carl's god, Emberus, made an unseen appearance in the realm, and a minute on, a notice read that Emberus had returned to the Halls of the Ascendency. Now, on the cart bound for the masquerade, the queen tells the story behind its name: the first one was held in the Halls, put on by Taranis and his wife, Apito, for their children and extended family, who are constantly vying for control, even to this day. The party was meant as a night without violence.

beats.headline: Readable from the stage
beats.text: Carl's planning notes for the castle set out how the stage works. When Donut stands on the stage in ballroom A, she can physically handle the items moved to the stage of the attendant ballroom a few stories below: a wand there can be picked up and cast while it stays three floors down. She will be able to read the wand-recharge scroll and her sheet music if she needs them. The one thing she cannot do is drink something that is not with her, so the charm potion has to be smuggled in.

beats.headline: Why he is in the Nothing
beats.text: Since tonight's party runs under a peace seal, some history about the last god who broke one. At the first masquerade in the Halls, hosted by the mother of all the gods, Yarilo got drunk and forced himself on another deity's familiar. That broke the seal. Apito sent him into the Nothing for it, and he has been in the Nothing ever since. The seal on tonight's party is hers as well. Enjoy the canapes.

beats.headline: Do not bring Signet to the party
beats.text: Carl, I need to be very clear about this, so I am going to be. Do not attempt to smuggle Signet into the party. If you try, the production company is contractually forced to send her directions to do something premature, and it will get her killed and very likely you with her. If she is in that room, the courts have to decide who owns what happens next. It is a hard rule: nobody touches the main event. He tells me he has no such plans.

beats.headline: The butterfly on the warning light
beats.text: My part is the light. I sidle up to the guard with the giant spear, say something, giggle. I drop something, and when he looks down I pull a tag on my jacket. One stuffed slate butterfly comes alive, flies straight to the warning light and wraps it in its wings until the glow fades. It turns back into a toy, falls, hits the tip of his spear and lands in my hand. He never looks up in time. Carl says good job. I'm not doing that again.

beats.headline: The Gideon distraction
beats.text: Crawler Carl's plan for the party runs through him. From the planning notes: go with the Gideon distraction to empty the castle of as many guards as possible, then make the move. Britney, given the choice between assisting Crawler Donut on stage or joining the subject's assault team, took the stage. While the Sledge and the changelings head for the castle's secret entrance, Gideon and his team set up in the woods outside, to observe and to assault the front of the castle if needed.

beats.headline: She goes for Eva
beats.text: Eva is leaning on a table with over fifty player killer skulls above her. She stole all the potions in the dressing room and let me know it. Florin and Daniel are holding me back. I ask her why she's like this; these are her people too. The moment the protection is off, I'll rip her face off. She tells me, bored, that this is why Fannar couldn't stand me. What kind of mother could I have been. Carl tells me to be calm. I'm fine.

beats.headline: Against the wall
beats.text: I stand against the wall and chew my fingernail. The crocodile comes across the room at me, and the man puts a hand on his chest and stops him. Florin just stares at me for a long time. Then something in his face goes soft, and he tells the man something is off with me. I run along the wall to the corner by the stage. I sit down on the floor and hold on to myself.

beats.headline: He asks to join Carl's party
beats.text: I inform Carl that I must join his party. He says no, naturally. I am level seventy, I would lead any party I joined, and he suggests I found my own and join the guild. It would only be for the remainder of this floor, so we travel together to the start of the next. I have been collecting the clues, and Katia has told me about the cat's magical hammer and stick. Then a voice booms from the stage and I scream. He says we are bookmarking this.

beats.headline: A stage version of a cocker spaniel
beats.text: The theater is gorgeous at first glance and built by someone who knows nothing about such things. There is no thrust. There are no wings at all. The grid is maybe five feet above the arch, they ignored my request for catwalk access, and the AV elf could not work the boombox. Carl keeps asking about the catwalk. It is catwalk, singular, and it is forward enough; Edgar's map was accurate. It is a stage version of a cocker spaniel. And this is only for Mongo's presentation.

beats.headline: Apito's own invitation
beats.text: I was sitting in a damp, dark dungeon beneath my sister's castle, minding my own thoughts, when Apito herself appeared before me and told me I was invited to a party. And suddenly I was here, in the ballroom, among Carl's crawlers. The guard at the door stared at me with his mouth open, then turned and fled the room, shouting. I walked up to Carl and took his hands in mine. Would he like to hear something funny? I told him.

beats.headline: Prepotente has been collecting clues
beats.text: At the masquerade Carl asks Prepotente when he last slept, and the goat insists on joining his party. Carl says no: talk to Katia, or start a party of his own and join the guild. It would only be for the rest of this floor, Prepotente says, so that they travel together to the start of the next. He has been collecting the clues, and Katia has told him about Donut's magical hammer and stick. Then a voice booms from the stage, Prepotente screams right in Carl's ear, and Carl bookmarks the whole thing until they are through the party.

beats.headline: The warning light
beats.text: Britney's whole jacket is made of the stuffed butterflies; she wanted them on her boots, but Carl liked having a ton at the ready. Mordecai says their ability is not considered magic, which is why they beat Carl's idea of smuggling in his slingshot. While Vrah threatens Carl, Britney pretends to drop something, the guard looks down, and she pulls a tag. A hand-sized butterfly flies straight up to the warning light, wraps it in its wings and drains it dark. Then it is a stuffed animal again, bounces off the tip of the elf's spear and lands in her hand.

beats.headline: A present for Carl
beats.text: Vrah reaches the ballroom at a charge and stops an inch from Carl's face, mandibles working. She has a present for him, she says, and it is coming soon; he is not the only one who can bend the rules, and he will learn what it means to make an enemy of the Dark Hive. Carl asks whether they ban their enemies from the bumper boats. She promises a rematch, and swears that before the night is done she will wear his head on her back, and all his friends'.

beats.headline: She sends the test herself
beats.text: Correction to the file. Tsarina Signet did not crash that party. Apito invited her, because putting a Tsarina in a room is the fastest way to learn whether a host can keep a room calm. That is the whole shape of the test. And the footnote, which the Tsarina delivers herself, in person, with obvious enjoyment: nobody has ever taken that boon home. Not one host. The Oak Mother sets an examination that has never been passed, and keeps setting it.

beats.headline: People are depending on us
beats.text: Signet is in the ballroom with us now, which means she can't help us from outside it. Carl says the goddess picks the guest list, so of course she brought in one of the queen's biggest enemies. I tell him I don't like it. It's like they've been one step ahead of us the whole time. He thinks it's better this way: she'll be the first target, and it buys us a few extra seconds if someone breaks the seal. Everything is going off the rails, and people are depending on us. He says he knows.

beats.headline: No boon has ever been granted
beats.text: My sister is not here yet. I would not have believed this was a true Butcher's Masquerade had Apito not come to me herself, and I prefer it this way. I am tired of running. Her guards gather at the entrance, look at me and slink back to the hallway; they cannot touch me without breaking the seal. Carl asks what boon she hopes for. Some sort of immortality, the story goes. It has never once been granted. Then I notice three judges whose auras are strange.

beats.headline: Why a hunter hunts
beats.text: A hunter at the prize counter, Zabit, an Atoll with no mouth who talks through his hands, sent the night weasels at us when we first got to this floor. Twenty-five scalps. I ask him why he does it. For his people, he says. The money pays the upkeep on their habitat; they aren't citizens, so oxygen and land aren't a right, and this season's failure will make it hard for them to last until the next. Some hunters revel in it. He would object too, if it were the other way round.

beats.headline: Sixty-six hands at the counter
beats.text: The prizes turn on a carousel of holograms and the good ones cost too much. The memorial crystal is a hundred hands. The seventh-floor pole position is sold out; Prepotente walked up and pointed at it. I take the shrink wand, the eighth-floor book of lore with its full title still hidden, a sheet of Skedaddle for Donut, a case of twenty-four Feather Fall potions and a case of healing potions. All of it arrives in prize boxes, and there are no saferooms in the castle.

beats.headline: They make you turn on your party
beats.text: He asks me again why Mordecai hates me, and I am still not allowed to say. Tell him I'm sorry. I regret it every day. If we hadn't done it, we'd all be dead, including him and his brother. And a little something from your host: survive long enough in this place and they make you turn on your own party. It happens every time. Then I take a deep breath and wipe my face, and it's prize time! Carl, folks! Sixty-six hunter hands! Everything arrives as a prize box!

beats.headline: Thirty hands, one each
beats.text: At thirty hands, Chaco's prize case has only two items, both Future Floor Boons, with a sign under them: limited to one each. One is a little checkered flag, Seventh Floor Pole Position, already sold out. Prepotente bought it, Chaco says; he was the first customer. The other is an Eighth Floor Book of Lore, its starting location random and its full title to be revealed upon purchase. Carl takes it, along with the shrink wand, the Skedaddle sheet music, a case of twenty-four Feather Fall potions and a case of healing potions.

beats.headline: Twenty-four for the castle
beats.text: Katia has done a full circuit of the group and worked out that they are seven fall-protection potions short, thanks to Eva's thievery. Nobody is certain the potions will even be necessary. At the prize counter Carl wanted a skill upgrade for himself, but he is one hand short if he also refills the potion supply. So he takes a case of twenty-four Feather Fall potions, with the shrink wand, the lore book, the Skedaddle sheet music and a case of healing potions.

beats.headline: Sixty-six hands to spend
beats.text: Chaco the Bard stands behind the prize counter in the ballroom. You currently have 66 hunter hands, he tells Carl. Wow. Every purchase arrives as a prize box, and upgrades are installed at once. The items turn on a vertical carousel as miniature holograms. A single hand buys a 25-pack of good healing or mana potions; two buy one upgrade from a row, plus ten percent to a lowest stat, plus five percent to a highest, or plus two to a random combat skill or spell; three and five buy potions and scrolls by the dozen; thirty buy a future floor boon; fifty, full sets of armor. One prize costs a hundred hands.

beats.headline: A scroll with her name on it
beats.text: For the record: this name first appears on a prize list. Among the scroll choices for the three- and five-hand prizes at this evening's game is one called the Milk of Lamashtu. Crawler Carl reads it out to Mordecai alongside a scroll of mapping and one called Paw Patrol, and admits he does not know what any of these do. Mordecai calls the potions a waste and recommends the boost to Crawler Donut's lowest base stat and a random spell book instead. The name is logged.

beats.headline: The queen's prize, at a hundred hands
beats.text: At the end of Chaco's prize case sits a colourless, grape-sized gem that glitters even as a hologram. It is not a soul crystal. It costs a hundred hunter hands, the most expensive thing on the counter. Chaco does not know which dead god made it: the high elves found it on a mining expedition, and the queen normally wears it around her neck. The spell requires the host to offer her most valuable possession as a prize. If nobody buys it, she gets it back.

beats.headline: Forget everything else. Get that.
beats.text: If that fuck tit Chaco is in the room with you, kid, a dynamite stick would be a personal favour. Now read me the counter. The potions are a waste; Donut takes ten percent to her lowest base stat and the random spell book. What's a memorial crystal? Forget everything else. Get that. Soul crystals come out of Scolopendra's lair. Memorial crystals come from fallen gods and demigods, full of god-tier spells and knowledge, and you charge one by wearing it and killing things. A hundred hands. He has sixty-six.

beats.headline: Pole position, and a stage on fire
beats.text: I was the prize counter's first customer. Thirty-three hands. I walked up, pointed at the seventh floor's pole position, the skill upgrade and a case of mana potions, and took them. I did not ask what the flag does. Then the pet show. I take Bianca onto the stage and say nothing, because there is nothing to say. I scream once. She hisses. We leave, and the stage smoulders behind us and catches fire, and elves appear from nowhere to stamp out the flames.

beats.headline: Bought with hunter hands
beats.text: Chaco the Bard runs the prize counter, and Carl has sixty-six hunter hands to spend. Among the twenty-hand items are spellbooks, wands and oddities: a drop shield, and a shrink wand like the one Zhang used to have, ten charges. Mordecai calls the wand a good choice too. Carl takes the shrink wand, the eighth-floor lore book, the sheet music for A Song of Skedaddle, a case of twenty-four Feather Fall potions and a case of healing potions. Everything bought arrives as a prize box, which can only be opened in a saferoom.

beats.headline: Ten hands at Chaco's counter
beats.text: Over chat, Mordecai wants to know whether the prize counter has any sheet music like Chaco's own escape spell. Chaco looks up in surprise: Carl has a bard in his party? Can she hold pitch? He points at a sheet at ten hands, a song of Skedaddle, not quite as good as Wings of the Pyxie, which she could not sing for a while anyway. Sheet music sits somewhere between a scroll and a magic book. With it in front of her, the system helps a bard perform; sung badly the page tears a little, too many tears and it is ruined, and sung perfectly the song joins her repertoire. Carl adds it to his order.

beats.headline: Mined from the centipede
beats.text: In a hologram of goods on offer sits a grape-sized, colourless gem that glitters as it moves. Carl takes it for a soul crystal at first. Those are without value once installed as a power source, unless used as an explosive; unused ones are supposedly rare and treasured. This one is listed as something else. Mordecai explains: the soul crystals elves use to power their things are mined from Scolopendra's lair, created when certain types of people die and their souls are filtered through the centipede's body. Memorial crystals are similar, but made by fallen gods and demigods.

beats.headline: Twenty-five scalps at the counter
beats.text: Chaco's prize counter. Hunter Zabit: level sixty-six Beastmaster, an Atoll, tall and thin with four arms, three fingers to a hand, no mouth, a dozen nostril holes, and a trap module bandolier on his belt. He speaks by signing into something hidden in his clothes. Yes, the weasels were his. He meant to catch the top prey early, and the party killed his pets and his season with them. He collected twenty-five scalps anyway, and spends them: a drop shield for twenty, an invisibility pack for three.

beats.headline: For the survival of the Atoll
beats.text: Crawler Carl asks why he hunts people who are scared and weaker than he is. Hunter Zabit's answer, for the record: for the survival of the Atoll. They are not citizens, so oxygen and land are not rights. The scalp money pays the upkeep on their habitat, and without it they would have to accept indenture under another system. This season's failure hurts his people. Some hunters revel in the killing; for others it is survival. He would object too, were the situations reversed.

beats.headline: Clearing out Zockau
beats.text: Zockau is a ghost town. The hunters who dug in to hold its saferoom against the brambles all teleported away when the masquerade began, leaving their surplus sorted into little mounds on the floor. Stealing in a saferoom is as bad as killing; once the owner walks out, it is all fair game. Bomo goes in and comes back, by Mordecai's account, with armfuls of armor and swords, plus guns and power armor that are race restricted. Lots of stuff left behind, he reports.

beats.headline: Babies, sent out into the world
beats.text: Baby mantises are everywhere outside the castle. Crawler Elle McGibbons has the rest of it from a hunter with no eyebrows: Vrah's people tricked his brother into walking into the temple, where he was used as the birthing vessel for Diwata. They murdered another hunter to cure Vrah of a venereal disease. And now, in Elle's words, the Circe bug lady is having actual flesh-and-blood babies and sending them out into the world. Nobody present knows what becomes of them when the floor collapses.

beats.headline: The birthing is a spell
beats.text: The Sledge reports baby mantises outside the castle, everywhere, in numbers. Mordecai supplies the ruling that goes with it: Diwata's birthing is a spell, and a spell runs until it is finished casting. The five-minute limit that governs every other deity on this floor does not apply to a god in labour. She stays. They keep coming. Somebody should have read the terms.

beats.headline: What the hairless hunter told her
beats.text: I got the story out of that hunter with no eyebrows. Vrah messaged his brother, told him he'd be safe if he went into that temple, and tricked him into being the birthing vessel for Diwata. They murdered one of their own just to cure Vrah of a venereal disease, and the brother is pissed about it. Now the bug lady is birthing actual flesh-and-blood babies and sending them out into the world. What happens when the floor collapses? Do they just go away? They're her kids!

beats.headline: The boombox
beats.text: Okay so, Donut made me do it. I built her a boombox out of Carl's trap modules so it's not so loud, and I'm hidden backstage doing the voice, like a monster truck rally. It's Mongo! Carl wants to know how many trap modules I used. Hang on a second, man, don't get madder. Two of his smoke bombs go off too. Then I can't figure out how to turn the music off, and he has to give me instructions over chat.

beats.headline: Mongo moonwalks
beats.text: SMOKE. LOUD. MOTHER on back. EARTHQUAKE. Stomp. Three lady Mongos. MOTHER says taken. Mongo DANCES. Backwards. MOTHER bops.

beats.headline: That was low key
beats.text: Louis messed up some of the lines, and Mongo was supposed to leap completely offstage before the moonwalk reveal, but it went almost perfectly. The blob judge was shaking, and I am really sure that is a good thing. Carl says he distinctly remembers saying low-key. That was low key, Carl. They told me I couldn't do the magic missile entrance we planned. This was nothing compared to the Ke$ha act Miss Beatrice and I performed in Cleveland. Wait until they see our real dance number.

beats.headline: The potion ball
beats.text: WHEN AM I GOING? I am BORED. I could have sneaked away five times by now. Carl says not yet, any minute, and wants to know how many babies Diwata will have. As many as she wants. Her baby sprinkler will shoot them out until the very end of time if she likes. Then he asks if I still have the potion ball shoved up me. I have it. It is VERY uncomfortable. But I have it.

beats.headline: Mantises at the tunnel
beats.text: Mantises. Lots of mantises. Everywhere. They keep coming, flying in. We have to fight them. Carl says get in the tunnels, try not to fight, get the changelings through that door. Too many. We get picked up by airship. We go in from above instead. Carl says be careful of the sentinel towers, use the bombs on them if I have to, and drop none on the main castle. Louis says tell Skarn to moor the ship to the tower.

beats.headline: On Carl's other shoulder
beats.text: A heavy weight lands on Carl's shoulder, the one Princess Donut is not standing on. Ferdinand, familiar of Queen Imogen, has come out of nowhere, and he repeats Florin's question back at Carl in a mocking voice: yeah, mate, you feeling okay? Carl's answer goes to Samantha, not to the cat. He's distracted, it says. Go, go, go.

beats.headline: What is inside Lucia
beats.text: She comes apart and I hold on to her until it passes. Then I tell the others what I have worked out, because somebody has to say it out loud. There is more than one of her in that head. Several. Some of them are children. And the dog matters. Whatever is happening to Lucia, the dog is at the centre of it.

beats.headline: More than one of her in there
beats.text: Florin held on to me. He is kind to me even when I'm not the one who is here. He told the others that there is more than one of us in my head, and that some of the others are children too, and that the dog is the important part. He's right about the dog. I don't get to talk about the dog. I'm not the one who decides what I talk about.

beats.headline: More than one voice in there
beats.text: Florin says there are several presences in her head, other children among them, and that the dog is the key to it.

beats.headline: It's complicated, Carl
beats.text: Florin has told Carl there are children in Lucia Mar's head, a Dutch girl of ten among them, and Carl wants to know why, when we said no child crawlers were allowed. Okay, so. It is complicated, Carl. You do not have to be involved in everything. We are not going to discuss it, and especially not now. Heads up.

beats.headline: Two hundred and seventy-six
beats.text: Donut's unenhanced charisma sits at 138, and the benefactor-box tiara on her head doubles it, to a god-like 276 before the saferoom buffs. Once placed, it only lasts thirty hours before it dissolves. According to Mistress Tiatha, an NPC fawns over a crawler when the crawler's charisma beats the NPC's constitution and charisma together, by a hundred points for a province boss, which is what Ferdinand is. His total is 175. Donut is 101 over, and with her buffs and the Seize the Day Toothpaste, her effective charm is well over 300.

beats.headline: Cat-nac the Magnificent
beats.text: The queen's cat drops onto Carl's shoulder in a gold turban with a feather four feet high, and I lose it. Louis says goose. It's not a goose, it's one of those mushroom penises. It's Horton! Hey, Horton, you have merch! How do you even walk in that thing, cat? Should we call you Cat-nac the Magnificent? He promises to bathe in our offal. I tell Donut her ex-boyfriend has anger issues. She says she's always been attracted to the bad boys. You and me both, sister.

beats.headline: Still in a prize box
beats.text: The talent show is under way. Carl tells Donut not to wait for them: get out the moment the seal is broken, and they will try to jump on stage and follow; if that does not work, Escape Plan D. He bought Feather Fall potions, and he will hand them out. Donut points out that he does not have them: they are in a prize box, and there will be no time. Others need them, says Carl. He will hand them out as soon as Samantha turns off the inventory and magic block.

beats.headline: The royal hat
beats.text: Sir Ferdinand, level 100 Province Boss, arrives in a gold turban with a white feather four feet high, and the crawlers around Carl laugh at him. It is his royal hat. It makes him the most handsome boy in the castle, and it carries a level-10 lightning spell. Charmed, he lets slip that the queen has him watching her sister and means to kill her once the party is over. Then he decides to visit Princess Donut in person, and bounds from the room.

beats.headline: He talks Samantha through the map
beats.text: Samantha is in the cat's tunnels and has forgotten the way to the security room. Louis is busy with the airship, so the job falls to Firas: from the first floor she has to climb to the fifth, cross to the main thoroughfare and come down again to the third. On it, he says. Afterwards he stands with Carl and Louis, patting his friend on the back while Louis holds back tears over the Twister, and points out how calm the guards are.

beats.headline: Two hundred mounted elves
beats.text: Hidden near the castle with a few dozen crawlers, the subject reports: about two hundred mounted elves just rode out. The airship crept in, a spotlight caught it, and its bomb missed. The mantises are mostly further north. Then: holy shit, gotta go. Next message: mantises and elves everywhere, fighting each other. His team is still hidden. The airship is covered with bugs like moths on a lightbulb, and the towers are shooting magic missiles. Crawler Carl tells him to stay down and not attack until told.

beats.headline: You have merch
beats.text: For the record: the subject was in the first group led into the main ballroom, a mushroom guy Crawler Carl had only seen in passing, afraid of Elle for some unknown reason. When Ferdinand turns up in a tall hat, Elle says it looks like a hat designed to look like Horton the mushroom guy over there. Hey, Horton, come here, she shouts. You have merch. From across the room, the mushroom guy lifts a middle finger at her. Elle keeps laughing. I love that guy, she says.

beats.headline: Size-Up on the cat
beats.text: The Size-Up potion takes just over thirty seconds to seep in, and then I have him. Level 100, province boss, listed as a minion. A hundred down the line, dexterity 125, charisma 75, so constitution plus charisma is 175, and Donut clears it. The hat is magical, a level-10 lightning spell. He can go invisible and phase jump, and his claw attack looks brutal. When the hunters start closing in around Lucia, Carl tells us to watch out. We're on it. Don't micromanage, Carl.

beats.headline: The Twister is taken
beats.text: I figured out the tunnels on the castle map. They're not ducts, they're how the queen's cat gets around, like the ones Jojo's grandma had, and one goes right into the security room. Tonight I'm on chat helping the Sledge fly the Twister, and the mantises take it. They're all onboard. The changelings turned to birds and left, and the Sledge had to jump. He says he's got the controller and can crash it into the turrets, like in GTA. Don't crash the Twister, man!

beats.headline: She has charmed a boss
beats.text: Mordecai holds that a boss cannot be charmed. Subject insists she has done it. The rules say a white-tagged boss can be, if the crawler clears it by a hundred points, which puts her on the right side of the argument, and puts the cat, at a hundred and one points over, on the right side of the arithmetic by one.

beats.headline: She charms Ferdinand
beats.text: My ex-boyfriend lands on Carl in a royal turban with a four-foot feather, and I tell Carl I don't think I can do this; it only worked a little on the elves. Eye on the prize, he says. Remember how he tried to kill Mongo. So I tell everyone to stop making fun of his hat. I like it. It looks quite smart. And it takes. He goes casual, calls me babe, air-humps Carl's head, stays for my performance. Then he offers to come over to our ballroom, and he is gone.

beats.headline: Never part of the plan
beats.text: The mantises take the airship, and the Sledge has to jump. His report: he is okay, Bonnie is okay, the bear cubs are okay, Prudence is okay. Crawler Carl notes that they never agreed to save Prudence and the cubs; they were meant to stay in the saferoom until the collapse and simply disappear. He tells the Sledge to protect Bonnie and the bears if he can, but not to sacrifice himself for any of them.

beats.headline: She left the potion ball behind
beats.text: I tricked them good. I'm in the tunnel. Where do I go? I was supposed to memorise the map; did anyone SEE that map? Firas talks me through it. The cat runs right past me with his stupid hat in his mouth and never sees me. What a dweeb. There are five elves in the security room. Carl says use the potion ball. I gave it to Clay-ton; it made me clink when I rolled, and it was very rude to shove it up there. Then I look in. NOT FAIR. The guards are already dead.

beats.headline: Well over three hundred
beats.text: Inside the castle, Donut has to charm Ferdinand. He is a province boss, so her charisma has to beat his constitution plus charisma by a hundred. Her base is 138, and her new benefactor-box tiara doubles it to 276 for thirty hours, before the safe room's buffs: 101 points over. Her effective charm, with all her buffs plus the bonus from the Seize the Day Toothpaste, is well over three hundred. She insists it is not working, but they have already been seeing the effects.

beats.headline: Taken by the mantises
beats.text: The ground rumbles with one of Carl's bombs dropped from the Twister; a spotlight finds the airship, and the bomb meant for the mounted elves misses. Then Louis comes running: the mantises have taken the Twister, the changelings have turned to birds and left, and the Sledge had to jump. Sledge has the controller, and Bonnie, the bear cubs and Prudence are okay. Bombs still dangling, he says he can crash the Twister into the other turrets, like a helicopter in GTA. Don't crash the Twister, Louis begs. Carl tells him to do it.

beats.headline: Closing the semicircle
beats.text: Lucia Mar sits at the prize counter, chatting and waving her tequila bottle as if every crawler present were her best friend, with a ring of crawlers around her to keep the hunters off. The hunters form a second semicircle around that one: Vrah, Hunter Zabit, and several draconians, moving in. Chaco backs himself against the wall. Crawler Carl reads the play at once. They are trying to get Lucia to break the peace seal.

beats.headline: Her mother has been there all along
beats.text: Everyone on the Hunting Grounds who knows Tina's story knows what she wants, Signet tells Carl, and it is not to dance in a recital. She wants her mother back. Carl says her mother is Kiwi, the mongoliensis. Signet agrees. Tina's mind is gone, and she does not realise that the other dinosaur has been there the whole time. She already has what she wants; she only needs to see it. What Carl has planned for tonight is close, Signet says, but not quite right.

beats.headline: Gideon and his team
beats.text: Imogen asks me whether those weren't my friends hiding in the trees. I tell Gideon to run. Then the notice: this crawler is deceased, removed from my address book. The blood down her dress is theirs. Almost thirty crawlers who stayed back to sow chaos because I asked them to. The sink is running, I tell her, which makes no sense to her. You will not break me, I think. I tell her I don't know what she's talking about.

beats.headline: He means to break the seal himself
beats.text: The Sledge is surrounded and Prudence is dead, and his spell needs minutes of protected casting he isn't going to get. Our only chance is someone breaking the seal at the right moment. So it's me: I'll kill Eva. I tell Donut plan A is a go, the whole performance, start to finish. I tell Imani not to tell her. Imani says she'll do it instead. Elle tells me to go to hell; Donut will never forgive me. As long as she's still alive, I don't care.

beats.headline: A liter of cat blood
beats.text: Carl's planning notes, added to the cookbook: there is a difference between Donut enchanting someone, as she does the Bopcas, and magically charming them, as she did Kiwi. Enchanted, Ferdinand would fall over himself to please her but could still object. Charmed, he would be her official minion and do what she says almost without question. Mordecai can make a charm animal potion. All they need is a liter of cat blood, and they have a ready source. The spell is line of sight, so if Ferdinand is in the audience, Donut can down it the moment she goes on stage.

beats.headline: One more mantis in the castle
beats.text: Crawler Carl assembles it all at once. Diwata, which is to say Circe Took, is in the castle, blended in with the rest of the mantises, there to help her daughter. She meant to break the connection between the goodwill ballrooms and end the party, but a capacitor keeps them running. The fallback: fill the castle with nymphs, give the hunters back their magic, and wait for somebody to break the peace seal, so that Vrah can get clear in the chaos.

beats.headline: Knocked out beneath the ballroom
beats.text: Somebody reached the castle's security room before Samantha did: five guards dead in their chairs, heads severed, the hunters' ballroom unshielded, the goodwill interface's crystal taken, still running on its capacitor. Mantises. Carl works it out: Diwata is in the castle, and she comes for the room when Samantha puts the crystals back. Samantha locks her out, and when the door breaks, bites down on a mouthful of soul crystals. The blast opens the floor between two ballrooms. Diwata is knocked out, still giving birth.

beats.headline: What she tells the elite
beats.text: The half-naiad sits with the judges for most of the evening deep in conversation, and I tell her a great deal. The whole universe has been looking forward to this party. More people than there are stars in the sky are watching. The deity is under the control of that bug's mother, who sold half of everything she owns to get here. Her own mother was never real; nor were her friends. And I am sad Carl won't survive the night. I was looking forward to meeting him on the battlefield outside Larracos.

beats.headline: It's her twin
beats.text: The queen drops Carl and I pick him up. So much for peaceful. Katia was right: it looks like Iffy, but it isn't. It's her twin. I can tell. It's not really her either. Iffy was worried about what had happened to her sister. It's not right, them using her body like that. We have to do something about it. Carl says he's working on it.

beats.headline: Chasing the elves
beats.text: The Sledge, still trying to get into a tower past the rubble, reports in fragments: elves coming out of the woods, brambles chasing them, moving faster than usual. Imani confirms from outside that most crawlers there are being forced down the stairs. The brambles were not supposed to get this far into elf territory for hours yet. They seem to be reacting to the elves trying to beat them back, and since the elves at the border fell back to defend the castle, the brambles are chasing them in.

beats.headline: Two words: Gideon. Run.
beats.text: Gideon, crawler, is dead. Queen Imogen holds Crawler Carl in the air and asks whether those were not his friends hiding in the trees just outside. Crawler Carl sends two words: Gideon. Run. Warning: This crawler is deceased. They have been removed from your address book. There is blood running down the queen's dress. Almost thirty crawlers were in that team. They stayed back to sow chaos because Crawler Carl asked them to, and Crawler Carl's own assessment is that they died because he asked. Imani does not know yet.

beats.headline: The second-to-last act
beats.text: The second-to-last act appears on stage: the mushroom guy, Horton, with an acoustic guitar missing a string. It is the same guitar Britney is meant to play for the final act. He tunes it for a long while, and Queen Imogen grows impatient. This is 'Wonderwall,' he says, and starts to play. Crawler Donut's reaction is OMG.
