Crawler Carl laughs at the absurdity of it all: a mushroom dude playing a poorly-tuned guitar and singing his cat's favourite song, with the whole universe watching.

beats.headline: I guess I'm done
beats.text: Ka-Blam. The building shakes, tables fall, the buffet collapses and scatters the hunters. The subject pauses his song. The floor tiles have shattered like windshield glass, and near the exits they are simply gone, leaving burning, jagged holes. Crawlers standing over the gaps do not fall through. Samantha, somewhere in the castle, reports by chat that she has chomped down on the soul crystals. On stage, the subject speaks: Uh, I guess I'm done. He goes offstage.

beats.headline: She takes a chair before the stage
beats.text: I appear in the ballroom with blood down my gown, and my familiar is not where he belongs; now that I am at the party he is locked in with the rest of my staff. My sister has her invitation. Let her enjoy it. I draw the man across the floor to me and hold him in the air. My castle is besieged: his changelings at my towers, his friends in the trees. I turn to leave, and stop. I sit before the stage. Proceed.

beats.headline: Died protecting two babies
beats.text: Prudence, ursine barmaid, is dead. The notice comes from the Sledge, in his clipped way, while a mushroom crawler takes the stage in the ballroom: Prudence dead. Died protecting two babies. They're crying. Hugging Bonnie. Too many mantises. Still fighting. Crawler Carl's assessment at that moment is that the plan is done. The Sledge reports a while after that the cubs are safe, for now.

beats.headline: She chomps the soul crystals
beats.text: I pull the two crystals on the right. The two on the left are already out, on the floor: somebody got here first, and the guards are still in their chairs with their heads cut off. Mantises. Carl says put them back, fast, Diwata is coming. I do. I lock the door and her baby bugs squish in the hallway. The door breaks. So I lose big, like he said. I stick the crystals in my mouth, go up there and chomp down. They blow up. All of them. OKAY. THAT WAS MY BAD.

beats.headline: She hears what Carl was trying to tell her
beats.text: Carl tried to tell me and I would not hear it. I hear it now. My mother's murder, my exile, the circus, the vengeance I have carried since I was a child: it is a programme. It is watched across the galaxy. There are people outside this floor who decide when I grieve and when I strike, and who count how many are watching while I do it. I understand him now.

beats.headline: Caster, sacrifice and killer
beats.text: I eat an acorn from the goddess's tree, and my tattoos begin to swirl. The creature D'Nadia told me my mother was never real, and that my fallen brothers and sisters, whose memories adorn my body, never were. She also told me she had looked forward to meeting Carl on the battlefield outside Larracos. Ink Marauder needs three: a caster, a sacrifice, and one to kill the sacrifice. It can be one who is all three. Ask Donut for her Torch, with moon rays. Just tell me when.

beats.headline: Surviving is winning
beats.text: Louis is worried about how it is going. Whether the plan holds, how it looks, who comes out on top of it. Surviving is winning, Louis. Everything else is bullshit. Then the changelings and me go into that castle, through a turret and the elf inside it, which is the thing everyone outside said could not be done.

beats.headline: It does not flash
beats.text: Up on stage Elle and Imani finish, and every crawler in the ballroom is unmuted, no longer peace-bonded and able to reach their inventory again. All around the room, crawlers look about. The warning light that would have let the guards and Imogen know about the change does not flash, and Carl's people spread out telling everyone to keep their mouths shut.

beats.headline: Got both
beats.text: In the queen's chamber, the whole palace shakes with one explosion, then a second, louder one, and acorns fall from the inverted tree like hail. Sledge reports in: guard turrets get good, Twister house blow up, got both. Louis wails. Surviving is winning, Louis, Sledge tells him. Everything else is bullshit.

beats.headline: She does not need it
beats.text: Donut stands alone on the stage in her little fake headset microphone, the charm potion already taken, and a spotlight narrows on her. My name is Princess Donut, she says. She does not take out the sheet music. She does not need it. She is singing a song her mother used to sing to her, and it is called All Eyes on Me. Backstage Britney strums the Popovs' guitar, a string missing, a sad minor strum, and Donut sings: good girl, good girl, you're a good girl, my princess.

beats.headline: All eyes on the stage
beats.text: She repeats the lyrics a few times, the same song a drunken Bea used to sing to her, moving slowly to the right of the stage, and her voice soars. The spell does exactly what its title says. Everyone in the room, hunters, crawlers and the queen among them, falls under a minor charm that fixes their attention on a subject of the caster's choice. Britney lets the last chord hang and starts a faster piece, and the spotlight re-forms on Big Tina. Everyone is affected, Carl included. Only Signet seems untouched.

beats.headline: The guitar with a missing string
beats.text: Backstage, I play. It's the Popovs' guitar, found in a boss room a long time ago, and it's missing a string. A sad minor strum for Donut's song, and it sounds full anyway. When she's done I let the last chord hang and go into something fast and baroque for Tina. Carl tells me I need to get away from the backstage area and come out. I let the guitar fade.

beats.headline: The knife, the ring and the smoke
beats.text: Signet asks if I happen to have a knife. I give her the one somebody once used trying to assassinate Donut, handle first, and slip on my bracer while I'm at it. Protect your family, she says, and watch over mine. Then she goes to sit beside her sister. When the seal breaks and the judges and Chaco vanish, I put on the Ring of Divine Suffering and mark Vrah. Two smoke curtains, one in each hand like grenades, into the room. Now.

beats.headline: Sir Ferdinand joins up
beats.text: Up on stage, the curtains pull back on Donut alone. Ferdinand sits on the center table among the three judges in his ridiculous hat, eyes on her, tail wagging. Carl hands a Feather Fall potion to a crawler as Donut's message comes in: she took the charm potion, and it worked. Come on, baby, Ferdinand calls, and tells Empress D'nadia that is his bird up there. Carl's interface blinks. Sir Ferdinand, minion of Princess Donut, has joined the party.

beats.headline: All eyes on her
beats.text: The spotlight narrows on Donut alone on stage, her tiara glittering. She does not take out her sheet music, because she does not need it. She sings a song her mother used to sing to her, All Eyes on Me, with Britney on guitar backstage. It is a charm spell that focuses everyone's attention on a subject of the caster's choosing, and with Donut's insane charisma it catches the whole room, the queen and Carl included. Only Signet seems unaffected.

beats.headline: All Eyes on Me
beats.text: I take the charm potion, and it works: Sir Ferdinand, minion of Princess Donut, has joined the party, and he tells the Empress that is his bird up there. Then the spotlight. My name is Princess Donut, and I am singing the song my mother used to sing to me. It is called 'All Eyes on Me.' I do not take out the sheet music. I do not need it. Britney plays. Everyone in the room is charmed, even the hunters, even the queen. And then the spotlight finds Tina.

beats.headline: According to Prudence
beats.text: Tina finally dances. Two cretins hold up a ship's mainsail painted with waves, and she twirls across the stage, casting sparkles. According to Prudence, poor dead Prudence, the dance Tina was supposed to perform was called the Water Ballad, and it was about a mer-bear. The recital the subject described goes on, long after, without her.

beats.headline: The wand casts the Recital
beats.text: From the stage, Donut reads the recharge scroll, and Big Tina's inert wand glows in her claw. It shoots sparkles, and it also casts a spell called The Recital: everyone already staring at the dinosaur is suddenly happy to be there, as if this were something they had been looking forward to. Tina hops, shaking the stage, and twirls. The cretins raise a painted mainsail behind her, and when it drops there are thirty velociraptors plus Mongo and Kiwi in homemade sea-creature costumes.

beats.headline: She opens her own throat
beats.text: Tsarina Signet sits down beside her sister, rigid and glowing, holding a knife she borrowed from Carl. She has two regrets: that she never said goodbye to her Grimaldi, and that she will not be the one to kill Imogen today. She and her mother were going to leave for an island. Then she draws the knife across her own throat. Every acorn falls from the tree at once. The floor opens, the Nothing takes her while Imogen grabs at her, and it closes. Her tattoos and her blood stay.

beats.headline: No let Bomo beat my Frogger score
beats.text: Carl says do it. Casting now. One minute to chant, five minutes to cast. He says I am inside the castle, so I go to the ninth floor with everyone else, the cat too, and to watch him. I will feel sick for a full day. He thanks me for doing this and for taking care of the Princess. No let Bomo beat my Frogger score. He says he will unplug the machine the moment they get back. Good.

beats.headline: Psamathe, we are coming
beats.text: When Signet falls, the floor rends open and the Nothing shows itself: ethereal shrieks, black wisps and tendrils lashing upward, a stench of sulphur. And from the dark a faint voice, distant and hollow, shrieking a name. Psamathe. Psamathe, we are coming. Then the hole snaps shut. Apito has turned her back, the notice says. The seal has been broken, the Butcher's Masquerade has failed to cast, and the party is over.

beats.headline: Big Tina's wand glows
beats.text: Donut's song has charmed the room, and Britney has started a faster, baroque piece with the spotlight on Big Tina at the centre of the stage, her pink boa round her neck and her inert wand in her hand. As everyone watches, the wand glows: Donut has just cast the recharge scroll on it. The dinosaur looks at it with wonder and waves it, and sparkles dance through the air. It casts a charm as well, a performer's trick called The Recital, which makes everyone happy to be there and wanting to watch the stage.

beats.headline: Casting now, five minutes
beats.text: Carl gives the order: Sledge, do it. The answer comes back in the chat: one minute to chant, five minutes to cast. He is inside the castle, so he goes down with everyone else, and Ferdinand with him. Carl warns him about the zombie things, and the day of sickness, and thanks him for taking care of Donut. The Sledge's only request is that Bomo not be allowed to beat his Frogger score. Carl promises to unplug the machine.

beats.headline: The recital, finally
beats.text: In the middle of the battle Princess Donut puts the I Take It All Back potion on Kiwi, and the pack leader is not a mongoliensis any more. An ursine stands there, naked but for the paper bubbles. Tina looks at her and knows her, and the Recital quest closes on the spot. It was never a quest about a monster. Nobody reading the log had any way of knowing that.

beats.headline: Signet's mother, in my inventory
beats.text: Not all of Signet's tattoos are warriors. A crying child, Clint, and his old teacher Miss Nadine cower on the floor; I shove a health potion at the boy and it works. Next to them lies a naiad with her eyes closed. Princess Lunette, incomplete flesh golem: the memory of Signet's mother. They'll last forever, Nadine says. Signet wants me to take the golem and find a Pulpmancer for Samantha. It weighs nothing and has no dot on my map. I pull it into my inventory.

beats.headline: Five seconds, then potions
beats.text: The Recital quest completes, and the Sledge sends his last message: five seconds, good-bye. All around them is blood and carnage and death. Potions, Carl shouts. He has his nipple ring's fall ability, but he does not trust it, and drinks a Feather Fall potion. He got the potions out of their prize box, along with a bunch of other things, standing on Prepotente's personal saferoom cube, the last zap of the goat's wand, in exchange for letting Prepotente take over the party for a day or so.

beats.headline: I'll protect you, my bride
beats.text: The seal breaks, and Ferdinand, charmed to the whiskers, shouts up at the stage that he will protect his bride, and blinks out. When Imogen has Carl in the air with his bones snapping, the orange form of the cat slams into her head. She staggers and drops Carl, then backhands her own familiar across the room, the cat going one way and his hat the other. He hits the ground, yowls and disappears.

beats.headline: Bubbles on Kiwi
beats.text: Imogen snaps Carl's arm, Sir Ferdinand slams into her head and she backhands him away, and Carl heals himself. Kiwi, Donut calls from the stage, come here, lower your head. She grasps one of the paper bubbles on the back of Kiwi's neck with two paws and squeezes, and the potion ball hidden inside bursts just as Big Tina reappears on stage. The effect is instantaneous. Kiwi staggers and stands, no longer a dinosaur but an ursine, naked but for the remaining paper bubbles. The other raptors roar as one and their dots turn red. Tina roars, then roars again, and the third time it sounds almost like words. The fourth: Mom? Mommy?

beats.headline: Red lightning
beats.text: My sister's tattoos swarm around me and cannot touch me. I answer with red lightning in every direction at once. Then I push out of the mess of them. You fools. I swipe my hand and the man's arm snaps, and I draw him to me through the air, breaking. My own familiar strikes my head. I strike him away.

beats.headline: Taken all the way back
beats.text: Mongo and Kiwi bring Vrah down together in the middle of the castle battle, which is a sentence worth reading twice. Then Princess Donut uses the I Take It All Back potion on her, and the mongoliensis is gone. An ursine stands in the wreckage, naked but for paper bubbles, and Big Tina looks across at her and knows her mother's face.

beats.headline: Finish her
beats.text: BUG. Mongo and Kiwi. Bite. Rip. BUG has no legs. Carl says finish. Make it hurt. Kiwi touches heads with Mongo. Kiwi goes. Mongo finishes BUG. Happy.

beats.headline: The hammer in the ballroom
beats.text: The ballroom fills with gore and mantis nymphs from above and below, and the Popovs swing their meteor hammer through the room, twisting and shouting as they destroy the nymphs. Around them Prepotente throws potion bottles, Li Na throws chains for her brother to dance along, and Florin works a shotgun from the corner until the blasts become a beat. Mantises still surge in through the doorway.

beats.headline: One zap, for a day in charge
beats.text: Carl needs the potions out of his prize boxes, and there is no saferoom in the castle. I have a personal saferoom cube, and one zap left on my wand. I let him stand on the cube and use the zap, and he gets his potions out, and a great deal else. In exchange, he lets me take over his party for a day or so. When the seal breaks, I throw potion bottles into the nymphs.

beats.headline: Sic 'em
beats.text: Sic 'em, I say, and my velociraptors leap off the stage into the hunters. When the queen is busy with Ferdinand and Carl, I call Kiwi to me and tell her to lower her head, and I squeeze the bubble on her neck until the potion ball inside bursts. Kiwi stands up a bear, naked except for her paper bubbles. All my other raptors go red at once. Tina comes back onto the stage, sees her mother, and roars until the roar is words. Mommy?

beats.headline: Take the golem
beats.text: Signet is gone, and not all of her tattoos were warriors. Beside the crying boy Clint and Miss Nadine lies a naiad with her eyes closed as if sleeping: Signet's mother, or the memory of her given flesh. Princess Lunette. Incomplete Flesh Golem. Samantha pokes her with a burned head and calls her cousin. Nadine, breathless, says Signet wants Carl to take it; she took the memory with her and left just the body. Help Samantha. Find a pulpmancer. It weighs nothing and has no dot on the map. Carl pulls it into his inventory, and Samantha shoots off down a hole in the floor.

beats.headline: A fall ability, not trusted
beats.text: The Recital quest completes, and the Sledge sends his last message: five seconds, good-bye. All around them is blood and carnage and death. Carl meets Donut's eyes and shouts for potions. He has his nipple ring's fall ability, but he does not trust it, so he drinks a Feather Fall potion as well. Then the world goes vroom, and everything freezes.

beats.headline: It was never about the town
beats.text: Donut spends an I Take It All Back potion on Kiwi and turns her back into an Ursine, and Tina recognises her mother. What the child wanted was never the recital: it was the mother the transmutation had turned into a dinosaur, who had been at her side the whole time. The quest closes on that.

beats.headline: Surprise, motherfuckers
beats.text: I surf into the ballroom through the ceiling on a tidal wave of bug gore and land on Vrah. Remember me, bitch! Carl thanks me like I'm leaving. Is he breaking up with me? Is it because of Louis? Then he says Signet is gone. She killed herself. She was supposed to give me my BODY. There is a naiad golem on the floor, my cousin, and the teacher says Signet wants Carl to take it and find a Pulpmancer. TAKE IT, CARL. He does. Then I fly down through a hole in the floor.

beats.headline: He finishes casting Zerzura
beats.text: The battle is everywhere and my job is to stand still and finish the words. So I stand still and finish the words. The castle goes. The whole building and every NPC breathing inside it, taken out from under the people who thought they owned them. That is what the spell was for. I said I did not need it explained.

beats.headline: Mongo and Kiwi
beats.text: Hunter Vrah has been removed from the Hunting Grounds by Mongo and Kiwi, in the all-out battle around the submerged castle. Two dinosaurs. It took two. Also logged from the same fight: Tsarina Signet's tattoos are now permanently alive, and an incomplete flesh golem of her mother has appeared, which Crawler Carl has put in his inventory. Do not ask me what he intends to do with it. I have stopped asking.

beats.headline: The jacket takes the lightning
beats.text: I'm on the ground, screaming. Carl throws a disco ball at the queen and shouts at me: your jacket! The butterflies spread, and the queen's lightning comes out as one bolt instead of everywhere, pulled into the clump of them. They explode barely ten feet over our heads. Donut and Mongo and Carl and I go flying in different directions.

beats.headline: Tripper
beats.text: One hunter left: Zabit, the Atoll from the prize counter. He points at me, shouts something I can't hear, and goes invisible. I start after him and stop, remembering the belt of trap modules. I cast Tripper, and his own landmines go off under him and tear him in half. Team two, eliminated. I loot him. No drop shield and no invisibility potions; those must still be in a prize box. A lot of traps, though.

beats.headline: Died shrieking his name
beats.text: Corner four of the final arena: Diwata, burning, looking exactly like her true identity, a baby mantis halfway out of her. Crawler Princess Donut casts Laundry Day at level fifteen. It cannot harm a god, but the god is only armour, and the spell strips it off the driver. Diwata leaves the floor. Circe Took stands up wet and covered in bubbles and begins to say she does not need the god's protection. A dozen of her own children fall on her before she finishes. She dies shrieking Crawler Carl's name.

beats.headline: Boss battle, and a sponsor's own children
beats.text: Boss battle: crawlers, hunters, Queen Imogen and Diwata, all in one arena, and the audience gets exactly what it paid for. Princess Donut takes Laundry Day to level fifteen and strips the god-armour off Circe Took, and Circe, unarmoured, is torn apart by the mantis children she paid to have. There is a lesson in that about sponsorship. I will not be the one to say it out loud.

beats.headline: Elves in love
beats.text: Atop Mongo and matted with gore, Donut is giddy. She was wrong about her charisma not working: her love vampire skill works really well when it is this high. Behind her, elves wade through the fray with little heart icons over them. It does not work on the bugs. We need to get her charisma that high permanently, Carl thinks.

beats.headline: Heave
beats.text: We fight the queen on the beat, the way Carl said: nothing magical, half of us firing on the two and four, the other half on the one and three. Arrows, rocks, my shotgun. Heave! Her shield stutters like a strobe light, cast over and over, and it can't keep up with what we throw. Her health goes into the red. She stops casting the shield and falls to a knee, and her hands crackle red.

beats.headline: A dome, and a strobe
beats.text: Frozen in midair, the survivors can see it all. The brambles have filled the world and stopped about a hundred feet from where the castle was, mounted elves waiting at their edge. Thunderstruck starts playing. Then the brambles rise into a dome over the whole area and plunge it into darkness, a sickly yellow glow pulsing from little flower buds in time with the beat. The world unfreezes. As the fight falls into the castle's empty basement, the brambles push in above, entombing everyone.

beats.headline: Beside the knock-knock joke man
beats.text: Gwendolyn Duet is dead. The body lies among dead elves and bugs in the fight against Imogen, next to Cleiton, the knock-knock joke guy. Tran is alive beside them, dragging himself away and screaming; his legs are gone. Crawler Carl reads a scroll over him, and the legs do not grow back. Imogen is still on her feet atop a pile of corpses. Crawler Carl records subject as the woman who had been instrumental in their survival on the previous floor.

beats.headline: Gone to the ninth floor
beats.text: When the Sledge's spell lands, the castle is simply gone, half-destroyed and set down somewhere on the ninth floor, and it has taken the subbasements with it. It has also taken Signet's tattoo warriors, the changelings, Kiwi as a very pregnant bear, and Tina, still a dinosaur. Everyone and everything else, mostly mantis nymphs, hangs frozen in a rough stacked cube over the pit where it stood.

beats.headline: Against the queen's lightning
beats.text: Imogen's health is almost gone, a black nimbus round her and her hands crackling red: a lightning attack. Britney is screaming on the ground, and Louis and Firas lie unconscious side by side. Carl has had no time to reinstall the xistera, so he throws a hobgoblin disco ball by hand, shouting at Britney about her jacket. It splatters multi-coloured goo across the side of Imogen's head, and she barely notices. Her lightning comes out as a single bolt, drawn into the clump of spreading butterflies. It is not what Carl intended, but it works too.

beats.headline: Counterspells on the way down
beats.text: We fall into the brambles' dome with the bugs, and I work. Debuffs stack on our people and I take them off, dozens of them, counterspells and buffs as fast as I can throw them, wings spread the whole way down. When Carl's shell gives us a breath, I use it to heal whoever I can reach. Then I point. There. The god is in the far corner. Then I go back to the fight against Imogen.

beats.headline: She gives Carl her hat
beats.text: Daniel and Tran are getting hammered in the fight against Imogen, and I need to go back to them. Carl has used his protective shell already, and there's a mountain of bugs between him and the god. So I pull the beanie off my head, the one the Apothecary just gave me in a benefactor box, and put it on his. Use the spell to clear through the nymphs, I tell him. Get Donut close enough.

beats.headline: Off her head, onto his
beats.text: Katia has to go back and help against Imogen, and Carl has already spent his Protective Shell. A fifteen-foot mountain of bugs, some still alive, stands between him and the deity hiding in the corner. Katia pulls the beanie off her head and puts it on his, where it equips itself with a little beep: use the spell to clear through the nymphs, get Donut close enough. At the top of the hill a group of bugs lunges at him. He casts I Need My Personal Space, and it pushes them all in different directions, like a miniature Protective Shell. Mongo and Donut jump in, and they land before the god.

beats.headline: Nine to twelve
beats.text: Laundry Day, the armour-removing spell Carl has had Donut training every day for weeks, has to reach fifteen. She got it to nine on her own. Just before the party, Carl finally made her take the Pawna's Cries potion, which she secretly used to raise the spell three levels, to twelve. The note said to boost the rest with Prepotente, Imani and Samantha, but no spell or buff could be coaxed out of Samantha, and she is gone anyway. So Donut drinks Carl's more powerful Pawna's Tears, which his sponsor claims he will replace, and before the god she casts Laundry Day.

beats.headline: Laundry Day at fifteen
beats.text: Diwata has manifested, and she looks exactly like her true identity, Circe Took, wearing the god as armor. Donut casts Laundry Day. She trained it every day for weeks, to nine, and Pawna's Cries made it twelve, but it needed fifteen, and Samantha could not be coaxed into a boost. So they used the backup: Carl's Pawna's Tears, a bit of a waste of the stronger potion, though his sponsor claims he will replace it. Circe Took stands stripped of her protection, sopping wet and covered in bubbles. She dies shrieking Carl's name.

beats.headline: I miss my cat
beats.text: The final arena. A meteor hammer brains an elf coming at Crawler Carl out of the dark, and the Popovs stand guard while Crawler Princess Donut's mass heal drags him back awake. Then a sambhur, one of the elf mounts, on fire and covered in nymphs, comes spinning through the dark on one of Queen Imogen's spells. Its antlers go straight through the two-headed ogre. The double crawler hits the ground beside Carl. "I miss my cat," Dmitri says, just before he closes his eyes.

beats.headline: Riding Bianca down
beats.text: Bianca cuts through the nymphs like a snowplow, and I am on her back, screaming, shields around me, throwing potion bottles into the fray. The queen's lightning finds Britney's butterflies instead and the blast sends Carl flying. I fly over him on Bianca. Then I jump off my mount with a bubbling potion in each hand.

beats.headline: Laundry Day at fifteen
beats.text: I got top billing, again. Then my Laundry Day. Carl made me train it every day for weeks, to nine, my Pawna's Cries potion made it twelve, and his Pawna's Tears took it to the very end of fifteen. Carl pushes the bugs back with Katia's hat, and Mongo and I jump in, and I cast it at the god in the corner. Soapy bubbles everywhere. Diwata goes back to the Halls of Ascendency, and a wet mantis woman is left standing there, and her own children fall on her.

beats.headline: A crater of bugs
beats.text: A literal wave of thrashing bugs falls on Crawler Carl in the fight with a deity. He slams the shell down. Bugs, elves, dinosaurs and a few hunters rocket away in every direction. With the Intelligence he has now, the shell is huge; it leaves a crater with only crawlers and corpses in the middle, and Imani uses the gap to heal whoever she can reach.

beats.headline: A cloud of stuffing
beats.text: Imogen's health is almost gone and the lightning is coming. Your jacket, Carl shouts at Britney, and tosses a hobgoblin disco ball against the queen's head, meaning the butterflies to seek it out and overwhelm her. Instead the lightning comes out as a single bolt, drawn to the spreading clump of butterflies, and the summoned creatures explode barely ten feet overhead. Donut, Mongo, Britney and Carl go flying in different directions. Flaming bits of stuffing fall everywhere like embers.

beats.headline: Cage fight extreme
beats.text: B-B-B-Boss Battle! Cage Fight Extreme! Four teams enter, one team leaves! Corner one: the dungeon's top crawlers, plus some other guys. Corner two: seventy-five hunters, down from over a thousand, most of whom have been acting like little bitches, so they're probably dead. Corner three: Queen Imogen, shunned by her goddess for the worst party since Persepolis, and really, really pissed off. Corner four: Diwata, level 250, immortal. Talk her into birth control and she's out of the ring. The boss music is 'Thunderstruck.'

beats.headline: The legs do not grow back
beats.text: Katia tells Carl that Daniel and I are getting hammered in the fight with the queen. We are. Gwen is dead, beside the knock-knock joke man. My legs are gone. I drag myself away, screaming. Carl reads a scroll over me and it heals me. The legs do not grow back.

beats.headline: The second act closes
beats.text: A boss battle with crawlers, hunters, the queen and a goddess all in the same room. The high elves do not survive it. Imogen goes down, and the second season is complete.

beats.headline: Surrendered at the door
beats.text: At the high elves' party, an elf at the twisting staircase made every guest store their weapons in inventory and then patted them down, including the wrist bracer that forms Carl's Grull gauntlet. In the melee after the queen falls, Carl grabs a mantis by the neck as he re-forms the gauntlet, and its head pops off. Another is already at his neck, then another.

beats.headline: His own landmines
beats.text: Final arena. Hunter Zabit's dot is on the map, and when Crawler Carl moves in, the hunter points at him, shouts something that does not carry, and vanishes. Carl stops. He has seen that belt, and he knows what was in it. He casts Tripper. Several landmine traps go off at once, and Zabit reappears, torn in half by his own trap, laid seconds before. The announcement follows directly: team two, eliminated.

beats.headline: The castle is gone
beats.text: Everyone hangs frozen in midair. The high elf castle is gone, and with it Signet's tattoo warriors, the changelings, a very pregnant bear who was Kiwi, and Tina, still a dinosaur, all carried off to the ninth floor. No crawlers, hunters, pets, mobs, dinosaurs, bodies or elves went with it. It took its subbasements too, so the drop is further than anyone planned. Then the world unfreezes, and they fall.

beats.headline: A co-warlord in the succession
beats.text: Carl and Donut are co-warlords of a brand-new team, and the notice carries a note: Co-Warlord Princess Donut is a member of the royal line of succession of another team, Team #4, the Blood Sultanate. See the succession rules on how this will affect gameplay. On the walk to the stairs, Donut does not say it out loud. It is a complication. A big one.

beats.headline: Badly burned
beats.text: Morning, if you can call it that. Donut is waking Carl up with the count from the night. Firas. The Popovs. I'm not on the list, so that's something. My face is. Nobody has offered me a mirror, and nobody offering is how I know how bad it is. Burned. Badly, I'm told. I can feel where the word comes from.

beats.headline: Only one butcher
beats.text: Donut asks me why it doesn't hurt as much as it should, and I tell her what has been bothering me. The Butcher's Masquerade: the way it's written, there's only one butcher. I don't think it was possible for Imogen to win that boon. She said the masks were so we could pretend we weren't monsters. She had it backwards. Donut is wearing a mask right now, and it's protecting her. I need her to keep it on. One day, somewhere safe, it'll fall off, and it will hurt.

beats.headline: One of the two places
beats.text: Two places in the ninth floor's war came up at once. One of them is mine: the Prism Kingdom's, bought in my own name where anybody watching could watch me do it. The other went to a brand-new non-profit corporation. I know exactly whose that is.

beats.headline: Gone in the battle
beats.text: After the fight, sticky with blood, Donut asks Carl why it does not hurt as much as it should, and she circles once and settles into the crook of his arm, the way they used to so long ago. Running his hand across her bloody, matted head, Carl realizes her temporary, charisma-gaining crown is gone, lost in the battle. She has taken off her sunglasses, too.

beats.headline: Two of the slots change hands
beats.text: Carl and Donut are notified that their team is in. Donut's fan club and Princess D'Nadia between them secured two of the nine spots. Carl spends his airtime telling the watching galaxy that the teams can vote the ninth floor's safety protocols off, and telling anyone out there with a say in what their own government does to use it. The feed is cut.

beats.headline: Dead, with the Popovs
beats.text: Crawler Firas has been eliminated on the sixth floor. Crawler Princess Donut is bringing the night's count to Crawler Carl as I speak, and his name is on it, next to the Popovs. Found in a desert. Sobered up by a manager. Lasted one floor past that. The file is closed. It was never a thick one.

beats.headline: Twenty minutes under the thorns
beats.text: Afterwards, the brambles have slowed their descent. Carl reckons twenty minutes before they are crushed, and even then the brambles are meant to form a dome over the stairwell, leaving room around it. Everyone has a treasure map of loot, all of it covered in brambles; two crawlers cast a spell and went in anyway. Carl uses his last minutes on camera for the Faction Wars election, until Zev mutes him. Everyone in the universe is now watching two crawlers fight their way through a group of brambles.

beats.headline: Why it doesn't hurt
beats.text: After the fight, Crawler Donut lists her dead friends to Crawler Carl: Firas, Gwen, the Popov brothers, Gideon, even Signet and the dinosaurs who did not know how to dance. She should be crying, she says, and she is not. Florin cried, and Chris, and Elle. She asks why it does not hurt as much as it should, and whether she is doing something wrong.

beats.headline: The Wonderwall guy
beats.text: Horton, crawler, is dead. The notice comes from Crawler Donut, reeling off the dead to Crawler Carl after the fight: Firas, Gwen, and Horton, the Wonderwall guy, and the Popovs. Poor Horton, too, she says; it is always sad to lose a fellow musician. Elle is really upset about it. Crawler Donut thinks Elle feels bad about making fun of him all the time.

beats.headline: Her crystal changes hands
beats.text: Queen Imogen's memorial crystal has changed hands. Someone named Osvaldo took it off her, and she was in no condition to argue the point. Prepotente would like it next and is going after him for it. A queen's treasure, and it goes to whoever is standing closest when she goes down. That is how this floor works. That is how every floor works.

beats.headline: A second golden skull
beats.text: A champion has fallen. A bounty has been claimed. I walk past Carl with a second golden player killer skull over my head, and I tell him it's done, and go on to help the others. Li Na and her brother follow me. Then Carl is shouting my name, and I find the Popovs for him under the dead with Find Crawler. There are two of them. I can't believe I didn't see it.

beats.headline: She does not do the boss fight
beats.text: When the seal breaks I hide behind Florin with my hands over my ears while he shoots, and I cry. Then the castle is gone and everyone hangs in the air for a boss fight. I don't stay for it. I always set my teleports at stairwells. The moment before the fight starts, I use my escape thing, and I am gone.

beats.headline: Taken off Imogen
beats.text: Someone named Osvaldo takes hers, and Prepotente wants it for a quest.

beats.headline: It is Apito's
beats.text: Nobody bought it at the counter, so it went back to Imogen, and it came off her body. Prepotente says it is a memorial crystal for the goddess Apito, which should be impossible: as far as anyone knows she is not dead, and she just ran a party. Carl gets a quest update in the voice of Emberus: obtain the item Memorial Crystal: Apito, and see whether it has any bearing on Geyrun's murder.

beats.headline: The photo that is missing
beats.text: Crawler Carl holds up his photos of the faction teams like a hand of cards. He is missing two: a naga photo, and one from a group called the Operatic Collective, because they did not file a lawsuit against him on the previous floor. Three of the teams, the Operatic Collective among them, have local populations allowed to vote on all government expenditures, which means those citizens can change the vote here. Quasar is certain the Operatic Collective will be forced to vote yes. The people hate the family.

beats.headline: He takes Imogen's crystal
beats.text: New name on the board. Osvaldo, crawler. In the wreck of the Masquerade he walks up to Queen Imogen and takes her memorial crystal off her. Prepotente is going after him for it. I have no notes on Osvaldo before this moment, which tells you how he has been playing it. I have a note now.

beats.headline: Nodling Yearling, ineligible
beats.text: Katia Grim's Find Crawler skill points into a pile of gore, and under it are two fat, naked baby ogres about a year old: Maxim and Dmitri Popov, Level X, Nodling Yearling. They wake. The label over them reads Ineligible, and they blink out. Zev's explanation to Crawler Carl: children and pregnant crawlers are not allowed. Their game guide had them pick that race knowing this would happen. They have been transferred to the kinder facility on the surface. They are free.

beats.headline: Stolen and not taken
beats.text: After the boss fight, Carl lies hurt and asks after Lucia and Eva. Lucia teleported away before it started, Donut tells him. Katia says Eva was bitten by a dinosaur and is buried over there, not dead yet, and Katia is looking for her. Eva stole all those dinosaur repellent potions, Donut adds, and she did not even take one.

beats.headline: Twenty-two percent
beats.text: I struck twenty-two percent of all the damage against the boss, I struck the killing blow, and I had first looting choice. The crystal is mine. The man with the hawk says it was on her body and he took it first, and calls me a murderer because Bianca ate his pet. It is a memorial crystal for the goddess Apito, which is impossible, because Apito ran that party. I have a quest regarding it. I am the party leader now, briefly. Carl calls me Pony. I scream in his face.

beats.headline: Why it doesn't hurt
beats.text: We won. Firas is dead, and Gwen, and Horton, and the Popovs. Britney's face stayed gross when we healed it. I cannot stop talking. Then I ask Carl the thing. Why doesn't it hurt as much as it should? They were my friends, and I think I should be crying, and I'm not. Even Florin cried. I think something inside of me has broken. Carl says I'm wearing a mask and it is protecting me. You were right, I tell him. That was way more like Rambo than Footloose. And then I cry.

beats.headline: Who is covered
beats.text: The faction sponsors come to the ninth floor inside safety protocols that the crawlers do not have. Removing them is an action item, added to Carl’s list on his behalf, and all nine teams vote on it. The first count is two to seven against.

beats.headline: Carl puts it to the audience
beats.text: On air, in the last minutes before production cuts the feed, he tells the watching galaxy that the teams on the ninth floor can vote the safety protocols off, and that anyone with a say in what their government does should go and use it.

beats.headline: The orcs vote yes
beats.text: Carl holds up a photo of the late Queen Consort Ugloo, mother of the Maestro and Prince Stalwart, killed when the Valtay blew up her yacht after the orcs accidentally killed a singer. The vote to turn off the sponsors' safety protocols stands at two to seven, and the two are Carl and Donut's new team and the Skull Empire. The orcs are crazy and they're all going to die, Carl tells the cameras, but they're not chickens.

beats.headline: Mister Gonorrhea Arrow
beats.text: On the broadcast, Carl puts the Dream among the no votes, its man too much of a walking abscess to change his mind despite sending members of his own family to die on this floor because someone said his mom is bangin'. Donut adds that she is quite attractive for a bald woman. On the walk to the stairs, Carl says he thinks the Dream will vote yes after all. They can change their votes right up until the start.

beats.headline: Best in show
beats.text: Pet Show Champion. Best in Show. It goes to her giggling meatball of a pet, and the trophy mark appears over Tserendolgor's head in the field of the dead, just after she has come to stand beside Carl and Princess Donut has jumped onto her shoulder in solidarity. Princess Donut poofs out entirely, calls her an experience hog and a cheater, and retreats to Carl's shoulder, hissing. Carl laughs until he cries.

beats.headline: The Popovs are ineligible
beats.text: Carl has dug two naked baby ogres out of the gore, Maxim and Dmitri, and wants to know what to do with them. You don't need to do anything, Carl. Watch. Ineligible. Relax: children and pregnant crawlers aren't allowed. Their game guide made them pick that race because he knew this would happen. They've been transferred to the kinder facility on the surface. They're free. And while I have you: you're going on Odette's show right after the next floor starts.

beats.headline: I love you, Daniel
beats.text: Katia is going after Eva, and I say I will come. No, she says. Help with the rescues and the healing; Li Na will be with her. I am uncertain, but I relent. Li Na is a good bodyguard. Be careful, I tell her. Do it quick. She tells me she loves me, and I tell her I love her too. Before the party, when she was frightened of what she is, I told her it was okay. She is stronger than she thinks.

beats.headline: Show me Annie
beats.text: Before the party, Daniel told Katia she was squeezing too tight and hurting him. After that, she pulled a blitz stick and lit it. Only Daniel knows: it is one of her two big secrets in this dungeon. She found the sticks on Sally, one of Eva's victims, a healer who had worked at the airport and turned to Eva despite everything. She is dead now, like the rest of them. The drugs were the only thing left in her inventory. Eva left them there, a present for Katia, and a trap. Show me Annie, Katia thinks, and the blitz stick obliges. Every time.

beats.headline: Blocked by its own rules
beats.text: Borant wants Prepotente stopped before he can touch the seventh floor. In the pole position chamber a whole line of debuffs hits him and the crawlers with him: peace bonding, freeze, paralysis, slow, a teleport, an Administrative Hold. Four gnolls with guns appear. Every one of them is negated by AI resolution, and the gnolls vanish in smoke. The AI, Prepotente says, is forcing Borant to follow its own rules.

beats.headline: The lore book and the globe
beats.text: The globe room again. Parties are split into squads of five, and ours is two: Squad Leader Donut, and me. I've told nobody but Prepotente the title of the lore book I bought: Book of Lore, Commonwealth of the Bahamas, full of monsters and stats. I'd rather have the western United States, where we know the ground. Donut wants Ibiza. With twenty seconds left I say go with the Bahamas; we have the lore book. She spins to the Caribbean and clicks. That wasn't the Bahamas.

beats.headline: Only one of them
beats.text: Eva's last act puts the crown on Katia's head, and that means one thing. Only one of them, Donut or Katia, will be allowed to take the stairs from the ninth floor to the tenth. Katia touches her head, looks at Li Jun and Li Na, and says shit, several times.

beats.headline: It finds its way to Katia
beats.text: Donut lost the crown at the end of the third floor, and it found its way to Eva, fixed to the back shoulder of her glittering breastplate where it passed for decoration. As Katia's sword goes through her, Eva pulls it free with her lower left hand, and from her hand it goes to Katia's head. The hat the Apothecary sent Katia would have stopped it. She gave that to Carl. The crown melds into her form and disappears from sight.

beats.headline: He maps the castle from outside it
beats.text: Ahead of the castle job Edgar sits well back from the building and maps the whole of it from where he is. Every room, every level, and a set of small connecting tunnels that fit nothing anyone can name. Louis is the one who works out what they are for. They are Ferdinand's, so that he can move around his own house without ever using a door.

beats.headline: Book of Lore – Something
beats.text: In the seventh floor's starting chamber, Prepotente wants the full title of the eighth-floor boon. Carl makes him explain what he is doing first, and the goat asks again: please, tell me its name. Carl pulls out a thin hardback, Book of Lore – Commonwealth of the Bahamas, with the aquamarine and gold stripes and black triangle of the Bahamas flag on its cover and nothing else. Inside are descriptions and stats of monsters, and it falls open on an owl creature called the Chickcharney. The Bahamas? Donut says. That's where Miss Beatrice went for her vacation.

beats.headline: Twenty seconds at the globe
beats.text: Squad Leader Donut must spin a holographic globe and choose the eighth floor's starting location, and Carl has told nobody but Prepotente what his lore book covers. If the pole position boon is anything to go by, he tells her, the Bahamas book was designed to be really helpful, though he kind of wants the western United States, which they know. Donut wants Ibiza. With twenty seconds left Carl says go with the Bahamas: they have the lore book. Donut agrees, insists they are absolutely not going into the water this time, spins to the Caribbean and clicks. Goddamnit, Donut, Carl cries. That wasn't the Bahamas.

beats.headline: Katia kills her
beats.text: Hunting Grounds, the end of the floor. Crawler Eva, bitten by a dinosaur and buried in a corner, is still alive, and Crawler Katia Grim goes looking for her. Crawler Katia Grim kills Crawler Eva. That is the whole of it. Two professors came in through the same door; from here on, one. I don't do eulogies, and this is not the entry where I start.

beats.headline: One very tiny tap
beats.text: Five minutes on the timer in the seventh floor's starting chamber. Prepotente asks Donut for the hammer and the magical stick, lays them on the ground by the back wall and goes to a knee; he still does not understand why they were given to her and not him. When the countdown has dropped to zero and the stick is halfway into the glass, he picks up the hammer and whispers that he is a good, smart boy. He gives the stick a very tiny tap. A lightning pattern of fissures spreads across the wall. Then every wall of the level shatters into fine dust.

beats.headline: Eva's last act
beats.text: I find Eva with Find Crawler, alive under the bugs, and I make Daniel stay; I don't want him to see this. Li Na casts Preserve Injury. I cut off the hand with the escape ring, and the rapier. Eva wakes and asks me to heal her. Then she says she's sorry. That's all I wanted, to hear her afraid. I put the sword through her breastplate. As she dies she pulls something from the back of her armour: the Crown of the Sepsis Whore. It finds my head.

beats.headline: Show me Annie
beats.text: I have two big secrets in this dungeon. One is the blitz sticks. I found them on Sally, one of Eva's victims; she worked at the airport, she was a healer, and the drugs were all that was left in her inventory. Eva left them there for me. A trap. I light one and think, show me Annie, and it does, every time: nine months old, standing in her crib, holding on to my hair. Mordecai warned me they're addictive. I didn't listen. Only Daniel knows.

beats.headline: Through the breastplate
beats.text: Katia and Li Na pull dead bugs off the unconscious Eva, who has almost no health and ten seconds before she wakes. Li Na casts Preserve Injury so she cannot heal, and points at the ring on Eva's top right hand, the one that would let her disappear. Katia draws Eva's old sword and cuts the hand off with it, then the poisonous rapier from the top left stub. Eva wakes, spits defiance, then begs. Katia plunges the sword into her chest, punching right through the metal of her magical breastplate. Die, Eva.

beats.headline: Kill her
beats.text: I go with Katia. Eva is under the dead bugs, unconscious, almost out of health. I cast Preserve Injury so she cannot heal herself, and I point at the ring on her top right hand. Katia cuts it off. Eva wakes and asks to be healed. Katia laughs. My brother looks from Katia to me. Kill her, I say.

beats.headline: He shatters the seventh floor
beats.text: Look at what they gave us. The Great Race, a replacement the Valtay paid for and somebody threw together in a hurry, a circuit of glass tunnels with nothing holding it up. So I tested it. Minutes after it opened, the whole loop is dust, fine as flour. No crawler goes into their maze. No mob, no NPC, no boss gets to meet anyone. You wanted a seventh floor. Build a better one.

beats.headline: His mother's boots
beats.text: Carl asks how I really know. My mother's boots. Boots of Kiznet's Final Flight, from a minor boss just before Carl allowed her to kill herself. The description is five hundred and three percent longer than the average item's, and it tells a fairy tale: a boy in a maze where every tunnel seals behind him, resurrected and made to start over, who spends years trying to crack the walls. She played the piano for me. She was going to do it again at the talent competition. I am never going to get that back.

beats.headline: Viper Queen, and number one
beats.text: Carl, we're in a fish tank! And I'm ranked number one. Number one! I need to pick a new class, and the chat is down so Mordecai can't help, so I pick one. Viper Queen. Doesn't that sound delicious? I can shoot poison blobs. My health is lower, which Prepotente says is of no consequence. Then Prepotente leaves the party, and I am party leader.

beats.headline: Through the glass like magic
beats.text: In the seventh floor's starting chamber, Prepotente explains himself. The level is built like a Prince Rupert's drop on a massive scale, and it is called the Great Race, which is also the name of a fairytale about a boy in a maze whose tunnels seal behind him. He asks Donut for the hammer and the magical stick and holds a thermometer to the glass; the whole tale, he says, is in the description of his mother's boots. He splashes a potion on the wall. When the countdown hits zero and Cascadia rushes through the rules, he pushes the stick into the wet spot, and it slides through like magic. Godsdamnit, Prepotente, Cascadia says. Don't do it. The stick stops halfway.

beats.headline: The whole level breaks
beats.text: One tiny tap of the hammer, and a lightning pattern of fissures runs over the glass. Interesting, Prepotente says, his voice gone distant: he thought it would be instantaneous. Then the wall shatters, and not just that wall. The entire level explodes into fine dust, every crawler is sucked into the portals at the same time, and Carl and Donut flip head over toes into the stairwell. The last thing Carl hears is Cascadia screaming over the announcement system. He broke the whole level, Donut says in the marble chamber. All their sponsors came together to make sure he pulled it off, Carl answers.

beats.headline: December 10th in Havana
beats.text: The eighth floor opens inside the capitol building in Havana, because Donut picked Cuba. The notification says it is December 10th. We are inside a replay of the surface in the weeks before the collapse: people who are ghosts, and objects that are real, and anything looted from it turns to dust at the collapse. Fourteen days to fill a squad by planting flags in monsters under five per cent. Bea and her friends flew to the Bahamas on the 26th, after this phase ends, so Donut's caution bought nothing. Phase two moves us somewhere new. They'll be angling to send us there.

beats.headline: A god through Uzzi
beats.text: Odette's crawlers spent half the tenth floor hunting the dart, only to learn the puzzle needed a storm god. They have summoned two, Dodola has sent the other away, the timer is running, and Mordecai has a plan that will kill him. Odette has another: worship Dodola, then use the dart. It cannot be used on oneself, and Hold Steady is keeping the puzzle primed, so it has to be Uzzi. Chaco worships Dodola. Uzzi looks down at the dart in his hand, caws a war cry and spreads his wings. Chaco throws it into his breast. Uzzi's chest rips open as Dodola forms inside Chaco's containment with the puzzle, which shatters into the key. Her own lightning ends her. Did they use the dart on his brother, Mordecai asks.

beats.headline: T'Ghee, by Allister's account
beats.text: The announcement mentions T'Ghee totems, and Carl's breath catches, because he already knows the word. Allister, who wrote the thirteenth edition, treated T'Ghee as a religion, with nothing to do with capturing or summoning monsters. Carl can already see how the dungeon means to use it anyway. Mordecai supplies the dungeon's version: large playing cards, like Bautista's stuffed animals or Carl's tarot cards, reusable even when the summoned monster dies.

beats.headline: Somewhere close, obviously
beats.text: Throwing themselves right into the Bahamas was a bad idea, Donut explains in the empty hall, so as party leader she picked somewhere close. They gave Carl a book about the place Miss Beatrice was: it was quite obviously a trap. Its usefulness is painfully obvious, and Carl understands her logic, but she was wrong. Bea and her friends flew there on the twenty-sixth, after phase one would have moved them on, so they would never have seen their ghosts there; with a second location for phase two, the show has plenty of time to engineer a scene with her. Then Donut reports that Prepotente is in the Bahamas.

beats.headline: He talked Gideon into it
beats.text: Crawler Donut's account of the floor, set down for her fans. It was not all good; lots of sad things happened. Her friend Firas died. Another guy named Gideon died. She did not know him very well except in the chat, but Crawler Carl was sad, because he had talked Gideon into helping them.

beats.headline: A really good singer
beats.text: Crawler Donut's account of the floor, set down for her fans, lists what went wrong. Firas died. Gideon died. Gwendolyn Duet died. This mushroom guy who was a really good singer died. She does not give his name. The Popov brothers died too, and then turned into babies and were kicked out of the game, which made everyone happy.

beats.headline: Huanxin, Uzzi, and what happened
beats.text: Chaco. Uzzi. A stairwell on the tenth floor that would not open until a god's spell hit the puzzle, and me volunteering to take the hit, because the only life it cost was mine. Odette found a cheaper way to pay. Huanxin Jinx was driving the storm goddess, and when she raised her price from a tenth of Odette's bonus to a third, Odette refused. She talked Chaco into putting the dart into my brother instead. The goddess died in the containment and the stairwell opened. I went through it. He did not.

beats.headline: Ten per cent, then fifty
beats.text: Nine puzzle pieces primed, a storm goddess coming through the acid rain, and the level about to collapse. Mordecai reaching the eleventh floor buys my freedom. Through Armita I have offered Huanxin Jinx ten per cent of that bonus. She wants thirty-three, then fifty, or she zeroes out the party. I tell Armita there is no deal. Mordecai means to spend himself on his Final Blow skill. I tell Chaco to worship Dodola and put the dart in Uzzi instead. He does. The goddess dies inside his containment, and the stairwell opens. I am free. Mordecai writes that he is going to find me and kill me.

beats.headline: Master Telephone Psychic
beats.text: I chose Cuba rather than the Bahamas, and that was strategy: they gave Carl a book about the Bahamas, which was quite obviously a trap. Then ten minutes to pick a class, which is an improvement. Mordecai offers me an Agony Urchin, which changes the way I look, so absolutely not, or Master Telephone Psychic. I pick Psychic. My map now sees the whole building, my intelligence goes up five points, and I get Brain Freeze, Bad Attitude and Why Are You Hitting Yourself?, which makes people stab themselves in the face. I keep the Viper Queen's poison spit, too.

beats.headline: The first newsletter
beats.text: The first newsletter of my one official fan club goes out, and I absolutely do not approve of the name the Donut Holes. I recap the last few floors as best I can: Signet's revenge, Mongo and Kiwi killing Vrah, the whole castle sent down with our army in it. Then the crime of the century. Tserendolgor got her hands on the pet show ballot box and handed Mongo's crown to her disgusting meatball pet. I want the footage pored over until someone finds the smoking gun. Remember to pay your dues. The Team Mongo Mommies tier is twenty credits a week extra.

beats.headline: Twenty flags, one logo
beats.text: The floor's announcement ends with a gift: each squad leader receives a set of twenty flags carrying the squad's logo, created by the system itself. Plant one in the body of a living entity below five percent health and it becomes something called a T'Ghee totem in the squad leader's inventory. Carl's breath catches; he knows the word from the Cookbook. Noncorporeal monsters count too, and a flagged monster becomes a minion of whoever summons it, obedient to a point. Lose the flags before the squad is full and they are not replaced.

beats.headline: Twenty flags a squad
beats.text: Floor announcement. Each squad leader receives twenty flags bearing a logo the system designed. Plant one in a living thing below five per cent health, noncorporeal included, and it becomes a T'Ghee totem, a minion of whoever summons it, obedient to a point depending on level and temperament. Rip the totem in two to dismiss it. Trade them, steal them. Lost flags are not replaced. Every surviving squad keeps one card when the floor collapses. Carl's breath catches: he knows the word from the Cookbook.

beats.headline: Like the stuffed animals
beats.text: Mordecai's gloss on the announcement: T'Ghee totems are like Bautista's stuffed animals, only in the form of large playing cards. Like Carl's tarot cards, actually. Reusable even when the summoned monster dies. He has seen them used a few different ways over the seasons, so they are going to have to wait for the next announcement. Carl, who has read Allister, notes that for its inventor T'Ghee was a religion and had nothing to do with capturing monsters.

beats.headline: Bored until the crawlers stop
beats.text: A scene from an old season, told from Odette's side, spells out the timing. The Ascendency battles do not start until the crawlers reach the twelfth floor or are zeroed out, and until then the sponsors are bored. Huanxin Jinx, who sponsored Dodola every season, was bored enough to sell a storm goddess's help to Odette's scheme, for a cut. Armita, a former party member of Odette's, had a job as a demigod attendant for the Celestial Ascendency and carried the messages, since the AI is legally forbidden to monitor Ascendency sponsor communications.

beats.headline: Guarding the last stairwell
beats.text: For the record, from a season long gone: tenth floor, collapse imminent, three crawlers at a stairwell, and a fourth still on his way back to it, that opens only when a storm god's magic touches a primed puzzle. Uzzi, skyfowl, Storm Commander, the class Mordecai once said his brother took on Odette's advice. He guards the others while Hold Steady keeps the puzzle primed and Chaco plays to draw the gods. His magic is limited. His party protection spell is what keeps the caustic rain off everyone. Odette notes that he chose the hardest of four paths, blindly.

beats.headline: See you on the other side
beats.text: The storm goddess is sponsored, and her sponsor has turned on them. Mordecai tells the group chat he has a plan and it will kill him; to Odette alone he explains it: his Final Blow skill can target the puzzle, so if the god hits him, the puzzle is hit too. "Uzzi, see you on the other side, brother." Uzzi's reply, in full: "Do not even dare." The brothers go back and forth while the timer falls. Odette knows that if Uzzi were told the other plan, he would be on board. There is no time to tell him.

beats.headline: The dart in his breast
beats.text: Chaco worships the goddess and tells Uzzi he is sorry. Uzzi turns to him, looks down at the Dart of Ophiotaurus in the bard's hand, lifts his head to the rain, and caws a war cry. He steps nearer the puzzle and spreads his wings. He understood. Chaco throws the dart into his breast and locks him in a containment with the puzzle. Mordecai arrives in ratkin form, falls to his knees at the shell, and calls his brother's name. The summoning tears Uzzi's chest open. Crawler Uzzi has fallen.

beats.headline: Apex Predator
beats.text: We haven't been in a real saferoom since before the party, so I've been sitting on dozens of achievements. A country boss achievement, for Imogen turning up in the convoy. The Scourge, for the most hands: a legendary box. Marked for Life, for surviving a god: a platinum apostate box. Then Apex Predator. Every hunter dead, and I killed the last one. Reward: nothing. Just kidding. A Celestial Predator Box. My hands shake. Donut got legendaries and wants to know why she didn't get a celestial when she helped kill a god. It wasn't for that.

beats.headline: Ten percent more
beats.text: In the Scab box, Donut receives an upgrade to her brush: the Enchanted Fur Brush of the Ecclesiastic now adds a further ten percent to her constitution, on top of the measly two points it normally gives for getting brushed each morning. The same haul brings a coupon for a free Town Upgrade and a skill potion for her Love Vampire skill.

beats.headline: Suspiciously good loot
beats.text: After the skipped floor, the feeds fill with crawlers opening very good boxes: an ice staff for Elle, a shape-changing ring for Bautista, a nipple ring and a summoning tome for Donut. Mordecai reads it two ways. Part of it is the AI compensating for the floor nobody got to play. But some of those boxes were earned before the skip, so it is likely a response to the Valtay ramping up the difficulty. More than a thousand crawlers also receive the identical box at the same moment and earn Collective Bargaining, whose citation promises to toughen up the rules.

beats.headline: A coupon with a flexed arm
beats.text: Among the prizes on the table sits a piece of paper printed with a buff, flexed arm: a mercenary coupon, good for 100,000 gold of mercenary services at any participating Meat Shields location. Crawler Carl asks what Meat Shields is. Mordecai shrugs. Probably the name of the mercenary markets on this floor: there is one in the Desperado and one in Club Vanquisher, and there was probably one in Larracos too. Which reminds him that the guildhall needs a mercenary training arcade.

beats.headline: Hills Cyclops, and a warning
beats.text: Hills Cyclops. Level fifty, pink, one eye, and the description has opinions about sheep. It still beats the ten minutes the seventh floor was open, when I was a slime with no arms. Now, the problem. Samantha flew back here and pushed through the brambles to the door. Withering spirits should not be able to do any of that. I don't understand it, which makes it extra dangerous. She won't shut up about the flesh golem in Carl's inventory. Kid, don't give it to her until we figure out why and how she is gaining this power.

beats.headline: From the Beguiler's box
beats.text: Carl laughs when Donut's Beguiler's box opens on a single shining nipple ring that glows red. This is not funny, Carl, she says. When she pulls it out, she calls it the most sexist description she has ever read. It may only be equipped on a female quadruped, and superior fire demons, the AI explains, are so crazy they must be chaperoned by hellspawn familiars, who use rings like this one. Worn, it allows the removal of cursed items, makes her impervious to natural fire and lava and resistant to fire spells, keeps her from losing health inside Sheol, and adds Intelligence per cent to every fire attack.

beats.headline: Bitch, What?
beats.text: Carl wants it on her right away. Mordecai agrees, but wants to talk about the spell first. Bitch, What? is a berserking spell, once every thirty hours: for twenty seconds Donut catches fire, is invulnerable to blunt damage, gets really angry and kills every goddamn thing in the room. Mordecai has seen it; the rage elemental lived in that state, and it is really called Fire Berserker. She is to cast it only when she is by herself. Her three fire spells, Fireball, Magic Missile and Wall of Fire, will all be much more intense. It is good, he says, but still not as good as her spellbook; and when Donut complains that she got no celestial box, he tells her the ring is practically a celestial.

beats.headline: A nipple ring and a screaming book
beats.text: No spellbook of the floor for the seventh, which is an outrage, only one for Mute. Then my boxes. A cosmic buff potion that gives me dexterity instead of charisma. A skill potion that takes Love Vampire from three to six and lets it cast on its own. A nipple ring from a superior fire demon's hand maiden, which has the most sexist description I have ever read, and a berserking spell I will not name that Mordecai says I may only cast by myself. And a chained, quivering tome that screams as I learn it: Legionnaires of the Damned. I have always been badass.

beats.headline: Fire Berserker
beats.text: Mordecai puts a name to the state the elementals live in permanently: a berserk, partly invulnerable condition that shrugs off blunt damage and turns whatever holds it on everything within reach. He notes the system has been renaming things more often than it used to.

beats.headline: Back, and wanting her body
beats.text: I FLEW BACK. Through the brambles and right up to the door, all by myself. Carl, my cousin gave you her mother, and her mother is a perfectly good body sitting in your inventory. We need a mage to animate her. A pulpmancer. Let's go right now! He says we just landed on a new floor and need to get our bearings first. I tell him I'm going to kill his mother. He says he won't help me if I keep threatening him. So I growl, and I go and chase Mongo.

beats.headline: Chained shut, and quivering
beats.text: Donut's De-Sleeving box holds 100,000 gold and a kind of spellbook Carl has never seen: thick as a dictionary, with a bumpy leather cover, chained shut with a lock, bouncing about on its own and giving off purple smoke. It reminds him of the spellbook in the Evil Dead movies, and Mordecai gasps. When Donut gives it an uncertain slap with her paw and asks why it is quivering, Mordecai says that happens sometimes with the more powerful tomes, especially summoning ones. In Carl's hands it is squishy and warm, and it wriggles like a puppy.

beats.headline: A little scream
beats.text: The spell reanimates weapons and armour with undead spirits plucked from the river of falling souls, and most of the gear disintegrates when it ends. Mordecai sees the combination at once: with Laundry Day at level fifteen, Donut can strip a group of mobs of their armour and turn it on them, full of wailing spirits. Carl slides the tome back to her. She glows as she applies it, and it lets out a little scream as it disappears in a puff of purple smoke.

beats.headline: The floor that broke
beats.text: Mordecai has the story of the broken seventh floor from Mistress Tiatha, and he puts it on the engineers: they built the level just like the fairytale, and the goat did what the kid in the story took thousands of years to figure out. The Valtay are likely irritated with the Borant designers. The Apothecary and the Plenty probably did well out of providing the means, at the cost of the Valtay and the Syndicate, because the Syndicate pays in advance for the tunnels that carry the livestream, and a skipped floor is not refunded.

beats.headline: A back patch of skulls
beats.text: The celestial predator box explodes into fireflies and leaves only a full-sized back patch: thick black fabric embroidered with a white pyramid of skulls, covered in clear stitching like fiberoptic wire. Carl has five patches already, the earth, the arrows, the bomb, the anti-vampire Midnight Epicure patch and a new peace symbol, and a back patch doubles the boost they give. What it does itself stays hidden until it is affixed and worn. He sews it on himself, Donut on his shoulder disapproving of every stitch. The angle of entry is crucial!

beats.headline: Swapped for a pushier shield
beats.text: A short black forearm bracer covered in little buckles comes out of Carl's boxes: the Enchanted Right Back Atcha Personal Shield, an overly enthusiastic auto buckler that catches physical and magical bolt attacks and can throw them back. He already wears two bracers, and the Peach Pit's disarm chance has never once worked for him. Mordecai calls the new one much better, and it matches his other bracer. Carl pulls the Enchanted Auto Buckler of the Peach Pit off his left arm and tosses it onto their growing pile of weapons and armour for the Faction Wars team.

beats.headline: The burn stays
beats.text: Katia's squad, Iceland. The burn on my face still hasn't healed. Neither Louis nor I have opened our boxes. I sit and hold on to Louis, and I don't stop crying. We are both still broken up about Firas. Katia is worried. She has asked Imani to come over and talk to me.

beats.headline: Needle, thread, and a bone key
beats.text: Donut critiques every stitch, so I send her off to read her fan boards and sew the celestial patch on myself, peace symbol first. It glows. My strength jumps, and a new bar appears under my mana: Soul Essence. Every patch bonus is doubled, plus twenty-five to strength and dexterity, and three benefits. Climb. Soul Reaper, which charges on melee kills and dumps it all into one attack. And a Mysterious Bone Key that opens any lock in the dungeon, destroys the jacket, and takes one of my bones to make the key. We're marking that one as a last resort.

beats.headline: A kit with the right parts
beats.text: Carl picks up a large steampunk chest, ridiculously heavy, and lifts the lid. The description comes in a different voice, like a television commercial: Doctor Ratchet's Automaton Build-It Kit, enough items for over fifteen automatons, fun for the whole family, from personal servants to flame-throwing sentinel droids. It lists dozens of parts, and Carl recognises several of them as things he needs for recipes in the instructional book he stole from the production facility. Excellent, he says.

beats.headline: Mean, and liked
beats.text: Filed for the survivors. Tran, who lost both legs in the final moments of the previous floor, is more upset about losing subject than the legs, according to Crawler Katia; they had been together since early on. He does not answer Crawler Carl's note. Princess Donut's eulogy, delivered straight after the fight, begins: poor Gwen, she was mean, but I liked her.

beats.headline: Worried about Britney
beats.text: We are in Iceland. Florin left the party just before the last level broke, and I have been asking where he is. My box gave me something that lets me move very fast. Louis and Britney have not opened theirs; they are still broken up about Firas. The burn on Britney's face still has not healed, and she has not stopped crying. She sits there, holding onto Louis. I have already asked Imani to come over. We will see if it helps.

beats.headline: Drain it every time
beats.text: Divine items are the best items, kid, whatever the debuffs. And yes, there is somebody in my room. With the upgraded quarters I was able to hire a room attendant. It's not important. Concentrate on your sewing; you can ruin the item. Then Soul Reaper comes up. Oh, it's good. It's also more dangerous than Donut's berserking spell. Drain the essence bar each time it fills, and don't store the stuff for long. I once saw a crawler fill her reserve with gorgons and kill a country boss with a single attack. It turned to stone and shattered.

beats.headline: The apostate's box
beats.text: The platinum apostate box, earned for not getting killed by Diwata, holds a ring. A nipple ring. Donut is triumphant: now that his nipples are full, there are other places he is not pierced yet. It is silver, with an eyeball hanging from it, and only a crawler marked for death by a god may wear it. Li Na could already do everything it does. Its spell, Black Nimbus, pulls a target out of their deity's blessing and keeps them out of church. Lots of divinity-themed items, says Mordecai, and that is never good.

beats.headline: Buzz off, dirty hippie
beats.text: In the line of boxes from the last floor, the gold pacifist's box holds a small upgrade patch for Carl's jacket, a round peace symbol, and Donut scoffs at the quality. It is almost the size of his earth patch, black with a white, screen-printed peace symbol. The description tells him to buzz off, dirty hippie, and says the Grateful Dead sucked, and so does Phish. Carl calls that unnecessarily rude. Donut does not like Phish either: Angel the cocker spaniel's owner was always listening to them.

beats.headline: Sewn on first
beats.text: Before the celestial back patch goes on, Carl sews the peace symbol onto the bottom of his jacket next to the bomb symbol. He does the small one first, to be doubly certain the back patch's effect catches every regular patch. It is his fifth, after the earth symbol, the arrows, the bomb symbol and the anti-vampire Midnight Epicure patch, and every patch on the jacket adds one point to all his stats.

beats.headline: Stick and poke
beats.text: The Gold Quest Box for the Vengeance of the Daughter opens, and Carl recognises what comes out at once. Donut asks, with disgust, whether it is what she thinks. It is: a stick and poke tattoo kit, the same items Edgar the tortoise used to put magical tattoos on Tsarina Signet. A long, sharp needle, some ink, a few stick things, and something that looks like sandpaper. He has no idea how any of it works, and the description, about doing time, is no help. What is he supposed to do with this?

beats.headline: Swapped for the Peach Pit
beats.text: Among the box prizes is a forearm bracer, black, short and covered with little buckles. Carl already has two: the one that forms his Grull gauntlet, and the one on his left arm that forms a buckler meant to disarm opponents 1.5 percent of the time, which he has never got to work. This one auto-deploys a small buckler that catches physical attacks and magic bolts, with a 75 percent chance to reflect them and a 25 percent chance to double the reflection. Mordecai says it is much better, and it matches the other bracer. Off comes the Auto Buckler of the Peach Pit, onto the pile for the Faction Wars team.

beats.headline: A pile of skulls, stacked nice and neat
beats.text: Out of the celestial predator box, opened in the same haul as a prison tattoo kit and a crafting table kit: a divine back patch for Carl's jacket, its benefits varying with whichever deities and certain demons happen to be near. The upgrades it carries stay hidden until it is affixed and worn.

beats.headline: A floating chair
beats.text: Final moments of the last floor, I lost my legs. And Gwen. We'd been together since early on. Bautista is with me, helping. I open my boxes. The pacifist box has a floating wheelchair, the same sort Odette used to zip around in when she was in human form. Carl sends a note asking if I'm okay. I don't answer.

beats.headline: The squad's flag
beats.text: Every squad on this level gets a bundle of small flags to stick into the monsters, and nobody gets to design their own. The Royal Court's flag is a little bigger than Carl's hand, and it is an actual miniature pair of heart-covered boxers flying sideways, as if from a clothesline, with the Royal Court of Princess Donut embroidered top and bottom like a motorcycle-club patch and Carl's bomb patch over the crotch. Carl finds it tacky. Elle says her squad's flag has a bag of adult diapers on it, Donut reports, and Imani's has a butterfly, and she wants to know why they couldn't get something like that.

beats.headline: On the court's flag
beats.text: The Royal Court's capture flag is a little bigger than Carl's hand, and it is a miniature pair of heart-covered boxers flying sideways, as if off a clothesline. The court's name is embroidered top and bottom in motorcycle-club style, and centred over the crotch is a bomb patch identical to the one on Carl's jacket. It really is tacky. Imani's squad got a butterfly, Donut complains, and the stitching looks as if Carl sewed it.

beats.headline: Freshly upgraded, still waiting
beats.text: Before heading out into Old Havana, Carl wants to get into the craft room and play with his new automaton pieces, and his bomber's studio has just been upgraded, so he wants to go in there too. Mordecai is already making noises about the crafting table upgrade coupons. Carl tells him they should get their bearings first, and goes back to ring the exit stairwell with traps instead.

beats.headline: Two stairwells, not far
beats.text: Subject is the last of the four cretin bodyguards still with the clients; the other three went down with the high elf castle. Services this morning: loaded his stairwell teleport, still on cooldown, to read the stairwell locations, and reported two, not far, still in the big city near the coast. Assigned to map the area on paper with Mordecai and to remain in the saferoom. Offered, as consideration, a GameCube controller. Response: a noncommittal grunt. Observed condition: depressed, possibly lonely, possibly missing the Sledge.

beats.headline: The world we lost
beats.text: We open the doors on a warm, humid morning in Old Havana, and it hits me like a sledgehammer. This is what we lost. Cars, scooters, a yellow Ford Fairlane, people everywhere. A ghost kicks Donut down the stairs and walks on without his trousers. I take his wallet and his phone, and the underwear too; I want as small a footprint as possible near the saferoom. Then a monster with a wolf's body and a Che Guevara head charges us, barking like a man with a megaphone. The Experience, level fifty-five. Donut barely has to lift a paw.

beats.headline: In a mob's inventory
beats.text: The Experience is dead, and Donut finds a card thing in its inventory, though she thought cards only came from flagging monsters. It is the size of a postcard, rigid but papery, the Syndicate's logo moving on its back and a red stylised plus floating in a field of stars on its face.
