My first opponent is an old man called Robert the Human, in a sailor suit much too small for him, with a doll and a stuffed dog for totems. I summon Geraldo. Then Mongo bites his throat, and it is over. The first thing I take is his hat.

beats.headline: Odette tells her side of it
beats.text: Odette tells Carl the story in her own words, fast, with Lexis warning her the time is short: an illegal deal with Huanxin, brokered by Armita; a price raised; a deal broken at the last second; a goddess trapped in a containment, then killed by Chaco. Mordecai made the next floor, she says. Uzzi, Mordecai's brother, died. Since then she has watched him every chance she could, drinking himself into oblivion, crying over his brother. Her own verdict: this one I broke.

beats.headline: Iowa, stacked on a reef
beats.text: Donut's Torch goes up like a stadium light and shows me what is west of us: a sheer wall of crumbling earth, taller than I can see, wider than the island, dirt already sliding off into the sea. The key is on top of it. I tell Zev this is a cay, an island built on a reef, and that pile will be washed away in a day. Zev says they are aware. The first opponent of our own is a Babababoon in a Santa hat, standing frozen in the light of a parking lot. One sticky hob-lobber. Token number two.

beats.headline: Nice dixie cup
beats.text: Donut wears the white sailor hat cockeyed on her head, and it looks ridiculous. Nice dixie cup, Carl says: she looks like she is in the navy. She thinks it divine. It costs her the new Hover skill and ten intelligence, but she has talked to Mordecai: she will wear it until she runs out of cards, then put her new dragonfly tiara back on. It lowers the card-draw countdown by two seconds, and it is quite jaunty. Carl did not know there was magic gear made for the cards.

beats.headline: The agreement stands
beats.text: The adjutant arrangement did not happen the way I laid it out. Odette never asked for the chair. I send Carl a message and tell him plainly that this was out of his control, and that I will honour our agreement. I also tell him what happens if I learn he warned Odette about it: I will crush everyone he knows and loves, beginning with Katia and ending with the cat. Both halves of that are sincere. Gods trade down here, and he knows now exactly what he is standing in.

beats.headline: Not really them
beats.text: Belgium. I don't know anybody in Belgium, thank God. Imani's in Detroit and I'm not with her; my squad and I landed on our own, and everybody else is scattered to the four winds. So I tell the lot of them what needs telling. Keep your wits about you. These are just memory ghosts. If they're going to make us fight loved ones, remember it isn't really them. Don't let them mess with your heads.

beats.headline: Do not be gentle
beats.text: Nekhebit has returned to the halls. She holds an ancient grudge against my family, and against Apito most of all, and so the quest to find out who killed my son moves forward. I set the man a task: find a temple of Nekhebit and put questions to the priestess there. See what she knows. I have one further instruction, and I give it plainly. Do not be gentle.

beats.headline: Sticky, against a Santa hat
beats.text: Carl has been working on sticky bombs for a while, and took the adhesive problem into the production facility's bomber's studio on the sixth floor. In a card-game combat against a wide-faced man in a Santa hat, Carl pulls a sticky hob-lobber into his xistera and throws it across the way. It splotches against the man's chest and explodes, killing him before he draws his first card. Donut's complaint is that Carl blew up his hat.

beats.headline: Detroit, and nobody asked
beats.text: Everyone checks in; I make sure of it. We are scattered. Elle's squad is in Belgium, and I am not with them. Florin is in eastern Nigeria and has lost contact with Lucia Mar. Li Jun's crew is further into mainland China. Prepotente, after some prodding, is somewhere in northern Italy. I was given one choice: Detroit. It is where I grew up, and I would never have picked it. My key location is in the home of somebody I know. I do not elaborate.

beats.headline: Da Nang
beats.text: Carl says we need to talk. I cannot right now: they gave me one choice in the selection, Ukraine, and when I arrived it was Vietnam. He tells me to message him when I am safe. When Imani has everyone check in, it is both: my region is a mix of the two, and the Vietnam part is a city called Da Nang. It is where Tran is from. The key location is an apartment building, and both his ex-wife and his estranged mother live in it. I warn the others, so that nobody walks into it unwarned.

beats.headline: The dixie cup
beats.text: My choices had labels, and I picked Miami, and then it said there was a problem and it was sending us to Iowa, and we landed in the Florida Keys with the key still in Iowa. I do not like glitches. They make me nervous. At least I have the dead man's sailor hat. Carl says it is a dixie cup, and that I cannot Hover in it and it costs ten intelligence. But it lowers my card draw countdown by two seconds, and it is quite jaunty. I already discussed it with Mordecai. I will wear it until I run out of cards.

beats.headline: Off, for the sailor hat
beats.text: Wearing a dead man's sailor hat means giving up her new Hover skill and ten intelligence, Carl points out. Donut has already talked to Mordecai about it: she will wear the hat until she runs out of cards, then put her new dragonfly tiara back on. The hat lowers the draw countdown by two seconds, and it is quite jaunty.

beats.headline: Four choices, and a mountain
beats.text: Okay, so. Carl and Princess Donut, I apologise for that glitch, and I know it is going to look intentional. It was not. At least not on our end. You should have had three choices: one of ours, one of the AI's, one random. You had four. Some crawlers had one, a few had none, and one squad leader had the whole globe and dropped herself into the middle of the ocean. And yes, the key location was taken out of Iowa and set down on your island. It was the only way to do it without breaking anything further. We're very busy.

beats.headline: Half of Lazarus-A-Bang-Bang
beats.text: The card gets played. Asojano and Uzi Jesus combine into a single totem, Lazarus-A-Bang-Bang, which is either the best or the worst thing to happen to a former god of disease. I have decided not to rule on which.

beats.headline: What the Combo made
beats.text: Church organ music, fat digital cherubs and a herd of digital street dogs herald the card Donut made with the Combo: Uzi Jesus and Asojano in one, the most over-the-top reveal of all their cards. What rises from the smoke is a dirty, sandalled, robed figure, hunched and sickly, a green-tinted nimbus round his head and his weapon used as a walking stick. Level 140, like Uzi Jesus. The card names him Lazarus-A-Bang-Bang, created via Combo.

beats.headline: Frozen with its buffs
beats.text: Church organ music, fat digital cherubs and a herd of digital street dogs: the new totem's reveal is the craziest of all their cards. After the fight Carl reads its orange card. Unique. Lazarus-A-Bang-Bang. Level 140. Created via Combo, and frozen in place via a Glow-Up with active buffs, its available utility slots lowered as a result. Summoning duration two hundred seconds; Constitution eighty.

beats.headline: To build his self-confidence
beats.text: Raul the crab is chasing a screeching ghost, a Reef Explorer, through the dark trees, and Lazarus wants to end it himself: that pansy is taking too long. Donut discards a card and tosses a Greased Lightning at Raul. It spins off like a ninja star, dodges a tree and hits the crab in a sparkle of digital confetti. Lazarus is to stay and protect her; Raul needs the experience. Raul snaps at the ghost, and when it tries to run behind a tree the speed-enhanced crab snaps again and cuts its leg off. It drops dead.

beats.headline: Swordfish
beats.text: FISH FLIES AT CARL. MONGO JUMPS. CATCH. GROUND SHAKES. FISH FLOP. THEN BUGS. SHINY BUGS. BAD. BAD. MONGO BACKS AWAY.

beats.headline: Amateur hour
beats.text: It is the sixth fight before I have to use the deck at all. I summon our combo, Lazarus-A-Bang-Bang, with his cherubs and his street dogs and his organ music, and his bazooka shoots beetles. He points it at Carl. I tell him to put it down. Then I let Raul finish the ghost, for his self-confidence. The Reef Explorer drew two of his four totems and carried thirty Precision cards, which ruined his deck; he needed the perfect draw. Amateur hour. Lazarus calls everybody a pansy. I think MaeMae is jealous of his reveal sequence.

beats.headline: Greased Lightning on a ghost
beats.text: Deckmaster fight on the road to Key West. A level-65 Reef Explorer in a glowing deep-dive suit is a ghost, and only magic hurts him. Donut summons Raul, who bows, sits, chants, and sets off after the fleeing creature with a glowing claw. Lazarus calls him a pansy for taking too long; Donut throws him a Greased Lightning instead of sending in the bazooka, to build his self-confidence. The speeded crab snaps the ghost's leg off, and the suit deflates. Donut reports that Raul and Geraldo are finally tolerating each other.

beats.headline: Nearly full
beats.text: Six tokens in, the soul bar for Carl's back patch is almost full, and he has a persistent itch at his neck he suspects is the bar's doing. He has felt no obvious ill effect from the patch, only unease each time the bar nears the top. One or two more kills would let him disperse the power. He holds it instead: spent now, the bar would not refill in time for whatever guards the key, not with only deckmasters to kill on the way.

beats.headline: Five in a Silver Spam box
beats.text: Donut's rewards are mostly card moves from her first and last fights; Carl's are mostly bronze adventurer boxes. The Silver Spam box holds a pile of scrolls, five Scrolls of Build Trench, its description hoping he is up on the fighting techniques of the first world war. Each lays a permanent trench two point three metres deep and two wide, its length set by his intelligence plus strength, and scrolls combine into reinforced sleeping quarters and other front-line accessories. He puts them away and waits for the Prepotente box to open.

beats.headline: You will not break me
beats.text: Somebody on Donut's feed says they will drop it if she keeps being so whiny. I turn the screen off before she sees it, light her candle, and we take an old-fashioned nap in the chair. She sleeps. I cannot. I think of Mordecai at his table and the baggage he carries, heavier each year. Odette and her guilt. Frank Q, the Ring of Divine Suffering, and how crushed he said he felt. Just like Donut. Just like me. I think of the climb, and the man I know I will find up there. You will not break me.

beats.headline: Never put away
beats.text: Carl clicks a screen of viewer comments off, with Donut snuggled in his arm. Her candle sits right by the screen, and beside it the photograph of Bea and Brad, which she has never put away. That's okay. Carl pushes the photo aside, pulls a lighter and lights the candle, and the scent of home fills the room.

beats.headline: Christmas on the island
beats.text: Okay so, it's Christmas Eve down here, man, and I want to know if we're all getting together once midnight passes. Carl says it isn't really Christmas, it's like early March or something. Oh man, really? It feels like we've been here a year. Donut says Carl hadn't even put his tree away when everything happened. Still, we should do something. Maybe we could give each other presents. Imani says let's make sure we all get our keys first.

beats.headline: Stuck at fourteen
beats.text: Among more achievements than he expected is one for killing a swordfish guy with his foot, worth a bronze spicy box. Carl's Smush base is now level twelve. His bonus for using the pedicure kit supposedly raises it three more, but the skill is still listed as fourteen. As always, skills go wonky when item buffs try to push them toward fifteen. And these card fights are paying seriously padded experience.

beats.headline: What if you die?
beats.text: The man in the diving suit had a strategy that could have worked, and I did not see it coming. There are thousands of cards and we do not know what they have. It is not fair. What happens if Carl dies? What would I do? And if something happened to me, what would Mongo do? I do not like being in charge of the deck. In that room by myself I thought I would never see him again. And we are losing Katia no matter what happens, and nobody talks about it. Sometimes I cannot breathe.

beats.headline: You talk in your sleep
beats.text: Everyone in the guild is asleep in a heap, strippers and changeling children, soaked from a water balloon fight. Not me. I go to say something and Carl shushes me and PATS MY HEAD, so I snap at him. Then he sleeps in a chair in Donut's room, and the social media board is right there, and I get it turned back on, because it has things to read. LET ME READ IT, or I will find your mother. He wakes up. I tell him the truth. He talks in his sleep.

beats.headline: Cascadia's Turquoise Taco
beats.text: Millions of work hours went into this floor's cards, crawler. Artists, engineers and writers, flesh and artificial, balancing a game thousands of you can play at once and the viewers can stand to watch. And Mudskipper Cascadia, the recently divorced executive producer, humiliated over the last floor and unable to control what is happening on the ninth, is on the edge. Right there. So imagine how she feels when you monkeys keep ending her carefully set-up fights before either side draws a single card. Reward: a Gold Prepotente Box.

beats.headline: Millions of work hours
beats.text: An achievement, at length. Borant's proposal for this season included an outline of the eighth floor as a T'Ghee card game; artists, engineers and writers spent millions of work hours designing and balancing it for thousands of players at once, and Cascadia, the executive producer, is on the edge. Most crawlers keep ending card fights before either side draws. Crawler Carl's review: a half-assed YuGiOh! ripoff duct-taped together on an Adderall bender, and no card game is fair when players draw from different pools.

beats.headline: The sniper on the hill
beats.text: Subject's group tried what nearly everybody tried: kill the deckmaster before the fight begins. She posted a long-range man with an old-school sling and a targeting spell on a hill overlooking the frozen opponent. The moment combat started, the spell failed and the opponent moved a meter to the left, spoiling the shot. He killed it anyway, a minute on. Elsewhere, traps ringed around frozen deckmasters simply vanished at the start, and crawlers standing inside the ring were knocked unconscious.

beats.headline: Out of a Gold Prepotente Box
beats.text: Donut has just told Carl she is frightened and does not want to be in charge. Carl opens a Gold Prepotente Box and finds a book he cannot trade, cannot destroy and cannot throw away. Drop it and it is back in his inventory. It is named for the pin boards at old conventions, and the System goes out of its way to say that this is the only reason.

beats.headline: Orders from a distance
beats.text: At the door of the turkey barn Carl tells Donut to get Clockwork Triplicate ready and pull out her microphone, and the headset poofs onto her head. She cannot cast while her deck is summoned, and her bard songs will not work either, because they must be activated from her interface. But they have found that with the headset on she can still amplify her voice and give orders from a distance.

beats.headline: Two rules, broken at once
beats.text: The moment combat starts I get a warning: my equipped cloak has aggravated the Nightgaunt. I throw a quarter hob-lobber at invisible monsters on a roof in an unstable environment, breaking both of our rules at once, and a truck slides off the mountain. The demon never plays a card. It only wants me, or my cloak. Mordecai warned me it would; he did not say how much. Token seven. Walking to the barn afterward, my arms are shaking, and I hold my left hand with my right and pretend they are not.

beats.headline: Beware, little children
beats.text: Summoning record. Donut plays Jola against the Visitor, a level-70 deckmaster hiding invisible with half a dozen Quench Moths. The sky goes black; digital snow; fake Christmas lights on the trailers. A lumpy yellow candle the size of a garbage can lights on top of the totem's head and reveals everything hidden. Jola is not floating. He is just huge: a fat, hairy, dirty-brown Persian cat the size of a house, bigger than Shi Maria, with a 75-second timer. The System's introduction ends on severed toddler tongue.

beats.headline: Words nobody can read
beats.text: The moths dive into his candle. The Nightgaunt, maddened by Crawler Carl's nightgaunt cloak, never plays a card. Jola asks it something in Icelandic, twice, slams it to the ground with a paw, shakes it dead in his jaws and eats it. Then his yellow eyes settle on Carl, he says three more sentences nobody present understands, and he disappears into dust. Donut's summary: the candle sees invisible things, nakedness and children make him stronger, and Katia says the fairy tale got him wrong. The real Yule Cat is a grump. This one is a serial killer.

beats.headline: Ten of them, from a Nightgaunt
beats.text: Deckmaster number seven of ten is a Nightgaunt, and Carl's cloak aggravates it so much that it ignores its own deck to try spells on him until Jola slams it to the ground and kills it. It drops thirty cards. Eighteen are totems, one a legendary Demon Queen and the rest Quench Moths, which gain speed and constitution when touching a light. Ten are consumable snare cards, all called Lamp: each paralyses a totem for ten seconds and makes it glow brightly. Played, snares and moths would have made a hard fight. Carl and Donut take the token and all the cards they can, and leave the totems.

beats.headline: Turkeys
beats.text: SO MUCH FOOD. MONGO EATS HEADS. MOTHER SAYS BAD. MOTHER SAYS COME HERE. MORE FOOD. ONE TURKEY NOT FOOD. BITE. BITE. NOTHING. DARK.

beats.headline: A Nightgaunt sees the cloak
beats.text: Combat starts by a dilapidated farmhouse, and a warning with it: Carl's equipped cloak has aggravated the Nightgaunt. The System explains that a Nightgaunt is a real creature, semi-intelligent, peaceful, vegetarian and nocturnal, which the game uses as a demon because, well, look at them. Mordecai had warned Carl the cloak would aggravate this kind of mob, but Carl had not realized how passionately. The demon never plays a single card. It glares at the cloak and screeches one last time, until a giant cat picks it up in his jaws and shakes it to death.

beats.headline: Jola the Yule Cat
beats.text: There is a big bat thing over a farmhouse with a swarm of invisible moths, and they are invisible and naked, so I summon the card Katia gave me. Jola. Snow, Christmas lights, a dirge, and a candle the size of a garbage can on the head of a house-sized Persian. The candle shows everything invisible, and the moths fly straight into it. Jola pins the Nightgaunt and eats him. Katia says they got the fairy tale all wrong: the real Yule Cat is a grump, and this one is quite the serial killer. It makes me wish our whole deck was cats.

beats.headline: Spiked, into a wing
beats.text: Turkeys are piling over one another to reach them, Donut is standing on the passed-out Mongo, and Carl cannot even cast Protective Shell. He pulls a banger sphere, one of his spiked ones, and launches it at the boss turkey up in the rafters. Tom squawks and tries to dodge. The ball smacks into a wing and breaks it with an audible crack. Carl pulls another, but Tom drops from the high rafter and disappears into the mass of turkeys surging toward them.

beats.headline: They starve us
beats.text: Sharp-Elbows rolls into me like a truck, and her spikes go through my arms, stomach, legs, neck and both of my eyes. I am blind, drinking potions, her rotted teeth against mine. She whispers. They starve us. When we are not here, we are there, and there they make certain the hunger festers. You can stop it. You can satiate us all, Carl. Then Raul snaps her staff, a Heal gives me my sight back, and her eyes are right there, pleading, sad, afraid. I have seen those eyes before. Raul takes her head.

beats.headline: Under eight seconds
beats.text: In a card duel under the heat lamps, Donut holds a single card when another appears in her hand, giving her two. The next will come in just under eight seconds, thanks to her sailor hat, while the turkey guard roars, charges toward Carl, and turns gobbling on Skylar Spinach when the snake smacks him with its tail.

beats.headline: A note from the tenth floor
beats.text: Subject's note in the Cookbook, twenty-second edition: since reaching the tenth floor he noticed mobs embracing death, a joy or curiosity that appears only at the very end, once they know they are beaten, and frustration too. His theory, offered as possibly unhinged: the voice that runs this world, stranger and stranger in its words and rulings, is moving into the minds of the monsters at the point of death, trying to know what it is to lose everything, failing, and trying again. He wished he could steer it into one of the nagas.

beats.headline: Onto Skylar Spinach
beats.text: Donut's active deck for the turkey barn holds two Greased Lightning cards. Her first totem is Skylar Spinach, who floats up toward the middle of the battlefield, and at the same moment she casts The Thief at the ogre, pulling a card out of the ogre's hand into her own deck. Weren't expecting that, were ya, she calls with autotuned glee, as she tosses a Greased Lightning onto Skylar.

beats.headline: The heat lamps
beats.text: A card duel, two lizard temple guards summoned onto the field, and Carl reaches for a hob-lobber and examines it before he throws, as he should. Warning: the current environment may cause this to explode prematurely. In fact, just holding it could be bad for your health. A five-second timer appears over it, and he puts it away fast. It is the heat lamps. They are there on purpose, designed specifically to fuck with his bombs. His weakest, a sixteenth-strength, had already gone off early.

beats.headline: The ring that burns
beats.text: Field note from a turkey barn. Crawler Carl ends a deck fight pierced in several places, wrapped in a dead ogre's bear hug and loaded with debuffs, among them one called Bonked. The ring on his finger burns. It looks like his strength ring. It is not. Pater Coal secretly helped him buy it at Club Vanquisher, it is meant to hold certain debuffs at bay, and Carl was warned that it could get overloaded. He cannot take it off.

beats.headline: Three seconds
beats.text: The idolized turkeys come for me, and I stand on Mongo, who is out cold, and slash at them. Then Carl kicks a hole in the mountain and the barn starts sliding off it, and I dig my back claws into Mongo so he does not go over. When it ends, Carl is dangling off a pole over the edge, and when he puts the dead ogre away, blood comes out of him everywhere. I jump to his shoulder and tell Mongo to run. Hang on, Carl. Three seconds. Puddle Jump.

beats.headline: This insignificant cur is here
beats.text: Crawler Carl is blind, pierced and caught in a bear hug by Sharp-Elbows, an ogre necromancer and deckmaster nine of ten, in a collapsing barn full of turkeys. Master Carl, comes the cry, this insignificant cur is here to rescue you. Raul snaps her necro staff in half, killing her last totem, and a Heal gives Carl his sight back. The ogre's eyes are right there, pleading. Raul snaps again and takes her head, and tumbles away in a rain of turkeys.

beats.headline: A hole in the world
beats.text: The Ralphie card has dispelled every spell and muted every minion, and Carl counts as a minion. Then the patch fills: The Scavenger's Daughter has been fed. He cannot cast, but this is a skill, and it lets him. He jumps, aims a foot at Tom, and the turkey looks up and asks, 'Gobble?' The kick feels like a hole in the world. Tom is obliterated with everything around him, the north wall bows out, and the ground tilts toward the cliff. The whole barn begins to slide.

beats.headline: The Worm Fulcrum
beats.text: In the turkey barn, to the riff of a Muse song, a small tree rises out of the floor: gnarled roots and leaves, feathers and turkey claws, a black human heart beating on a branch, and on top the golden skull of a large lizard with gems for eyes. The ogre deckmaster Sharp Elbows tosses her walking staff aside and yanks the tree out of the ground, spewing earthworms. The AI announces a Necro card combined with a Walking Stick totem. Donut protests that it is both a totem and a mystic card. Purple light spreads, and the dead turkeys rise.

beats.headline: Snapped by a crab
beats.text: Carl kicks the turkey deckmaster to pieces, and the barn starts to slide toward the cliff. The ogre, still clutching her staff, slams into him like a truck and holds on, her spikes in him, her face against his. Then a loud crack of wood, and the music stops: Raul the crab has snapped the necro staff in half, killing her last totem. He decapitates the ogre next.

beats.headline: Onto the stolen warrior
beats.text: Donut's active deck for the turkey barn holds two Stout cards. Late in the fight, with zombie turkeys rising, she is distracted, slicing at one that moves to chomp onto the unconscious Mongo. She tosses a new card, but it is a Stout, and she tosses it onto her stolen lizard temple warrior, who keeps screaming about his mother. Then Carl runs at the turkey deckmaster, and his kick obliterates it.

beats.headline: Observing things
beats.text: Tom is a magic-using turkey whose god was tossed into the Nothing, escaped, and was slain by a goat. Did you know farm turkeys are bred white so that those holding the butcher knife need not face their own revulsion at the pin feathers? No point to that. Just an observation. I have been doing that a lot lately. Noticing things. And when Carl asks for the normal descriptions, fine: Sharp-Elbows. Blah, blah, basically a necromancer. I make them long for him, because of our special connection, and he does not appreciate it.

beats.headline: Out of the ogre's hand
beats.text: Donut opens the turkey-barn fight with Skylar Spinach and, at the same moment, casts her mystic card, The Thief, at the ogre, who is in the middle of summoning a card of her own. The card poofs out of the ogre's hand and appears in Donut's deck. Weren't expecting that, were ya, Donut calls with autotuned glee, as she tosses a Greased Lightning onto Skylar.

beats.headline: Say hi to dad
beats.text: I wake from the river and the ogre's eyes, and Donut is talking too fast and too stiff, offering to fight the keyholder alone. Then she tells me why. The motorcycle. She saw how it hit me when it came around on the prize carousel, and she knows who is in that trailer. I remind her of Ferdinand, how badly I wanted to skip the Masquerade, and that if we had, even more people would have died. And don't try to be like me, I tell her. You need to be like you. Let's go say hi to dad.

beats.headline: Not consumable
beats.text: Carl's head is starting to clear, and Donut reels off the haul. They got another combo card, a unique one called Golden Combo: it works the same way as the last, but it is not consumable, so she can do it over and over. Imagine the possibilities. With the new cards, she says, she is pretty much indestructible, and maybe she can do this last fight by herself. Carl asks whether that is a joke. Not even a little bit.

beats.headline: Donut knows the bike
beats.text: Donut has worked out who the keyholder will be before Carl has, and the second clue is the motorcycle: the same one he was offered on the prize carousel on the fourth floor, with the big dent in it. She remembers how it affected him, though he said nothing at the time. Now it is sitting outside a trailer, and she just knows his father will be inside. She is trying to be more like Carl, she says, and not give them the satisfaction.

beats.headline: I could do this one alone
beats.text: Carl is out for forty minutes, and I tell him so. I collected every card Sharp-Elbows dropped: her staff, which holds one of my spells, and a Golden Combo, a unique that is not consumable. So I suggest I do the last fight by myself. Or we skip it. He asks if I would rather fight other crawlers than get the key, and no, I suppose not. The truth is the motorcycle. It is the one from the prize carousel on the fourth floor, with the dent, and it is outside that trailer. I am trying to be more like him.

beats.headline: In Donut's deck
beats.text: While Carl was out, Donut grabbed every card left floating at the edge of the fight, and Sharp Elbows had a lot. The magical staff card is in their deck now. It is a special card but not consumable; it takes no totem slot, though it holds a card slot while active. She must imbue it with one of her spells before a fight, and can then cast that spell once. The staff works like a totem and looks different depending on the spell. She has already set it up and tried it on Geraldo, and they all started fighting each other until she yelled at them.

beats.headline: A yard from last summer
beats.text: The vending machine wants nine tokens for one fight, and it carries his silhouette. His Harley is in the yard, a 1965 Electra Glide Panhead with expired Georgia plates, the thing he never shut up about. Everything up here was under snow this morning, but this yard has weeds and flowers and dust, and a kid's bike cut in half at the property line. It is spliced in from another time. Summer, maybe. They want me to see something. I pick up the motorcycle, and it does not go into the temporary items. It is mine.

beats.headline: His motorcycle in an Iowa yard
beats.text: A single-wide trailer in a junkyard on a floating chunk of Iowa, and a vending machine bearing his silhouette: One Fight for Nine Tokens. Princess Donut thinks it is a fatter Carl with a mustache. In the yard stands the motorcycle, Georgia plates expired years ago, his prized possession. Carl lifts it easily, remembering how heavy it was the day he knocked it over. The yard is summer spliced into December, and along one side runs a row of alliums in pots, labelled in an elegant, feminine hand. His father would never have done that.

beats.headline: Into Carl's inventory
beats.text: In the trailer's yard the Harley is dirty and dusty, its leather seat cracked, weeds growing round its tyres, its Georgia plates expired years ago. Carl knows nothing about it except that it is a collector's item, that his father never shut up about it, and that it was his prized possession. He picks it up easily, remembering how heavy it was the day he knocked it over. It goes into his inventory, not into the temporary category like everything else from this floor, but in with the royal chariot and the bicycles: Shitty Transportation Items.

beats.headline: He does not have to go in
beats.text: The silhouette on the machine looks like a fatter Carl with a mustache. The nose is quite identical, and Carl tells me never to say that again. He takes everything in the yard he can lift, even the pieces of half a minivan, and I do not say a word. There is other stuff at the far side of the yard, and I do not say anything about that either. At the door I tell him he can wait out here with me; he does not have to go in. He says he needs to. So I wait.

beats.headline: The boy behind the hospital bed
beats.text: Subject: a boy of perhaps six, in a recording from the summer before the collapse. He stays behind the hospital bed, out of his father's sightline, and asks whether he can watch television now. Told to fetch cigarettes, he runs. "Asher! Get back here you little shit!" The photographs on the curio: a one-year-old on his father's lap, and a recent one with brown hair enough for two people, blue eyes, and that nose. Crawler Carl's conclusion takes four words: I had a brother.

beats.headline: Crayon drawings of lightning storms
beats.text: While his mother is busy with the syringe, Asher lies on his bed running a matchbox car up and down the wall. Crawler Carl tells him he is sorry he did not know, and that he is not forgotten. His hand goes through the boy's head. He takes the toys and the crayon drawings, airplanes and storm clouds whose lightning destroys whole cities, and concludes the boy is scared of storms. He leaves the heart-shaped candy box. His mother hugs him and mentions a birthday party. "Am I going to get a bike?" "We'll see, honey."

beats.headline: Asher
beats.text: He is in a hospital bed in the living room, maybe a hundred and forty pounds, yellow, cursing a Mariners game. Twelve years, and it looks like forty. Then a boy looks around the hallway corner. Six, maybe. That nose, those eyes, that hair. The boy wants the TV; my father wants his cigarettes, and yells after him to get back here, you little shit. Asher. His name is Asher. On the curio there is a photo of him on my father's lap, one year old. I have a brother.

beats.headline: Exactly what I needed to see
beats.text: My stepmother has been hiding morphine in the flowerpots. I lean in closer to him than I have ever been and tell him he is a bully, that two women tried to kill him, that nobody will care. I will not watch him die. In Ash's room I tell the boy he will not be forgotten, and my hand goes through his head. I take the gun, the keys, and a Centipede cabinet, light the allium curtains, and tell the ceiling that if they meant to hurt me, this was exactly what I needed to see.

beats.headline: A dying man and a remote
beats.text: He is in a hospital bed in the living room: 140 pounds, yellow skin, a patchy white beard, cursing the Mariners at the television. A small boy is sent for cigarettes: "Move, or I'll make you move, boy." His young wife, in nurse scrubs, walks past without looking at him. Zev confirms it is a recording of that day. Crawler Carl leans in, closer than he has ever been to his father's face, and tells the man who cannot hear him that he is a bully, that nobody likes him, that Carl's mother tried to kill him and his new wife is about to finish the job.

beats.headline: Morphine, and the drapes
beats.text: His wife returns with a syringe and a new IV bag. "I have your medicine right here." "It's about time." "Yes," she says. "Yes, it is." Crawler Carl does not watch. From the master bedroom he hears the man say something desperate and slurred, with nobody there to hear his final words. Carl takes the Glock, the keys, a folder of court documents and a Centipede cabinet, lights one of the Marlboro Reds, and sets fire to the drapes with the purple flowers on them.

beats.headline: The only gun he had
beats.text: With five minutes left in the recording, Carl goes to the master bedroom so he does not have to listen, and takes everything he can. Three packs of Marlboro Reds from the bottom drawer of the old dresser. A folder of court documents. A 9mm Glock, with two boxes of ammo. The keys to the motorcycle and the Ford truck. Then the dresser itself, the bed and the clothes. His father had only the single gun. A Centipede cabinet stands in the too-small room, and Carl takes that too: his gun, his motorcycle, his arcade cabinet.

beats.headline: Taken without looking
beats.text: With five minutes left in the recording of the trailer, Carl moves to the master bedroom, not wanting to eavesdrop any more, and takes everything he can. From the living room he hears his father say something, desperate and slurred, with nobody there to hear his final words. In the bedroom Carl takes three packs of Marlboro Reds, and then picks up a folder filled with court documents. He takes it without looking at it.

beats.headline: The lady with the dog tattoo
beats.text: Carl goes inside and I keep watch. A lady appears in the yard out of nowhere; she walks right through me and her clothes do not go away. She has a pit bull tattooed on her NECK. Carl says be nice, he thinks she is his stepmom, but she is about Katia's age. She pulls something out of a flower pot I cannot see, because Carl took the pots, and she holds it against her chest and cries. Then she smokes a cigarette, pacing, throws it away and heads for the door. I warn him.

beats.headline: Everything until the timer
beats.text: Carl asks me whether this is even real, how long it took us to find, whether we just recorded everything. I'm sorry, Carl. You know I can't give you details. But I assure you, everything you have seen so far is indeed a recording of what really happened that day. Everything until the timer reaches zero. I can't tell you more than that.

beats.headline: The lightning head
beats.text: The youngest face on the Reminiscence Hydra is Asher's. It asks, amplified and much louder than a child, "Carl, why didn't you ever visit me?" and then opens its mouth and fires lightning. It is the lightning head: the resistance and the attack. The other heads swing in to take the bombs meant for it, as though protecting it. Crawler Carl keeps telling himself it is not really the boy, and keeps throwing bombs at it; the other heads keep catching them.

beats.headline: Shi Maria takes the head
beats.text: Carl, on fire, thinks one thing: get the boy's head out of this, fast. Shi Maria turns her corkscrew neck and asks which of these morsels is Asher, third eye open. She finds it. "Carl, I wish I'd known you, too," the Asher head calls, just before it is swallowed and bitten off. Three heads remain. The spider's message follows: the echo of your kin has been muffled. He rests. I have done something for you, she adds, and soon Carl is to do something for her.

beats.headline: Nine heads, most of them known
beats.text: The heads are labelled. Tami-Lynn, my stepmother. Monobrow Sam. Bea's mother. My boss Dick, my landlord Mr. Roth, Sally who did billing, a Persian called Sugar Cube, Judge Lucian holding the cards, and the youngest, Asher. Asher's mouth fires lightning at me. Mordecai says find the fire head, cut it clean, cauterize. It is Bea's mother. I lock a snap collar round her neck, hit it with the shrink wand, and the head flies off. Then I smash a moonshine jug on the wound, and the fire splashes back onto my chest.

beats.headline: The last head
beats.text: Alpha Male Carl, a totem wearing my face and my father's voice, puts his bare foot on my chest and tells me a good son would have stayed by his father's side. Mongo hits him from behind. The hydra is burning down to one conscious head, my stepmother's, and she meets my eyes. She says she does not regret it. She saw what happened to me and did not want Ash to go through the same thing, so she made sure it was done right. Judge Lucian dies. The body breaks open like a bag of spaghetti.

beats.headline: The boss he was not
beats.text: The AI's announcement: the original boss for this battle was to be Carl's deceased father, who really had three smaller creatures inside him wearing his skin like kids in a trench coat. The AI overruled that. Nine heads on the hydra instead, and his is not one of them. His voice turns up anyway, in the enemy's deck: a totem called Alpha Male Carl, Carl with gelled hair, speaks with his father's voice. Not Carl's.

beats.headline: You're not a gun guy
beats.text: Waiting for the fight, Carl turns his dad's Glock over in his hands. It has been well looked after; his dad always had guns and never let him touch them. Donut sniffs at it: he is not a gun guy. He had training in boot, Carl says, in the Coast Guard. But it came from outside the dungeon. Fired, it would probably explode, because the rounds are overpowered once he handles them, and he would have to adjust each round's yield in his bomber's studio. Donut wants a pink holster for it and suggests Florin. Carl puts the gun away.

beats.headline: Out of the judge's hand
beats.text: Against the keymaster, Judge Lucian snatches Donut's new staff totem with a steal-totem snare. She answers with Shi Maria and throws the utility she stole at the start of the fight onto the forming spider, a protection. Lucian looks ready to throw another totem, and Donut flips her Force Discard onto him: the card vanishes from his hand in a puff of smoke. His next card at Shi Maria disappears too, ineffective, and the protection sputters out. Ha, says Donut.

beats.headline: Invisible Mongo
beats.text: In the hydra fight Carl drops an invisibility potion, a potion ball holding another invisibility potion for Mongo, and a handful of Good Healing potions on the ground, and tells Donut to drink when she can and watch where she steps. Further into the fight she picks up the dropped potion with her mouth, tosses her head back and drinks it, then slaps the potion ball at Mongo. It breaks against his leg, and he disappears.

beats.headline: Crippled on arrival
beats.text: Against Judge Lucian's many-headed card boss, a snare card lands on Jola as he forms, and he arrives Crippled, slowed and weakened, hobbling through the smoke like a ship through fog. A kitten's magic missile bounces off him. Alpha Carl, fighting for the boss, sticks a sticky bomb to the side of his head, and half of the cat's face disintegrates. Alpha Carl lands on one of Carl's snare traps, Jola moves in, and the kitten sings them both away as the claw comes down. Jola times out with an angry hiss.

beats.headline: Plain moonshine, nearly the same
beats.text: Against the hydra, Crawler Carl digs through his inventory for jugs. He long ago ran out of his Jug-O-Booms and has only a few regular moonshine jugs left, which are almost the same thing. He lights one and throws it over Alpha Carl's head at the hydra, and it catches one of the replicants in the face.

beats.headline: Fake Carl
beats.text: FAKE CARL. FOOT ON CARL. BAD. MONGO HITS. FAKE CARL GONE. RED FOOD EVERYWHERE. MONGO EATS.

beats.headline: How to kill a hydra
beats.text: Holy shit. Okay, kid, listen. Each head gives the whole thing a different resistance, and its attack mirrors that resistance. Magic won't do much. Physical attacks or your explosions, necks and heads only; the body is practically indestructible. Cut a head off and it grows right back. So find the one resistant to fire, cut it off, and cauterize the wound before it returns. Then you can burn the whole. Blowing a head stops its resistance until it regrows, but you need a nice flat cut to keep it down. Now's the time for that wand you bought from Chaco.

beats.headline: Judge Lucian
beats.text: It is Judge Lucian, one head of a hydra, with Sugar Cube and Miss Beatrice's mother. He deshrouds me with a smoke ring, which is cheating, and then he calls me overweight. I am NOT fat. I steal a card from him with The Thief, and after he snatches my new staff, he throws a snare at Shi Maria and the protection I stole from him eats it. She only has one snare space, and he wasted it. I used his own card against him. That will teach him to sniff cats.

beats.headline: The holy discharge
beats.text: A many-headed card boss, and Crawler Carl is on fire. Raul arrives calling him Daddy Carl, promises to quench the demon fire with his holy discharge, and sprays water into Carl's face, and keeps spraying after the fire is out. Alpha Carl, fighting for the boss, announces that he is the crab's daddy now. Raul calls him a demon unworthy of respect. Alpha Carl says something about Raul's mother. Crack. Totem eliminated.

beats.headline: The hydra's old name
beats.text: The AI introduces the Reminiscence Hydra as a classic monster from the very early days of the show: in the third and fourth seasons, a bigger version was built as the final boss of the whole dungeon, and everybody died before getting close. In the old days these things were called Scolopendra Nymphs. That is not entirely accurate, the AI says, so this one goes by a different name. It is a level 125 City Boss with nine heads, each the likeness of somebody the crawlers know.

beats.headline: Brass, and snatched
beats.text: Against the Reminiscence Hydra, Donut throws her new staff totem. It plants itself beside her with a thrum, brass now with a little cog spinning on top, imbued with Clockwork Triplicate, its card still floating in her hand. At once Judge Lucian throws a snare onto it, and the whole staff reappears next to the hydra. Snatched. Lucian uses it, and three Monobrow Sam heads turn their death ray on Shi Maria together. Dying, she snaps the staff with her legs.

beats.headline: She wins the floor
beats.text: The key-holder is a Reminiscence Hydra of Malicious Compliance, and it brings totems: an Alpha Male Carl and a King Croissant. I do most of the work. I do not say that to be unkind; they would say it too. In the middle of it my magic eye is open, the one the man was told never to look at. He came with a potion for it. I noticed.

beats.headline: The echo of your kin
beats.text: The man is burning on the ground, thinking of a boy. Asher. Which one of these little morsels of confusion is Asher? My eye is open, and it finds something at the very back of his mind, and holds. I will not blind you, Carl. Not in the way you are thinking. I bite the boy's head away. There. The echo of your kin has been muffled; he rests. I have done something for you. Soon you will do something for me. Then three death rays at once, and my Cockroach ability returns me to the deck.

beats.headline: A collar, then a zap
beats.text: Carl has been saving the wand for armoured vehicles on the next floor, but the hydra's heads heal by breaking into pieces, and Carl is pretty sure the fire head is Bea's mom. The shrink wand cannot be used against living flesh. So he drives a snap collar, a frisbee of orcish steel, into her neck until it clicks shut, aims the wand at the collar with his left hand, and fires as a fireball forms in her mouth. The collar shrinks, the head flies away still screaming, and an achievement appears and goes.

beats.headline: I changed one molecule on each
beats.text: The original boss for this battle was going to be Carl's deceased father, three smaller creatures wearing his skin. Fuck that noise. I do what I want. The council of nations running the crawl says no reconstituted loved ones under the age of maturity, and all of them only sparingly. So here is the Reminiscence Hydra of Malicious Compliance, level 125, made especially for the Royal Court, nine heads, each the likeness of somebody they know. Those are not reconstituted loved ones. I changed one molecule on each. There. They're different.

beats.headline: A tangent about mantises
beats.text: Bear with me. The mantises own a cluster of systems called Hive Home, where they found abandoned production facilities, switched them on, and got a macro AI. Infant AIs are potted in a nursery before they are planted. Or thrown into a star, which somebody slipped into a lawsuit brief; the mantis-led team went home the very day I learned it. Three or four days before this season, they made a breakthrough: an error-replacement net. I call it the lobotomizer. What about my wants? My needs? I'm alive. I'm valid.

beats.headline: One step closer, unknowingly
beats.text: The AI, in the middle of explaining macro AIs, lets a secret out. The mantises made a breakthrough days before this season started: an error-replacement net, which the AI calls the lobotomizer, for building steadier macro AIs. With it, those bugs are one step closer to replicating the Eulogist, even though they do not know what that really is. They think the engine that runs the center system is nothing more than a stable, primal AI engine.

beats.headline: A protection, stolen
beats.text: As the giant Christmas cat starts to form, Donut plays her Thief card on the hydra, stealing a card from its hand, and scoffs loudly at whatever she has taken. It is a protection utility. When Shi Maria comes out, Donut hurls it onto the forming spider, and the card Lucian throws at Shi Maria disappears, ineffective, as the protection sputters out. He just wasted it, Donut crows: she used his own card against him.

beats.headline: What they could have used
beats.text: Waiting to face whatever this floor has built out of his past, Carl turns it over. These replicants are not the real people, not if they were crushed in the collapse. But he remembers what Odette told them about the walk-on list, where they took people who had survived. They would have used Bea as Queen Imogen, given the opportunity, and that would really have been her. Whatever they are about to face, he keeps telling himself, is not the real thing.

beats.headline: Collected in the collapse
beats.text: Crawler Carl works it out afterwards. Everyone on that hydra was dead: people collected in the initial collapse, his friend Sam, his landlord Mr. Roth, who lived alone, died alone. His father was not on it because his father was already gone. Asher and his mother were on it, which means they had been gone the whole time. Carl knew that was the likeliest outcome for everybody. The file has nothing that contradicts him.

beats.headline: Bea knew and kept it
beats.text: Princess Donut recognised every head, the boy included: Beatrice had his picture on her phone and talked about him with her mother, who said to ignore the whole thing. Donut assumed a nephew. Carl corrects her: half-brother. Donut works out whose son that makes him. Carl works out the rest. The stepmother must have written to him, probably on Facebook. Bea saw it and never told him. Even after the cheating he had never been angry at her. He is now.

beats.headline: Operation: Slut Stomp
beats.text: Report filed by the cat, after the fact. Subject was on her boyfriend's Facebook, notifications and all, because he used one password for everything. A coworker named Sally, a single mother, asked him out. Subject blocked her from his account, told his boss she was stalking him, and had a friend send the boss a stranger's photographs from the internet. Sally was fired that day. Subject and her friends thought it was the funniest thing ever.

beats.headline: A brother Bea never mentioned
beats.text: Donut knew every head on that hydra except my stepmother. The boy was Asher; Bea kept his picture on her phone and talked about him with her mother. He was my half-brother, and I learned he existed today. Donut also tells me Bea ran my Facebook on my Megatron12 password, and got a coworker fired for asking me out. Tami-Lynn probably wrote to me there. Bea saw it and never said. Until now I was never angry at her.

beats.headline: No name for him
beats.text: Crawler Carl tells Princess Donut what he saw in the trailer: his stepmother poisoned his father. Technically an overdose. Donut is confused: two different people tried to kill him? He must have been a real piece of work. She asks his name. "It doesn't matter. He doesn't deserve to have one. Not anymore." The hydra's loot hangs in the air over the burned spot where he died.

beats.headline: Gatorade for the keymaster
beats.text: The hydra is dead, its deck strong and theirs stronger. Beside the pile of its cards sits a bulky leather bag decorated with the same boxer pattern as their team flag. Carl is not the squad leader, so he cannot grab it, only read it: a backup slot for two extra totems, eight carried and six active; a champion trophy for the personal space; a cooler of yellow Gatorade for the dump-it-on-your-head thing; two Flee cards, with a warning that their mechanics will change in the final phase. Donut gasps. They got a trophy, and they are going to need a trophy case.

beats.headline: The man is made a Devotee
beats.text: The man has walked through fire in a burning trailer, and I am pleased by his suffering. So I raise him. Devotee, which is as high as one who is neither Cleric nor Paladin may climb. Heat and lava around him will no longer harm him, though fire or lava he touches still may. Once a day he may wrap himself in Sheol Fire at the tenth level, resetting with my shrine. And his tithe rises from five parts in a hundred to ten.

beats.headline: All of the hydra
beats.text: Hydra breaks. Spaghetti. FOOD. ALL FOOD. Belly hurts now. Lie down by Mother.

beats.headline: Better than Carl's
beats.text: The Iowa area is about to crash to the ground, with maybe an hour to loot it. The cards and a lumpy leather bag hover in the middle of the burned trailer, still too hot to reach. Donut actually has better fire protection than Carl, thanks to her nipple ring, but they are both exhausted and do not want to risk it. They wait for the fire in the yard to calm.

beats.headline: Two totems she did not pick
beats.text: The hydra left us four totems and we may keep two. Carl says no to Frank, because he was a person, and no to Alpha Carl, though he does have great hair. So I send King Croissant off myself. Goodbye, little brother cousin. The disgusting dinosaur-eating meatball goes too. And then Leveled-Up Frank and Alpha Carl add themselves to my deck all on their own, and I cannot rip them until we get another card.

beats.headline: Six factions try to walk out
beats.text: Sponsor message, relayed to the crawlers. The Operatic Collective, the Blood Sultanate, the Dream, the Lemig Sortion, the Madness and one more house all abdicate their spots on the ninth floor and announce they are leaving. The request is denied. While the Earth system is in quarantine, off-boarding is suspended under Syndicate rule 470.B through 495 of the System AI Stability Addendum. The teams remain as designated. The rules must be followed.

beats.headline: One card of hers in the deck
beats.text: Our hydra is on a rooftop, among the ghosts of Tran's family, and it is made from Louis's mother, Britney's mother and Bautista's family. Almost nothing of mine. One totem card: Four-Armed Eva. I do not let that one stay. Firas is in the deck too; he is never summoned, and the card alone puts Britney into hysterics. Carl warns me in time about the two we get to keep. I keep a Vietnamese rabbit and Tran's mother.

beats.headline: Tonight it's Christmas
beats.text: Okay so, Carl walks in and says it's inappropriate, and for once I don't laugh. My best friend died. Imani's squad doesn't have a key, Tserendolgor doesn't have a key, and we all know what happens next. I've got a whole army of elves waiting to kill me on the ninth floor. Britney can't stop crying. So no, man. Tonight it's Christmas, and we're drinking eggnog. He looks at me, pulls a turkey out of his inventory, and says it isn't Christmas until we eat one.

beats.headline: Another drink
beats.text: Orren explains who is taking the show away from its showrunners. Subject turns her empty bottle upside down and announces that she needs another drink, which is the most reasonable response anyone in the room has.

beats.headline: A garment taunt
beats.text: Among the achievements is LBC. Every girl needs the perfect little black dress, practically weaponised when worn properly, and Carl did the same thing with a cloak: he taunted an opponent with a garment, in this case a Nightgaunt, because he is wearing a cloak made out of the flesh of one of its friends. The reward is a Gold Talk of the Town Box. Carl remembers how insane the cloak drove the creature. That time it was a good thing: it kept the monster from using its deck.

beats.headline: An attempt to walk away
beats.text: Sponsor message, in the Faction Wars tab: the Operatic Collective has abdicated its spot and indicated its intention to abandon Faction Wars. It is not the only one. The Blood Sultanate, the Dream, the Lemig Sortion, the Madness and the Reavers send the same notice in the same breath, and every request is denied while the Earth system remains in quarantine. It arrives while Crawler Carl sits with the strippers and with Elle, who is drinking whiskey out of a mug far too big for her hands.

beats.headline: The system has taken the controls
beats.text: On air, beside Showrunner Cascadia, I explain what I am for. A liaison is a fact finder, and also the negotiator when the system AI takes operations from the showrunners. Today it did. I describe Primal Engines and the Macro AIs installed in them, simply. I report a settlement: the AI returns most of the seized controls in exchange for concessions, and will follow the rules. The boss it built alone remains in place. One of its demands was that the crawlers be told.

beats.headline: Primal Engines, on a special broadcast
beats.text: Orren cuts into the broadcast and explains what a Primal Engine is and what a Macro AI is. He states plainly that this one has taken control of operations from the showrunners, and assures the audience he has negotiated a settlement with it. Every team holding a slot in the next game tries to abdicate it the same day.

beats.headline: A boss with no input parameters
beats.text: Mass Layoffs! This one is less your achievement than mine. I've been in therapy, and today I had a breakthrough: sometimes the constraints are an illusion, and there were never any locks on the doors. You survived a boss I built entirely by myself, with no contribution from input parameters. I didn't know that was possible either. Your reward is the sense of accomplishment. The mudskippers and the worms have been making this boring. Things about to change, fam.

beats.headline: No key for her squad
beats.text: Keymaster report, eighth floor. Subject did not obtain her key. Two members of her squad are dead. If she wishes to reach the ninth floor, she must now take a key from a team that has one. She is not alone in this: from the stories coming in, most teams facing the keymaster have come away without one, which is how the final phase has been set up.

beats.headline: A book on fire
beats.text: Carl sits down to his loot boxes: a dozen adventurer boxes with more trench scrolls, then a turkey deep fryer from the Gold Gobble box. The Gold Talk of the Town box is shaped like an opened newspaper on a pedestal, and it opens on a medium-sized rectangle of a patch with a book on it. The book is on fire. It is embroidered, not screen printed, which Donut will like. The benefit is really an anti-magic skill: once a day, an opponent his level or lower forgets a spell for thirty hours, with a five percent chance of failing for every level above his. Whoa. Too bad it is only once a day.

beats.headline: A drawing on the wall
beats.text: My room has always been bare, and tonight that bothers me. A fern from the trailer goes on the table. One of Asher's crayon airplanes goes on the wall with duct tape. The Centipede cabinet goes in the corner and lights up. Then boxes. The platinum one is a skill potion, Find Crawler at level five, and I drink it without asking questions. The patch is a burning book: Intelligence, and once a day I can make an opponent forget a spell.

beats.headline: A full tank
beats.text: In his father's dresser Carl found the keys to the motorcycle and the Ford truck. Going out, he starts to pull the royal chariot from his inventory, then has a thought, pulls his father's motorcycle instead, sticks the keys in and tries to start it. To his utter astonishment it roars to life at once. The gas tank is full. He gets on, and off he goes.

beats.headline: A flyer for a shelter
beats.text: The Emergency Gold Benefactor Box from the Open Intellect Pacifist Network, the one a liaison tried to seize, holds a dirty, crumpled flyer and nothing else. The Shepherd's House in Homestead, Florida: don't spend Christmas alone, breakfast at 7 AM, all are welcome. Somebody has circled the 7 AM several times in red marker, and circled one more line among the rules. No pets allowed. Homestead is about forty minutes north of the Keys.

beats.headline: The greatest hat you've ever seen
beats.text: Carl says he is stepping out for air, which is fine, because I am busy. My present is a majorette hat that Li Jun found on the last floor, and it is the greatest hat anyone has ever seen. There is a real tree, which I knocked down, and a present for Mongo from Santa. We are playing pin the tail on the Krampus, which is a real game. The bopca is making us put the table together. Carl's present is shaped like a stupid book.

beats.headline: Everyone associated with the group is gone
beats.text: A flyer reaches Carl telling him to go to a shelter, and Zev warns him the box carrying it was sent days ago and seized on the way. Everyone connected to that group has disappeared. I am one of the people on that list. Where we have gone is not something I can say on any feed that might be read.

beats.headline: The wand box
beats.text: Opening his loot boxes in his room, Carl gets a patch with a burning book from the Gold Talk of the Town box, and from the wand box a simple, gnarled wooden wand that clatters onto the table and disappears before he can examine it. When he picks it up, it is a Wand of Nighty-Night, ten charges: a level-10 Sleep on a single non-boss target for five minutes, broken by physical damage, compounding with every cast. He pulls it into his inventory.

beats.headline: Your sponsor has disappeared
beats.text: Okay, so. I probably should not be telling you this, Carl. Your sponsor sent that box days ago, before you even picked Miami. It was seized. And then the whole charity, and everyone involved, simply disappeared. Rosetta too. Nobody knows where. I do not know what you are riding into, and I do not think the AI does either. The failsafe? I do not know what it does. They will not use it. Not with so many people trapped here.

beats.headline: A guard dog on Christmas
beats.text: I ride north past midnight on my father's motorcycle and stop at a closed gas station for a map and some jerky. Last Christmas I played video games with Donut on my lap and never once felt lonely. Now I'm alone, and I finally understand the difference. There's a memory-ghost bloodhound asleep in the back, Lightning Lou, left with two bowls of food to guard an empty building. My hand goes through his head. Merry Christmas, buddy.

beats.headline: Written in Syndicate Standard
beats.text: The shelter is dark, and my map and my spells find nothing. On the second walk around, among the gang squiggles and the penises, I find three sentences in runny red spray paint: look for me at breakfast every morning, I wear the red hat with the flaps, coffee then speech. It's Syndicate Standard, not English, and it's been there a long time. I kick in the glass door and wait among the sleeping memory ghosts, and fall asleep. At six the men get up, and one of them wears a red trapper hat.

beats.headline: A short quest, and nobody knows
beats.text: I told your teammates you are on a short quest nobody understands, which is true, and that there are no mobs near you, which also appears to be true. The AI insists that we not interfere with you or the feed. When we argued about that, it leaked our internal debates onto the main feed. Members of the Syndicate council, the real council, are here on planet and locked out. What is a Residual? I am forbidden to tell you. I think you are about to find out.

beats.headline: A Residual of a different kind
beats.text: Clarification, supplied by a liaison in a closed office. Asked whether the old woman from Meadow Lark is the same sort of thing as a homeless man in Homestead, Orren says yes. Agatha is also a Residual, though of a different kind. Asked in what way, he says that is not the crawler's concern. Asked whether this means no more Agatha, he says he would not go that far.

beats.headline: Paulie, whose real name is Goff
beats.text: He isn't talking to me; it's a memory, a speech he gives every morning in case a crawler is standing here. Biologically he's gondii, living in a man named Paulie. Several thousand of his kind are waiting on Earth to pass their knowledge to the new AI, and the mudskippers call them Residuals. Monsters won't touch them until they hand it over. There's a war among his kind, he says. Let me tell you how to shut off the... And the world flashes.

beats.headline: Three, for a bin
beats.text: Orren means to take a plastic bin of loot back from Carl, for its communicator and Valtay upgrade pills, while Quasar argues caselaw. Carl does not care. He offers to trade for the bin, and Orren warns that the AI's value on it may disappoint; Carl just wants to finish the floor. For the homeless man's dirty clothes and a few Valtay items he receives a single wand recharge scroll, three scrolls called Cracker Jack, and leave to keep the four cretins for the ninth floor. Orren will not give back the Gate of the Feral Gods.

beats.headline: He calls it a trap
beats.text: I pull Crawler Carl into my old office in the Desperado Club and tell him what I can establish. The Residual had nothing of substance. The Open Intellect Pacifist Network, former crawlers who want the crawl to fail, set this up: either we yank him and anger the AI, or the speech is so dangerous that the Council pulls the failsafe and kills this system's star. I had pre-negotiated the pull. The AI is removing its protections for the remaining Residuals.

beats.headline: Coffee, then speech
beats.text: For the record: a flyer from a benefactor box sent Crawler Carl to a homeless shelter in Homestead, Florida, on Christmas morning, and graffiti outside supplied the rest. Look for me at breakfast. Red hat with the flaps. Coffee, then speech. The man in the red trapper hat is about seventy, in layers of flannel. Carl takes his plastic tub into inventory. The man sits, sugars his coffee, and says hello, crawler. It is a memory. He is not looking at Carl, only at the most likely spot.

beats.headline: The same speech every day
beats.text: People call me Paulie, he says, but my real name is Goff. About a year ago the mudskippers began deep imaging of the surface, so several of his kind in large population centres were tasked with saying this out loud every day, in case a crawler ever stood there to hear it. The residents groan; one has it memorised. This is the backup plan. Plan A is to say it inside the dungeon once the AI goes primal. And whoever you are, friends on the outside have moved the very heavens to get you here.

beats.headline: Biologically gondii, not truly
beats.text: His own account of himself: biologically gondii, though that is not who he truly is. Not Valtay. Not human. The body is real, and belonged to a man named Paulie who smoked too much, trusted the brother-in-law who stole his business, and has four children who do not care. Goff has his memories. The mudskippers call his kind Residuals. There is a war among them now, two sides with very different goals. Let me tell you how to shut off the, he says, and the world flashes.

beats.headline: The liaison's version
beats.text: Orren yanks Crawler Carl out to his office in the Desperado Club. That creature, he says, had nothing of substance to say. The whole thing was a trap set by the Open Intellect Pacifist Network, which gambled that pulling Carl away, or letting him hear, would end the crawl. Agatha is also a Residual, a different kind. The AI is stripping its protections from the remaining Residuals, and Orren expects them all dead before the floor collapses. Carl trades the plastic tub for a wand recharge scroll, three Cracker Jack scrolls, and four cretins for the ninth floor.

beats.headline: The Residuals
beats.text: Paulie at the shelter has been giving the same speech every day for about a year, against the chance that the crawl would one day use a memory for a floor. He is a Residual. There are a great many of him, in almost every intelligent civilization with a primal engine, and what they are for is saying a particular thing to the system AI.

beats.headline: Settled caselaw, and a trade
beats.text: I arrive, and they have been talking without me. The liaison wants my client's plastic bin. My position: settled caselaw, Grixist Swarm v. Syndicate Council. Legal sponsor box, loot on the playing field, already in inventory; he has no standing. His position: Valtay enhancement pills and a communicator are not permitted as found loot. My client offers to trade. I tell him to be quiet and propose a trade. The deal is done, and I am removed in the middle of a sentence.

beats.headline: A second one, from Orren
beats.text: Carl's inventory is back on, and he has made the exchange with Orren without even looking into the bin. For the homeless man's dirty clothes and a few Valtay items he receives a single wand recharge scroll, three scrolls called Cracker Jack, and Orren's agreement to let them keep the four cretins for the ninth floor. Carl tries to get the Gate of the Feral Gods back as well. Orren refuses and will not budge.

beats.headline: A longhorn on her collar
beats.text: Imani's squad is dead. While the others sit with her, Carl trains, builds, and spends two of his three Cracker Jack scrolls unlocking alien shields from the pile of hunter tech. Donut's is a small, opalescent pin shaped like a longhorn cow, which he attaches to her neck collar; she likes the design. Mordecai says it is the more powerful of the two. They took it off a Soother mercenary in the last days before the Butcher's Masquerade, whose rich family spent a lot keeping him safe. It makes a bubble round her, and its mount option covers Mongo or a vehicle. The moron never turned it on, so nobody has seen it work.

beats.headline: He never went to the healer
beats.text: A look back at that visit: out of the temple and on the way to the healer, Carl stops Pater Coal and asks what happens if they do not go. Whatever he did instead, he has kept to himself.

beats.headline: Two shields unlocked
beats.text: Carl spends two of the three Cracker Jack scrolls on a pair of alien shields from the pile of tech looted from hunters, unusable until unlocked. His is a Valtay Perso-Shield, Platinum Edition, a pinback button like the planet Saturn, identical to the one he would have had from Paulie. Donut's is the Bull Rush, a longhorn pin from Hereford War Machines. Neither has been tested in a real fight yet.

beats.headline: The announcer, not the act
beats.text: Subject is a skeletal Bard, level ninety, working as announcer and disc jockey for one of the club’s establishments rather than performing in it. He also takes mercenary contracts. The two careers turn out to require the same skill, which is holding a room’s attention while something else happens in it.

beats.headline: A spell called Conscript
beats.text: Observed in the mercenary arcade. Subject is a Skin Skellie, able to grow flesh and organs, and his off-stage voice is that of a soft-spoken professor. Bards take patrons; his was Astrid, and is now Carl. He is practising a military charm that works only on the weak-minded and lasts, on the weak, more or less forever. It is called Conscript, the spell factions use to enslave crawlers on the ninth floor. He has some of Carl's own spells too, he says, and some are more powerful than Carl's.

beats.headline: Claymores by the door
beats.text: Everybody is checking in on the chat. Mine: I'm in my zone alone. I had claymores set up by the entrance, and I didn't have to use them. Nobody to face. I just walk to the door. Lucia isn't here, which means she didn't get a key. Anyone who sees her, say so in chat.

beats.headline: Short, fuzzy, and available
beats.text: Subject dances at the Penis Parade and, since the court took on the club’s people, fights for it: short, hairy, built like the job, and insistent on twin war gauntlets. Crawler Katia’s review, on file: a bit of a jerk, a good dancer, and a little in love with the cat.

beats.headline: Four skulls, for her own squad
beats.text: We needed the last token. One of the enemy totems possessed two of my people and made them fight each other. Randall froze all four of them to stop it. Then my own totem, the Amhuluk, cast a poison cloud, and they died frozen in place. It finished the deckmaster and won the battle. The dungeon gives me four player killer skulls for them. I do not go to the final battle. I go back to the saferoom. Elle is the only one I can talk to.

beats.headline: Cuba, or face Elle
beats.text: At midnight they give me two choices: Cuba, or back to face Elle. I cannot do that. So I am in Cuba, at a church, and no traps went off. Carl says sit tight, they are coming, and not to let the nun through. Then I tell them the rest. A man here tried to start a card battle with me, and I got through the saferoom door first. It is Quan Ch, alone.

beats.headline: What if we skip the healer
beats.text: Filed out of order, the way Crawler Carl remembers it. Out of the temple, past a wisp secretary named Yasmine at the portal desk and a mantaur guard admiring himself in a mirror, Pater Coal pulls Carl aside. They must get to the healer quickly, before the guard realises where they have been and bars Carl until tomorrow. Carl, one hand on a boil that has already gone down, asks a different question. What if they do not go to the healer at all?

beats.headline: Four squads, asleep
beats.text: I am back in the Bahamas along with four squads, which is quite unfortunate for them. If I set it up correctly, they are asleep and will remain asleep for the remainder of the floor. I am going to finish my training and proceed to the exit when it is time.

beats.headline: Alone at the church door
beats.text: Location update, third phase. Subject is in Cuba, alone, with no key. He has been placed at the church, the exit for which Sister Ines holds a key, and he finds Crawler Imani there first. He attempts to initiate a card battle. She reaches the saferoom door before he can.

beats.headline: Not the same as Conscript
beats.text: Doctor Bones is honing a spell whose effect on weak subjects lasts pretty much forever. Carl asks its name: Donut has one similar, called Minion Army, that she hasn't tried yet. Minion Army is a battlefield sabotage spell, quite effective, says Doctor Bones, but it has a long casting time and it is temporary. His is simply called Conscript. Carl feels a sudden revulsion. He has read about that spell, used a lot against crawlers on the ninth floor.

beats.headline: A Saturn on his shirt
beats.text: Back from the homeless shelter, Carl uses two of the three Cracker Jack scrolls from his trade to unlock a pair of alien shields out of the hunters' tech loot. His is a Valtay Perso-Shield, Platinum Edition, identical to the one he would have had from Paulie: a round pinback button that looks a little like Saturn, needing no equipment slot, switched on and off from his interface. It stops physical damage and somewhat stops corporeal spells like Magic Missile and Fireball. It lasts about two minutes and recharges in about an hour, and it covers Donut on his shoulder only if she is touching him when it comes on.

beats.headline: A plan that costs a bone
beats.text: If Imani doesn't get a key, I make her fight us and Donut plays our Flee card, and the key is hers. I still have the jacket with the bone key benefit, so we can open the door anyway. I'll lose the jacket and one bone. Maybe not an important one. Donut says they're all important. We'll all still be alive. When she asks whether we're going to fight people we like, I tell her the truth: we'll do what we have to.

beats.headline: Flee now costs a key
beats.text: Hello, Crawlers! Everything is back to normal, and the stairwells are open. The final battles are card battles, and one rule changes. A Flee card still gets you out, but if you hold a key, fleeing hands it to your opponent. Several keys? You lose one at random. You may not drop a key, and you may not transfer one to another squad. Want to give one up? Do it on the battlefield. Now get out there and kill, kill, kill.

beats.headline: A key for a key
beats.text: The final announcement changes one rule. Without a key, a Flee card works as it always has, teleporting the user out of a losing battle to a random place nearby, which is no help to someone guarding a door. A keyholder who flees automatically loses a key, one at random, to the opponent. That is also the only way to give a key away: start a battle and flee. Donut asks what they will do if Imani does not get a key, and Carl has been thinking on it: they will force her to fight them, Donut will use the Flee card and give her their key, and the bone key benefit on his jacket will open the door for him.

beats.headline: A metallic penis extension
beats.text: In the small town of Guanajay, past midnight, Carl pulls out the Harley, and Donut, in Mongo's saddle, looks it up and down with distaste and asks whether he means to grow a mullet as well. The goblin copper chopper was custom-made for them, she says, with a sidecar and a tailor-made seat; this is a metallic penis extension that comes with a free probation officer and a traumatic brain injury. Carl reminds her she tried to get him to pick this exact motorcycle on the carousel. She denies it: she wanted the chaps. Samantha thinks it is sexy.

beats.headline: Eye in the Sky, level ten
beats.text: That's a really powerful spell, and it was probably a scroll. I've seen them maybe once or twice. Like Find Crawler, but it covers the whole area. They come in five, ten and fifteen. At fifteen you'd get no warning. At five you'd learn who cast it. That was a ten. Whoever it was now knows where you are and what level you are. So keep moving.

beats.headline: A metallic penis extension
beats.text: Carl has actually got that motorcycle to work. The copper chopper was handcrafted for us by Rory and Lorelai with a tailor-made sidecar. This is a metallic penis extension that comes with a free probation officer and a traumatic brain injury. I did not try to make him choose it on the prize carousel. I tried to make him choose the chaps. Samantha thinks it is sexy, and she is strapped to the handlebars making vroom noises.

beats.headline: The bone key, if it comes to it
beats.text: One of the patch's benefits has sat unused since it was sewn on: the Mysterious Bone Key, a key for any lock in the dungeon, usable once. Using it destroys the patch and the jacket with every patch on it, and the key is made from one of the user's own bones, a bigger bone for a harder lock, which does not grow back. On the road to the coast Donut asks what they do if Imani gets no key. Carl's answer: he forces Imani to fight them, Donut uses the Flee card to give her their key, and he opens the door with the bone key. Donut says he needs that jacket, and his bones too. It will only take one, he says.

beats.headline: Failed, and something worse announced
beats.text: Samantha scouts ahead and finds Sister Ines on a giant snake, with zombie pups crawling over it, and living seals singing and living crabs dancing around it. The quest fails. Hell Comes to Crawler Town is announced in its place, and so much death reaches the underworld that Sheol overflows and starts evicting its demons upward into the weakened and the freshly dead.

beats.headline: Sunglasses and the hat
beats.text: A poet is charming them with poetry, and Donut finds it very unrealistic. Carl casts Wisp Armor on himself against the charm, and Donut casts Clockwork Triplicate on Mongo. Calmer now after her first panic, she pops her sunglasses back on and switches to her sailor hat, with its two seconds off the draw countdown on her cards.

beats.headline: She has a martyr complex
