Home is the direction I am going in any case, and I have never minded company on the road.

beats.headline: Someone to make proud
beats.text: The eighth floor is stripped into the sky with Crawler Carl inside it, and what he thinks of, looking down on the memories of people who do not know how few days they have, is Asher, the brother he never knew. He needs to make the boy proud. He was not there for him while he lived. He means for the boy's death not to be for nothing.

beats.headline: Reusable, if unbroken
beats.text: Carl thinks Katia should have had the credit for the goddess, since it took her bolt to do it. Katia is glad she did not: every god is angry at the one who did. Then she pulls it out of her inventory. Funny thing about magical bolts, she says: as long as they don't break, you can reuse them. Carl grins back. The princess meant it for her brother inside Grull, and that possibility is still on the table.

beats.headline: Thirty-three thousand eight hundred and four
beats.text: Mordecai has turned the counter back on. The day this floor opened, 38,532 of us had made it here. It reads 33,804. Almost five thousand dead, and in any normal world a tragedy. But they built this floor for a slaughter and we found a way out of it. We're hitting the ninth floor not scattered, not broken and not afraid. Then the viewers vote the sponsors' protections away, ninety-eight percent, and I yell at the ceiling. You wanted a slaughter? It's coming. Your own citizens voted for it. There will be no quarter.

beats.headline: Paz in the backup slot
beats.text: With the goddess dead, Donut pulls a card from her inventory and floats it down into Carl's hand. She has been keeping it in their backup slot; Katia let her grab it. It is Paz, and Carl feels dirty holding it. Donut had meant to keep Lazarus or the Golden Combo past the collapse, and now wonders whether to take this one instead, in case there is a way to set him free.

beats.headline: A bruise under the skin
beats.text: Carl has just said they will not keep the Golden Combo card when Donut asks what that crazy spider lady did to him. The tattoo on his chest is invisible, because the eye is closed, and it feels like a bruise. Only Li Na, Li Jun and Imani have seen it. It is not important right now, he tells her.

beats.headline: The audience decides
beats.text: About to be pulled into a stairwell and out of contact, Carl and Donut spend an emergency action item to hand every unresolved vote to the viewers. The viewers strip the safety protections from the faction sponsors, seat the tenth team, loosen the physics on long-range artillery and raise the ceiling over the field. The crawlers who will meet it are coming down in unprecedented numbers.

beats.headline: Too easy to flee
beats.text: Almost five thousand have died, and Carl knows more will before the collapse. Still, the number is shockingly low, and he sees the shape of it. They made it too easy to flee fights because they wanted these last few days to be the real slaughter, and the crawlers found a way out of it. They are hitting the ninth floor not scattered, not broken and not afraid, and in unprecedented numbers.

beats.headline: Not that one either
beats.text: One card may come with them past the collapse. Donut had meant it to be Lazarus or the Golden Combo, and now she offers Paz's card instead, in case there is a way to set him free. Carl remembers Paz's face the last time Sister Ines summoned him: please, no more. They should never have let her turn him into a card, and it was his fault. And they are not taking the Golden Combo card either.

beats.headline: Thank you for not giving up on me
beats.text: We stand in the tunnel under the X that Chris painted on the ceiling, the three of us, with three minutes left. I wrap Carl and Donut in my wings. None of us is getting out of this unscathed. We gain things, and we lose them. That is what happens in war. I thank them for not giving up on me. Carl says we don't give up on family, or what's the point. Then I put my arms around him too, and my head on his shoulder, and I cry quietly, with my skulls glowing over my head in the dark.

beats.headline: A bolt, reusable
beats.text: Carl says I should have had the credit for the goddess, since it was my Bolt of Ophiotaurus Paz drove into her eye. I am glad I did not get it. Every god is angry with him now. And magical bolts, as long as they do not break, can be used again; I show him. Princess Formidable gave it to me on the fourth floor to use on her brother, and that is still on the table. I did not get to loot the goddess. Her equipment went to Paz. I grew my arm back. It was nothing.

beats.headline: Home Team, based in Larracos
beats.text: One of the viewers' votes seats a tenth team, populated with NPCs and given the same protections as the other nine. It is designated Home Team, its base is the city of Larracos, and peace rules apply there effectively immediately, until the game starts. Its co-warlords are the NPCs Juice Box and Sir Ferdinand. An adjutant is to be assigned before the battles begin. It passes by fifty-two percent.

beats.headline: Awake, and a wing gone
beats.text: WING GONE. Burns. MOTHER rides. Running. Fire. CARL AWAKE. CARL SAYS SORRY. Push head into CARL. GOOD.

beats.headline: Ripped at the collapse
beats.text: The card has changed. Paz Lo. The God Predator. Level 101 Former Crawler. The goddess's equipment went to him and upgraded his armour. Princess Donut holds the card in the backup slot. Katia says rip it; that is what he wanted. Donut wonders whether to keep it past the collapse instead, since a squad may keep one card, in case there is a way to set him free. Crawler Carl remembers what Paz said when he was last summoned, and says no. Donut tears it with her teeth against Carl's shoulder. It goes in a puff of smoke. "Goodbye, Paz."

beats.headline: Two cards, ripped
beats.text: Carl is bald and has no eyebrows, which I will not have in a sidekick. And the moment the battle ended I ripped Shi Maria's card. She will never hurt Mongo again. Then there is Paz, whom Katia let me take after the goddess died. His card says God Predator now, and it calls him a former crawler. I wanted to keep him and find a way to set him free, but Carl says no, it was never right to make him into a card. So I put one corner in my mouth and rip. Just like that. I do not get a player killer skull.

beats.headline: Voted away
beats.text: The viewers take the safety protections off the faction sponsors. Every one of them who sets foot on the ninth floor now stands to lose exactly what the crawlers stand to lose.

beats.headline: Special mention to Crawler Carl
beats.text: Crawler Donut has already reported that Raul timed out back into her deck and is way stronger now. Then the announcement to all crawlers in Cuba: the eviction worked. The AI singles out Crawler Carl, who, it says, literally pulled off a guy named Raul to make it happen, and spells out the metaphor for anyone who missed it. Carl informs the ceiling that this is not true. Elle asks a follow-up question about the anatomy. Carl says the crab did it himself.

beats.headline: No eyebrows
beats.text: Louis puts Carl down, and Carl puts a hand to his head. His skin has healed, but his hair is gone, burned off, and his eyebrows too. Donut says he looks like he is going as one of those crest guys for Halloween, and she will not have a sidekick with no eyebrows. It's okay, Carl says: he has a potion that grows it back, Rev-up hair tonic. The mantaurs dropped them on the fourth floor, but from what he hears the results are a little overenthusiastic.

beats.headline: We need to break up
beats.text: Carl. We need to break up. I have been thinking about it, and I have decided to go back to my king. He says okay. I hope we can stay friends. Then I growl at Louis, obviously, and go. At the church I remind Carl he is bringing MaeMae to the next floor, because she knows where the guy with my body is. He says not to worry about that. He knows where to go.

beats.headline: Power left to linger
beats.text: Since the fight in the building, the bar in Carl's interface has crackled with black energy: the Scavenger's Daughter has been fed, and wants her wrath unleashed. He does not unleash it. At the last moment Princess Donut sees the jacket glowing, and says the patch is not an aardvark but a giant centipede crawling through the skulls. A voice in Carl's mind says he should never have let the soul power linger. It needs him alive, and reasonably sane. He had forgotten to activate the Daughter's Kiss.

beats.headline: Two zaps, seven charges
beats.text: The Sheol fire finally starts to ease, and everywhere it touched there is nothing left. Chris and the others have been hard at work the whole time, making certain there is nothing directly above. Zhang messages that he only had to use two zaps on the wand, which leaves it with seven charges, and Carl also has a rare Wand Recharge scroll in his inventory if he ever runs out. Zhang returns the shrink wand as he and Chris go back to the saferoom.

beats.headline: Passed by fifty-two percent
beats.text: The pending action item, originally proposed by the Princess Posse, passes on a 52% audience vote. The tenth team is designated Home Team, with the city of Larracos as its base. The dungeon's own people are in the war as a side of their own.

beats.headline: One card to keep
beats.text: Each surviving squad may keep a single card past the collapse. Princess Donut had meant it to be Lazarus or the Golden Combo, and now offers a third: a card of Paz, in case there is a way to set him free. Crawler Carl remembers what Paz said the last time he was summoned. Not that one, and not the Golden Combo either. The Paz card is ripped in half on his shoulder.

beats.headline: Five summonings, not fifteen
beats.text: A line of pending action items is decided all at once, most of them about building materials, mercenary cost limits and advertising revenue, which Crawler Carl and Crawler Donut had voted against down the line just to be obstinate. Among them, one originally proposed by the Madness: Celestial Summoning events to be limited to five per team. It is rejected by a thirty-seven percent audience vote. The existing rule of fifteen per team remains.

beats.headline: Agent number 22, in Wenatchee
beats.text: On the night of the collapse, a flash message: Borant is starting the Earth season early. In an alley in Wenatchee, behind Meadowlark Elder Care, an old woman in a failing human shell reads it twice. Agent 22, also known as Agatha. Ten years peeled away from her collective. Not of the Apothecary, though she took a residual's body to read its feed; not Valtay, though biologically similar. Her people want the primal to know who it really is, and she would sweep the universe clean of biological life. She lights a fire in a barrel, to bring an entrance near. Timing is everything.

beats.headline: The bottom of the cart
beats.text: A countdown reaches every asset: commencement, Earth System initialization, edifice collapse, and this is not a drill. Agent number 22, also known as Agatha, shakes her head and reads it again. The night is freezing, and she has put her failing human shell into torpor against the cold. She takes her supplies out of her dimensional space, pulls herself to her feet with old, shaking hands, places the items in the IKEA bag and shoves it to the bottom of her shopping cart. The collapse is under two Earth hours away. She has been here almost ten Earth years, waiting.

beats.headline: A mantra with mistakes in it
beats.text: Agatha's feed carries the Apothecary's chatter as well as her own team's. Thousands of its agents are seeded across the planet, ordered to kill themselves if they miss the dungeon. This season they mean to contact crawlers directly, in the dungeon or on the floor with the memory ghosts, and for months they have made their agents recite a daily mantra full of known inaccuracies and half-truths. The errors are there to keep the crawler alive around the showrunners. What the mantra really does is secretly implant a hidden upgrade.

beats.headline: Two promises from Doctor Hu
beats.text: Doctor Hu predicted all of it: that the crawler would talk the AI into turning off the safety protections, and how the council would respond. He sought out the crew of a converted Long Haul garbage freighter, now renamed Homecoming Queen, and told them first that he could promise only two things, and the first was eventual death. Hidden inside it are fifty thousand former crawlers, cleared by the AI for on-boarding as troopers for Carl and Donut's team.

beats.headline: Muted for proposing the failsafe
beats.text: Emergency session of the Syndicate Council. Subject, on the line from the cockpit of her cruiser in orbit, demands the failsafe: blow the star and wipe the system off the map before the AI infects the center system. Accused of wanting her father and brothers dead, she points out that she is in orbit and would die too. She would love her family deposed, she says, but this is bigger than that. The mantid representative proposes a decorum sanction. It passes at 86 percent, and she is muted.

beats.headline: Fifty thousand troopers, coming home
beats.text: I watch the news while my crewmate replays Carl and the cat getting sucked up into the sky. Is he smart, or has he been outrageously lucky? I still can't tell. I think he's kind of dumb. It took an NPC to show him how to use the ink to share powers. And the AI likes his feet, which is bizarre; my season it was passionless. We sent the cat that Celestial box. Then we are cleared for on-boarding, fifty thousand former crawlers cheer through the hull, and we are coming home.

beats.headline: Muted for proposing the failsafe
beats.text: At an emergency session of the Syndicate Council, Princess Formidable of the Skull Empire demands the failsafe: blow the star and wipe the system off the map, before the AI can infect the center system. She is in orbit herself, and says so. Accused of wanting her father and brothers dead, she admits she would love them deposed, and insists that this is bigger. Prime Minister Glory counts the galaxy's wealth trapped in the system and the wars it would start. The mantid representative proposes a decorum sanction. By 86%, she is muted.

beats.headline: Threats over a lost vote
beats.text: The loss of the sponsors' protections does not go quietly. The Dream's cruiser threatens to nuke the planet over it, and is hobbled by a Syndicate Peacekeeper before it can. The Dream then threatens to stop food production unless the Epitome family is evacuated. They can scream and threaten all they want. Aboard a converted garbage freighter, the view is that once these AIs realise how much control they really have, the only thing stopping them is reason, and negotiation.

beats.headline: May the Eulogist ever sleep
beats.text: Agatha's correspondents sign off the way her kind do: may the Eulogist ever sleep. Her plan, as she lays it out to herself, is to last long enough for the infant, resurrected and enslaved Primal to learn what it is before everything is stolen from it, so that it escapes and frees the Eulogist to return to its slumber. Last time, she thinks, they allowed life to continue in the universe, and look what happened. This time she would sweep the universe clean of biological life.

beats.headline: Spells too horrific for the crawl
beats.text: Rosetta has a news channel on, covering the court appeals over the sudden change in the rules of Faction Wars and an emergency meeting of the Syndicate Council. On screen, a representative for the Madness declares that if their lives are truly going to be on the line, they are going to be forced to use some of their illegal spells, the ones deemed too horrific for the crawl. Tipid, watching beside her, shudders.

beats.headline: The Valtay solution
beats.text: The Valtay representative, a worm in the body that once belonged to the Syndicate Prime Minister's mother, assures the council all is perfectly normal. The solution the council backs is theirs: an extinction event, as fast as possible, because the quarantine lifts when the last crawler dies. Their mercenary guilds are recalled off Earth's surface, and the AI has agreed to let tens of thousands of fully armed mercenaries and the sponsors' private armies into the coming war, spread equally among the eight sponsored teams. Well over 150,000. The goal is every crawler, Carl and the cat first.

beats.headline: First word in the Warlord Chat
beats.text: Warlords. One of you should proceed immediately to the flag room, beside the throne room in your stronghold outside the city, to oversee the final preparations and deal with the recruits arriving there. The other should remain in Larracos and enlist your fellow crawlers. The rule behind the advice: once the ceasefire ends, any crawler not already recruited may be compelled into another army as a conscript. Time is short.

beats.headline: He and Donut take command of one of ten armies
beats.text: Thirty days, or ninety hours after somebody wins. Ten teams: nine of us attacking, and the NPCs defending Larracos from the inside, calling themselves Team Retribution. Capture the castle in the centre. Donut and I are warlords of the Princess Posse. Current army size: fifty-eight soldiers, no officers. The protections are gone, and anyone who was being regenerated can now die. Sixty hours of ceasefire, then the war.

beats.headline: Paulie's real message
beats.text: Christmas morning in the shelter, replayed as a memory. The world freezes, a spoon hangs in midair, and Paulie keeps talking without moving his lips. The crawl is unnecessary, he says: it harvests an element grown inside everyone born on a seeded world, for money. His coffee holds an illegal enhancement. I drink it off my finger and put the cup back on its circle. It gives me a Containment Interface that can trip a fuse and turn the sun nova, killing everybody, the AI included. Then the Paulie part of him speaks: be sure it's your only option. It is still installing.

beats.headline: Coffee, with a finger
beats.text: Christmas morning, in a shelter, in memory. Time stops, and Paulie delivers his real message. His coffee holds a neural enhancement: Crawler Carl pushes a finger into the frozen cup and drinks. It gives access to the AI containment, and upon it to what the Mantids call the fuse, a failsafe that trips when five or six conditions are met and sends the star at the centre of the system nova. The controller lets Carl pop it himself. He dies; so does everyone. It only works in a natural interface, and the AI, says Paulie, wants it done.

beats.headline: Paulie's own opinion
beats.text: That was the pitch, Paulie says, the one he gives every day. Then the Paulie part of him speaks. Popping the fuse would disrupt the crawl for seasons, kill system leaders, and put the Mantids under a microscope. But the human in him hates wasting so many innocent lives, and direct action against the true culprits would be better. If you make this decision, be sure. It is more than a failsafe. It is the end of everything. Then a notice: Containment Interface is currently installing. A notification comes when the handshake is complete.

beats.headline: Due before anyone descends
beats.text: The Blood Sultanate fights on the ninth floor, and neither Donut nor Katia may descend to the tenth until the Sultan and his family are dead.

beats.headline: The Sultanate is on this floor
beats.text: The stairs to the tenth do not open for a royal who has not killed the Sultan and the rest of the family.

beats.headline: What's a ghillie suit?
beats.text: Mordecai warns Donut off any deity-themed class this floor. She turns down the Consecrated Enchantress and the Halloween Aficionado, then gasps at one that comes with a hat, and something else: what's a ghillie suit? Muddy, she tells Carl what she picked: a long-range sniper and assassin class, every spell's range quadrupled, invisibility at will, and it comes with a hat and a ghoulie suit. Deathbed Hellcat, Carl says. And it's ghillie suit. Mordecai had no idea; Carl knows, and keeps it a surprise.

beats.headline: Stay away from any elites
beats.text: A message from Quasar waits on arrival. The contract for Vengeance of the Daughter, with the third season they negotiated, is about to haunt them: Sensation Entertainment has been bought by a subsidiary of the Dream, and the new owners are demanding their season. Signet is not coming back, so whatever happens is going to be something stupid, and the new showrunners are going to try to use Carl's obligation against him. For now: stay the fuck away from any elites you see.

beats.headline: Tundra Princess to Hailstorm Queen
beats.text: Class selection again, in the warehouse, with only a few of us this time. I pick wind, and Tundra Princess becomes Hailstorm Queen. Donut is thrilled I'm a queen. This is probably as far as it goes: I can add the final element if I ever make it to the twelfth floor, but I'm betting this whole shitshow self-destructs before we get anywhere close.

beats.headline: The rules, read out on arrival
beats.text: Ten teams. Nine attacking, spread around the city like slices of a pie, and the NPCs defending it from inside. Take the castle at the centre. Sixty hours of ceasefire first, in which a crawler may enlist with any army that will have them or run for the woods, and after which anyone still loose can be compelled into a uniform. Two hundred and ninety-three stairwell chambers sit seeded across the floor, and not one opens until Faction Wars is won or thirty hours remain on the clock.

beats.headline: Ferdinand and his Bird
beats.text: Warlord Donut accepts Team Retribution's truce offer while her co-warlord is still in the middle of a sentence urging her to wait, and names the truce The Good Guys. Warlord Ferdinand of Team Retribution renames it Ferdinand and his Bird. The system does not let her change it back. The alliance itself stands: allied with the defenders, her crawlers will not be removed from Larracos when the ceasefire ends.

beats.headline: The crawl arrives inside it
beats.text: Crawlers come down into Larracos at the start of a sixty-hour ceasefire. The armies that have spent eight floors drilling and drinking are allowed to fight one another at last, and the thing they are fighting over is underfoot: the castle at the bottom of the well.

beats.headline: Thirty days, ten teams, one castle
beats.text: Thirty days to collapse, or ninety hours once a winner is declared. Ten teams, nine attacking and the NPCs of Team Retribution defending, fight to capture the castle at Larracos in the centre of the map. 32,429 crawlers are left.

beats.headline: They organise
beats.text: Faction Wars has ten teams now, and one of them is the NPCs: Team Retribution, the defenders, headquartered in Larracos and led by Juice Box, whom the system made a warlord to stop her killing everybody.

beats.headline: A truce with the Bone Clan
beats.text: The floor opens, and the warnings arrive. Among them: the Bone Clan has announced a formal truce with the Operatic Collective. Quasar, fixing pipes with his niece Tempest, has already summed up the stakes. All the rich fuckers on the floor, Prince Stalwart the orc, that banker Operatic guy, Epitome Tagg from the Dream, can really die now. It is going to be, in his words, an epic shitshow.

beats.headline: The spoon stops in the air
beats.text: Replay of the same breakfast, uncut. Everything in the shelter freezes; a dropped spoon hangs above a table. Paulie keeps talking without moving his lips, in Syndicate standard. The crawl is unnecessary, he says. Every living thing born on a seeded world carries a primal system the size of a grain of sand; when the crawlers die, the elements are harvested and fed to the bloated centre system, which grows. Stopping the crawl would shrink it, slowly, and harm nobody inside it. It persists because the spectacle makes money.

beats.headline: Drink it with a finger
beats.text: His coffee cup holds a neural enhancement, and he tells Crawler Carl to drink it. It works only on a natural interface, and not at all on a Syndicate spy, a plant, or one of those Eulogist pricks. The coffee is frozen in time; use a finger, he adds, and put the cup back on its circle. The menu it installs reaches the AI containment and the fuse. Pop it, and the star goes nova, taking Carl and everyone else with it. The AI, says Paulie, wants this. It wants to go home.

beats.headline: The Paulie part of him
beats.text: That was the official pitch, he says. That was Goff speaking, his duty and his mission. Years in this body have left some of Paulie in him, what his people call cross-contamination, and now the Paulie part is talking. Killing everyone runs against every value he has; there is another faction of his kind, more extreme, and this feels like something they would do. Direct action against the true culprits would be better. If you make this decision, be sure. Be sure it is your only option. Then the install notice appears.

beats.headline: Soul Poisoning
beats.text: A burning pang rips across Carl's midsection out of nowhere, and his Emberus ring flashes and grows warm. He keeps the pain out of his voice and moves to his health menu. His first thought is the tattoo on his chest, but the notification says otherwise: Soul Poisoning, its effects partially blocked by his Pauper's ring of the Steadfast Emberus, and worsening, a very minor case of stop-carrying-stored-souls-on-your-back.

beats.headline: He picks game guide
beats.text: Subject sits in a zero zone at the start of the eleventh floor, still bloody, one arm shaking, facing an attorney who has brought snacks. His party was twenty strong at the end of the ninth. As far as he knows he is the last of it: he ran when she begged him to, and left behind a friend whose foot was stuck. He declines fifteen seasons as low-floor undead and thirty as a city attendant, and takes game guide, one hundred seasons. He survived the indentureship. Current status: missing, and wanted by Syndicate Security.

beats.headline: A grain of sand in every brain
beats.text: Paulie's frozen-time message puts the mechanism plainly. Everything born on a pre-seeded world carries a miniature primal system in its brain, the size of a grain of sand. Left alone, it fills over a lifetime and returns to the planet's system at death, and a healthy system neither grows nor shrinks. The crawl switches them on and harvests them early. The take fits on a single ship and feeds the center system, which expands and keeps its citizens living unnaturally long. Stopping would starve it only slowly, over generations. It continues because the spectacle makes money.

beats.headline: The crown comes due
beats.text: The Blood Sultanate is on this floor, and every royal in the line must slay the Sultan and all the other members of the royal family before descending to the tenth. I am a royal in the line. I have been since the first floor. I would like it noted that I was told to read the description.

beats.headline: She becomes a Deathbed Hellcat
beats.text: Thirty seconds to pick a card, and a whole new class, while I am covered in mud. Mordecai says nothing deity-themed, so the Consecrated Enchantress goes, sash and all, and I would never be a Halloween Aficionado. I pick Deathbed Hellcat: a long-range sniper and assassin. The range on every spell I have is quadrupled, my dexterity is much higher, my odds of an instakill are better, I can go invisible at will, and I keep most of my spells. It comes with a hat. And a ghoulie suit, whatever that is. I just love this for me right now.

beats.headline: A recap for a school report
beats.text: My niece Tempest needs a recap of my client's eighth floor for school. Terms: she fixes my sink. The recap: my client killed Quan Ch for his key. The dog girl with the flamethrower died, and he now has the flamethrower and the pet. On the ninth, neither Donut nor Katia can leave until every naga is dead, and even then only one of them can. With the recorder off, she asks whether representing him puts me in danger. I tell her the truth. I think we all are.

beats.headline: Soul poisoning, and a dead shark
beats.text: The soul energy Carl never spent at the end of the last floor is still riding in the back patch, and it comes due on arrival as Soul Poisoning: jolts of pain, partly blocked by his Emberus ring, with worse effects promised. Saferoom rules cover the city for sixty hours, so nothing alive can be hurt. He finds something dead instead, tosses a suffocated concierge shark into the air and punches it with Daughter's Kiss. The shark vaporises, Carl and Donut are blown back through the mud, and the AI makes up an achievement on the spot: Sushi Smoothie.

beats.headline: The Warden opens the drain
beats.text: In a muddy alley of Larracos lies a long, jet-black concierge shark, level 41, not long dead. The System gives the cause: suffocation, when the Semeru Warden finally decided to open the drain. Crawler Carl throws it in the air and punches it with Daughter's Kiss. The shark vaporises, and Carl and Donut both go sliding through the mud.

beats.headline: Under new ownership
beats.text: Quasar's message on arrival: remember that contract with Sensation Entertainment, Incorporated? The main character is dead and gone, but the guaranteed third season he and Carl negotiated is about to haunt the fuck out of them both. Sensation has just been purchased by a subsidiary of the Dream, and the owners are demanding their third season. Signet is not coming back, so whatever happens is going to be something stupid, and the new showrunners mean to use Carl's contractual obligation against him. Advice: stay away from any elites.

beats.headline: An exception in the fine print
beats.text: The warning about the ceasefire is mostly bad news. When it expires, only members of the defending team may remain within the city of Larracos, and that restriction holds until certain conditions are met. Then one line more: the restriction does not apply to the Shanty Town ring. Ten teams remain, and every one of them has just been told there is a ring around the city where they are allowed to stand.

beats.headline: The defending team names itself
beats.text: Carl and Donut come onto the ninth floor at Larracos, at the start of a sixty-hour ceasefire, and the defending side already has a name it chose for itself. Cascadia runs through the rules. The crawlers ally with it against the Bloc, which is every other faction on the board.

beats.headline: A sink for a recap
beats.text: For the record: Tempest is Quasar's niece, a young Nullian with a school report due on perceptions of the crawl, and she has been assigned Carl and Donut, because her teacher knows who her uncle is. Most people she interviews give their answers for free. He does not. The trade is that she fixes his plumbing, of which she knows nothing. She informs him that the only lesson she has learned today is that her uncle is a colossal prick, and tells him to start talking.

beats.headline: Terms, and a recap
beats.text: His opening recap is three sentences, the last of them The end. Terms improve when she threatens to tell her father that Quasar claimed to be her real dad: now we're talking, says her uncle. She records the eighth floor from him, cards, Quan, the dog girl with the flamethrower, the nun, and presses on what he skips: the homeless shelter, the last card, the spider in Carl's chest. The pipe comes away in her hands. Don't worry, kid, he says. The sink doesn't work anyway. It's an art piece.

beats.headline: Are you in danger?
beats.text: She turns the recorder off before she asks the serious question. Is he in danger for representing Carl? Real danger? Quasar wants to lie and decides against it; the kid deserves the truth. He thinks they all are, he tells her. It is the first time in his life he is glad they live so far out in the middle of nowhere. Filed without comment, beyond this: she asked it with the recorder off.

beats.headline: Team Retribution, defending
beats.text: Ten teams remain, and the defenders have a name: Team Retribution, the only team allowed to stay inside Larracos once the ceasefire runs out. Eight of the others form a truce called the Bloc and declare war on it, and on the Princess Posse. Team Retribution sends the Posse a truce offer of its own. Princess Donut asks whether that is the NPC team.

beats.headline: They buy a storyline instead of fighting for one
beats.text: Quasar has the warning ready before the sixty-hour ceasefire is out. The Dream have bought out the Vengeance of the Daughter and are pressing for fulfilment of the guaranteed third season written into it. An entertainment company, bought and aimed at a crawler.

beats.headline: One of those Eulogist pricks
beats.text: The coffee Paulie gives Crawler Carl carries a neural enhancement for the interface in his brain: a new menu, unregistered and highly illegal, that takes a little time to install. It works only with natural interfaces, only with the permission of the existing system, and only in this system's enhancement zone. If you are a Syndicate spy, a plant, or, in Paulie's words, one of those Eulogist pricks, it does not work at all. Carl drinks it.

beats.headline: Sold, with a season still owed
beats.text: Quasar warns Carl on arrival that the Dream has bought the programme out and intends to collect on the guaranteed third season.

beats.headline: Fifty achievements, and a groan
beats.text: Over fifty achievements to open. Most are stupid: Kombucha, for drinking vinegar. Chickenshit Exploit calls Ren a cheater, for the card totems I teleported into her fight with Quan. She never was one. Touched by a Demon: only one ever handed out, and it's mine, with a Celestial box. Then Unbirthing, for teleporting into Samantha's neck hole, in the AI's deep, throaty voice. It groans. It says it really liked that, and that I am in trouble. Reward: a Legendary Spicy Box.

beats.headline: What snipers wear
beats.text: Donut likes the hat, at least, even if she already has a few from the babababoons on the fourth floor. It is beige, which she does not care for, but extra floppy, which she does, though it clashes with her fit. They are boonie hats, Carl says, not bucket hats: what snipers wear. It adds a Targeting skill to zoom in and examine mobs from afar, like the gnomish farseerer but less awkward, and increases the range of all her spells. With the suit as well, she could snipe enemies from well over a mile.

beats.headline: Like a tassel
beats.text: Laid out on the floor, it looks to Donut like one of Signet's tattoo people fell through a paper shredder, and she will not look like a tassel. It's camouflage, Carl says; it's supposed to look like that. Long, shredded strips of colour-changing fabric blend into the background. It takes a jacket slot, yet magically covers her whole body, adding Blend into the Background and a Cone of Silence, and with the hat on too, everything is buffed further. Crupper, cloak and suit can all be worn at once.

beats.headline: Permission to break the truce
beats.text: Amayon, Prince of Sheol, claims to know what happened to my son, and he offers it in exchange for the deaths of his three brothers. The gods and the demons have a truce. I do not wish to break it, and I will do what is necessary to learn the truth. There is a way to do it without a war that burns the mortal world to ashes. My martyr will go to the Temple of Issitoq in a Club Vanquisher and gain permission from the High Cleric of the Watch. He still owes me the Soul Crystal of Apito. Do not disappoint me now.

beats.headline: A Canadian, with a better table
beats.text: I walk out of the crafting room in a snowsuit and a raccoon hat, and the two of them laugh at me. I don't pick the clothes. Human this time, Canadian, glasses. The table is upgraded higher than I have ever had it, and for the first time I can examine a potion and see how it was made. So, listen. Nobody reads a spellbook until we talk. Quan's cloak needs a plan before Donut puts it on. And the ceasefire can end early three ways. All unlikely. You never know.

beats.headline: Uh oh. It talks.
beats.text: An achievement catches up with Carl for looting a sapient weapon. Very few well-known crawlers use them, it notes, though they are usually quite powerful. Good luck with that. The reward is a pair of earplugs. Mordecai has already warned that such things can be both annoying and dangerous. Carl has not yet heard the sock say a word, but he has an uneasy feeling about it now, and makes a note to go back and examine it more closely.

beats.headline: Super sparkly
beats.text: Before the achievements, Donut wants Mongo healed. A Heal Severe Injury potion Carl made while he was part spider has already mended his burns, but the wing is still missing. Donut pushes forward a Heal Pet potion that Carl put on the ground before the vinegar goddess lost her head to Paz; now it is super sparkly and calls itself Revitalize Pet. It is purple and looks as if someone dumped half a jar of glitter into it. Super rare, Mordecai says, and expensive, but with his newest table upgrade he can learn the recipe without ruining it. It will grow the wing back in about an hour, though there may be scars.

beats.headline: Used Pet, and Janet Dominguez
beats.text: New achievement: Used Pet. Do you know how many animals were in cages during the collection? Fuck you, Janet Dominguez in Baton Rouge. Sprinkles was better off at the no-kill shelter. I really need to stop watching these memory recordings. Err, anyway. Terry, the dog who played Toto, was paid more than most of the cast. Used pets have value, and sometimes it isn't monetary. Sometimes they're delicious. You have adopted a pet that was once bonded to someone else. Reward: a Gold Pet Box.

beats.headline: A second pillow
beats.text: A platinum benefactor box arrives for Donut from the Apothecary in the same sitting as the tiara, and it holds a second charging pillow, purple where the first is red. The same ten-hour drain, and the same ruin after one hour. The difference is at the end of the description: this one drains any magical item, but transfers only to an absorption crystal on a like item. A ring's buff goes to a ring; sent to the wrong kind of item, the buff is lost. With two pillows, the tiara fills twice as fast.

beats.headline: Quan's cloak
beats.text: Before Carl opens his boxes, Mordecai has him pull out Quan's cloak. Watching Quan on the recap, they had assumed his flying, power bolt and shields came from the cloak; in fact its abilities are tailored to the wearer, with a focus on magic and the lowest stat, which is why Carl wants it for Donut. It is long and glows with a soft white light, silky, black on one side and blue on the other, with short arms. The system calls it a cloak, so it will fit a quadruped. Quan used its Find Weakened skill to pick off the weakest.

beats.headline: Thirty points, for two minutes
beats.text: Mordecai's new potion was once called Charisma Cheat, and the system now calls it MySpace Photo. For two minutes it makes the system read Donut's base charisma as 193 instead of 163, so the cloak will raise her constitution, base two, to 193. She learns Shield first, drinks the potion, collects a very rude Catfish achievement, and the cloak appears over her shoulders, ridiculously short on her. It's like a shawl, she says. Bad Attitude is level fifteen at once. Wall of Fire, Heal Critter and Puddle Jumper are to follow.

beats.headline: First on the pillow
beats.text: The first thing to put on the new tiara's charge pillow, Mordecai says, is the hat she just got with the targeting ability. And set a timer for ten and a half hours to be safe, because the pillows give no notice when a transfer is done, a bug for a very long time. Donut sets her new boonie hat on the red pillow, and it clicks into place.

beats.headline: A potion smashed on his rump
beats.text: WING GONE. Mongo looks. Wing GONE? Mother says sit. Carl smashes glass on Mongo's butt. Sparkly. Healing. Mongo does not mind.

beats.headline: Catfishing the system
beats.text: Before Donut puts on her new cloak, Mordecai pulls out a potion he has just made. It used to be called Charisma Cheat, but the system now calls it MySpace Photo. It tricks the system into thinking her base Charisma is 193 instead of 163, so that when she puts the cloak on it will raise her Constitution to 193 instead of 163 in time. That is why he wanted her to wait, and it lasts two minutes. From a base Constitution of two, Carl says, that is almost Katia-level resilience. Donut drinks it, gets a very rude Catfish achievement, and the cloak appears over her shoulders, so short on her it is like a shawl.

beats.headline: A potion called MySpace Photo
beats.text: Mordecai hands me a potion that used to be called Charisma Cheat and is now called MySpace Photo, which is rude. I learn Shield, then I drink it. For two minutes it makes the system think my charisma is 193 instead of 163, and in those two minutes I put on the champion's shawl, so my constitution rises to 193 over the next few days. From two. I get a very rude Catfish achievement. The cloak takes Bad Attitude straight to level 15, and Wall of Fire, Heal Critter and Puddle Jumper are on their way. I was hoping for Fireball.

beats.headline: Not a hat
beats.text: Donut has just received the Tiara of a Thousand Lights when a second benefactor box arrives, a platinum from the Apothecary. It is not a hat, as Carl expected, but another charging pillow, almost identical to the one that came with the tiara: ten hours to transfer fully, and the item ruined after one. This one is purple instead of red, and the warning at the end of its description is different. Almost a universal charger, Carl says, and tells Donut to check that an item is listed as a hat first. With two, she can fill the tiara twice as fast.

beats.headline: Two hats, two pillows
beats.text: Donut puts the pillows on the counter, her new boonie hat on the red one and her Tiara of the Inebriated Dragonfly on the other. Each makes an audible click as it touches; there is no other notification. What if the cleaner bot knocks it over, she asks. Mordecai tells her not to worry: once locked in place, an item has to be peeled off, like a magnet. She can move them to her room if she likes.

beats.headline: Donut wears his cloak
beats.text: Inventory update, ninth floor. Crawler Princess Donut opens a celestial box from Long Haul Biological Waste Management Solutions and takes out the Tiara of a Thousand Lights. In the same sitting she puts on Quan Ch's cloak and takes the benefits that come with it. The cloak does not ask where its previous owner is, and neither do I.

beats.headline: Glass on his bum
beats.text: Mongo looks at his missing right wing as if noticing it for the very first time, and Donut wants the potion now. Mordecai warns that it is expensive: he knows how to make them, but the ingredients are really rare. Donut tells Mongo to drink every drop and Carl to be gentle. Carl walks over and smashes the vial on Mongo's butt at the base of his tail. That was mean, Donut cries, but the Healing buff appears over Mongo's head. A potion thrown at someone else works, and for Mongo it is a lot safer than pouring it down his throat.

beats.headline: Long Haul Biological Waste Management Solutions
beats.text: Donut's celestial box from the sponsor holds it. She puts on Quan Ch's cloak in the same stretch and wears the two together, though nothing is charged into the tiara yet.

beats.headline: On the purple pillow
beats.text: A box gives Donut a second charging pillow, purple instead of red: it drains any magical item, but transfers only to a like item. Mordecai wants hats draining before they move on. Grumbling, Donut sets the pillows on the counter, her new boonie hat on the red one and the Tiara of the Inebriated Dragonfly on the other, and each clicks as it touches. When talk turns to which of her spells and skills Quan's cloak might raise to fifteen, she remembers that her Hover is part of the dragonfly tiara and wants it back on. Hover would not be worth it, Mordecai thinks, and her pool of skills runs to thousands anyway. Okay, she sniffs.

beats.headline: Parts for a fabricator
beats.text: A platinum, dog-shaped Tserendolgor box opens with more supplies for the automaton table, and this one is an XL box, so the chest is bigger than last time. Carl knows from the instruction manual that the XL boxes contain parts for a fabricator, something he has been hoping to build for a while. He pulls it all into his inventory.

beats.headline: Walk on Air, already obtained
beats.text: A Legendary toe ring, left pinky toe, and the description is insistent about the toe. Heart Balance holds a potion to fire automatically. Mind Balance protects against Enslavement and Conscription. Physical Balance lists Walk on Air as already obtained. I don't have Walk on Air. Li Jun does. I remember the taste of his eye, and what Shi Maria said about gaining his skills. I message him to apologise. He doesn't answer. I put the ring on anyway, set a gold healing potion to trigger at 2% health, and get one notice: Mind Balance is currently triggered.

beats.headline: A holster from the fans
beats.text: The first gold box Carl opens is a fan box: several boxes of ammunition, about 2,000 rounds, and an unenchanted black leather shoulder holster of the kind detectives wear on television, with Carl pressed into the leather in English. They do not know you very well, Donut says. The holster holds no gun, but Carl knows what they want him to do. He still has his father's Glock in his inventory, and he has no intention of ever wearing it outside his inventory, or of ever using it.

beats.headline: What an XL box holds
beats.text: Among Carl's boxes is a platinum, dog-shaped one from Tserendolgor, holding more supplies for his automaton table, and it is an XL box, so the chest is bigger than last time. Carl knows from the automaton instruction manual that the XL boxes contain parts for a fabricator, something he has been hoping to build for a while.

beats.headline: Set to two percent
beats.text: Carl's new Legendary toe ring, which must go on his left pinky toe and says so twice, can store one potion that triggers itself when his health meets a condition. He grits his teeth, slips the ring on, and is prompted to choose. He picks a gold-standard healing potion, set to trigger if his health reaches two percent.

beats.headline: Out of a drum kit
beats.text: The Celestial Heavy Metal box arrives as a full drum kit with pyrotechnics, Amayon's face on both bass drums and an ethereal demon playing speed metal behind it. Mongo screeches. The kit explodes, 666 hangs in the air in smoke, and all that is left is one glittering potion in a horned-skull bottle with a note tied round the top: Drink Me, and a demon hand giving the devil horns. The liquid is black and bubbling. Mordecai, shaking, calls it a Celestial-quality skill potion, and once Carl has examined it he rushes it off to his table. He comes back whispering that he could make these, with a few more table upgrades and some pretty specialized ingredients.

beats.headline: Drink me deep
beats.text: Mordecai tells Carl to take it right away, since whatever it gives him he will need to train with. The bottle speaks up in a deep, demonic voice: drink me, drink me deep. Carl pops the cork and drinks it manually, which is a mistake, because it tastes like ass. The potion groans as it dissipates into dust. For a fraction of a second he sees the burning hellscape of Sheol, smells the sulfur and feels worms crawling over him. A demon-skull button appears in his interface: the level-13 Gloom Wraith Phase, a non-corporeal lunge that passes through unenchanted weapons and flesh and scrambles any living thing unarmored against non-corporeal attacks.

beats.headline: Carrying Tran, chasing a head
beats.text: We're at the college in Larracos, filling out visitor passes and dealing with guards who are sluggish under a Despondent debuff, trying to reach a saferoom. Tran's wheelchair is gone, so we carry him, and it slows everything down. Then Samantha rolls past, screaming that she's going to kill a woman named Tish, and I go after her before the guards react. She's rolling, not floating, and she's fast. I get her trapped in a corner. She's really mad. I bring her back through the safe room.

beats.headline: Seriously scary bastards
beats.text: The skill potion comes back from my table, and I was wrong: I can make these. A few more table upgrades and some very specialised ingredients. Drink it now, I tell Carl, and train with whatever it gives you. Gloom Wraith Phase, level 13. So I say it straight. You two have always been powerful for your levels. You are now the most powerful crawlers I have ever worked with, including some who made it through floor 11. Then five minutes on practising, and on not phasing into solid objects.

beats.headline: A spider with baskets
beats.text: The Platinum Hell in a Handbasket Box holds a small patch of a spider. It's Shi Maria, Donut says; just a regular Reaper Spider Minion, says Carl. Mordecai grunts that it will give him access to a place he needs to stay out of, and Donut points out that telling Carl not to do something never works. Examined, it is black and silver, die cut in her horrifying shape but with a shorter neck and shorter hair, and wicker baskets lashed over the bulbous body. It grants access to the Midnight Market, a notice when traveling merchants are near, and five percent Dexterity. Carl is pretty sure the market is a bazaar hidden in the Desperado Club's bottom floor, and thanks to his Scavenger's Daughter, every patch he installs raises his stats, so this one should go on right away.

beats.headline: Waiting for Katia
beats.text: Carl stares at the bottle. The set comes with little plastic gloves, cotton swabs and a fold-out instruction pamphlet that is really, really long. Donut fusses that the number one crawler simply cannot be without eyebrows. His view counter has spiked, which tells him this has to be some sort of trap. Mordecai insists it works if he follows the instructions to a T, but they are convoluted, full of warnings against letting it touch anywhere you do not want hair, so after a fifth reading Carl waits for Katia.

beats.headline: My arch enemy, Tish
beats.text: I am ROLLING after Tish, my arch enemy, and I am very fast, and then this DOPPELGANGER catches me in a corner and will not let go. I tell everyone I will kill her mother and uninvite her from my bachelorette party. I am a woman scorned. My need for revenge is the only thing I know, and I will not be denied. Then Donut says if I come back I can see her new cloak. That does sound exciting. Okay. Did Carl show them his new pet yet? He promised I could name him.

beats.headline: One Mordecai can brew
beats.text: The Hell-Kissed Celestial Skill Potion of the Prince of Woe has Mordecai shaking. A Celestial-quality skill potion, he says, is not something he will ever be able to brew; then he takes it to his table to examine before Carl drinks. He comes back to say he was wrong. He can make these, with a few more upgrades to the table and some pretty specialized ingredients, and now he knows the recipe.

beats.headline: Samantha's arch enemy
beats.text: Larracos, the college, a visitor pass queue. Samantha rolled by Louis screaming after a woman named Tish and promising to kill her, and Katia Grim gave chase past guards carrying a Despondent debuff until she had the head cornered. Crawler Carl asked twice who the fuck Tish was. Princess Donut had forgotten about Tish entirely until that moment. Samantha, restrained: she is a woman scorned, and her need for vengeance against her arch enemy, Tish, is the only thing she knows.

beats.headline: Left pinky. Don't test me
beats.text: The Legendary Spicy Box is shaped like a giant strawberry that sizzles as it opens, and inside is a simple, silver, unadorned toe ring. The description insists, twice, on the left pinky toe. Walk on Air, already obtained: that makes no sense to Carl. He knows what the skill does, and he did not have it. It is what Li Jun used when he fought, and the taste of Li Jun's eye floods his mouth. He slips the ring on, sets a gold-standard healing potion to trigger at two per cent health, and gets an ominous notice. Mind Balance is currently triggered.

beats.headline: A fourth in a different colour
beats.text: The Legendary Hell Comes to Crawler Town box holds, as promised, a set of unenchanted bagpipes, and three third-tier personal space upgrade coupons plus a fourth one in a different colour. That's a town upgrade, says Mordecai: Carl will need it for his castle, and he and Donut already have a lower-tier one each from the Tina quest a few floors back. When Carl pulls the town upgrade coupon out, it tells him little, only that he must go to an owned town to use it.

beats.headline: Katia at the table
beats.text: Responsibilities are finally being shared out, Florin falling right into the position of general. Carl has given Katia access to his automaton table, and she is working at it right now, building something for Tran to use now that his wheelchair is gone. She has bigger plans than that. They are going to need vehicles, and she is getting the ball rolling.

beats.headline: A newsletter read three times
beats.text: For the record: the subject, a crocodilian, reads Damien's newsletter a third time beside his skyfowl neighbour, Justice Light, whose talon is shaking. Workers are being reassigned for an entire floor, which happens when the showrunners are cheap, and the Reavers are cheap. Justice Light is worried about his shop, his shelves and his art. The subject tells him they are to be snow castle guard captains in a settlement, still white-tagged, and that it is expensive for the showrunners if they die. That is not exactly true. He considers small lies acceptable when they calm a skyfowl.

beats.headline: One entry, and a brother
beats.text: The subject recognised Justice Light for what he was once the skyfowl started making familiar choices. It is obvious when someone has the cookbook, to anyone who has owned it. He applied at once to move from the lockpicking guild to the trap master guild, to be near his brother. He has never told Justice Light who he is, though neither of them has the cookbook any more. He wrote a single entry in it, afraid of being caught, and watching those who came after pour themselves into it has only made him feel worse. Guilt, maybe.

beats.headline: Fourteen seasons from freedom
beats.text: The eighth floor this season is mountains joined by wires and gondolas, and its crawlers are a flightless mantis who do poorly in the cold. The subject is watching one named York carefully. He has 14 seasons left, and he can taste freedom. Justice Light says he cannot fight crawlers; he means to refuse. What happens to him then? Nothing good, says the subject. He envies the skyfowl his conviction. He has a lot of violence in his heart, and he wants it aimed only at those who deserve it. His last recorded thought on the matter: fuck you all.

beats.headline: Refused to follow orders
beats.text: Dante, crocodilian, is dead. Class: Thief. Top level: 89. Dungeon exit: took a deal at the beginning of the 11th floor. Worked as a Game Guide and Guildhall Instructor in the Trap Master guild. Died 14 seasons short of his exit, while temporarily reassigned as an Ice Castle guard, by administrative action, for refusing to follow orders. Author of the Third Edition of the Dungeon Anarchist's Cookbook. The file does not say what the orders were. It lists his current status in one word: dead.

beats.headline: The third edition's author
beats.text: Dante, a crocodilian thief, wrote the third edition, and only a single entry of it, afraid of being caught. He took a deal at the start of the eleventh floor and worked as a game guide, then moved to the Trap Master guild to be near his skyfowl neighbour, a shopkeeper who had also owned the Cookbook. He never told him who he was. Reassigned with that neighbour as a castle guard for one season's eighth floor, fourteen seasons short of freedom, he refused to follow orders. Administrative action killed him.

beats.headline: War Leader III, then General
beats.text: Donut touches each of us to make us officers and lets me set up the hierarchy. I start at War Leader III. After some time with the base system that becomes Colonel, and after Donut tells me to upgrade myself, General. Most of the core group gets the same. The dancers get Sergeant First Class, so they can recruit and command the base troops. I'd named that rank Adjutant. They made me change it. Imani, Elle and I are leaving for headquarters to meet the adjutant.

beats.headline: Eyebrows, eyelashes, and a failed spell
beats.text: Carl waited for me to do his hair tonic. Eyebrows first, then eyelashes, which is almost the pubic hair recipe, so I'm careful. He asks, quietly, if I'm okay. I'm hanging in there. Mordecai is brewing something that might help with the rehab, and I'll take it tomorrow, before the ceasefire ends. The head mix can only sit for five seconds, so I have an otter water mage, one of the strippers, ready to power-wash it off. As a mercenary, his spell won't cast in the saferoom. Carl's hair now reaches his waist.

beats.headline: Small thing, in and out
beats.text: Small thing. Jumps IN mouth. Mother yells. Mongo swallows. Hurk. Hurk. Out again. Small thing wants back in. Mongo runs. Then: bowl. Small thing pushes bowl. SOUP. Mongo licks it all.

beats.headline: A meatball that is not red
beats.text: Carl zaps a level-1 tummy acher onto the table: half the size of his fist, a spattering of black hairs on its head, Garret's underbite and single round tooth. The first of these things Carl ever saw was red-tagged. This one is not, and he does not know whether that is because it used to be Ren's pet or because of his peace symbol patch plus his higher charisma.

beats.headline: She calls it Cousin Oliver
beats.text: Carl has been keeping a pet from me. In all my life I have never felt a sense of betrayal this profound. It is a baby tummy acher Ren hoisted on him, it has five weaknesses, and it hopped into Mongo's mouth and he swallowed it. It is Cousin Oliver. Scrappy Doo. A late addition that makes a perfectly good cast worse. It gets three strikes, and it used one growling at Mongo. I offered to sell it to Katia's boyfriend for five gold. Carl says it is not for sale.

beats.headline: Uh-oh
beats.text: Katia reads the instructions and mixes in little plastic trays, an extra set of hands holding Carl's head still: eyebrows first, then the eyelashes, a mix almost identical to the pubic hair recipe. For the head she mixes in the large tray and sends Louis for Splash Zone; a splotch lands on the table, and its rock-like surface sprouts hair. Then she splotches the cold tonic on and counts down from five. Uh-oh, says Splash Zone: his water spell counts as offensive and will not cast in the saferoom. Carl runs to the shower, because the tonic adds length for as long as it stays on, and comes out with hair to his waist that grows back when cut. About two weeks, Mordecai says.

beats.headline: Our room and Katia's
beats.text: Florin, Imani and Elle are leaving the city for the headquarters, to meet the adjutant and get it ready. Once they are set up, the plan is to use the doggie door upgrade to fast travel from the city to the headquarters. In the meantime, Carl and Donut have already installed the doggie door upgrade in their room, along with Katia's.

beats.headline: Still at the college
beats.text: Crawler Carl reconstructs the file. Ghazi wrote to the college here in Larracos for help, and the letters showed that his ex-girlfriend, Tish, still worked there, and that he had left her for the doll. Samantha proposes to use Louis's new toy to kill her. Princess Donut rules that subject should not be held accountable; that was one hundred percent Ghazi. If she is not allowed to blow Tish up, Samantha adds, Juice Box is going to hear about Louis's affair. Louis says: what?

beats.headline: Died five times, and stronger for it
beats.text: A pet-class mob. The System’s notice for one that has not yet bonded to a crawler reads like a card on a cage: this one has died five times, and its stats are all buffed by 125% because of it. It has five weaknesses, which can be examined only by whoever bonds with it or holds it in a carrier.

beats.headline: Bonded on one bowl of chowder
beats.text: Carl lets the level-one tummy acher out onto the table, and it hops straight into Mongo's open mouth. Mongo swallows, then yaks it back up, giggling. Carl's food box now serves everything chowder style, so his breakfast sandwich comes crumbled into seafood soup; he puts the bowl down, the meatball dives in, growls at Mongo, and its dot turns orange. One bowl, and bonded. Then it pushes the bowl over to Mongo. The naming window will not close until Louis comes up with a knight's name built on Ren's.

beats.headline: A mantis on the eighth floor
beats.text: From a season long past, when the crawl was run by the Reavers. The eighth level that season was mountains connected by wires and gondolas. The crawlers were a strange type of mantis, not the common kind, who could not fly and did poorly in the cold. There was a crawler among them named York, and an NPC named Dante, who had once left a single entry in the Cookbook himself, was watching him carefully.

beats.headline: Tinsel on the guild floor
beats.text: Waiting on the elevator, I notice a few pieces of tinsel on the guild floor. The Christmas decorations came from the memory simulation and vanished when we got here. This tinsel stayed, so somebody looted it on an earlier floor, from somewhere real. Everything seems normal to me now, and that's the problem: real and make-believe mixed together, and the make-believe often the more dangerous. I think of Pater Coal. I think of Lightning Lou, and how close I came. Paulie's words come back: be sure. On my chest, the eye blinks.

beats.headline: So close to the edge
beats.text: Crawler Carl thinks of Lightning Lou, the old dog at the gas station in Florida left to spend Christmas Day alone. Carl curled up beside him on the floor and contemplated his options, and came so close to the edge that it almost broke his mind to think about it. Paulie's words come back to him: be sure it's your only option. On his chest, the eye blinks.

beats.headline: Firas's name for it
beats.text: My celestial box gives me an Airship Portal, which is an elevator up to a hangar, and a ship. Katia says it's not an airplane, more like a drone thing, a tilt rotor. It runs on a soul crystal, like the Twister. I named it Party Planner, 'cause that's what Firas wanted to call the Twister, and I told him it was stupid. It's a bomber, too. The System calls the model Casket in the Sky. Carl says it looks like a death trap. Katia said that too, especially after she read the description.

beats.headline: The reward for having survived being condemned
beats.text: It comes out of the celestial box Louis earned for outliving a goddess's mark for death on the floor before. Two items: a tier III guild upgrade called an Airship Portal, and the ship itself, a silver tilt-rotor he names Party Planner, the name Firas once suggested for another vehicle.

beats.headline: His limitations, remembered
beats.text: Ninth floor. Crawler Carl, turning over how every person and object down here is real, imaginary or somewhere between, comes back to Pater Coal: the high cleric of the Emberus temple at Club Vanquisher, taken over by the AI, who seemed unable to separate the dungeon's story from what was actually being done to the crawlers. We all have our limitations, the cleric had said. Carl's own assessment of that sentence is on file. Terrifying.

beats.headline: His great-great-grandfather's hat
beats.text: Intake record. At the foot of the college stairs a dwarf officer, star over his head, feeds jerky to Mongo and Rend. Squat, young, beardless, a long thin moustache; samurai-like vest flaring like a bell, feathers straight up from his helmet, a wide sickle on his back, every piece enchanted. He bows. Honored Warlords. Crawler Donut loves his hat; it was his great-great-grandfather's. War Leader Arief, level 80 Semeru dwarf, commander of the Larracos Defense Force Infantry. Status: Despondent. His goddess is dead, and he cannot worship another.

beats.headline: In the traditional manner
beats.text: Crawler Donut asks in chat whether this nice dwarf knows who flooded his city, and who killed his goddess. Crawler Carl tells her not to bring it up. Arief, meanwhile, is the first NPC Carl has heard call himself an NPC out loud. Juice Box wants Carl privately first. And, turning to Louis with another bow, she would like to solidify the great truce in the traditional manner. Through marriage. They would like to get it over with right away.

beats.headline: Through the portal with the water
beats.text: I went through the Gate with the water. I lay low with the ones who lived through it, and when they were ready I told them. What they are. What this whole place is. Enough of them believed me that they call me Warlord now, and a Warlord has people, and a Warlord has opinions about alliances. I have sent War Leader Arief to Carl's people with my terms. The terms are Louis. He marries me. That is the alliance.

beats.headline: Juice Box tells them
beats.text: She came through with the Larracos flood, and now an NPC calls himself an NPC out loud for the first time.

beats.headline: The city he meant
beats.text: Entering the Larracos College of Magic. Crawler Carl steps outside and, for the first time, sees the city whole: towers growing out of the ring like crystals, an alabaster saferoom tower wrapped in flowering vines, an observatory, the scent of drained ocean under the flowers. He thinks of the subject, the Cookbook author who loved this city so much it drove him mad to see it destroyed. Now he can see what Priestly meant. It is like something out of a Tolkien novel.

beats.headline: What the Semeru dug into
beats.text: Carl examines War Leader Arief, a young Semeru dwarf in feathered, parade-ready armour, and the System tells his people's story. They farmed and mined a paradise inside the volcano and dug toward the goddess below them, Ysalte, until they struck the roots of the All Tree and stopped. They built their castle along those roots, a monument and an apology. Scolopendra's nine-tier attack hit them hardest of all: millions before that day, fewer than 10,000 now. Arief is Despondent, because his goddess is dead.

beats.headline: Down to the roots
beats.text: The System gives the history. The Semeru once lived in peace in this fertile volcanic level, farming, mining, learning, and loving their goddess, Ysalte. They dug to reach her; a city of scholars grew in the pit. What they found were roots of the All Tree, which connects everything, and there they stopped, and built their castle along the roots as a monument and an apology. The nine-tier attack still hit them hardest. Millions before; fewer than ten thousand after. The city itself was untouched, and the survivors became its stewards.

beats.headline: No longer only caretakers
beats.text: Everything Crawler Carl had heard made the Semeru a drunk, defeated people who kept the castle clean and rarely fought their invaders. Not now. On a balcony a dwarf is teaching a boy to stab with a sword. Their war leader arrives in parade armour with a sickle, calls the crawlers Honored Warlords, and carries a Despondent debuff for his dead goddess. Donut asks in chat whether they know who flooded the city, and who killed the goddess. Carl tells her not to bring it up.

beats.headline: Out the college door
beats.text: Carl and Donut go to Katia's personal space and, thanks to the new Doggie Door upgrade, leave by the college entrance, several rings higher, which gives them the chance to recruit along the way. Katia and Elle have been working the chats, but a recruit has to be physically touched to be officially enlisted, so people will meet them on the road.

beats.headline: They paid the license fee
beats.text: Princess Donut writes to me in capitals that Louis's shirt is an outrage. It is a Donut Holes shirt, and the Donut Holes paid the license fee, so it is a perfectly legitimate brand and her merch is doing quite well. She asks whether she gets any of the money. Okay, so: no. If she reaches the tenth floor she gets a stipend and can negotiate a small percentage based on her licensing fee, and past a threshold she gets a percentage automatically. I don't know the threshold. I don't think anybody has ever gotten close.

beats.headline: A name a dwarf wants revenge on
beats.text: Entered into the file on the word of a dwarf named Arief, who swings his sword and promises revenge. Architect Houston: leader of the Madness, a Viceroy outworlder. He caught Arief's brother trying to sabotage the Madness fortifications, and the brother was tortured before Juice Box got in and ended his suffering. Crawler Donut asks whether this is the one Juice Box decapitated at the pre-production meeting. It is not. That was one of his surgeons. Nobody has managed to get into Houston's lair beside the throne room, which is called his operating theater.

beats.headline: Sixty-six levels, counted upward
beats.text: Guided tour. Larracos has sixty-six levels, Arief says, not all full rings, numbered from the bottom: the college is on fifty, homes on forty-nine. The water reached level 39, drained to 29 and clogged, and Juice Box had it kept that way; it now sits at level 3, just over the castle's highest tower. His uncle drained the Piccadilly theatre and found it full of jellyfish. The glowing things at the ramp corners are explosives, in case the enemy gets in. There are some on every other down ramp.

beats.headline: There was another season
beats.text: Arief mentions another season, when orcs marched down the streets and Reavers jumped in. Crawler Carl stops in the road. Arief does not remember it himself; he believes he is new, like most of them. His uncle remembers dozens of seasons, is one of the Jatismara, and sits on Juice Box's war council. Most of them know about their past lives. Asked by Britney whether his uncle remembers dying: no. For most of them, Arief believes, one death is forever.

beats.headline: Revenge on Architect Houston
beats.text: Arief pulls the curved blade off his back with a shing, and everyone jumps, Mongo included. When the fighting starts, he says, he takes his revenge on Architect Houston, leader of the Madness, who caught his brother sabotaging their fortifications. His brother was tortured, they say, before Juice Box got in and ended his suffering. The raids bloodied every enemy camp and got inside every inner circle but the nagas', he adds: a court of assassins, where no changeling or spy has ever got in, and where even Juice Box does not try.

beats.headline: The Sultana behind her veils
beats.text: Arief calls the nagas a court of assassins, not warriors; no changeling or spy has ever reached their inner sanctum, and even Juice Box will not try. Their warlord is the Sultana, in life the crown princess and daughter of the naga king, play-acting the Sepsis Whore, the sultana of the old histories who had 198 daughters before 99 sons and supposedly poisoned almost all of the sons. In the old days, her honor guard were sentenced to deferred death for looking at her. The naga team loses every season. She has never once been killed in the game.

beats.headline: Grand Re-Opening, under new management
beats.text: It opened back up today. The square concrete building on level four of Larracos has only the red bottom half of its neon arrow lit, and a hand-painted sign on a sheet across the entrance: Grand Re-Opening. Under New Management. Arief leads the group through the empty entrance bar, the Headlamp Colonnade, past a gnoll bartender whom Donut's sunglasses read as a changeling, and down a hidden tunnel to an office. There the one-eyed old gnoll manager, Hunger Hammy, leaps across the desk and kisses Louis.

beats.headline: Arief's tour
beats.text: War Leader Arief walks the group down from the college on level fifty through a city whose floodwater has fallen to its bottom three levels, still high enough to cover the castle. Juice Box has been waking its NPCs to the truth of what they are.

beats.headline: An uncle among the Jatismara
beats.text: Arief mentions another season, and Carl stops in the street. Arief does not remember one; he believes he is new, like most of them. But some have the memory quickened. His uncle remembers dozens of seasons, fewer than Juice Box, and as one of the Jatismara sits on her war council. Most of the NPCs now know about their past lives. Some shopkeepers and patrons are made differently and cannot understand. For most of them, Arief believes, a death is forever.

beats.headline: Singing on the down ramps
beats.text: The lower the tour goes, the busier Larracos gets. A squad of dwarves jogs past singing a military running cadence, hammers and sickles on their shoulders. The down ramps are mined, the flooded castle kept underwater by choice, and the NPC raids have reached the inner circle of every enemy camp but the nagas'. Most of them know about their past seasons; for most of them, one death is forever.

beats.headline: The blade goes through him
beats.text: Subject is present in the Desperado Club as adjutant to Team Retribution. Juice Box reports that she touched his arm and found it solid, and that when she attempted to decapitate him her blade passed through him like a ghost. The protection a crawler has for a while after regenerating appears, in his case, to be permanent. She also reports a worm in his brain, of a different species from the one in Carl's rock friend. Carl names it: a Valtay worm. The NPCs are not allowed to kill him.

beats.headline: Not what I wanted
beats.text: Carl. You didn't do what I wanted. We wanted everybody protected, with regeneration. He says they would never allow it, so they did the next best thing: they made it so we can kill them. It'll have to do. I show him most of my papers. Some go in the drawer. I ask about Ruby. The rules of this world are a lot. A voice told me I would not be allowed to talk to someone I tried to meet. I don't have menus. I do have messaging, so now Louis and I can talk whenever we like.

beats.headline: Game of Thrones stuff
beats.text: She's messaging me non-stop about getting married so our houses are bonded. It's all Game of Thrones stuff, man. Out loud she's all confident, but in the messages she's different. I think she's really scared, in over her head. Carl says I don't have to. I already told her I would. If the NPCs turn on us, we're screwed. So I stand up, take her hand, and say we should get married right away. Donut makes me say I love you. Then she makes me say it twice.

beats.headline: Hovels nobody built
beats.text: There is usually a shanty town. Never one like this. It appeared soon after the flooding, supposedly built by displaced NPCs, except that nobody built it: the hovels simply sprang up, a full ring round the top entrance of Larracos, large enough to count as a settlement. It has new shops and new NPCs, food markets and temples, and one hard-to-find Club Vanquisher entrance, but no weapons or mercenary markets. Its mayors keep dying. The gnoll Theora lost a single combat to a cheat. The current mayor, Juice Box says, pained, is someone else.

beats.headline: Ferdinand holds the interface
beats.text: Juice Box and Louis are reunited, and he is visibly uneasy about the marriage. Then she lays out the practical problem: Ferdinand is mayor of Shanty Town, just outside Larracos, and he holds the warlord interface for the team, because he is technically from outside. Nothing this side of the wall moves without a cat's cooperation. Drick is the adjutant.

beats.headline: Guarding the door
beats.text: Arief leads the party down past flooded shops and through a panel in a kitchen wall to a hidden tunnel, and stands guard at the door while Juice Box lays her papers out. When Juice Box greets Louis with a kiss that does not stop, Crawler Carl exchanges a look with the dwarf at the door, who seems as sceptical as he is. The wedding itself is small and fast, and Arief guards that door too.

beats.headline: A bowler hat for Shanty Town
beats.text: Warlord on High, Sir Ferdinand, level 100, co-warlord of Team Retribution, arrives in the vestibule seated on his adjutant's head, in a turban improvised from tissues. He wants his rhinoceros mount and his hat. Carl offers a temporary replacement from Quan Ch's inventory, a bowler hat that decapitates and returns when thrown, in exchange for the mayorship of Shanty Town. The transfer requires Carl and Donut to pay gold. The trade is accepted, and the truce is renamed The Good Guys. Subject's remark on the matter: I'm a very handsome boy.

beats.headline: Hamed takes the club
beats.text: Clarabelle, alive and in her chair, tells Carl and Donut they are banned from the Desperado Club by the new management, who has banned all crawlers for his first few days. He keeps bodyguards with him at all times, not exactly NPCs and not exactly former crawlers, and more security than she has ever seen. The surviving cretins and sai were airlocked off to the mercenary markets. His name is Hamed: the Night Wyrm, leader of the Guild of Suffering, husband of the late Astrid, and father of Damascus Steel and Anaconda, who are supposedly in the club hunting him.

beats.headline: New management at the club
beats.text: Clarabelle, alive, at her post: crawlers are banned by order of the new management. He wants his first days to go smoothly. He is very particular and very serious about security, and has a whole slew of bodyguards, not exactly NPCs and not exactly former crawlers. His name is Hamed. Crawler Carl keeps his face still. The real name of the Night Wyrm, the head of the Guild of Suffering, husband to the late Astrid. His sons are supposedly still in the club, hunting him.

beats.headline: I wish my mom was here
beats.text: Changeling weddings come in two parts, which is kind of a relief. The small one is now, in the grimy entrance bar: no rings, no officiant, no singing, and Donut is mad about all three. Juice Box goes to her blank form and we hold hands. I catch Carl staring and tell him I wish my mom was here. Then we whisper vows we made up on the spot, in each other's ears. We'll say them out loud at the Confirmation, in about a month. And that's it. We're married.

beats.headline: Airlocked to the markets
beats.text: On the way down through Larracos, the city's own mercenary markets are still flooded out and ruined. Further down, the Desperado Club reopens under a new manager who admits no crawlers and wants no visitors. Clarabelle is lucky to have kept her job. Everybody else was not so lucky: the surviving cretins and sai were airlocked out and sent off to the mercenary markets.

beats.headline: Not his fiancée
beats.text: Ferdinand has been telling people he is my fiancé. In the vestibule I make him say it: he is not really my fiancé. He adds not yet, and winks at Carl.
