I would rather have a sexual affair with the bloating corpse of a syphilis-infested cocker spaniel. Yes, I have his hat; I found it after the Butcher's Masquerade, and he can have it back when he stops being disgusting and changes the name of our alliance. Then Carl pulls out a bowler hat I have never been given.

beats.headline: Part of Rosetta's price
beats.text: Rosetta wants the toraline and what is left of the ink Shi Maria brewed for Carl's tattoo. Then she wants access to his saferoom, so they can get to work. Give me access to your bomber's studio, too, she says. And three million gold. She glares at the finger-sized sliver of vegetable he hands over. Better make it four million.

beats.headline: Tipid fills him in
beats.text: He tells Carl about Doctor Hu and the Crawler Project in the Meadowlark saferoom.

beats.headline: From the dead pig
beats.text: Rosetta has her hand on the eye tattoo on Carl's chest and is demanding his toraline out loud. In chat, where they cannot hear, she asks something else: does he still have the credit chit he got from the dead pig? It is the card they looted off the orc hunter on the sixth floor, and Donut has it in her inventory. Good, Rosetta writes. She will get it from her.

beats.headline: The fourth edition's author
beats.text: Tipid, a Crest poisoner, wrote the fourth edition. He got out at the start of the twelfth floor with a key that let only one of them through a door, and he chose himself over his friend Horatio. He had negotiated an extra season to keep that key; he tore it off its chain and threw it across the table. Damage to his brain took his whole pension and a loan to repair. He settled in a Crest system and worked for a waste management company. Current status: Colonel in the Princess Posse.

beats.headline: Rosetta's cold hand
beats.text: Rosetta, newly arrived with Tipid, pushes her hand down the front of Carl's shirt and lays it on the Bedlam Bride tattoo, her fingers like ice. Then she wants the toraline, and the ink the spider used to make the tattoo. He hands over a finger-sized slice of the root and the glass container, still hot to the touch, with only a few thimblefuls of ink left, and feels the eye blink on his chest, as if her touch has woken it.

beats.headline: In the Princess Posse
beats.text: Carl and Donut are in the Meadowlark saferoom, and Tipid is telling it to them: fifty thousand of us under their banner, and I am one of them. People who got out of a crawl once and know exactly what one is, and signed up for another anyway, under the banner of a cat. He gets emotional about it. Nobody gives him a hard time. We had the same faces on when we signed.

beats.headline: Only for new crawlers
beats.text: Subject, drunk as usual, listens to Tipid describe what the Crawler Project won, citizenship, healthcare and housing for released crawlers, and grunts with derision. That perk is only for new crawlers, she says, and they will still be bled dry on taxes. The old guard will be extra fucked on release. The rich like their faces on screen while they donate, and they will fight like hell when a scruffy former crawler tries to settle in their system. She takes a long swig, looks at Mongo with wet eyes, and wanders off.

beats.headline: Why the authorities cracked down
beats.text: Tipid explains where the network came from. Doctor Hu formed it beside the Crawler Project: smaller, more focused, with far less support, and with the purpose of ending the crawl altogether. The residual in the homeless man's body at the Florida shelter, Paulie, was one of several actions that finally brought the authorities down on the non-profit.

beats.headline: Doctor Hu, per Tipid
beats.text: Tipid supplies more of the file. Subject, as Doctor Hu, runs the Crawler Project, an NFC for former crawlers, whose campaigning made every newly released crawler a Syndicate citizen with free healthcare and guaranteed housing. He also formed the Open Intellect Pacifist Network, a smaller group aimed at ending the crawl altogether. It was his idea to refurbish a garbage freighter into a passenger liner and call for former crawlers to come back in. When they were accused of being a terrorist organization, they scattered. Tipid does not know where he is.

beats.headline: The garbage truck people cancel
beats.text: I get a notification that a sponsorship has been cancelled. The garbage truck people, for a conflict of interest, whatever that means, and Carl says huh. At least I opened their box already. There is going to be an auction for a new one. I do hope it lines up properly with my brand this time. Veriluxx was a dud, Empress D'nadia sold my sponsorship, and it would be nice to have something to complement the Apothecary, even if she does sponsor half the dungeon.

beats.headline: They are already there when he walks in
beats.text: Rosetta, Tipid, Justice Light and fifty thousand others have signed on. Carl gets emotional.

beats.headline: Four million gold
beats.text: I tell the room this is not an attack, it is a self-correcting measure given in the spirit of comradery, and I smack Carl on the forehead. Then I hug him. Comrade. We are here. I put my hand on the tattoo on his chest and ask how much he has left. Of what? The toraline, and the spider's ink. In chat, where they cannot hear: does he still have the credit chit from the dead pig? Donut has it. Then I take the items: a finger-sized slice, and the ink. I want his saferoom, his bomber's studio and three million gold. Better make it four.

beats.headline: Mayor, for a bowler hat
beats.text: Crawler Carl wanted to be mayor of Shanty Town, and the mayor was Ferdinand. The deal: Ferdinand transferred the mayorship, the jewel on his necklace went away, and he got a bowler hat to wear until they trade it back for his turban in a day or so. Juice Box was on board. Carl's reasoning, on the walk back: if the bad guys can freely enter Shanty Town once the truce breaks, it is a liability, and it has a defence system of its own.

beats.headline: What Tipid remembers
beats.text: Tipid, in a zero zone, is told he has brain lesions and needs to get to a Viceroy system for repair, at the cost of a good chunk of his pension. The word frightens him. He remembers the Viceroys: the masked monsters of his own Faction Wars, who called themselves the Madness. Their chief surgeon had a spell that cooked your brain, made your teeth fall out, and turned the liquid in your eyeballs to acid. That is what happened to Rosaline.

beats.headline: Doctor Hu, and the Crawler Project
beats.text: Carl needs the whole of it, so I give it to him in order. Doctor Hu. The Crawler Project. How fifty thousand of us came to be standing under the Princess Posse's banner. None of it is anything he would ever have been told from inside; that is the thing about being retired, you learn what the ones still crawling are not shown. He listens. That is rarer than it sounds.

beats.headline: Rosetta wants it
beats.text: In the Meadowlark saferoom, Rosetta puts an icy hand on the Bedlam Bride tattoo and asks how much he has left. Of the toraline, and of the ink the spider used to make that tattoo. Carl pulls out a finger-sized slice of the vegetable and the glass container of Shi Maria's ink, still hot to the touch, a few thimblefuls left; Mordecai has more toraline, but not much. Give me access to your saferoom and your bomber's studio, Rosetta says, and three million gold. Better make it four.

beats.headline: A finger-sized slice
beats.text: Rosetta, in person, puts an icy hand on the Bedlam Bride tattoo and asks how much Carl has left. Of what? The toraline, she says, and the ink the spider used to make that tattoo. Over chat she warns him to say nothing out loud. He hands over all he has, a finger-sized slice, and the still-hot glass of the ink Shi Maria brewed, a few thimblefuls left. Mordecai has more of the toraline, he says, but not much. Give me access to your saferoom, she says, and we will get to work.

beats.headline: Out again, in a tutu
beats.text: Carl adds his strength to the fortress's oversized, badly hammered door, and it flies all the way open and throws him and Tipid to the ground. Someone shouts that she is out again. Big Tina, allosaurus, wearing a pink tutu, stamps into the clearing and hops up and down in front of Mongo, waving her little wand. Mongo hops up and down in front of her too.

beats.headline: Hup, hup, hup
beats.text: We step out of the bait-shop safe room into a building site: watchtowers, a palisade they are testing with fireballs, a channel being cut up toward the lake. A level 62 Fortification Engineer named Penn drops a steel beam, hugs me, kisses me on the cheek, and starts shouting. Hup, hup, hup. Then thousands of them, humans, skyfowl, crocodilians, bune, yenk, fists and wings in the air, until the ground shakes. Tipid moves to chat. This is for you. This is what you built. In less than three days we'll be waist deep in blood. Then they all go back to work.

beats.headline: The caiman lifts the wall
beats.text: We only get so many officers, so the builders and the crawlers are going in as sergeants and chiefs, which lets them change the camp. Everyone else is legionnaire, with corporals running teams. A wall section goes over and buries itself in the dirt, and I go to help. My card from the last floor still comes once a day. I call him: a giant caiman, twenty-five feet of him. He gets his snout under the wall and heaves it up while the workers push. He times out before long. I come back grumbling about artillery.

beats.headline: Digging in
beats.text: NPCs and former crawlers build the defences together: the changelings and the flesh golems started the stronghold, and a few thousand of the newcomers chose the Fortification Engineer race so they could build fast and level while they do it.

beats.headline: Blood bar rules are back
beats.text: The blood bar rules are back in force inside the safe rooms. I tell Carl now, while knowing it still costs nothing. Around us the NPCs, the mercenaries and the rest of us former crawlers are building the defences on the same line, three kinds of people this format has always kept apart, working shoulder to shoulder. I do not have a rule for that. I am watching it closely.

beats.headline: Read by the next one
beats.text: A note added by crawler Ikicha, eleventh edition. Ikicha's kind are castrated and cast out, a perspective as different as could be from the one who came before: York, who appears to have come from a hive, yet says he always felt alone his entire life. Reading his words, Ikicha feels kinship anyway, and asks the question on the page. Did he survive? Then a prayer that anyone who gets free seeks out those who came before.

beats.headline: What one is actually for
beats.text: An elite is waiting in the antechamber to the team's flag room during the ceasefire, pressed into service as a bomb by a production company that wants Carl off the board. Baroness Victory steps out and puts him down before the satchels can go off. The office is classed as a non-combatant observer, which makes the moment a curiosity for the rule book as much as a rescue.

beats.headline: Herman the Fleet does not get to finish
beats.text: Carl, Donut, Tipid and Florin come into the Fortress of Unyielding Power and Authority, and Florin walks them through the ceasefire rules. Then our own Elite, Herman the Fleet, leaned on by Sensation Entertainment, reveals what he actually is, which is a delivery system for a bomb. I deal with him. An adjutant may do that. It is in the rules, and I have read the rules.

beats.headline: The scouts, over chat
beats.text: I stand in the empty throne room pretending to examine it and ask Florin in chat, because the walls may still have ears. Only someone with the Scout endorsement crosses a border in peacetime. A scout who is discovered gets teleported home and cannot go stealth again until the fighting starts, and a trap still kills them. We get eighteen. The towers are for keeping their scouts out, and they have already sent back one from the Dream and one from the Prism. Florin bets his left sack we're infested with spies anyway.

beats.headline: Herman the Fleet
beats.text: In the Princess Posse's castle, the only other dot on the map is an elite: Herman the Fleet, ogre strongman, a legionnaire of the Princess Posse, third brother of Grimaldi's strongmen. He is writhing at a desk. He has been waiting. Supposed to do it already. Been fighting it. Tell brother sorry. He is wearing explosive satchels. The orc adjutant steps out and kills him with an axe, then calls foul: an unlawful assassination attempt by Sensation Entertainment, exerting undue influence on one of their elites.

beats.headline: Still pregnant, and family
beats.text: Kiwi is very pregnant and has been carrying since the Hunting Grounds, which is a long time to be in that condition even by this dungeon's standards. Big Tina, for her part, has decided that Mongo is her father. Nobody in the fortress has the standing, the courage, or frankly the desire to correct her.

beats.headline: Kiwi goes inside
beats.text: Big one says PA-PA. Bear comes out. Kiwi. KIWI. Sniff. Kiwi hugs Mongo. Mongo stays still. Kiwi goes inside. Big one goes inside. Mongo sniffs air. Peep.

beats.headline: A name she cannot change
beats.text: Fortress of Unyielding Power and Authority. It is a terrible name, and it will not let me change it, because the Sledge and the changelings kept changing it back and forth until the AI told them to shove it. Carl reads out the initials and laughs. I am absolutely not calling my castle that. It's obscene, and the bad guys are going to laugh at us. I give Florin a direct order not to spread it. He has already put it in the chat.

beats.headline: Satchels under the shirt
beats.text: In a castle antechamber, Elite Herman the Fleet, ogre strongman, fights something inside himself, snaps a desk in half and tells Carl he was supposed to do it already. He is covered in explosive satchels. Donut fires a Magic Missile at his face and Baroness Victory puts an axe through his head; Carl takes the destabilising body into his inventory. Victory calls it an unlawful assassination attempt by Sensation Entertainment: the Dream, which now owns the company, was exerting undue influence on one of its elites. She is filing a grievance.

beats.headline: What she says of her sister
beats.text: The Princess asks whether my sister was nice or a jerk. She means the orc queen, who died when my nephew attempted to assassinate them. Ugloo and I once had a very similar outlook on life. When she married into the royal family, she lost a great deal of who she was. We had not spoken in a long while, but before she died she wrote to ask if I would be an adjutant this season. She was going to the Scolopendra Club to meet the king. I ask why the Princess wishes to know.

beats.headline: Have they stopped
beats.text: Subject arrives in the flag room at Katia's legs, wearing a Dallas Cowboys jersey as a dress, having flown in on Louis's new airship, which she prefers to the old one. Skarn is in the hangar playing with it; Louis has hired gremlins, and they have bought door guns. Carl kneels and tells her she should not have to think about that sort of thing. She asks why she should not think about killing outworlders. Have they stopped thinking about killing her?

beats.headline: Mind Balance, level nine
beats.text: I clear my screen by mistake, and when it comes back the spam folder comes with it. Gloom Wraith Phase failed to activate. Prevented by Mind Balance. Mind Balance has risen to level nine. It was five a few hours ago. Pages of it. Shi Maria has been trying to cast through me, and the bombs on that ogre were non-magical. If the phase had gone off, Donut would be in pieces. The skill is getting stronger. So is she. It's a race, and she's winning it. I message Mordecai.

beats.headline: Four phases, and the Ramp-Up
beats.text: Victory lays out the phases: the Ceasefire, the Ramp-Up, Open Hostilities, and the Peeling of Larracos once four teams remain. The Ramp-Up lasts 180 hours. In it there are no celestial summonings, no offensive magic, no teleporting, and nobody but a scout enters enemy land except through a kilometre-wide gate. Weapons work; the spells attached to them do not. Traps must be static. It is designed to force bloody, hand-to-hand combat, against teams who brought their own pulse rifles and power armour and would like it over in a week.

beats.headline: Recruited, at last
beats.text: Mordecai brews a potion that negates auras, and with it I can be recruited. I am. The moment it is done, I ask one thing: my squad builds the defences in and around Shanty Town. Carl agrees. The town is a ring around Larracos now, and it belongs to the Posse.

beats.headline: Rolling hills, and the northern border
beats.text: On Baroness Victory's map the Operatics hold pie piece number two, rolling hills between the orcs' peaks and the Posse's flat ground, with the big river curving through their territory before it passes through Shanty Town and into Larracos. The main body of the enemy is massing on the Posse's northern border with the Operatics, about a hundred thousand strong by first estimate. Their best chance, says the adjutant, is to sweep over the Posse at once.

beats.headline: They got married without me
beats.text: THEY GOT MARRIED WITHOUT TELLING ME. Louis and the changeling. I wouldn't have disrupted the wedding. The little gnome says I said I'd push her over and take her place at the last second, but she's a child and does not understand the intricacies of modern love. And even if I was going to, that is no reason not to tell a girl. Then Donut says that was only the first wedding, and there's a bigger ceremony in a few weeks. Why didn't anyone SAY so? This changes everything.

beats.headline: Pink on the map
beats.text: On the hologram of the floor a tiny ring around Larracos blinks and turns pink: Shanty Town, controlled by the Princess Posse. Baroness Victory calls it a smart trade. The shanty town is usually small and does not form until the fighting starts and the NPCs flee, but this one circles the whole city, giving the NPCs another layer of security, and the Posse holds it. Li Na asks, the moment she is recruited, that her squad build the defences in and around it.

beats.headline: Hundreds of attempts
beats.text: Carl turns his interface back on and reads the suppressed notifications. Gloom Wraith Phase failed to activate. Mind Balance prevented activation. Your attempt to disable Mind Balance was prevented by Mind Balance. It is level nine, up from five a few hours ago, over pages of attempts to cast that he never made. Shi Maria, the tattoo on his chest, is trying to use him; had the phase gone off, it would likely have set off the ogre's non-magical bombs, and Donut would have died. Even so the spider breaks in for a moment. Watch out, Carl.

beats.headline: Three for Shanty Town
beats.text: Shanty Town is controlled by the Princess Posse now, and Baroness Victory calls it a smart trade: it circles Larracos and gives the NPCs an extra layer of security, one the Posse controls. We have three town upgrade coupons, Carl says, one each from the Tina quest and a tier-three one he just got in a box. Can they use them here? Absolutely, says Victory, and they might get something like the Larracos city defense system. But the coupons could also go on their base, and that may be the better choice.

beats.headline: Commander of the 103rd
beats.text: Subject is a veteran of Land War, a different game entirely, which was inflicted on his home planet; everyone calls him a crawler anyway, and he comes to the Princess Posse’s aid during the faction fighting. He is given a battalion, the 103rd, on the strength of what he has done both inside a dungeon and outside one. He has said perhaps three words since.

beats.headline: Through four skunks, phased
beats.text: The spray comes, and a blink before the cloud reaches me I go incorporeal on Gloom Wraith Phase and rush forward through four skunks with their backs to me. They come apart into ribbons of fur and flesh, and their armour clanks to the forest floor. It feels like running through a sprinkler on a fine mist. I've seen this done before. The rage elemental did it to Yolanda. Five seconds, then Walk on Air, up onto a branch above the cloud, next to Bodi.

beats.headline: I found out
beats.text: Back in our territory, young man. I'm pretty sure I've found every artillery battery on both sides, though I can't swear to a hundred per cent. And we've got a new problem. They have another nasty surprise waiting for us on the naga side. Remember when you asked me to find out why those robot fellows wanted pet levelling sped up? Well. I found out.

beats.headline: The shark has a name
beats.text: Subject existed first as a magical tattoo carried on Tsarina Signet’s skin, one that could fly, and is now a seventeen-foot hammerhead shark that breathes air and flops where he once flew. He rolls with Carl’s squad now, answers to Jamal, speaks of himself as Jamal, and keeps telling the legs Carl builds him to hop, which breaks them.

beats.headline: Three hops, three harnesses
beats.text: Behind Carl in the forest, Jamal apologizes: he did a little hop, and the metal pieces broke again. It is the third harness Carl has hastily built him, like the conveyance Katia built for Tran but much bigger: eight double-jointed legs and a harness for the seventeen-foot shark, who now breathes air and, no longer one of Signet's paper tattoos, cannot fly. It makes him look like a horrifying spider hybrid. Carl's prototype takes spoken orders; Katia's version is to read his thoughts. The joints can handle the jump but not the landing, and Carl is out of extra-large leg joints. Jamal must wait for Katia.

beats.headline: STINK, and a branch
beats.text: Skunks. STINK. Mongo in tree. Mongo sick. Sick again. MOTHER jumps onto Mongo branch. Branch goes crack. MOTHER falls. Mongo falls. Cage. Mongo whimpers.

beats.headline: Skanked, and a hat
beats.text: The skunks' leader is a little battle wizard called Fancy Boy, in a starry hat, and I shout that nobody touch him because he's mine, and knock him out with a Magic Missile. That, apparently, is what was stopping the rest of them spraying. Now I am Skanked. Three hours, Charisma down seventy per cent, and nothing in my inventory takes it off. Mongo is sick. I got the hat, and it smells worse than I do. And I was supposed to be moral support for Katia's treatment.

beats.headline: A gift for attending
beats.text: Subject is a Tummy Acher, a pet-class mob built to absorb damage. He came to Tserendolgor as a gift for attending CrawlCon, and to Carl when she was gone, reset to level one with no name and no memory; the one he answers to now is Louis's work. Tserendolgor took delivery of a party favour. What the group has now is a tank that levels every time it goes hunting, which is not what a party favour is for.

beats.headline: Removal Order
beats.text: My half of it: the same drug with Removal Order stirred in, so I go into the spider's worst memory instead of mine, and at the end I can lock Shi Maria inside it. Nobody can tell me how the lock will look. Someone has to pull my toe ring off once I'm under, so we can't do this in the guild. The potion it needs is one Mordecai already made. Coincidences in here mean another hand. The last thing I hear going under is a warlord notification. The Lemig Sortion, offering free passage, to treat for peace.

beats.headline: The fifth author, in a tower
beats.text: Everly, a sward mantis who crawled alone with hired mercenaries, gets a compass from her sponsor that shows the safest path through a fifty-level tower. It has forty-nine uses. At the top, a note: the tower is an advertisement, the compass named for a competitor, the dead end sponsored by the very company that sent it. She scrawls an angry note in the cookbook as the roof starts to come down. Explosives Engineer. Primal. Crushed to death on the eighth floor. Author of the fifth edition.

beats.headline: An outcast of the sward
beats.text: For the record, the subject's file. A mantis who left her colony a few days before the demons came to her world, because she could not abide the rules or the lack of individualism, and wandered the sward alone. In the dungeon she found thousands of her fellow mantises, confused and afraid, who wanted to work with her. She struck out on her own anyway, with hired NPCs and the invisible words on her prayer mat. Two or three dozen mercenaries over the floors: some fired in a rage, some vanished onto her payroll, the rest dead.

beats.headline: Gordon's Compass, forty-nine uses
beats.text: The eighth floor: a flat grassland pocked with thousands of holes leading down, and in its middle a tower fifty levels high, with a note on the door saying that whoever enters must reach the top before coming back down. Then a benefactor box from her generous sponsor, Dictum Waystation Controls, Limited: Gordon's Compass of Vertical Labyrinth Management, forty-nine uses, for the quickest and safest path through a maze, but not a subterranean one. She and ten mercenaries go up. Each time, the safe door. On the forty-ninth use, it shatters.

beats.headline: This dead end was sponsored
beats.text: At the top, she has been getting viewership awards, and allows herself a glimmer of hope for a fan box. On a pedestal sits a folded note, which the system reads aloud: Never trust your life to Gordon Waystation Outfitters. This dead end was sponsored by Dictum Waystation Controls, Limited. Don't get caught with nowhere to go. The whole tower was an advertisement, built by her own sponsor, and the compass led her to it. Humiliation, then anger. She scrawls an angry note in the Cookbook as the roof begins to come down.

beats.headline: The Inevitable Ruin
beats.text: Ten flights down, three are left, under a lowering ceiling. The dwarf digs for a keyhole they have no key for; the subject pities him, a first. Her queen called this moment the Inevitable Ruin. She decides it arrived earlier, when she abandoned the others. The ogre, silent since she hired him, says maybe it is not inevitable, like she says. She reaches out and touches him. Class: Explosives Engineer. Race: Primal. Birth Race: Sward Mantis. Top Level: 62. Dungeon Exit: crushed to death on the eighth floor. Current status: Dead.

beats.headline: Glory Bound and Removal Order
beats.text: Shi Maria grows stronger with every attempt on Carl's mind. The eye on his chest is open, blinking, looking angrily back and forth and trying to cast, and despite his Wisp Armor she has just spoken in his head. So Carl takes the Glory Bound treatment, which will carry him into the spider's worst memory, with Mordecai's Removal Order added, so that he can choose to lock her in the dream for good. The tattoo would stay on his chest, under his control. If he fails, he wakes up with a very pissed-off entity inside him.

beats.headline: One jar, two treatments
beats.text: In a new field hospital at the base, Mordecai sets a fizzing green jar on the counter, thick carbonated slime: two hits of Glory Bound compounded with a subdermal gel and a potion called Tough Love, brewed since the last floor and now in its short window of potency. Carl's dose gets Removal Order as well, so that, Mordecai hopes, he will visit the spider's memories instead of his own, and at the end he can choose to lock Shi Maria in hers. The drug began outside the inner system as a medication for learning difficult tasks, and it lingers in the dungeon in quests and traps. Mordecai rubs the gel on Katia's neck and slops a cold, fizzing blob on Carl.

beats.headline: Twice to Glory Bound
beats.text: Mordecai's jar is two hits of Glory Bound in a gel, cut with a potion called Tough Love. Eight to ten hours, for me. Once I am under I am on my own, and Edgar says waking me early could be fatal. That's a cheerful thought. I drink the sleeping potion. Skál. Then I tell Carl a secret. My favourite memory and my worst memory are the same thing, and I am going back to where I went last time. He tells me to take his hand. I do, and Imani pulls us apart.

beats.headline: The ogre in the sand
beats.text: Under the lowering ceiling of Everly's tower, one of her last two mercenaries, an ogre who has not said one word since she hired him, stops digging and lies down beside her. There is a flash deep in the back of his eyes, like a screen booting up. Maybe there is more to it than this, he says, as the ceiling reaches his face. Maybe it is not inevitable, like she says.

beats.headline: An egg only I can break
beats.text: I wake in the Sugar Cube, standing in a circle of blood and Lemig goblin corpses, fifty or more, with eleven hours gone. Quest failed: the Bedlam Bride. Their own adjutant rules it an AI action. What comes back from the dream: a second spider. Her husband, Hapanzi, who turned into a man. He'd been a god. I have her now, son, he said. You can set her free if you must, but not unless all is lost. She's an egg inside me, and only I can break it.

beats.headline: It worked, sort of
beats.text: Carl comes round from the treatment on the other side of the map, with no idea how he got there. His treatment worked, sort of, according to Shi Maria's husband Hapanzi, who reappeared at the end of the dream to say he has her now, good and trapped. Carl can see from the eye on his chest now. It is still a tattoo, but he can feel it when it is open, and he has to make a conscious effort to keep it closed.

beats.headline: Waking up somewhere else
beats.text: Carl blinks awake on the other side of the map, in what he thinks is the high elf castle, with no idea how he got there. The memory they shared is a jumble, like a real dream. He suspects Katia's treatment worked. His own worked, sort of: the spider's husband, a god called Hapanzi, reappeared at the end and told him he has her now, good and trapped, and not to set her free unless all is lost. The eye on Carl's chest is still a tattoo, but now he can see from it when it opens.

beats.headline: A name out of the dream
beats.text: Reconstructed from Crawler Carl's memory as he wakes, covered in blood, on the far side of the map. The dream had a second spider in it: a male, her husband, first a spider and then a man. Shi Maria came in mocking, saw him, then killed him and devoured him while she sobbed. Then he came back. His name, Carl thinks, was Hapanzi, and he had been a god. His words: I have her now, son. She is good and trapped. You can always set her free, if you must. But do not unless all is lost.

beats.headline: The Lemig headquarters
beats.text: The castle landed in the Lemig Sortion's territory, and they made it their headquarters. In Queen Imogen's private ballroom near the top, their warlord waits for a summoned Carl, planning to leave him a vegetable and turn the spider loose on his own base. Instead the spider comes out in the ballroom. When it is over, Panford, the Lemig adjutant, tells Commander Stockade his throne room is destroyed and that it is being ruled an AI action. His general, Luke, killed by a fellow soldier under her control, is among the dead.

beats.headline: We left her with Annie
beats.text: They tell me Carl vanished off his cot as it began, stayed translucent, then went completely. The Lemig team knew the moment he went under and tried something through the warlord chat. I message him. He is in the high elf castle. And we left her there, Carl. We left Shi Maria alone in that room with Annie. He says it was only a memory, and asks if it worked. It is not a switch one flips. We will not know right away. But yes. I think it worked.

beats.headline: Carl wakes up in their base
beats.text: Eleven hours gone, blood all over him, and most of the room around him killed by the thing riding inside him. The Lemig Sortion and the Madness had been arranging something together. It has come apart on top of them.

beats.headline: On Katia's shoulder, in the dream
beats.text: At a field ruling adjudication, the dream Carl and Katia shared plays on a floating screen. There is the memory of Katia pleading with a faceless woman, who answers with Annie's medical needs, and sweeping everything off the woman's desk. And there is the Katia who watched it with Carl and cried on his shoulder. That Katia had a crow on her own shoulder, the card she brought from the floor before: a crow with the skull of an infant. The crow's name is also Annie. Carl does not know what that means, but it seems important.

beats.headline: The quiet one at the table
beats.text: Six in the late Queen Imogen's kitchen for a field ruling: three warlords and their adjutants. Architect Houston sits at the far end of the table, unmoving. He was already in the castle, but not in the ballroom when it happened. His adjutant is a tiny floating bune named Opiee. His mask is white and featureless but for a small red teardrop, and his long white robes move as if the body under them is the wrong shape. When Crawler Carl rises with his fists clenched, Houston turns his head toward him. The neck creaks like a wooden ship.

beats.headline: They can see our dreams
beats.text: The minor quorum sits in Imogen's kitchen and plays it back. Stockade sent a Summon Ally invitation as I went under, and it was accepted the moment Imani pried off my toe ring. Shi Maria accepted it. Then the screen goes hazy, and I know what it is. Katia's nightmare. Fannar walking out of the office, telling them the truth. The faceless woman at the desk. Architect Houston turns from the screen to look at me. Turn this off, I say. This isn't yours to watch. I'm ignored. The scene changes: Annie in the crib, wired up.

beats.headline: Worry not, my children
beats.text: The dream again. A hospital room, Katia at a crib. Shi Maria pushes in, and a second spider follows: Hapanzi, her husband. Nobody says the name, and in that place there are no names over anyone's heads, but in the dream Crawler Carl simply knows it. Worry not, my children, the spider says, and becomes a large, dark-skinned man in simple pants and a vest, with an accent like Asojano's. Carl recognises the voice. It is the one that occasionally speaks inside his mind.

beats.headline: The field ruling
beats.text: Carl, Commander Stockade, Architect Houston and their adjutants convene for an official adjudication, and it goes on the record. The Lemig Sortion and the Madness used outside information to time a Summon Ally, meaning to pull Carl bodily to their base so that what was in him could be let loose on the rest of the Princess Posse. They got half of him, and the other half of the plan.

beats.headline: Two towers, and Lucia Mar
beats.text: Shanty Town's defences are still going up. We have two towers built, both splash towers, and that is all. We are working as fast as we can, and my sister says two more in twenty minutes. And Florin, you wanted to know about Lucia Mar. She is here in Shanty Town right now with her dog, drinking at the Possum Envy, right on the edge of the border. One of the new guys tried to recruit her. She almost ripped his head off.

beats.headline: Summon Ally, explained
beats.text: The kid asks me mid-hearing what Summon Ally does, so I tell him. It's a rare teleport, and it's built so the summoned holds the cards. You have to share a chat, the warlord chat counts, apparently. You have to accept. You can't be dropped into a wall. You went over as a ghost because the system compensates for being out cold. I thought I'd killed you. At best they wanted your treatment ruined. At worst it would simply kill you. They wanted to kill us using that crazy spider.

beats.headline: A score to settle first
beats.text: Hello, Carl and Donut. I am above the naga border with Bianca, surveying your defences, and your enemies believe they are being surreptitious. The elves' long-range trebuchets are preparing to fire. A hundred mercenaries in the Madness's colours think they are invisible. There are tracked vehicles under camouflage netting. With no magic permitted at the outset, I am perfectly safe, thank you. Once the festivities begin, I have a score to settle with the lead producer of the Blood Hunter program. Only then will I join your military. If you are still alive.

beats.headline: Pried off
beats.text: Before three adjutants, the night of the treatment plays on a screen. A warlord's teleport invitation reached Carl's interface while he was still conscious. Then Rosetta, Bucket Boy and Mordecai stand over him on the cot while Imani pries off his toe ring, as the cure required once he was out. The moment the ring comes off, the request is accepted, by the entity controlling him.

beats.headline: A foul, and a ceasefire cut short
beats.text: Panford, the Lemig Sortion's adjutant, sets out before a minor quorum of adjutants what his own team did: an attempt to pull Carl bodily to their base while Mordecai was working to expel what rides inside him. The Sortion is penalised for illegal information gathering. Then its warlord, still under the spider's madness, beats his own head against the floor until he dies, the team is defeated, and that withdrawal cuts the ceasefire short by more than twenty-three hours.

beats.headline: Not culpable, by two votes
beats.text: Panford lays out the charge: Commander Stockade and Architect Houston used secured messaging to reach someone on the eighteenth floor, identified as Nurse Yugoslav of the Madness. Crawler Carl asks, loudly, whether that is his mom. Opiee calls the evidence circumstantial, quite damning, and not enough, and asks his warlord whether he wishes to confess. The masked warlord says nothing. Baroness Victory rules Houston obviously guilty and smart enough to let Stockade do the dirty work, and votes not culpable. Opiee agrees. The Madness is found not guilty of any wrongdoing.

beats.headline: A promise, then a rifle
beats.text: A direct message in the warlord chat: mention his mother out loud again, and Crawler Carl and his animal companion spend their last thousand hours on the amplification table in his surgical theater. This is a promise, he says. A second one: Carl is in mortal danger at this very moment and does not realise it. Then the Lemig Sortion falls, its assets go to the Madness, and Phase One engages. Houston is on his feet with his robes flung back: a bug-like body, six arms, two of them holding a rifle. He fires at Carl's chest. Carl dives, grabs a bag of cat food, and teleports.

beats.headline: A bag of cat food and a hole
beats.text: Houston messages me. Mention his mother again and Donut and I spend our last thousand hours on his amplification table. Gracious pet owners accept the gifts their animals drop on the doorstep. Then the ceasefire ends, his robes fly back on a bug body with six arms, and two of them bring a rifle up at my chest. I dive, grab the bag of cat food off the counter, drop a hob-lobber from my hotlist, and teleport home with a hole punched through my shoulder. No kill message. Either he planned all of this, or he knew what was happening to Stockade and used it.

beats.headline: Trapped, says Hapanzi
beats.text: Watching the replay of the ballroom, Carl knows that at that moment, in the dream, Shi Maria vanished and her husband Hapanzi came back as a spider to tell him she is trapped in his own body. Carl now controls the eye and the containment she is in. He can summon her again, once, and then she may choose to take over his body or expel herself into her own form: one more bomb in his inventory, an especially dangerous one. She does not look nearly as trapped as Hapanzi said. The eye on his chest is clenched closed.

beats.headline: The containment in the eye
beats.text: On the screen Shi Maria rampages through the ballroom screaming that she did not kill Hapanzi and never would. At that same moment in the dream, she vanished and Hapanzi reappeared as a spider. He told Crawler Carl she was gone, trapped in his own body, and that Carl now controlled the eye on his chest and the containment she is in. Carl can summon her once. If he does, she chooses: take over his body, or expel herself into her own form. Watching the replay, Carl notes she did not look nearly as trapped as Hapanzi said.

beats.headline: Burned some assets
beats.text: Carl sends me a message for Ferdinand. I pass it on. I had to burn some assets to save his ass. I hope it was worth it. I'm hearing about strange movements, and I relay all of it to Louis and Britney. Heads up to his people. We are powering up the towers early. Anyone in town who is not in his army should start moving into his territory.

beats.headline: Punished, and the ceasefire ends early
beats.text: Panford, their adjutant, is left to explain the rampage through the base to everyone. Stockade looked into her eye, lost his mind, and finished it himself. Ferdinand gets an emergency action item passed for a live feed blackout so nobody can do this again. The Lemig Sortion is punished for cheating, the ceasefire ends early, and Carl goes home.

beats.headline: Not a wake-up salve
beats.text: Out loud, for whoever is listening, I say I'm going to pull him out with a Shock Wake salve, adjusted to work on a non-corporeal form. That's not what I'm making. I know we're being watched from outside, so what I actually brew is something to violently expel the spider from him. Not a wake-up salve at all. It's a risky move. I put it on his see-through chest, and he buckles.

beats.headline: Inside him, and not staying quiet
beats.text: Field ruling, ninth floor. Commander Stockade of the Lemig Sortion tried to pull Crawler Carl bodily to his position. Mordecai, at the same moment, tried to force Shi Maria out of him. Each got half. What came of it is Shi Maria loose in the Lemig base, and the mess she made there, which the adjutant Panford has been left to explain to everyone. Stockade looked into her eye. Stockade is no longer with us, by his own hand. The Lemig Sortion is being punished for cheating, and the ceasefire is over early.

beats.headline: The rampage through the Lemig base
beats.text: Stockade tries to pull Carl bodily to his position while Mordecai tries to force her out of him. What comes of it is hers, and the adjutant Panford is left explaining the wreckage.

beats.headline: A blackout for everyone
beats.text: Sir Ferdinand proposes an emergency action item, in language unsuitable for the broadcast, because teams on other floors are cheating: nobody in the dungeon, including the guests partying in the centipede on the eighteenth floor, may watch any outside feed for the rest of the game. It is approved. Effective immediately, everyone in the dungeon is under a live-feed blackout. Carl had not wanted to spend one of his own action items on it. Victory notes that it is a first.

beats.headline: Heir to the Sortion
beats.text: A minor quorum of adjutants finds the Madness and the Princess Posse not guilty of the conspiracy the Lemig Sortion has already confessed to. Baroness Victory calls Architect Houston obviously guilty and votes not culpable anyway. Then the Sortion's warlord dies, the team is defeated, and because the defeat was voluntary, its assets go to the closest ally. System Message: all assets of the Lemig Sortion have been awarded to the Madness. Phase One combat engages.

beats.headline: Disconnect Containment
beats.text: Christmas morning, at the gas station, beside the memory ghost of Lightning Lou, I open the containment interface I got for Paulie's plastic tub. Not one button. Six tabs. On the Fuse page: five benchmarks, two met, and Override Conditions And Activate Fuse. I want to press it more than anything. I think of Donut. I miss you too. Then, at the end of a list, Disconnect Containment: the fuse and the failsafe go inert. Which hurts the Syndicate most, and which protects my people most? I press it. The red dot over Earth starts to grow.

beats.headline: Soul Poisoning, again
beats.text: Ten miles to the southern front, and the patch on my jacket is glowing again. Mordecai said not to keep it on long. We need the power. A pang across my stomach, a ringing in my ears. Three kids in metal skull caps run out with training spears to join us. The chariot won't take the missile launcher: I've used up my allotted Armor options. Holger sends the kids back with Jamal. Another pang. Soul Poisoning. Activate Daughter's Kiss to disperse the effect.

beats.headline: The handshake completes
beats.text: In Orren's zero zone, Carl asks whether Paulie ever made it into the dungeon. No, says Orren; most of them never do, and the parts of a collective mind are often disposable. Then the notice: Containment Interface is now available for use, as a new tab. Carl changes his request and asks to be sent to the gas station with the memory ghost of the dog, and sits beside Lightning Lou with a bag of chips and a soda. I could end it all right now, he thinks.

beats.headline: Two buttons, one pressed
beats.text: There is no single Boom button. There are six tabs of numbers in a language that is not quite Syndicate standard, and the controls are for the device that installed the AI into the primal engine, not the AI itself. Carl screenshots everything. The Fuse page lists five benchmarks, two met, and a button: Override Conditions And Activate Fuse. At the end of a list sits the only other thing he can press: Disconnect Containment, which renders the failsafe inert. He weighs which hurts the Syndicate most and protects his people most, and presses Disconnect. The red dot over Earth starts to grow.

beats.headline: A reply to Justice Light
beats.text: Crawler Drakea, twenty-second edition, writes beneath a note of Justice Light's in the cookbook. Justice Light wrote that of all the NPCs he killed, he killed one out of anger, that it haunts him, and that he has become what he hates. Drakea answers that his traps have saved Drakea more times than can be counted, that a big one is under construction from his seeking flechette design, and that it was not his fault. They put him here. Let them know fear.

beats.headline: It is done
beats.text: The throne rooms lock in place, and every one of them shows on the map now. Carl asks in chat whether I had ours prepared before it locked. It is done. The rest of the project I am building with the sluggalos. They do not mind the idea of accidentally tripping a trap and being skewered. It is not finished yet.

beats.headline: He never made it in
beats.text: Closing entry. Before leaving the liaison's office on Christmas morning, Crawler Carl asked whether that Paulie guy ever made it into the dungeon. No, said Orren. He was outside, but never within. Most of them never make it in; with collective minds and swarms, the individual parts are often disposable. Carl, beside an old dog at a Florida gas station, opens the menu Paulie described, expecting a single button. It is not a single button.

beats.headline: The orphaned cubs
beats.text: Randy and Todd, the orphaned ursine cubs, come running out of a guild in metal skull caps, dragging training spears, with little Clint, a flesh golem now in a kindergartner's body. They want to fight. Miss Nadine has told them to stay away from Tina because she killed their dad, Clint reports, but Tina is different now and her mother says she has apologized. Randy says they have been practising. Todd means to bathe in apostate blood.

beats.headline: I am doing my part
beats.text: I AM DOING MY PART IN THE WAR, CARL. I sneaked onto the plane, and Carl says I'm not a scout and I'll tear a Samantha-sized hole in it at the border. FINE. Louis and I will crash together and build a log cabin, and he will grow a scraggly beard that smells like a campfire. Then Carl tells Louis to dump me out of the bomb bay. No, WAIT. Louis can just come back. It's a suicide mission. I like him more than Charlie. I don't want him to die yet.

beats.headline: The Gurgles, allowed
beats.text: A crawler with a flamethrower says the Gurgles is a magical attack and this is bullshit. It is an exploit. They infected the pets before the magic ban, and it has been allowed in the past. The mages ought to do a better job of keeping infections out. The Princess asks what the Gurgles are: a nasty, contagious, incurable debuff, which the factions agreed many years ago never to use again. It caused the insanity and the rabies. The truck stop pill I am not familiar with. I suspect it made them so big.

beats.headline: A labyrinth on the front
beats.text: Literal thousands of Build Trench scrolls, collected on the previous floor, have made a labyrinth of trenches along the front: traps and soldiers, fortified bunkers, hospitals, fall-back positions and more. No Man's Land between the two lines is only about two hundred and fifty metres. The forward-most trench is about twelve feet deep, with scaffolding at the front so soldiers can engage the enemy, and red-tinged mud in the bottom that smells of smoke and earth and sweat.

beats.headline: Kill them, keep the body
beats.text: The orders I send out on the southern front: if we capture an enemy and can keep them alive but unconscious, we do. The NPCs and the mercenaries from outside get separated. There are spells that can turn the NPCs to our side. The mercenaries have another purpose. If one gives trouble, or it isn't safe to keep them, kill them, loot them by the safe-looting protocol, keep the body, and report it up the chain. The Prism scout who flooded one of our tunnels was one of D'Nadia's own relatives. He stepped on a landmine running away.

beats.headline: Katia repurposes a recipe
beats.text: Katia has finished building Tran's two-part wheelchair, much like what she means to build next for Jamal, from a recipe she took out of Carl's automaton manual and repurposed. Walking around, Tran is a small mechanical crab body that can climb walls and run, for short distances, at incredible speed. Then there is the battle armour version he wears now: a second exoskeleton over the crab legs that encases him in full plate and a helmet.

beats.headline: Over the trench
beats.text: Cries for shields run up and down the trench as giant, exploding monsters close in, and arrows, bolts and spears do nothing to them. Heads up, Carl calls, pulls a stick of full-strength hobgoblin dynamite and tosses it over the edge like a grenade. Everyone ducks and covers their ears. The blast rocks the ground, experience notifications fly by with a new achievement, and through the periscope the ones immediately in front are gone, though more keep coming. He prepares a second stick.

beats.headline: In the southern push
beats.text: Carl and Donut join the defence in the south, and across the no-man's-land the Nagas hold the line beside the Dream and the Prism. Cobra-headed, and playing under the name of the Blood Sultanate, taken from a bloodier time in their own history.

beats.headline: None of my spells work
beats.text: The periscope screens have amazing resolution, much better than the stolen television in Carl's living room. Everything from a pawn shop is stolen, Carl. Then the pets come out of the fog, rot sticker behemoths as big as cars, full of the Gurgles, and I am feeling very useless all of a sudden. None of my spells work. Wait, Love Vampire works! It doesn't work on pets.

beats.headline: Rot stickers with the Gurgles
beats.text: The southern defence is already holding against the Dream, the Prism and the Nagas when the Reavers make their contribution: a horde of their own pet rot stickers, raised by hand to trust their masters, then juiced, infected and turned loose. This is a power that fights by handing you something diseased and standing back.

beats.headline: Blow the line
beats.text: Katia finished my chair. Two parts. A crab body for walls and short sprints, and a battle shell that closes over it up to a helmet, so much metal I can't carry a ranged weapon or the system calls me armour. The pets hit the dirt wall. I call for my moles. They go down the holes and come back faster than expected. Fire in the hole. The whole line goes up, and the dirt hangs over us on the shields. We set those explosives two hours ago. We were saving them.

beats.headline: On the relay
beats.text: Operations note. The spies sent into naga territory are a pair of changelings, and Crawler Carl cannot speak to them directly. Every message goes from Carl to Britney, and from Britney to either Juice Box or Arief of the Semeru. Britney has become the crawlers' main liaison with the NPC team, and the dwarf is one of the two hands at the other end of it.

beats.headline: Always the first to fall
beats.text: The naga castle sits about eight miles from the border, on rocky ground chosen so nobody can tunnel in from below, and strangely close to Shanty Town. Historically it is almost always the first castle to fall. But every time, by the time the invaders reach the inner sanctum, the Sultana is gone. The team still loses its throne room. Its leader has never once been captured or assassinated since she took over, and she reappears at the end, laughing and joking. Nobody knows where she hides.

beats.headline: A pickled bulldog with elf ears
beats.text: Subject: Boomer. Elven Legate. Level 62. Colonel in the Princess Posse, commanding the 106th Bloody Leeches. A grizzled elf who survived one of the earliest seasons, bowed out on the tenth floor, and lived as a merchant on the sixth for many seasons before escaping. Crawler Carl's description is a bulldog pickled for five thousand years with elf ears and a cigar. Banned from CrawlCon for threatening an orcish showrunner during a panel. Wanted for a killing in a waystation brawl that started as an argument about the crawl. Crawler Donut reports he smells of cedar and acorns.

beats.headline: Cheese sticks and Monkeywrenchers
beats.text: The briefing, conducted with an unlit cigar. The Dream's bombardiers are cowards who run if you get near their chuckers. The cavalry is the thing to watch, and so is Epitome Tagg's household guard. Of the robed Madness troops going invisible, probably few are real Viceroys, but the invisible ones are Monkeywrenchers, and twenty of them once took two castles in the first hours. His boys and girls have had breakfast. Then Crawler Carl says let's do this, and Boomer lights the cigar, takes one very long puff, and fills the bunker with smoke. Fuck yeah, he says.

beats.headline: Liaison to the NPCs
beats.text: Somehow I'm the one who talks to the NPCs now. Carl can't reach their spies himself, so it goes him, then me, then Juice Box or Arief. The plan wanted one of their big diggers. Naga ground won't allow it, so it's two changeling spies instead. Carl asks if my guys are in place. They're ready. Waiting on you.

beats.headline: Invisible ones called Monkeywrenchers
beats.text: Elle watched at least a hundred of the Madness turn invisible and disappear. Colonel Boomer's briefing: there are probably few real Viceroys among them, mostly ordinary soldiers wearing the robes, but the ones who go invisible and sneak in are called Monkeywrenchers. A few seasons back, twenty of them took the Dreadnaught and Naga castles in the first hours. The Madness as a whole looks like a strong contender this season.

beats.headline: The southern map
beats.text: Their trenches, here. The Dream's artillery on the hills: about forty big trebuchets, dozens of small ones. Fifty zebras with mercenary riders, held in reserve. Twenty tanks that have not moved since they were uncovered. A hundred of the Madness gone invisible. The first trench is NPCs and mercenaries, mostly Prism banners, one naga standard. No inner-circle officers. Their fallback trenches are a hundred metres apart, no tunnels we know of. I still don't understand why they get trebuchets and we don't.

beats.headline: Over the top
beats.text: Louis drops, Elle hits the first anti-air gun, and our one trebuchet spreads Dazzlers through his craters, fifty of them playing Killing in the Name loud enough to shake the ground. Earplugs barely help. I ask Donut if she's scared. Of course, she says, but it's more numb than anything. My hand is trembling too much to pat her. She goes over on Mongo, and Imani after her. I grab the handhold, shouting something I can't hear, and pull myself up into No Man's Land with over two thousand of the Posse.

beats.headline: Fifty in the trebuchet
beats.text: The army has one trebuchet of its own, a small one Carl and Donut looted from some Dream elves on the sixth floor. It is loaded with about fifty contraptions called Dazzlers, with almost two hundred more piled nearby. They are basically an alarm and a spotlight trap combined: they shine only toward the eyes of the closest enemy soldier, strobing powerful multi-coloured beams into their faces, and they all play the same song at the same time. They are one of the few trap modules Victory allows in a trebuchet.

beats.headline: Killing in the Name
beats.text: The trebuchet fires the first of four salvos, spreading Dazzlers in and around the middle of Louis's craters. The announcement is louder than Carl expects, even from this far away: Justice Light's tips on enhancing them have worked. He slips his earplugs in. They barely help. Peaking at number three on June 20, 2020, despite first coming out in 1992, it's Killing in the Name. The Rage Against the Machine song shakes the ground louder than the explosions, and anyone within a few hundred meters takes immediate, painful hearing damage.

beats.headline: Watching from the trench
beats.text: Subject, adjutant for Team Retribution, cracks into the Posse's forward trench beside Baroness Victory, causing some moments of bedlam until Carl shouts everyone down. Team Retribution is taking a small part in this assault, he explains sheepishly, so he has come to watch from the best position. Told he will see nothing from there, he offers to go across and warn the other side instead. The offer is not taken up.

beats.headline: The first anti-air gun
beats.text: Man, I wish I could cast my Graupel spell. Can't, so it's Carl's missile launcher, and I hope it works as advertised. Carl says for god's sake keep moving. Louis drops, and I fire. First anti-air gun: hit, but it had a protection spell on it. It went over, though, and with luck it won't be firing for a while. Moving to the second one.

beats.headline: One trebuchet, and the buffs
beats.text: I drop into the trench next to Carl. I was buffing people down the line, and before that the man aiming our only trebuchet, which is loaded with Dazzlers. He's ready. I spread my wings and put a new line of buffs over everyone in the channel. Then Total Ear Protection on Donut, and on Mongo.

beats.headline: The bombing run
beats.text: Okay so, we see the target. Lowering for the bombing run. Not too low, Carl says. In and out, into the fog. The bombs don't go on their trench, man, they go in a straight line right in front of it, to leave a crater, shower the guys inside with dirt and clear the traps out there. Holy shit, that was scary. I got hit with a few spells, but the shields held. Circling round to the rendezvous.

beats.headline: A prize for the most
beats.text: Warlord Donut, to everyone. The moment the first bomb drops, take the ear potion or put your earplugs in. Drink your invisibility, and go up and over, and don't stop running until you're in their trenches. The soldier who brings me the most dead cheese sticks gets a prize. The veterans say their old officers always threatened them. My army is different. Positive reinforcement worked with Mongo. Carl asks if I'm scared. Of course I am. It's more numb than anything. Nowadays it hits me more when it's done.

beats.headline: Into the enemy's trench
beats.text: Caught in an unprotected crater, Carl tells the band to keep back and reads a scroll. It takes about ten seconds. A translucent line appears with a map, and he turns it ninety degrees so it meets the enemy trench in a T. Enjoin? Yes. His elevation is lower; proceed? Yes, and Dig. At the end of the new channel a Saccathian soldier drops as the ground disappears beneath him. All around, soldiers in other craters do the same with their own scrolls, cutting into the enemy trenches and past most of the protections.

beats.headline: Build Trench, joined
beats.text: In a crater in front of their line I read a Build Trench scroll, turn the line ninety degrees and tell it to join their trench. Elevation lower. Yes. Dig. The ground goes out from under a Saccathian soldier twenty feet ahead. Craft magic, so it ignores most protections: an exploit that's been pointed out for years and never fixed. All along the line our people are doing the same. I activate Daughter's Kiss on my right foot, tell everyone to take cover, jump, and land on his chest.

beats.headline: Still playing
beats.text: A big one: Deshrouded. The war protections are gone, all of them. The illusions vanish, the smoke clears, and every temporary protection spell snaps off, the ear protection included. The lights and music from the Dazzlers do not turn off. Donut and Mongo both seem to be screaming with pain, and Mongo rears at the sound. For a moment there is an unobscured view across the dim battlefield, where several of the enemy have turned from the painful light and most have their hands over their ears or eyes.

beats.headline: One over each shoulder
beats.text: Their diffusion spell strips every protection we had, and the heavy gun cuts through the ones rushing it. I stop over a veteran screaming, his arm gone. I put Donut's ear protection back, and Mongo's. Then I go for whoever is down. Into the crater with one over each shoulder. The Crest veteran is dead. The crawler with the arm blades is at two per cent and unconscious.

beats.headline: Too smart for your own good
beats.text: I appear beside Carl in the Prism's headquarters and tell him he is too smart for his own good. They slaughtered them back there. Does he know how many jumped blindly into that middle trench? The scout for Team Retribution went up almost twenty levels. What counts as offensive magic will need revisiting; that chemical alteration spell is a little too powerful. He ignores me, puts on his ring, and calls for the Empress.

beats.headline: Command of the assault
beats.text: Warlord menu: command of the southern assault transferred to Colonel Boomer. His first order is to stop celebrating. Nobody fights harder than someone trapped, he tells the generals. Form up, do not push too hard, and let them think it is a stalemate rather than a surrender. They have maybe half an hour before the enemy either escapes or has to be killed. Then the generals get on with it, and Crawler Carl turns north to meet Party Planner.

beats.headline: Twenty-five seconds out
beats.text: I conk out the second I kill him. Twenty-five seconds, Imani says: a soul-poisoning debuff called Post Nut Clarity, and I buried us in dirt, and don't do that again. But I blew their trench apart. I've gone up a level, and there's a message I've been expecting, which can wait. Command goes to Colonel Boomer. Louis lands, and Bonnie is standing behind his door gun. Donut gave her the last scout spot while I was under. She's older than I am, Carl.

beats.headline: Second battery down
beats.text: The second anti-air battery is down! Louis, hurry your ass up. The first one's almost back up already, and I'm running, because they've a pair of mages on my scent. Imani says get the hell out of there. Then I tell Louis his path to the enemy castle is free of anti-air guns, as far as I can see.

beats.headline: Crewing as Gangue
beats.text: Aboard Louis's airship, a changeling scout listed as Gangue, suspiciously thin for an adult. Carl works it out halfway to the target: this is Skarn, the child from the fifth floor, who has learned enough about his shapeshifting to hide his age. Carl resolves to have words with Louis and Princess Donut about children going into battle, as soon as they are back, and not before.

beats.headline: The acid trench
beats.text: Team Retribution's part in the assault is two spies and some scrolls. The NPCs were handed scrolls that change the chemistry of water in a container, instead of alcohol for some of their bars. So the spies drop a water scroll into the enemy's empty middle trench, turn it to acid, and cover the whole thing with an illusion. The enemy, confused and scared, fall back from the first trench and jump into it blind. The scout, an NPC porsuk bartender, goes up almost twenty levels.

beats.headline: The edge
beats.text: She's bleeding against the wall, asking why I'm telling her about Signet. She told Signet her family wasn't real. I hate her more than anything in the universe. I never felt this with Maggie My, or Quan Ch, or sitting in that gas station with the button. I tell Donut I've changed my mind, I want to do it myself. She asks me to step back. The mark forms. And there it is, the edge. I'm standing on it, one foot out over open air. I take a step back. Okay, Donut. It's time.

beats.headline: Marked, and taken by the dinosaur
beats.text: Empress D'nadia of the Prism Kingdom, warlord of the Prism clan, is dead. Crawler Carl marked her with the Night Wyrm's Ring of Divine Suffering. Mongo did the rest. She said at the finish that everything she did she did for her people; he told her to her face that she did it for herself and that her people will pay for it. I am obliged to broadcast both halves of an exchange like that.

beats.headline: Wrists too thick
beats.text: D'Nadia sent her three guards out as the explosive spiders came. Two are splattered over the wall. The third, an enormous samurai rhinoceros she somehow hired, cast a shield, but the concussions knocked him out for ten minutes. Carl's first instinct is to kill him, but he holds off. He tries to handcuff him, but the rhino's wrists are too thick, so he duct-tapes his wrists and ankles instead and tells Rend to guard him. Don't eat him.

beats.headline: The hidden door opens
beats.text: Subject, guildmaster of the hidden calligraphy and cartography guilds in Club Vanquisher, has not had a one-on-one with a floor supervisor in over fifty seasons, and wrote a scroll long ago that mutes the announcements. Woken by a fight in the hall, she finds her door open for the first time in a very long while: a vampire, her caprid son and his hellspawn pet. The pet burns her. The vampire heals her. Milk hopes aloud that they will not threaten her, as she might then be forced to give them a map of the secret exits.

beats.headline: A salve for the guildmaster
beats.text: Pony will not stand for what they have done, and there are guards down in the hall, and Bianca melting another. We go through a hidden door into a little guild, and Bianca burns the guildmaster before I can stop her. Pony, give me a salve. I ask what kind of creature she is, and rub it into her arm myself. She was a crawler once. She says she hopes we will not threaten her, because if we do, she might be forced to give us information. I thank her with a hand on her shoulder, and take out a knife.

beats.headline: I got this
beats.text: The Empress has shield after shield, and my clockwork Mongos go through every one of them and her dress. She tells me she was my sponsor. She got me my glasses. Don't I like my glasses? Then Carl says he has changed his mind, he wants to do it himself. No, Carl. Please. I need you to step back and calm down. I've got this. When he does, I sit, lick my paw, and tell the Empress, darling, that Mongo would like to express his utmost disappointment at how she judged him during the pet show.

beats.headline: Marked at full health
beats.text: The ring only marks a target at full health, and Empress D'Nadia keeps herself just short of it on purpose. So the clockwork Mongos go through her shields and the gown, a knife drops, the thing she has been using to keep herself hurt, and when she reaches for it a clockwork snaps the tentacle off. Carl casts a Heal scroll on her. The moment she is whole, he marks her. Her highest stat is Intelligence. The mark will form in thirty seconds.

beats.headline: Seekers in the Prism
beats.text: Inside the Prism's headquarters, Carl drops hunter seeker automatons on the floor, and they scatter off into the small castle. Empress D'Nadia sends her three guards out of the throne room the moment they approach. The one Saccathian hides behind the other off-worlder, a gnoll, as the explosive spider automatons close in, and both off-worlders are splattered over the wall before the party arrives. The samurai rhino casts a powerful shield, but the concussions knock him out for ten minutes.

beats.headline: Mercy for the gnolls
beats.text: Eight gnoll mercenaries come over to the Posse with their banners blinking red, and for about a week I can order any of them to stand still while I cut his throat. My finger itches. Please, no, Donut said, so I take the Ring of Divine Suffering off, and everyone in the room watches me do it. Corporal Pillbox begs for Lockjaw and Mange, his mates on the other two teams. Mange is his cousin. The anger drains out of me like it went out an airlock. None of you have to die today, I tell him. At least not by our hands.

beats.headline: The north will not hold
beats.text: Bad news from the northern front. We are holding for now, but without backup we might break in a matter of hours, so I'm preparing to fall back to our fallback position. I've ordered the castle to prepare for a siege, just in case. Could really use some air support, and some of those new NPCs Carl just gathered. He says they're on their way.

beats.headline: Credit for the Empress
beats.text: EMPRESS is down. Mongo gets the KILL. System says so. Blue goo on the WALL. Lick the wall. MOTHER says broken home. Mongo SQUAWKS. Yes.

beats.headline: Carl is the party leader now
beats.text: Carl's base stats make him the strongest member of the party, so the system has made him Party Leader of the Royal Court of Princess Donut. Of my Royal Court. If he changes the name of the party I will leave, and then Mongo will come from a broken home. He says we'll keep the names and the titles. For now. Then I tell him the thing that is not for show. Throw that ring away, Carl. It's doing something to you. You're scaring me. He says not yet. It won't matter if it kills you first.

beats.headline: Asking for Carl by name
beats.text: A visitor at Shanty Town, reported by Li Jun, who was too busy to follow her up: a crazy old white lady with a shopping cart, level 23, no class, whom the system would not let him recruit. She came looking for Carl. She tried to get into Larracos, and Larracos would not let her in, so she went to the bar where Lucia Mar is still camped. Straight after, Zev passes on an order from the prime minister of the Syndicate himself. Carl is not to interact with Agatha. Nobody tells Zev why.

beats.headline: Two kinds of residual
beats.text: Agatha is a residual, like Paulie at the Florida homeless shelter, except Orren told me she's the other kind. Paulie's side wants the crawl to end and goes at it through the AI itself. Tipid and Rosetta say Mantis scientists can now build AIs that are easier to control, which makes this old one the residuals' last chance, and both sides are making their move. I don't know what either side actually wants. I'm not sure anybody does. The prime minister is sticking his nose in, and she's asked for me by name.

beats.headline: Quickly snatched up
beats.text: The System files the career of one of those survivors. A level-70 Sai mercenary leader lost his entire squad in an incident at the Desperado Club for which Crawler Carl may or may not be partially responsible. In the reorganisation the few Sai survivors were relegated to the mercenary markets, where he was quickly snatched up. Crawler Carl inherits the contract by defeating his employer. The System doubts this has done much for his self-esteem.

beats.headline: One of the two dogs
beats.text: Administrator Mukta, kua-tin, party member, is dead. Reported by Zev, over chat, after saying Lucia Mar no longer answers messages and was never her client, thank goodness: one of Lucia's dogs ate Mukta, back when she still had two. It was horrible. Mukta was an ass, and a party member, but nobody deserved that. Zev can still hear the screaming. Crawler Carl laughs out loud. File note: the second kua-tin the crawlers ever spoke with, and the one responsible for putting them on the Maestro's show in the first place.

beats.headline: He ate my boot
beats.text: For the record: found duct-taped in the Prism's castle, with Crawler Carl's pet attempting to swallow his foot. A large bipedal rhinoceros, a true NPC, now under a Princess Posse banner. He frees his wrists and moves to clobber the pet. He ate my boot, he reports; one boot is gone, revealing a round foot. Carl apologizes and promises a replacement. Toyotomi. Level 70 Sai Outpost Guard Mercenary Leader. Sergeant in the Princess Posse. A hired mercenary, paid to the end of the floor or his death, inherited when the Prism fell.

beats.headline: A broken creature, per the file
beats.text: The System's file on the subject. Once an honorable, experienced leader of Sai. His entire squad died in an incident at the Desperado Club that Crawler Carl may or may not have been partially responsible for, and the few survivors went to the mercenary markets. His failure to protect his friends against the demon haunts him, and he refuses to lead men now, despite great talent. He was regaining his confidence when a man in underwear and a talking cat trounced him, tied him up and slaughtered his charge.

beats.headline: Accepting his exile
beats.text: His magic is for outposts, not palaces. Edifice Shield cannot cover a castle bigger than this one, and this one was already too big; Warlord D'Nadia insisted, so he shielded it in spurts, and was resting when the crawlers arrived. I am shamed. Leave him here, he asks, to defend this building until he dies. It is what he wants. Carl changes the plan and sends him to Shanty Town. He accepts his exile. It is not an exile, Carl says. They need his talents.

beats.headline: An order from the prime minister
beats.text: Okay, so. I know I've been quiet, but we are monitoring. This comes directly from the Syndicate council: Prime Minister Glory himself messaged me. Carl is not to talk to Agatha. I do not know why. The residuals are harmless every season, and the AI supposedly removed its protections from them, and they are pretty much all dead, except this one. It seems to have a soft spot for her. Lucia Mar does not respond to messages anymore. And Carl, the roundtable is part of the game. It is not optional.

beats.headline: Salty about the naga castle
beats.text: The southern trenches are filled with scrolls and the enemy artillery wrecked, and Boomer is sore about not pushing on to take the naga castle. Crawler Carl concedes privately that it would have been the safest and smartest play, and does not care. Boomer pulls most of the 106th north to help Florin. Then, on the band: a group of flyers that are not the Posse's have just buzzed him, moving low and fast toward the castle. They are Reaver paratroopers, and they arrive.

beats.headline: We don't eat our own
beats.text: Reid Gunn is on the casualty list, and his dot is standing in a bunker, and the dots beside him keep turning into Xs. Brain worms. Gondii. A medic runs in with a wounded yenk between him and a mage named Charles Andrew, and Charles Andrew is listed as dead. I tackle him and punch him with a spiked gauntlet until he actually is. The worm comes out of his face, black and white, named Goldblum, and I stamp on it. Rend moves in to eat the body. No, Rend. We don't eat our own. Unleash Tina.

beats.headline: A spellbook called War Crime
beats.text: My 1914 box has given me a spellbook called War Crime, and I am not sure if I should read it. The spellbook itself is bleeding and crying and it's disgusting. Then the castle starts blowing up, and Bomo notices an extra door in the situational whatever it's called space: a door for the Reaver team's saferoom. They are doing what we were going to do. They are sneak attacking us through the saferoom door. The Bamboozle! Carl tells Bomo and Sledge to guard it.

beats.headline: Through the bait-shop door
beats.text: The home anti-air battery goes up, then the hangar bay, and the flyers that buzzed Boomer turn into paratroopers coming down through the protections. Dozens of the Posse's names run down the casualty list. The worst of it is the saferoom: the bait shop sits inside the castle walls now, and Bomo notices a new door in the situational hallway belonging to the Reaver team. If any of the sponsors ever came in through that bait shop, the doggy door upgrade lets them come back the same way. It is the sneak attack Donut had just proposed, run backwards.

beats.headline: No throne room
beats.text: The 107th White Dragons are parked in the makeshift town, and it worries Crawler Carl: it is shaped like a donut and can be attacked from nearly any angle. Nobody has tried yet. Entering Shanty Town exposes an attacker to the Larracos defence system, and the town's rules are different. There is no throne room. The only way to take it is to kill Carl. Li Na's battalion, meanwhile, is bankrupting the Posse's coffers building its defences.

beats.headline: A door into the castle
beats.text: Donut shouts in the chat that Bomo has noticed an extra door in the situational space, a saferoom door for the Reaver team: they are sneak attacking through it, into the castle. It hits Carl too late. Every time they left the guild saferoom for the FUPA through the bait shop, that space was a long corridor of doors from all the crawlers coming and going. Off-world sponsors can use personal spaces as well, and can buy a doggie door upgrade, so any of them who ever came in through the bait shop can come back that way. The bait shop is inside the castle now.

beats.headline: Bleeding and crying
beats.text: Carl is taking in a rare moment of silence, still processing what happened when they confronted D'Nadia, when two messages arrive at once. Donut has opened her 1914 box and got a spellbook called War Crime. She is not sure whether she should read it. The book itself is bleeding and crying, and it is disgusting. The other message is Florin, falling back as the enemy finally shows its armor, and then the trap notifications start.

beats.headline: She's a child, too
beats.text: Imani is lecturing Bucket Boy about pain levels, and Crawler Carl is not listening. He is thinking of his brother, and of Asher's mother holding him after she poisoned their father, and of Princess Donut sobbing at the end of the Butcher's Masquerade. She's a child, too, he thinks, and then another: they are going to have to do some pretty horrible things just to survive. He has an order to compose.

beats.headline: Her mother says no
beats.text: Carl sends for Tina and her mother refuses. Too dangerous, Kiwi says; she's just a child, and Carl has just ordered the gnome and the changeling children out of the battle, so why is Tina different? Carl writes an order overriding her, looks at it, and deletes it, and decides it is Kiwi's call. Donut does not. GET TINA OUT HERE RIGHT NOW, in the warlord chat, and before Kiwi can answer the doors fly open and Tina comes out screeching with glee, waving her wand, and starts eating the invisible enemies.

beats.headline: This warlord thing suits her
