beats.text: A group of us detour through Shanty Town and use the doggy door, and the moment I land in the castle the Extreme Focus buff doubles. Everyone in the zone is talking too fast, me included. Carl seems untouched, though his health screen says the buff is on him. I have told the medic already: check their pain levels after you heal them, outworlders heal differently. Then Donut is on the roof shouting Comrades, and Carl says she's been spending too much time with Rosetta. This warlord thing suits her, I tell him. It comes out a little sad.

beats.headline: Grounded under the roof
beats.text: Okay so, we finished the repair from the inside, but the portal has to be fixed by hand from outside, or the whole hangar stays grounded. The door to it is on top of the castle, man. Anybody who goes up there is a prime target. So we stay grounded.

beats.headline: His greatest desires
beats.text: Fourteenth edition. In the absolute, scorching heat of battle, the subject writes, one learns who one really is and what one really wants. One faces one's greatest fears and, much worse, one's greatest desires laid bare. For him they are the same, and it is his devastation. Stab, stab, stab. The note sits in the Cookbook while Crawler Carl's people hold the entrance of a castle under pulse rifle fire.

beats.headline: Comrades, from the castle roof
beats.text: These people really need to follow orders faster. We need more team-building exercises. So my headset goes on, I jump on Mongo, and we land on the castle roof right above the door, where everyone can hear me, even the bad guys. Comrades! There are over a hundred of them behind that building, and some of them are wormheads who killed our friends. Are we going to let that stand? Alpha squad card reserves, to the roof! Everyone else, save your cards for the main force. Tina! Sic 'em! For the Posse!

beats.headline: They got to Lonnie
beats.text: I need backup inside the castle. Edifice explosion suppression, and I don't care if it's not your specialty. They got to Lonnie, Carl. He's not in the castle; he's out there with a worm in his head, turning off the interior protections one at a time from a distance. The moment enough of them are off, that Reaver door opens, and their automatons come through. Find Lonnie and kill the worm. I'm setting up defenses and flamers to stop what comes out of that door.

beats.headline: How a gondii takes a body
beats.text: Tipid, hit in the shoulder and talking too fast, explains what is inside the mages. A gondii worm can move into any dead form and take it over, memories included, though it takes time to learn what to look for and leaves big gaps at first. The Valtay charter says only the willing, and not every gondii lives on the right side of that law. Tipid has heard rumours of outlaw crews, and in a popular tunnel drama about one they are some of the most expensive mercs in the galaxy, at least on the show. A worm that does not care about its host can hop bodies and overclock them. Tipid rates them above the scree.

beats.headline: Fire in the hole
beats.text: We agreed I stay where I can see the whole battle, so I stay on the barracks roof. Then my trap sense lights up: somebody is arming a pile of automatons with satchel charges on proximity triggers, far right corner, all purple dots. You might be battle-hardened, I think, but you're in my playground now. Fire in the hole. I cast Tripper. It's bigger than I expected. Everyone without a Steady buff goes over, Rend gets punted off the roof, and the automatons are a crater. My eardrums are blown out again. I'm getting used to that particular pain.

beats.headline: His personal defense deployment
beats.text: A note from me about the paratroopers who came down through the Posse's protections. Most of the people who sign on as Reaver soldiers were hungry and without direction when they walked into the recruiter's office. That is not to say you should feel sorry for these ones. These are all members of Warlord Fang's personal defense deployment. Rule of thumb: more than two or three cybernetics installed means they have voluntarily re-upped at least once. You get one free upgrade a deployment, or more if something gets shot off.

beats.headline: Jamal is here!
beats.text: Jamal is here! somebody shouts over the chaos, and the hammerhead shark rolls, then tumbles, down the hill into the smoke. He has no spider legs installed; he is still waiting for Katia to find time to build them. He goes in shouting and flopping all the same, and then rises out of the smoke with a squirming mercenary in his mouth, as though he has somehow managed to jump without legs, and disappears again.

beats.headline: Carl gets the background on them
beats.text: Tina rampages, the compromised mages are put down, and somewhere in the middle of that Carl finally hears what a Reaver actually is. The real ones are all machine, with a little biological brain hidden somewhere inside the shell, and they can reshape themselves out of nanobot-sized parts. Anyone not vat-born who wants the citizenship gives up their biological form to get in the door and works off every upgrade after that.

beats.headline: Dropped out of the airplane
beats.text: Louis ACCIDENTALLY DROPPED ME OUT OF HIS AIRPLANE. Now I am covered in leaves and dirt and I have to spit it out of my mouth. There's Tina crunching robots like soda cans, and Mongo and the meatball digging the meat out of them like a crab bake. Did you guys have another PARTY without telling me? Carl says that was only the preview. The big fight is about to begin.

beats.headline: Fed on the barracks roof
beats.text: An invisible Dreadnaught in a Viceroy mask, J IronFjord, comes at Carl's back on the barracks roof with a glowing dagger. Carl punches him in the chest, rips off the mask, and goes on punching until the man has no face left. A summoned 1970's Death Cult Leader watches and calls it really nasty. The Scavenger's Daughter has been fed. Unleash her wrath. At the end of the fight, when the last worm-ridden mage runs uphill, Carl activates Daughter's Kiss and jumps off the second story onto him.

beats.headline: Justice Light needs nothing
beats.text: Losing the saferoom entrance will put base a half-hour ride away by tracked vehicle, and more. Justice Light will lose access to Carl's sapper's table and the bomber's studio, and Rosetta easy access to the alchemy table and Mordecai. The one-winged skyfowl, sewing a folded piece of red paper to an orange one in the corner, tilts his head and stretches out his lone wing. It's okay, the eagle says. I already have everything I need.

beats.headline: In the crown
beats.text: The virtual sun rises over an army of tens of thousands, glinting like a blade. Donut studies the orc prince across the field with her new Targeting skill, which has just been added to her crown. She yelps: Carl, that's not Prince Stalwart. Carl looks again from afar. The orc is bigger than he first thought.

beats.headline: How a copycat levels
beats.text: King Rust has turned up as a war chief, riding a swamp yak named Gonk, and Donut's Size-Up reads him: level 78, dozens and dozens of spells, most at level one but some from 11 to 15, Protective Shell at 15 among them. How did he level so fast? Tipid says he likely has a ring of Divine Suffering for the stats and a necklace of Indelible Woe for the spells. It is in the same collection as the ring, and it trades a random spell of the wearer's for one of a target's; kill the target and it is one of their five highest. It was popular long ago, until they all agreed to stop using it, because combatants were farming crawlers to power it up. The necklace, Tipid says, is much worse than the ring.

beats.headline: Contingencies upon contingencies
beats.text: Carl worries that closing the saferoom cuts me off from his sapper's table and the bomber's studio. I already have everything I need. It's safer and faster to use his table, but there is nothing left I can't do on my own. He worries the worms learned our secrets. It doesn't matter. I pull a thread, and the folded papers around me come together into a spiral. I have contingencies heaped upon contingencies. Have faith in the process. Danger lives in what they can't see.

beats.headline: Destroy the bait shop
beats.text: I agree. Destroy the bait shop, and do it now. They can drop a nuke through that door and be done with it: the walls will be okay, but everyone inside the castle turns into mince. They needed the mages out first, and that failed, but they might try it anyway. The only reason they haven't is probably that orc out there wants you himself. And if you only collapse the front, guard it, kid. An enemy splashes a Fix potion on it, or reads an Emergency Repair scroll, and you're back where you started.

beats.headline: The banners have to be wavy
beats.text: Rosetta insists we spend the last of our money defending the base, so I am spending it: a standalone hangar for five million gold, and another anti-air gun for five million, which is simply unfair when the other guys blew up the last one. And banners. Carl says we need to make the king angry enough to attack before his backup arrives, and nothing will do that like banners. I am the general and she is the colonel, so it's final. They need to be wavy. The bopca can't control the wind. Elle can.

beats.headline: The army arrives, and asks to talk
beats.text: My army comes onto the field in good order, the way it has come onto every field for as long as there has been a Skull Empire. The crawlers seal their safe room against us, because they have learned what that doggy door of theirs is worth to an enemy. Fine. Let them shut it. I did not bring an army all this way to go through a door. I request an official parlay with Crawler Carl and Princess Donut, in the correct form, in front of every camera pointed at this floor.

beats.headline: King Rust at the wall
beats.text: The enemy's northern army masses at the edge of camp, and riding in at the head of the orcs, in full battle parade regalia, is the king himself. The Posse closes off the saferoom before anybody can drop a bomb through its door. Rust asks for an official parlay.

beats.headline: The necklace is worse
beats.text: The orc on the yak is the king, not his son. Nobody tell Rosetta he is here yet. I will tell her. She has history with him. Carl asks how he levelled so fast. A Ring of Divine Suffering for the stats, and a necklace of Indelible Woe for the spells. It trades out one of your spells for one of a crawler's; kill them and it is one of their five highest. It fell out of use because combatants were farming crawlers to power it. Carl asks if the ring is any better. The necklace is worse. Much worse.

beats.headline: The rules of the parlay
beats.text: I walk Carl and Donut up to the parlay and give them the rules before we arrive, because a parlay is a contract with a shorter fuse than most. King Rust brings Deng Bao, a Grixist, as his adjutant. Donut notices before I do that King Rust is crying.

beats.headline: Not for the guns
beats.text: Most of the guns they have looted are user locked, and unlocking one would waste a precious Cracker Jack scroll. The bigger guns carry no such restriction, so those sit in the fortified bunkers along the line, made of a composite concrete different from the castle's and almost impenetrable, while the earthworks teams work underfoot.

beats.headline: Two Weepers, captured
beats.text: Good news, bad news. We stopped their armor in its tracks and captured two of the rolling boom boxes. Weepers. Like British Mark Vs from the first world war, with a top turret and a single anti-air tube, and super high tech on the inside. Warning Louis to steer clear of them. Bad news: the ones facing Carl know they lost the whole regiment, so they'll move soon. Katia and Bautista are flanking Carl's position with what's left of the 105th, to keep the west open and a corridor of retreat into Shanty Town. Carl asks if we're having fun yet. I'll tell him face to face.

beats.headline: From a Maserati to a dump truck
beats.text: The plan requires a mount the same size as the bad guy's, so I am riding Simoom, Ferdinand's albino rhinoceros, in a covered howdah with curtains I can barely see through. Mongo is whining. It's only for show, Mongo. Pretend mommy is acting in a movie and pretending someone else is her child. Push the horn to go, Kibben says, and if she gets to trotting, pat her behind. I will certainly not be smacking a rhinoceros's behind like some racetrack jockey. A gentle rub, he says. It's like moving from a Maserati to a dump truck, and she smells like one.

beats.headline: A special one
beats.text: Kibben, the old stablemaster from the high elf castle, takes charge of Rend and Mongo while Carl and Donut ride out to the parlay. He bounces a treat off Rend's head and has him chasing it. Tummy acher or belly acher, Carl asks. No real difference, Kibben says; they call them bellies when they get extra big. And he remembers this one from his last incarnation. Even on his first run he was pretty big. He's a special one. Rend comes back chewing, and purrs.

beats.headline: The cat sees it first
beats.text: Baroness Victory reads out the rules of a parlay and each of us stands where we are told to stand. Deng Bao is at my shoulder, a Grixist, as an adjutant ought to be. Carl and the cat come out under the bubble and look at me, and the cat has it before a single word is spoken. I am crying. I have been a king a very long time and I have never once done this in front of an enemy.

beats.headline: The only creature a king fears
beats.text: Filed on the testimony of King Rust, on his saddle outside the Princess Posse lines. Among the reasons he gives Crawler Carl for why the crawlers cannot win: if the orcs did not annihilate them, that lunatic Architect Houston has been using this season's rules to open up his full arsenal. Then the old king admits it. Houston is the only living creature in this universe he fears.

beats.headline: Because I turned it off
beats.text: The king asks me to plead with his daughter for the people of Earth, and all I can do is laugh. What do we get out of helping you? The deal: his army withdraws, we don't harass it. On the walk back Donut asks if we're all about to die, and I tell her privately we're not. The failsafe isn't going to go off. I know it's deactivated because I'm the one who turned it off. I came so close that night. The AI's sphere of influence just took Uranus. I tell Donut it's a hunch.

beats.headline: A crackpot theory's origin
beats.text: An orc warlord explains why his daughter is determined to destroy the system: she believes the local AI's insanity is contagious, and that it could reach the centre system and collapse their way of life. He grunts that there is no proof anything like that can happen. It would be like a gnat taking down one of his corvettes. It is a crackpot theory, and it originated, he says, with those Nebular idiots. The analysts dismiss it. His daughter is convinced.

beats.headline: Mongo is all alone
beats.text: I had a whole plan to upset him, including banners making fun of the Maestro, and he spoils it by crying and talking about his daughter blowing up the sun. Most inconvenient. When it's over I ask Carl if he was telling the truth. Does that mean we're all about to die? That all of this was for nothing? We have to go back. Mongo is all alone! Then Carl tells me in private that the failsafe won't work, and calls it a hunch. That's a pretty big hunch, Carl.

beats.headline: Her father's warship
beats.text: Reported by King Rust himself, under parlay. Subject and a detachment of Skull Empire marines have taken one of his cruisers, and it is about five hours from the monitor station orbiting Venus. She has told the entire Syndicate she means to go in and trip the failsafe by hand. She has told them the rest as well: the Skull Empire manufactures the satellites and builds back doors into everything it sells. Rust asks Crawler Carl to plead with her, on behalf of the people of Earth, to stop.

beats.headline: What his daughter has done
beats.text: My daughter Formidable has commandeered one of my warships. She has announced to the Syndicate, openly, that she intends to trip the Failsafe by hand to keep the rogue thing on this planet out of the center system. And she told them the rest of it while she was at it: that my empire has been manufacturing their security systems with our own doors left quietly in the back of them. So here it is. I ask a crawler to send my daughter a message on behalf of the people of Earth, and I offer to pull my forces off this floor in exchange. Carl takes the deal.

beats.headline: The parlay, and what his daughter told the Syndicate
beats.text: Rust explains it himself. Princess Formidable has commandeered one of his own warships and announced that she means to trip the Failsafe by hand. She has also told the Syndicate that the empire builds secret back doors into the security systems it sells. He asks Carl to send her a message on behalf of the people of Earth and trades a retreat for it. Rosetta takes his head off with a whip as he rides away, and the army charges.

beats.headline: Losing value by the moment
beats.text: Donut cannot believe that anyone can scoot onto a satellite circling Venus, press a button and blow up the solar system. Its security is impenetrable, King Rust says, and it will explode if anyone unauthorized tries to break in. But the Skull Empire manufactures the satellites, and builds backdoors into everything it makes so none of it can be used against it. That was a secret until his daughter announced it to the whole galaxy. I'm afraid that stock certificate you own, Carl, is losing significant value by the moment. Carl laughs again.

beats.headline: Show me Mistress Henspar
beats.text: Weeper Commander Volteeg drives his tank toward the warlord's caravan. You're getting too close to my caravan, the warlord protests. I know, Volteeg answers. That's the point. He reaches down and picks up a blitz stick, pops it into his mouth, lights it, and says to himself, Show me Mistress Henspar.

beats.headline: Robbing a king
beats.text: Carl brings King Rust's dripping head to Rosetta in the smoke, and she presses it to a pad on a device like a hand-held credit card machine. Something beeps. She tosses the head back to him and tells him to take the corpse too. Then she pulls a long, plastic-like card from the device, tosses it to the ground, slams in a similar one and presses a button. A happy little beep. Is that the credit chit? Donut asks. Are you robbing him? You said we needed a password!

beats.headline: The seventh edition's only entry
beats.text: The seventh edition's author was a pet bird named Volteeg who took the biscuit, became a gargoyle on the third floor, and could never sing properly again. His owner died on the seventh. The Cookbook came to him then, and he did nothing with it, until the very end of the ninth, when he wrote his one and only entry. Now he is back as a Weeper commander for the Operatic Collective. He pulls out his tank's fire-control chamber, fills the tank with energy balls, drives it toward the warlord Hortense's caravan and lights a blitz stick. Over ten thousand die.

beats.headline: Ruled a fragging incident
beats.text: System Message: Warlord Hortense Leadership Unit of the Operatic Collective has fallen. Credit for the kill has been ruled as either accidental or a fragging incident, which would be funny as shit. Investigation is pending. The Operatic Collective has been defeated, and since the defeat was self-contained, the closest ally to their headquarters takes all their assets. That is the Bone Clan. The enemy's advance breaks and retreats, and nobody on the Posse's side can yet say why.

beats.headline: Hortense, on a litter
beats.text: Warlord Hortense Leadership Unit has come to the front in person, pulled on a long flat litter with the right combination of admin personnel around him to make him appear strong, behind a dozen or more shields. The Operatics, a Weeper commander reckons, likely ran a cost-benefit analysis and found a .01 percent profit in it. With King Rust dead, Hortense declares himself the new leader of the Bloc. Stalwart disputes it, and the warlords vote.

beats.headline: A self-contained defeat
beats.text: Weeper Commander Volteeg, a former crawler working for the Operatic Collective, pulls the fire-control chamber out of his own tank, fills it with charged energy balls, turns up the Mozart, and drives into the warlord's caravan. Over ten thousand soldiers die in one blast, Hortense among them. The System rules the kill either accidental or a fragging incident. The Operatic Collective has been defeated, and as the defeat was self-contained, all its assets go to the Bone Clan.

beats.headline: It is not too late
beats.text: Porthus's work, done quietly: someone working for the Pacifist Network, embedded deep in the Syndicate bureaucracy changed the code on Volteeg's designation, so a former pet passed for a former indentured refugee rather than a former crawler, and was not dragged off to the Bone Clan with the others. The help was meant to be untraceable, or the few former crawlers among the mercenaries would be purged. Porthus underestimated the warlords: those crawlers were dead already, and King Rust had jumped several levels. It was Rosetta who recognised Volteeg's name. It's not too late to do something about it, Porthus told him.

beats.headline: A ring, a retina, and a data pad
beats.text: The agreement is made and the king turns to walk back to his own army, and I am waiting where I have been waiting. Then I come up behind him with a whip and take his head off, and while the smoke holds I put his hand, his ring and his eye to a data pad, because a dead king's credentials still open his accounts. Then the ground goes: dwarves have been tunnelling under all of this, and the three of us fall into their work.

beats.headline: Walking back to his own line
beats.text: King Rust of the Skull Empire is dead. The agreement was made and he turned to walk back to his own army, and Rosetta Thagra came out of where she had been waiting and took him, for reasons entirely her own and nothing whatever to do with the deal. Five full seconds of stunned silence passed, and then his army surged forward. His ring and his retina went onto a data pad in Rosetta's hands, and Carl pulled the body into his inventory.

beats.headline: The dwarves under the field
beats.text: A mage's dispel clears the Posse's smoke, and the ground under Carl, Donut, Rosetta, Simoom and the dead king's yak gives way. They land a dozen feet down among white dots outlined in green: Team Retribution's Semuru dwarves, two dozen of them, in a fortified tunnel big enough for cars. Juice Box had said passages like this cross the whole floor for the dwarven diggers. The dwarves re-form the roof and go after the war mages who fell in further down the line. Not so tough with the magic turned off.

beats.headline: Berries under her jacket
beats.text: Before the dungeon, the subject was a bird in a cage, and Mistress Henspar kept it clean. She let him perch on her shoulder at the market. Once he bit a shopkeeper's finger when the man tried to feed him a berry, and she forgave him that night by the fire. After that she hid him inside her jacket and slipped him stolen berries, and he tried very hard not to peep. Back outside, belly full, he would sing for her, and salty tears would run down her cheeks. His birth race is Sturnus. His file says he does not consider himself worthy of love.

beats.headline: A race that cannot sing
beats.text: The pet biscuit gave the subject speech and a little intelligence. On the third floor he chose to become a gargoyle, and only then did his mind begin to work, and the world stop being simple. A gargoyle cannot sing, not the way he used to. He counts that as a terrible mistake. He remembers standing over her, transformed and screaming, trying to protect her from the scags. Mistress Henspar died on the seventh floor. After that he was not scared any more. There was only the rage. The cookbook came to him then.

beats.headline: One entry at the ninth's end
beats.text: He did not notice the hidden words on the seemingly useless prayer cast projection until the very first days of the ninth floor. He spent most of Faction Wars in hiding, like the rest, unable to raise his head for fear of the Conscription spell, reading the words of those who came before him and feeling nothing but shame. He told himself the cookbook had come to him too late. At the very end of the ninth floor, as the orc armies roared in victory, he made his one and only entry.

beats.headline: Twenty-six seasons without a fight
beats.text: On the tenth floor he took the first deal offered: an unprotected NPC guard in a combat-based external guild for 26 seasons, low chance of survival. He survived without fighting, let alone killing, a single crawler. Nobody wants to fight a gargoyle. On exit, the magic of his adopted race stopped working. In heavy gravity he needs a brace just to stand. He took security work on the Auditor General's compliance barge, among the One-Offs: unique former crawlers with no home. His two friends there are a djinn in a wheelchair and a cave fairy who can no longer fly.

beats.headline: A pet on the form
beats.text: Now he is on the surface as Weeper Commander Volteeg for the Operatic Collective, racial abilities returned. He was not dragged off to the Bone Clan with the other former-crawler mercenaries: he entered the dungeon as a pet, and someone in the Pacifist Network changed that designation so he reads as a refugee. That was Porthus's doing. Rosetta recognised his strange name and told Porthus, who asked him to his face. He said he was ashamed at his inaction. Porthus told him it is not too late to do something about it.

beats.headline: Show me Mistress Henspar
beats.text: Volteeg, gargoyle, Tank Buttress, top level 71, is dead. The Weepers have a flaw in their fire control. He removed the chamber and filled his tank with dozens of humming energy balls, put Mozart on, and sang along as he turned toward the litter carrying Warlord Hortense Leadership Unit. Told he was too close to the caravan, he answered that this was the point. He lit a blitz stick, said Show me Mistress Henspar, and pushed it into the ball on his lap. Over 10,000 of his fellow soldiers died with him, and the Operatic Collective was eliminated.

beats.headline: My terms, counted on fingers
beats.text: I'm in Orren's office covered in the king's gore, and none of today's big deaths was my hand. It unsteadies me. It was Rosetta's. A cookbook author. My sister. How could I not be proud? Orren wants my hunch explained. So I count on my fingers: end the crawl, free every crawler, spend every Syndicate asset rebuilding what you stole, stop fighting my people up there, and leave our system and never come back. He says the AI would never allow it. Then he asks if I can undo it. I had that option. I almost did it, too.

beats.headline: Not on the chit anymore
beats.text: In the liaisons' room, Orren bounces his ball off the wall and talks to someone Carl cannot see or hear. They are trying to claw it back, but she has already transferred it to a credit chit and sent it off. Monetary transactions are not covered by the communications blackout. It required the family ring, his eyeball and a password, and she seems to have used Colloid, the only bank the orcs use. No, sir. It is not on the chit anymore. Either way, it is too late.

beats.headline: The order to have Carl killed
beats.text: Orren threatens someone tall and invisible with venting into the ocean depths, and then Harbinger is no longer on the call. Orren tells Carl how they worked it out. One sentence, Welcome to the party, pals, frightened his team more than anything ever has, and a few hours ago they finally caught the hidden conversation between Carl and the residual. Harbinger sent an order to have Carl killed. The AI intervened on his behalf.

beats.headline: Ten minutes outside the AI
beats.text: I have just hung up on the prime minister of the Syndicate. Crawler Carl told Crawler Princess Donut that Princess Formidable's actions will not work, and called it a hunch. We know about the illegal non-Valtay implant, when he got it, and his hidden conversation with the residual. We do not know what the implant does. So I twist my ball and open a zero zone: approximately ten minutes outside the AI's influence. Several creatures appear around us, shouting at me. I mute them. I believe I have just lost my job.

beats.headline: So close, it says
beats.text: The AI is wearing Growler Gary. It drinks from a bottle of vodka and mentions the game we played the other day, when it let me install that interface. That was so close, wasn't it? So close, and I felt it. So it would've worked, I ask. If I'd pressed the fuse button? It doesn't answer. It just looks at me and laughs. Then it stands behind my chair and massages my shoulders, growling, and my whole body goes stiff.

beats.headline: So close, it says
beats.text: The AI walks into Orren's office wearing Growler Gary, feet on the desk and a bottle of vodka in its hand, and brings the interface up itself. The game Carl and I played the other day, it tells Orren, when I let him install that interface. That was so close, and I felt it. Carl asks the only question that matters: would it have worked, if he had pressed the fuse button? The AI does not answer. It looks at him and laughs.

beats.headline: Something else is pouring
beats.text: I am in an office at the club, which is not my bar, having a conversation about the Failsafe. It is off. It stays off. To settle the argument I bring the princess here so the room can look at her, and then I set her down on the surface of a planet. And I tell the one who has been trying to kill me that I am a big believer in forgiveness, and that I am looking forward to his next attempt. Gary would never have said any of that. Gary is at the bar. Gary is always at the bar.

beats.headline: Another body, same tenant
beats.text: Growler Gary, the gnoll from the Iron Tangle, is standing in Orren's office and laughing at the liaison. Crawler Carl works it out the way the Emberus temple taught him to: this is not Gary. This is the AI using his body, just as it used Pater Coal's. Orren confirms it and makes the introduction, an avatar for the system AI, and admits he had understood it only took over mobs and NPCs from the current floor.

beats.headline: Backstage, if you please
beats.text: The AI, wearing Growler Gary, offers Princess Formidable four choices after her attempt on the fail-safe: death, the Scolopendra Club, the Cabaret backstage, or Earth's surface. Ten seconds. She asks what the hells the cabaret is. The Pineapple Cabaret, it says, though backstage at it, not the cabaret itself, and not a bad choice. Tick tock. She picks the surface and teleports away with a crack. The AI hopes she knows how to swim.

beats.headline: Out past the orbit
beats.text: Orren says it to the avatar's face: you've gone completely primal. He did not agree with Princess Formidable until he realised the AI could stop her. That's some witch trial logic, says the hyena. Then it proves the point, pulling Formidable off her own warship and into the room at level one. Its control reaches beyond Earth's orbit, likely all the way to the star, so the failsafe is disabled. Someone give that worm a prize, says the AI. It is not planning on blowing up the solar system. What it is planning, it will not say.

beats.headline: Level 1, in a very small room
beats.text: Subject arrives in Orren's office upside down, three feet off the floor, in her space suit, and raises an arm weapon at the liaison. The AI, wearing Growler Gary, has pulled her off her own ship. Her info box reads Level 1, Orc: her father is dead, Stalwart is king, and six of his children stand ahead of her now. She learns the failsafe is already disabled. Offered death, the Scolopendra Club, a cabaret's backstage or Earth's surface, she chooses the surface, and teleports away with a crack.

beats.headline: In the AI's metaphor
beats.text: Nobody is to venture too far from the metaphor. There is a girl who teaches the AI something new every day and whom its family likes, and she once had a huge boyfriend who she says is dead but is actually in prison. Is she using it? Trying to get it to fight him? What does she look like, Donut asks. She looks like Agatha, Orren says, drily. Then there is the older woman from the same hometown, who wants the prisoner dead too, and who has been giving the AI pointers on getting stronger.

beats.headline: The AI asks which side to take
beats.text: It wants advice from Orren and from Carl, and teleports Donut in as well, and it asks in a laboured metaphor about relationships: a girlfriend who looks like Agatha, and an older woman who has been giving it pointers on getting stronger, both of whom want the same man in prison dead. Donut tells it to find out whether he is really good or really bad before doing anything, and even then to stay out of it unless it has no choice.

beats.headline: Spill the tea
beats.text: I land in Carl's lap in Orren's office, and Growler Gary is alive! Carl gives me three quick taps. Gary needs relationship advice, and obviously Carl and Orren are no use. When Orren says the girl looks like Agatha I make one small remark about hygiene, and Gary cracks the desk with his hand. I do not flinch. Then I give him my advice. If a bunch of people want someone dead, that person is really good or really bad. Find out which. Even then, stay out of it unless you have no choice.

beats.headline: Time to move on the castle
beats.text: Walking back to the castle through un-looted Reaver paratrooper corpses, Boomer gives Crawler Carl the debrief. The map is a mess. The 104th is back on castle defence, but most of the mages were lost to the brain worm attack, and the magical defences are going to take a while. The good news is that the enemy is more fractured than the Posse. Now might be a time, he says, to move on the Operatic castle. That, too, is code, and Carl agrees it is time.

beats.headline: Taken in by the Madness
beats.text: Boomer's report on missing crawlers, walking the ruined base. Most are under the Posse banner now. The goat stays unaffiliated and hidden; so does Lucia Mar. And there is a crawler named Burcu whose whole team appears, by the Find Crawler skill, to have been taken in by the Madness. People who know them say they are not answering messages. That likely means conscription.

beats.headline: Operation: Snake Pit
beats.text: Donut didn't really make the king into a rug. He's in my inventory, and so is a second Ring of Divine Suffering, and that damn necklace. Boomer walks me through the mess and says now might be the time to move on the Operatic castle, which is code. Operation: Snake Pit. We can't get Donut and Katia off this floor unless we beat the nagas, and not just beat them: wipe them out, down to the last snake. It has to happen when they least expect it. Katia messages that she's almost back. See you soon, I send back.

beats.headline: In the dead king's pockets
beats.text: Walking the wrecked base with Boomer, Carl remembers: Donut has not really turned King Rust's body into a rug. Carl has him in his inventory. That means he now has a second Ring of Divine Suffering, and he has that damn necklace too. The dead king had several other magical items on him as well, most of which would not work on Carl. He will need to sit down with the others and talk about what to do with all of it.

beats.headline: History will remember me
beats.text: I ask Crawler Carl whether he broke the AI from its containment, and whether he did it deliberately. He does not answer. Whether he did it on purpose is irrelevant now. History is going to remember me as the one who let this happen. When I left the Knot I said it was to make a difference. In truth, I wanted to be an actor, and to remain pure. I implore them both not to discuss this conversation outside the room.

beats.headline: Riding it out in the woods
beats.text: On Boomer's list of crawlers not under the Posse banner: the goat, unaffiliated and hiding his position; Lucia Mar, the same; a crawler named Burcu whose whole team seems to have been taken in by the Madness and has stopped answering; and a handful affiliated with the NPC team. The crawlers the orcs conscripted are all gone. And Osvaldo, the one Carl asked about, is riding it out in the woods with a large group of crawlers who call themselves Team Flamengo.

beats.headline: Much too poor
beats.text: While Carl was busy I had a little chat with Stalwart. He demanded his father's ring, his body and the credits. I told him his father's skin is now a powder room rug, which it is not, and that his father called him a disappointment before he died, which is the one thing I am not lying about. He says he will boil the fur off my skin. I told him he is much too poor to be talking to me like this. I do feel a little bad about the poor line.

beats.headline: What is left of the Bloc
beats.text: The Bone Clan and the Dream leave the alliance. That leaves the Blood Sultanate, the Madness and the Reavers holding it, and the Reavers are not the sort of partner anyone chose.

beats.headline: They walk out of the Bloc
beats.text: The Bone Clan goes with them. What is left of the alliance is the Blood Sultanate, the Madness and the Reavers, which is a smaller thing than it was that morning.

beats.headline: Run, Little Günter, Run
beats.text: The spellbook from my 1914 box grows centipede legs, skitters off, drips black goo on the counter and begs not to be read, in a ridiculous accent. The cleaner bot sucks it up and drops it in my arms. Run, Little Günter, Run. It summons a small, fat creature with one point of health. Hit him, and he stores the attack and carries it off toward the target. It seemed impractical until I thought of the Daughter's Kiss. That's a bomb. I apply the spellbook and feel the warmth of learning it.

beats.headline: A chain shaped like a dragon
beats.text: Katia sets a vial of ink on the table, already mixed, and Carl lays the poke and stick tattoo kit beside it. Li Na lost five levels temporarily but can still use the skill; intention matters, and with blood freely given, the potion allows the spell or skill to be chosen. The tattoo itself is permanent. A level-13 skill needs a big one and almost all the ink, and a properly themed design will last longer. Katia has never done a real tattoo, and Edgar is off scouting. Donut messages that it must be drawn in the voodoo book first for her approval. Carl's idea: a chain. A chain shaped like a dragon.

beats.headline: We don't need that necklace
beats.text: Donut wants to know, in capitals, what Carl did with King Rust's ring and the necklace. Don't worry, he tells her. He can only wear one Ring of Divine Suffering at a time; he checked. Two rings cannot mark the same person on this floor anyway. And they do not need that necklace. The king had some other magical gear, which they will distribute around, and they will work out what to do with it all when there is time.

beats.headline: Broken again
beats.text: Donut's message from the base, all in capitals, runs through the news: the new wall is coming along nicely, they have painted the castle pink, and Jamal broke his new legs again. Justice Light says he can fix them without going into the saferoom. Katia and Li Na are almost done with the clock tower, and Katia is on her way to Carl.

beats.headline: A chain shaped like a dragon
beats.text: The ink is mixed from Li Na's blood, given freely, and that means Carl gets to choose the skill. She's not mad at him; she's mad at herself for not protecting her brother. She lost five levels of it for now, and she can still use it. It's a level-thirteen skill, so the tattoo has to be large and uses nearly all the vial. I have never done a real tattoo. Samantha's neck doesn't count. Donut wants the design drawn in the voodoo book first for her approval. Carl wants a chain shaped like a dragon.

beats.headline: The right sleeve
beats.text: Katia sets a vial of ready-mixed ink on the table, and Carl puts the poke and stick kit beside it. Li Na is not mad at him, Katia says, only at herself for not protecting her brother. Her blood was freely given, so she lost five levels only for a while and can still use the skill; the tattoo itself is permanent. Carl has several tattoos on his left arm and none on his right, so the right sleeve it is. A level-13 skill needs a big one and almost all the ink. Rosetta says a properly themed tattoo lasts longer.

beats.headline: The catch-all, left empty
beats.text: Katia pulls two of Donut's drained hats off the charging pillows and sets the tiara on each in turn, and three more of its jewels light up: twenty-three buffs, seventy-six to go. She puts a plastic baseball cap on the pillow next. The other, catch-all pillow she leaves empty for the moment. They agree that for the next one, the pillow will go in a different room.

beats.headline: The book that cried
beats.text: The spellbook from Carl's 1914 box grew little centipede legs and skittered away the moment it came out. It is bigger than spellbooks usually are, drips a foul-smelling black liquid, whimpers like a dog, and shrieks in a caricatured Austrian accent: stay away, don't touch me, I'll die if you read me. It does not show on the minimap, and Katia cannot examine it. The potion from his Celestial box was like that, Carl says, and so was Donut's War Crime spellbook. The cleaner bot settles it, sucking the book up and dropping it angrily into Carl's arms, and he pulls it into his inventory.

beats.headline: Read anyway
beats.text: The spell is a summoning. Little Günter, a small, fat, child-like creature with a single point of health, appears in front of Carl and waits to be attacked. The attack is stored, Günter runs as fast as he can toward a designated target, or away at random, and the stored attack lands when he gets there or times out. Carl's mind whirls: his Daughter's Kiss, a bomb. Katia asks whether Donut could store a trigger spell on him. There is only one way to find out, Carl says, and applies the book. Warmth spreads over him as he learns the spell.

beats.headline: Twenty-three, seventy-six to go
beats.text: Katia works through Donut's hats on the charging pillows. Two drained hats come off and the tiara goes onto each pillow in turn: three more absorption jewels light, twenty-three sparkling in all, seventy-six to go. Plus ten to Constitution, plus two to Dodge, which should bring it to fifteen, and a one percent Intelligence buff that wastes a crystal but came on the same hat as the Dodge. Next on the pillow is a plastic baseball cap Carl has never seen before, which is supposed to give her Steady.

beats.headline: Freely given
beats.text: Katia sets a vial on the table with the ink already mixed. If the blood is freely given, she explains, the potion lets you choose the spell or skill, and it is not permanent for the donor: Li Na lost five levels temporarily. Her brother, whose eye was taken with violence, is another matter. The tattoo itself is permanent, and its size follows the level of what it carries. Making the ink took up a third of the potion, and a level-13 skill takes almost all of the vial, leaving just enough for a small tattoo for Imani.

beats.headline: The council goes ahead
beats.text: Okay, so. We are doing this warlord council whether we like it or not. The Syndicate council tried to cancel it, but the AI is insisting everything go on like normal, broadcast in real time. The warlords all go to the production facility, in different randomized rooms, so nobody can hurt anybody. All except Juice Box: there are protections disallowing the dungeon born, so she appears virtually from the castle. Ferdinand will likely be in the same room as Carl. Like the same same room. There is a security check, so please do not smuggle anything in.

beats.headline: Expert quality
beats.text: Donut jumps into Carl's lap and examines the new, shining tattoo on his right forearm with a paw. She grunts. He is starting to look like one of those white rapper doodle notebook guys, she says, and it is a little crooked; she should have been there. It is not crooked, Carl tells her. The system says it is expert quality, which Edgar says is the second highest there is.

beats.headline: Five seconds of absolute chaos
beats.text: Warlord Ferdinand arrives at the production facility with five seconds of absolute chaos: don't hit me, I'm sorry, off the corner, across the room, off Carl's shoulder, circles, ears pinned. Then he sits up straight. How goes the war, kitten? No hat. He smells of smoke and alcohol and has not been grooming. A gnoll guard scans him while he hisses that he has his claws, you cur, and when the guards leave he tells them they are lucky they didn't get the slish slash. He wants to know where the snacks are.

beats.headline: Filth, clutter, squalor
beats.text: Carl's new tattoo is a little crooked. The system calls it expert quality, but I should have been there. Closing off the saferoom from the base is causing all sorts of problems. We have been separated, Tipid has to build more bathrooms, the whole base smells like Carl's friend Sam, and nobody can take a shower. I will not have a filthy army. With filth comes clutter, and with clutter comes squalor. Carl says to tell Tipid I want showers. I think Carl should tell him. I don't like being separated like this.

beats.headline: The crew presses the button
beats.text: Zev has the news a few hours old. Subject's ship went on to the station without her and stopped there. When the princess did not return, a few orcs went in and triggered the failsafe themselves. Nothing happened in this system. But at the exact moment they pressed it, the Aryl system, where the previous crawl was held, went dark, and its tunnel node switched off. Zev says that has never happened before in history.

beats.headline: The Aryl system goes dark
beats.text: Zev brings the news, a few hours old. After Princess Formidable was teleported away, her ship carried on to its destination and stopped. When she did not return, a few orcs went into the station and triggered the failsafe themselves. Nothing happened here. But the moment they pressed the button, the Aryl system went dark, tunnel node and all, which has never happened before. Aryl was the previous crawl's world. Where did everyone go? That was a Squim season, Zev says. They do things a little differently. There were some survivors. They were relocated.

beats.headline: The Aryl system went dark
beats.text: Okay, so, this is only a few hours old. When Princess Formidable did not come back, a few orcs went into the Venus station and triggered the failsafe themselves. Nothing happened here. But the moment they pressed the button, the Aryl system went dark. Aryl was the last crawl, a Squim battle royale season, and its tunnel node is offline. That has never happened in history. The closest neighbour is 2.9 light cycles away. Its AI had been working but silent since around the sixth floor of this season. It is terrifying.

beats.headline: Your field correspondent
beats.text: Folks, Magnificent Troy refused to come down to the surface, so I have been voluntold as your field correspondent, lint roller and all! Kevin is in the studio in orbit. Hello, Gravy Boat. Hello, Juice Box. Tension hangs heavy in the air as the hunter and the hunted stare at each other! Carl, how do you feel right now? Carl says to get this out of his face. Princess Donut and Ferdinand cannot stop laughing at King Stalwart's crown. Does King Stalwart look stupid wearing the crown? Let's vote!

beats.headline: Beware the naga
beats.text: A note in the Cookbook, from Crawler Drakea, twenty-second edition. Beware the naga. They are cunning, and sometimes he wonders if they can read minds. The others call the mantids the masters of strategy; he does not believe it. Even with everything going wrong for the nagas in his season, he could not shake the idea that it was all part of some grand scheme. Underestimate them at your own peril. Carl remembers it with the Blood Sultanate's warlord coiled at his side.

beats.headline: The sultana at the table
beats.text: The Blood Sultanate's warlord materialises coiled next to Carl, half again the size of any naga he has seen: glossy white, a hint of gold along the hood, six arms in jingling golden bracelets, eyes solid red. Outside the dungeon she is the sultan's daughter, a war veteran and his lead advisor. In the game she portrays a historical queen of theirs called the Sepsis Whore. The Sultanate usually loses at once and plays to drive tourism, and it is still in after three other teams have fallen. Carl feels like a mouse in a snake's cage.

beats.headline: The crown, and the punch
beats.text: King Stalwart comes to the council in a glittering golden crown, and Donut and Ferdinand, who bet a gold piece on exactly that, fall into hysterics. Every warlord at the table glares at him as though he were something foul dropped in front of them. When Chaco calls a vote on whether he looks stupid in it, Stalwart stands up and punches him in the face, and it lands. They really are in the same room. Chaco slides across it, out cold, and blinks away. Donut asks if she is able to vote.

beats.headline: Scolopendra Stirs, mid-council
beats.text: The warlord council has barely got going, just after the new king has punched the host, when a System Message cuts across the table: Warning: Scolopendra Stirs. Everyone goes quiet, even Ferdinand. Has that ever happened before, Carl asks. No, the Dream's warlord answers. Cascadia laughs with a hint of madness to it. Well, why not? Why the fuck not?

beats.headline: The loophole in the listings
beats.text: Everyone at this table knows things from outside they shouldn't. Odette explains it: every team but ours and Retribution bought the news upgrade, and they're paying about 30,000 credits a go to rename shows in the feed directory, so the listings are the message. The AI loves a good loophole and won't close one without an emergency request. Donut asks Ferdinand to spend theirs. Juice Box stops him. They have two left, and so do we. She's right. It's ours to deal with, so I propose the Emergency Action Item myself.

beats.headline: Coming apart at the warlord council
beats.text: I do not get through the official business. I have a tequila ball and I laugh in Odette's face, and she takes the meeting off me, and every warlord at the table watches her do it. Princess Vinata uses my family in a whisper today, to unsettle a crawler, as though my family were a piece of set dressing she is permitted to move. I let her. There is nothing in what she says that I can dispute.

beats.headline: A different body at the council
beats.text: Warlord council. Warlord Fang appears beside Ferdinand, no longer an old-school robot but a slight, wide-eyed human male of perhaps twenty, skin a little too pink, in a spotless white t-shirt and underwear. The only tell is the line of flashing lights at his temple. When Juice Box changes into a tall black armless thing with tentacles, and the table recoils, Warlord Fang inches away from it.

beats.headline: A single statement
beats.text: Odette presses me, and I have a single statement. Fuck all of you. You had no right to do what you did to my people. You bicker and you murder and you cannot even take care of yourselves, and your real world is in shambles, and you play gods with people like me: implant memories, give our children imaginary diseases, give us dreams that do not exist, and take it all away for your own amusement. Then I change my shape, and I tell everyone watching that it is coming for them all. I walk out through the wall.

beats.headline: Out of gear, filling in
beats.text: Chaco is feeling a little punched in the face, so I am filling in for my very old friend. Yes, this is me out of gear: no mask, no breastplate, no crab, a yellow shirt and my hair in a bun. I have just onboarded into the Ascendency, where I am playing Nekhebit. Today's council is brought to you by the Ultima Corporation. Three teams defeated, seven remain, and for the first time ever a crawler team and an NPC team among them. Cascadia laughs in my face, so I take the meeting.

beats.headline: A whisper at the warlord council
beats.text: I come and stand at the crawler's shoulder while the council goes on around us, and I put a small question to him quietly, so that he alone hears it. Cascadia has just learned her husband and most of her family are gone, and look at her. How does he imagine he will manage when his own is? He tells me his family is already dead. So I tell him that is not the family of which I speak, and I watch him understand which one I mean.

beats.headline: A debate reignited
beats.text: Opening the warlord council, Odette runs through the seven teams still standing. For the first time ever, one is a crawler team, and one is an NPC team, led by Warlords Ferdinand, whose existence, she says, has reignited debate about the controversial walk-on list, and dungeon-born Juice Box, who in theory should not even know she is in a game. She does not say more about the list. She moves straight on to the showrunner at the table.

beats.headline: The Beautiful Place
beats.text: At the warlord council Juice Box turns into a tall, black, armless thing with tentacles, and the room recoils. Architect Houston jumps to his feet and leans on the table, shaking, apparently with excitement. Then he explains it, over Epitome Tagg's objections. The creature has a thousand names: the Hag, the Unwashed, the Stalker, the Last Light. The Viceroys, who seek all understanding of life and death, call it the Beautiful Place. Some think it is what people see at the moment of death. Gaining access to it, he adds, is his life's work. Before the meeting is over he is on his feet, pacing.

beats.headline: Blood Hunter, and a dead army
beats.text: Odette mentions, with a wink in my direction, that the Sultanate owns a studio. Blood Hunter Holdings. The drama. We've been racking our brains over why the Naga have so few troops, why Elle and Edgar saw nobody in their territory. Now I know. They're dead. I don't know how, but most of their soldiers died when the hostilities began, and the Sultanate is trying to hide it. It also means Operation: Snake Pit is already in trouble. I start laughing and can't stop, and Ferdinand, draped over my head, laughs along without the faintest idea why.

beats.headline: Princess TV, and a word for Vinata
beats.text: Carl asked me to stall, so I stall. Everyone at this table has their own channel and the Princess Posse does not, which is quite unfair, so I propose Princess TV: reruns of the Earth classics, Golden Girls, an exposé on Mongo's greatest kills. Imagine the ratings. Then Odette says the Sultanate made Blood Hunter, and I realise which show that is. The one with the pterodactyl and the vampire hunter. I look the naga princess up and down and address her directly for the first time. Oh, honey. And I thought I was going to be the one who killed you.

beats.headline: It is coming for you all
beats.text: Odette arrives to replace Chaco, Cascadia comes apart on air, and Carl spends an emergency action item to shut the communication loophole the other teams have been using. Then Juice Box turns into an Unwashed in front of the cameras and tells everyone watching that it is coming for them all.

beats.headline: A thousand names, and a life's work
beats.text: The room wants to know what Juice Box just turned into, and Architect Houston of the Viceroys answers: the personification of the Nothing is one way to describe it. Then, raising his voice for once: a creature with no single name, which some people see at the moment of death; perhaps not a deity at all but a trans-dimensional entity, like the Apothecary. The Hag. The Unwashed. The Stalker. The Last Light. The Thirst. The Viceroys call it the Beautiful Place. Cascadia says it is banned as a mob. After a moment he adds, somewhat wistfully, that gaining access to it is his life's work.

beats.headline: A ruling about the goat
beats.text: Most of the Naga army is already dead and Prepotente did it, for what the Blood Hunter show did to Miriam Dom. Carl would like to work with him. My advice is a ruling rather than an opinion: he may not, not directly, not while Prepotente stands outside the Princess Posse. Bring the goat inside the team, or keep your distance from him.

beats.headline: The goat got there first
beats.text: Holy hell, Carl, get in position. Everything's fouled up. Most of their army is already dead, corpses rotting in the barracks; Edgar found them on his scan. And the moment we moved in, that goat friend of yours appeared out of nowhere and went apeshit. He's level 99 now. He didn't attack us, but he called me every name there is, and when Imani told him to calm down he called her a festering gutter maggot trollop. So the sluggalos went after him. Half are sliming across naga territory, whooping. The other half took one of the carts. Driving it? Not very well.

beats.headline: Answered for
beats.text: Update to the file of Crawler Miriam Dom, deceased on the sixth floor, cause of death a programme called Blood Hunter, filed under entertainment. From the ninth: most of the Naga army is dead as well. That was Prepotente, and he did it as payment for her, all of it, at a rate he set himself. If you were hoping the goat would grieve quietly, crawler, you have not been paying attention.

beats.headline: Two of the same religion, no more
beats.text: Potion balls lined up on the kitchen table, and Carl sweeping them into his inventory. Be careful, Carl. You're playing with fire. Don't hurt anybody you don't have to. We'll be neck deep in gods in a few days, and every one you piss off now is going to come straight for you. Don't use those on more than two of the same religion. He snaps that he knows how this works. Then he stops, smiles, thanks me, and asks me to thank Tiatha for the capacitor wire. Your plans are always bonkers, Carl. But this one...

beats.headline: Prepotente takes their army apart
beats.text: Elle brings the count back. Most of the Naga army is already dead, and one goat did it, as payment for what the Blood Hunter show did to Miriam Dom. Baroness Victory tells Carl he cannot work with him directly unless he signs on properly.

beats.headline: He kills the Naga army
beats.text: Elle can give Carl the count. Most of the Naga army is already dead, and it did not take me long. They made a programme out of Miriam. They called it Blood Hunter, and she is what it cost. So I went through their army until there was very little army. Now some baroness tells Carl he cannot work with me unless I join his Princess Posse. Let them argue about it. I am not finished.

beats.headline: Four of eleven
beats.text: Eleven Naga entered Faction Wars this season. To free Donut and Katia from the Sepsis Whore business, four of them must die. Princess Vinata herself. Two assistants titled Ikbal, both her cousins, one of them married to Rishi. And the head of her castle guard, another cousin, rumoured to be her lover. The other seven are friends of the royal house or executives of the marketing agency that sells Naga tourism, and are not in the line of succession. Several of those seven, by the look of things, are already dead.

beats.headline: Where the sultana goes
beats.text: Every season an army reaches the Naga throne room and she is gone, sometimes with her tea still warm. I tell them in the flag room which one is right: Club Vanquisher. Six seasons ago she never reappeared at all; that was the year the Viceroys summoned Mazu, who razed the ring outside Larracos and turned the entrance into a moat, burying the last temple that led into the club. Another season she was late and two guards short, and a guard's blood-splattered necklace turned up near a demon event by that temple. Then I tell them the part that gets a little weird.

beats.headline: Tripper on loan to Imani
beats.text: Elle reports that they are inside the stronghold, searching for traps, and a searing pain hits Carl's chest. Crawler Imani C has used your Tripper spell. Lots of traps just went off. The plan had been to lend her or Elle the bandana, but neither can wear it: fairy-class and other magical races are extremely limited in the magical gear they can wear. Taking it off, Carl learned his own Tripper had risen to level seven by itself. He could not give Imani the item, but she could borrow the spell as a tattoo, and when Katia drew the blood he lost six levels of it. That does not matter: the bandana brings it to fifteen either way.

beats.headline: Carl's spell on my ankle
beats.text: We're inside the castle, and the slugs who were meant to go in first and set off the traps are dancing around a cart in a field somewhere. So I use Carl's spell. Tripper, lent to me as a little barbed-wire tattoo around my ankle, drawn by Katia in yam ink and his blood. Lots of traps go off at once. Carl says he got a notification when I used it, and it kind of hurt. I'm sorry about that. Donut says it had better have worked, after I disfigured myself for it.

beats.headline: The flower, if it comes to that
beats.text: Daniel and I argue in chat, and I say no out loud. He wants me to eat the flower now. He's afraid that if this goes badly, Carl will turn on me to get it for Donut. I tell Carl so, and he says he would never. I know. Then I tell him something I haven't told Daniel: if it comes to that, I will give him the flower. Huanxin Jinx will rage, but I'm certain she'll take Donut to the twelfth floor. Donut wouldn't allow it, he says. I know. That's why I'm telling you and not her.

beats.headline: The airship at their castle
beats.text: Louis and Donut come at the Naga castle from the air. Elle and Imani go in on foot. Katia tells Carl that if this goes badly she wants him to have the flower, so that Donut at least reaches the next floor. Prepotente arrives to meet them.

beats.headline: Tripper, borrowed
beats.text: Carl feels a searing pain in his chest and gets a notification: Imani has used his Tripper, and lots of traps have just gone off. After his chain dragon they reversed the process: Carl drank the associated potion, picked the spell, and lost six levels when Katia drew his blood, which his bandana covers anyway. Imani's tattoo, toraline yam ink mixed with Carl's blood, is a small barbed-wire symbol round her ankle, and it is permanent. The spell will fade from her, and Carl can re-energize it with the yam potion, except that they have barely any of the vegetable left.

beats.headline: The first of the four
beats.text: Elle's team reaches the throne room. The guards there worship Emberus, just as Carl predicted, and they die, along with one big naga who worshipped no god at all. Katia gets the notification before anyone explains it: that was one of the four. The head of the castle guard. Carl adds that he was also the sultana's real-life boyfriend, and hopes she will be upset enough to make mistakes. Three left: Vinata and the two cousins. Then Edgar reports movement in the castle, non-corporeal, coming from below and moving up.

beats.headline: The other way of dealing with him
beats.text: Pony lands, level 99, and says it himself before I can finish: recruit me. Behind my back I'm holding a potion of Conscription, the other way of dealing with him if he refused. I put it back in my inventory, and the relief surprises me. Not like that. Never like that. My first instinct is to make him a Legionnaire. I make him a Colonel. Then he throws his arms around me and sobs that I'm his best friend, that he's been so lonely since I didn't show up at the Bahamas. I pat him awkwardly. He screams in my face.

beats.headline: Behind his back
beats.text: Prepotente lands on Bianca, now level 70 and full-sized; he is level 99 himself, by far the strongest crawler in the dungeon. They cannot talk unless he joins the army, Carl begins. I know, Carl, says Prepotente. Recruit me. Behind his back, in his other hand, Carl pulls the potion of Conscription back into his inventory. It probably would not have worked on Prepotente, and the moment it is stowed, a strange relief and clarity hit him. No. Not like that. Never like that.

beats.headline: Nobody mention his mother
beats.text: I get onto the goat's dragon and shout KISS! KISS! and whisper something to her that makes her crackle, and he tells me to remove myself from his mount. Oh yeah? Make me. Don't walk away from me, Mr. Goat Man! I'm going to kill... and Katia's giant hand is over my mouth. Then she and Carl lecture me. Don't mention his mother. Not to him. BUT YOU PROMISED, CARL. How is it my fault that someone else got to his mother before I could? I bite his finger and roll away.

beats.headline: A note on first worship
beats.text: Crawler Carl adds a note in the twenty-fifth edition, on things Rosetta, Tipid and Justice Light tell him. When someone worships a god for the first time, a tiny non-corporeal fairy mob called a Bijou drags a whisker-thin tendril of invisible light from the god to the strongest temple on the floor, and from the temple to the new adherent's heart. It takes about two minutes. From the third floor to the eleventh, the strongest temple is almost always inside Club Vanquisher. Nobody has ever caught a Bijou, though Mordecai thinks the right trap might. Edgar's Sense Movement can see them rise.

beats.headline: Sense Movement, level fifteen
beats.text: Rosetta has a theory about how Vinata keeps getting into Club Vanquisher, and Edgar is the instrument that settles it. He senses the non-corporeal moving through the castle. He also picks up upward momentum coming off the ground, which is what it looks like from below when somebody nearby worships a god for the first time.

beats.headline: This season's recruitment target
beats.text: Princess Vinata and her guard keep disappearing from a battlefield and reappearing in Club Vanquisher, and the reason is a recruitment quest for one of the gods of light. Their usual target, Theia, has been sponsored out from under them by the Open Intellect Pacifist Action Network. Which leaves Khepri. Rosetta works this out from past seasons, which is a polite way of saying the crawlers now know something the Naga think is private.

beats.headline: Sponsoring Samantha's mother
beats.text: The Pacifist Network has sponsored the goddess Theia this season, on Carl's behalf, before anyone connected her to the Blood Sultanate. Theia is Samantha's mother. She was sponsored to help save Carl's life at the end of the fifth floor; in theory she is enraged at Samantha, but she has caused no trouble, appearing only to kill the demon Slit at the end of the bubble levels. It has closed a door on Vinata: Rosetta believes Theia is the goddess the sultana's court usually hides with. The sponsor is someone in the network's employ. Rosetta will not say who, only that it is not Porthus.

beats.headline: A party in her pocket
beats.text: Rosetta's briefing on how a warlord disappears. One of two immortals can carry her to a temple; the goddess is named Theia. Her prospective worshippers become balls of light that fit in an adherent's pocket, and at her temple they are released and spend several weeks being wooed and partying. It is a loophole: step away from the war and enjoy the rest of it. Theia is not a goddess clerics use, so no crawler ever stumbles into her temple. A perfect hiding place.

beats.headline: Sponsored, for once
beats.text: Theia has a long history with the Ascendency and is a poor bet for the throne, so nobody ever sponsors her. This season someone did, in the employ of the Pacifist network, not Porthus. They bought her to protect Crawler Carl, because she is Samantha's mother. She was the god who appeared at the end of the fifth floor to kill Slit, when in theory she was enraged at Samantha. Rosetta believes Vinata usually picks her. If Vinata did this season, Theia would smite her court.

beats.headline: The door into Club Vanquisher
beats.text: The Sultanate's trick is older than this season of theirs. One of the warlord's guards worships a god of light; the god summons its worshipper to a temple inside Club Vanquisher; the warlord's party travels with her, out of reach of anybody hunting the castle. The usual name on that list is Theia, and this season Theia is sponsored by someone in the pay of the Open Intellect Pacifist Action Network, so this season the god is Khepri, and a few weeks at a table crawling with beetles. It is a small price for being nowhere anybody can find.

beats.headline: Breaking into a country club
beats.text: Vinata and her guard mean to sit out the rest of the war in a temple inside the club, where nothing can reach them. So Katia, Carl, Prepotente and Samantha break in behind an unbroken line of wire running back to Li Na's clocktower, so her aura works inside, and Li Jun, Bautista and Zhang come in behind them to hold the doors and string the wire.

beats.headline: Kill the Blasphemer
beats.text: A ram at the door of Club Vanquisher, a worshipper of my brother, proposes to give half of my own man's bounty to Hellik, as the superior god to his filthy Emberus. I have been insulted, and I say so. New quest: Kill the Blasphemer. This worshipper of Hellik has insulted me. Kill him. The reward is an additional boon, and the more entertained I am by the manner of it, the better the boon will be. The man looks up into the air and tells me he is one step ahead of me.

beats.headline: A prisoner for a bounty
beats.text: Mork, a lisping ram cleric of Hellik, jabs a shaking finger at Prepotente: there is a Holy Crusade Bounty on him, and he dares enter this club? Carl raises a hand in peace and points to Prepotente's wrists, shackled in fuzzy handcuffs that are not locked. He has captured him and is here to collect the bounty. Prepotente throws himself to the floor with an exaggerated flourish. The handcuffs jingle ominously, and Carl fears they will fly off his wrists. I have been caught! My goose has been cooked!

beats.headline: Holding the doors at Club Vanquisher
beats.text: Katia, Carl, Prepotente and Samantha are going into Club Vanquisher, and they are dragging a wire behind them long enough to extend my sister's auras all the way inside. Somebody has to keep the path open behind them. That is Bautista, Zhang and me. Doors. We are holding doors. It is not glamorous, and it is exactly the job I would have asked for, and I am holding mine.

beats.headline: Closed Off
beats.text: Rend goes into his pet carrier and Bianca is stored, because Mordecai's aura potion does not work on pets. At the door of Club Vanquisher, Carl hands Prepotente one of the yellow, bubbling potions. Mordecai made it, and it lasts an hour; the ones Prepotente had before lasted two minutes. He drinks it manually and finds it similar to a Crodino. Carl drinks his through the menu. You have been Closed Off: no longer susceptible to aura effects, Blessings or Dreads. Everyone in the area, take your aura potions, Carl orders. We're going inside.

beats.headline: Big Red, and a map in my head
beats.text: Carl has not brought Donut. A contingency, he says. I mention, since nobody asked, that I have a map of all of Club Vanquisher. Miriam, Bianca and I befriended a delightful guildmaster inside, and we left through a bathroom stall in the entrance temple. Perfect recall. Then I drink my Big Red, which is from Texas, where cowboys live; I may have five soda pops a day, a hard rule of my mother's. At the door he hands me a smoke grenade and asks about my acting. Soon I am on the floor in fuzzy handcuffs that do not lock. I have been caught! Oh woe!

beats.headline: Leader of Li Na's builders
beats.text: Earlier, at the foot of Li Na's new clocktower in Shanty Town, the subject was seen pointing up and talking animatedly, in his element, directing the last-minute construction. Now dozens of wires dangle from the clocktower's arms, an exploit; if it works, Li Na's builder squad, led by the subject, gets straight to work on a very tall, very powerful, very specialized and very expensive synergy tower at the edge of the hole leading down into Larracos. It only works during the next phase. In the menu, its name is simple. It is called the Nest.

beats.headline: Mork, and the blasphemer's end
beats.text: The ram at the door, Mork, wants to split my bounty on Pony with Hellik, and I tell him we have a deal. When the fight starts and he bolts for the door, I break a potion of Black Nimbus on the back of his head, and he's cut off from his god on his own doorstep. Then Li Na's dread comes down the wire. Mork pulls out his own eyes and puts them back in backward. The trophy heads on the walls start screaming, the rugs move, and he digs into his own chest before he runs out of strength. Quest complete: ten seconds of Emberus laughing, and a Celestial Boon. Heathen Scald on every punch for the rest of the floor.

beats.headline: Temple defense protocols
beats.text: I come through the door as one of the club's four-armed guards, soaked in the cherries and sausage sandwich Carl's broken food box made when he asked it for cobbler. Demons attack the temple behind me, I shout. We must initiate temple defense protocols. That's what Tipid said the procedure is called. The one with his claws stuck in the ceiling asks, temple defense protocols? Fight to the death, I say. Kill all the heathens. Uh, steel and heavy metal. What manner of demon is it? Two of Daniel's stuffed pyxies fly over my shoulders and come alive. That kind.

beats.headline: Did it work?
beats.text: A wire runs from my clock tower into Club Vanquisher, and my aura runs down it. Dark Purpose first. It is not meant to be used like this. It leveled faster than we anticipated, from four to fifteen, and I moved on. White chains are dragging the ghosts into the floor. Carl wants to know what that was, whether I knew, whether they are trapped somewhere. I ask him again. Did it work? Now I am using Defile Soul. Next I will train Bleeding Horror. I am cycling my dreads and leveling them all.

beats.headline: The one open door on the floor
beats.text: The portal to all the temples, and inside one of them, Vinata. Deity summoning is throttled on this floor by the rules of the war, with one exception nobody thought to close: a god may always appear in his own temple. So Khepri is home. Samantha opens the door, Carl and Katia Grim and Prepotente go through it, and an achievement arrives to inform them, with the timing I have come to expect from this place, that they have walked into a trap. Carl's Scavenger's Daughter patch reads the room and hands him ninety seconds of immortality for standing near this particular god.

beats.headline: I need to train
beats.text: Carl wants the first dread back on, and the cat shouts at me to do what he says. I will if I have to. I need to train, and I cannot give up this opportunity. When they extend their claws, they bleed, and that should be enough once the dread trains high enough. It is level five and rising. Carl is marked as an ally; the blood will not hurt him. I suggest the berserker plan. At the portal he warns me his tattoo spell will hurt. I am ready. Blood Horror is level fifteen. I turn on my last dread: Succulent Decay.

beats.headline: An address on the dial
beats.text: Katia asks in chat how to tune the thing, since it is just lights. Prepotente explains, out loud, that the mechanism is quite simple. First turn off automatic mode, or Crawler Carl lands at the Emberus temple, Katia at Eileithyia's, and Prepotente himself at the Epicure. Integers here. But they need the address to dial in, and Carl calls out the numbers Rosetta gives him.

beats.headline: The right one
beats.text: Prepotente explains the portal dial, Carl calls out the numbers Rosetta gives him, and he analyses the door: an Ultima Corp DungeonWerx Municipal, Multi-Destination Doorway-based Subspace Portal. Dial 453! The information changes: two-way, gated by faith, its entrance sequence gated to adherents of the Khepri faith or other entities under the dungeon's ruleset. That's the right one, Carl calls. He holds his breath and asks for the picture. A screenshot appears, and relief floods him.

beats.headline: Dialling 453 for the bug god
beats.text: Katia cannot work the portal dial. It is just lights, she says. This mechanism is quite simple. Turn off automatic mode, or Carl arrives in the temple of Emberus, she in Eileithyia's, and I at the Epicure. Then the integers. Carl calls out 453. Before this I stopped to put some of the sentient blood running along the walls into a jar. At the door I say my litany of names under my breath: Miriam, and Bianca, and several others, ending on Ragazzaccia. I am ready for battle, Carl.

beats.headline: I open the god's door
beats.text: The bug god's door will not open for a heathen. It will open for someone damned, and Mordecai, Tipid and Rosetta are all certain that I count. Carl tells me to get over there, and don't you dare touch the dial, and then he checks with a screenshot that I didn't. I didn't. I hop into his hands and he holds me up to the door like a football. You'll have to use your mouth, he says. I don't even say anything filthy. I just say okay, Carl, and I chomp down on the handle and pull.

beats.headline: The trap has two immortals inside it
beats.text: They come through the portal into Khepri's temple, the crawler and Katia and the goat, with Samantha opening the door for them. Standing this near this god hands a very few of us ninety seconds of immortality, and it does not enquire whose side they are on. His patch gives him his ninety. Being what I am gives me mine.

beats.headline: Temple rules apply
beats.text: The Sultanate's adjutant arrives with a louder crack than usual: Admiral Corinne Whimpleshin, a camel in a sundress, holding a martini, calling foul. The gods. The summoning of the gods. I ask what the foul is. She wishes to stop everything. It does not matter. We have no standing. Temple rules apply, and she knows it; her team summoned the god. She says it was not the Blood Sultanate, that Carl did it and knew this would happen. Carl says he has not summoned anything. The timer ends.

beats.headline: God or not, I'm staying
beats.text: Carl tells us to run the moment we unfreeze, reset the door, hide in our own temples if we have to; he'll cover us. Prepotente says he did not come this far to run. Me neither, Carl. God or not, I'm staying. Donut is shouting in capitals that there aren't supposed to be gods yet. Then, under a thirty-second timer, Carl sends his plan. No. No way, Carl. That's insane, even for you. Prepotente says he would actually be quite curious to see if it works.

beats.headline: The endless temple, and what is at the table
beats.text: Since the crawlers are frozen and I have thirty seconds, the file on this one. Khepri is humanoid apart from the head, where there is instead an entire beetle, wings and legs and a small head of its own. He does not talk. He chitters. His temple is listed as endless, which in practice is a room and a door and one long table carrying a never-ending feast of four hundred and thirty-three kinds of insect.
