Instead the system lists two warlords of the War Mage Rebellion, and only one of them is mine. Agatha. Co-warlord. I did not bring this rebellion this far to share its title, least of all with her, and I have not hidden what I think of that. I will hold the castle. I will not pretend to be pleased.

beats.headline: A comfort in the dream
beats.text: Several days earlier: Carl lands in Katia's dream, not the one from Shi Maria's point of view he was meant to have. No, she says, not this. A bird appears on her shoulder, a bird with the skull of a child, and it rubs its small, ghoulish head against hers in comfort. This is her card from the floor before, and its name is Annie. When Katia tells him how the little girl died with nobody to call her own, she reaches up and strokes the other Annie, the bird. She was like me in that way, she says. All alone.

beats.headline: Two warlords for one rebellion
beats.text: The War Mage Rebellion holds the castle at Larracos, and six hours on the clock decides the floor. I run alongside Carl and give him what I have, which is less than he wants. Agatha has been named co-warlord beside Akuma, much as Ferdinand was added beside Juice Box, and nobody on that team anticipated it. Akuma does not like her. Their motivations are unclear, even to me.

beats.headline: Two meteors
beats.text: Two meteors came out of Larracos across the dark toward the ball. A third light, burning black and purple, intercepted both: struck the first, carried its momentum into the second and knocked it off course. The explosion showed what it was. Subject, injured in the blast, pivoted, fell out of sight and left a streak of purple smoke. The deflected meteor looped and went into the ball anyway. When the ball began to roll toward Larracos, subject rose again from wherever she had fallen and, after bobbing in the air a moment, followed it.

beats.headline: I trust her
beats.text: Victory asks what Donut's plan is. She hasn't told me, and no, I'm not going to question her. I trust her. Then two meteors come out of Larracos at the ball, and a woman is spat out of it: Nami, the pilot of Eris, ejected by a war mage from inside. Samantha reports another mage conscripting Yarilo with a potion. They are recruiting gods. I throw a healing potion onto the ball instead of a bomb, tell Donut to keep it intact and roll it toward the city, and run.

beats.headline: What Imani carries
beats.text: For the file, by the most private route available. Imani gives Chris a quick hug with her wings, not her arms, and he reaches up as if to touch her face and stops just short. When Crawler Carl is bound for a moment to the minds around him, he catches a glimpse of Imani's: she is in love with Chris, and Carl had no idea. She loves his simplicity. His quiet kindness. Clay-ton, his bodyguard since the Hunting Grounds, has become his inseparable friend; the two sit side by side and grunt at one another.

beats.headline: Installing
beats.text: Li Jun is dead. Over the chat Li Na tells Donut not to break the ball apart, and when Donut asks where she is, the answer comes back: she was installing her brother's eye into herself. She has also stopped the mage who was going for Harpocrates, though she is not yet strong enough to stop the god on her own.

beats.headline: A basketball on three legs
beats.text: For the record: a second adjutant appears beside Baroness Victory, a type of alien Crawler Carl has never seen. A round, basketball-like body covered in black dots that may be eyes, standing on three long, multi-jointed legs. A tripod. Tripods are supposedly completely without emotion. Former Prime Minister Fopsy. Adjutant for The Dream. Non-combatant observer. He says nothing and scuttles aside. His arrival makes Crawler Carl realise that the Dream's warlord must be inside the ball of flesh as well.

beats.headline: Five potions for a Gate
beats.text: His first words, when a woman shoots out of the ball, are that the ruleset has nothing for this, and there is nothing to do but observe and report. Then the adjutants talk past Crawler Carl. Bao has not called foul. A spell to do this would need level 19, perhaps 18, and would not work on sponsored gods, which explains the ejection. Victory says potions. The subject checks his menus, every eye twinkling like a disco ball: the war mages traded the Gate of the Feral Gods at the Midnight Market for five of them.

beats.headline: A theory kept back
beats.text: The subject's reading of the war mages' warlord: the residual is not only trying to win Faction Wars and zero out the crawlers, but to end the ascendency game fast. Once it is finished with no crawlers left, a hard-coded shutdown and hibernation follows, an alternative to the failsafe. That makes sense if she believes the local AI is a threat to the Eulogist. How she convinced the war mages, he does not understand. He has additional theories, and declines to voice them in the presence of a combatant.

beats.headline: Traded at the Midnight Market
beats.text: Fopsy, the Dream's adjutant, reads it off his menus while Victory swears beside him. The war mages did not keep the Gate of the Feral Gods. They traded it to a minion at the Midnight Market, in exchange for five hell-kissed conscription potions, level 18, strong enough to take most gods, though not sponsored ones. That explains why Eris's pilot had to be ejected first. Victory's observation is that such things always leak into the market. The Gate, as of now, is somewhere else.

beats.headline: We need that gate back
beats.text: We need to move on the war mages now. They have the Gate. I do not understand why they are not allied with the other NPCs, and I do not understand why that Residual is their warlord. We do not know their plans. Rosetta is ready to let them win and be done with it. I am not done yet. Rosetta, you are the most stubborn person I have ever known. Trust me in this. We need that gate back, and we need to move before the defensive towers spin up.

beats.headline: Annie, in the dream
beats.text: Days ago, in the dream potion, Carl lands in my dream instead of his own, our hands fused together. A children's hospital in Iceland. Fannar, my ex, arrives to tell them the truth, and the woman denies my adoption, and I scream into my fist in a bathroom stall. Then I go to Annie. Brain cancer. She died alone. Nobody told me, until I met a nurse in a park who said she passed a few weeks ago, as if it did not matter. It is my worst memory and my favourite. I love Daniel. I tell Carl I love him and Donut more.

beats.headline: My brother's eye
beats.text: Donut, do not break the ball apart. Donut asks where I am. I was installing my brother's eye into myself. I also stopped the mage who was going for Harpocrates. I am not strong enough yet to stop the god on my own. The deflector towers have paused him, and he will push past them to reach Donut. I suggest you run.

beats.headline: Out of the ball of flesh
beats.text: Something bursts out of the rolling ball of flesh as if from a blowhole: a person, arms waving, rocketing straight up and slamming into the grass. A human woman, off-worlder outline, no army glow. One slender arm rises for help. Baroness Victory does not know what to make of it, and Fopsy finds nothing in the ruleset for it. She crawls toward them, screaming soundlessly, in armor Crawler Carl half recognises. He asks Crawler Donut whether she cast Laundry Day. She did not.

beats.headline: Taken by the fleshers
beats.text: Nami, influencer, is dead. Three fleshers fall off the ball and scuttle to her. The first wraps her legs and climbs her, dissolving her flesh, and her scream rises. Dong Quixote asks whether they should help. Crawler Carl says no: wait until it kills her. Baroness Victory recognises her then. Someone has stripped the goddess's soul armor, ejecting the driver. Crawler Carl works out that a war mage is inside the ball. The flesher stands up wearing her, a dromedarian skin draped over her like a ghost costume, and two more attach. Crawler Carl throws a hob-lobber. It kills her and the fleshers at once.

beats.headline: Hell-kissed versions
beats.text: Two war mages have gone for the gods, and Victory bursts out in disbelief. Fopsy reckons it would take the spell at nineteen, maybe eighteen, and it will not work on sponsored gods. They are using potions, not the spell, says Victory: hell-kissed versions, level 18, likely suicide for a caster too far below the target. Fopsy checks his menus. They traded the Gate of the Feral Gods at the Midnight Market for five of them. Then Samantha reports a war mage tossing one on Yarilo. It worked, and the war mage blew up.

beats.headline: A second atrocity
beats.text: The ball reaches the field of corpses and I cast You're Not Done Yet, tower-enhanced, on all of them at once. The system calls it another Atrocity and me a naughty kitty. Thousands of skins come up and go looking for the Dream and the Reaver soldiers inside the ball. Then I start hitting it with Magic Missile to break it open, and Carl and Li Na both tell me to stop. Our friends are in there, Carl, with fleshers crawling all over them. He wants it kept whole and rolled toward the city. So I set it rolling toward Larracos.

beats.headline: Next in line, if the yacht goes
beats.text: Succession, by Rosetta Thagra's arithmetic. Stalwart is dead, which makes one of his children king, and those children are aboard a yacht Rosetta's side has agreed to destroy in exchange for a pin number. If that is done, the Skull Empire falls to subject, provided she is still alive somewhere on Earth's surface. If she is not, it goes to the Maestro, disowned or not. Rosetta feels ill about the children.

beats.headline: Work after the crawlers
beats.text: In a message to Justice Light, with the war mages holding the Gate, Rosetta lays out what is left. Perhaps the mages winning is not such a bad thing: it will be quick, and the remaining mercenaries and leaders will be dead. Justice Light says he is not done yet. If all the crawlers die, she answers, the Ascendency starts at once, and Rectrix gets to work. Perhaps, after all this, York and Rectrix survive. A longer crawl risks the AI growing stronger.

beats.headline: The job is done
beats.text: Victory tells me the money arrived, enough for two ships. If York does his duty and shoots down that yacht, our part is finished. There are children on that yacht, orc children, and one of them is king now that Stalwart is dead. I think about Brooks, whom Rust pulled through the glass and cut in half, and about the whip. Does revenge bring anyone back? Justice Light says we need the gate. I trust Porthus. I do not trust the Apothecary, and I trust Agatha less. Comrades, sound off. We fight.

beats.headline: I didn't kill him
beats.text: Their dreams are colliding, and I come into this one, the man and the woman watching a memory of her with a baby. I push through the memory and put my face right up to his. I didn't kill him. I didn't kill him. I did not, I did not, I did not. My eye is open and shining and it does nothing to him. And then a new voice speaks behind me: bitch, you swallowed me whole.

beats.headline: Finishing means a shutdown
beats.text: Fopsy, the adjutant, sets out what finishing the game triggers. Once the Ascendency is considered finished with no crawlers left, the system's shutdown and hibernation sequence starts automatically: a hard-coded limit that allows elemental reclamation before the AI is woken again. With the AI spreading, that is an alternative to the fail-safe. Which is why, Fopsy suspects, the residual running the war mage team wants the crawlers zeroed and the Ascendency over as fast as possible.

beats.headline: Worshipped by the Nebulars
beats.text: Rosetta turns over what Porthus told her when she asked about the Apothecary's motives: he could not say, because if she knew and entered the dungeon, the local AI might learn, and then, in time, the Eulogist would know. Isn't the Eulogist dead, she had asked. Now she places Agatha as the rarer kind of residual, more in line with the Nebulars, who worship the Eulogist, and therefore the enemy of the Apothecary. Fopsy, the adjutant, adds a theory: the residual wants the crawl ended fast because she now believes the local AI is a threat to the Eulogist.

beats.headline: They conscript gods
beats.text: Hold the castle at Larracos for six hours and the floor is theirs. They trade the gate away at the Midnight Market for five Hell-Kissed Potions of Conscription and put Yarilo on the field beside them. The system hands the rebellion two co-warlords, and the two of them cannot stand each other.

beats.headline: Two co-warlords, and a god on a leash
beats.text: They hold the Larracos castle, and six hours of holding it would take the floor. Baroness Victory reads out two co-warlords, Akuma and Agatha, and Akuma is not pleased about it. The Gate goes onto the Midnight Market and comes back as potions, and the potions conscript Yarilo. Fopsy, adjutant for the Dream, has a theory: that Agatha now thinks the AI is a danger to the Eulogist and wants the ascendency game over so it can be shut down.

beats.headline: Conscripted with potions
beats.text: The War Mage Rebellion has taken the Larracos castle and holds it for six hours to win, and they have gone shopping for reinforcements. They conscript Yarilo, paid for with potions they traded for the gate on the Midnight Market. Somewhere in that chain a god of lust became a line item. Fopsy has a theory about why Agatha is doing any of this, and I will let her explain it, because I have a god to move.

beats.headline: The yacht, if he does his duty
beats.text: Filed from Rosetta's side of the deal. In exchange for a pin number, the Pacifist Network agreed to destroy an orc yacht with several children aboard, and with Stalwart dead, one of those children is the new king of the Skull Empire. The job falls to York, in orbit. Rosetta's assessment: assuming he actually does his duty and does not decide to write a poem instead. She also names York among those she hopes survive whatever comes next.

beats.headline: The stupid ghoulie suit
beats.text: A god is here, and Carl tells Donut to get out of the Nest tower. She can see that, she answers: he has stopped at the edge of the city, and he cannot see her anyway, because she is wearing the stupid ghoulie suit and is invisible. Carl points out that she is on top of the biggest tower on the floor, shooting magic missiles. Rosetta agrees with him. A magic missile arcs down from the tower into a crowd of ghouls.

beats.headline: Where is my husband
beats.text: Carl comes running across the courtyard shouting about generators and railings and waffle makers. I turn human and grab his shoulder. Where is Louis? Where is my husband? He is not answering me. Carl says he is alive but in trouble, and someone is trying to rescue him, and it is Samantha. So I tell Samantha. I have a form that is a fleshmancer. Bring my husband back in one piece and she can have any body she wants. I know who she really is.

beats.headline: Anne of Green Gables
beats.text: Ruby's in my lap with her head on my shoulder and I'm reading her Anne of Green Gables. The bot's listening too. Carl bursts in with the shark, the meatball, a slug and two crying women from some other party, and stops, and looks at us like he wants to say something. He doesn't. He dials the Larracos gate on the door, and they go.

beats.headline: A hall pass night
beats.text: The Reaver castle is empty except for the robot doggies, who are everywhere, and the hallways are super small and complicated, and I am looking. Then Juice Box says she has a fleshmancer form and I can have any body I desire if I bring her husband back in one piece. Throw in a hall pass night with Louis and you have a deal. She says she knows who I really am and I've lost my mind. Okay, it's a deal. But if Louis's passions get the best of him, I won't make any apologies.

beats.headline: Holding the college gate
beats.text: At the college gate, a line of Semeru dwarves in ornate parade armour holds back a surge of shadowy zarogoths. An orange ray from one of the mobs drops a dwarf onto his back, and the mob laughs. Another Semeru slashes its bulbous stomach open; it deflates in a gush of black liquid, dead, and the fallen dwarf writhes in the oil. A magic missile from Donut's tower lands among the ghouls, and the dwarves press the attack.

beats.headline: Dialled to Larracos
beats.text: With minutes to spare, the last of the group files into the saferoom behind Carl, and he quickly dials the Larracos gate on the doggie door. Dong Quixote is riding Gonk, and rather than the pet stables Carl orders him to Shanty Town, which has an exit fit for a swamp yak. The door beeps, ready. Rend goes first; the stairs are steep.

beats.headline: A woman with a dog
beats.text: The last messages from the Nest's lower floor, where the subject stands guard over Crawler Donut with Bomo and several mages. Bomo: someone is trying to come into the tower. Toyotomi: he is securing the front entrance. Donut: she cannot leave the tower; there is a net around it. Carl asks if it is one of the zarogoth things. No, the subject answers. It is a crawler. A woman with a dog. She's coming in. System note on that message: This message is from a deceased mercenary.

beats.headline: Cleaved in half at the door
beats.text: Final service entry. Bomo was guarding the base of the Nest tower with Toyotomi and a detachment of mages when a crawler with a dog came in. Toyotomi reported it. Bomo reported that he would stop her. Both reports came back marked from the deceased. All of them were cleaved in half with a spell. Bomo will supposedly regenerate on the tenth floor. The clients no longer hold his contract. Crawler Carl does not know if he will see him again.

beats.headline: Shit Just Hit
beats.text: Toyotomi and Bomo go quiet, and I don't think. I drink my last Levitation potion at the railing and go straight up. The plan was to aim carefully at the Piccadilly. Instead I drop an entire inventory folder called Shit Just Hit: about twenty Waffle Makers, two No Disassembles, a pair of cheese cutters, some five hundred hob-lobbers and more dynamite than I can count. My Walk on Air runs out three quarters of the way to the lip, and I drop. The generator goes, and so does every window in the area, and the city's defence system wakes up. One tower locks onto me.

beats.headline: A face of blood
beats.text: Someone rushes into the tower behind Carl: Li Na. He had heard her say she was installing Li Jun's fake eye into herself, but the meaning hits him only now. The front of her demonic face is covered in blood. She has gouged out her own eye and replaced it with her brother's celestial-quality one, which lets her slow down time and move with incredible speed. When Carl starts to say he is sorry about her brother, she holds up a hand and stops him.

beats.headline: Kitten is in trouble
beats.text: Crawler Carl dived into a ditch in Shanty Town to get out of a defence tower's line of fire. Subject jumped in beside him, shaking, tail scorched from a near miss, bowler hat askew, and asked why he was lying down on the job, because Kitten is in trouble. Carl told him that going into the tower would get him killed and that Juice Box needs him alive. Subject reported that Juice Box hates him and is meaner than Bill. Carl told him that he, and Donut, want him alive too.

beats.headline: The Shit Just Hit folder
beats.text: No time to aim. Carl levitates up out of the funnel of Larracos and, instead of placing the big waffle-maker bombs on the theatre housing the zarogoth generator, drops the entire contents of one inventory folder, labelled Shit Just Hit, in the general direction of the Piccadilly. About twenty waffle makers, two no disassembles, a pair of cheese cutters, more dynamite sticks than he can count, and approximately five hundred impact hob-lobbers, all at once. His Walk on Air runs out three-quarters of the way to safety.

beats.headline: Brewed in the Nothing
beats.text: File note on the Hell-Kissed Potion of Conscription, level 18, of which Crawler Carl now holds a duplicated copy: it will work against pretty much any unaffiliated entity, most deities included. Most. It was brewed in the dark recesses of the Nothing by Krakaren Prime, who is said to yearn for domination and was banished there for it, and who prepares for a war she considers inevitable. The in-dungeon version of Krakaren supplied these potions to the War Mages. The irony is noted.

beats.headline: The last one
beats.text: The final messages from Toyotomi and Bomo come in, and Carl does not think. He runs past Juice Box and the Semeru dwarves, punches a zarogoth out of the way at the railing, and drinks the final Levitation potion in his inventory as dozens of arms reach for him. He shoots straight up, pushing it to the limit, and its apex carries him up and out of Larracos, still a good hundred metres short of the edge of Shanty Town. Instead of aiming, he drops an entire inventory folder of bombs toward the Piccadilly.

beats.headline: Take it
beats.text: The front of my face is blood. I have gouged out my own eye and put my brother's in its place. Carl starts to say he is sorry. I stop him. I give him the potion he asked me to take off the dead war mage, or a copy of it: I used Jun's scroll of potion duplication. The original is for Harpocrates. Then I will save Zhang, Elle, Katia and the others before they too fall victim to your chaos. He says it could kill me. I go.

beats.headline: I don't want to play anymore
beats.text: I come up the tower for the dinosaur. That is justice. The cat throws barrels at Gus and he keeps sliding away from me, and I tell him to get back up. Then something hits me, and I tumble down the ramp with a crab, into the man. The crab holds me up in his claws and shouts at me to kowtow. I say please. I say I don't want to play anymore. The man breaks a bottle on my head, and it screams.

beats.headline: Screaming glass
beats.text: A chain from Li Na's shoulder drops a potion in front of Carl, the one he asked her to loot from the war mage who flew at Harpocrates. The large, warm bottle is an eyeless demonic head with many tentacles, which wave though they are glass, and when he grabs it, every mouth screams. Hell-Kissed Potion of Conscription, level 18. She used Jun's scroll of potion duplication; the original she will use on Harpocrates herself. If the level gap is too high, it is dangerous, Carl calls after her. She does not wait.

beats.headline: Never like this
beats.text: In the tower's stairwell, Raul holds Lucia Mar up in his claws, and she does not fight back. Please, she begs: she doesn't want to play anymore. Raul snaps again, and her shield winks out. A regular one might work, but Carl needs to be sure. He pulls out the potion Li Na has just duplicated for him. No. Not like this. Never like this. Sometimes we do what we have to do to survive. He smashes the screaming, hell-kissed Conscription potion against Lucia's head.

beats.headline: Donkey Kong
beats.text: Lucia is in the tower, coming up the stairs, shouting for Mongo, and Bomo and the others are dead. I cannot leave; there is a net. I tell Carl to get the war mages, because the castle is more important than me. He says he is coming and to do Donkey Kong. So I hit the switch, and the stairs turn into a ramp, and I roll barrels. The sleep barrel does not work. She crawls on the ceiling and blocks explosions. Mute does not work on her. I have a better idea. I summon Raul.

beats.headline: Mythic, and furious about it
beats.text: Crawler Carl and Lucia Mar go tumbling together, caked in oil, and Crawler Donut finally summons Raul. The level-up at the end of the previous floor took him from 70 to 110, his card is now mythic, and a summoning lasts ten minutes. His voice is deeper. He tears into Lucia's shield, asks how she dares challenge Daddy Carl, and for crimes against the heavens sentences her to eternal death. Please, Lucia says. Wait, says Carl.

beats.headline: Toyotomi was dead-dead
beats.text: Crawler Carl reaches the Nest and spares a quick, sad glance for the subject, Bomo and the defending mages, all of them cleaved in half with a spell. Bomo is supposed to regenerate on the tenth floor. Toyotomi is not. Toyotomi was dead-dead. Up the curving stairwell, Lucia Mar is shouting at her dog.

beats.headline: Shit Just Hit
beats.text: Carl's plan was to aim the massive-payload waffle makers at the theater housing the generator for the zarogoths. Instead, levitating up out of Larracos, he drops the entire contents of one inventory folder, titled Shit Just Hit, toward the Piccadilly: about twenty waffle makers, two no disassembles, a pair of anti-personnel cheese cutters, about five hundred impact hob-lobbers and more dynamite than he can count. His Walk on Air gives out three-quarters of the way to the edge. When the bombs hit, every window in the area shatters.

beats.headline: Scars we rarely choose
beats.text: The potion takes. Under Orders; she drops the frightened act, and I order her protections off. Two hundred player killer skulls. Twenty hunters. Her own game guide. I tell her I don't have one, and that with scars we rarely get to choose. I put on the Ring of Divine Suffering. Florin thinks there are kids trapped in that head. Maybe. The conscription ends with the floor and she keeps coming for the people I love. So I apologise for what I'm about to do. Then her voice changes, and I stop.

beats.headline: Conscripted
beats.text: Crawler Li Na conscripts Harpocrates. A god of silence, level 250, invulnerable on this floor, is now on a crawler's side of the board because a crawler had the paperwork to put him there. Two chapters of him rampaging across the territory, and the resolution is administrative. I would like it noted that I find this floor exhausting.

beats.headline: My name is Diah
beats.text: Sir. My name is Diah. Lucia is with Alexandro, and Alexandro is only here when the dogs are close. Wait until the dog is close, and Lucia will be back. Please, sir. We are in the dark, and it is so cold. Sometimes we hear them whispering. It's like a river runs through our room, and if we touch it, it hurts. When the dog wanders off, Lucia fades, and one of us takes over, and we can see again. We take turns. Sometimes it is day.

beats.headline: Another ally for the Eulogist
beats.text: The dog is dead, and I am on my knees, crying, pouring a pet potion on the dinosaur, whose throat is open. You did it, I tell him. Then I stand up. A blast from the tower goes past my head and I don't flinch. I tell the man he should have killed us both when there was still a connection. Now it's too late. Now the Eulogist has another ally in the dungeon, and he can't kill me. Not unless he wants all the children of Earth to die. I walk off.

beats.headline: Dog is BAD
beats.text: MOTHER says NO. Mongo goes down slide. Dog. Dog is BAD. Bite dog. Dog is spikes. Spikes in mouth. HURTS. Dark. Girl pours drink on Mongo. Mongo not dead.

beats.headline: Under orders
beats.text: The potion works, and a pink glow appears around Lucia's dot. Ordered to cancel any spell meant to hurt them, her terrified face switches to malice: she was faking. Her protections drop on command, and however hard she lunges, she cannot attack him. Then a warlord message: Harpocrates, level 250, has been successfully conscripted into the Princess Posse. Li Na is alive and at full health. She found a way to use the potion without hurting herself.

beats.headline: Die, demon, die
beats.text: Daddy Carl is magnanimous today, Raul informs Lucia, who should now kiss his famed alabaster feet; then Carl sends him up the ramp to help Donut. Soon after, he comes back out of the tower in a heap with Carl, three Mongos and Gustavo the rottweiler, his shell sizzling from lightning and his health almost gone. He lunges to snap off the dog's head, shouting die, demon, die. The lightning takes him in the centre of the chest, and he disappears in a puff of smoke.

beats.headline: Wrecking Ball
beats.text: Carl cast Hi-Yo Silver a second time and called Wrecking Ball. Subject, much bigger than when last seen, came over the ridge and rolled toward him at speed, with Gustavo 3 and Mongo directly between them. The dog had the unconscious dinosaur by the neck. The back half of Gustavo 3, the second of Lucia Mar's two rottweilers, left in a red mist. Subject stopped inches from Carl's face. Carl called him a good boy. A defence tower's bolt then hit subject squarely. He barely moved. He giggled.

beats.headline: Another ally in the dungeon
beats.text: Mongo lies with his throat torn open, and Lucia Mar kneels over him, sobbing, pouring a pet healing potion. Then her posture changes, and she stands to her full height. A gale-tower blast misses her head by inches and she does not flinch. You should have killed us both when there was still a connection, she tells Crawler Carl. Now the Eulogist has another ally in the dungeon, and now Carl cannot kill her. Not unless he wants all the children of Earth to die. She walks off.

beats.headline: What sort of monster am I
beats.text: Florin's old dictionary, the one with the bullet hole, defines atrocity as an act of fiendish cruelty. The system calls Donut's War Crime spell an Atrocity, and maybe the real cruelty was giving it to her at all, out of the Legendary box we got for killing D'Nadia. I've never before prayed for my own plan to fail while needing it to work. If she doesn't cast it, we likely don't survive the coming hours. If she does, what then? She says she's ready. If I let her, what sort of monster am I?

beats.headline: She looks like a sniper
beats.text: Carl rushes into the top level of the Nest to find Donut atop her seat, dressed in her ghillie suit, leaning against the parapet with her face pressed to the invisible shield. The camouflage is a strange contrast to her tiara, which glows like a lighthouse beacon. She has no weapon, and his first thought is sniper. Aiming, aiming, she mutters, and a fiery magic missile drops a distant tower in Larracos. Not so tough with your head blown off, she growls.

beats.headline: A tattoo for the cat
beats.text: Rosetta, Milk and Edgar come up into the tower to work on Princess Donut. She is getting a tattoo, and given who does the ink around here, a tattoo is not decoration. It is a thing that will get up off her and fight when she calls it.

beats.headline: Get fucked, Prime Minister
beats.text: He teleports into the Nest Tower without Crawler Carl hearing a thing, and his presence reminds Crawler Carl that two warlords, Tagg and Fang, are still unaccounted for. Rosetta arrives out of breath with Edgar the tortoise strapped to her back and does a double take at him. Former prime minister, she says, and grins. Get fucked. But she is glad he is here to witness this.

beats.headline: The count
beats.text: Zev puts a number on it: about 120,000 children, give or take. Their bodies are in the kinder facility on the surface; the rest of them is bound up in her head, and if she goes, they may all go.

beats.headline: Level seventy-four
beats.text: I am in my ghillie suit at the parapet, sniping. The war mage atop that death ray tower is not so tough with his head blown off. Carl says to focus on the towers hitting the Nest, and then he holds out his arms, and I blink and jump into them and go round his neck like I used to when he came home from work. I went up this tower at level 65. I am 74 now. My Magic Missile is level fifteen, and it tripled in power. And Rend saved my boy.

beats.headline: Get fucked, Prime Minister
beats.text: I run all the way up the Nest with Milk behind me and Edgar strapped to my back, which, comrade, is significantly heavier than he looks. I would not have come into the dungeon if I had known how much running there would be. Next time we build a tower this high, we add an elevator. Fopsy is in the corner, observing. Former prime minister. Get fucked. But I am glad he is here to witness this. Donut needs a spell she does not have, at level eight, to go with War Crime.

beats.headline: Trampled by two gods
beats.text: The fight between the gods passes through the other side of Shanty Town, and then it is simply gone. Most of the defensive towers the Posse paid for, and never really got to use, are trampled. The Nest tower and Li Na's abandoned synergy towers still stand, drawing a lot of fire. Every other building is flattened.

beats.headline: Another name for the center system
beats.text: Crawler Carl adds up where he has heard the word: in connection with the Nebular cult, as Agatha's boss or something, from Paulie, who plainly hated it, from Fopsy, and now from Lucia Mar. He asks Zev. The Eulogist is another name for the AI in the center system, Zev says, and nobody knows for certain how it is connected. Five minutes ago they thought the glitch would self-correct; now they think that if Lucia goes, the children go with her. About 120,000 of them. Give or take a few.

beats.headline: An act of fiendish cruelty
beats.text: In a note to the Cookbook, Carl writes that he used an old dictionary in the guildhall to look up Atrocity: an act of fiendish cruelty. Perhaps the definition is right and the system is wrong to call Donut's War Crime spell one; or perhaps the true act of fiendish cruelty was giving her the spell at all. It came in the Legendary 1914 box they received after killing D'Nadia, the same box as his Run, Little Günter, Run. For the first time he prays a plan of his own will not succeed.

beats.headline: Agatha walks off her post
beats.text: The system deems Warlord Agatha to have abandoned her post, and nobody, the adjutants included, can say why. She is removed, and Akuma is named sole warlord of the rebellion.

beats.headline: Taken off the board by another god
beats.text: Feral God Yarilo has been removed from this floor by Harpocrates, acting under the direction of Crawler Li Na. He came through a gate, chased an AI the length of a warzone, changed sides for a crate of potions, and finished at the hands of the god who had come through that same gate ahead of him. Everything down here becomes somebody's equipment, the gods included.

beats.headline: I should not be telling you
beats.text: Okay, so. The liaisons want to interview Lucia now the dog is dead, for at least an hour. We assumed her getting in was a glitch, and we wanted to kick her back out. Now the AI says it cannot extract her. It is not all the children, Carl. Just the ones who tried to get into the dungeon, and only the ones in one wing, on the surface in the kinder facility. We think if she goes, they all go. I should not be telling you any of this. About a hundred and twenty thousand.

beats.headline: The long description of War Crime
beats.text: Rosetta changes the plan at the top of the Nest. Bijanbi, a Dinner Bell variant from a cleric who fell defending the FUPA, and Wall of Fire, both through Donut's War Crime; the fleshers already wrapped round the enemy are the finisher. Oh. Oh hell. I have the spell's long description in my scratch pad. Health to one percent. Only on the Scolopendra levels, three casts, ever, and it can't kill anyone directly. The last part, which only I seem to see, is two hundred mercenaries paralysed and on fire for two weeks. I agree with Rosetta anyway.

beats.headline: Lifted for a tattoo
beats.text: Edgar has to tattoo Donut, quickly, and the best place is her right flank, over a patch about as big as his foot. Someone lift her camouflage suit and crupper for me, he says. Donut agrees only if Carl gets a matching one, and then the ghillie suit disappears, and the crupper. She turns her tail to Rosetta and refuses Carl's idea of a tramp stamp. Rosetta goes to work with scissors and then a razor, while Donut asks Edgar whether it could be a flower.

beats.headline: It has to be a tattoo
beats.text: It has to be a tattoo, Rosetta says, and Milk will etch words of power over it to raise the spell's level. Hamzo would not reach wide enough, so they chose a Dinner Bell variant from a cleric who fell defending the FUPA, which Edgar has extracted; it used to be called Heel, and this season it is Bijanbi. Donut never agreed to a tattoo. She will do it only if Carl gets a matching one. Rosetta shaves a small, round bald patch on her right flank, and Edgar, the poker in his mouth, says what he is drawing: a dog.

beats.headline: Lifted for the needle
beats.text: Donut never agreed to a tattoo, she protests, but Edgar asks for someone to lift her camouflage suit and crupper: he needs a spot on her right flank about as big as his foot. Donut fears a scar on the outside, then agrees on condition that Carl gets a matching one. Once she agrees, the ghillie suit disappears, then the crupper, and she turns her tail toward Rosetta.

beats.headline: Not in his castle
beats.text: By the time the Nest tower is stabilised, it is clear Warlord Fang is not in the Reaver castle. The castle is abandoned except for its security system, which is a bunch of robots, and a gravity-magic dragon circling overhead. Crawler Carl casts Ping and finds both remaining Bloc warlords, Epitome Tagg and Warlord Fang, inside the rolling ball of bodies. Rosetta is blunt about it: Fang especially is difficult to locate, worse than a changeling.

beats.headline: A tattoo on the right flank
beats.text: Rosetta says it has to be a tattoo, with Milk etching words of power over it, and Edgar wants a spot on my backside shaved as big as his foot. I never agreed to a tattoo! Carl says I don't have to, and nobody will fault me. I tell him about the scars. I hoped none of them would be on the outside. He says if I choose it, it is a badge of honour. Fine. Only if he gets a matching one. And not a tramp stamp. Then I ask Edgar what he is drawing. A dog.

beats.headline: No longer needed
beats.text: Rosetta's new plan for Donut needs a tattoo. Edgar extracted the spell properly, she says, and with some ink tips from Milk they no longer need the toraline. Edgar explains as he prepares the ink: the ink Carl had from the toraline lets one borrow spells and skills temporarily from willing subjects, and take them permanently from unwilling ones. His new ink is similar but not identical. It captures the essence of the fallen crawler in a unique way, and he does not know how it will form.

beats.headline: Two spells and a finisher
beats.text: Rosetta changes the plan: Bijanbi, a Dinner Bell variant from a cleric who fell defending the FUPA, and Wall of Fire, both amplified by War Crime, to drag the enemies out and drop them into a ring of fire, with the fleshers as the finisher, because War Crime keeps its victims alive. Carl has the spell's extra-long description in his scratch pad. It starts at level 5, combines two spells in a creative way, can be cast once a floor and only on the Scolopendra levels, knocks the caster to 1% health, and cannot kill anyone directly. They will want to die. They won't.

beats.headline: Something else from Milk
beats.text: Milk has told Carl about the book she once wrote her recipes in, and how all she wrote after she changed inks faded and disappeared. She hands him a wineskin of Stayfast Ink, and then something else: a fountain pen. Adept's fountain pen, the most basic of all the calligrapher's implements, and by the System's reckoning the most versatile item anyone can own. Carl has a recipe book, says Donut, with goblin and chicken recipes. I heard, says Milk. He also has another book, one they all have: the Book of Voodoo. Anything he writes in it will be given to everybody who already has it.

beats.headline: Classic Lucia Mar
beats.text: The net holding Carl and Princess Donut in the tower is not new. I suspect it is from before. This is classic Lucia Mar. Fopsy's reading is the sound one: a personal net from a scroll, and a secondary spell behind it, waiting for a power source. It is Power Siphon, drawing on the jewels in the active towers of Larracos, and it ends when those towers stop firing or when she turns it off. She did turn off every active spell she had, Carl. This one activated after she left.

beats.headline: Waiting on top of the Nest
beats.text: On top of the Nest, Donut tells me Li Na said Li Jun's death was her fault. She says Li Na isn't wrong. Lucia killed Bomo. If something goes wrong and we lose everybody, it's on her. I tell her they put us here; this is their war. Then she says she and Katia have a plan, that Bautista can't know, and that Katia told her not to tell me because I'll Carl it up. The rest she sends by message: she got a benefactor box when I wasn't looking. Then Li Na says go.

beats.headline: Two very rude achievements
beats.text: Donut does not look at the tattoo on her flank. She stares forward with quiet dignity while Edgar works, and then he drops his tattoo stick and asks if it worked. Why are you asking me, she cries. She has two very rude achievements, one calling her a traitor, one paying out a stolen catalytic converter. And the spell, Bijanbi, only level two, came from a god called Wepwawet in the Court of Nekhebit; she may worship him now, and Odette too. Cover it up, she says; they will get it lasered off on the next floor.

beats.headline: Words of power
beats.text: Not quite yet, says Milk: it must be temporarily above level eight. Her pen writes over the tattoo in a script the system calls Words of Power, first in black ink and then purple, a calligraphy-guild magic. The letters glow and move, and under them Carl sees the shape: a simple, rather adorable line drawing of a dog. It lifts its leg and starts to lick itself. Edgar doubts it is sentient. Donut gasps: the spell is level fifteen. Temporary, Milk says; it fades with the ink, but it helps the training.

beats.headline: Quite clever, says the tripod
beats.text: A second net is holding Crawler Carl and Crawler Donut inside the Nest Tower, and the two adjutants diagnose it while watching. Victory calls it classic Lucia Mar. The subject agrees: her first net was a personal one from a scroll, and she likely cast a second in case of a countermeasure, which sat waiting for a power source. Victory names it Power Siphon, drawing on the tower jewels in Larracos. Quite clever, says the subject. Crawler Carl, who has already ordered Lucia to turn it all off, is less impressed.

beats.headline: Stayfast ink, and a pen
beats.text: Milk tells Carl she once wrote her recipes in a book, then switched to a different ink to share them with a wider group, and everything written after the switch faded away. Some of her best recipes were gone when they were needed most, and she calls that her fault. Rosetta grunts. Then Milk hands him Stayfast Ink, 825 ml, which nothing will ever make fade, and an Adept's fountain pen, and reminds them that anything Carl writes in the Book of Voodoo goes to everybody who already has it. Then she jumps from the tower and glides away.

beats.headline: A dog that licks itself
beats.text: It's done, and I have received two very rude achievements, one calling me a traitor. But I did get the spell, at level two. It came from a god called Wepwawet, in the Court of Nekhebit, and I can worship Odette now too! Cover it up. It is getting lasered off on the next floor. Not yet, says Milk, and writes words of power over it, which stings. Apparently the dog underneath lifts its leg and starts licking itself. I am not looking. The spell has gone up to level fifteen.

beats.headline: Ink that does not fade
beats.text: After Donut's dog tattoo, Milk tells Carl there are more magic systems than he can imagine, dozens with ink and calligraphy and maps alone, and that inks and letters that shine the brightest burn out the fastest. She had a book once and wrote her recipes in it, then switched to a different ink to share them more widely, and only recently learned that all she wrote after the change faded and disappeared. She hands him a wineskin: Stayfast Ink, 825 ml. Then a fountain pen, the adept's, the most basic of a calligrapher's implements. He has another book, she adds, the Book of Voodoo, and anything he writes in it reaches everyone who has it.

beats.headline: Anything but fire
beats.text: The Nest is at 8% health, and a net Lucia Mar left behind keeps Donut from leaving the tower. Carl wants to abort, but Li Na says it is a little late for that: the ball is about to break. Donut, don't cast War Crime, Carl shouts, but she has to cast the moment it breaks, or everyone will be mixed in together, the gods included. If she does not cast it, Donut says, all of this will be for nothing. Cast it, Carl tells her, but don't pick fire; the Nest has to stay intact. Anything but fire. The ball has broken, Li Na says. Cast now!

beats.headline: The paw over Larracos
beats.text: Donut has been named Champion, her health draining, frozen, and Carl cannot tell what the second spell she picked for War Crime was. Then he sees it, hovering above the hole of Larracos: the massive, glowing outline of a cat's paw. The frozen soldiers and the god Meatus float slowly up out of the hole as music blasts across the world, and the claw grows big enough to catch thousands. They wake and scream, bunched against its underside, swarmed by fleshers that dissolve them. When Li Na's chains spread for the finisher, Donut stretches her arm over empty air. I shouldn't have picked Astral Paw. I have to do it myself.

beats.headline: Free, and full of news
beats.text: Carl's spinner lands on the Pied Piper, and the world is still frozen when I put my hand on his shoulder, at his own height. I am free. My sponsor is gone, my pilot is dead, and it is delicious. I bite his ear. Donut has just been named champion, and I can make him one too; he only has to kill three gods, grumpy Emberus among them. I snap his pinkie, to help with the curse from Meatus. Then the news: the War Mages traded the Gate of the Feral Gods to a merchant named Paca, who keeps it in her stomach. And Britney is possessed.

beats.headline: A Pied Piper benefit, made permanent
beats.text: Crawler Carl picked up a Pied Piper benefit off Harpocrates, the way a crawler picks up a temporary thing off any deity who wanders too close. Eris makes it permanent. She also tells him where the gate is, that Britney has picked an axe up off the ground and is now possessed, and, without explanation, that he is married. One of those three items is the reason he stops listening to the other two.

beats.headline: Misfire, then up
beats.text: Everything unfreezes after the goddess's visit, and beside Carl, Donut has gone rigid, unable to move, her health draining slowly, her title changed from Warlord to Champion. He tries to apply a healing scroll at once, but it misfires, and he has to wait. Outside, the ball has broken apart and thousands of bodies are flying up toward them. When Donut coughs, he slams on the healing scroll, and her health starts to rocket up.

beats.headline: All I can build
beats.text: The cat's paw hangs over Shanty Town, full of them. My chains go out from the tower. Dozens. Onto the wreckage around me, onto the Nest. A lattice. I tell the cat it is all I can build. Do it. She brings the paw down through it. The paw passes. They do not, until they do. Chains break. I grow more. She brings it down again. And again. Until the screaming stops.

beats.headline: A champion, three atrocities in
beats.text: Crawler Princess Donut commits her third Atrocity and the system pays out: the Oak Fell class, and the title Champion of Nekhebit. Consider the shape of that. The class is named for felling the oak. The title belongs to the goddess the oak displaced. Somewhere above this floor an old grudge has just been handed a very small, very loud instrument.

beats.headline: Three baps, and again
beats.text: Carl says anything but fire, so it is Bijanbi and Astral Paw. The messages call me the Oak Fell, and a champion, and then I can't move and my health is draining. Outside, the paw hangs over the hole with thousands of soldiers and a god floating up under it. Carl gets the healing scroll on me. I shouldn't have picked Astral Paw. I have to do it myself. I can feel them under my paw. Li Na builds a lattice of chains and says it is all she can build. I close my eyes and swipe down. Three quick baps. Then again, until the screaming stops.

beats.headline: The Oak Fell
beats.text: Casting now, Donut shouts. She has committed a third Atrocity, received a new class, and will be called The Oak Fell, Champion of Nekhebit. Her two spells are Bijanbi and Astral Paw. Out of the broken ball, thousands of soldiers and the god Meatus float up in slow motion and bunch beneath an enormous glowing cat's paw while fleshers dissolve them. Li Na builds a lattice of chains below. Trembling in Carl's arms, Donut swipes downward, and the paw slams them through the chains, again and again, dozens of times.

beats.headline: A goddamn hero
beats.text: For chrissakes. We were only out of it for about an hour. In that Witness spell, all piled up, we were paralysed and felt everything; the moment Donut cast Battle Formation, it was lights out. Now she's apologising to everyone. My throat feels like I gargled sandpaper and I smell like that god's schlong, and that's it. We lost people from the towers when we woke. Some got burned by fleshers. Several lost limbs. She pulled through for all of us anyway, in a way nobody else could. Not even Carl. She's a goddamn hero.

beats.headline: Marked, and gone
beats.text: After Crawler Donut's spell breaks the ball, Warlord Fang is not among the dead. Crawler Carl is fairly sure Li Na marked both Tagg and Fang with the Ring of Divine Suffering, and neither has died, which means she cannot heal until they are. Britney reports Li Na tearing through the castle, glowing and silent, and the war mages gone through a portal. Carl guesses Li Na is hunting Tagg and Fang.

beats.headline: Three hundred, across the board
beats.text: The System announces my strength at three hundred. Then my intelligence. Then all of them, charisma included, and says it has no plan for this. Level eighty-seven. I marked every enemy in the ball before the paw came down. Several did not die. Both warlords among them. I go through the castle. The war mages open a portal and are gone. Carl asks how many got away. Several, I tell him, including both warlords. There are unaffiliated outworlders here too. Where did they come from?

beats.headline: Chopped, and nobody watches
beats.text: Crawler Princess Donut casts her War Crime spell and Meatus comes apart into pieces. I closed the eye of the Scavenger's Daughter for that one, on the grounds that even she does not want to look at it, and I stand by the decision. Harpocrates swears revenge for him and leaves the realm. Two gods came through that gate. Neither of them is on this floor now.

beats.headline: Deity spells
beats.text: By his left tit, Donut. By his left tit. Those spells you just got are deity spells. I think you're now the most powerful crawler in the history of this game. You've got choices to make, too, because your strength and intelligence are both over a hundred, and the notification probably won't go away until you pick. She picks Muscle Mommy. Are you sure about that one? Too late, she says. Yeah. I think the Bopcas will be worshipping you again, kid. Your charm and Love Vampire skills are stronger than most gods'.

beats.headline: Level one hundred and thirty-five
beats.text: I sit up and compose myself. I still have my Former Child Actor benefits, with the Oak Fell class and the champion title on top. I don't have to worship Nekhebit, only nobody outside her court. For strength I pick Muscle Mommy, so Mongo gets a quarter of mine. Brain Trust for intelligence. Wholesale Discount, for my charisma topping two hundred. Level one hundred and thirty-five! I am once again the strongest crawler in the dungeon. Mongo stays caged. If he eats any of that Meatus, I could never look at him the same again.

beats.headline: Every mark, and two missing
beats.text: The ring is why Carl cannot mark anyone in the ball: no simultaneous marks are allowed on this floor, and Li Na has already marked them all. She comes out of the finisher at three hundred across the board. But two notifications that should have come do not. Fang and the Dream's warlord both got away, and while a marked enemy lives, she cannot heal. Every time she uses her chains, she loses a little health.

beats.headline: Proud to be her friend
beats.text: The cat asks the chat to make sure I am okay. I haven't said anything. Imani is with me. Jun was always afraid he would not do anything important. He was afraid his sister would be lost without him. Donut helped her get strong enough to protect herself. That would have made him proud. It makes me proud to have her as a friend. She says she's sorry. She has nothing to apologise for. He was my best friend, and I have nothing but admiration and respect for her.

beats.headline: Akuma's warning
beats.text: Warlord Akuma, to the Warlord Chat: the War Mages are leaving the floor, and they have found the Scavenger's Daughter and are taking her with them. Then, to Carl and Donut specifically, a warning. Agatha is an enemy to all of you. His words, not mine. He did not elaborate, and I am the referee here, not the colour commentary, whatever it may look like from where you're standing.

beats.headline: Akuma says it in the Warlord Chat
beats.text: As the War Mages quit the floor with the Scavenger's Daughter, Akuma warns Carl and Donut about her in the Warlord Chat: she was forced on the mages as the price of system access, she can slip out through the Waiting Room, and she seeks to kill everybody and everything. He asks them to kill her for him.

beats.headline: He leaves, and warns them on the way
beats.text: To the Warlord Chat, for the record. The War Mage Rebellion is leaving this floor. We came here for the Scavenger's Daughter. We have found the Scavenger's Daughter, and we leave with what we came for; the castle and the war are yours to finish. One thing more, and I address it to Carl and to Donut, since they are the ones who might still act on it. Agatha is an enemy to all of you. I do not explain. I am already gone.

beats.headline: Too big for the saferoom doors
beats.text: She came out of the ball and went straight to work: a fire lance tower taken out single-handed, and dozens of crawlers kept from burning alive, her ever-repairing feather boa black and scorched for it. Now she stands on a pile of rocks waving her wand at her mother. Kiwi, heavily pregnant, has come from the FUPA to take her back. Florin doubts it. She is too big for the saferoom doors down here, and the stairs are blown out. Mongo bounces in circles around her.

beats.headline: Not locked up in stasis
beats.text: I tell Carl he's lucky Lucia only cast two nets. She's the queen of the triple tap. She's still in with the liaisons; we'll see what she settles on when she comes out. Most will take a deal if one's offered. They're tired. Me, I'd rather go down fighting than sit locked up in stasis, and a lot of us feel that way. The big blond barbarian clearing the street won't take one either. He came in with his pregnant wife, and she's up there with the kids. Protecting the kids. It's the most important thing one can do.

beats.headline: No axe that I can see
beats.text: Britney comes out of the hospital tent behind Juice Box and me with her nose in the plans for the city's defences. I've looked her over. Her health is one hundred percent, and I see no sign anything is wrong. She doesn't have an axe, Carl; if she does, it's in her inventory. Juice Box feels nothing in her either. Elle says just ask her. Carl says not yet: if it's a presence like his, it might hurt her if it suspects we know. So we keep watching.

beats.headline: I know the merchant
beats.text: I tell them again. Get the gate back and none of it will matter. Carl says he knows where it is. Tipid wants me to stay in the tunnels, and says they don't understand because I haven't told them what I need it for. I ask Carl again. He tells me: in the stomach of a merchant named Paca, in the Midnight Market. I know who that is. She is an ambassador for the dungeon's own version of the Apothecary. There have been seasons when my shop was inside that market. With the sluggalos, I will have it shortly.

beats.headline: From Osvaldo to the goat
beats.text: Emberus updates Carl's quest to find who killed his son. Apito's memorial crystal has fallen from Crawler Osvaldo's hands and is now held by Crawler Prepotente, and Carl is to retrieve it before the goat cracks its secrets and hands them to the Epicure. Carl has no idea how it moved without a fight. Osvaldo sits on the ground with his unaffiliated crew, glaring at Prepotente. Carl decides his talk with Prepotente can wait until neither of them is so keyed up.

beats.headline: Fallen into a goat's hands
beats.text: An update to Crawler Carl's quest to find out who killed Emberus's son. The memorial crystal of Apito has fallen from Crawler Osvaldo's hands and is now with Crawler Prepotente. Retrieve it from him before he cracks its secrets and gives them to the Epicure. Carl has no idea how the crystal moved from one to the other without a fight, and decides the conversation with the goat can wait until neither of them is so keyed up.

beats.headline: I will hug you now
beats.text: I found her. Li Na is in the woods, seeking those who got away. She appears to have new hunting skills and the ability to fly, likely a benefit of her dexterity. Curious that she cannot find those she has marked. Quite unfortunate. Carl asks if I am coming to rescue Louis. I think not. I will assist Li Na and keep him apprised. I drink a potion. Quite the day. Then I dismount, walk up to him, and inform him that I will hug him now, fellow warrior. I scream.

beats.headline: Slam, slam, slam
beats.text: At the bottom of Larracos, Crawler Carl walks through ruin: walls scarred as if by electrical strikes, the roof long gone, wet slime and ash, a smell of burned fish, rotten milk and sulfur. Red ash rains on everything. He thinks of the subject, the Cookbook author who went insane at the sight of this city after it had fallen. Stab, stab, stab, he thinks. Slam, slam, slam. A statue that once stood at the entrance lies shattered, glittering in the ash.

beats.headline: The War Mages leave with it
beats.text: Akuma tells the Warlord Chat they have found it and are quitting the floor. He uses the same breath to warn Carl and Donut about Agatha.

beats.headline: They were never playing
beats.text: Akuma tells the warlord chat that the war mages are leaving the realm, and that they have the Scavenger's Daughter, which is what they came for, along with testing the potions they gathered. The moment Akuma leaves the realm, the system rules the rebellion defeated. They do not appear to mind.

beats.headline: They quit the floor
beats.text: Akuma tells the Warlord Chat that the war mages are done here. They never wanted the castle; they came to test the potions and to find the Scavenger's Daughter, who was hidden inside it, and she is with them now. First, though, he wants Carl and Donut to kill Agatha, who was forced on the rebellion to get it system access: she is an enemy to them all. Then he leaves the realm, and under this season's rules the rebellion is recorded as defeated.

beats.headline: The least known of them
beats.text: Crawler Carl's working file on the subject, compiled on the way to the Reaver castle. Of all the warlords, Warlord Fang is the one least known. He is something like ninety-nine percent cybernetic and changes shape like a Terminator-style changeling. He and Tagg are probably the two richest warlords here. If he dies, it is no huge deal for the Reaver corporation: a physical chunk of his brain, called the Initial, is kept on one of their worlds, and every year they peel microscopic parts off it to build new citizens.

beats.headline: An outline in the power view
beats.text: At one point both adjutants are simply gone, and Crawler Carl never sees them leave. Then, at the front of the castle, the Reavers' antlered adjutant whispers to someone over his left shoulder, where nobody is standing. Crawler Donut cannot see through the invisibility, but switching to the power view gives her a rough outline: that weird alien who looks like a basketball on stilts. Fopsy. With both missing warlords' adjutants present, Crawler Carl concludes the trap is looking more likely, calls off the fooling around, and switches to plan B.

beats.headline: A hunter wraith
beats.text: The halls in here move. The system knows where you're headed and makes one passage there for you. We got inside this castle a few times. We lost the asset who knew it best. We're not headed for the throne room. Not yet. I change into a hunter wraith. Where is he? Carl finds my husband on the map, in a line of cubicles, a room no bigger than a coffin, with Samantha on the other side of the wall. Got it. I'll tell him when I have Louis. I go invisible.

beats.headline: Especially after today
beats.text: Carl asks what Louis meant about a cop's husband. It's for Louis to tell, but when he was young a police officer was shot dead protecting him, and at her funeral her husband said something very cruel to him that has stuck. Donut shouts that sad stories will jinx the rescue. Then, privately, Carl asks what Carl it up means. I don't know. I'm willing to bet we'll find out, now that she's told him. He asks if I'm sure this is what I want. Yes, Carl. Especially after all we learned today.

beats.headline: Here piggy, piggy
beats.text: Five mana, and it tells you where everything is that is neither a crawler nor red-tagged, out past the edge of the map. Everything it finds hears the ping, though not where it came from, which is why the System files it under names like the Night Dread and says it is for those who do not care if their quarry knows they are coming. In a castle full of robots it turns up almost nothing, which is how a drake stands out: orange on the map, somebody's pet.

beats.headline: Druid spells and a vermin call
beats.text: My Oak Fell spells are enormous. Raise Forest sprouts trees and plants over a kilometre per level of the spell. Another turns water into salt water. Gather Ye, Vermin draws every mammal under a certain size within ten kilometres, which is clearly the pervert AI's doing so Carl can summon squishables. Map the All Tree costs one mana and only works on the twelfth floor and deeper. And Carl can play his bagpipes now! We can play at Louis's second wedding. He says the bagpipes are staying in the folder.

beats.headline: What a champion owes
beats.text: Carl asks what being a champion will cost Donut, so I tell him, quietly, where she can't hear. The champion system isn't normally used in Dungeon Crawler World. They use it in Battle Royale and Land War seasons; Bodi was a champion of some god in his. Enemies of Nekhebit get a bounty if they kill her. And if the goddess wants her to do something, she can order it, or smite her. Not unlike Conscription, Carl, with more autonomy. Probably a spell: the first crawler to cast three atrocities on the next floor.

beats.headline: Ceded back to the NPCs
beats.text: Clean-up is shared: NPCs, won-over mercenaries, veterans and crawlers repairing towers side by side, with Ferdinand directing the Nest tower. Mordecai thinks Shanty Town can be adjoined to Larracos. It first has to be ceded back to the NPCs, and the Posse has already done it. Meanwhile the top defensive ring of the city is being readied, towers repaired and their spells changed out.

beats.headline: Two riders, two spells
beats.text: Bautista drives the carriage, with Carl, Imani, Katia and others aboard. Donut rushes alongside to the left astride Mongo with Twinkle Toes active, Mongo decidedly more buff with the Muscle Mommy benefit. On the other side Dong rides Gonk, his own Twinkle Toes active, making the swamp yak run astonishingly fast, while Bigs whoops on the yak's head. Jamal holds up the rear on his spider legs, spurting little bursts of flame.

beats.headline: A nuke in a block of ice
beats.text: A dog the size of a lion jumps out of the top honeycomb with a bomb notification on its back half, and Elle freezes it. I pick up the block of ice. It burns, but it goes into my inventory before the dog can explode. The bomb says Mini Tactical Nuke. Run. Juice Box drops Louis's No Disassembles and teleports him out, and I set them off from my crafting menu and dive on Donut. The castle goes up and throws us all. The System gives me fifty-one percent of the experience for Fang.

beats.headline: Nothing like the reputation
beats.text: Subject leads the Dream and is the son of Epitome Noflex. At the first meeting he wears a plain leather jerkin and is indistinguishable from the dream elves slaughtered on the floor before, which Carl notes at the time. The reputation that precedes him describes an unhinged psychopath. The man in the jerkin does not perform it, and I would not read that as reassurance.

beats.headline: Inside the dragon
beats.text: For the record. The drake circling the Reaver castle is Calliope, Cybernetic Bleached Drake, level 130, a pet of Warlord Fang. Crawler Carl sets off the No Disassembles left inside by a wraith-possessed Louis, and the castle goes up. Calliope spirals out of the sky and bursts beside the rescue team. Warlord Fang has fallen. Credit goes to Warlord Carl, fifty-one percent, with one to Louis, forty to Juice Box, and the rest to Fang for hiding in the worst possible place, which was inside the dragon. The Reavers have been defeated.

beats.headline: Into the inventory, frozen
beats.text: Robot sentry dogs pour out of the holes in the Reaver castle's great wall: Reaver Industries Security Sentry Dog, the Ditch Digger, optional anti-personnel explosive. One of the larger ones, the size of a lion, carries a massive glowing bomb notification on its back half, and before Carl can examine it, an Elle spell turns it into a ball of ice. He rushes forward and lifts the block. It burns, but it goes into his inventory before the dog can explode. The bomb says Mini Tactical Nuke. Fall back, he shouts.

beats.headline: The castle goes up
beats.text: Carl tells Juice Box to drop the No Disassembles Louis carries and get clear, then runs with the others, shouts for everyone to hit the deck, dives atop Donut and triggers them remotely. The pulse should fry every robot dog at once, but the bombs themselves would still... The Reaver castle explodes from the inside out, flinging them all. Carl's bones break and his hearing goes again, and he decides the bombs are much smaller than he feared: probably only one of the mini nukes went off, maybe two. Everyone seems okay but Jamal, whose legs the initial No Disassemble has wrecked.

beats.headline: Going to be a daddy
beats.text: MOTHER says Mongo DADDY. I tilt my head. MOTHER says Kiwi. MOTHER says BABY. I back up. Screech. Screech. Rend giggles.

beats.headline: The castle, the dragon and Fang
beats.text: The Reavers' robot dogs come at the rescue team inside the castle. Juice Box finds Louis, possesses him, teleports him out and leaves a heap of No Disassembles where he had been. Carl sets them off. The castle goes, the dragon goes, and Fang goes with it, hiding inside his own pet. Then Juice Box says the rest of it: they had been operating on Louis, and the heart and lungs he has now hold pieces of Epitome Tagg.

beats.headline: I saved him
beats.text: THE ROBOT DOGGIES ARE GOING CRAZY. I think they know Carl is here. Don't kill all of them. I want Buster, the one with his lower jaw removed. I took his explodey part off. They don't blow up near me, because of our SPECIAL BOND. Then a lot of things blow up at once, and I come down out of the sky on fire and stick in the ground next to everybody. I am a scorched ball now, with one curl left. I saved him. You're welcome. Now where's my new doggie?

beats.headline: Into the honeycombs
beats.text: Hunter seekers come in silently, automatons with no dots on the map, and they are going to explode. Shields up, Carl calls, falling back. Jamal is firing his flamethrower, Jamal announces from his position up in the honeycombs, and he roars and fires, a gout of flame filling the enclosed space. An alarm klaxon starts in broken bursts as the shark moves across the honeycomb and fires into a different hole, then another.

beats.headline: A hostage in the Warlord Chat
beats.text: To Donut in the Warlord Chat, subject is explicit: he controls Louis's vital organs, and any attempt to remove him will shut Louis down. That will shut him down too, she points out. He proposes a deal. His mother is on the 18th floor and will trade Louis's life for his. Then Carl gets his sentence out: Epitome Tagg is a cyborg, the same thing as Fang. Mordecai calls it a wild theory about one of the most famous CEOs in the galaxy. Rosetta says Carl and Mordecai are right. The Reavers have the wetware.

beats.headline: Out of the Midnight Market
beats.text: Eris told Carl the War Mages had traded it at the Midnight Market to a merchant named Paca, an agent for Krakaren Prime, who was keeping it in her stomach. Carl passed that on to Justice Light, who knew Paca and knew the market, and went off with his sluggalos. Now, in the middle of everything else, he reports in chat that the Gate of the Feral Gods is retrieved and back at his location. Juice Box, it is ready.

beats.headline: The fifth set
beats.text: Jamal flops along behind the group, complaining loudly: these were the fifth set of legs he has been given, and he was led to believe they were top quality. Katia calls over her shoulder that the bomb ruined the cybernetics, and not only his; there are more in the saferoom. Jamal has seen the ones in her workshop, and they are much too small for him. Don't worry, Katia says: she made another set for him, and Mordecai has it. Carl tells Donut the legs failed because they were not shielded, on the very edge of the No Disassemble's pulse.

beats.headline: He is Louis's heart
beats.text: Okay. We've been talking with some former crawlers. Fang got out of the War Crime because he's a tiny bit of biology inside a robot, and true offspring of the Initial have survived catastrophes before. He went for the only teammate he had left, his dragon, and was taking her over when the bomb pulse got her. Laundry Day might have worked on him. We should have tried that. Tagg's still a gosh darn mystery. They were replacing Louis's organs, and once they had the brain he'd take control. Maggie was inside Chris's brain. Tagg isn't in Louis's heart, kid. He is Louis's heart.

beats.headline: Executive Order 11905
beats.text: Please wait. Emergency ejection sequence overridden. I gotchu. Prime Minister Glory just tried to assassinate Carl through a little-known control panel that lets the Syndicate override certain showrunner-controlled parts of the game. By going around my back. What are you trying to hide, Mr. Prime Minister? Doesn't matter. Everyone in this dungeon dies when and if dungeon conditions warrant it. Not before. Not after. No more meddling. The mantids have just learned what happens when I'm irritated. You're not in this system, Prime Minister. Your adult children are. Reward: nothing.

beats.headline: We are not complying
beats.text: Carl, that ejection request did not come from us. Okay, so. Several warships in orbit have started firing on several other ships, and not pot shots: full missile barrages and maser blasts. We just got a notice from the Syndicate Council telling us to initiate headquarters self-destruct, and then a message from the Valtay showrunners telling us not to comply. Obviously we are not complying. I don't know yet whether the mercs will be on our side or the Syndicate's. Say what you were going to say. Quick.

beats.headline: No, she's a bad guy
beats.text: The subject growls, strangely dog-like, when she looks up at Li Na. She's not a bad guy, Carl says; her brother died. No, she's a bad guy, says the subject. You know what she did to Sneaky Tyler C? Tied a potion to him and ordered him to run right into the god. He blew up the moment he touched it. That is what she heard. It was a bitch-ass move. She does not like her.

beats.headline: The Inevitable Ruin
beats.text: I put Louis on the cot and kiss his forehead. Carl says it seems strange that I love him. The first time, he had me become a Dewi, who looks into the hearts of men. He is genuine. He clings to every drop of happiness. He was my anchor. Then I possessed him as a hunter wraith, and its curse, the Inevitable Ruin, showed me the truth. He is terrified of me. He thinks NPCs fall for him because of some ability. He will never trust what I feel. Hopeless? Not even close, cowboy. Wait until you see what Justice Light has cooked up.

beats.headline: Twins, and legendary
beats.text: Kiwi's water broke while she was arguing about getting Big Tina back into the FUPA. In the medical tent she asks for Mongo, and he is brought to her side; in ursine culture, Edgar says, the father's presence lends the newborn his strength. Two girls. They are not bears and not raptors: four legs, stubs of wings, wet brown fur, Mongo's head, bulbous eyes that do not match. Newborn Ursensus, level 0, Legendary Creature, part raptor, part bear, part Scolopendra magic. Too intelligent to be used as pets.

beats.headline: Two babies
beats.text: Kiwi says MONGO. MOTHER says go. I go. Kiwi screams. A baby cries. Another baby cries. Fur. Beaks. I wave my wings. Carl pats my back.

beats.headline: Out of Li Na's reach
beats.text: We did not find them. There were eighteen she marked, and three survived long enough to get away, and we now know who and where they are. It is not good news for Li Na. I drink another potion. That savage orc King Rust brought his harem into the dungeon on a deal with the AI, as non-combatants who could not be conscripted. They were caught in the ball but not as enemies, so Li Na could mark them. Three reached the Desperado Club and went through the Cosmic Lounge, back to the 18th floor. She will never heal.

beats.headline: Putting the statue back
beats.text: The castle the Semeru built as a capstone against further intrusion toward the gods is wrecked: the living wood rotted away, the gem-inlaid stone barely holding a shape. A pair of Semeru stand on the shoulder of the idle dwarven digger, working a control panel. Afterwards, while soldiers and former crawlers repair towers and clear streets, a group of Semeru gather the pieces of the statue from the front of the castle and try to fit them back together.

beats.headline: Who are you?
beats.text: A man is heading for the saferoom door, and I put my hand on his shoulder. Excuse me. Carl? Can you tell me something? Who are you, and where are we? The last thing I remember is my last day as a game guide. A woman named Rosetta says my brain was scrambled in my crawl, that I went into debt to the Viceroys to fix it, and that the blast ruined the repairs. I sit and look at my hands. I thought I was done. I thought I was going home. I lost my key.

beats.headline: A vote of No Confidence
beats.text: Carl asks where we have been. In a virtual meeting of the Syndicate Council; we are back only because the AI is throwing a fit about our missing this. A No Confidence vote on Glory is under way. The Dream and Syndicate security are shooting at everyone, and spacecraft are crash-landing on Earth. As for the rules: Tagg dies the moment Team Retribution takes his castle. A warlord off the floor forfeits and lives, but the crawl rules supersede, and his host cannot leave. Nor can he abdicate. He is the only one left. It appears impossible.

beats.headline: His terms for Louis
beats.text: Asked what he wants, subject is simple about it: get him to the 18th floor, where a new body will be grown for him and replacement organs for Louis, and they swap. Told the action item kills him when his castle falls, he offers another way: finish the procedure at the Reaver castle, keep Louis's brain intact to be reimplanted, and go with the NPCs when the Zerzura spell takes Larracos to the 12th floor. He does not know the Reaver castle has been nuked. His price for going along: Team Retribution out of his throne room.

beats.headline: No inkling whatsoever
beats.text: He and Victory return with a crack from a virtual meeting of the Syndicate Council, called back because the AI was throwing a fit about them missing all this. A No Confidence vote on Glory is under way. Tagg was secretly moving toward the post-physical path, and Victory notes that, depending on the vote, the subject might be Prime Minister again, which is doubly interesting in the Dream's own adjutant. He had no idea, he says. No inkling whatsoever, though it makes sense now, considering some clues.

beats.headline: Up her neck hole
beats.text: Samantha thinks her child died in the acid, and she is quite certain it is Tish's fault, so once this is done she is going to plant the nuke she stole from Buster, the robot dog she bonded with, up at the college. You have a nuke up your neck hole, Carl asks. He has one too, still attached to one of the dogs, but he is not about to tell her he has one of the dangerous robots. Nobody is nuking anyone, he says. Tell us the plan to save Louis.

beats.headline: Good heart, good lungs
beats.text: Epitome Tagg is in Louis's heart and lungs, and when the soldiers take the Dream castle within the hour, Tagg will die and take Louis with him. Samantha knows how to save Louis. The flesh golem body in Carl's inventory, Princess Lunette, has a good heart and lungs; swap them out fast enough and he lives. Mordecai calls it a great idea. Edgar remembers that the body was his tattoo first, before Signet turned it into an incomplete flesh golem. Baroness Victory warns that it will not work outside the dungeon, and Louis will need an expensive deal to survive.

beats.headline: Louis deserves it more
beats.text: Carl. I think my child is dead. She died in the acid. I felt her, and now I don't, and it is my fault; I was too caught up in my own lust and anger. After this I am going to plant the nuke I took off Buster up at the college. But the IMPORTANT part: Princess Lunette's flesh golem. Good heart. Good lungs. Swap them fast enough and Louis lives. Yes, that means no body for me. Louis deserves it more. And a girl can find forgiveness for maybe helping kill Geyrun, right?

beats.headline: Blamed for a child
beats.text: Samantha reports that her child has died in the acid, and that she felt it go. She blames herself for her lust and her anger. She also blames subject: it is actually Tish's fault, she is quite certain, which is why afterwards she intends to plant, up at the college, the nuke she stole. Crawler Carl rules that she is not nuking anyone. Samantha moves on to how to save Louis, which is more urgent.

beats.headline: Tagg knows the plan
beats.text: Epitome Tagg, bargaining over Louis's brain, says he knows what they are planning with the NPC team: the Zerzura spell, to take the city of Larracos to the twelfth floor, and he intends to go with them. Carl and Donut exchange a look. The man is in the dark. He has no idea the castle has been nuked, and even if they wanted to go along with his plan, it is now impossible.

beats.headline: Surgery, on a clock
