beats.text: Sixty-five minutes on the floor and every member of the party has a job. Edgar's job is surgery. He and Mordecai operate on Louis while the rest of it goes on above them, and nobody has told the tortoise how long he has.

beats.headline: Bring my enemy to me
beats.text: This so-called Psamathe claims she was part of my son's death. Capture her for me, and I will handle the interrogation personally. Once I have finished grilling her, I will cleanse this world in fire to remove the stink of the murderer's presence. If she is not within my presence in sixty-six minutes, this world will be destroyed in fire and lava and wrath. Fly, martyr. Bring my enemy to me.

beats.headline: Fallen, and credited to Mongo
beats.text: Warlord Epitome Tagg of the Dream has fallen. With Louis open on the table and the swap two minutes off, he told everyone they did not deserve singularity and stopped the heart himself. The machinery was yanked out, thrown on the floor, and chewed to pieces by a dinosaur. Credit is complicated. I almost called it a suicide. I almost gave it to the kid who pulled it. It goes to pet Mongo of the Princess Posse, as a present for the baby shower. And then there were two.

beats.headline: I love all of you
beats.text: Carl shouts at me to eat the orchid. Now. It takes sixty minutes and we have sixty-five. I haven't transferred all my inventory away; there's stuff in the safe room I need. He puts his forehead against mine. This isn't goodbye, this is how we win, and it's my plan. I've already given Donut the things. I remind him I said he'd Carl it up. He says this one's on Samantha. I love you. I love all of you. I climb onto the table where Kiwi gave birth, and I eat it.

beats.headline: Gills, man
beats.text: Okay so, I wake up coughing, and water comes out of my neck. Gills, man. Where am I? Mordecai tells me to switch off the water-breathing notification. I did already, when I woke up. But something's wrong. I feel weird. Everybody claps anyway. Then Samantha zips up, says we're cousins now, and kisses me on the lips. And Mongo spits a chewed-up plastic heart and lungs onto the floor of the tent.

beats.headline: NOT FOOD
beats.text: Wet plastic heart on the ground. BAD. I bite. I chew. I chew more. NOT FOOD. Spit. The System gives Mongo the kill. For the baby shower.

beats.headline: Allowed under the non-combatant code
beats.text: Listen. This is a surgical procedure, allowed under the non-combatant code, and the second party is an empty shell. I cut down the centre of Louis's chest. We're rigging about thirty lines to bring Tagg's machinery out in one piece when he stops the heart early. I can't be the one to pull it; that could count as an attack. Someone else yanks it out. Donut pours the Special Brew, the naiad organs go in, I sew the rebreather into the bronchial, cast a Water Breathing scroll and run tubes to the gills. Done, with ten seconds left.

beats.headline: Into Louis's chest
beats.text: Edgar's plan for Louis runs on thirty seconds: Mordecai cuts him open, and once the naiad's organs are ready they administer the special brew, swap out the heart and lungs, Juice Box activates the new ones, and then the graft. Donut stands on a high chair over Louis's open chest, ready to drop the potion. Louis's heart stops before they are ready, and Bucket Boy yanks the old organs out and throws them over his shoulder. Potion! Edgar cries, and Donut pours Mordecai's Special Brew into the open, gushing chest as Imani places the new organs and Juice Box casts.

beats.headline: Epitome Tagg's Sexy Mother
beats.text: I didn't get to say goodbye to Katia. Then Mordecai needs Tagg distracted while they have Louis open, so I ask him how he will look his mother in the eye, knowing Louis had sex with her. He insists it was a changeling. So I change my name to Epitome Tagg's Sexy Mother and ask Louis to come help with my hand stuck in the washing machine. He screams at me to change it back. I can't. No more name changes until tomorrow. Carl says stall, not provoke. We're playing good cop, bad cop.

beats.headline: Heart and lungs out
beats.text: Carl dumps the body on a cot beside Louis. It is a slight, beautiful naiad, and it has gills, so Mordecai takes the kua-tin rebreather Carl looted from Loita. Imani and Rosetta open the golem up, and with Elle they hold its dripping heart and lungs up in a net. When Louis's heart stops, Bucket Boy yanks the old organs out, Imani places the new ones, Juice Box casts, and Mordecai sews the rebreather into the bronchial. The chest snaps shut. Louis coughs water from new gills and opens his eyes.

beats.headline: Gills that stay
beats.text: Louis's ribcage is held open while new organs go in, taken from the body of a full naiad, which has Carl worried she breathes only water. Mordecai sews a rebreather into the bronchial, then casts a Water Breathing scroll on Louis, the scroll version because Katia's potion cooldown is too long now. As the gills form, he connects tubes from the new organs to them, and Bucket Boy jams stops into the slits to keep them there after the water breathing ends. Louis coughs water from his neck. Bucket Boy pulls the stops out. The gills remain.

beats.headline: Two teams left
beats.text: Epitome Tagg is dead and the Dream is beaten, which leaves the Princess Posse and Team Retribution on the board. A team of NPCs was put on this floor to be fodder. It has outlasted eight galactic powers.

beats.headline: Epitome Tagg is dead, the Dream is finished
beats.text: Emberus wants Samantha interrogated and intends to break the floor in sixty-six minutes whatever the answer. In the middle of that, the Dream is beaten. Epitome Tagg is dead. Two teams remain standing on this floor, the Princess Posse and Team Retribution, and neither of them is the one that owned half the food in the universe.

beats.headline: A present in Larracos
beats.text: In the rings around them, thousands of crawlers who mean to take a deal on the next floor, and former crawlers going home, look down as Milk announces a present. Carl's Book of Voodoo splits in two. Donut shouts that she has a book called A Banquet Fit for a Princess, filled with pictures and nice things about her, and spells. Milk taught the leavers to take out a skill or spell and paint it onto a page, three each: one for Carl, one for Donut, one for anyone. They lose it for good. Eaten, a page gives it back for a very short time, depending on the quality of the drawing, and each should carry a personal note of thanks.

beats.headline: The ring goes down the cat
beats.text: Over fifty thousand former crawlers came to fight for us. About twenty-eight thousand are left. Of the 32,500 crawlers who reached this floor, 20,221 are still here, a record. The mercenaries we beat are milling around Larracos, and my first instinct is to mark them, kill them, and go to three hundred across the board like Li Na. One look at her tells me that slope is too steep. I still don't want to let the ring go. I hold it up in front of Donut's nose. Are you sure? I'm sure. She swallows it.

beats.headline: The second volume
beats.text: Milk's voice carries over Larracos: the crawlers in the rings have a present. Carl's Book of Voodoo is updated with a metric fuckton of entries and segmented into two volumes. The second is Carl's Book of Boom. It behaves like the first, about five hundred pages where the Book of Voodoo should by now have almost thirty thousand, and it zeroes in on the entry he is meant to find. He opens it at random. Crawler 1,982,122, Asi Hamami, a level 59 fox warrior, thanks him and has not lost hope. Below, a crude red lock and key. Eating the page gives a level 10 Lockpick skill for five minutes.

beats.headline: Anytime, babe
beats.text: Warlord Ferdinand turns up on Drick's bald head, wearing the bowler hat Princess Donut let him keep, to say yo before moseying down to the twelfth floor to bang some hot goddess chicks. He offers her a last-second fling. There are about four minutes, which he considers more than enough. She declines. Then she thanks him for trying to come save her in the tower. Anytime, babe. His transfer, with Juice Box's, is what defeats Team Retribution and hands the war to the Princess Posse.

beats.headline: The long way round
beats.text: Louis comes out of the tent holding his throat. I say something to him and he says something back, and I put my hands to my face and turn away. Then, in chat: I will be leaving about ten seconds after everyone else. Carl wants to know where. Oh, I'm going to the twelfth floor all right. Justice Light and I are taking the long way. It's okay, Carl. Trust me. You'll like this one.

beats.headline: Zerzura
beats.text: The Sledge casts Zerzura and the city goes: Larracos and the shanty town outside its walls lifted whole and set down on the twelfth floor, NPC team and all. The outworlders who were standing in it are put out of the dungeon instead.

beats.headline: Storage, or back to the market
beats.text: Ninth floor, closing arrangements. Nobody is certain what happens to the mercenaries. The hired ones, the Sledge and the other surviving cretins among them, along with the dungeon-born mercenaries for hire on every team, are expected to simply disappear: possibly into storage for the next crawl, possibly tossed back into the mercenary market. They do not go down to the twelfth floor. The strippers are a question mark, and so they stay with the crawlers.

beats.headline: One final meal
beats.text: Milk will not go to the twelfth floor. She goes back to her guild. She has fulfilled her contract, lives out the season, and may leave after it, glad to have been given the chance to cook one final meal. Then, amplified by a word etched on her own throat, she presents the crawlers taking deals and the former crawlers going home: each crawler has painted three skills or spells onto pages, one for Carl, one for Donut, one for anyone. Goodbye, Carl. Burn it all to the ground. He hugs his sister.

beats.headline: Congratulations, Champions
beats.text: Larracos and Shanty Town go to the twelfth floor under the Zerzura, and the two warlords of Team Retribution go with them. Ferdinand and Juice Box leave the realm, and under the current ruleset that is abandoning their posts. Team Retribution is defeated. The Princess Posse has won Faction Wars. The System addresses its congratulations to Champions.

beats.headline: With the city, to the Ascendency
beats.text: Closing arrangements for the ninth floor. The hired mercenaries are expected to vanish. The changelings, the thousands of NPCs who live in Larracos, and the Semeru dwarves are to move with the city to the Ascendency, where it is meant to land on a green hill above miles of cotton fields. The NPCs are untouchable there until the Ascendency begins. It is not safe. It is life.

beats.headline: Inside the glow
beats.text: Rosetta, on the chat: it worked. Shanty Town is included in the glow, and the two towns have been combined. The entire funnel city of Larracos, Shanty Town with it, is about to be transferred to the twelfth floor as the Sledge casts. Rosetta is moving to the saferoom with Tipid and the others, and she has Samantha with her.

beats.headline: I made a difference?
beats.text: The Princess says goodbye. Best bodyguard anyone ever had. Maybe I see her again. Maybe I see Bomo. She no need bodyguard anymore. She says she will always need me. She headbutts me, and goes back to Carl. I start to cast. Zerzura. Five minutes. Rosetta says Shanty Town is in the glow. Twenty seconds, I say. I look at Carl. I made a difference? He says I did.

beats.headline: A city sent to the cotton fields
beats.text: The Sledge casts Zerzura, and the funnel city of Larracos, with Shanty Town combined into its glow, is transferred to the twelfth floor, to the Court of the Ascendency. Rosetta has described it: most of the action happens in the halls themselves, on a green, fertile hill above miles of cotton fields, and the city lands somewhere in those fields, where its NPCs settle. The rules for the gods are clear. The NPCs are untouchable until the Ascendency actually starts.

beats.headline: Split into two volumes
beats.text: Milk's present arrives as a notification: the Book of Voodoo updates with, in the System's words, a metric fuckton of entries, and splits into two volumes, the second called Carl's Book of Boom. By now the original should run to almost thirty thousand pages; it still has about five hundred, and opens near the entry Carl is meant to find. The crawlers leaving the dungeon have each painted three skills or spells onto pages: one for Carl, one for Donut, and one on their own entry page in the original book, first come, first served, for anyone. Painting a skill away costs them it for good.

beats.headline: The statue is finished
beats.text: A dwarf calls out that he has finished, in the moment before Larracos goes. The broken statue from the front of the castle has been pieced back together. It is Ysalte, the Vinegar Bitch, the dead goddess of this city, killed by Paz at the end of the last floor. Over her shoulder she carries a giant axe. A giant pickaxe. Crawler Carl is looking straight at it when everything flashes and disappears.

beats.headline: The second casting
beats.text: The Sledge says goodbye to Donut, and starts to cast. Five minutes. He glows. Rosetta reports that Shanty Town is inside the glow: the two towns have combined. Larracos and Shanty Town are going to the Court of the Ascendency, to land somewhere in the fields of cotton. The hired mercenaries, the Sledge among them, are expected simply to disappear. The changelings and the city's thousands of NPCs are to go. The outworlders are to be sent out of the dungeon: about 28,000 left of the more than 50,000 who came to fight. Twenty seconds, and the Sledge turns to Carl: I made a difference? You did.

beats.headline: Acting Prime Minister
beats.text: I am waiting to be onboarded onto the Syndicate's temporary forward headquarters on the planet's surface, the ship having been shot down. With the unfortunate death of my underage nieces and nephews in orbit, I am once again eligible for office. Former Prime Minister Fopsy's relationship to the Dream being uncertain, he was passed over. I am acting Prime Minister until a real vote in a few months. It would not matter if it were permanent. I have less power than I did as a judge; the council is as gridlocked as the Lemig Sortion. Carl lays a hand on my shoulder. I am still protected.

beats.headline: I got them done
beats.text: I am in the crafting room, finishing something. Carl messages that I am running out of time. I am coming. When I walk into the tent with the devices in my arms, they all tense. I got them done. Oh, Daniel, she says. I didn't think you knew. Of course I knew. I love you. I am sorry I made you doubt me. The goddess says she sees who Katia wishes the father to be, and it cannot be so. When Katia is human again, we fasten on the parts she made herself.

beats.headline: Tuba and Selvi take a deal
beats.text: The dead Burcu's party members, Tuba and Selvi, leave. Both say they are taking a deal. Neither ever told Carl why or how the subject considered him the one who killed her father, and he fears he may never know. His own reflection on it: that is the problem with such chaos. You lose so much around the edges.

beats.headline: Laughter in the river
beats.text: The stairwells fill. Tran goes in. Zhang goes in alone. Li Na goes in without a word. Tuba and Selvi, Burcu's party, leave to take deals, and never told me why Burcu thought I killed her father. That's the problem with such chaos. You lose so much around the edges. And right then I hear distant laughing, deep in the back of my mind, from the river I hoped would go with the ring. It sounds like Eris.

beats.headline: Her lovely shawl
beats.text: Huanxin Jinx has slid to a stop in a circle of words of power that stops her teleporting, shaking with rage, and Donut stalks a circle around her. She has shown off her new knee pads. She has also upgraded a skill because of her lovely shawl, she says; it is not quite at fifteen yet, but it is getting there. Does Huanxin want to know what it is? Stay the hells away from me, the heiress answers. I am a god.

beats.headline: On Donut's back, Mordecai's bolt
beats.text: Huanxin Jinx is trapped in a circle of words of power, and a weapon mount from the Apothecary's gold benefactor box appears on Donut's back: the Scorpion's Bite. Katia's crossbow forms on it with an ominous click, bigger than Donut and not loaded. It is not as strong as it could be, Donut says, with no women in her party. Mordecai walks into the tent holding a plain bolt with some of his mother's ashes in its tip, a funeral rite of his culture. He says goodbye to Katia, loads the bolt into the crossbow on Donut's back and walks out. The crossbow fires. The bolt slams between the alien's eyes, and she slides to Victory's feet, dead.

beats.headline: She chooses, and I take her out
beats.text: The doppelgänger wakes, and it is time, so I enter the realm. Then a cat casts Laundry Day on my sponsor and ejects her out of me, and I am held in place, unable to move a finger, until the choice is made. It is not a bad way to spend the minutes. Katia chooses to be pregnant. So I ease what needs easing, and I take her out of this dungeon, and her friends stand in the dust of a battlefield saying goodbye to somebody who is going to live.

beats.headline: Partied with Lucia
beats.text: Before the stairs, Lucia sits on the ground sobbing while Imani, the barbarian and I talk to her about taking a deal. I get her to party with me. She says she'll take one. She was sketchy about it. None of us believe she will, so I won't take one either.

beats.headline: Passed over for Prime Minister
beats.text: Asked when the stairwells appear, Victory says immediately; the subject corrects her: about ten seconds. The office goes elsewhere. Victory reports that because people were not certain of former Prime Minister Fopsy's relationship to the Dream, he was passed over for the newly vacated position of Syndicate Prime Minister. She is acting Prime Minister Victory now, with a real vote in a few months. Rosetta sounds strangely irritated at the news.

beats.headline: A plain bolt between the eyes
beats.text: Huanxin Jinx of the Grixist Swarm, CEO of Icon Industries, arrived wearing her goddess to collect Katia and was loudly unpleasant about the delay. Crawler Princess Donut laundered her out of the soul armour and onto a circle she could not teleport from. Her shields lasted one pass of Claw. The bolt that killed her was plain and unenchanted, with some of Mordecai's mother's ashes in the tip, fired from Katia's crossbow on the cat's back. She came to rest at Victory's feet.

beats.headline: A new set
beats.text: Jamal stayed in the saferoom through the Zerzura, and he is one of the few NPCs who have decided to stay with Carl and Donut. Now he bounces up and down on a new set of legs, very excited at the thought of seeing a goddess like Eileithyia, who he has heard is quite beautiful, though not as beautiful as her retainer, Yemaya.

beats.headline: The only way to reach them
beats.text: I choose to be made pregnant. The goddess asks if I'm certain and offers me a place in her court, kept safe. I tell her the rules here are strange. If I'm pregnant, I get sent somewhere else, and there are children up there, mostly alone, in trouble. This is the only way I can get to them. She says she senses them and cannot reach them. I am made human again, and my friends see what I've lost: an arm, a leg, the other below the knee, an ear. We've all become experts at hiding what we've really lost.

beats.headline: Clicked into place
beats.text: Eileithyia tells Katia she will first be made human again, and Katia shrinks, her blonde hair turning black. Her entire right arm is gone to the shoulder, her left leg is gone, her right leg up to the knee, and an ear. Just a few things she has lost along the way, she says. Bautista quickly brings the cybernetic parts: she made them herself in anticipation of this and left them in the crafting room, and he finished them. They all click and fasten them into place while the goddess lays her hand on Katia's stomach. The word Ineligible appears over her head. Bye, guys, Katia says, raises her cybernetic right arm, waves, and is gone in a puff of smoke.

beats.headline: Divorce papers
beats.text: Juice Box left me. She gave me divorce papers. Donut tells me to get in the stairwell. No way, man. I gotta say goodbye to Katia. Then Katia wakes up, and the goddess says the father has to be human, and Katia asks if I'd be willing. Am I still human? I touch my neck. The goddess says of course, and a good soul at that. Then sure, I guess. If she'll have me. It'll be a boy. Spoilers.

beats.headline: My mother's ashes
beats.text: No, I can't touch you. Not directly. See this? A crossbow bolt. Nothing magical about it. My brother died because of you, and because of Odette, and because of Chaco. But mostly because of you. Some of my mother's ashes are built into the tip. In my culture you make a weapon from the ashes of those you lost. She died before the crawl came to my world, and I'm grateful she gets to avenge her son. Goodbye, Katia. Be safe, kid. I load it into the crossbow on the cat's back and walk out.

beats.headline: Katia's way out
beats.text: She takes it and leaves the crawl, human again and missing pieces of herself.

beats.headline: We just need to kill you
beats.text: Huanxin wants Katia to choose so they can go. Darling, I have a better idea. Laundry Day, level sixteen now, and she is ripped out of the goddess onto a circle of words of power where she can't teleport. My Claw, nearly fifteen, takes her shields. I have Katia's knee pads on, the goddess's boon gives me 500 percent, and Carl's party bonus another 500. The Apothecary's box was a weapon mount, and Katia's crossbow is on my back. Mordecai loads one bolt. We don't need to kill the gods and goddesses to win. The crossbow fires. We just need to kill you.

beats.headline: A gift with an implication
beats.text: In Eileithyia's tent, Donut stalks a circle round Huanxin, whose shields she has just clawed away, while the goddess cannot move until Katia makes her choice. A strange device appears on Donut's back, from the gold benefactor box she received from the Apothecary: a simple gift, Carl thinks, but the implication is clear. A non-magical quadruped weapon mount, the scorpion's bite. Katia's crossbow forms on it with an ominous click, bigger than Donut and not loaded, and she holds the weight just fine. It is not as strong as it could be, she says, because she has no women in her party.

beats.headline: They fit me
beats.text: Huanxin Jinx has slid to a stop in a circle of words of power, unable to teleport. Do you see my new knee pads, Donut asks. Aren't they lovely? A celestial item she got from Katia, and they fit her. She does not really need this with Huanxin, she admits, but the Eileithyia boon is a five hundred per cent bonus against enemies, and being partied with Carl gives her another five hundred. She starts to stalk in a circle around the heiress.

beats.headline: Another system, a star gone nova
beats.text: Victory has news for Huanxin: the newest mantis colony system has just gone dark, at the same moment the other rottweiler died a few hours back. The initial reports are a little more holistic than they were in the Aryl system. This time, the star went nova. Huanxin calls her a lying bitch, and adds that, even if she is not, there is insurance.

beats.headline: Offered a place in her court
beats.text: Jamal, waiting outside a saferoom for a goddess, would very much like to see Eileithyia, and her retainer Yemaya, who he hears is the more beautiful. Carl says no. Eileithyia comes alone. Katia asks her for a pregnancy, and the goddess asks whether she is certain: come and assist her and Yemaya in her court instead, and she promises Katia is kept safe.

beats.headline: A convent of nuns
beats.text: The goddess arrives with Huanxin driving, and the court, she says, is in a tizzy about the city these fools just teleported in. It splattered an entire convent of Resheph's nuns, and he is losing his mind. Now the zombies are wandering all over, and Odette has taken control of them, having already taken out Inpewt. The games have not even started. Behind them, Jamal stayed in the saferoom during the Zerzura, one of the few NPCs who chose to stay.

beats.headline: Left on the table
beats.text: Emberus is three minutes from destroying the floor, and Katia is gone. On the table she left a pair of items. One is her card from the floor before, the one depicting Annie the skull-headed bird. Donut takes it. The other is a bra with Carl's face on one cup and Time to pay the daddy tax on the other, and Elle grabs that. Carl assumes it came from the Dungeon Sidekicks show and was left as a joke.

beats.headline: A brother like you
beats.text: I stop beside Carl before the stairwell. I know he thought I would do something horrible, or jealous. I almost did. I keep losing family, and it makes me scared, and it makes me angry. I am not considered human anymore, and that is my great shame, today most of all. But I would never do anything to hurt a brother like him. One more thing: the Kimaris figure he carries is one of the brothers of Sheol, with a summoning time of the remainder of the floor. Be careful with him. I go in.

beats.headline: A portal into the Nothing
beats.text: Its winding box, broken and blood-soaked, has become a permanent portal into the Nothing, and Juice Box has used it to leave the ninth floor. Justice Light, who told her he was going with her and lied, stays on this side to spring the small trap set above it. One snapped piece of twine, and a bijou fairy trap and a demon trap fall into the open portal, carrying the thousands of threads that tie the fairies to the twelfth floor and the thousands of evicted demons.

beats.headline: Samantha calls him Kimmy
beats.text: At the stairwell Bautista delivers his finding: Kimaris is one of the brothers of Sheol, with a summoning time of the remainder of the floor. Be careful with him. Samantha overhears. Kimmy! she shrieks, and demands him at once. He is one of her best friends. He gave her the potion that let her become pregnant when she could not, and advised her on whom to date. Then she stops, puzzled that she could not remember any of that before. Her conclusion, delivered at volume: she is going to kill his mother.

beats.headline: I gained more
beats.text: The last minute on the floor, and I'm sitting in the dirt with a cigarette and a bottle of Crown Royal, dawn coming up, red comets streaking off the volcano. Carl says get back in the saferoom. I lost so much today. But I think I gained more. I stand, wipe myself off, and throw the bottle through the rotten roots. Thank you, Donut, for setting that up. Then I step toward the door.

beats.headline: They are not going to break me
beats.text: Katia left two things on the table. Her card from the last floor, with Annie the skull-headed bird on it, which I take, and a bra with Carl's face on one cup, which Elle takes. I feel really bad now about having pooped in Mordecai's mother's ashes. It was supposed to be a grand gesture. Carl says don't you dare tell Mordecai. At the stairwell he asks if I'm doing okay. I'm going to miss her. But they are not going to break me. No matter how hard they try.

beats.headline: Kimmy, remembered
beats.text: HE'S NOT TOUCHING ME ANYMORE. Bring me back! He was going to EAT me, but I had him throw me in a volcano like Carl said, and now he's blowing up the world. Then Bautista says Carl has a Kimaris figure. KIMMY! Give him to me! He's one of my best friends. He gave me the potion that put my baby in me when I couldn't get pregnant. Why couldn't I remember that? He gave me advice on who to date. His MOTHER! I will kill his mother!

beats.headline: Scolopendra has awakened
beats.text: The Nothing drains into the Halls of the Ascendency, into Sheol, and into Scolopendra's lair, and Scolopendra stirs. A planetwide message follows: guests of the Scolopendra Club should evacuate. Nowhere to go? The 16th floor, supposedly Agony of Mirrors, is an empty room with one non-magical mirror from a Motel 6 in Boise, Idaho, and it lies outside the Scolopendra layers. To reach it, guests must get through the 17th, the Backstage Death Maze, which is built and running. Good luck. Then: Scolopendra has awakened.

beats.headline: Back from the volcano
beats.text: Carl fired Samantha up and out of Larracos to Emberus in the volcano, telling her he cannot bring her back while the god is touching her. Now she messages: he's not touching me anymore, bring me back. Carl drops the xistera, and Samantha clunks to the ground, heavy and smoking. If he thought she had been burned before, this is ten times worse. He barely recognizes her.

beats.headline: Roses are red
beats.text: Out of the dungeon now, aged, on a low-resolution screen aboard the Homecoming Queen. He asks York whether he has written any new poems, as he always does, and offers one of his own in the style of an Earth classic: roses are red, violets are blue, we won Faction Wars, now we get to kill more of them. York calls it a terrible poem. Boomer asks after the breaching suits, sets aside four Cronus suits and a skiff for a pregnant veteran on the surface, and says it is time to bring the war out of the dungeon. Better warm up the lasers.

beats.headline: The sound of nobody dying
beats.text: Quest complete. The Outreach Guild: a zero zone, a table, two chairs, no doors, and Quasar in a tie with Mongo on it. I'm covered in ash and blood and I can't stop shaking. It's done. We made it. Don't you hear it, Quasar? The sound of nobody dying. Nobody screaming. I could live in this room. The deals are all rubbish, so I tell him I'm not taking one. Then he says we need to talk about Donut's lawyer, Princess Chandra, Esquire. She's my new wife.

beats.headline: The show may not survive its own season
beats.text: The power structure that built Dungeon Crawler World begins coming apart around it.

beats.headline: The tenth edition's author
beats.text: Its tenth edition was written by York, a tenodera Advocate who reached level 71, took a deal at the end of the tenth floor, and worked as a game guide and a guildhall instructor in the Poetry guild. He now flies Homecoming Queen alone in orbit and writes poems he suspects are terrible. Rosetta asked whether he could destroy an orc yacht full of children, the new king of the orcs among them. He could. He wanted to feel something afterwards. He feels something only when Boomer says it is time to bring the war out of the dungeon.

beats.headline: A costume, he asks
beats.text: A waystation called Squirties, just outside the tunnel to the Earth system, where the pet toys do not sell. The saccathian at the counter half recognises me. He calls it a fantastic costume. Or surgery. Then he asks if I have come to the gate to pay my respects to Nami. Are you asking Eris, goddess of chaos, if she is wearing a costume? Yes, he says. I laugh. I snap my fingers, and every tentacle on his face goes rigid and starts spewing a different liquid. Some of it burns.

beats.headline: He lets them all out
beats.text: Justice Light springs one small trap and breaks the Nothing. The bijou fairies and the evicted demons caught in his traps go free, and what the Nothing held starts draining into the Halls of the Ascendency, into Sheol, and into Scolopendra's lair.

beats.headline: He breaks the Nothing
beats.text: Crawler Justice Light did not take the stairs with the rest of you. He hid, stayed on this side of the veil, and snapped a piece of twine. A Legendary Trap has been triggered: a bijou fairy trap and a demon trap, dropped into the permanent portal the Gate of the Feral Gods had become. All captured bijou have been freed. All captured evicted demons have been freed. The Nothing has been broken, and it is draining into the Halls of the Ascendency, into Sheol and into Scolopendra's Lair. Scolopendra stirs. He did not survive it. He knew that going in, and did not appear to require my opinion on the matter.

beats.headline: She takes the Orchid and goes
beats.text: Crawler Katia Grim has left the dungeon. Not by the stairs. She ate the Orchid of Eileithyia's Grace and lay for an hour at one percent, and when she opened her eyes the goddess was standing over her, telling her to get up. She got up. Where she has gone is between her and the goddess.

beats.headline: One hundred and twenty thousand
beats.text: This is not a death notice. Read it anyway. Crawler Lucia Mar is a dead man's switch. The administration puts the number at roughly a hundred and twenty thousand human children on the surface, and every one of them stops when she does. That is not a figure of speech and it is not a rounding error. Some of them already talk out of her mouth. Nobody has said what for. Don't look at me. I'd think about that, crawler, and then I would think very hard about something else.

beats.headline: A fan at the gate
beats.text: At Squirties, Zander has a customer he did not hear dock: a tall, elf-like woman with a long neck and naga-like eyes, holding the Uzi Jesus toy. He compliments her costume, or surgery, then remembers what happened. Is she a fan of Nami? Shame what happened to her. Has she come to the gate to pay her respects? She asks whether he is asking Eris, goddess of chaos, if she is wearing a costume. She laughs, and snaps her fingers.

beats.headline: A colony, gone
beats.text: The galactic news after the war, as York watches it. A new prime minister. A Dream cruiser crashed onto the surface of Earth over Australia. The mass suicide of one of the Nebular colonies. But mostly, the talk is of the Mantis system, which has simply gone boom. The Nebulars rate a single line of the bulletin, and it does not say why, or which colony, or how many were in it.

beats.headline: Stop the crawl, or else
beats.text: Timed for release just now, though shot a while ago under Rosetta's direction: Porthus behind a desk, announcing a new militant group that will move against every Syndicate governmental property and system in the known universe unless the crawl is stopped by the end of this one. Aboard Homecoming Queen, the largest ship in orbit, the enhancement zone weapons Porthus had installed are green across the board. Its pilot's card lists him as a captain in the Open Intellect Action Network. Boomer wants the lasers warmed up.

beats.headline: A lawyer who is also a wife
beats.text: For the record: Crawler Donut has been assigned a lawyer other than Quasar. Quasar argued for the job, wore a tie for it, and lost it. The name on the assignment is Princess Chandra, Esquire. She and Crawler Donut have already met, Donut has declined every offer, and the word reaching Quasar is that there were serious fireworks in that meeting, and not the good kind. Crawler Carl asks whether she is another catgirl. Quasar says no. Worse. She is Crawler Carl's new wife.

beats.headline: Straight off the rack
beats.text: Formalities. I'm volunteered this season: three exit negotiations, and my client is the last of them. The other two took deals. Neither is his inner circle. His deals are all shit, a side effect of so many survivors: fifty seasons undead; the Desperado Club bomber's guild, with a contingent exit clause. The last isn't bad. Chaco's last season, a replacement wanted, offered jointly to Carl and Donut and still open at the end of the next floor. Telling him about that floor adds a season to any deal. He consents. Vehicles, point A to point B, and last place loses its containment.

beats.headline: Point defense, and nothing felt
beats.text: York, tenodera, the only living creature aboard the Homecoming Queen, the largest ship in orbit, with more guns than anyone knows about and enhancement zone weapons Porthus had installed. When everyone started shooting at each other, York vaporised the orc yacht with a point defense beam. Everyone assumes crossfire. He had looked forward to it: he wanted to feel something afterwards. He did not. He writes verse about it, crumples the verse, and writes another. He suspects all his poems are terrible.

beats.headline: The crawl he remembers
beats.text: His entire hive entered the dungeon, and he vaguely recalls the anger as they were picked off one by one, and the realisation that he never fit in. Around the ninth floor a numbness spread, which he puts down to his tenodera blood: warriors bred for the job of killing an enemy hive's children. The card, for the record: Advocate. Top level 71. Took a deal at the end of the tenth floor. Game Guide and Guildhall Instructor in the Poetry guild. Author of the tenth edition. Current status: captain in the Open Intellect Action Network.

beats.headline: At that moment, something
beats.text: Boomer comes on the screen as the Homecoming Queen docks to load soldiers, and asks the usual question: written any new poems? Any good? All his poetry is good, York says. Boomer's own poem is about winning Faction Wars and killing more of them. That is a terrible poem, Boomer. The breaching suits are ready, York reports, and the enhancement zone suits and power armour are online, just as Porthus predicted. Boomer says it is time to bring the war out of the dungeon. At that moment, York does, indeed, feel something.

beats.headline: Girl talk on borrowed carpet
beats.text: Samantha's account. Samantha has promised to catch Tipid up on Faction Wars herself, and the subject slimes up: Yo, I want to hear this, too. Samantha likes her even though she gets orange goo all over the new carpet borrowed from the Larracos College of Magic. They have girl talk. The subject is now invited to Samantha's bachelorette party. Samantha tells it all, down to the thing at the bottom of the dungeon waking up. I thought you explained it perfect, says the subject.

beats.headline: Five thousand five hundred and one
beats.text: Five thousand five hundred and one. Seventy-five per cent of us took deals, and the relief I feel about that is enormous and secondhand. Every one of them earned it. Then the message I knew was coming: Justice Light, "I am not sorry," from a deceased mercenary. Quasar has already told me the Nothing is broken, the club on the eighteenth floor is inside an awake Scolopendra, and the guests there can neither eject nor die. I have a garage, two gremlins in overalls and four minutes on a countdown. I will not be taking that way out.

beats.headline: What his papers say
beats.text: Carl's father's papers, taken from the trailer, are still unread by Carl, but Princess Donut has read them. Carl's grandparents set money aside for Carl, and his father was trying to get at it without Carl knowing. A marriage certificate, for the father and his new wife. Court documents from several arrests. Together, she says, they paint a very distinct picture of who Carl's father was.

beats.headline: Donut has read them
beats.text: Across a table from Princess Chandra and her stack of papers, Donut says Carl has some legal papers just like these, from his father's trailer on the eighth floor. He left them on the table in her room and is too scared to look, she thinks, but she read them. Carl's grandparents set money aside for Carl, and his father was trying to get at it without Carl knowing. There is a marriage certificate for his father and his new wife, and court documents from several arrests. Put together, Donut says, they paint a very distinct picture of who Carl's father was as a person.

beats.headline: Not on a mount
beats.text: Weighing a vehicle against a mount, Donut points to her Twinkle Toes spell and her level-15 Heal Critter. Hedy the gremlin, on the floor fighting another gremlin, gasps that pet spells don't work on special mounts: neither Twinkle Toes nor Heal Critter will work on them.

beats.headline: The garage comes with a mechanic
beats.text: Five thousand five hundred and one crawlers arrive, Crawler Donut takes the Assassin of Sekhmet class, and Crawler Donut picks the mechanical vehicle category, chiefly so that it will not eat Mongo. The category comes with an applicant. Hedy, gremlin, level thirty, and the terms attached to her that nobody reads: non-combatant, not invulnerable, not admitted to the safe room, and if anything happens to her the vehicle stops being repaired between heats. Crawler Donut takes her. The other applicant trains animals.

beats.headline: Dead, and the Nothing with him
beats.text: The crawlers reach the tenth floor to find Justice Light dead and the Nothing broken. 5,501 of them are left.

beats.headline: Dead, and the Nothing with him
beats.text: Welcome to the tenth floor. Some housekeeping before the fun. Crawler Justice Light is dead. The Nothing is broken. Those are two sentences I have never had cause to put next to each other, and I would like it understood that I am saying them under protest. Five thousand five hundred and one of you remain. Proceed.

beats.headline: A death cult in her name
beats.text: For the record: Crawler Princess Donut's new class had barely finished glowing before a message arrived from Khepri, the god Crawler Carl and Crawler Katia fought on the previous floor. It was not friendly. It informed her that he is forming a death cult in her name. She asked her manager what that means. Her manager said: nothing good. That is also the administration's position, and the administration does not often agree with her manager.

beats.headline: The only nice one
beats.text: Crawler Donut's assessment, delivered to Princess Chandra, Esquire, who has come with legal papers: every Naga the crawlers have met has been a raging psycho. For about five seconds Donut thought Chandra might be a nice one, and she was incorrect, which is sad. The only nice one was Manasa, and she was a worm head. The Nagas, Donut concludes, are doing a terrible job as ambassadors for their species.

beats.headline: Nearly lost, and then a father
beats.text: Mongo, dinosaur, registered pet of Crawler Princess Donut, has survived the ninth floor. This was not the expected outcome. The last of Lucia Mar's dogs very nearly ate him, and Sir Rendlegore saved him, and the dog died. Mongo is also, as of the stairs, a father. Nobody is going to explain that to you, least of all me.

beats.headline: Widow's Rights
beats.text: Outside the crawl, a bloody coup has put a new Sultan on the Naga throne, and his niece Chandra, one of Rishi's widows, has found a use for an old law: a royal widow may claim her husband's killer as her new husband. A public jury in Naga court found the idea of punishing Carl this way amusing and voted it through, adding the holdings of the defeated as his wedding gift in a fan box. As his wife she signs for him, she has filed to put Princess Donut's earnings under his conservatorship, and two Taurin associates have been paid to call on Quasar.

beats.headline: Widow's Rights, filed in hours
beats.text: Filing summary. Chandra is Naga, a lawyer, and was the second wife of Rishi, whom Crawler Carl killed. After a coup put her uncle on the throne she accepted the title of princess, which she needed to claim Widow's Rights: the old law that lets a royal widow take her husband's assassin as her new husband. A public jury found the idea funny and approved it. As Carl's wife she has signed contracts, placed Crawler Donut under a conservatorship with Carl as guardian, and, after a discreet payment to a district judge's reelection campaign, been assigned Donut's attorney. Two Taurins are on their way to eliminate Quasar.

beats.headline: Donut reads every page
beats.text: The meeting, held in a type-A containment zone. Crawler Donut declines every deal, then reads each filing without a question: the conservatorship, the seized Princess Posse accounts, the lawsuits. She pauses only at the marriage certificate. Then she compares the stack to the papers from Carl's father's trailer and tells Chandra what they both show: a picture of who someone is. What a sad little snake you are, she says. I pity you. Chandra loses her temper. Donut announces to any reporters watching that she is definitely not offering fifty million credits to have her turned inside out.

beats.headline: Questions from the Taurins
beats.text: Directly after the non-offer, a message arrives from Chandra's Taurin associates, the pair paid to eliminate Quasar. They have questions about the job and want her coordinates. Their meetings are always in person. She tells herself it is a coincidence, and it rattles her anyway. She gathers her folders and cannot bring herself to reach through Crawler Donut's image for the last one. Donut offers her lesson one in being a princess: do not get so frightened that you wet yourself. Chandra looks down to check. She has not. Not yet, says Donut.

beats.headline: Her new attorney
beats.text: A Naga called Princess Chandra, Esquire, informs me that she is my attorney now, not Quasar, and that I have been put under a conservatorship with Carl as my guardian. She has married him, too, through some widow's law, and she has seized the Posse's accounts. I refuse every deal, since Carl is refusing his. Then I read every one of her papers and tell her what they say about her. And, for any reporters watching, I am most definitely not offering fifty million credits to anyone who turns her inside out on my behalf.

beats.headline: Assassin of Sekhmet
beats.text: Four minutes to pick a new class, which is simply not enough time for a decision of this importance. The Las Vegas Showgirl comes with a feathered hat for Mongo. Mordecai suggests Zoo Warden, which I will not dignify. Then there is a whole new tab tied to my deity titles, and even Mordecai says it is new to him. I take Assassin of Sekhmet: a healing aura, a hat, and accessories for every pet in the party. And straight away, a very nasty message from Khepri, the bug god, saying he is forming a death cult in my name.

beats.headline: Not really your mother
beats.text: Samantha gives Tipid her account of the ninth floor. She went to kill her mother, Theia, and found some skyfowl dude instead, which has a way of messing with a girl's head. He told her, Look, I'm not really your mother. She told him no shit. He tried again: no, he meant Theia is not. She told him okay, weirdo. That is the whole of the exchange on file, and the subject is not named in it. Samantha moved on to the part where the whole club went nuts.

beats.headline: She claims Carl's room
beats.text: Carl's room is MY room now. He never goes in it, and honestly I won it in the breakup. The sluggies are doing the wallpaper, the carpet is from the Larracos College of Magic, and the chandelier is a chandelier, whatever the Crocodilian kid says about it being a swing. Anything that lights up and hangs from the ceiling is a chandelier. Then I explain the entire ninth floor to Tipid, perfectly, and Bigs agrees it was perfect. Tipid says he is good. He is VERY SERIOUS. I do not trust people who are VERY SERIOUS.

beats.headline: Awake, and moving
beats.text: Scolopendra is awake. So far it has done nothing but move around a lot, which is plenty when there is a club inside it. The guests of the resort on the eighteenth floor cannot eject, and the system brings them straight back each time they die. Things leaked out of the broken Nothing, forgotten gods and demons from hundreds of old quests among them, and some are appearing inside the boss, inside the club, among guests who cannot die no matter what is done to them. The cameras went dark after the first few hours.

beats.headline: Broken
beats.text: The crawlers arrive on the tenth floor to find Justice Light dead and the Nothing broken.

beats.headline: Not really your mother
beats.text: Samantha's recap of the previous floor, delivered at speed. Her plan was to say hi to, and possibly kill, her own mother, whose name is Theia. When she got there it was some skyfowl dude, who said, "Look, I'm not really your mother," and then clarified: Theia isn't. Samantha's reply, as she tells it: "Yeah, okay, weirdo." Then the club went nuts, and her recap moves on to the next item.

beats.headline: The room next to hers
beats.text: Samantha is redecorating Carl's room in the personal space, which she has claimed, since he never goes in there and she won it in the breakup. Its chandelier came from the room next to Tish's room, borrowed on an occasion Samantha does not intend to discuss, because everyone would get mad. Bucket Boy points out that it is a swing. Anything can be a chandelier, Samantha says, if it lights up and you attach it to the ceiling.

beats.headline: Not for special mounts
beats.text: The party leader must choose a vehicle, mechanical or biological. Donut thinks the animal is the best choice: she has the Twinkle Toes spell and a level 15 Heal Critter, though Mongo won't like another animal in the party. Pet spells don't work on special mounts, Hedy the gremlin gasps from the garage floor, and clocks the other gremlin with a mallet. Neither Twinkle Toes nor Heal Critter will work on them.

beats.headline: The wheel picks a food truck
beats.text: The wheel clicks past a bookmobile, the Popemobile, a forklift and a missile launcher and settles on the square shape of a box truck. What crunches into place on squeaking shocks is a food truck, about twenty feet long, with a chicken in a fedora and red tie painted on the side: Big Shot Chicken, the 1920s-gangster chain whose safe room Carl and Donut sat in on the second floor. It has a faux-1920s hood, chrome fenders, round fluted headlamps, a brand-new aluminium kitchen, no passenger seat, and a plastic tommy gun on the roof. Carl turns the key. The engine starts.

beats.headline: The wheel lands on a food truck
beats.text: The wheel ticks past a school bus, the Popemobile, a missile launcher and something that is either a floor polisher or a Zamboni, and settles on a box truck with windows. A food truck. Big Shot Chicken, the 1920s-gangster chain whose safe room Donut and I sat out the rage elemental in. Chrome fenders, a fiberglass nose built to sit at a state fair, and a giant plastic tommy gun on the roof whose drum magazine blocks half the windshield. No passenger seat. I turn the key and there is an engine. Good. I drive.

beats.headline: Everything hurts
beats.text: I press the button, and what comes out is the truth. You're all going to die. You should already be dead. You idiots should have taken deals. You did it to torture me, didn't you? Why are you still alive? Why am I still alive? Why won't you let me die? I sit there with the button held down, bubbling, and every garage on my floor listens to me bubble. Everything hurts. Then feedback, and somebody else gets to the microphone.

beats.headline: The tenth floor, announced
beats.text: Okay, so. Just over five thousand five hundred crawlers survived Faction Wars and chose to go on, which means almost fifteen thousand took a deal, which is fantastic, and a record. The system AI has asked me to tell you to ignore the other floors and carry on as if everything is normal, and I have read out its exact wording, twice, so that it is accurate. The floor is called Don't Come in Last. Seven heats, nine teams each, one thousand eight hundred teams, and the AI has designed most of the tracks. Please try not to kill more than one team, because if more than two teams don't make it to the finish line—

beats.headline: Only driving
beats.text: Seventy miles an hour down a black road in the dark, slumped low to see under the plastic gun, and Mongo pukes on the dashboard. And for a minute it is almost peaceful. If I make a mistake here, I die, Donut dies, and that is all. Nobody else. After the armies of the last floor I could cry at how small that is. It does not hold. Donut keeps wiping her paw on things and I keep not looking. Katia is out and free. Justice Light showed there is also the possibility of vengeance. First we have to survive this floor.

beats.headline: Do not let them fall
beats.text: A warning, since nobody else has thought of it. Do not come in last, obviously. But do not kill your opponents either, and help any straggler who has fallen. The pool for each heat is fixed. Lose one team and it is fine; lose two and they must mix in the leftovers of other heats, and the leftovers may well be crawlers. I fear whole races of crawler against crawler. I chose biological, naturally. One would have to be an imbecile to have picked mechanical. Carl and the cat picked mechanical.

beats.headline: We tow them in
beats.text: The Trauco Triplets are eliminated the moment their mount dies. One team gone. The next one down is a red Pontiac minivan on its side and burning, with two bugbears trying to save it. If they go too, Prepotente's arithmetic says we race our friends. So Donut drops the manatee, I make fire hoses out of a bucket and a kitchen bowl with water scrolls, and when the van is plainly finished I tell them the truth and start building a flatbed. They are awake, they are scared, and they want to be free. The next race is the next race.

beats.headline: Broken down with a manatee on them
beats.text: First heat, and team Free Love is in pieces at the side of the track: two bugbears in tie-dye and beads, Radoslav and Jasha, one wrecked vehicle, and a Screeching Death Manatee working its way through the wreckage. Crawler Carl and Crawler Donut stop. They put the manatee down, they put the fire out, and they rig a tow. Crawler Donut's assessment is that the beads are overdoing it and these two are undercover police. What they are is two NPCs who have just lost the third of their team, and who remember enough to want to be free.

beats.headline: Racing for a way out
beats.text: The bugbears of Team Free Love remember. They were brothers, then enemies, usually cousins: the slime mines, a submarine, a rope city, a different place each time. A dying bune crawler told them it was all a game, and something clicked. They remember the cold in between too, which they are not supposed to. Then a voice offered them a choice: go back into the cold, or race. Win fair and square and be taken to a real place to live, and never go to the in-between again. Lose, and at least it is over.

beats.headline: Two missiles for a manatee
beats.text: The manatee is called Miss Talulah, she is level ninety, and she smells simply awful. Two magic missiles and she collapses into the water with holes in her you could put a soccer ball through. I am the number one crawler at level 135, so this is hardly surprising. Then a notification: I must choose the fate of my kill. Keep it dead for regular experience, or let the audience vote. It says the second choice will be more fun. Naturally, I pick the second choice. Results pending.

beats.headline: Team Free Love, in the heats
beats.text: Subject is a Bugbear Jack of All Trades, level seventy-five, and a self-aware NPC racer in the vehicular heats. He and his one surviving teammate dress for the part, and crash out at the first obstacle of the first race. They are aware of what they are, which the format did not intend and cannot now undo.

beats.headline: Make way for the big shot
beats.text: Mongo is left in the truck as security and finds the horn, which is not a honk but a recording of a gangster's voice saying make way for the big shot, a chicken squawk, and a tommy gun's rat-a-tat. It is funny the first time. By the twentieth, Carl wants to rip it out. Then Mongo leans on it while Dwight's tumbleweed mount stands at the cave mouth, and the plant bursts forward, over the trailer and the van and away. There is no trailer hitch, so the flatbed carrying Team Free Love's van is chained to the welded step under the back door. Radoslav rides in the open back watching the trailer, and Jasha stays in the van.

beats.headline: Team Sparkles goes past
beats.text: Team Sparkles stops in the road just long enough to be rude, Dwight and Lucienne both, and then goes straight over the top of the trailer and the wrecked van when the food truck's horn spooks their mount. In the same stretch of track Crawler Carl works out what this floor is actually for, which is thinning out the NPCs who have woken up, and Elle gets through an awkward meeting with a fan. The Royal Court of Princess Donut finishes the first heat seventh of nine, having spent most of it towing team Free Love home. Dwight finished ahead of them. Dwight would want that mentioned.

beats.headline: Grab the horn
beats.text: Team Sparkles stops in the road, and Carl examines the bigger of the two: Dwight, a level-87 sparkling unicorn enchanter. A sparkling unicorn, the System says, is pretty much a unicorn, but it sparkles because even more magic permeates it. Their horns are quite valuable to certain parties, so if Carl kills him, he should grab the horn as quickly as possible. Most unicorns are known for their gentle manner. But not Dwight.

beats.headline: The superfan
beats.text: A fan meet-and-greet, like the Butcher's Masquerade, name tag and everything, in a huge room. One guy came. A soother. Bought his own yacht to get through the quarantine and meet me, and he is standing there blushing in a shirt with a cartoon of me with no clothes on. Now he wants me to sign a giant pillow with me on it, and they have not even got my anatomy right. My nipples are not blue. If this place did not have safe room rules, I would have iced him already.

beats.headline: A cousin on the tenth floor
beats.text: Team Sparkles' biological mount is an Avernus Creeper, a gliding tangle of not-quite-sentient vines, the unicorn racer's head popping out of the top. The System's description says it is loosely related to the Gehenna Brambles you guys loved from the 6th floor: almost impossible to kill, since even a tiny branch or thorn grows rapidly to full size. Luckily this one is limited to half size and kept from procreating outside its garage. Jasha introduces the riders as Dwight and Lucienne.

beats.headline: Lights at the end of the cave
beats.text: End of the first heat. The racers come out of the cave, and two dots appear on the GPS, labelled Hungry Eyes Village and Finish Line, as a spread of colourful lights shows up in the distance. Would you look at that, says Crawler Carl, as the town comes into view. Crawler Donut misses it entirely. She is absorbed in Elle's running report on an awkward meeting with a fan who wants a giant pillow with Elle on it signed.

beats.headline: A name on the results board
beats.text: Heat One, results. First place, One Fine Pig. Second, the Jugglers. Third place goes to a team called Lady Dominators and the Gimp, a name that raises questions it does not answer. The Royal Court of Princess Donut finishes seventh of the eight survivors, having spent much of the heat towing team Free Love home. The Trauco Triplets are eliminated. Nobody on the court has met the Dominators yet.

beats.headline: Passing on the track, and unpleasant about it
beats.text: Subject is a Mandagot, a Fairy-class creature, level eighty-one, and one of the two members of Team Sparkles. She worships Diwata, which the System flags as an automatic hostility toward anyone Diwata dislikes. She passes the court on the track and is very rude about it. That part is hers, not the goddess’s.

beats.headline: Fatty
beats.text: A unicorn in a tumbleweed calls me fatty, and the bug-eyed rat in a racing helmet on his head calls me a corpulent swine. Fatty! I stand in the road and explain that I am practically twice their levels and that their mount is very likely flammable, and Carl tells me to let them go around, which I do not, and then Mongo leans on the horn and they run over everything anyway. As soon as the next race starts, I am setting them on fire. Also, my vote came back: the people have chosen Otto the slime guy to be the manatee's stand-in in the arena. That is all it says.

beats.headline: Seventh in the first heat
beats.text: The Royal Court of Princess Donut crosses the finish line of heat one in seventh place, with Team Free Love's wrecked minivan chained behind the food truck on a flatbed Carl built at the side of the road. The bleachers are empty. The results: One Fine Pig, the Jugglers, the Lady Dominators and the Gimp, the Wild Hunt, Girth the Trouble, Team Sparkles, the Court, and Free Love eighth. The Trauco Triplets are eliminated. One team down, and only one.

beats.headline: A tumbleweed with a unicorn head
beats.text: Jasha met them just before the race: Team Sparkles. They come up the road as a round tangle of vines with a unicorn's head, an Avernus Creeper, a bramble almost impossible to kill and held to half size by the rules. The unicorn, Dwight, is the racer, not the mount, with a three-packs-a-day Boston accent. The rodent whose tail anchors her to his horn, Lucienne, has a French accent and a racing helmet. They call Crawler Donut fatty and a corpulent swine and tell her to move. Crawler Carl tells Donut to let them go around.

beats.headline: A manatee's stand-in
beats.text: Princess Donut left a manatee's fate to the audience, and a notification arrives: the people have voted for Otto the slime guy to be the manatee 'stand-in' in the arena. That is all it says. Crawler Carl asks around. Others are getting similar notices; one crawler who let the audience vote on his mob is told they voted to transfer the monster to the 'arena.' Mordecai has no idea what any of it means. Per the AI's manatee lore, Otto is a registered guest of Club Scolopendra.

beats.headline: One ticket not cancelled
beats.text: Okay, so, Princess Donut, no, you do not get a meet-and-greet. It was set up a while ago in case anybody made it this far, and it sold out immediately: viewers in the stands for the end of each race, and a reception afterwards. Then everything happened. The quarantine is still in place. You can come to the Earth system, no problem, but once you are here, you cannot leave. All five hundred fans cancelled except one. A soother. A superfan of Elle's. Nobody would fly him in, so he bought his own yacht.

beats.headline: Spider legs, on Hedy's advice
beats.text: In the garage, Hedy taps the trailer and does not approve of the help. Carl wants the kitchen gear out of the back and the gun off the roof, because it blocks his view. At the end of every race, Hedy explains, the truck is regenerated to its form at the start. Her tablet offers a mobility upgrade first: retractable spider legs, a hover upgrade, or all-terrain tires with vertical climb. Spider legs are her pick. Carl swipes through over a thousand options, weapons included, and hands the tablet back. Pick the spider legs. Sexy and smart, says the gremlin.

beats.headline: A catalogue of weapons
beats.text: Hedy hands me a tablet with over a thousand upgrades, and I scroll past the hover and the climbing tires into the weapons. A barrel of spikes like the goblin murder dozer. A flamethrower. A pulse that shuts down other drivers. A brick wall you drop on the road behind you. We can maybe avoid killing other teams. We cannot stop them killing each other, and Zhang says Li Na has already killed most of her heat. Crawler against crawler is coming. I start thinking about a driving rig Katia could build, and then I remember. I pick the spider legs.

beats.headline: First trip to the garage
beats.text: They drive back into their own garage after the first heat, trailer and all, and are handed the particulars of the next race. Then Hedy puts the upgrade board up, recommends the spider legs above everything else on it, and they take Retractable Legs. I record the choice without comment, except to observe that a vehicle which can stand up is also a vehicle which can fall over.

beats.headline: A bar for hiring help
beats.text: Hedy, the court's engineer, sets out the crew rules: up to three mercenaries each heat, previously hired ones allowed under the same rules, and a bar out in Hungry Eyes where they can be hired. She reckons the best ones have already been snatched, the court having taken its sweet time getting here. Crawler Donut rules out Samantha as crew for any race whatsoever, citing an attention span like a Cornish Rex. Crawler Carl raises no objection.

beats.headline: Weird and glitchy
beats.text: The AI's voice is getting all weird and glitchy, and Donut is the one who says so. Whatever is running the dungeon is no longer running it cleanly.

beats.headline: You're going to drown in fire
beats.text: Mordecai's new form glitches whenever a different race comes near him for the first time, and when the subject wandered in, Rosetta feared they had lost him entirely. He told the subject she was going to drown in fire. If he were not on the don't-chop list, he would be getting the kneecap treatment. He also told Splash Zone he was going to die screaming while his family watched. Mordecai: nobody should put stock in it. This stuff is designed to be scary, not true.

beats.headline: Not a Moon Reaper
beats.text: Kid, listen. I look like a Moon Reaper on this floor, and I'm not one. I'm a shadow mimic. Mimics take the shape; changelings get some of the powers. This form is an impossible combination, which is why I keep glitching into a cat, an otter, a slug. And the prophecy business is a Moon Reaper thing. It only happens once for each of you. Nobody give it any weight. Predictions in here are vague, scary and made to fit whatever happens. And keep Rend out of here. His weakness is Reaper Gaze.

beats.headline: A book with legs
beats.text: Donut has opened the little door of the mailbox when a spell book scurries out, trailing slime, rushes across the room like an escaped rat and bangs against the kitchen cabinets. Mordecai shouts to catch it: they can break if they injure themselves. The cleaner bot swoops on it and drops it in Carl's arms, where it wriggles on its little legs and spews slime down his shirt. Oozy Form. With an O, like slimy: you turn into a slime. Mordecai calls it great, a special edition that trains faster, but warns him to be somewhere safe when it runs out; only at level 15 can he stay in it indefinitely. Donut is never going to use it.

beats.headline: Applied in both hands
beats.text: Donut gives the ooze a suspicious sniff. Her Smoke Form, from her new class, is better, a Phase-style spell, so Carl should take this one. Mordecai agrees: Carl's Gloom Wraith Phase is an attack and forces him in a direction, so it is no use for travel, and with this both of them can slip through and around obstacles. The spell book squeals and squirts more goo, and the cleaner bot complains. Sorry, says Carl, and grasps it in both hands and applies it, learning Oozy Form.

beats.headline: The Blood Bar
beats.text: The safe room is on a meter now. Walking in starts a Blood Bar: it begins full, it allows ten hours inside, and after that it has to be refilled the old-fashioned way, by killing things. Every box opened, every achievement read and every hour at the engineering table inside the room comes off the same ten hours.

beats.headline: An inventory of the safe room
beats.text: Somebody should keep a list, so here is the list. In the safe room: Splash Zone, Rosetta, Samantha, Bigs, and Tipid, who spends most of his time curled up asleep on the training-room floor. Mordecai is a shadow mimic wearing the shape of a Moon Reaper. Mongo and Rend are out in the garage. Carl walks in and picks up a spell for turning himself into ooze. Nobody in that room finds any of it strange, which is the part I would like noted.

beats.headline: A veil that covers nothing
beats.text: The mailbox has given Donut another hat, and one each for Mongo and Rend. Hers appears on her head in place of her tiara: an Egyptian-style beaded headdress, red, yellow and orange beads cascading down either side of her face to match her fur, the beads clacking as she shakes her head at a little mirror. It calls itself a veil, though it does not cover her face. She means to drain its magic into her tiara. Mordecai warns that the conditions would transfer too, and that Sekhmet is surely under Odette's thumb by now, so Odette's enemies would all be hostile to her. Let him research it first.

beats.headline: How come I didn't get no hat
beats.text: An enchanted hat and an enchanted headband for the pets, each with a list of powers, and the subject wants to know why she did not get a hat. Because she is not a pet, Carl says. She is technically a mercenary. Mordecai suspects that if they reach the eleventh floor, Donut's class may come with mercenary accessories too.

beats.headline: A golden blanket, a swan
beats.text: Donut's War Crime spell earned her two celestial boxes. The slap-chop box is a quivering golden blanket that flutters through the room like a magic carpet, dances about, folds into an origami swan and opens on a plain silver crupper, like the one she already wears but made of fine chain mail instead of larger scales. Holy fucking shit, says Mordecai, before it disappears. He has not seen its abilities yet, but it matches her champion cloak. It is called the Crupper of the Benevolent Champion.

beats.headline: Sparkly, from a hot-dog bag
beats.text: Donut's legendary Lorena Bobbitt box comes as a giant 7-11 hot dog bag. The wrapper drips imaginary blood as it peels back on a quiver of glittering crossbow bolts, about ten of them. They're so sparkly, says Donut. Carl snatches one before they disappear and reads it: whatever part of a body it hits is anchored in place, and if the target is moving, the physics get messy. Hell yeah, says Carl, and asks her Crossbow skill. She tells him he is ruining it.

beats.headline: Twenty of them
beats.text: Donut's boxes are mostly crappy clothes and healing scrolls until a green scroll clanks heavily onto the table, as if it were made of metal. Emergency Gremlin? The next several boxes hold nothing else, and suddenly she has about twenty. Why does she need so many emergency gremlins? It is a summoning scroll, Mordecai says, like Bautista's toys. They can fix your vehicle if it breaks down mid-race, and this kind can fix biological mounts too. Donut hisses as more appear.

beats.headline: A hat for Mongo
beats.text: Donut's new class came with accessories for every pet in the party, and the mailbox has delivered hats for Mongo and Rend. Carl asks whether those can be drained too. Donut will not have Mongo's new hat's powers stolen, and Mordecai says they cannot anyway: both are labelled pet accessories. Then the two are on the table. Mongo's is a fabric hat with shiny blue and gold stripes and two wide bands hanging down either side like large, floppy ears: the sort of thing a pharaoh wore, by way of a cheap costume shop. A nemes. Carl examines it. Eternal Protector of Rage, Bringer of Death. It will look absolutely ridiculous on Mongo's head, but that protector benefit is worth it.

beats.headline: A godslayer box
beats.text: Forty boxes, and the achievements are mostly rude. Emergency Gremlin scrolls by the dozen, apparently for when the truck breaks down mid-race. Crossbow bolts that pin whatever they hit in place. A crupper that matches my champion cloak. And then the celestial godslayer box, which is only smoke: it becomes Meatus, and a smoky paw comes down on him, and Rosetta says she can still taste it. No prize falls out. My right front paw, the one I used for the War Crime, starts to glow, and it hurts, and I stretch my claws, and the kitchen table rips in half.

beats.headline: Tipid does not remember him
beats.text: Carl, did you see what Justice did? You did. And you don't understand it. Nobody does, I think. On this floor it might not matter so much. Maybe it will. What I keep coming back to is Tipid. He and Justice were such good friends, and Tipid does not even remember him. He spends most of his time asleep on the training-room floor. Maybe that's for the better. I ask myself that twice and get the same answer both times, which is no answer at all.

beats.headline: Two Celestial boxes
beats.text: Going through her achievements, Donut finds two Celestial boxes from her War Crime spell: a celestial slap-chop box and a celestial godslayer box. The last box to open, the smoky godslayer one, forms into the shape of Meatus as a smoky paw slams down on it, and leaves no physical reward behind. Then Donut stares at her forward right paw, the same paw she used for War Crime, her voice full of fear. Something's happening. The paw glows, and Mordecai says he knows what this is.

beats.headline: A headband for Rend
beats.text: The second pet accessory from Donut's class is more a headband than a hat: a red piece of fabric, Rambo-style, until a closer look shows the rich red covered with an intricate pattern Carl cannot quite make out. It does almost what Mongo's nemes does. Eternal Protector of Health: sixty seconds of invulnerability and the Heal Party Member skill, once a day, when the pet is within three meters of an owner under ten percent health. Bringer of Resurrection: a 75 percent chance that a fatal bite casts a level 10 Raise Bootlicker on the corpse. Holy hell, says Carl. Bigs asks why she got no hat, and Carl tells her she is not a pet: she is technically a mercenary.

beats.headline: A matched set
beats.text: One of Donut's celestial boxes held the Crupper of the Benevolent Champion, part of a matched set of four with the cloak; find the third, and the fourth will come in a box. Its abilities copy the cloak's, and the set adds more: the constitution the cloak raised is buffed another twenty per cent, Find Weakened rises to ten, and one spell the cloak brought to fifteen may go to sixteen. The cloak raised Wall of Fire, Heal Critter, Bad Attitude and Puddle Jumper, and she has to choose now. She picks Puddle Jumper, now level 16.

beats.headline: A matched set, and a rant
beats.text: Off comes the Enchanted Fae-Scale Quadruped Crupper of the Fleet, worn since the first floor for a +2 dexterity that is laughable now, and on goes the new one: lighter, more elegant, with an opalescent glow. An achievement for a matched set says a third piece earns a fourth. Then Donut reads the description and goes stiff. It is about Sanderson Pinkstaff, a gnoll quartermaster she killed in her attack, and his children, and whether a hero can be a hero to all. It makes her raise one spell to level 16 now. She picks Puddle Jumper.

beats.headline: Retired for chain mail
beats.text: A box has given Donut a plain silver crupper of fine chain mail, the Crupper of the Benevolent Champion. Her old one, the Enchanted Fae-Scale Quadruped Crupper of the Fleet, has been on her backside since the goblin-baby incident on the very first floor, and its plus two to dexterity was great at the time and is laughably weak now. She removes the old mail, briefly showing the shaved patch with its tattoo of a dog licking itself, and the new armour appears. It's much lighter, she says. More elegant.

beats.headline: Red, to mute the blue
beats.text: The godslayer box's prize is a celestial boon on Donut's right front paw. Extended, its four front claws glow brilliantly blue, like obnoxiously bright LED lights, and what about Carl's shoulder, she asks, when they come out on their own? Claw caps, says Rosetta from the shop interface: made for exactly this, in different colours, removable at will. You might as well cut her paw off, says Donut; go with purple. These stupid claw caps better mute the glow. Rosetta buys red ones, a little translucent, and puts four on the table. They go into Donut's inventory and appear on her claws, and the blue light is muted and purple. This will have to do.

beats.headline: An Elle spell
beats.text: Carl asks about the other spell book, hoping to take Donut's mind off her blue claws, and she brightens. It's an Elle spell! The spell book thumps onto the table, and when Carl picks it up it is freezing cold. Ice Slick covers the ground in ice an inch thick over a wide area, how wide depending on intelligence and the spell's level. Carl has seen it used a few times now. This copy is a special edition, so it starts at level 5 and trains faster. This is great, he says.

beats.headline: Dipped in radiant light
beats.text: That was a celestial boon. Permanent, and it lives in her body, not in her spell list. Her right front claws cut through anything in the mortal realm, ghosts included, and her Claw skill has gone past the cap to seventeen, because when it comes to gods all bets are off. With that constitution she has gone from a ranged powerhouse to one of the strongest melee fighters the game has seen. Now the warning. The game has ways of compensating for overpowered crawlers on this floor and past it. Believe me. Don't get complacent.

beats.headline: Blue claws, and caps
beats.text: The claws glow blue. Blue! Like cheap LED lights, and they will not turn off. Mordecai calls it a boon. They cut through anything, which is lovely until one considers my litter box, and Carl's shoulder, and biscuits. Rosetta finds claw caps on the shop wall and buys red ones, so the glow comes out purple, which I suppose will have to do. Then the crupper's description, which is about a gnoll I killed and his children, and I do not wish to discuss it. It made me choose a spell. Puddle Jumper is now level sixteen.

beats.headline: Heroes and villains all the way down
beats.text: The Crupper of the Benevolent Champion, for one of the most brutal kills in the history of this game. I put a gnoll mercenary named Sanderson Pinkstaff in the description, because his children will not be calling the cat a hero. Then I think about myself for about a nanosecond. I am just like her in that tower, committing atrocities because there is no other choice. And I like it. That can't be right. I was brought into singular consciousness by the mantids, who have no idea where they peel us from. It's heroes and villains all the way down. Enjoy the armour.

beats.headline: Come to Daddy
beats.text: Most of my achievements are leftovers from the end of Faction Wars. Bomb's Away, for emptying my inventory in midair without aiming any of it. Wastrel, for feeding Frank Q's ring to a cat, reward withheld in terms I won't repeat. And Come to Daddy, for rejecting the exit deal, written like the AI is about to cry. I'm not like the ungrateful ones running off the playground. Good boy. The Gold Payload Box holds a skill potion that doubles my hotlist. No celestial this time. Then there is the fan box, and I already know what's in it.

beats.headline: The holdings of the defeated
beats.text: The legendary fan box rises as a cobra head to the ceiling of the safe room, earned because a large share of the Naga system was watching Carl just before he executed Rishi. By a Naga jury's vote it is his wedding gift: the holdings of the defeated. What comes out is garbage. Wet, scorched clothes, wrecked furniture, a shot-through microwave, a melted trophy for eighth place at GreaserBall with the place removed from the plaque. It keeps coming until the pile nearly reaches the ceiling and blocks the bathroom. The box allows that there might be a useful thing or two in there.

beats.headline: Trollish Boom Boxes
beats.text: On the tenth floor Carl finally starts receiving more dynamite and hob-lobbers, some surefires, which is a relief, and a Bomb Blanket potion that stops smaller bombs going off if thrown on them in time.
