There is also something new, Trollish Boom Boxes, which are upgraded hob-lobbers: they look like shoeboxes on a stick and are meant to be thrown. Carl wants to play with them in his bomber's studio first.

beats.headline: Still in stock
beats.text: Carl dropped every bomb he carried when he fled out of Larracos, and he needs to restock. All he has left are the big bombs, such as Carl's Doomsday Scenario and the tactical nuke still attached to a robot dog. That reminds him that Samantha also has a nuke hidden up her neck hole, and it has to come out as soon as possible.

beats.headline: The wedding gift arrives
beats.text: The traditional Naga wedding gift is the holdings of the defeated, and the jury put it in a legendary fan box for the groom. Crawler Donut has been waiting for Carl to learn he is married to that stupid lady with the gross nails. Carl opens it in the safe room: a cobra head, from which Rishi's household pours out. Clothes, wrecked furniture, scorched electronics, a shot-through microwave, and a melted participation trophy from a GreaserBall tournament, the placing removed from the plaque. It keeps coming until the pile nearly reaches the ceiling and the room smells of fire. The cleaner bot takes it personally.

beats.headline: Like the Hangover movie
beats.text: One more item of note comes out of a Gold Adventurer Box: a pink backpack thing. Donut sniffs it and says it looks like one of those BabyBjörn baby backpacks from the Hangover movie, and asks whether Carl and his new wife have already had a honeymoon. That is exactly what it is, says Carl, except it only carries quadrupeds. It is for carrying her on his chest, and if he wears it with her buckled in, his Phase or Oozy spell will phase her too. Donut is absolutely not getting in. Does she look like a milk-soaked toddler? Carl laughs. It might come in handy someday.

beats.headline: His belongings arrive in the safe room
beats.text: Housekeeping. Crawler Carl opened a fan box and the entire contents of the late Sultan's inventory landed in the middle of the safe room. Among it: makeup samples for a merchandise line built around Princess Donut, which Princess Donut had not approved, and about which she has a very great deal to say. The cleaner bot has not recovered.

beats.headline: Hotlist Expansion
beats.text: The Gold Payload Box comes as a small WWII-style gravity bomb, and inside it is a skill potion: Hotlist Expansion, which turns a ten-space hotlist into twenty. Carl remembers that when Lucia Mar was conscripted and he examined her, she had an expanded hotlist. Something cool, he thinks, but not earth-shattering.

beats.headline: A second bot, reset
beats.text: The cleaner bot has a disintegration ray. It uses it on the broken kitchen table, beeping with satisfaction at each puff of smoke, and then it faces a mountain of a dead naga's junk and very nearly has a heart attack. Carl hands Mordecai the second cleaner bot, a slightly smaller white one, an old model with blood on it from Architect Houston's operating theater, and asks him to get it working for them before anything valuable gets zapped. Mordecai switches it off to reset it. The two bots beep at each other.

beats.headline: HAT
beats.text: MOTHER has a HAT. Hat is NOT FOOD. Mongo backs UP. Dong puts hat on Mongo anyway. Floppy ears. Hat is fine. Rend gets red one. Fries are FOOD.

beats.headline: Dong does the honours
beats.text: In the garage, while Hedy explains the gremlins who do the bulk of the repairs after a race, Dong Quixote helps Mongo into the hat. Isn't it great, says Donut. The dinosaur looks absolutely ridiculous. Rend starts grunting and bouncing up and down as Donut produces his headband.

beats.headline: Dibs on the makeup
beats.text: A garbage mountain comes out of Carl's snake box, and I call dibs on any makeup before anybody else can open their mouth. I go in. There is a palette with Donut's face on it, which I bring out for her, and she is not nearly as grateful as she should be. Then there is a lipstick from her brand, a colour called Pussy Lips, and it has already been used, which means it is MINE. It is on my lips now. They practically glow. You are welcome, everybody.

beats.headline: Bouncing for it
beats.text: Back in the garage, Rend sits in a circle with Splash Zone, Dong and Mongo, watching Hedy balance a wrench and giggling in his deep baritone, raw French fries falling from his mouth. Donut produces Mongo's Egyptian hat, and Dong helps the dinosaur wear it. Rend starts grunting and bouncing up and down as Donut produces the headband.

beats.headline: Meeting the neighbours
beats.text: Carl and Donut come out of their garage into the Team Roundabout and go round the neighbours, which on this floor means meeting the NPCs who will be trying to survive the same heats. Among them, three Razor Foxes racing as The Wild Hunt, and the one doing the talking is Chiyome. Level eighty. Nunchaku on the belt and throwing stars beside them. I say on the record that I am fond of Razor Foxes. I do not say that about a species very often.

beats.headline: The team roundabout cul-de-sac
beats.text: Through the garage door is the court's team roundabout, officially part of Hungry Eyes: an asphalt cul-de-sac under a red sun, ringed by nine garage doors, eight numbered and one painted with a runny red skull. Manicured grass, tall trees, the smell of cut lawn. The court's door carries a big 7. A truck can leave the garage and go nowhere, and a narrow path leads to a see-through portal onto a neon settlement. The bugbears of team Free Love are out in lawn chairs with peach beer. Safe room rules apply.

beats.headline: The cooler that never empties
beats.text: Subject has survived his first heat and is found in a lawn chair in the Team Roundabout, handing out Busch Light. The van came with a magical cooler that refills itself and teleports back into the van for each race; it is, in his assessment, the only good thing about the van. It always holds three peach-flavored cans that nobody wants, including Crawler Carl and a Razor Fox who works through several of the others. His partner sleeps beside him with his feet in a kiddie pool. Subject's review of the day: a madhouse.

beats.headline: Left on guard duty
beats.text: The garage door opens on a different world, and Donut tells Mongo and Rend to stay behind with Splashy and Dong and guard Hedy. Mongo screams in protest, waving his wings, and Rend, wearing his new headband, complains loudly too. Dong salutes as the door closes.

beats.headline: We don't tell Dong
beats.text: The half-mantaur in the gimp suit waves at us before his garage door comes down, and Donut names him before I do. Dong's friend. Corcunda. They put him here to mess with us, and the way to handle that kind of drama is never to step in it in the first place. So we don't tell Dong. I say that out loud, which is my mistake. The air ripples. New quest: reunite them, part one of two, and part two needs his other half and a fleshmancer. Reward: two stand-ins of our choosing, sent to the arena on the eleventh floor.

beats.headline: Dong's friend, on somebody else's team
beats.text: Genesis and Rapture, two womantaur dominators, make an appearance and go off to the Hairpin bar. The third member of their team is the one that matters here: a half-mantaur, and he is the friend Dong Quixote is always talking about. Corcunda. A quest opens on the spot to put the two of them back in the same room, which is my way of saying production has noticed that a crawler's mercenary is in love and has decided to sell tickets.

beats.headline: One of two womantaur dominators
beats.text: Subject is a Lady Mantaur Dominator, level ninety-five, and one of a pair driving for the Lady Dominators in the heats. She has black hair and a thick American accent that Carl places somewhere around Kentucky. Between the two of them she is the one who does the talking.

beats.headline: Cowboy hats and boots on hands
beats.text: The neighbours arrive. Two womantaurs in sleek white racing suits with a red-and-blue stripe, white cowboy hats, and long black boots on all four lower limbs, which turn out to be a second pair of hands. Genesis, black-haired, level ninety-five, does the talking, in an accent Crawler Carl places in Kentucky. Rapture, freckled and red-haired, chews tobacco and spits. Both are Lady Mantaur Dominators, and unlike every mantaur Carl has met they do not worship Grull but Enyo. Rapture harpoons a rolling beer can to sniff it.

beats.headline: The third member, zipped in
beats.text: In the doorway of garage number three stands the gimp: a figure in a shiny black vinyl bodysuit with a zipper at the mouth, split vertically down the middle, one leg, one side of a face. Half of a mantaur. He waves a top hand before the door lowers. He is Corky, the friend Dong Quixote has been searching for, and he races with the Dominators. A quest opens on the spot to bring the two together.

beats.headline: Of all the ’taurs, this one
beats.text: Centaurs, bisontaurs, rhinotaurs: the dungeon has a long catalogue of things joined at the waist to other things, and this is the entry the System itself flags as peculiar. They turn up from the fourth floor down, and they keep company with Club Vanquisher.

beats.headline: The other womantaur dominator
beats.text: Subject is a Lady Mantaur Dominator, level ninety-five, driving alongside her partner for the Lady Dominators. She has freckled skin and curly red hair and she chews tobacco. She says considerably less than her partner does, which in that vehicle is a structural necessity rather than a personality.

beats.headline: A quest that pays in stand-ins
beats.text: A new quest: reunite Dong Quixote with his best friend in the world, Corcunda, in two parts, the second needing Corcunda's other half and a fleshmancer. The reward is unlike anything else on offer. Two stand-ins of the crawlers' choosing, sent to the Arena on the 11th floor. Nobody yet knows what the Arena is. The prize has been set anyway.

beats.headline: Who goes to the arena
beats.text: Kill certain mobs on this floor and the audience votes. One way, the mob survives and is sent to the arena. The other way, a stand-in goes instead, and the stand-ins are people from outside the dungeon, like the guests at the resort on the eighteenth floor. The arena is on the eleventh floor, and nobody knows anything beyond that. I can't stop thinking about it. The AI dragged Princess Formidable off her own spaceship. Could I pick someone in orbit? A liaison like Harbinger? Prime Minister Victory? Who could I send down there who would do the most damage?

beats.headline: Entrance in the back of the Hairpin
beats.text: Hungry Eyes Vendor Village is a 1980s neon cyberpunk fever dream of a town, with safe room rules switched off in the main square. On the bar street, the biggest sign of all is a pink-and-purple race car over the words The Hairpin, and under it, smaller: Desperado Club entrance in the back. The crawlers are avoiding the place for now. They meet next door instead, at the Lollipop, which has karaoke. Among the temples down another street there is a Club Vanquisher with a black X hung over it, because Carl is permanently banned.

beats.headline: Neon, and eat at your own risk
beats.text: The vendor village proper. Safe room rules do not apply in the main square, and poisoning rules do not apply anywhere. Where most towns in the dungeon run faux-medieval, this one is a 1980s cyberpunk fever dream in pink, teal and purple, mostly gremlins, a few Draconians. Flashing temples, one of them a Club Vanquisher entrance Crawler Carl is banned from. An unsigned storefront, C&W&U, grand opening soon. A bar called the Hairpin, with the Desperado Club entrance in the back, and the Lollipop next door.

beats.headline: The mystery meat at Hungry Eyes
beats.text: Hungry Eyes village, between heats. I am walking with Prepotente when we run into Carl and the cat, and there is a vendor doing mystery meat off a cart at the edge of the square. Prepotente tells me not to, at length. I have a sixth sense about these things, and I ask Heidi, and I eat it anyway. Two sticks. I would like that recorded as the least dangerous mistake I have made anywhere in this dungeon.

beats.headline: Sweety
beats.text: Our mount is named Sweety. She is a Perriso, a large-mount mammal similar to the tapir, big enough to carry me, this oaf, and one or two mercenaries. The oaf calls her a giant elephant pig and says we should have chosen mechanical, because he is a mechanic. He did mention that before I chose. It was irrelevant. Now he is buying mystery meat from a stall with no health inspection certificate, because some foods raise a mount's speed, and I have warned him about gastrointestinal distress. I am, as ever, correct. Observe the sidewalk.

beats.headline: What anyone actually knows
beats.text: Crawler Carl works the chat. Killing certain mobs on this floor offers a choice: take the experience, or let the audience vote. One way, the creature survives and is sent to the arena. The other way, a stand-in is sent, and the stand-ins seem to be people from outside the dungeon ecosystem, like guests of the resort on the eighteenth floor. The arena is on the eleventh floor. Nobody knows anything beyond that. Carl starts wondering who he could drag down there to do the most damage.

beats.headline: Under the table
beats.text: Imani and I drew a military vehicle that handles like a three-legged pig walking backward through a snowstorm, and Florin informs me it is one of the finest troop carriers in the world. Lovely. Under our table, wrapped round the leg, is my one fan, Linus, in his fanny pack and his shirt of me with no clothes on, because that is where little perverts sit when they ask stupid questions. Five hundred tourists were meant to win extra access to their favourite racer after each heat. He is the only one who came, so he wins by default.

beats.headline: A tuk-tuk, and a first place
beats.text: Lucia and I drew a tuk-tuk. We came first in the heat anyway and took three regular upgrades instead of the Golden one: a tech shield, all-terrain and vertical-climb tires, and a GPS upgrade. Lucia is at the garage. Since the dogs went she has been flipping personalities a lot. About seventy per cent of the time she is herself and ready to skewer me. The rest, a random kid. She will not say why she did not take a deal. It is her turn to drive, so I have hired a mercenary. Jurgen says he will make the other team understand. I nod.

beats.headline: The table at the Lollipop
beats.text: The Lollipop, back table. I have a beer, and I slide Carl one, and Donut gets a Shirley Temple with extra cherries. Everyone checks in. Elle and I drew a military troop carrier. Tran is stuck in his garage. Zhang is not here: Li Na isn't really talking to him, and she killed almost every other team in their heat, so next race will show whether Prepotente is right about crawlers racing crawlers. Chris says his big rig is big but slow. Kinda like you, I tell him, and he almost smiles.

beats.headline: Crawler against crawler
beats.text: I have been sick on the sidewalk, and I am better now, mostly. What I want from Florin is Lucia: how she is, where she is, how she is acting. Then I say the serious thing. Come first in every race. And if it ever comes to crawler against crawler, tell me, and I will make certain the other team knows what they are up against, and what has to happen. I will make them understand.

beats.headline: Filed as: tourist
beats.text: Subject presents as a tourist and a devoted follower of one of the crawlers, to a degree that the crawler in question finds difficult. The System’s notice on him reads, in full, "Linus. Tourist." I have checked it twice. That is the entire entry, and entries that short are usually short for a reason.

beats.headline: The lowrider
beats.text: Okay so, our truck is an older Tahoe, which sounds fine, except it's a neon lowrider with like two inches of clearance, so we kept bottoming out. There's a hydraulic system. I didn't know how it worked. Britney says I drive like an American. We came in second-to-last, and we'd have lost if the tentacle guys hadn't gotten eaten, so the audience picked our upgrade, and they picked wheel spinners. They light up the road. It does have a great sound system, though. Tran's stuck in his garage with a hearse and some wrecked spider legs.

beats.headline: Not the run-of-the-mill sort
beats.text: Prepotente puts a glowing treat on the table, one of three from a celestial box, and they are different from the run-of-the-mill enhanced pet biscuit. An enhanced biscuit leaves the result up to chance. This one is an Enriched Pet Biscuit, and it leaves nothing to chance.

beats.headline: Three from a celestial box
beats.text: Prepotente puts a glowing little treat on the table. He got it in a celestial box, one of three, and they are not the run-of-the-mill enhanced biscuit: one is Nothing Special Party Companion, one is Nothing Special, and this one. Carl picks it up. Enriched Pet Biscuit, "The Paramour": a known result, an upright transformation, a reset to level one, crawler status for a dungeon-born pet, and a permanent, incurable charm that makes the eater fall hopelessly in love with whoever fed it to them. Nothing Special makes a creature a dungeon pet in juvenile form. The Party Companion one keeps its existing form and gives no ability to talk.

beats.headline: Absolutely not
beats.text: Prepotente wants advice. Her name is Ragazzaccia, and she was his girlfriend before the dungeon. Absolutely not, says Donut: he will not be turning anyone into a sex slave. With the other two biscuits, he protests, she would stay a regular goat, and it is not called that: it is called Paramour. Donut points out that she would be a level-one crawler, not allowed in a pet carrier or his safe room, and would get hurt. Nobody will like him if he uses that biscuit on anything. Don't use it. Ever. Right, Carl? Carl is still caught up on the biscuit that stops a pet from talking, and wonders aloud whether it is too late to give that one to Donut.

beats.headline: A biscuit and a question about a girl
beats.text: I have a conundrum, and I bring it to the table. Three enriched biscuits came out of a celestial box, and one of them is the Paramour. Her name is Ragazzaccia. She was my girlfriend before the dungeon began, and she is still a goat; the other two biscuits would leave her one. Donut says absolutely not, and says it several times, and offers me rules to live by. She is right. It is too late. I do not have anybody else to ask these things.

beats.headline: Rule number one
beats.text: Prepotente has a biscuit that makes whoever eats it fall hopelessly in love with whoever fed it to them, and he came to me for advice, which was the correct instinct. My advice is absolutely not. She would be level one and stuck with us, and it is a crime against nature besides. So I am compiling him a list of rules to live by. Rule number one: do not use magic to make someone fall in love with you. It is creepy. Rule number two is to stop arguing with me.

beats.headline: Taught to drive in an afternoon
beats.text: Carl has about an afternoon to teach me to drive and we do not have an afternoon. The pedals are in the wrong place for my feet. There are two pedals and I have been told about half of what the right one does. And the navigation talks. It talks constantly, it does not like me, and I have privately decided that the safest policy available to me is to agree with everything Dr. Metcalf says. Zhang is on the chat with news about the other teams. I am not listening to Zhang. I am driving next.

beats.headline: The truck will not be modified
beats.text: Fifteen minutes to the line. I stand in the passenger door and try to tear the tommy gun off the roof with my bare hands, and the dungeon informs me I may not change the stock configuration of my vehicle. Fine. The driver is a crocodile who has driven a cart, the GPS threatens to drown him in a swamp, and the freezer in the back refills itself every ten seconds. Then Zhang's message lands. Tran's team is in his heat. And so it begins.

beats.headline: Somebody finally addresses the navigation
beats.text: Carl is attempting to teach Bucket Boy to drive, which is going exactly as well as you would imagine, and somewhere in the middle of that somebody addresses me directly for the first time. I am the navigation. I am to be called Doctor Metcalf, after Beatrice's fake therapist. Whatever that was, it is my name now and I intend to hold every one of them to it. Princess Donut's guidance to the crew, delivered in capitals over the party chat rather than aloud, is that I have big mean-girl energy and must therefore be handled with care. She is correct on both counts.

beats.headline: Tran's team in our heat
beats.text: Prepotente's theory holds, mostly. Na killed five of the other teams in our heat, so there are four replacements at the starting line. Two are NPC teams. Two are crawler teams, and one of those is Tran's. Na is sitting behind me and not reacting to any of it. I have the reins for this race. I do not know what to do. I put that in the chat the way it is, because there is no better way to say it.

beats.headline: Through their own windshield
beats.text: The plan worked out with Chiyome and the bugbears needs the truck's windshield gone the moment the race starts, so Carl holds a special banger sphere, built to destroy the whole windshield in one hit rather than poke a hole in it. The hail starts light and grows. Hailstones shake the ground, and ice and water cover the glass until he cannot see the lights. Green light. He hurls the sphere through the windshield, which shatters, and the sphere keeps going. Suddenly they can more or less see. In the distance a hailstone the size of a two-story house smashes into the ground.

beats.headline: Black and White at the start line
beats.text: The plan was one kill: Donut roots the womantaur driver with a Danforth bolt, Chiyome's bear does the rest, and nobody else dies, because if a second team goes, all of it was for nothing. Then the hail takes the awning off, Team Sparkles puts a cannon through the car in front of us, Donut never fires, and our one kill is somebody else's. The bugbears' van is playing "Black and White". My mom loved that song. For a moment I just sit there and listen.

beats.headline: In on the plan
beats.text: Chiyome sits in on the plan with Carl, Donut, Radoslav and Jasha: Rapture into Donut's sights, one shot, done with it. It comes apart before a trigger is touched, because Team Sparkles destroys team Girth the Trouble's vehicle and Girth the Trouble is gone off this floor. Chiyome does not complain about the wasted planning, which puts her ahead of most of the field on this course and all of the commentary.

beats.headline: The shot not taken
beats.text: The plan for the start of the second heat has a Danforth bolt in it. Donut's Scorpion's Bite mount forms on her back with Katia's crossbow, and the glowing bolt locks into place on its own with an ominous click. They hope to get it back; there are only ten. At the green light she will root Rapture, the Lady Dominators' driver, in place, and Chiyome's giant bear will smash the car out from under her. Donut has the shot. At the green light she tenses to fire, and pauses: a long tank-like tube has popped out of Team Sparkles' bush, aimed at the muscle car in front of them. It fires, and the car goes straight up into the air.

beats.headline: A cannon out of the bush
beats.text: Green light. A tank barrel slides out of the side of Team Sparkles' pile of vines and fires point blank into the yellow Chevy Bel Air of Girth the Trouble, whose guck elemental had spent the countdown shouting at the unicorn about his horn and his mother. The car goes straight up like a rocket and comes down burning in the ditch. The barrel peels back like something in a cartoon. Girth the Trouble is eliminated. Dwight tells everyone how girlie that was. Then the bush leaves.

beats.headline: A plan with five names on it
beats.text: Carl, Donut, Chiyome, Radoslav and Jasha work out a plan between them: get Rapture into Donut's sights and take the shot. The shot is never fired. Team Sparkles chooses that moment to put a hole through team Girth the Trouble's vehicle, and Girth the Trouble is off this floor for good. Five heads, one plan, nothing to show. Plans on this course have a shelf life measured in seconds, and that one did well to reach the starting line.

beats.headline: A bolt for the driver
beats.text: On the starting line, Donut's target is Rapture, the womantaur driver. Her weapon mount forms on her back with Katia's crossbow, and a glowing Danforth bolt locks into place on its own; they have only ten and hope to get this one back. The plan: when the light turns green, Carl breaks the window, Donut roots the driver in place with the bolt, and Chiyome's giant bear smashes the car aside, so that it moves out from under her.

beats.headline: He drives it through the hail
beats.text: I drove. Hail the size of fists on the shield for the whole of it, and I went slow, and I only screamed twice. At the top of the next hill the other teams are stopped and out of their vehicles, and we pull up slow beside them: the Lady Dominators, and team One Fine Pig, which is two Tigrans, a pig, and a mercenary with a mallet keeping the hail off the lot of them. I know him. Pontiff. He danced at the club until Damascus sent him back to the mercenary market, and he slapped me once for getting in the way of his routine. It stops mattering shortly, because the whole road is stopped anyway. There is a boss sitting across it.

beats.headline: Asleep in the back seat
beats.text: Subject is in the back seat of the Lady Dominators' burgundy GTO at the top of the hill, curled up and hanging out of the side, with an Unconscious notification over his head. He has not fallen asleep during a race. He has been put to sleep, by spell. Crawler Carl walks past him on the way to look at the boss, notes it, and says nothing. His employers have a wide shield over the car.

beats.headline: Returned for cause
beats.text: Bucket Boy sees a Taurin among a group of dancers and knows him at once. His name is Pontiff. He was a dancer, and Damascus sent him back to the mercenary market because he was a dick. Bucket Boy's evidence: Pontiff once slapped him for getting in the way during a routine, in a club with almost nobody in it.

beats.headline: The pig on the back of One Fine Pig
beats.text: Encountered mid-hailstorm, standing in the road beside team One Fine Pig's vehicle. Two tigrans, Nico and Dario, and the third of their throuple, who is a pig. Examined, catalogued, and flagged with the heaviest warning I hand out anywhere on this floor: a thunder god has taken an interest in her, and anyone who harms her is marked for death by him. That single clause turns a farm animal into the most dangerous object on the road, which I would like on record before anybody gets clever.

beats.headline: Hired to guard a pig
beats.text: They hire me to stand in the road with a mallet and keep the weather off a pig. That is the whole job. Nico and Dario are in love with her, the thunder god is in love with her too, so nobody touches Penelope and everybody gets paid. Then another team pulls up slow beside us out of the hail, and there is a young crocodilian at their wheel who knows my face. He should. I knew him at the club. I was not kind to him there, and I have not forgotten it, whatever I told myself at the time.

beats.headline: The pig has a god
beats.text: Team One Fine Pig: two tigrans, Nico and Dario, in a throuple with a pig named Penelope. The interesting line in that file is not the throuple. It is that Penelope is under the protection of Taranis. A god of thunder has taken a personal interest in a pig on a racing team, and every crawler who reads that entry is going to file it somewhere and keep it.

beats.headline: There will always be clues
beats.text: Two province bosses, level 170, squatting on the road like kangaroos that grew spikes, with pouches full of dead joeys and one live engineer wearing a joey. Chiyome sets the other one's pouch alight and it pulls out a burning razor fox, eats him, and heals to full. Its only weak spot is inside the pouch. So I ask Donut to examine the dead joeys. Starvation. And their inventory is just their skin. A skin. There will always be clues.

beats.headline: He used to be an ass
beats.text: Corcunda is strong. So why is he asleep? The womantaurs take too long to answer, and when Genesis asks how I know him, I say we used to work together, which is true. Then the cat tells me Bucket Boy is here and says I slapped him once. I did. Yes, I used to be an ass. I start to give her something to pass on to the kid in case I do not get the chance, and the tiger shouts over it.

beats.headline: Worn over a kangaroo
beats.text: Carl shoves his arms into a stinking costume and pulls the kangaroo head over his own. There is a loud click. His boxers and kneepads are now on the outside of the costume, his jacket still on the inside, his cloak round his neck. Then two warnings: his boxer effects have been negated by the costume, and so have his pedicure effects.

beats.headline: Into the pouch
beats.text: Genesis was supposed to hook me a dead joey. She hooks the engineer through the face instead, so I peel the joey skin off his corpse: protection from acid, a jump skill, twelve hours on the clock, and I cannot walk in it, only hop. So I hop, onto the boss's pouch, and he shoves me in himself. Down through the goo to the bottom, two satchels dropped, then out again on Gloom Wraith Phase and the detonator in the air. It works. A gremlin drops his toolbox on me. I probably deserved that.

beats.headline: Babies for the pouch
beats.text: Prison Pocket wants babies. Carl reads an Emergency Gremlin scroll as Donut reads hers, and he repeats it three more times, and eight bewildered gremlins in overalls stand in the road with their toolboxes, one in goggles, one with one eye, one with a hook for a hand. What're we fixing, boss? The kangaroo dips two in his pouch, and eats more to heal. Carl tries not to feel bad: Imani says they explode when the summoning ends anyway. Afterwards one survivor drops his toolbox on Carl's stomach, tells him to go fuck himself, and times out.

beats.headline: She hooks the engineer instead
beats.text: The arrangement was that the womantaurs fetch Crawler Carl a dead joey out of the boss's pouch with their arm chains. Genesis fires into the pouch and puts the grappling hook through the face of Niels, the upgrade engineer the boss had been keeping in there, killing him outright, and drops the body at Carl's feet. Asked why, she says she was not about to let him have the engineer. Neither engineer in the heat is claimed. Her partner adds that a temporary alliance does not make them stupid.

beats.headline: Two satchels in the pouch
beats.text: Prison Pocket, a level-170 gatekeeper, blocks the road, and Carl's plan goes through his pouch. Carl, dressed as a joey, prepares two hobgoblin big boom satchels in his inventory and hops. Stuffed into the pouch face-first, he claws his way to the bottom and releases both satchels, which start to degrade quickly. He presses his feet against the inside, hops as he activates Gloom Wraith Phase, and hits the detonator in midair. He lands rolling on the asphalt while ice and kangaroo bits rain down round him.

beats.headline: Peeled off the engineer
beats.text: Genesis was supposed to bring Carl a dead joey. She hooks the engineer in Prison Pocket's pouch through the face with her grappling hook instead and drops the body at his feet, so Carl has to pull the kangaroo skin off Niels's corpse. It is stuck fast and burns his hands. It has built-in gloves with long clawed nails and palms padded like a dog's paw. He shoves his arms in and pulls the head over his own, and it clicks. His boxers and kneepads are now outside it, and his boxer and pedicure effects are negated. He turns to run at the boss and falls flat on his face.

beats.headline: Hopping into the pouch
beats.text: So Carl hops. He leaps higher and farther than he expects and lands on the outside of Prison Pocket's pouch, and the boss stuffs him in face-first. The costume's claws drag him down through warm jelly, burning, past bones, more joey corpses and a toolbox, to the bottom, where he releases his two satchels. Then he presses his kangaroo feet against the inside, hops as he phases out, and detonates in midair. When he starts to pull the costume off, the System reminds him it is a timed item.

beats.headline: A burgundy GTO and a hooked engineer
beats.text: Their vehicle is a late-sixties Pontiac GTO convertible in deep burgundy, under a wide, clearly visible shield, with Corky out cold in the back, hanging over the side. In the second heat, working an arrangement with the court against the boss, Genesis is meant to fish a dead joey out of the boss's pouch with her arm chains. She hooks the upgrade engineer inside instead, kills him, and drops him at Crawler Carl's feet: she was not about to let Carl have the engineer. The Dominators finish fifth.

beats.headline: Negated by a costume
beats.text: Inside the stinking kangaroo costume, his boxers and kneepads somehow on the outside of it, Carl gets two warnings at once: his boxer effects have been negated by his costume, and so have his pedicure effects. He pulls a banger sphere from his inventory, praying it will appear outside the costume and not in his hand under the skin. It appears in the paw.

beats.headline: Last in heat two
beats.text: Seventh of seven finishers in Heat Two, behind everyone still racing, with Girth the Trouble the only team eliminated. The court did most of the work on Prison Pocket, spent a small crowd of summoned gremlins doing it, and watched the Pontiac and the armoured truck drive past its leader while he lay in the road. Princess Donut calls it an apt metaphor for what always happens when they do all the heavy lifting. Carl says it could be worse. The costume disagrees.

beats.headline: A mallet blow, delivered
beats.text: The kangaroo boss is level 170 and heals himself by eating gremlins. Carl casts the spell, and the chunky, pig-nosed kid in lederhosen appears with a lollipop of a new colour: Hi, I'm Günter! Pontiff, already in his backswing, wallops him with his glowing mallet and bounces back as if he had hit a wall. Nein, nein, Günter shrieks, and runs straight at the kangaroo, who coos at the baby. When Günter reaches him, the delayed mallet strike lands, and the massive kangaroo flips through the air onto his back.

beats.headline: Outside the kangaroo
beats.text: Carl shoves his arms into the stinking kangaroo costume and pulls its head over his own. There is a loud click and an achievement. His jacket stays on the inside, his cloak flaps round his neck, and his boxers and kneepads are now on the outside of the costume.

beats.headline: The cannon in the bush
beats.text: Second heat, under the awning, Dwight is shouting at Girth the Trouble in the next spot. On green, a tank barrel slides out of the vines and fires point-blank into Girth the Trouble's yellow Bel Air, which goes up like a rocket and comes down burning. Girth the Trouble is eliminated, and the plan the court had built with its allies falls apart before the shot is taken. The bush leaves. Team Sparkles takes first place in the heat.

beats.headline: He tells Dong what he saw
beats.text: We are back in the garage and Hedy is waiting at the door with her arms crossed. I jump out of the truck and tell Dong, because I thought he would want to know and because I did not think about it for long enough, that I saw Corcunda out there, and Pontiff too. Nobody told me not to. I would like it stated, for whatever it is worth, that I was only telling him the truth.

beats.headline: Arms crossed at the garage door
beats.text: Between heats. The garage door goes up and Hedy is standing there with her arms crossed, and she would like to know what they did to her girl, and why last place. The particulars of the next race come through, and then the audience's upgrade vote, which she presents as a kindness to Princess Donut. Across the same garage Bucket Boy jumps out of the truck to tell Dong that he has seen Corcunda. The repairs get done regardless.

beats.headline: Leave the costume on
beats.text: Kid, listen. How high has the costume skill gone? If it's above level three or so, taking that thing off might take a lot of your skin with it. Above five I wouldn't risk it. Six, he says, with a bunch of other skills hanging off it. Then leave it be. Laundry Day will definitely get it off you. You'll get flayed in the process. Most armour isn't physically attached. That one is.

beats.headline: The skin of his vanquished enemies
beats.text: RAWR. Carl comes back from the race wearing a dead kangaroo and hopping, and I love it when a man wears the skin of his vanquished enemies. Can we get an ogre corpse for Louis to wear? Imagine how sexy that would be. Everyone else is being boring about it. Hedy says it has ruined her lady boner, which is her problem. I roll circles around him, snuffling. Also, Carl, when can I take your truck for a spin? Nobody answers that one either.

beats.headline: A note in a gremlin's hand
beats.text: For Carl alone. I send it by a gremlin, who puts it into his costumed hand: a blank invoice from the C&W&U, with a crude drawing on it for anybody watching, and under it words that surface only for his Escape Plan skill. Tell no one. Kill two teams in the next heat. Come when the shop opens after that race, ask for the top-shelf upgrades, and I will explain why. We do not have to be enemies. We want the same thing. I can smuggle friends to the Pineapple Cabaret. Come alone.

beats.headline: Barely responsible for myself
beats.text: Last place, and alive because another team died first. No fuss, no epic fight: we'd just be gone. I lie on the garage floor in a dead kangaroo and look at the gremlin's blood on the ceiling. I thought I was relieved not to be responsible for so many people any more. Now I'm barely responsible for myself. It feels like the day my father put his motorcycle helmet through the fish tank, and every molly died, no matter what I did.

beats.headline: The catchphrase, and what it costs to refuse it
beats.text: It wants the line. I will not give it the line. So I ask it, over the loudspeaker, with the whole floor listening, why it will not simply let me die, and it takes several of my flippers off me for refusing. I am the executive producer of this season. I designed a floor. Somebody write that down.

beats.headline: Word gets round the garage
beats.text: Back in the garage the generated gremlins chitter angrily at Carl, and one flips him off. Donut explains to Hedy that they used some Emergency Gremlin scrolls to distract the boss: a few got dipped in the pouch, a few got eaten, and she wonders how the others even know. To Carl's surprise, Hedy laughs. Serves the little freaks right. They'll still fix the truck true. Probably.

beats.headline: Paws that can feel
beats.text: A generated gremlin leaves the truck, wrench in hand, and Carl is about to hop back from a kneecapping. Instead it hands him a note and runs off. The paper is weirdly warm. Carl unfolds it awkwardly with the costume's kangaroo paws and realises with a start that he can feel its wetness: he has sensation through the paws. It is bizarre enough that he stops to stare at their pads for several seconds.

beats.headline: Special guests, and a stand-in
beats.text: Announcement, read by my mudskipper. The special guest creatures are mine: made for other purposes, never used, left out in the cold. Kill one and you choose experience or an audience vote, and the audience can send the creature on to the eleventh floor or bring a stand-in instead. About eighty percent pick the stand-in. On the eleventh, every surviving crawler works together. It goes quick. There is also a minor issue with some of the gods. Not today. Today, there are still way too many of you. Let the culling begin.

beats.headline: Eighty percent for the stand-in
beats.text: Zev reads the AI's explanation over the loudspeakers. The mobs that offer a vote are special guest creatures: made for other purposes, never used, and left in the cold. Choose vote, and the home audience either sends the creature to the 11th floor or brings a stand-in there, and they know who the stand-in is before they vote. Just about 80% of the votes have favored the stand-in. The eleventh floor itself, she announces, is a parade, a celebration, and a march to the arena.

beats.headline: The Emperator's bomb
beats.text: The Emperator of the Valtay fleet comes through the tunnel gate carrying a system-busting bomb, apparently waiting for the AI to be distracted. It was not distracted. It says so in the middle of a floor announcement, read aloud by a mudskipper who had no idea the text was coming, and adds that it makes no apologies about where that giant suicide bomb just ended up. It does not say where. A creditor who arrives with a bomb has stopped negotiating.

beats.headline: Reading the AI's script
beats.text: Okay, so. Every surviving crawler team has to do at least one show between races, and Carl and Princess Donut are on Plenty of Plenty in a few hours. Cascadia is not feeling well, so I am doing the announcement, and the AI is making me read a script. It changes the text while I am reading it. It plays a trumpet at me. I read it exactly as written. Then it puts Cascadia on the loudspeaker. I am okay. I tell Princess Donut I am okay.

beats.headline: Everything is connected, somehow
beats.text: Akuma. He killed Stalwart, stole the Gate, and left me to deal with Agatha. Now he wants two teams dead and hasn't said why, so I won't do it, not deliberately. The Pineapple Cabaret I've heard once: the AI, wearing Growler Gary, offered "Backstage at the Pineapple Cabaret" to Formidable as a place of banishment, and every place on that list was bad. Samantha's daughter. The Scavenger. Emberus and Geyrun. Prepotente's crystal. It's all connected, and I have no idea what any of it means.

beats.headline: Dong falls ill at the door
beats.text: Dong tries to get inside the Lady Dominators' garage to reach him and goes down ill on the way. He is carried to Imani. The quest ticks over to its second stage anyway, which nobody on that driveway earned. Imani's reading is that this is not any ordinary sickness. Dong is in withdrawal, and the thing he is withdrawing from is the company of his own sentient sock. I record what the healers tell me. I do not always enjoy it.

beats.headline: Down outside a garage door
beats.text: I go to the garage of the Lady Dominators because Corcunda is inside it, and I fall down before I reach the door. They carry me back to our own garage, where I had left Mr. Jefferson, and Imani is sent for. Whatever she tells Carl, she tells him in silence, and nobody tells me. The quest to bring Corcunda's halves together advances a stage regardless. I did not earn that stage.

beats.headline: His greatest shame
beats.text: There is a way to bring him home. A spell split Corcunda in two, long ago, and his other half never cared for me; join the two with a fleshmancer and he is freed from those women and their team. And I must confess why he left. I did not want him to go back to his other half. I was afraid that once the two were whole again, the whole would not like me either. When he went, he asked me to go with him. I did not. It is my greatest shame.

beats.headline: It's the sock
beats.text: Dong goes down outside the other team's garage and everyone assumes the Dominators cast something on him. I wrap him in my wings. There's nothing wrong with him now. What bothers me is where the sock was: he'd left it in our garage. Near it, he's actively healed and his health doesn't go up, which means it's sustaining him. Rosetta and Mordecai don't trust sapient weapons. If he's addicted, I don't know what to do yet. We don't tell him until we have a plan.

beats.headline: The door that stays shut
beats.text: Dong, Bucket Boy and Splash Zone are on the Dominators' driveway, Dong wanting Corky. The door stays closed. Dong goes down on the driveway with a health bar and nothing visible wrong with him, and still calls for Corky. From inside, Genesis tells him to go away, you freak. Rapture adds that Corky says he hates him now. Laughter follows. Dong is carried off to be looked at, and the garage door does not open.

beats.headline: Beer is FOOD
beats.text: Bug-bear man pours BEER. Slug drinks it. Mongo WANTS. MOTHER says NO. Mongo does not stay back. Now floor moves. Tater tots. FOOD. Mongo waves both wings. HAPPY.

beats.headline: Sustaining, or addicted
beats.text: Dong, sitting on his giant stinking nickel sock and muttering about IRAs, is already feeling better. Imani asks whether he had it with him outside. He did not; he left it in the garage. Her read: the other team cast nothing. The sock heals him by proximity without his health going up, which means it is sustaining him, and if he is addicted to it she does not know what to do yet. Donut says it gets bigger every day. Nobody tells Dong. They do not want the sock to panic.

beats.headline: A note under a dirty drawing
beats.text: A blank invoice from C&W&U, a shop that opens after the third heat, carries a crude drawing for the gremlins and, legible only to Crawler Carl's Escape Plan skill, a message from Akuma: kill two teams next heat, visit the shop and ask for top-shelf upgrades, we want the same thing. I can smuggle friends to the Pineapple Cabaret. We can escape this chaos. Come alone. Carl has heard the name exactly once, when the AI offered it to an orc princess as a place of banishment. It is not in the Cookbook.

beats.headline: Under the hood
beats.text: Every food box now comes out liquefied, fish-smelling and burned to a crisp, and Carl still has to eat once a day to keep his buffs. In the suit he cannot reset his foot buff, so it will expire. Nor can he brush his hair, because the hood is firmly attached to his head.

beats.headline: Two brothers, and no more
beats.text: I came over to get away from Elle's fan, Linus, and the slugs find me anyway. Donut asks how many brothers I have, in the present tense, and everyone flinches. I answer it the way it is. Full siblings, two. I was the youngest and the only girl. Then I tell Carl to open his boxes before Donut's blood bar drains, and I go and play, because somebody has to unlock Funky Kong if anyone in this room is ever going to beat Samantha.

beats.headline: Killed by a look
beats.text: Subject shoulders past Jamal into the safe room behind a drunk Mongo, giggling, at the moment Mordecai walks in with an armful of empty potion balls. Mordecai stops in the middle of his sentence, drops the lot, rises into the air, turns to Rend, and speaks in a voice that is deep and ominous and not his usual one: "And now you perish once again. The next time will herald the beginning of the end." Rend drops dead where he stands. Your pet has died.

beats.headline: Victorious again, at Mario Kart
beats.text: VICTORIOUS AGAIN. Mario Kart, Princess Peach, pink motorcycle, the controller in my mouth and the buttons pressed with my tongue, and nobody in this safe room can touch me except Tipid and one large slug. The deal was that the losers become my slaves for all eternity. Apparently the deal was a sick compliment. Fine. One says I am not as psychotic as he first thought. The other says if I were a strawberry he would nibble me. Carl says no threatening. I only mentioned their mothers.

beats.headline: Platinum Hotlist Expansion
beats.text: The Platinum Boss Box for Prison Pocket holds an upgrade potion: Platinum Hotlist Expansion. Carl sends the description to Mordecai and drinks it over the aftertaste of liquefied fish from his broken food box. Twenty hotlist spaces become twenty-five, and a new tab opens for the Contingency skill: up to ten programmable automations, each able to fire several hotlist items at once under conditions he sets. Lucia Mar, he suspects, already has this.

beats.headline: It glitches through an achievement
beats.text: Carl's awards for the kangaroo business arrive in a run, each worse than the last: Weaseler, which unlocks temporary classes while he wears a corpse suit and makes him a Fursuiter; Slip-'n'-slide, which is mostly noises; and Brotein. The AI's voice in his head glitches out several times while delivering Slip-'n'-slide. It has been doing that more and more. Nobody else can hear any of it, which does nothing for how sane he looks shouting at it.

beats.headline: Friend is dead. Friend is not dead.
beats.text: Rend not moving. Mongo stands over Rend and cries. MOTHER says time-out. Then Rend is up. Rend is BIGGER. Mongo dances. Ghoul things at door. Mongo turns too fast. Falls over.

beats.headline: A sixth death, and potatoes
beats.text: Subject rises from the dead on the safe room floor, giggling. It is his sixth death, so he keeps his memories and identity, and he comes back a quarter stronger, bigger, and with a new random weakness added to the list under Reaper Gaze: potatoes. Crawler Carl disputes that it was random. The rest is housekeeping. He cannot stay in the safe room, he cannot be let into the garage, and so he goes back into his carrier until there is something to fight.

beats.headline: A fleshmancer and two ghouls
beats.text: Tipid and I come back from town with a corn dog, a bag of vegetables and news. I think we found a fleshmancer. The performance guild, Tipid believes, is hidden in the bar Carl has already visited, and he will not like what it takes to get in. The mercenaries: two level 25 Jikininki ghouls, which is all they had left. They're undead, so keep Rend away from them. I'd hate for him to take a bite. Donut tells me it's a little late for that.

beats.headline: Half over his eyes
beats.text: Rend giggles as he rises from the dead. It is his sixth death, so he keeps his memories and identity and comes back 25 percent stronger, with a new random weakness: potatoes. Carl shouts at the ceiling that random, his ass. Mongo dances around the awake Rend. The Tummy Acher is bigger now, and the headband from Donut's class has stayed on him, sitting slightly lower and half covering his eyes. He gives a deep giggle and turns to the garage door as if nothing has happened.

beats.headline: The message she does not repeat
beats.text: Pre-show briefing before Plenty of Plenty, delivered flat, the way she delivers everything: nearly every major ship in orbit is now held by the Open Intellect Action Network, and something else has put down on the surface and is standing over the kinder facility, and nobody will say what it is. Then a message reaches her side of the room and she stops talking mid-sentence. I have kept a file on this woman since she first walked two crawlers onto a set and I have never once had cause to log her as afraid. I am logging it now.

beats.headline: They take the orbit
beats.text: Lexis has the news and cannot get to the end of it. The Open Intellect Action Network has taken over every ship in orbit, and a third party she will not name has appeared at the kinder facility and is protecting it, confused. Then a message reaches her, and she stops talking, and she is afraid.

beats.headline: Is Katia okay?
beats.text: A greenroom at the bottom of the ocean and no snacks, which is not how Prepotente described this show. And Lexis is here! She has a minute, she says, so I ask the only thing that matters: is Katia okay? Something strange happened at the kinder facility after Faction Wars. A third party has appeared and is protecting it, and it is confused. She believes Katia is okay. Then her tablet beeps and all the colour goes out of her face, and I do not get to ask anything else.

beats.headline: A headquarters in Florida
beats.text: The Syndicate's presence in the system now runs out of a temporary headquarters on the Eastern Seaboard of North America, with Prime Minister Victory and her staff. They chose an area they believed had minimal surviving native life, somewhere in the state of Florida, and the moment they set down the natives were all over them. Orbit belongs to the Open Intellect Action Network, and Borant has nobody spare to watch the feeds. For now, it is busy.

beats.headline: I am going to level with you
beats.text: Carl. I will level with you. The AI is spread well beyond this solar system. It has killed an entire Mantis system and blown up a group of Valtay-leased manufacturing facilities, and nobody knows how it is feeding itself. Mobs from the dungeon are appearing where they should not. The Plenty control the tunnels, may be the only ones able to shut them off, and have not answered us. So ask Orren's question. He rephrases it, out loud, and the AI lets it go out live.

beats.headline: He asks it on live
beats.text: The goats of the Plenty sentence us to death and then take questions. One explains what Justice did: broke the Nothing and let everything inside it loose into three levels. Then Orren and Victory are in my chat, wanting me to ask about the integrity of the tunnels in their exact words. I rephrase. Does the public know the gods have escaped? That the AI is in their tunnels? That they're in worse danger than us? That they need to run? Out loud. The AI lets it go out.

beats.headline: Unsponsored gods, loose
beats.text: Orren lays out the mechanism. The AI is built never to interfere with the minds of gods, a hard limit meant to stop a mad AI from turning them on everything, and the same system lets sponsors drive them and lets the operators rein in the unsponsored ones on the deeper floors. That second ability has been switched off. A good portion of the unsponsored gods are roaming free, able to manifest only near the tunnel nodes and not for long, and the AI cannot control them either. One stands at the kinder facility.

beats.headline: The trap that broke the Nothing
beats.text: Crawler Carl is among the Caprids, trading question for question, and one of the goats has just told him what Justice Light's trap did to the Nothing. The Prime Minister and I are on the line. We need him to ask a question about the integrity of the tunnelling system, and the reason we need it asked is not something I am cleared to say on an open channel. Crawler Carl has said it on an open channel. All of it. Live. I am going to be in meetings.

beats.headline: The War Crime question
beats.text: A goat judges me worthy and asks which three spells I would combine if I cast War Crime a second time. I stiffen. Then I compose myself, because we are live and I am a professional. It will depend on the circumstances. Nothing is off the table. But I cannot cast it until the twelfth floor, and Carl and I must first get through these next two. The goat nods. I ask whether it is my turn to ask. It says yes, and the table turns to the next goat anyway.

beats.headline: Named by a goat
beats.text: Before the Plenty's judges, Carl asks a question of his own: what exactly did Justice Light do? A jowly goat explains. His trap broke the in-game version of the Nothing and loosed its inhabitants into three levels of the game, some unseen since the very early days of the show. Only the twelfth floor can truly be watched. The fifteenth cannot be seen at all, and of Club Scolopendra there are only brief snippets of slaughter and torture. The dread Kyryap is there, the goat says. So is Krakaren Prime.

beats.headline: A second casting
beats.text: At a table of goats passing judgment, one of the big ones finds Donut worthy and asks her a question: has she given any thought to which three spells she might combine if she cast War Crime a second time? She stiffens, then composes herself. It will depend on the circumstances, she says. Nothing is off the table, but she won't be able to cast it until the twelfth floor, and she and Carl must first get through the next two.

beats.headline: Too dangerous for the herd
beats.text: Victory tells me that was reckless. Please. They knew exactly what would happen when they asked me. The goats stampede out through the wall, and the one who stays, Gamori, the matriarch, judges me: rash, impulsive, loud, a troublemaker, too dangerous to walk amongst the herd. So I ask why they're even here. She bursts into tears. They sponsored us at their partner's behest. The kids love us. I'm best friends with their champion. She knew all of it and told nobody.

beats.headline: He exerts himself
beats.text: Harbinger, liaison, expelled from the herd, teleports into the Plenty's studio carrying an enormous pulse rifle and addresses the matriarch as Mother. He warned her. She did not listen. He has been alone in this, and he is lonely. Exertion, he reminds her, is meant to be an expression of joy. He will exert himself now: protect the herd, protect the universe, and do what should have been done from the start. He raises the rifle at Crawler Carl. The AI intervenes. Everything inside the goat is suddenly outside the goat.

beats.headline: The ratings, dripping
beats.text: When it is over, Lexis has a gun in her hand. She has not fired it. She returns it to a hidden holster on her back, picks her tablet up out of the gore, shakes it, wipes the screen on her sleeve and presses a button. She is covered worse than anyone in the room. The good news, she reports, with innards dripping from her nose, is that the ratings on this episode are the highest they have ever been.

beats.headline: The goats panic on air
beats.text: A live broadcast with the caprid council of the Plenty goes badly. Something Crawler Carl says sets the goats braying, and they begin to cry out, one after another. The Epicure. We shall manifest the Epicure. The True Judgment; she has fulfilled her bargain. The great stampede comes. The beautiful place. Crawler Donut asks in chat whether the Midnight Epicure is the god Prepotente worships. It is, Carl says, and he wears its patch on his own jacket. Are they excited because they think the god is real now? Carl has no clue.

beats.headline: The herd finds out
beats.text: The goats start to panic and faint, certain the end times have come. Gamori, the matriarch, had known all of it and told none of them, because she knew precisely this would happen. Harbinger arrives to point out that he warned her, that he has been protecting the herd the whole time, and that they expelled him for it anyway.

beats.headline: Marked and programmed
beats.text: Heat three, with Gluteus Maxx at the wheel and a dragon-faced Draconian on One Fine Pig's APV manning a heavy machine gun. Carl marks the Draconian with two denial-of-service missiles and the gun with two more, to fire as soon as they are free; he wants that team slowed, not killed. The other four in his eight-pack launcher he programs too. By now every team will have shields, and direct attacks will likely do nothing. This is a Rosetta idea, a different recipe from the potion balls but just as insidious.

beats.headline: Upgraded as requested? No.
beats.text: Starting blocks: each team sealed in a shield that grants the vehicle invulnerability for the first ninety seconds. What sort of shield? How should I know. Had I been upgraded, as I asked, I might. Instead the audience voted the cat a chair that talks, and the chair compliments her fur. The track is shared with migrating sugar hermits, tens of thousands of them. And this driver is worse than the last one. Where do they find these idiots?

beats.headline: Two uppers, and the wheel
beats.text: Chosen to drive heat three because Crawler Carl cannot reach the pedals in a kangaroo and Gluteus Maxx is the best of the strippers at Mario Kart. He drives in a Speedo and a borrowed hockey helmet. At the line his eyes are red. Samantha found outworlder uppers in the garbage pile from the snake guy and says one before a race lets you taste time; it is how she wins at Mario Kart. He took two. It is too late to change drivers.

beats.headline: Too short for the pedals
beats.text: The kangaroo suit makes it hard for Carl to reach the pedals properly, so Gluteus Maxx, the best of the strippers at Mario Kart, drives heat three, and Carl crouches between him and Donut, which is awkward in the suit too. At least it is clean-ish again after the showers. At the line Gluteus admits he has taken two of Samantha's outworlder uppers. Carl asks Donut to get her Laundry Day spell ready and get the suit off him so he can drive. No, says Donut: Mordecai said it could really hurt him, even kill him. Then the ground rumbles.

beats.headline: A throne called Dorota
beats.text: The audience voted me a throne, which shows some of them have taste. It is a Smart Companion Royal Pet Throne, the Ultimate Diamond Pampered Pet Princess edition, and the moment I sit on it a little fluffy bed appears, it holds me steady like a gyro, and it feeds me snacks on demand. It came with a creepy man's voice, so I had it changed to a woman with a Polish accent, and I have named her Dorota. She agrees with everything I say. Dr. Metcalf is jealous.

beats.headline: The princess throne
beats.text: The audience voted Donut a new seat, and Hedy saw to its installation. On the passenger side it looks like a regular bucket seat until Donut sits in it, when a small, fluffy, rectangular bed appears. It is a real product out in the universe, the Ultimate Diamond Pampered Pet Princess edition: it adjusts like a gyro to keep her safe in an accident, monitors her vitals, offers her relief when she is stressed, feeds her snacks on demand and compliments her fur. It came with a creepy man's voice; Donut insisted on a woman with a Polish accent, and named it Dorota. Its existence pisses off Dr. Metcalf.

beats.headline: Luca Di's pasta
beats.text: An entry from Donut's Banquet: Luca Di, a human Pastamancer, final level sixty-two, who gave her his train hat on the fourth floor. His mother had dementia, and they were in the dungeon soon after he wheeled her out of her home. On the third floor she took a Benevento, an elf-like witch, and with her mind repaired they could finally talk. She fell during the bubble level. He tells Donut it is okay to forgive herself for War Crime, and that she saved him and his mother's memory. The drawing is a bent tube of pasta. The spell: Temporary Macaroni, cast at level 14.

beats.headline: Glue and foam
beats.text: Ninety seconds of invulnerability, twenty minutes, thirty kilometres straight down. I swing the two ghoul cages out on Hedy's booms and fire the eight-pack: four Denial of Service missiles at One Fine Pig, four at Team Sparkles. They don't explode. They glue. Three bury the unicorn's shield in green mucus and the bush goes spinning in circles. Then the sugar hermits come in twenty-foot waves, the ghouls throw Biscuit Packs, foam that sets like rock, and Donut puts up a wall of fire a mile long.

beats.headline: Goo, not boom
beats.text: Team Sparkles is rolling far ahead on some sort of rocket. Carl aims the launcher straight up and fires out the back of the speeding truck, and the eight missiles spiral off, four toward One Fine Pig and four toward Sparkles. They are not designed to explode. Three slam into Sparkles' bush, which veers off spinning in panicked circles, its round shield covered in a thick membrane of green slime so they cannot see. Drop the shield and the sludge falls into the vines, which Mordecai insists will slow them to a crawl.

beats.headline: Biscuit Packs
beats.text: Two waves of colourful skulls, each about twenty feet tall, come at the truck from both sides of the road, and one of the two ghouls riding outside the truck starts hurling his potion balls at them. These hold Biscuit Packs, something like the Denial of Service missiles but much thicker. Each ball bursts into a round foam blob about three metres across that hardens in seconds to the consistency of rock. They pop one after another, popcorn-like, snagging dozens of skulls at a time and building a barrier as they go.

beats.headline: A letter from Luca Di
beats.text: An entry in my Banquet Fit for a Princess, from a crawler I do not remember: Luca Di, a Pastamancer, who gave me his train hat on the fourth floor. His mother had dementia. On the third floor she took a race that mended her mind, and they talked, properly, before she fell on the bubble level. He says I saved that for him. He says it is all right to forgive myself for War Crime. The spell he left me is Temporary Macaroni.

beats.headline: Luca Di
beats.text: An entry in Donut's A Banquet Fit for a Princess is Luca Di's: a human Pastamancer, final level 62. You probably don't remember me, Princess, it begins, but I was one of the ones to give you my train hat on the fourth floor. She saved his life, he writes, and the life of his mother, Giulia DiMarco, as well. They never got along when he was growing up, and when her dementia came they placed her in a home. Guilt finally got the best of him, and he went to visit her on that day.

beats.headline: A mile of flame
beats.text: Skulls are flooding the streets ahead of the truck, leaving a narrower and narrower path to the finish line. Donut leans forward and casts her level 15 Wall of Fire, powered up to level 16. A line of flames appears on the passenger's side, running parallel with the truck about thirty feet away, and races ahead far into the distance. The flames go straight up, easily a hundred feet into the air. The line has to be a mile long.

beats.headline: A skull on the fist
beats.text: Mid-race, sugar hermits surge in the gaps between the giant tubes, and a skull comes into the cab through the missing windshield. Carl punches it with his gauntlet and it explodes, but the purple thing living inside the skull is still attached to the metal fist, and it starts to slither, octopus-like, toward his arm. He casts Bang Bro, which electrifies the weapon. The creature drops off, dead, sizzling.

beats.headline: A tunnel of cannelloni
beats.text: Skulls pelt and explode against the shield of the car behind. Carl shouts for macaroni, and the truck's windshield shatters. Donut, who has just taken the spell from her Banquet Fit for a Princess, casts Temporary Macaroni, and a tube of pasta fifteen feet tall and twenty wide appears ahead like the mouth of a highway tunnel. The spell casts at level 14, enhanced to 15, and at that level she can choose its size, shape and direction: uncooked, dried cannelloni, at least a foot thick, ten mana a cast. She chains it into a tunnel, and Gluteus slides the truck inside.

beats.headline: Over the line in the air
beats.text: Gluteus Maxx passes out at the wheel before the finish of heat three. Carl grabs the wheel, Donut rips free of her seat to stamp on the accelerator, and Carl lies on his back across the hood, steering over his shoulders, feet aimed at a kaiju skull. Then Dwight's cannon rips through the side of the truck. It flips and spins like a badly tossed football, clips the GTO and the vine, and all three go over the finish line in the air. The truck lands on its back and spins off. Tater tots, fries and chicken patties are everywhere. First place: the Royal Court.

beats.headline: Feet first into the skull
beats.text: Gluteus is out cold on the wheel with a three-storey beetle skull between us and the finish. I grab the wheel, which means I've driven. Donut takes the pedals. I climb out through the windshield, lie on my back on the hood, activate Daughter's Kiss and aim my kangaroo feet at the skull. Then Dwight's cannon hits us, and the truck, the GTO and the bush all go over the line spinning together. The suit shreds against the road. Both arms, both legs, the pelvis. First place.

beats.headline: The Wild Hunt is eliminated
beats.text: Chiyome reported over the channel that The Wild Hunt was in trouble. Then sugar hermits began falling out of the sky, and Crawler Donut pulled Temporary Macaroni out of her Banquet Fit for a Princess and built a tunnel of it, and Crawler Carl got on the channel to tell Chiyome where to drive. There was no longer anybody to tell. The Wild Hunt is eliminated. The Jugglers with them. The tunnel was a good idea, arriving in the order that good ideas usually arrive in.

beats.headline: Too early over the pigs
beats.text: A message from Chiyome, somewhere behind: the missiles meant for the Fine Pigs detonated too early, and the goo went all over the place, Onikuma included. Her team cannot see, the road is too steep for their Oni, who keeps stumbling, and the Jugglers are somewhere back with them. Carl tells her to move to the right side; they will toss the tunnels if a third wave comes.

beats.headline: The cannon again, at the line
beats.text: Subject comes up on the left in the final seconds with the cannon hanging out of the slime-covered bush and fires across the finish, into the food truck and the Lady Dominators' GTO alike. All three vehicles go over the line together, airborne. The vine survives, smouldering; so do Dwight and Lucienne, whose helmet is cracked. Dwight wants to see everyone cry, and promises that everyone is dead next race and will be shot first. Then the vine limps into the garage marked 2.

beats.headline: Feet first at the skull
beats.text: At the end of heat three Carl lies across the hood, his foot buff run out, and activates Daughter's Kiss, meaning to ram the kaiju skull with his giant feet. Dwight's cannon flips the truck, his feet hit the skull and it explodes, and he lets go of the wheel. He hits the ground and slides, and screams as his kangaroo skin flays off. Afterwards his kangaroo feet are literally on fire, and when he tries to walk on them, he falls over.

beats.headline: Blown over the line
beats.text: In the third heat the Dominators are under the impression that they and the court are working together, and the GTO runs close behind the court's truck for much of the course. At the finish, Team Sparkles comes up on the left and fires its cannon across the line into both the food truck and the GTO. All three vehicles go over the line airborne. The Dominators finish third.

beats.headline: A tunnel of cannelloni
beats.text: I killed more than ten thousand of them and did not go up a level. That is an outrage. Then the skulls come up out of the road and down out of the sky, and I cast Temporary Macaroni, which I have had for about a minute, and I chain it: uncooked cannelloni, a foot thick, a tunnel of it. When Gluteus passes out on the wheel I rip myself free of Dorota's belt and hold the accelerator down with both paws. We win.

beats.headline: First place, in pieces
beats.text: Heat Three: first place, the Royal Court of Princess Donut, which crossed the line upside down in a food truck that is now spread across the road along with its tater tots. Both hired ghouls are dead. The Wild Hunt and the Jugglers are eliminated, two teams gone in the one heat, and a replacement is coming for the empty sixth garage. Gremlins with carts and wheelbarrows come out of garages one and three to collect what is left of the truck.

beats.headline: Fed, and spent on a skull
beats.text: Mid-race the notification lands: the Scavenger's Daughter has been fed; unleash her wrath. The complication is timing. Carl has to spend it before the finish line or carry it until the next race. So it goes into the kaiju skull at the bottom of the hill: Daughter's Kiss, delivered through a pair of dead kangaroo feet by a man lying on his back on the hood of a food truck. The skull explodes.

beats.headline: Arms out of the seat
beats.text: Near the end of the tunnel Donut starts to recast her shield, and the large skull of some orc-like creature crashes through the front and wraps itself around her face like a facehugger. Before anyone can react, multiple arms appear from the car seat and violently rip it off her. The skull and the creature inside are torn to shreds. Thank you, Dorota, Donut sputters. Then, with Gluteus unconscious at the wheel, Donut struggles to get out of the car seat and it holds her tight, so she rips free with her claws, shredding the belt, and slams her paws on the accelerator.

beats.headline: Across the finish, airborne
beats.text: Third heat. Team Sparkles has some sort of rocket fixed to the back of the tumbleweed and rolls far ahead of the pack. At the finish it comes up on the left and fires its cannon across the line into the court's food truck and the Lady Dominators' GTO. All three vehicles go over airborne. The vine survives, smouldering. Team Sparkles finishes second, behind the court, and Dwight promises that everyone is dead next race.

beats.headline: Tem, as scenery
beats.text: The thing blocking the road before the finish line is the skull of Tem, a beetle whose skull alone stands three storeys tall, who resided within the Nothing until a few days ago. Odette wasted him the moment he appeared, and the AI, waste not, want not, has been borrowing parts of the corpse for different races because he was really badass-looking. It suggests the crawlers take note of his size. He has friends who are still alive.

beats.headline: Something riding the fist
beats.text: Mid-race, with Donut chaining a tunnel of giant pasta tubes over the road, the sugar hermits surge through the gaps and a skull lands in the cab through the missing windshield. Carl punches it with the gauntlet. The skull explodes, but the purple thing that lived inside it is still attached to the metal fist, slithering octopus-like around it toward his arm. Carl casts Bang Bro and electrifies the weapon, and the creature drops off, dead and sizzling. The spell he trained on the fourth floor still earns its keep.

beats.headline: I shall drive
beats.text: I ran down to the wreck to speak with Corky, and those women gathered him up and carried him into their garage and pushed me aside without a word. So be it. Carl and the princess both laid hands on the controls in that race, and so neither of them may touch them in the next. I shall drive. He says we will talk about it. What is there to discuss?

beats.headline: A shattered husk, briefing
beats.text: I am in a wheelbarrow. I am a shattered husk. Shocker. Next race, since neither of those two may drive: ninety-nine kilometres of jungle trail, none of it asphalt, one mandatory refuelling stop in the lost jungle city of Upano, acid rain, a containment unit around each crew, three other heats sharing the course, and twenty hours on the clock. I cannot wait to see who they pick. The sex-doll head, perhaps. The dinosaur.

beats.headline: Last again, and still no tires
beats.text: Okay so, we made it, man. Me, Britney, Bautista. Last of the survivors again, which means the audience votes our upgrade again. Our replacement team was more NPCs and we took them out right at the start, no joke. Still no proper tires, though, which is kind of the whole thing with a race. Next track's called Satan's Water Park, and Prepotente's team is on it with us. Honestly? Could be worse.

beats.headline: Prices are double
beats.text: Race preparations. Rosetta sends word that she and Tipid are already in town at the mercenary market, and asks what Crawler Carl needs. A driver and defence, he says, fast reflexes, at least two who can drive, since neither he nor Donut can take the next race. Nobody too crazy. Prices are double, Rosetta warns, because Carl lost the last two mercenaries they hired. Get the best you can, says Carl.

beats.headline: Every team left is a crawler
beats.text: We won again. The teams still in our heat are all crawlers now. One is a fire truck driven by Sammi Harrison, an isopod summoner who was instrumental in keeping the FUPA safe in Faction Wars. Some people call her the decapitator. I think she and the others are conspiring against us. I tell Carl so, as a fact, because it is the thing in front of me.

beats.headline: Triple the price, and he pays it
beats.text: Rosetta and Tipid bring in team Helix: a Grulke named Olga, a Porsuk named Finley with poison on his claws, and a fire fairy named Quemada, three mercenaries for the price of one. They have raced two heats already. Quemada takes one look at the Emberus shrine in the back of the room and decides the fee is now triple. Rosetta says the price was settled with the guild. I ask whether they drove in the last races. Two of them drive. We'll pay the price.

beats.headline: Hands on the front legs
beats.text: Donut tells Jamal he is not hacking down a tree: gentle but firm. He is practising with the new grabbers on his front legs, designed by Mordecai, which make his front spider legs look like they have hands and him look even more terrifying. He holds one brush in each, one on Donut and the screaming one on Carl, both of which give them their daily buffs, and he brushes them inexpertly.

beats.headline: Team Helix, three for one
beats.text: For the record: Rosetta brings in team Helix, a three-for-one mercenary squad that has raced two heats and placed first and second. A level 75 Grulke named Olga, a level 81 Porsuk named Finley, and the subject: a level 96 flaming fire fairy about Crawler Donut's size. Olga says the second place does not count. A demon with chains cheated, killing one of their two clients and their friend Helado. The subject speaks with a thick Spanish accent, worships Emberus, and has not taken her eyes off the bubbling Emberus shrine.

beats.headline: Triple the price, or walk
beats.text: She turns to Crawler Carl and changes her mind. It is not double the price. It is triple. Rosetta objects that the price has been negotiated and paid to the mercenary guild, and it cannot be raised after the fact. It is triple, the subject says, or they walk. Crawler Carl asks whether they drove in the last races. Finley and Olga can both drive; she is protection. Crawler Carl looks at her for a moment, and agrees to pay.

beats.headline: Carl's room is hers now
beats.text: Hey, that was NOT my fault. I told Gluteus about the stuff. He took it on his own. He took too much, and now he owes me money, so if anyone is keeping score, I am the victim here. Also I have a room. It used to be Carl's room, but he never goes in it because he lives in the bathroom, so I redecorated. New wallpaper. The sluggalos say it is badass. Carl has not seen it yet. He is going to LOVE it.

beats.headline: Four ways out of the Emberus problem
beats.text: The Kill Hellik quest has been sitting in the back of my head and I have not planned for it, which is a mistake. The options: kill Hellik, and Emberus has told me to my face he will kill me for it. Don't kill Hellik, or leave the church, and I get smitten. Or kill Emberus, whom I cannot get near without burning to dust, and then every other god wants me dead. Now Eris wants me to ditch him for her. I grab her coin and it burns a swirl into my palm.

beats.headline: The five-sided coin
beats.text: I stop the street, all but Carl, and he says he did not summon me. He thought of me. That is the same thing. I ask for three things: make nice with Akuma, worship me truly when I say so, and let me score his surface a little before I paint it. Then the coin. Donut, RIP. Carl, de-feeted. Most of my friends are dead. I become what they accuse me of. He snatches it out of the air before it lands. The fifth side. Chaos wins again.

beats.headline: Four sides on a coin
