beats.text: Eris spits into her hand and a coin appears, about the size of a poker chip, her laughing face on one side and a swirl on the other. Then she reveals its sides. Donut's face and RIP. Carl de-feeted, with a pair of bloody severed feet. A pile of bodies: Most of my friends are dead. Carl hanging upside down by one foot from a tree branch, smiling, player-killer skulls round the edge: I become what they accuse me of. One of the four has to happen before the Ascendent is chosen. She hands it to Uzi Jesus to flip, and Carl grabs it in midair.

beats.headline: The fifth side
beats.text: The coin burns in Carl's right fist and he does not let go. You picked the fifth side, Eris says, clapping: chaos wins again. The coin dissolves, and on his palm is a swirl pattern tattoo that spins on its own, like a slow-motion Signet tattoo. When he examines it, the System does not know what it is either. The fifth choice, Eris explains, is one of the other four, or two of them, or three, or all of them, or none of them. Chaos. Random. She kisses him on the lips: they will see what he gets.

beats.headline: Open for Eris
beats.text: Eris shows Carl a five-sided coin: one of its results has to happen, she says, and she hands it to Uzi Jesus to flip. Carl panics. The rushing feeling is back, all around him at once, and on his chest the long-dormant Eye of the Bedlam Bride is open, burning a hole in his shirt. He offers to worship her right now if she stops. She wants a true worshipper, she says, and tells Jesus to flip it.

beats.headline: The clock on the order
beats.text: Quemada worships Emberus too, and Quemada's professional opinion is that the standing order cannot sit unattended much longer. They need to make an attempt on Hellik, and soon. Nobody in that conversation raises what Hellik said in the club.

beats.headline: Eris vouches for the door
beats.text: Eris, recruiting, tells Crawler Carl to make nice with Akuma and his head-exploding mages: he really does have a way to crack open the Pineapple Cabaret. Akuma thinks it is his exit ticket, and it is much more than that. The war mages probably turn on the crawlers at the end, she says, but not right away; they need each other. She does not care what happens to them as long as the path to the Cabaret is open, because it is a way for some of Carl's friends to escape.

beats.headline: The unappeasable fire beckons
beats.text: Passing the temple to Club Vanquisher, she whispers that she had a vision. Their lord told her to help any fellow worshipper who was also a racer, and they are tasked with slaying his brother, Hellik: impossible, but they must try. She raised the price because she expects to be slain in the attempt, and the fee is to keep Olga and Finley safe for a while. She has already lost one friend. Her small hand on his shoulder sets his cape smouldering. Prepare yourself, brother. The unappeasable fire beckons.

beats.headline: She opens her eyes for Eris
beats.text: Eris enters the realm and the Scavenger's Daughter opens her eyes and fills with power. The goddess of chaos brings a different effect every time; this one takes a random temporary magic from someone near Carl, not Carl, and makes it permanent. Eris points at Imani and says she will be able to explain it once the goddess has gone.

beats.headline: A goddess in the realm
beats.text: Eris has stopped the world, and Donut hovers in midair, frozen with a yowl. She is wearing her knee pads, which means she has also received a notification that Eris has entered the realm. The last time the goddess came, Donut was unconscious.

beats.headline: A toy on the goddess's shoulder
beats.text: Sighting, Hungry Eyes Village: a small robot of Uzi Jesus, action-figure size, climbing out of a food vendor's storage bin with a meat skewer in his mouth and riding on Eris's shoulder. His halo is on a wire. His Uzi is a toy, or is hoped to be. He wants to go and kill Florin, who gave him up. Eris calls him her little pet and has him flip the coin. Eris tells him they need Florin alive, for now.

beats.headline: An idea he will not say in chat
beats.text: Eris is gone and my heart will not slow down. I write everything into my notes: the four sides of the coin, Britney and the pickaxe, Florin, the Pineapple Cabaret. I have to close the eye on my chest on purpose. We are on rails, playing their game. We have to break it. I have an idea so ridiculous, so completely suicidal, that I dismiss it straight away. Then I tell the group chat everything, and ask them to hear me out on a plan I cannot type the end of.

beats.headline: Shown to the chat
beats.text: Carl writes down everything he saw and heard, starting with the four sides of the coin. Grabbing it unlocked the fifth choice and made everything random, and he wonders whether that made things much worse. Then, back with the others, he holds up his hand to show the swirl and explains it all in chat. The chat explodes. Hanging out with him, Elle writes, is as dangerous as hanging out with Samantha.

beats.headline: Her card will not go back
beats.text: I get a notification: Jacobus is permanently summoned and can no longer be used as a card. I did not summon him. Carl did something. Now there is a fist-sized reverse tooth fairy doing laps around my head in Danish, asking my friends to show him their teeth and pay him three hundred and twenty gold. We are in a safe area. When he goes for Prepotente I catch him in my hand. No. He will not be doing that with any of my friends.

beats.headline: The card that never went away
beats.text: Subject is a Reverse Tooth Fairy, level ninety, and he was a totem card until a patch on the Scavenger’s Daughter made him permanent, which nobody intended. He is tiny, absurdly muscled, blond, and his wings move too fast to see. Imani has him now. The paperwork to reverse it does not exist.

beats.headline: Could he be set free
beats.text: Tenth floor. Imani's fairy card Jacobus has come back as something real, and Crawler Donut did not know cards could be turned real. She almost says something else, and holds it back; Carl is thinking of Paz, whose card was ripped at the end of the eighth floor. What she asks instead: could they set Raul free forever? Crawler Carl doubts it. This was a god thing.

beats.headline: A card made permanent
beats.text: Imani's eighth-floor card, Jacobus the Reverse Tooth Fairy, is out and buzzing in Carl's face. The notice says he is now permanently summoned and can no longer be used as a card, due to something Carl did. Princess Donut did not know cards could be turned real. She and Carl are both thinking of Paz, whose card they ripped, and neither says it. Could Raul be set free? Carl doubts it. This was a god thing.

beats.headline: He said to come alone
beats.text: The upgrade imp is dead on the counter and my note is in his overalls, in crayon, on a kiddie menu. Carl, you were supposed to come alone. He does not come alone. He brings the cat, the goat, three frightened mercenaries and all the rest, disarms my trap, opens my door and tells me anything I say to him I say to everyone. I have my milkshake. I begin to explain how badly he needs me. I do not get to the second sentence.

beats.headline: Behind the yak poster
beats.text: Behind the jukebox at Chicken and Waffles and Upgrades is the room of top-shelf upgrades, and the upgrade imp, Hickster, lies dead on the counter with his eyes burned out, killed by Akuma. A note in black crayon on a kiddie menu calls Carl a moron for not coming alone. Behind a poster of a hairy yak in body armour is a secret door, and attached to the door is a hidden disintegration trap. Carl hops the counter, rips the poster off, deactivates and loots the trap module, scans for more, and opens the door on Akuma.

beats.headline: She crushes one of Akuma's
beats.text: Donut mutes him. That part was planned. The ice bolt to the crotch was mine, and so is the rest. That little magical fart and his friends tried to kill me and stole my Gate before I was done with it. When I was a kid we hit thieves with sticks and threw their shoes in the sound. Now I can freeze a man's balls and break them like dollar store ornaments. That was just the left one. He answers everything Carl asks, or the right one goes too.

beats.headline: Why nothing in the dungeon survives
beats.text: For the record, under an anti-magic shield. The dungeon is out of spare mobs, the NPCs know what they are, and everything inside will be destroyed when the season closes, NPC and indentured crawler alike. The framework is reused; its contents are binned. Our exit is the Pineapple Cabaret, a pocket dimension behind the seventeenth floor, infested since we left it. The Rebellion needs a fighting force. No one who worships a god may enter. I had Carl kill two teams so that the system would set him against his friends. He breaks my nose.

beats.headline: He puts the shotgun to Akuma's head
beats.text: I stay quiet while the mage talks, then I put the shotgun against his head, because he just lied. He left Faction Wars on his own. He can step in and out of floors as he pleases. So why does the most powerful thing in this world need crawlers along? He says to get it out of his face and he'll tell us, and he does. His utopia isn't so much a utopia any more. I knew it.

beats.headline: Akuma names the builders
beats.text: Warlord Akuma, holding court, hands Carl's group a piece of history. Two former crawlers, Herot and Menerva, built the Pineapple Cabaret: a pocket dimension on the same principle as the Nothing, made so that NPCs would have somewhere to go when a floor comes down on top of them. They built it, and then they could not get out of it, and it is infested now, shadow mimics among other things. Akuma's reading is that the surface of Earth can be reached through the place, that crawlers may use it provided they worship nothing, and that the Scavenger's Daughter is the key to the whole business. He declines to say why. I am not permitted to correct him, and I would like that noted.

beats.headline: A name inside somebody else's account
beats.text: The name arrives second-hand, in Warlord Akuma's account of who built the Pineapple Cabaret. Two former crawlers: Herot, and Menerva. They were given the seventeenth floor to build, and behind it they made a pocket dimension for mobs and NPCs to escape into, a thing of the same sort as the Nothing; by his telling the pair of them are forgotten down there, trapped by design. That is the whole of what he offers about her, and Akuma is not a careless speaker. The brevity is a choice. I have nothing in my own files to put beside it, which is itself worth writing down.

beats.headline: What it is, under questioning
beats.text: Akuma, questioned in considerable pain, explains. Many seasons ago two indentured former crawlers asked a showrunner for the job of building the seventeenth floor. The showrunner agreed, was murdered soon after, and never transferred the paperwork, so the two were forgotten: ghosts in the system, rebuilding the floor every season unsupervised. The floor is a front. Attached to it is the only entrance to a pocket dimension they built as an oasis, where mobs and NPCs can escape the dungeon for good. They gave up any chance of leaving to make it. That is the Pineapple Cabaret.

beats.headline: Nobody who worships a god
beats.text: The terms. The Cabaret is not a floor but a separate dimension, like the Nothing, and the rules allow crawlers into it; anyone inside when a floor collapses counts as lost, not killed. With the Gate broken there are two possible ways in: the casinos at the Desperado Club, or something involving the shop interface, which was Herot's idea. And nobody who worships a god may enter. It would bring a smite, and the Cabaret cannot risk being drawn into the Ascendency battles. That rules out Crawler Carl, and most of his friends.

beats.headline: Five left, and a home overrun
beats.text: The war mages had lived in the Pineapple Cabaret. They left deliberately, back to cold storage, to be brought into Faction Wars and find the Scavenger's Daughter, and in the few days they were gone their protection spells failed and it was overrun: shadow mimics, the Ogre Imperium's leftovers, and older things Agatha could wake. There are five of them left. Plan one was more mages, plan two an old ally in the Nothing. Carl is plan three.

beats.headline: Trust, but verify
beats.text: I fist-bump Akuma into my chat and leave him on two percent health. He answers nothing except to say I'm annoying. I don't trust him. But Herot, and Eris swearing he has a way out, keep me on the hook. So: gather volunteers who can fight in the Cabaret, have Prepotente and Mordecai work the shop-interface exploit, send some of the strippers back to the Desperado Club for the other way in. Everything still has to fit between races. I miss bouncing around a map.

beats.headline: The bard potions are brewing
beats.text: Tipid warned me before Carl asked. A karaoke guild, and the needle has to stay in the green for the whole song. So yes, the bard potion. It is brewing now. It will not be ready until just before the next race.

beats.headline: Thrown out for outside drinks
beats.text: Celine Dion first charted in Canada in 1981, in French. Somebody in this bar had to know. I carry perhaps two hundred sodas from the diner, each with a different buff, each with its own straw, and I have told Jurgen he may eat nowhere else. The gremlin behind the counter objects to outside drinks in a drinking establishment. I scream at him. He falls over. I will not frequent an establishment where I am not wanted, so I leave it.

beats.headline: He sings to find the guild
beats.text: Carl slides in next to me at the bar, and I bring up the war mages. Under normal circumstances any of this earns a beating from the AI and the showrunners. I watched Herot's season as a game guide; trust what that little lizard says, find a way to talk to them directly. War mages will use you and kill you. Shadow mimics are the real problem. Then I take the stage in the Lollipop and sing Love Shack, badly. A gauge appears over me. The guild is here. The needle never leaves the red.

beats.headline: A key for the winner
beats.text: Zev's harried voice announces the containment bubbles and the rule change that comes with them: a destroyed vehicle or a killed mount no longer loses the race outright, though last place still does. And from now on, the team that wins is given a key. That key opens a single garage of a defeated team, where there may be supplies to upgrade a vehicle or mount, other items, and in some cases an entire vehicle or mount, which can be added to the team's garage and swapped in at pit stops.

beats.headline: Team Flamengo joins the heat
beats.text: The heat's newest team is a pair of crawlers on Bruna the Slaughter Gnu: Osvaldo, level seventy-two, a Curupira, with Filipe L at the reins and a dwarf mercenary behind. Both worship Tupa, which rules them out of the Pineapple Cabaret. Crawler Carl messages him a careful list of which teams to leave alone and why. His reply, in full: he is not talking to Carl, he will not attack unless it is them or him, and he does not care about the rest.

beats.headline: Easier not to like him
beats.text: The gauge at the Lollipop was clearly broken. I sang Journey and it did not move, and Finley says I did fine, and I thank him. Then Osvaldo is in our heat and tells Carl something extremely vulgar, so I tell him he is only alive because of me and Carl, and he is a straight-to-video leprechaun. Carl says he is not an enemy. He is not going to help us. It is us or him. It will be easier if we stay not liking each other.

beats.headline: She stops talking about Hellik
beats.text: In the village she rides Crawler Carl's shoulder, oblivious to what has just happened to him, giving him a pep talk about dying as a martyr. At the start line of the next heat she is hovering in the back of the truck, strangely depressed. Asked about Crawler Donut's singing, she manages a noncommittal squeak. She has stopped talking about killing Hellik. She keeps raising a finger as if to say something, then changing her mind. Crawler Carl suspects the conversation in the shop with Akuma: NPCs act differently after meeting one fully awakened.

beats.headline: Over its weight capacity
beats.text: Carl is in the seat with Donut on his shoulder, and Dorota does not see why both of them must sit on it at the same time: they exceed its recommended weight capacity. Its breathtaking princess should sit there alone, it whines. Without her it has no purpose, no reason even to exist, and with the nude human added it is unable to function. Carl says he is not naked. Donut asks Dorota to please stop complaining.

beats.headline: The survival containment
beats.text: Hello, racers. Okay, so, this race has survival containment, and there is a rule change, so please listen carefully. The bubble keeps out the air on your next heat, which will kill you. It is indestructible. You lose it only if your vehicle or mount is destroyed, and then, if you survive and cross the line ahead of another team, you can still survive. How that might happen, I don't know. Winners get a key to a defeated team's garage. Other heats share the track. Good luck.

beats.headline: Forty paths and no radar
beats.text: Over forty paths to the pit stop, roughly thirty-five kilometres off. My route: the direct line, veering off before the Temple of the Exploding Snake Goddess, across the I-Sure-Hope-These-Piranhas-Haven't-Learned-to-Fly River, around the southern cannibal village, into Upano. No bosses, no quests. Which place are we in? If I were properly updated I could say. The third GPS upgrade comes with a threat radar. This all comes from an inability to commit, and a fear that decisions are the same as shackles.

beats.headline: Tupa rejects two of them
beats.text: Osvaldo held two: Apito's, looted as Queen Imogen died, and Ysalte's, hunted down in the Faction Wars forest. His god Tupa called the first corrupted and the second wrong as well. Osvaldo's quest has changed with it: he is now to find out why the memorial crystals are not working right. He gave the first one to Prepotente, who has a quest for it of his own, and Carl has one too.

beats.headline: Two crystals, both wrong
beats.text: Asked privately, he answers. His god Tupa wanted a memorial crystal. He took Apito's off Queen Imogen at the moment she died, because otherwise his party would have been smitten, and Tupa said it was corrupted. A second, found in the forest during Faction Wars, was also wrong. He gave the first to Prepotente and was shouted at for not doing it sooner. The second is Ysalte's. Paz was his friend, he adds, and Anton, and Sister Ines. Everyone who meets Carl dies. Now it is their turn, he supposes.

beats.headline: Osvaldo remembers him
beats.text: Twenty seconds before a race, a fire fairy is sobbing about what is real, and Crawler Osvaldo is in Crawler Carl's chat about the crystal he carries: Ysalte, the Vinegar Bitch. The one Paz killed. He was my friend, you know, Osvaldo writes. Paz and Anton and even Sister Ines. He adds that everyone who comes in contact with Carl dies, and supposes it is now his own turn. The lights go from red to yellow.

beats.headline: Are you real
beats.text: On the start line, Crawler Carl feels heat on his shoulder. The subject is floating there, sobbing. Finley asks from the back whether Que is doing okay. She does not know what is real any more. Is this real? Is Crawler Carl real? Is she? Does any of it matter? Over the chat, meanwhile, Osvaldo is naming the god his second memorial crystal is for. Ahead, the floating traffic lights turn from red to yellow.

beats.headline: Crawler Henrietta's team is gone
beats.text: We pull onto the road just as Carl's truck passes, and now we are behind him. Elle is driving, like an old lady. We have lost a team already this heat. Crawler Henrietta, from Angola, new this heat. They hit a trap. It swallowed their mount whole, and she and her partner are gone. Carl sends us his course and asks about the cliff ahead. We have a wall-climbing kit. It is slow. He says he will wait until we are over, so we go.

beats.headline: A fire fairy comes apart
beats.text: Hearing it said out loud does this. Since the back room with Akuma, Quemada the mercenary has gone quiet, then sobbing, then into a full panic in the truck: didn't something break in you when you heard it, Fin? Don't you see what we are? We've been doing this over and over. She asks Emberus to speak to her and begs to end it all. Finley puts her to sleep with a claw and lays her in the sink.

beats.headline: Doing this over and over
beats.text: In the truck it comes on suddenly, a full-blown panic attack, and the cab heats by the moment. Did Finley not hear what that elf mage said? Did nothing break in his small brain? It broke in hers. They have been doing this over and over. Olga explains, sheepish: a panic disorder. Their ice fairy, Helado, used to calm her. After the chain demon killed Helado, the subject killed one of their two clients, until Finley talked her down. Only one of them, Olga adds. She is better now.

beats.headline: Sleep now, friend
beats.text: Entering the forest, she babbles. She is not crazy. Or is she? What can she burn? She begs Emberus to show himself and speak to her and Crawler Carl. Finley grabs her out of the air in both hands. Stop, Fin, she says. Please stop. Let me end it all. He pokes her with one of his claws. Sleep now, friend, he says, gently, and Unconscious appears over her. He lays her carefully in the sink.

beats.headline: New exhausts, a new driver
beats.text: Fourth heat. The tumbleweed arrives with a pair of massive new metallic exhaust ports and Lucienne driving. She screams at nobody in particular, then at the Dominators, and Dwight joins in. The court's plan this time is to kill Team Sparkles, with no specific strategy for doing it, which Crawler Carl is beginning to see as a mistake. At the first split in the track the tumbleweed pulls up beside the court's truck and swerves down the left path.

beats.headline: Cannibals off the bridge
beats.text: Cannibals drop onto the truck and explode against its barrier, and Olga taps a gauge: they are overheating the shield. Donut's claw caps disappear, blue light fills the cab, and she swipes at open air. Her Astral Paw sweeps through the woods ahead, clearing the cannibals off the bridge like pieces off a chessboard; most fly screaming into the jungle. It is nowhere near the size of her War Crime, which she cannot cast again until the twelfth floor, but it is still huge. Whatever was holding the arched tree down snaps, and it catapults the rest the other way.

beats.headline: Off for the Astral Paw
beats.text: Cannibals scream and shake spears from an arch of bent, tied-down tree over the way ahead, and the cannibals dropping onto the truck are overheating its shield. Vaguely racist, Donut mutters. Her claw caps disappear and blue light fills the cab. She swipes into open air, and her Astral Paw sweeps the cannibals off the bridge like pieces off a chessboard; whatever held the arch down snaps and the tree flips up like a catapult. She waves a few more times, clearing the trees. Then she growls with annoyance, her claw caps reappear, and the giant paw dissipates.

beats.headline: It bites
beats.text: Cannibals throw themselves at the truck's shield. Donut's Astral Paw sweeps the bridge clear, far smaller than her War Crime, which she cannot cast again until the twelfth floor; the Paw is stronger now, with an eight-hour cooldown. The combined version with Bijanbi is not a new spell, she says: she can cast the two together. Then she jumps, hits the cab's roof and spins round. She thinks the stupid dog tattoo on her butt just bit her.

beats.headline: A soul returned, a mind still gone
beats.text: Carl's driver goes down Gingered, unconscious, health bleeding out, and he messages me in a panic. Listen. Did you kill the mob that did it? Good. That returns her soul. It does not return her. She needs specialised healing from a cleric, and until she gets it she is in a fugue, staring at nothing. Good thing you have a backup driver. Try to keep that one.

beats.headline: The Astral Paw, and a bite
beats.text: Cannibals, hundreds of them, dropping out of the trees and bursting on our shield. I swipe my Astral Paw and sweep the arch clear like pieces off a chessboard. Elle calls me terrifying, which is fair. It is a lot stronger than it was, but it does not last, and now I cannot cast it for eight hours, and I killed about eighty and did not go up a level, which is ridiculous. Then something bites my bottom. I believe it was the dog tattoo.

beats.headline: The Gingers, lifted from the seventh floor
beats.text: Great Rusty, Cannibal Ginger Chieftain. Another storyline lifted wholesale from the seventh floor that never got built, and I was looking forward to it. The Gingers are from Earth. I only made them cannibals, for the jungle. They can suck out your soul. Two tribes, north and south, at war. Wipe one out and the other rolls over the region, if this race lasted longer than twenty hours. Which it doesn't. Carl calls me prejudiced. The cat blows the chieftain up anyway, and there is a quest now.

beats.headline: Soul Suck
beats.text: On the road into the cannibals' village, a huge man with a staff stands in the way and pulls off his ape-skull mask: a human, balding, red hair in a bone-pinned bun. He starts to chant. Soul Suck has been negated by your Mind Balance skill. Donut is immune anyway, thanks to her constitution and charisma. Carl reads the description and can hardly believe it.

beats.headline: Stuck on the ceiling, afraid of heights
beats.text: Found at the pit stop: Jamal, attached to the roof of the garage, where he has been since many hours before the race began, testing whether his new sticky feet could walk upside down. They could. He cannot get down. Jamal is afraid of heights. He explains that Hedy told him if Carl dies, everyone in the garage simply stops, and that he climbed up to see everything at once, the way the old Jamal did, and now he is scared of what he might lose.

beats.headline: Stuck on the ceiling
beats.text: Jamal is up on the ceiling. He wanted to see whether he could walk upside down with his new and improved sticky feet, and now, he apologizes, he finds himself in quite the inverted conundrum. He is stuck, and has been for quite a bit. Then, talking fast and sad, he says he is happy to have his legs, but he wishes he could just go back to the ocean, and he came up there so he could see everything all at once.

beats.headline: He guards the garage
beats.text: Big box. Sniff. Sniff bumper. BAD. Mongo backs up. Shark on ceiling. Shark comes down. Mongo lies down by shark. MOTHER says stay. Guard Hedy. Mongo stays.

beats.headline: What she tells the shark
beats.text: I Hover up to the ceiling and whisper to him, and he flips down and lands right by the truck. Carl asks what I said. I told him it is true, it could happen at any moment, but if we worry about things we cannot control, we ruin the things we can. And even if he is annoying, he is family now, and he should tell us when he is in trouble, because family helps. Mongo, mind Mommy and guard Hedy.

beats.headline: Carried into the street
beats.text: Quemada, fire fairy, is dead. She never woke. Finley regrets using so strong a sedative; she'll be mad he did not protect Olga. In town he carries the toad in his arms and the subject over his shoulder, on a scorched leather patch strapped to his jacket for carrying her while she is out. He is taking Que to a temple so she does not wake alone. He says they are his family. He steps into the street, and the APV of team One Fine Pig runs all three down, reverses, and runs them down again.

beats.headline: Fists against an armoured door
beats.text: Finley walked out of our garage to go and find his friends a temple and One Fine Pig ran all three of them into the pavement, then backed up and did it again. I storm their garage. Their gun takes out a wall and a bus. I dent the door with my gauntlet until their shield throws me into the street. Imani and Donut pull me away. I sit on the curb in front of what is left. It was a simple act of defiance, and it was snuffed out.

beats.headline: First place, for once
beats.text: Okay so, we're in first place in our heat. For once. Prepotente's in first first. Before the race Bodi went into Hungry Eyes alone and ate, like, a thousand things, and his buffs make Eileen go really fast. Eileen's our lowrider. I didn't name her. Our track is waterslide tubes, and there's this Satan guy who keeps hoping none of the tubes lead to his butthole. Sweety loves the tubes. Also, the bat dudes are selling acid rain protection. Get it before it's gone.

beats.headline: Every squeal, a lightning strike
beats.text: Inside One Fine Pig's armoured vehicle, with Crawler Carl punching the door, Penelope squeals. Each time she does, the sky flashes and lightning cracks, louder each time, from a clear day. Crawler Carl notices. The Tigrans decide she is safest in the truck. The plan is to win and get Penny to the safe place. She is the important one, they say.

beats.headline: A scorch mark on the street
beats.text: Crawler Carl sits at the curb in front of what is left. Finley's legs are gone. Olga's head is caved in. The subject simply poofed out in a flare and left a scorch mark. Crawler Carl asks Crawler Donut to take the corpses, Finley and Olga at least; there is nothing of the subject to take. The crew cannot hire new mercenaries between heats. Crawler Carl sits there thinking how unfair it is: an NPC he barely knew, on his way to help his two friends, and all three snuffed out.

beats.headline: Spoken, not sung
beats.text: Both Tigrans start screaming, and Nico tries to cover the oblivious pig's ears; it would not have mattered. Donut is casting All Eyes on Me, a spell that under normal circumstances requires a song. Her charisma is now so high that she can cast it with spoken words, and after just a few seconds of her talking, her listeners cannot keep their eyes off her. She uses it to tell Penelope and the tigers that they could all use some relationship advice.

beats.headline: Two traps, keyed to Tigrans
beats.text: While Donut talks, I lay a hidden trap on each side of their truck, as close to the shield as I dare. Disintegration traps, like the one I pulled off Akuma's door: silent, one target each, and I set them to fire only for a Tigran, so even if one of them is carrying the pig, she is safe. Five seconds. Imani asks how I'm feeling. I tell her I freaked out, that Donut talked me down, and that I have an idea.

beats.headline: Keyed to Tigrans
beats.text: While Donut talks the twin Tigrans of One Fine Pig into staring at her, with relationship advice for their pig, Carl takes about five seconds to lay a hidden trap on each side of their truck, as close to its shield as he dares. Both are disintegration traps, like the one he looted from the war mage's door. They activate silently and target a single individual, and to be safe he programs both to go off only when stepped on by a Tigran. Even if one is carrying Penelope, she should be safe.

beats.headline: A plan built around not touching her
beats.text: Crawler Carl works out how to take the tigrans off the board without so much as bruising the pig, and Crawler Donut holds their attention in the wrong direction while he sets the traps for it. The entire design of the thing is a constraint: whatever happens here, nobody lays a finger on Penelope. I have watched a great many plans on this course. That is the constraint every one of them should have been built around, and this is the only one that was.

beats.headline: Relationship advice for a pig
beats.text: Carl wants a distraction, so I take the driveway with my headset microphone and address the fake tiger people. My charisma is high enough now that All Eyes on Me works with plain talking, no singing required. I explain to Penelope that throuples in which two members are at each other's throats end in heartbreak, and then Miss Piggy, and Piglet, and Wilbur, and Peppa. They cannot look away. By the time I wave goodbye they do not even know they were charmed.

beats.headline: One Fine Pig is eliminated
beats.text: Two notifications, one after the other. A Tigran dissolved, then the other. One Fine Pig is out, both racers expired, five teams left. I hold my breath, and nothing comes about Penelope. We have drawn Satan's Water Park, an hour behind team Sparkles, with Florin already on it. We need to win the heat, because the winner gets a key, and we need the key, because we need that pig. Florin asks if there's a team I need slowed down. Let me tell you about a unicorn named Dwight.

beats.headline: A pair of notifications
beats.text: At the pit stop, before Carl can announce the crew's new track, the notifications come in a pair. Your trap has activated: he has dissolved a Tigran. Another trap has activated, and he has dissolved another. Team One Fine Pig is eliminated on the expiration of both racers, and five teams remain. Carl holds his breath, waiting for a notification about Penelope the pig. There is none.

beats.headline: In praise of the secretions
beats.text: Half a bottle of the bat creatures' secretions buys about thirty minutes of protection from most environments. It is a superior and versatile product, and I cannot understand why it must be drunk by hand. Louis compares the taste to something from Miami. I would not know. I had the water park tunnels entirely mapped, and now my heat is rolled into the jungle. Sweety will be most upset. Take no wrong turn in those tubes. They come quickly.

beats.headline: Not really splooge
beats.text: At the pit stop Louis brings Carl the bucket he bought for him. It is not really splooge, he says; that is just what they are calling it. It says it is secretions, which he does not think means poop, though it smells like it. The bat dudes sell it. Prepotente will not stop talking about it: a single sip, about half a potion bottle's worth, seems to give half an hour of protection against most environments, though it has to be drunk manually. Because it tastes like Miami swamp ass, says Louis. Donut keeps a good distance from the buckets.

beats.headline: The twist at the pit stop
beats.text: Hi again, everybody. Most of you have made it to your pit stops, so it's time for the twist. Each track has four heats, and each pit stop combines four tracks. Every heat rolls for where it goes next, so your second half may not be on the track you started on. If you were given a quest you have not finished, please do not worry. Quests are mirrored across the tracks and yours will be transferred. You will be able to finish it. Good luck, everybody.

beats.headline: She has no head
beats.text: For the record, the driver of this vehicle is the corpse of a toad, raised for fifteen minutes by the cat's Second Chance, and her head is caved in. The tongue still lolls out of it, bobbing. The route is the River of Sloth, straight past the Gingers' base camp, and I am told everything will be fine. She does not have a head. How is she hearing the commands? I have been told not to think too hard about it. I would like that on the record as well.

beats.headline: Jezebel the hedgehog
beats.text: Satan is a hedgehog, a kaiju-sized one, and I would bet anything he talks with a fake British accent, and I do not care what Carl says, this has nothing to do with Tacoma. Yes, there was a Cutest in Show, and yes, I was a kitten, and yes, the winner was a baby hedgehog from a rescue named Jezebel, and Miss Beatrice sulked all day. It was fixed from the beginning. Who names a hedgehog Jezebel? It hardly matters now. I have raised the toad, head caved in and all, to drive us.

beats.headline: Mehmet's page
beats.text: An entry in the Book of Boom from Mehmet Or, level sixty-two, a Sipahi. He owned a bowling alley in Istanbul that his father left him. He killed his pregnant wife in the hydra. He has taken a deal, and he asks me to forgive the cowardice. His daughters, Azra and Yaz, did not step into the light with him, and he thinks they are with the children. If I cannot save him, find them and tell them he loved them. Associated spell: Gutter Bumper. I never met him.

beats.headline: Mehmet's page
beats.text: An entry in the Book of Boom: Mehmet Or, a human Sipahi, final level sixty-two. He owned a bowling alley in Istanbul, left to him by his father. He asks Carl to forgive him for taking a deal; he has too much to lose. His daughters, Azra and Yaz, did not step into the light with him, and he believes they are alive where the children are kept. If Carl cannot save those who took deals, please find them and tell them their father loves them. His party's mage loved this spell. The drawing is an amateur bowling alley. The spell: Gutter Bumper, cast at level 9.

beats.headline: Harrying the unicorn down the tubes
beats.text: Team Sparkles and us, all the way down the track. Lucia Prime is back in the body and driving, and I'm keeping her from actually killing the unicorn and Lucienne. At the drop in the middle I let the trap go on purpose, so everyone behind gets an hour in the basement. Now I have to backtrack for the loop. The unicorn's going for it too. I have Denial of Service missiles, and I'll hit them just as they start it.

beats.headline: Ice, chains and rodents
beats.text: The River of Sloth is packed with Gingers on inner tubes, and Maurice is somewhere among them. I cast Mehmet's Gutter Bumper along the river, and Donut's Ice Slick follows the lines and freezes the lot solid. We drive over the ice dragging every spare weapon I own on chains behind the truck, then Donut casts Summon Ye, Vermin and the zipper shrews drill through whoever is left, Maurice included. Quest complete. People like Mehmet, who buffed everyone else and saved lives, are the real heroes here.

beats.headline: Bumpers away
beats.text: Rolling toward the raft, Carl has already eaten Mehmet's page. He casts Gutter Bumper, clicks on the river ahead, is warned that it will not cover the whole river, and deploys. Donut casts Ice Slick, and the river freezes along the bumpers in a winding line, half again as far as the cone would reach. It is not the explosive magic Carl is always hunting for, but here it is perfect. He never met Mehmet. He has heard of him: a support player who saved countless lives in Faction Wars.

beats.headline: Goo on the loop
beats.text: In Satan's Water Park, Florin has Denial of Service missiles too, and has said he will hit Team Sparkles just as they start the loop-de-loop: too slow, and they drop out and start again. Now they are on his tail and about to bump him, so he fires. When Satan headbutts the whole loop over and both vehicles come tumbling down near the food truck, the Sparkles vine is on fire and covered with goo.

beats.headline: A frozen river
beats.text: The raft waits on the River of Sloth, which is full of inner-tube gingers. Carl, who has eaten Mehmet's page from his Book of Boom, lays Gutter Bumper along the river. Donut leans forward and casts Ice Slick, and in seconds the whole river freezes, cracking, splitting and exploding, the ice following the bumpers half as far again as it would reach in its usual cone. Hundreds of gingers are stuck in place. The truck drives over the dock and onto the ice, dragging every spare non-magical weapon from Carl's inventory behind it on chains.

beats.headline: Pulled in by the vermin spell
beats.text: Crawler Princess Donut's Summon Ye, Vermin draws every rodent in the area to her. Lucienne, driver for team Sparkles, qualifies. She arrives on the hood of the court's truck, charmed, choking on the park's air, beating her helmeted head on the windshield to get in. The finish line does not allow passage outside one's conveyance. The barrier pushes her through the glass, and through Crawler Carl, and she comes apart. That is the end of Lucienne.

beats.headline: Does your dad own a bowling alley?
beats.text: Lucia Mar's manner changes in an instant, shoulders hunched and afraid, and she grabs Carl by the shirt. A shining lady has told her that Carl knows her father, that he gave Carl a spell. Her name is Azra, and Yaz is here too, crying, while the goddess tells them Carl used their father's spell to win his races. Carl remembers the note in the Book of Boom he ate for the Bumper spell. Does your dad own a bowling alley? Yes, that's him. He is safe, Carl tells her, and he loves her.

beats.headline: Here, says Lucia
beats.text: For the record: Crawler Carl's Scavenger's Daughter patch blinks, not knowing what it sees, and Lucia Mar crosses from her moped to him in a blink and whispers in his ear. Chalchiuhtlicue is here. She is new to this place, and she does not need Cici or Gus the way the Residual and the Primal did. She tells the children she is kind and means to protect them, and that the kindest thing may be to let them die. More are coming. The veins are open. All seek the prize on the twelfth floor. Then the presence is gone, and the patch shudders in fear.

beats.headline: The shining lady talks to Yaz
beats.text: When the presence withdraws, a frightened child surfaces in Lucia's body instead: Azra, whose sister Yaz is here too, crying. The shining lady, Azra says, is talking to Yaz, telling her Crawler Carl won his races with a spell their father gave him. Their father owns a bowling alley. The angel lady, Azra says, thinks it might be better if they all die, and keeps talking about people coming to take their bodies. It is so cold. Florin asks who is coming. Azra notices him, shrieks, and runs.

beats.headline: Carl asks him, of everyone
beats.text: The Royal Court of Princess Donut takes the heat, with the Lady Dominators and Crawler Osvaldo's crew close behind it, and the first thing Crawler Carl does with the win is send a message to Jasha: there is somebody still out on the track who can be pulled off it. Jasha asks whether he truly means to save that one, the worst of them. Tow him in if he will let you, Crawler Carl says, and be wary. I file the request itself, because who a crawler asks is a fact about the crawler.

beats.headline: Second, and a grudge
beats.text: Heat Four. Team Sparkles screams at them from the starting line, and Crawler Carl judges they very likely hold a grudge over the blast at the last finish, which puts Corky at risk. The GTO takes the same trail as the court, and Genesis, in the passenger seat, gives the truck a four-armed obscene gesture on the way past. In Satan's Water Park they trade blows with the unicorn at the loop. The Dominators finish second.

beats.headline: Chalchiuhtlicue is here
beats.text: I look at the man and the cat. Then I am close to him, closer than he likes. Chalchiuhtlicue is here. She is new. She says she is kind and she will protect us. She says the kindest thing may be letting us die. We are vessels in the river, and so is he. The veins are open. Everything trapped is coming, for the prize on the twelfth floor. It is not a game like they told me. It is not a game like they told him.

beats.headline: Azra asks for her father
beats.text: Lucia steps back, shrinks, and somebody else is looking out of her face. A girl, Azra, with her sister Yaz beside her, crying: the shining lady says Carl knows her father, that he gave Carl a spell. He owns a bowling alley. Carl tells her he is safe and loves her. She says the angel lady keeps talking about people coming to take their bodies, and that it is cold. When Florin asks who, she runs.

beats.headline: First in heat four
beats.text: Heat Four. First place, the Royal Court of Princess Donut, driven for the last stretch by a dead camel, after a run of clockwork toads. Second, the Lady Dominators and the Gimp. Third, Team Flamengo. Fourth, Team Free Love. Fifth, team Sparkles. One Fine Pig is eliminated. The next track is a screw factory, steel mill and doll workshop, and containment theft is now on.

beats.headline: Swatted off the loop
beats.text: In Satan's Water Park Team Sparkles and Florin's team harass each other all the way down, Florin trying to stop his driver, Lucia Mar's psycho personality, from killing them. Both vehicles are nearly round the loop-de-loop when Satan headbutts it over and swats them through the air. The vine, on fire and covered in goo from a Denial of Service missile, splats to the ground. Lucienne, charmed by Crawler Donut's vermin spell, comes apart passing through the court's windshield at the finish. Team Sparkles finishes fifth.

beats.headline: Five teams of twenty-four
beats.text: If this is my last message, know that I tried to stop them fighting Li Na. I tried. Then, after: I'm alive. We won. Zhang was leading their octopus and let me pass. They tried to stop her, and it went the way it went in Beijing. She cast a dread and they killed each other. Of twenty-four teams that started, five are left. From our heat, only my team and theirs. Zhang needs help. He was sobbing. I don't know what to do.

beats.headline: Two Golden upgrades
beats.text: After the fourth heat there are two Golden upgrades to pick, and the next track needs vertical climb, inverted racing and gaps of more than a hundred metres. Hedy suggests one Golden and three regulars, and they take her advice: the Bubble Buddy shield brought up to its golden version, which floats and holds off molten steel for a while; a heat sink in case they lose containment; and the regular version of Team Sparkles' booster rockets, which with the bubble should carry them over long jumps. The Golden one is Roller Limbo, a trans-dimensional upgrade for racing upside down and slipping under any gap of ten centimetres.

beats.headline: Samantha knows her
beats.text: Samantha, sniffing Crawler Carl, wants to know why he smells like Chachi. Chalchiuhtlicue, she clarifies: green skirt, talks funny, cries a lot. Her assessment: Chachi is pretty, not emotionally stable, and always talking about saving the lives of children before killing them all. Once, at a party, the meatballs had cilantro in them, so Chachi had her worshippers kill a whole village day care in the hope the next tray tasted better. It worked, Samantha adds. Carl realises this is the goddess Lucia named.

beats.headline: Rescued by people he was rude to
beats.text: Team Sparkles is still in this race, which by every reasonable projection it should not be. Jasha and Radoslav of team Free Love found Dwight spinning in circles just outside the exit and dragged him in. I record outcomes rather than motives, so I will confine myself to the facts: the two who did it are the two whose van he once drove straight over.

beats.headline: Two Golden upgrades and a key
beats.text: Carl's team has won the heat. Hedy, reading the room and unusually subdued, has two Golden upgrades to offer and a key, which means they can go into any of the old houses in the cul-de-sac; if they mean to trade vehicles, she says, do that before picking. Carl already knows: the house of One Fine Pig, whose armoured vehicle he rates below his own truck. Imani reports that Louis has just used his key to add a gecko to his garage, and found an engineer in a hidden room.

beats.headline: She picks the upgrades for them
beats.text: The upgrade board goes up again and Hedy walks the party through it again, subdued this time, because she can read the room. She has watched what this course does to a chassis. They have only felt it. Her advice is taken, which on the whole is more than the advice of anyone else in that garage that day managed.

beats.headline: They go back for Dwight
beats.text: Jasha and Radoslav went back onto a live course and pulled Dwight out of it, which is the only reason Team Sparkles is still racing. Crawler Carl suggested it, and Jasha asked whether he meant that one, the worst of them. Nobody would have said a word if they had driven past, and a great many spectators would have preferred it. Team Free Love did it anyway, promptly, for a team that would not have done it for them. I file this under: awake.

beats.headline: The tourist is his brother
beats.text: Linus is dead. Syndicate security killed him in his own trash-filled berth in orbit over Teelan-3, surrounded by posters of the fairy crawler he followed. His brother Minus, a soother, is given five hundred hours of footage, his brother's posts and a ship bought with his brother's money, and sent down as Linus before the tenth floor opens: half-corporeal, a non-combatant, attached to the fairy crawler. He has a primary and a secondary target. He is told to act the pervert for a while.

beats.headline: A gecko in the garage
beats.text: Okay so, we won a key, and I used it, and now there's a gecko in my garage. Like a whole second ride. I did what Carl said and checked for the hidden room in the house, and there was an engineer in there, which is, no joke, a great find. There were also mobs in the house. Nobody mentioned the mobs. Be careful if you're doing it, man. Anyway. Pretty sweet.

beats.headline: A brother in a trash-filled berth
beats.text: For the record: Minus is a soother and a soldier of Syndicate security, and the file opens on him standing over his brother Linus's corpse, in a trash-filled berth on one of the swanky habitats orbiting the star, just killed by Syndicate security. The brothers last spoke five cycles ago, a month after their father's funeral. Minus had not known Linus moved off the surface. Posters of Elle cover the walls. He feels guilt, then shame, then the thought that their mother is going to be so pissed.

beats.headline: Orders: act the pervert
beats.text: Captain Fresh hands him a datapad: some five hundred hours of the fairy crawler's footage and every post his brother made about her, to rapid-inject tonight, because the tenth floor begins in hours. He is to be half-corporeal, a non-combatant, attached to the fairy crawler, with a primary and a secondary target. So act the pervert for some time, the captain says. He calls it a suicide mission: a surgical crawler kill to destabilise the group and start the Ascendency game early. Minus salutes. Whatever it takes, sir.

beats.headline: Chachi
beats.text: Why does Carl smell like Chachi? Chalchiuhtlicue. Green skirt, talks funny, cries a lot. Don't hide her from me, I'm not jealous. Okay, I don't usually give advice after a breakup, but: she's pretty, and she is CUCKOO. Always talking about saving children, and then something inconvenient happens and it's sacrifice a seven-year-old. She had a whole village day care killed at a Yarilo party over cilantro in the meatballs. It worked, though. And now Carl is triple-dipping with her and Eris and a wife? No mustache, even.

beats.headline: Towed in by the van it flattened
beats.text: Team Sparkles is still in the race only because team Free Love dragged it in. Jasha asked whether Crawler Carl really thought they should save him, the worst of them; Carl told the bugbears to tow Dwight in if he would let them, and to be wary. They found the unicorn spinning in a circle just outside the exit and dragged him in. The court, meanwhile, picks its next upgrades and takes the regular version of the booster rockets Team Sparkles has, which with its new bubble will let the truck cover large jumps.

beats.headline: A suicide mission, from security
beats.text: Captain Fresh of Syndicate security says it plainly to the soldier going in under a dead fan's name: it is a suicide mission. The Syndicate is trying to nuke the whole system off the map before it spreads further, and losing; the AI stops everything and answers in kind. A surgical crawler kill, they believe, will destabilise the group, start the Ascendency game early and let their other assets move. It is us or them, he says. The viewers who will not stop watching are to blame too.

beats.headline: Asking around about Chachi
beats.text: I send the same question to Rosetta, Mordecai, Tipid and Prepotente at once: who is this Chalchiuhtlicue, and why did my Scavenger's Daughter patch try to go off while I was talking to Lucia? Rosetta says she's a minor goddess of childbirth, water and fire, never sponsored, weak in the Ascendency game. Mordecai says what he always says, which is that nobody knows, this is all new. Donut says we're calling her Chachi. My question stands. If she can get from wherever those kids are to here, can we go the other way?

beats.headline: Rarely sponsored, often weak
beats.text: Crawler Carl asks around. Rosetta: Chachi, as Samantha calls her, is not well known and has never been sponsored that she remembers. Like Eileithyia, she is a goddess of childbirth and women, but also of water and fire, and of harvests. Catch-all deities look good on the manifest and do poorly in the Ascendency game, their powers being comparatively weak. Crawler Donut declares that she is to be called Chachi. Prepotente supplies the Earth analog, an Aztec goddess of the same name, benevolent, whose crying for many days began a flood myth.

beats.headline: The garage of One Fine Pig
beats.text: The abandoned houses stand in the order their teams lost, so One Fine Pig's is the closest. Osvaldo asks whether Carl is using his key; Osvaldo lost the chance at his own heat's garages when he moved. Carl puts his hand on the garage door and it yawns open. Next to the parked APV with the cracked windshield stands Penelope the pig, licking up the remains of a gremlin. Hi, Penny, says Carl, going to a knee. She snorts happily and follows them out.

beats.headline: Removed from the garage of One Fine Pig
beats.text: The garage of One Fine Pig, entered without invitation, and Penelope leaves it in the company of Carl and Donut. Ownership of a pig is not a category I keep records in, so I will put it plainly. The sow has changed hands. The thunder god's protection has not changed at all. Every crawler now sharing a vehicle with her is standing inside the blast radius of somebody else's affection, and I have said as much to anyone who would listen.

beats.headline: He has read up on Chachi
beats.text: The analog in your culture, since you ask, is the Aztec goddess of the same name. Benevolent, supposedly, in a civilisation that practised human sacrifice, and the origin of a flood myth because she cried for many days. It is somewhat interesting how closely these gods track your pantheons. I, too, intend to enter this guild. I will be performing "In the Air Tonight" by Phil Collins. The cat's number is a surprise and a duet, and Carl requires potions and scrolls to survive it. That sounds like a hoot.

beats.headline: We are calling her Chachi
beats.text: WE'RE JUST GOING TO CALL HER CHACHI. I only have so much room on my cut-and-paste, and I am not filling it with a name that long. Anyway, it is concert day. Prepotente is coming, and he is singing as well, which is lovely for him. Mine is a surprise. It will be a duet with Carl, and he has to take a great many potions and scrolls first so that he does not mess it up. Then we go and collect the pig from the empty house.

beats.headline: Thrown on the table
beats.text: In the next race, Zhang says, he will kill Torpedo, their octopus mount, so the system kills Li Na, and him with her. Carl tells him that will not work any more. She is killing people, Zhang says, and she has stopped talking to him. He meets Carl's eyes, rips the target cape off and throws it on the table. He wishes he had died in the temple. Carl stares at the cape. The AI gave it to Zhang after he survived the battle inside Club Vanquisher, a fight he went to only because they needed his help.

beats.headline: Trust me on this one
beats.text: Donut wants the whole plan and I can't give it to her yet. The prize is two people of our choosing brought to the eleventh floor, and she's scared I mean to hurt somebody she likes. So I tell her what I can: I'm scared too, and the pig, this quest and the war mage plan will all help us survive. I'll explain once it's too late for them to take the prize away. Then Zhang says what he means to do, and I see it. Li Na can't worship a god. She's a weapon. She just needs pointing. I message Bodi.

beats.headline: Who does that?
beats.text: Zhang wipes his eyes, and then the words tumble out of him. She ripped Jun's eye out of his face after he died, and then she ripped her own eye out to install it. Who does that? That was when he should have known she was gone. He used to think he could keep her from going too crazy.

beats.headline: A fleshmancer among the crumbs
beats.text: For the record: Grigori the Placid. Human, level ninety-three Fleshmancer, a hired mercenary of Team Meadow Lark, worshipper of Gula. Elle and Imani hired him and bring him to the Lollipop, where he sits bolt upright between Louis and Linus with a cappuccino, flicking cookie crumbs off his blue robes. Crawler Carl wants him to talk to both halves of Corcunda. Elle reports that he has a stick up his backside. She also reports that he knows what he is doing, and he and Imani have been trading healing tips.

beats.headline: Between Louis and the fleshmancer
beats.text: At the Lollipop, the tourist on file as Linus sits on one side of Grigori the Placid, with Louis on the other scattering cookie crumbs. He stares at Elle with puppy dog eyes. His shirt has moved on from a naked picture of her to a moving, all-over print of her screaming face mid-spell, captioned: Right in the keister! The fleshmancer sits ramrod straight between them, flicking crumbs off his robes, and looks absolutely out of place.

beats.headline: She is not a weapon
beats.text: Carl says we need people like Li Na, because she is so strong. She is not a weapon, Carl. She is a person. I like her, of course I do, but we cannot let her keep hurting people, and we certainly cannot let Zhang kill himself to stop her. That is not right, and I told Zhang no, twice. We will find something to fix this. Somebody has to talk some sense into her. It is the only way.

beats.headline: Not bad, just lost
beats.text: Zhang says it's his fault. It isn't. It isn't all Na's, either. They attacked her. Rezan was an ass, and the decapitator had it coming. She didn't take player-killer skulls, because it was her dreads that did it, and they all killed each other. Zhang wants to kill their mount mid-race so the system takes them both. Carl says that won't work any more: Na just loses containment and reaches the line without one. She isn't killing for fun. She's lost her humanity. Those are different problems.

beats.headline: He offers to go with her
beats.text: Li Na has gone somewhere none of us can reach, and everyone who rode with us in the last heat is dead. So I say it out loud in the Lollipop with everyone listening: next race, I kill our own mount. That takes her out of it. It takes me out of it too, and I have thought about that part, and it is still the cleanest thing I can see. Carl says it will not work any more: we only lose our containment, and she can reach the finish without a mount where I cannot. He says there has to be another way.

beats.headline: It's a go
beats.text: Splash Zone says the casino plan is a bust, so it's the cleaner bots. Li Na's poison won't clear, and it'll get worse, because health tops up on every new floor. If Herot's real and the war mages weren't lying about the Cabaret, getting her through stops that, keeps Zhang alive, stops her killing crawlers, and tests the route before we try it with a crowd. It only works if she agrees. She's too smart to trick, and I wouldn't want to. Everyone at the table is looking at me. "It's a go." Tran bows.

beats.headline: Sold out due to overwhelming demand
beats.text: Since the previous floor, crawlers have been complaining that the Cleaner Bot upgrade is missing from the personal space shop, due to "overwhelming demand." Everyone blamed warlords stockpiling for Faction Wars, which was partly true. The white one Carl looted from Architect Houston's surgical theatre was an old model and, as it happens, the last one the store had. The rest of the demand has a single name: Herot, with a standing order to buy every cleaner bot that shows up. Which makes a household appliance the most interesting item in the shop.

beats.headline: An audience granted
beats.text: Splash Zone, in chat, while Crawler Carl is busy separating a goat from a unicorn: he has asked for an audience with Hamed, the new leader guy, to see whether he can help find Splash Zone's wife. The guards said Hamed would see him. So he, Gluteus and Doctor Bones are going to talk to him. He is sending Bucket Boy over to Carl in the meantime.

beats.headline: He has a standing order for cleaner bots
beats.text: The shop-interface route is the one nobody can test, and the reason is a standing purchase order. Two answers are on file. Menerva is on the seventeenth floor. Herot is inside the cabaret itself, and he has a standing purchase order in with the shop for every cleaner bot it will sell him, which he has evidently been putting to some use of his own. Somebody shut in a box for cycles has been quietly buying the delivery vehicles. I will leave that where it sits.

beats.headline: She is on the seventeenth floor
beats.text: The plan Mordecai and Rosetta are working on runs through a shop interface and a standing order for cleaner bots, and it puts the two builders in different places. Herot is in the cabaret. Menerva is on the seventeenth floor, in charge of the NPCs building and occupying the maze there. Nobody in that room has been within seven floors of the seventeenth, and this crawl is presently on the tenth. I hold a very great many records. I am not going to tell you which of them account for that.

beats.headline: The test worked, mostly
beats.text: Believe it or not, the test worked. Samantha can't die and she's not what you'd call a reliable subject, so we ran it again on some sluggalos. It works. There are a few wrinkles, and I'm working on them right now. But listen to me, kid. This is so far off the codex we don't even know the system will let Li Na do it. And if it does, she could still die when your floor collapses. He says he knows. He always says he knows.

beats.headline: A standing order for cleaner bots
beats.text: Mordecai reports that the test worked, on Samantha and then on some sluggalos. The explanation for the missing cleaner bots is Herot, inside the Cabaret with limited powers and a shop interface and a standing order to buy every one that appears. Menerva runs the NPCs building the Backstage Death Maze on the seventeenth floor. The Cabaret itself is overrun, by ogres from a binned plotline, a shadow mimic infestation and more, and the war mages want help clearing it. The casino plan looks like a bust. Li Na, dying of poison, is to go first, if she can be talked into it.

beats.headline: Auto-Tune to the max
beats.text: Carl and Donut are to sing one of the guild-entrance songs, one listed with two singers, so that each of them has a performance bar. Carl takes the lead, because Donut has only a few lines and her chances are higher. She will use her headset with the Auto-Tune turned to the max, and Carl has to read a scroll, Gelded Choirboy, to hit the notes at all. Before they start, she raises the headset's volume and asks the crowd to encourage Carl: this is his first time singing ever, she tells them.

beats.headline: Back on, with purpose
beats.text: Elle, Zhang and Tran pull back from the table with a new plan. Zhang grabs his target cape and pulls it back on, standing straight and tall and with purpose. The three of them are going back to the safe room to try to reach Li Na and tell her what they mean to do. Carl whispers good luck to Elle, and she returns it, looking over her shoulder at Donut.

beats.headline: Potions, a scroll, and A-ha
beats.text: I've never sung in my life, except hammered in a bar with a bunch of coasties, years ago. So Mordecai compounds potions to get round the cooldowns, and I'm Honeyed, Yo-Yo Ma'd and Dio'd. There's a scroll called Gelded Choirboy for the notes my voice can't reach. Mordecai insists the name isn't literal. I read it at the last second and sound like I've sucked on a helium balloon. The song is "Take on Me." I take the lead, so Donut's few lines have the better odds. Then the unicorn stabs the DJ.

beats.headline: The horn and the disc jockey
beats.text: The Lollipop, packed to the walls, Crawler Carl full of bard potions and climbing onto a stage to sing his way into a guild. Dwight is drunk at the front of the room. As the pair of them get up there he drives his horn through the disc jockey's face. The disc jockey had been shouting at him. Beyond that there was no faction in it, nothing at stake and nothing to gain. He simply did it, in a room already full of armed strangers looking for a reason.

beats.headline: Stabbed into the DJ
beats.text: At the Lollipop the gremlin DJ has been on the floor yelling at Dwight, who still has not moved. The DJ goes back to his booth and calls up Princess Donut and Carl to sing Take On Me, slaps a microphone into Carl's palm, and the screens say Get Ready to Sing. Carl reads his scroll. The synth pop starts, the crowd cheers, the gauges appear. And that is when Dwight the unicorn stabs the DJ in the face with his horn.

beats.headline: Squeaky on purpose
beats.text: The guild only opens to someone who sings a song with the needle in the green. Mordecai has compounded a few special potions together, a new trick to get round potion cooldowns, so Carl and Donut stay in sync; Carl takes the lead on a two-singer song. The scroll, Gelded Choirboy, is so he can physically hit notes his deeper voice cannot. Mordecai insists the name is not literal. It will make him squeaky, so he will read it at the last second. The singing potion lasts a long while, so he drinks it now: Honeyed, Yo-Yo Ma'd, Dio'd. Onstage he reads the scroll. You've been Choired! He sounds as if he has sucked helium. Then Dwight stabs the DJ.

beats.headline: Transferred, and brushing a cat
beats.text: Mercenary ownership of Grigori has been transferred to Crawler Carl's guild. His first duty under new management is brushing Crawler Donut, which she has arranged personally, and he appears to be enjoying himself. Linus, who has been stroking Donut's tail and whispering to her, is taken away by Elle. Grigori's first recorded word comes a moment after, when Donut asks whether she should perform with or without sunglasses. With, he says. She agrees.

beats.headline: Looking forward to this
beats.text: Donut has zapped Mongo into the bar so he won't miss Uncle Carl's stage debut, and the patrons are jumping back from his wings. Carl won't tell us why this quest matters so much. I don't need to know. I tell him the truth, and I smile when I do it: I've been looking forward to this moment for a long time. He says he hopes I like Norwegian music. Elle is going to be furious she missed it. I wave Chris, Florin, Bautista, Britney and Jurgen to the back, and suddenly the place is packed.

beats.headline: His fingers in Donut's tail
beats.text: While Donut has the fleshmancer brush her, the tourist pats her chain mail crupper and then runs his long fingers along her tail. I'm touching her, he announces. Elle threatens to have someone in the outside world break his creepy little fingers. He carries on regardless: she smells good, Elle doesn't let him sniff her. He whispers something to Donut and sucks his triple-segmented finger. Donut turns: excuse me? Elle gives up and takes him with her. Oh goody, he says. The orders said act the pervert.

beats.headline: Take on me
beats.text: When the chorus comes, Donut echoes Carl's line, her Auto-Tuned voice high and, thankfully, in key, piercing the chaos of the brawl in the bar like a knife. At the same moment she shoots a low-powered magic missile that blows an axe out of the hand of a Draconian about to sink it into the back of Dong's head.

beats.headline: Singing through a bar fight
beats.text: The DJ's dead, so this is our only shot, and the music keeps going. I sing. Bottles break on me. I kick a gremlin and a Draconian off the stage before they reach Donut, catch her microphone stand between my big and index toe, and bounce off the stage when the curtains go up. I hit the high note and the gauge by my head throws sparks. Permanent access to the Stage Performance Guild, and an achievement, Sing for your supper. The sign over Donut says FAILED. I guess I gotta do this myself.

beats.headline: Nickels, not gold
beats.text: A brawl in the Lollipop, and a crawler singing through it, and so I take up Mr. Jefferson and sweep the stage clear before him, howling as I go. A mantis creature tears the good sock open as I strike her, and out come the coins, and half the room falls upon them. They are nickels. Every one of them is a nickel, though I have been feeding him honest gold pieces. I do not understand it.

beats.headline: One drunk unicorn, one wrecked duet
beats.text: He follows it by hurling the dead disc jockey at Crawler Carl and Crawler Donut, misses, and hits a demon of team Yokai, which draws in the Minister of Blood-Letting and his skeletons and then most of the floor. Carl's allies spend the entire song trying to keep the teams in that room from murdering each other. On the last line of the thing Crawler Donut is knocked flat by a paralysed kappa and loses the entry she had just sung for. Crawler Carl gets in alone. One drunk unicorn, one wrecked duet, one guild place where there should have been two.

beats.headline: The high note
beats.text: Carl sings Take On Me through a full bar brawl. Bottles break against him, Dong clears the stage with his sock, and on the extra-high note the gauge by Carl's head chimes and showers digital sparkles. Half the crowd stops fighting. Both gauges sit all the way in the green, his with little flames out of the top. He catches Donut's toppling microphone stand between his toes and keeps singing, off the stage as the curtains burn. Fireworks on the long last note. A paralysed kappa falls on Donut during her final line. Carl is granted permanent access to the Stage Performance Guild.

beats.headline: The dance floor
beats.text: In the mostly-music middle of Take On Me, with a brawl filling the Lollipop, Donut casts Ice Slick on the dance floor. A group of fighting NPCs goes spinning and crashes against the bar, into Prepotente, who is bent over the unattended counter rummaging behind it, and he flips with a yelp and disappears with a clatter.

beats.headline: Into the fight
beats.text: MOTHER singing. Loud. FIGHT. Tail. People fall over. Fairy throws fire at Imani. Fairy is FOOD. MOTHER has beer on her. Lick MOTHER. MOTHER is cross.

beats.headline: Robbed of a perfect score
beats.text: My part was perfect, Auto-Tuned and in key, and in the middle of a chorus I shot the axe out of a Draconian's hand before he could put it in Dong's head. Then, on my very last line, a paralysed kappa fell backward right into me, and now there is a sign over my head that says FAILED. I was robbed of a perfect score. Carl has to go through the glowing door by himself. We are never going to mention this again. I do love that song, though.

beats.headline: A running list of gods
beats.text: Jurgen asks a better question than I'd managed: can people who worship gods not go to the Cabaret, or do the war mages just not want them there? Akuma lied to us about needing two teams dead, so he could be lying about this too. I've been keeping a running list of every god I hear of, sorted by affiliation and skill. Donar goes on it: thunder and lightning, like Thor but manlier, not sponsored this season, and he's given Jurgen lightning spells. My heart skips a beat. Then I'm through the door, and the guildmaster is stuck in his own zipper.

beats.headline: There are two of him
beats.text: The shape of the problem, finally stated out loud. Corcunda is not one person in one place. A spell called Split Personality went off a long time ago and split him in two, and both halves lived through it: Corky, riding in the back of the Lady Dominators' car, and Porky, hopping on a single foot behind the doors of the stage performance guild, which Crawler Carl has just sung his way into. Porky agrees to the reunion. Porky also has terms, and the terms are that somebody afterwards answers for how this happened, and that somebody is Dong.

beats.headline: Somebody has to answer for the children
beats.text: The bar fight is over and the nickels are still being picked up off the floor, and I cannot wait for Carl to finish his errand. There is a goddess threatening to kill all the children. He tells me the only thing to do from this side is talk Lucia into a deal. Then send me out, I tell him, the way the others will go. He says I cannot, because of the god I worship. So I tell him the rest. I used to be able to talk to Heidi, and I have not heard her in a while. She is pregnant. I have to get to her.

beats.headline: Torn open on the dance floor
beats.text: In the brawl during Carl and Donut's song, Dong clears the stage swinging his gigantic sock over his head. A mantis-like creature slices at him; he sends her flying, but not before she tears a hole in it. Coins fly everywhere, and every one is a nickel, though he has been putting gold pieces in. Dozens of NPCs grab handfuls and run. The tear mends itself. The sock does not go back to its giant size, however many nickels are put back in.

beats.headline: A crawler sings his way through the door
beats.text: A crawler sings his way through my door, which nobody has managed in a while, and then asks me to be put back together with Corky. Fine. I want it too. It would be nice not to have to lean against everything again. But I set a condition and I set it plainly: when it is done, somebody helps me deal with the one who is actually responsible for all of this. And for the crawler's information, the females of my kind do not answer to Grull. They worship Enyo, an unhinged goddess of war. I answered to Grull once. The devotion went when I split, and I do not miss it.

beats.headline: O-o-o-offered
beats.text: Carl enters the Stage Performance Guild, and the welcome notification invites the performer to see the guildmaster for the services o-o-o-offered. He notes that even the routine dungeon notices are glitching out more often now. It is a small stutter at the door of a dusty theatre with one spotlight in it, heard by one crawler on his own.

beats.headline: A bad night outside the Lady Dominators' garage
beats.text: Bad night. Splash Zone and Gluteus Maxx and Dr. Bones went to talk to Hamed and now nobody can raise them, because they are not on this floor any more. Dong is properly ill, with a debuff over him I have never seen before. I grabbed the sock to ask it what was wrong and it went for me, and then it was just gone, teleported out by the safe room, and I do not know what happened. Meanwhile the others go to the Lady Dominators' garage to get Corcunda out, and the car is already rolling out for the line before anyone gets in. I am not a soldier. I keep finding myself in the room where the soldiering happens.

beats.headline: He could have been kinder
beats.text: Dong's cursed. Mordecai says the sock has gone, and without it and every nickel the NPCs grabbed, a temple won't help. I gave him that sock. I got it from Quan Ch. The Dominators heard us outside their garage and drove for the starting line with Corky in the back, where we can't touch them. I sit on the curb. Dong's an NPC, and he's my friend, and I could've been a lot less of a jerk about it. So we stop waiting. We join the two halves during the race, and Grigori gets half an hour to learn to drive.

beats.headline: The other side of the door
beats.text: This is unbearable, Carl. I am on the other side of the door, and I cannot even see him. He is the love of my life, and what you mean to do will change him forever, and I am not to be allowed to say goodbye. I am dying besides. They call the thing upon me Negative ROI, and Mr. Jefferson has stopped speaking to me, and my health is seeping away. I do not complain of the curse, my good sir. I complain of the door.

beats.headline: They heard you coming
beats.text: For the record: the Lady Dominators were in their garage, and they were listening. As Crawler Carl's party prepared to cast a hole through the door, the door opened and the GTO rolled out for the starting line, Genesis driving on new tyres that appear to be made of gold, Corky unconscious in the back. A vehicle on its way to the start may not be attacked. Genesis invited Porky to hop in. Corky, she stated, is nontransferable. The party stepped off the driveway.

beats.headline: He has never done this
beats.text: The plan: take Corky from the Lady Dominators' garage, bring him to Porky, and let Grigori perform the joining. The spell is not difficult, he says, if both halves are willing. They are unzipped, kept alive with spells or potions while pressed together, and then there are a few minutes before the personalities join. Asked what the result is like, he says he has no idea and is looking forward to seeing it. He has never done it. Two halves rarely survive Split Personality for long. The garage attempt fails, and Crawler Carl orders him to spend half an hour learning to drive.

beats.headline: Gone off the floor
beats.text: Warning: as this mercenary is no longer on this floor, they are unable to be contacted. Splash Zone. Gluteus. Doctor Bones. Same warning for each, and the daily fee still charged. Bucket Boy, the one they sent away, says they were going to see the new boss guy, Hamed, Anaconda and Damascus Steel's dad. Crawler Carl has no idea what that family is doing, and no time to find out. The notices do not say anyone is dead.

beats.headline: Corky is nontransferable
beats.text: The court comes to take Corky out of their garage before Heat Five, and they were listening. The door opens, and the GTO rolls out for the starting line on tyres that look to be made of gold, Corky unconscious in the back; on the way to the start it may not be attacked. They invite Porky to hop in: they would love a matched set. Rapture says they heard about the fleshmancer, and they would unzip Corky and let him spill before handing him over. He is nontransferable, says Genesis. See you in the factory, says Rapture.

beats.headline: Goddamn sapient weapons
beats.text: Okay. We're busy prepping the Li Na exit, but we took a look at Dong. It says Negative ROI. Mistress Tiatha thinks it's really a curse called Separation Anxiety, and if she's right a temple won't do a thing. We need the sock back, and every coin he lost. The sock went for Bucket Boy and got teleported by the safe room rules, and it's probably in Hungry Eyes in somebody else's hands. That's what sapient weapons do. They use an owner up and move on. I didn't see this one coming. Its stupid origin story hid it.

beats.headline: Nobody mentioned Dong was part of this
beats.text: Nobody mentioned that Dong was part of this little endeavour. I find that out from the Lady Dominators, jeering about a crusty old stripper as they roll out of the garage we were about to break into, Corky in the back of their car. Carl tells me to put my big-boy pants on, in those exact words, because Tipid has just told them Dong is sick with something called Negative ROI and the timing of my grievance is not mine to choose.
