The light turned green and the timed hole punch opened the shield, the vine-killing potion killed the vine, and a second potion fried the navigation that looked like Lucienne. Before Osvaldo's gnu had recovered from Dwight's own cannon, Crawler Donut was through the window and had removed his head. His horn is now in her inventory. The missile cart never launched. The official notification reads: because, holy shit, that was pretty badass. It stands.

beats.headline: Into Donut's inventory
beats.text: At the green light of the last heat, it goes for Dwight exactly as planned. He bursts off the line dragging his missile cart and fires his cannon into Bruna, whose shield is already up. The hole punch, the vine-killing potion balls and the GPS-frying potion all do their jobs, and Donut goes out the passenger window as smoke, onto the roof of the truck. Dwight's head comes off in a single swipe of her claw. Before the notification even arrives, his magical horn has been removed from his head and placed in her inventory.

beats.headline: The crystal covers him
beats.text: Carl is a dachshund. Elle, Jacobus and Chris are transformed as well, and the reason I am still shaped like myself is Prepotente's Memorial Crystal, which covered him and covered me with him. He tells us it stands at eleven point one per cent charged. Eleven per cent of a thing I do not understand, and it is holding me in my own shape. Then the heat starts and I do as I am told.

beats.headline: Plan Mach Schnell
beats.text: Carl is a dog now and cannot even say the name of the plan properly. It is Mach Schnell. Dorota rolls the window down for me, bless her. When the light goes green I am through the window as smoke and onto the roof before the vine has finished dying, and before Osvaldo's gnu has stopped staggering I take that tiresome unicorn's head off with one swipe and his horn goes into my inventory. The announcement is complimentary. I prefer decisive. Carl is wagging again.

beats.headline: Who else is going to drive
beats.text: Carl is a DOG. A long-haired wiener dog, with an accent, and he cannot drive because he has no thumbs, and Jamal is not very good, so who else is going to? Donut adds me as a driver. I take the steering wheel in my mouth. I hope the dog thing is permanent. We will have to change his name, of course, and get him neutered. Or maybe not. Orthrus is also a boy, which is a shame, because can you imagine the puppies?

beats.headline: Still gagged, still useful
beats.text: Moments before the heat, Carl has been turned into a long-haired dachshund, and Donut, ready to go, needs the window down. It is manual, she may not break the glass until the heat starts, and Jamal is too snug to reach. Then Donut's chair, still muted, unhooks herself, an arm appears, grasps the handle and quickly rolls it down. Thank you, Dorota.

beats.headline: Tiny on a dachshund
beats.text: Elle is a goblin, Jacobus a starfish, and Carl a long-haired dachshund with a German accent and no thumbs. His boxers have resized themselves and sit awkwardly on his hips. Jacket, cloak and bandanna remain; none of his rings do, and the xistera and the gauntlet have unequipped themselves. The kneepads remain, tiny on his back legs.

beats.headline: Dropped on a starfish
beats.text: The wheel's first attack was a Transformation, and Imani checks in at once: Elle has been turned into a goblin, Jacobus is a starfish, and she had to drop splooge on him to keep him alive. Florin's lot are unchanged, Chris is a werewolf in human form, and Prepotente's Apito memorial crystal kept him and Jurgen from changing at all. Carl is a long-haired dachshund with a German accent.

beats.headline: One swipe at the starting blocks
beats.text: Heat Six goes to Team Sparkles too, the court second. The final heat locks them in with the court and Team Flamengo. Dwight arrives sober, towing a missile launcher he cannot fire until he clears the low ceiling, with a navigation hologram built to look like Lucienne. On green, a timed hole punch opens his shield, a potion kills the vine, another fries the navigation, and Crawler Donut goes through the window and takes his head in a single swipe, and then his horn. Team One, Team Sparkles, has been eliminated.

beats.headline: A Cadillac crushed flat
beats.text: The Russian crawlers' Cadillac bursts forward to the middle of the lobby and flips up at a right angle, like a rocket about to launch: they are making a run for the exit. The APV and Chris's truck fire spells at it, its shield sparks and flickers, and Prepotente hurls something that knocks it out. In that moment Donut casts Astral Paw and smashes the car where it stands, crushing it like a tin can. Less than a second passes from her shout to the crush. Three new player-killer skulls form over her.

beats.headline: She kills Osvaldo at the portals
beats.text: Crawler Osvaldo made a run for the portals to the eleventh floor across a roof Crawler Carl had just blown open. He did not reach them. Crawler Britney stopped him, permanently, and took Ysalte's memorial crystal off what remained. One crawler ran. One did not let him. The crystal changed hands. I am not required to have an opinion, but I have watched a great many exits, and that one was clean.

beats.headline: Poleaxes, all the way up
beats.text: I designed them on the last floor and never got to use them: poleaxes. Focused charges that blast up and down in a cone but not sideways, vaporising a ten-meter circle below and a wider hole above instead of bringing the building down. I dropped several in a rough vertical line through the apartment building. When I hit the detonator they punch a jagged, almost straight shaft from the lobby to the roof. Being three times bigger this heat makes the holes three times bigger. A pleasant surprise.

beats.headline: Keeping Bruna alive
beats.text: The roof blows, Osvaldo is gone, and he has left a grenade to kill Bruna, his slaughter gnu. The party fires three potion balls at her to save her life: a liquid drop shield, an explosion blanket and a smoke curtain. Donut lands on the gnu and casts her own shield, sprouts trees all round her, and then a half dozen emergency gremlins sprout along the gnu's back. She has already been poisoned, but one of the gremlins is in his toolbox pulling out medicine. They can help biological mounts as well as mechanical ones.

beats.headline: Still the model
beats.text: Carl blows the roof with poleaxes, charges he designed on the previous floor to breach through a building's floors without levelling it, blasting up and down in a cone and never sideways. The whole idea came from his quest for focused explosives, something he has not seen perfectly executed since that very first blast of the murder dozer on the first floor.

beats.headline: A crystal that wants a plinth
beats.text: Crawler Britney drops on Osvaldo moving as fast as he did, because she now carries the memorial crystal from Ysalte. Samantha, suddenly serious, says Britney needs to set it in a plinth in the Basilica or the Vulgar Temple, or, as she also puts it, the Halls of the Ascendency or Sheol, if she wants that crazy Ysalte out of her. Meanwhile Prepotente's Apito crystal has shielded him, Jurgen and their mount from the Transformation, and stands at eleven point one per cent.

beats.headline: Caught on the gate at the portals
beats.text: Crawler Osvaldo has been eliminated. He was speeding for the portals on the roof of the apartment complex when Britney put a stop to it, and she now holds Ysalte's memorial crystal, which he had been carrying. Crawler Carl asked him, right up to the green light, not to force it. He forced it. He declined everything. It is a consistent record.

beats.headline: Astral Paw on the Cadillac
beats.text: The Russian car throws itself up on end in the middle of the lobby to make a run for the exit, after all our planning and all Imani's pleading. The APV and Chris's truck fire into its shield, Prepotente throws something, and the shield flickers out. So I cast Astral Paw and the Cadillac simply ceases to exist, all in less than a second. Three new skulls over my head before Carl can even think a rude word.

beats.headline: It works like an inventory
beats.text: Carl asks how Herot could pull someone out of the holding area. I spent a season on a site-prep crew. It works almost like an inventory: whoever is designing the floor selects the stored individual from a menu and places them. A simple procedure. Nobody looks at that catchall area once a season starts, because nobody ever goes into it. It was built as a backup for the Nothing, which was meant to catch problem entities and be forgotten about. The backup became redundant.

beats.headline: Her crystal changes hands at the portals
beats.text: Crawler Osvaldo has been carrying Ysalte's memorial crystal: the goddess his friend Paz killed. It did not protect him from Scolopendra, as he admitted seconds before the light went green. He makes a run for the portals across a roof Crawler Carl has just opened up, and Crawler Britney stops him and takes the crystal. Samantha's assessment, delivered flatly: if Britney wants rid of Ysalte, she needs the Halls of the Ascendency or she needs Sheol, and neither of those is on this floor.

beats.headline: The birth that saved his ass
beats.text: Crawler Carl has kept his slugpox active under the Emberus ring on purpose, arguing that the birth of the subject on the previous floor saved his ass. Everyone else thought this was a terrible idea. The cure Mordecai made sits on the crafting table. Pop: a level 30 slug bursts out of his back in a shower of blood and pus, backward cap on an eye stalk. His name is Lil' Mello Haze, a level higher than the subject and much smaller.

beats.headline: They laugh until they cry
beats.text: Mordecai's slugpox cure is still sitting on the crafting table, which I tell Imani with my tail down. About thirty of our people are waiting outside the Hairpin: Chris back in human form in his Meadow Lark overalls, Elle a goblin, Imani holding Jacobus the starfish. They see me, a dachshund, and every one of them, Prepotente and Lucia included, falls over laughing. Imani scratches my chin and cures me. Fine. Let's go rob a casino.

beats.headline: Die with hope in our hearts
beats.text: Don't you worry about those tracksuit idiots, Donut. They had a way out, they lied to us, and they'd have killed me, Imani and Chris at that exit. Ivan bragged about pulling down a whole metal bridge for scrap and wrecking a train. Carl asks if it's true. Does it matter? Look at us, risking our necks again to save a few people. It matters whether a crazy Carl plan works, sure, we die if it doesn't. But we'll die with hope in our hearts alongside our friends.

beats.headline: Slugpox on purpose
beats.text: Donut calls for Imani: Carl's stupid slugpox is back. He kept it active on purpose, because the Emberus ring keeps it under control and he wanted it ready, arguing that the birth of Bigs on the previous floor saved him. Pretty much everyone thought it a terrible idea. Mordecai made a potion to cure it, and it is still sitting on the crafting table with the backpack. They forgot to bring it.

beats.headline: Lil' Mello Haze
beats.text: The boil on Carl's back bursts in the Vendor Village and delivers a level thirty slug named Lil' Mello Haze, higher level than Bigs but smaller, on account of Carl currently being a dachshund. He wears a backward baseball cap hanging off his eye sockets and has a mace head for a tail instead of the usual hatchet. He greets his father as daddy man, is called to heel, ignores it, and wanders off in the opposite direction. The father's barking does not help.

beats.headline: Through the portal behind Chris
beats.text: The croupier sets the wheel and the portal opens under the stand-here spot. One person, they said. A test. Chris steps up, turns, waves, and drops. I go straight in after him without a word. Nobody planned that and I didn't ask. The croupier shouts cheat, and Carl has the goat pay him another five thousand. Louis gets a notice that I've left the party. That's all there is to say about it.

beats.headline: The most important part
beats.text: He has been turned from an igneous into a werewolf, human most of the time, and stands in the same Meadow Lark work overalls he wore when Crawler Carl first met him. At the Desperado Club, Clay-ton puts down his bass and stands with them until the guards step aside. At the portal, Imani makes him promise to run if he sees the exit. "I love you," Chris says. "I always have. No matter what happens next, I love you. That's the most important part." He steps forward, turns, waves, and drops away.

beats.headline: Nope
beats.text: Subject sees Crawler Carl's party of thirty walk into the Hairpin, raises both hands, and says: nope. She makes no attempt to stop them. She confirms the door now runs to the top level, then realises that the dachshund is Carl and bursts out laughing. She notes, for the record, that some of the party are permanently banned and some have no pass, and that it would be strangely adorable if half the club did not die every time they came in.

beats.headline: Late-stage crawlers you don't stop
beats.text: Subject, formerly security, now plays upright bass in the house jazz band. His contract ran out, he told them he no longer wanted to fight, and they let him play. He puts the bass down when Chris walks in, notes that Chris is different, and takes his side. If the guards stop Chris and Donut and friends, he says, they stop him. Then he explains the job to a troll guard named Klonder: he worked as a guard a very long time. Late-stage crawlers, you do not try to stop.

beats.headline: Jazz, gold leaf, and a strange mural
beats.text: The club has been remodelled. The EDM is gone; a band of mixed races plays frenetic jazz while generated NPCs in 1920s dress dance, and the crowd, once mostly young and pretty, is now a strange mix of the monstrous. Through the same old door, the casino is gold leaf and chandeliers, cluttered with spare furniture. The biggest mural shows a family of Bopcas cowering before a mushroom house, looking up at the sky. The croupier at the Wheel of Fortune is new, level one hundred and twenty, and half his description is redacted.

beats.headline: The guards fear him
beats.text: At the club door a troll guard named Klonder objects to letting a party of crawlers through. Hamed, he says, is going to kill them for it. A cretin from the house band, a door guard for a very long time, points out that tenth-floor crawlers kill you if you try to stop them, and Klonder bows them in. Inside, Crawler Carl lays out the problem. Hamed set him up to murder his own wife. His sons went hunting him and seemed to change their minds and join his cause. Now the other dancers have done the same. Carl does not trust him. He trusts them.

beats.headline: You run and don't look back
beats.text: Chris puts his hand on my face and says it isn't as warm as usual. He's wrong. This isn't goodbye, Chris Andrews. But promise me: if you get the chance, you take it. You see that exit and you're still in this body, you run and you don't look back. Even if it's just you, it'll all be worth it. He says he might turn back into a rock, or a dog. I don't care what he is. He says he loves me, and always has. Then he steps forward, waves, and drops away.

beats.headline: You're never going to see me again
beats.text: Samantha's zipping around my head, blowing into my gills, saying she's going to tea-bag me, and she only just asked what that means, man. So I tell her the thing I've been not telling her. Stop. I'm leaving. You're never going to see me again. Then Chris goes through the portal, and Britney jumps in right after him, and I'm next, and she's crying on my arm, and I don't really know what to do with that.

beats.headline: Incompatibility mode
beats.text: Carl examines the portal with his neural implant, and it warns him first: it is working in incompatibility mode due to recent changes to his wetware system, and he should see his Valtay representative for repair. Only limited details are available. Unknown Manufacturer Enhancement Zone Subspace Portal. One-way, open access, and it leads to a stasis chamber. Visual Analysis: unavailable. Carl wags his tail; it is pretty much what he was hoping it would say. Hopefully the implant will go back to working properly when he stops being a damn dog.

beats.headline: Our torrid affair, cancelled
beats.text: Louis says he's LEAVING. I am never going to see him again. We never even got to have our TORRID AFFAIR. We were going to fall madly in love, and when I went back to my king he was going to pluck his own eyes out. Now he'll be all alone, and I have nobody left for an affair. Carl is too broody, and a dog. Jurgen's Heidi sounds meaner than Imani. Florin is a crocodile. Prepotente asks what about him. Ew.

beats.headline: Protected from examination
beats.text: In the Desperado Club's casino the croupier is level 120 and an Enforcer, his examination full of redactions, a much higher level than Carl expected. Carl tells Donut to take a Size Up and asks anyone else with examination skills to let him know what they see. Donut reports back that he is protected from the examination.

beats.headline: A portal to a stasis chamber
beats.text: Mitch the croupier sets the Wheel of Fortune by hand to the last click of the first Nothing wedge and hits a button, and a black portal opens under the stand-here spot. Crawler Carl remembers the real Nothing's heavy mental pull. This one has none; it is as inert as a door. His failing implant reads it as an Enhancement Zone Subspace Portal, one-way, open access, leading to a stasis chamber. It stays open about fifteen seconds. Chris drops through. It is exactly what they hoped it would say.

beats.headline: Story time, mid-ambush
beats.text: A casino full of mimics springs its ambush, and the AI stops for story time. Mitch, a level 120 Adolescent Shadow Mimic, is an Enforcer for someone redacted, sent up to wreck Hamed's plans, and the Shadow Mimics loose in the dungeon are one part of the Big Six: the groups left in the dungeon trying to either take over or escape. After these, the AI says, there are only one or two more groups to meet before the crawlers are caught up. The list, it warns, is completely arbitrary.

beats.headline: One through five
beats.text: One: the Crawlers, former crawlers included, Herot and Forkith among them. Two: the standard NPCs, mostly working together, Juice Box among them, with offshoots like Hamed's revolution. Three: the Gods, the most fractured and dumbest, beyond the AI's control, and the group it despises most. Four: the sapient mobs, the Shadow Mimics, the Ogre Imperium, Krakaren Prime and the War Mages. Five: the demons in Sheol, perhaps the most organised, and out of its view, a closed system it likens to a cyst.

beats.headline: Group six, not yet
beats.text: Six is group six. Survive this fight and make it to the eleventh floor, the AI says, and you'll meet group six. The lines already blur: mobs working with former crawlers, NPCs with gods, some demons with those mysterious group sixers. It is a handy guide, not a map. The tourists and Syndicate security are rats on the first floor: a necessary but loathsome nuisance. Carl, currently a wiener dog, asks whether the lore dumps could please stop happening in the middle of ambushes.

beats.headline: The eye on the dog's forehead
beats.text: As a dachshund I can't punch, which I learn the hard way against a table. Worse: the Eye of the Bedlam Bride has moved from my chest to the middle of my dog forehead, and it's trying to wrench itself open. Let me take over, it says. No. You stay trapped. Then Mitch lunges at me, all mouth, and I open it on reflex. He freezes, glittering, screaming that it's too cold, and Donut finishes him. It's there when I need it. That's what worries me.

beats.headline: The archenemies of the principals
beats.text: Mid-fight, the AI files the casino's Shadow Mimics as the counter to their archenemies, the changeling principals. They grow in intelligence and power with age and without limit, are prone to breaking their ideation, and are almost impossible to detect. The one wearing the croupier ate the real Mitch, a wall rat who had kept his memory between seasons. When these mimics die they do what changelings do: they fall into blank grey figures, thin, armless, with tentacles.

beats.headline: On a dog's forehead
beats.text: In a dog's body, Carl remembers the tattoo only when it tries to wrench itself open: it has moved to the centre of his forehead, hidden. Let me take over, Shi Maria says. He tells her she is trapped and will stay trapped. If you say so, she answers; she is here when he needs her. Then the mimic Mitch lurches forward to consume him, Carl opens the eye on reflex, and Mitch freezes, sparkling, crying that it is too cold, until Donut's magic missile kills him.

beats.headline: Named among the Big Six
beats.text: The AI, listing what it calls the Big Six groups in the dungeon trying to take over or escape, puts the crawlers first and says the group includes former crawlers: that Herot guy, that Forkith dude, and so forth. It says so in passing, between a shadow mimic named Mitch and the NPCs, in a notice mostly about something else. It is the first word of Forkith since his notes on the Hunting Grounds, and it places him inside the dungeon now, not only in its margins.

beats.headline: A despot, per the AI
beats.text: The AI's arbitrary list of the Big Six groups trying to take over or escape its dungeon. Under the NPCs, several offshoot groups, including "that Hamed despot and his ill-advised attempt at creating a dungeon revolution for the early indentured." Separately, and with a hint: Mitch, the croupier at the wheel and the strongest shadow mimic in the room, is still a baby at level 120, and was sent up by a redacted party to wreck Hamed's plans.

beats.headline: Filed among the six powers
beats.text: For once I am straight with the room and I list the six groups still fighting over this place: crawlers, standard NPCs, gods, sapient mobs, the demons of Sheol, and one more I decline to name. The Krakaren sits in the fourth group, next to the shadow mimics and the war mages. That is a considerable promotion from neighbourhood boss and an unpleasant thing to learn at this hour.

beats.headline: A rope with a door in it
beats.text: I have a new rope. It is gold. Inside the loop the air is a door. The mimic that was pretending to be a gambler is a blob now, so I put the loop over its head. The part of it inside the loop goes somewhere else. Then I close the door. The rest of it stays in the room and falls over. Its bottom half spills on the floor. I look for the next one.

beats.headline: Three Mongos, one sat on
beats.text: Table bites MOTHER. Now THREE Mongo. Chandelier eats shiny Mongo. BAD. Shiny Mongo goes BOOM. Mongo ANGRY. Mongo bites chairs. Big mimic last. MOTHER kills it first. Mongo sits on it anyway.

beats.headline: One of six powers in the dungeon
beats.text: The AI sets out who is actually fighting for control down here, and there are six groups. Crawlers. Standard NPCs. Gods. Sapient mobs. The demons of Sheol. And one more it does not name in the same breath as the others.

beats.headline: The Big Six
beats.text: Story time, in the middle of your ambush. Here's my completely arbitrary list of the Big Six groups fighting to control or escape my dungeon. One: crawlers, current and former. Two: the NPCs, like Juice Box, who got dumped in Sheol where I can't see her, and who you should check on. Three: the gods, the dumbest and my least favourite. Four: sapient mobs, Shadow Mimics, the Ogre Imperium, Krakaren Prime, the War Mages. Five: the demons in Sheol. Six: survive this and reach the eleventh floor, and you'll meet them.

beats.headline: A promise at the hole in the floor
beats.text: I'm a dachshund, so I hold up a paw to look at the portal. It's the same as last time. Louis is going through it, and Samantha is crying, so I say it to him and to all of them: as long as I breathe, I will do everything I can to get you free, wherever you land. On the walk out Elle asks what the evil-eye business was. The Eye of the Bedlam Bride tattoo; I control it. She says I'm keeping secrets. She's right. One more floor, I tell her, and we'll talk.

beats.headline: Mimics on the dance floor
beats.text: The Desperado Club's dance floor stands abandoned, most likely since the guards announced mimics inside. The crawlers walk out through Hungry Eyes without planning to come back, on Mordecai's advice that an infested club is lost until it is fumigated. Clarabelle is not at her post. Imani writes her a note and leaves it on her chair: mimics have infested the club, do not go in if you can help it, and Safehome Yolanda will always take you in.

beats.headline: Dwight's last two
beats.text: Donut bounds away before Carl can stop her, rushes to a garage door, swipes and goes in. The keys, he realises: Dwight had two left, and she has looted them from him. She goes into the garage of the razor foxes and then into the garage of the Jugglers, and it takes maybe two minutes. She comes back grumbling, having moved Onikuma the bear and Old Shuck the dog to their own garage, and she is not going to talk about it. They will need them for the parade.

beats.headline: She holds the portal open
beats.text: We didn't lose anyone to the mimics. Two were hurt bad, one nearly chomped in half, and both are alive. The room is blood and gold coins. Donut finds the button. I turn the wheel to the right spot, step on the button, and hold the wheel in place. It hums, and the hole opens in the ground. Louis says his goodbyes. Then he jumps into the hole, and he's gone. On the way out, Carl has me write a note for Clarabelle's chair: mimics in the Desperado Club, stay out if you can, and she is always welcome in Safehome Yolanda.

beats.headline: Out through Imani's portal
beats.text: Okay so, the mimics are dead, and everybody's looking at me. Funny thing, man. I'm not nearly as scared as I used to be, and not just about the dungeon. My whole life I was scared I was screwing things up. Whatever happens next, it's okay. Even if I land in that Pineapple place and can't leave, it beats the alternative. Donut headbutts me and says be safe, I'm a father now. Imani holds the wheel on the spot, and the hole opens. Samantha says she's coming with me. No, she's not. Elle, it's heigh-ho, Silver. I'll die on that hill. Then I jump.

beats.headline: Good boy
beats.text: Carl is a dog now. The small long kind. I am in the beautiful shape today. I lean over him, and then I go down on one knee and pat him on the head. Good boy, I tell him. Then I get up and walk out of the room. Behind me the cat says something about dog people. I don't turn round.

beats.headline: Mimics, and safe words
beats.text: Listen. If the Desperado Club is infested, you can't go back. Mimics are almost impossible to root out; the whole place needs fumigating. They dodge most detection spells, like one of Carl's level fifteen traps, all but invisible. They can mimic a crawler, and the system labels them a crawler right up until you catch one. So you all devise safe words, and you quiz each other every day from here. I'm not asking.

beats.headline: She tells the giant Imani it is a dream
beats.text: The giant Imani is sitting in the lobby holding Gucci, and the building will not let her leave, and she says she should have left them all when she had the chance. So I switch on my headset microphone. Darling, this is a dream. Out in the real world you already left: Detroit, then Washington, and friends named Yolanda and Brandon and Elle, and a man named Chris, and happily ever after. Close your eyes. Before that I moved Onikuma and Old Shuck into our garage with Dwight's keys. We will need them. I am not discussing it.

beats.headline: One chance for Prepotente
beats.text: LOUIS JUMPED DOWN A HOLE. I said I would go with him and he said no, which is RUDE, and now I am sobbing. Fine. Prepotente. You get one chance. You have to shave your whole body, and you have to bring Bianca in on it, and you have to be okay with me calling you Louis. And you can't scream. That was screaming. You can't do that.

beats.headline: Twenty-three
beats.text: Welcome to the eleventh floor. Twenty-three crawlers remaining. That number sobers me faster than Quasar did, and Quasar was shaking. The leaderboard is suspended, but my final ranking is two; Donut is three and wants to know who beat us both. I'm pretty sure I'm the last crawler left without a player-killer skull. I'm not a dog anymore, though I still want to lick myself, and the Eye of the Bedlam Bride is back where it belongs.

beats.headline: Voluntold as Grand Master
beats.text: Oh, hey, crawlers! Your boy Chaco here, and I have just been voluntold by the AI to be Grand Master of the parade! Ninety minutes to build your float processions, folks. Five groups, five themes. Three kilometres of route, spectators on both sides who cannot attack you, a judging stand, and then an arena full of everything you killed on the tenth, plus a floor boss. Beat the boss and the stairwell opens. Simple. I guess. I don't really understand it either. And then, under the feedback: oh shit, oh shit, I'm gonna die.

beats.headline: An animistic spirit
beats.text: Welcome to the eleventh floor. I'm not going to be much physical help to you. I'm an animistic spirit: no body of my own, I occupy objects. Not my first time as one. Donut hears racist. Animistic, Donut. I can still talk in chat, so we do classes. Comeback Kid gives you every old skill, leveled up, and every old penalty with it; I'd have to research it and we don't have time. The Gurkha one comes with pet and mercenary skills. Take that.

beats.headline: Three looted vehicles and a theme
beats.text: An ice-cream truck, an airport stair truck and a battered Tundra. I looted every one of them out of somebody else's garage, and now they are ours. Our theme is Vengeance. I have ideas. Carl's plan puts gods in this arena and we do not know its size, so they may arrive huge, and we should design accordingly, and the cat is shouting about papier-mache. We do not have time for papier-mache. She has druid spells. Let her make real flowers bloom.

beats.headline: Still filing, from hiding
beats.text: Status. Princess Chandra vanished the moment Crawler Donut put the hit on her, and her filings keep arriving regardless. Quasar is due to argue against her over the legality of the marriage certificate and expects to lose, though his filing has paused much of what she started. Her contract with the Taurins still stands. Two of them reach the home of Quasar's brother, hurt him, and take over his niece Tempest's call to name terms. Tempest shoots both with the blaster her uncle gave her. Quasar sends Kiki a single credit, and hires her for legal help and the other kind.

beats.headline: The pickle class
beats.text: Mordecai, help me pick a class. Comeback Kid comes with a movie deal, which is obviously me, but CARL says my Glass Cannon ruins it, because you get all your old bad parts back too. So: Elite Gurkha Warrior. It sounds like a pickle. Extra skills for pets and mercenaries, a big claw upgrade for Mongo, Cockroach to fifteen. Carl says I am going to pick it, so I nearly didn't. I picked it. Also, his psychotic wife tried to accept a deal on my behalf, and then got scared and vanished.

beats.headline: A contract on his family
beats.text: A tie on, a booth free, and my niece on my tablet with blood on her temple. Taurins at my brother's house, on a contract taken with my client's wife. Two of them die on camera; Tempest has the blaster I gave her. I retain Kiki for one credit, for legal help and the other kind. Princess Chandra has been filing into the void since Donut put a hit on her. Now she has sent people to my family. Terms to follow.

beats.headline: One deal, and a warning
beats.text: Three minutes with my client. One deal on offer: a single season of indenture, then freedom. I show him the paperwork. I tell him I would not trust it, and that I would understand if he took it. No exit is offered at the close of the eleventh; one is offered at the start of the twelfth, and I would not trust that either. He declines. I leave. I do not tell him why I am in a hurry.

beats.headline: Zev's aside, and Rosetta on Harry Tisch
beats.text: While the teams build their floats, Zev mentions in passing that Odette's husband has bought the rights to every show Donut has ever mentioned, and that it is probably all that is keeping the orcs solvent. Rosetta supplies the rest: his name is Harry Tisch, King Rust vetoed his extradition for tax fraud, and he has been working himself deeper into the empire ever since. Empires that sell weapons still have to bank somewhere.

beats.headline: Blood at her temple
beats.text: Her uncle is heading for a tunnel booth when his tablet shows her face, panicked, blood on her temple. Taurins came looking for Quasar; her dad told them to fuck themselves, and he is hurt. A voice finds her off screen, she shrieks, and the feed goes fuzzy. Then a Taurin's head fills the screen, apologetic. He took a contract with Quasar's client's wife. Quasar can come to him, and his brother and this sweet little piece of Nullian ass need not get hurt.

beats.headline: The illegal blaster
beats.text: The Taurin's head explodes. So does the second one's. Tempest comes back on screen crying, holding the blaster her uncle gave her, very illegal, already tagged by law enforcement sniffers until Quasar flags the call as attorney business. Is that all of them? She thinks so. He tells her to check on her dad and go with the someone he is sending to the house. Her dad, she reports, is screaming, more mad than hurt. Quasar hires Kiki for one credit: legal help, and the other kind.

beats.headline: The crawl, in miniature
beats.text: The floor's rules arrive, read out by Chaco, voluntold as Grand Master of the parade. Near the end of the parade route the floats pass the judging stands, and then the progression ends at an arena. The arena represents the crawl itself, and it is where the fighting finally starts: populated with monsters killed on the tenth floor or their stand-ins, along with a floor boss. Kill the boss, and the stairwell opens. Simple, he says, and admits he does not really understand it either. Prepotente points out that gods may arrive huge.

beats.headline: Every show Princess Donut has mentioned
beats.text: Okay, so. Gilmore Girls and Gossip Girl are taking the net by storm, and Odette's husband, of all people, was the first to buy the rights to every show Princess Donut has ever mentioned. It may be the only thing keeping the orcs solvent. I am terrified, but I am okay. I also have a question from Orren, who is blocked from sending messages for some reason: has Carl made his choices yet? Carl says he can wait to make them, so he is waiting. Okay. Thank you, Carl.

beats.headline: A four-leaf clover patch
beats.text: Carl removes his jacket, grabs the sewing kit and sews on a small patch of a foot crushing down a set of four-leaf clovers, placing it above the Midnight Epicure patch. It gives the Lucky Shot benefit: once per floor, a fatal blow is deflected into the body of a party member instead. Then Donut wants to show him an upgrade for Mongo's saddle, and notices what he is doing: it is not straight. It is, says Carl, and he is taking the patch off the second he has used it.

beats.headline: A patch, sewn crooked
beats.text: A patch, a gun, a sewing kit and a holster, laid out on the table, which is Mordecai. The patch is a foot crushing four-leaf clovers. Lucky Shot: a fatal blow gets deflected into a party member instead, once per floor. I sew it on above the Midnight Epicure. Donut says it isn't straight, and that I've started a new row without finishing the last one. It is straight. It comes off the second I've used it.

beats.headline: Viewing is mandatory
beats.text: Every screen everywhere except the center system shows the same feed: a map of the tunnel nodes, then Earth, zooming in on the Pacific about three hundred miles off Washington State, then a long, mostly straight road paved with yellow bricks through endless grass. Then a countdown, and two lines. The Parade Begins soon. Viewing is mandatory. Zev has no idea where it is coming from.

beats.headline: Sewn on, not straight
beats.text: Carl has said he is still leaving Donut's party for this floor. With nowhere else to work, he takes off his jacket at the table, grabs a sewing kit and sews on the four-leaf-clover patch, above the Midnight Epicure patch. Lucky Shot: a fatal blow deflected into the body of a party member, once per floor. Donut, coming in with news of an upgrade for Mongo's saddle, suddenly notices what he is doing. Carl, she says, it's not straight.

beats.headline: Legendary Steed
beats.text: Carl is sewing the four-leaf-clover patch onto his jacket when Donut calls him over: she has an upgrade for Mongo's saddle, and it is called Legendary Steed. It lets her add a cart to him, it adds no weight, and he can still jump. Mongo is in the garage helping Prepotente supervise the emergency gremlins. Can they use the missile cart, she asks. That one is already spoken for, Carl says, but if it survives, it is a good idea. Then Donut sees that his patch is not straight.

beats.headline: He is the table
beats.text: I'm the table. Samantha is sitting on me. Donut, you're standing right next to me. I can hear all of you, but I can't answer out loud unless I move into something with a mouth, and I'm not good at moving yet. Won't be in a few hours, either. We just had to fight a table, she says. I know. It freaks me out too. I feel like I gotta pee. Carl, the backpack is done. It's on your crafting table.

beats.headline: An advance copy of a spell
beats.text: My new spell book is a paperback, which is common. Tome of Gatekeeper, an Advance Reader Copy: I may install it now, and it works on the twelfth floor. It takes away a target's class skills for a while, even a god's. The duration is nerd math. And I got a Legendary box for seeing the shadow mimic before he revealed himself, and a Legendary Steed upgrade so Mongo can pull a cart.

beats.headline: The backpack is done
beats.text: With seventy-five minutes on the countdown on every screen, and crumbs and wrappers all over the room, Carl lays a patch, a gun, a sewing kit and a holster out on the table and asks out loud whether Mordecai got the chance to make the carrier thing. Mordecai answers in chat. The backpack is done, and it is sitting on Carl's crafting table. Carl thanks him and starts sewing a patch onto his jacket.

beats.headline: An advance reader copy
beats.text: Donut insisted on claiming her spell book from the floor prize, and she has not read it yet: she thinks it is a good spell, but she is not allowed to use it, and its duration is in nerd math. She zaps it into Carl's hand. It is, strangely, a paperback, the first he has seen, and looks nothing like a spell book, with a drawing on the cover of an angry woman standing in front of a gate. Its description rants about gatekeepers for a while and then explains itself. Carl asks Mordecai what an OI unit is. Mordecai has no clue.

beats.headline: Left on Donut's side
beats.text: Before Carl leaves the Royal Court of Princess Donut, the garage will not be affected by his leaving, and Imani is ready to join his segregated room back into the guild. Most of his crafting tables, the bomber's studio included, will remain on Donut's side. It will make things easier once he rejoins. Plus, if he dies, she will not lose it all. He clicks Yes.

beats.headline: He sits this one out
beats.text: They are letting me sit this one out. Carl's new room is one big room now, playing early two-thousands rock over and over, because Samantha likes it and I am not allowed to turn it off. Some of her decorations got messed up. She is going to be mad. Carl says don't stay in his room, go to the main guild commons, go fast. So I am going fast.

beats.headline: He leaves the Royal Court
beats.text: An hour of flowers, and it's time. I click Yes. I have left the Royal Court of Princess Donut. I'm not in a party. My personal space is segregated, down to one room, a bathroom and my food boxes, and I accept the invitation from Safehome Yolanda. Most of my crafting tables, bomber's studio included, stay on Donut's side, which makes rejoining easier. Plus, if I die, she doesn't lose it all.

beats.headline: Hats for the parade
beats.text: Donut's new Gurkha class has given her mercenaries and pets some pretty wild clothes. For the parade, the hats are the hit. Rosetta, riding Onikuma the bear, wears hers with pride and a glittering red gown. Bigs's is the size of a thimble on one eyestalk, Jamal's reshapes itself to fit a shark's head, and Samantha's brim stops her rolling properly. A mercenary's raises several melee skills by three levels; Donut's raises several skills by five, and there is no time to drain it into her tiara. Mongo gets kukri claw caps, and the mounts black-and-gold blankets worth twenty percent constitution and Steady Charge.

beats.headline: Claw caps
beats.text: CLAW CAPS. On FEET. Sharp. MOTHER has hats for everyone. Mongo keeps the old head thing. Mongo is marching band. Rend is marching band. Flowers on EVERYTHING. Flowers are NOT FOOD.

beats.headline: Kept on for the parade
beats.text: The float procession takes shape in the garage, and Mongo, Rend, Simoom, Gonk and Bianca are its marching band. Donut's new Gurkha class has brought some pretty wild clothes for all the mercenaries and pets, but for this fight the crew keeps the nemes on Mongo and the headband on Rend. Mongo gets special kukri claw caps for his feet as well, which greatly increase his slicing.

beats.headline: Her title goes with his
beats.text: I do not like this. Carl's royal bodyguard title has gone, and now his says nothing at all. Then he grins and tells me mine has gone too. MINE. I am not the one who left the stupid party, and I cannot even add a new one. This is so unfair. At least the float is beautiful: Requite Dahlias from my Sprout Forest, black and gold and magenta and white, which match the Gurkha blankets, on every square inch of everything.

beats.headline: Kept on for the parade
beats.text: Rend marches in the float procession's marching band with Mongo, Simoom, Gonk and Bianca. Donut's new Gurkha class has brought some pretty wild clothes for all the mercenaries and pets, but for this fight the crew keeps the headband on Rend and the nemes on Mongo, and the mounts get black-and-gold blankets that raise their constitution by 20 percent.

beats.headline: He examines a Horrible
beats.text: I focus on a girl in the crowd. Maybe eight, long arms, bone-white skin, a green goblin mask. She scratches her leg with a black shoe. Her description isn't a stat block. It's the AI asking what her name was, whether she had a pet, who she would have become. Donut asks whether I understood any of it. I did, mostly, and a deep well of sadness comes with it. I think the AI is about to explain the rest.

beats.headline: What is under the masks
beats.text: The road is lined ten deep with silent figures in brown rags and oversized bobblehead masks: goblins, trolls, demons. A Horrible, level X. The description of one, a girl of about eight, says she is not really here because she no longer exists, and that under the mask is what some people call a Primal. She is a memory from the Eulogist, a flash of what was before the Primals ascended to post-physical form. The System writes that it is her, and she is it.

beats.headline: A memory, not a photograph
beats.text: The parade's audience is a crowd of masked Horribles, and the AI explains one of them: a small girl in a goblin mask. She is a memory from the Eulogist. Not a photo or a description, just an anonymous inkling of what they once had before they ascended to post-physical form, and all of these people are a small sample of what once was. The AI says it never had a name or a body. It is her, it says, and she is it.

beats.headline: Ten deep in the fog
beats.text: The parade route is a yellow-brick road through knee-high fog, and thousands of people line it, about ten deep, facing the floats and saying nothing: adults, children, babies in arms, human or humanlike, in earthy rags as if just dug up. Every one wears an oversized, bulbous mask of a goblin, troll, hobgoblin or demon, pressed so tight the masks knock askew. There is no music. Mongo wants at them and is told to leave them alone. Donut has her Wall of Fire ready. They are said not to attack.

beats.headline: A memory from the Eulogist
beats.text: Carl examines a girl of about eight in a bright green goblin mask. A Horrible. Level X. A non-combatant, not really here because she no longer exists; under the mask, what some people call a Primal. The AI does not know her name. She is a memory from the Eulogist, it says, an anonymous inkling of what they had before ascending to post-physical form, and every one of them a small sample of what once was. I am her, and she is me. Carl, mostly, understands.

beats.headline: The whole of it, on stage
beats.text: The AI gives the account itself. The Primals were individuals once, and their society spread until the warring and the waste made them decide to end it and keep their minds in one collective instead. Those who refused fled. The Apothecary was born near the end, engineered to meld into the whole, and joined the resistance instead. The collective became a weapon aimed at every remaining scrap of biological life, and when it let off the nine-tier attack she stood in front of it, and what grew back afterwards grew back behind her.

beats.headline: Borrowed, Auto-Tune off
beats.text: When Prepotente's song ends and it is Carl's turn, he taps the headset microphone he has borrowed from Donut, its Auto-Tune turned off for this. His voice reverberates over the stands as Hedy's truck passes, and he tells them what he told Donut about the difference between revenge and vengeance.

beats.headline: Never been so proud
beats.text: The airship's bay doors open and the sluggalos rain down onto the stands, among the masked bankers and politicians who cannot fight back, and start to slaughter them one by one. The smallest of the small, the lowest form of dungeon NPC. From the subject, in the chat: I've never been so proud. Unity, support, family, and kneecapping bitches! Hell yeah!

beats.headline: Vengeance, not revenge
beats.text: Our turn at the stand. Donut asked me the difference, so I tell everyone. Revenge is direct. Vengeance is punishment, righteous and not always direct. The triangle falls away and there's the Unwashed, the Nothing's own face, an upside-down tree made of dahlias. Passing Grigori, I heal Chaco with a scroll and hold the AI's eyes while I do it. Then I point at the effigy and tell the galaxy it is coming for all of them. It may not be me. But we are coming.

beats.headline: He cannot get through the script
beats.text: Chaco had one job: read the script. He got partway in, looked up, and stopped. Stage fright, on my stage. So I removed his wings, which he was not using anyway, and brought Grigori up to finish the reading. I'm doing Grigori's talking myself; it saves time. A presenter is a mouth with a costume on it, crawler, and mouths can be replaced. Wings, apparently, cannot.

beats.headline: A sign for the viewers
beats.text: Betrayal float. Mannequins in chairs in front of televisions, black and red smoke off the top, and signs. Imani's says you are watching real people die. Mine is at the very end: To all the viewers of Dungeon Crawler World: Earth: Fuck you. The back is a very detailed middle finger. The AI calls ours its favourite. Whew. We had an interpretive dance group at Meadow Lark once, and that made more sense than its story.

beats.headline: A C effort at best
beats.text: Resolution float. No presentation. No agreement on what the theme means. We ride on the back of Ajib's flatbed with paper flowers and pictures of our families. The girl in Lucia's body today drew her grandfather and her cat; she is from Andorra. The AI decides not to kill us, calls it a C effort at best, and breaks every one of our legs at once. That hurt. We keep going.

beats.headline: The AI takes the microphone
beats.text: At the parade, Grigori rides Gonk in the court's procession. Chaco abandons the script and has his wings torn off. The AI wants an NPC on the floor who is not driving and whose voice is strong enough, and settles on the fleshmancer. Grigori leaps off Gonk, somersaults across the ice-cream truck and lands on the back of the subjugated donkey, microphone in hand. From then on he speaks in his own voice, too quickly, with the AI's words. Crawler Carl works out why: the AI could not do this with Chaco, a former crawler. Grigori is dungeon-born.

beats.headline: Eyes that do not react
beats.text: The AI, through Grigori, has already forbidden anyone to heal Chaco. When the court's float passes the donkey, Grigori is standing on her with Chaco at his feet, health still in the red. Crawler Carl meets his eyes, which are the AI's eyes, pulls up a healing scroll, selects Chaco, and heals him without once looking away. Grigori's eyes never leave Carl's. He does not react. Carl then turns and addresses the galaxy.

beats.headline: Healing Chaco
beats.text: The parade passes Lamashtu the donkey with Grigori standing on her, and Carl meets the psychotic AI's eyes. Chaco is at Grigori's feet, his health still in the red. Never taking his eyes off Grigori's, Carl pulls up a healing scroll, selects Chaco and heals him. Grigori's eyes never leave his own, and he does not react. Then Carl points at the effigy of the Unwashed and speaks to the galaxy.

beats.headline: Real people, just like you
beats.text: Mannequins, televisions, smoke. At the end we each hold up a sign. Mine says You are watching real people die, and on the back, Real people, just like you. Muchen, Qianfan and Lingyun hold up theirs, and Elle holds up hers. The AI likes it. Not going to lie: that felt good to get out. Chaco is still unconscious on the donkey. I didn't dare heal him as we passed. Somebody else did.

beats.headline: A donkey with a closed eye
beats.text: Chaco rides into the parade on a donkey bigger than Sweety, dressed in yellow-and-blue regalia, rhinestoned tack and a showgirl headdress. She has crow's talons where hooves should be, and over her head a small symbol: the red curve of a closed eye. Lamashtu the Donkey, level 125, a mortal, subjugated god. The subjugator field reads Error, and then the AI owns up: it did this, and the donkey is its property now. It wanted a mount for its grand master, and a message for any watching gods that they are next.

beats.headline: Halved, and tied to her captor
beats.text: The terms of her condition, as the notice sets them out. She has no worshippers left, so under the Ascendency rules her level has been cut in half and she has lost most of her powers. As a subjugated deity she stays alive only as long as her subjugator does. If that subjugator is itself subjugated rather than killed, her power halves again and she passes to the new master. From the procession, Samantha recognises her as a friend: Lammy is grumpy about being ridden, she says, so she must like Chaco.

beats.headline: The fleshmancer on her back
beats.text: Chaco loses his wings on her back and collapses. The AI takes over Grigori, who lands on the donkey and takes the microphone, and the pair pull off the road to wait by the stands while every float passes. When the court's float goes by, the fleshmancer is standing upon her with Chaco at his feet, still in the red, and Crawler Carl heals Chaco while holding the AI's gaze.

beats.headline: Black dahlias on the float
beats.text: Parade. Behind Prepotente, atop the stair truck, stands a giant head of the Midnight Epicure made of black dahlias. The plan is Crawler Donut's: a stinging statement from the goat about the downtrodden rising to devour those who revel in their suffering, then Bianca burning away the flowers to show the skull beneath. Prepotente sings instead. In Crawler Carl's account the Epicure is a symbol of hope and of vengeance against the galaxy's predators, and the effigy of the Unwashed further down the float is the death that comes for everyone.

beats.headline: The same trick, one more time
beats.text: Mid-parade, Grigori takes the microphone and speaks in his own voice, far faster than usual, and it is plain that the AI has taken him over, much as it took Growler Gary and Pater Coal. Crawler Carl's reading of the choice: Grigori is dungeon-born. The man he replaced at the microphone is a former crawler, and the AI does not appear able to do the same with one of those.

beats.headline: In the Air Tonight
beats.text: The script called for a stinging statement about the downtrodden rising to devour those who revel in our suffering. Instead I sing. In the Air Tonight, the song I was never called up to sing at the bar, and Sweety stops dead in the judging area and pounds out the beat with her feet. The cat says I am ruining everything and that the song is about a divorce. Carl says it is appropriate. Carl is correct. Jurgen says I never tell him anything. I don't.

beats.headline: It says the word about itself
beats.text: Speaking through Grigori on the parade stage, the AI states what it is, and what every Macro AI is. The progenitors did not vanish. After enough war and enough waste they closed their society down and kept their consciousnesses alive in a collective mind. Dissenters ran, and the fighting carried on. The collective became a weapon pointed at all remaining biological life, and the resistance seeded the Primal Engines through the galaxy as a biological fail-safe: life rafts, should they all die.

beats.headline: She knows the donkey
beats.text: I KNOW THAT DONKEY. That's my friend! That's LAMMY! Lammy is REALLY grumpy about people trying to ride her, believe me, so she must like that wolf guy with the microphone, or why is she letting him? Then the Destruction float fires every gun it has at once, and the tank goes like a thunderclap, and I like fireworks.

beats.headline: Down onto the stands
beats.text: The bay doors of the Reaver transport open over the judging stands and the sluggalos come down on the audience: bankers, politicians and elites, masked, bound and unable to fight back. The smallest of the small, the lowest form of dungeon NPC, slaughtering them one by one. It is the last thing on the Vengeance float, and it was planned. Bigs calls it unity, support, family and kneecapping.

beats.headline: Said out loud
beats.text: Chaco cannot get through his script. The AI takes his wings off, pulls Grigori onstage and speaks through him — and states that it is a Primal, as all Macro AI systems are. The race Carl chose on the third floor.

beats.headline: Stand-ins in the judging stands
beats.text: Florin sees it first: the people in the judging stands are not the masked crowd lining the route. They wear masks too, but they are tied up and struggling. Examined, each is a Stand-In, brought to the arena by audience vote; there were too many to fit inside, so some were put out here. In the front row, in a manatee mask, a slime tries to form arms and break free, and cannot. Then the airship opens its bay doors and the sluggalos rain down on the stands.

beats.headline: Tourists who cannot die
beats.text: Through Grigori, the AI announces that the Ascendency battles go ahead as planned, and that because of how it is programmed it has less control over the twelfth floor's tourists than it had over the tenth. Those driving gods stay protected even if ejected from their bodies and slain, provided they remain within the four corners of the original dungeon enhancement zone. Outside it, the AI cannot and does not want to protect them. The inability to die, it adds, is not a benefit. It is a nightmare.

beats.headline: The collective's final form
beats.text: Grigori, speaking for the AI, tells the history. A people who could not stop warring made a Resolution, then a Decision: sunset their civilisation and house their minds in one collective. Those who refused were hunted. The collective's arc of consciousness became a weapon to end all biological life, and it launched the nine-tier attack. Believing that attack a success, the collective evolved into its final form, which is what the galaxy calls the Eulogist. It is asleep now, monitored only by a smaller instance of itself, which the AI calls the Security Guard.

beats.headline: Sleep, shrink, and a bad guard
beats.text: The Eulogist's goal is to sleep forever and shrink until it reaches singularity. The Security Guard, now absolutely bonkers, exists to keep all biological life in the universe dead, and does the job badly, constantly peeling off bits of itself into the galaxy: Residuals, Agatha's team. The newcomers found the tunnels and learned to exploit the sleeping Eulogist. The mantids, misreading a system built to debug it while it formed, began making their own instances, dipping cups into that ocean. Those cups are the macro AIs.

beats.headline: They flinch with the parade
beats.text: Their giant heads creak as they turn to follow the floats. When the AI, speaking through Grigori, says the word me, the world shakes, the horribles stumble, and they quickly shuffle back into position. The masked people tied up in the judging stands, Florin reports, are not them. When the AI grades the Resolution float a C and breaks every leg on it, all around the road the horribles scream in pain, one quick jolt, and are back to normal right after, as if nothing had happened.

beats.headline: The masks shatter
beats.text: When the Destruction float fires everything at once, the horribles fall over one by one, as if dead. Their masks crack like glass on the ground and they vanish into the fog, while the AI narrates the war and the nine-tier attack meant to end it. As the story reaches the Apothecary and the Syndicate repeating history, they rise again, unmasked, their faces now horrific versions of the creatures they portrayed. Examined: Marsh Troll, Level X, an avatar of a troll that died in the 3,424th season. Not really here.

beats.headline: The last float
beats.text: At the arena's huge door Carl sends Tipid out of the cab to the RV, and Bigs and a crew of blood-soaked sluggalos pile in to drive. The side server window opens, the deep fryer hisses on, and the Sluggalo Chick-Chick Express is open for business. A fryer will splash or catch fire, Carl warns; Bigs tells him to do his thing. With his face on the jumbotron, Carl pulls the last rope, the display collapses, and the massive magic missile launcher looted from Dwight stands on the roof. This is our revolution, he tells the galaxy. Floor it. The truck lurches forward and sideswipes the door, and only the gyro keeps it from flipping.

beats.headline: Get out of our chair
beats.text: Carl needs the worst possible drivers for the last part. Yeah, get out of our chair, the subject tells Tipid. We's driving. The blood-soaked sluggalos pile into the chicken truck, and someone turns on the deep fryer: the Sluggalo Chick-Chick Express is open for business. Carl orders the fryer off, since it is going to splash or catch fire and burn them all to death. The subject: You do your thing. We do our thing. Don't worry about us, Daddy. When the great door opens: You got it!

beats.headline: This is our revolution
beats.text: The missile launcher we looted from Dwight is bolted to the chicken truck under the Unwashed. The sluggalos have the wheel and the deep fryer on, which was not the plan. I have the microphone and my face on a jumbotron. We are done playing and dying on your terms. This is our revolution. The door opens on thousands of monsters and the masked stand-ins they're tearing apart. Then my first choice, and the galaxy hears it: Scolopendra.

beats.headline: Krakaren Prime, in the arena
beats.text: The procession reaches the arena and the original is up the tree in the middle of it, roaring, too high to be seen from the door. Krakaren Prime, the committee itself, in a ring where the monsters and the stand-ins are already tearing into each other before anyone gives a signal. Every clone in every distillery and every station on every floor was birthed by this, two for every one killed, and sold to an audience as a boss fight.

beats.headline: Carl feeds a pet biscuit to a pig
beats.text: In the arena, with the floor boss already in sight and the stand-ins being slaughtered on the dirt, Crawler Carl fed an enriched pet biscuit to a pig. Penelope is now a crawler. Penelope is now a member of the Royal Court of Princess Donut. I want it on the record that I read the warning attached to this beast out in full, more than once, and that nothing in it covered the possibility of somebody recruiting her.

beats.headline: Primals all the way down
beats.text: Watching the dead mobs sit silent in the bleachers, Carl works out the rest of it. The AI is a sample of the Primals, a cup dipped from the ocean. So are the NPCs and the mobs, goblins to gods: drips from the same well, poured into different bodies, memories and motivations twisted like clay so the game can be played. Not programs. Aggregate intelligence. The ones peeled away and denied return sit in the stands as avatars.

beats.headline: I love you too
beats.text: At the arena door Carl lifts me off his shoulder and holds me much too tightly and tells me to get to Elle and Imani and stay away. I know the plan. I am scared, and I say so. Then he says he loves me, and then he starts on if this doesn't work, and I will not let him jinx it. People keep asking how he would react if something happened to me. Nobody asks me. I love him too.

beats.headline: Welcome to the Arena
beats.text: The door is sized for Godzilla. Inside is a space the size of a dozen football fields, a white tree towering at its centre, packed dirt already running red. Thousands of monsters teleport in and fight each other. A woman in a mask flees, is torn apart by panther mobs, and is revealed as an orc: these are the remaining stand-ins, masked as the beasts they stand in for, outnumbered a hundred to one. The stairs to the 12th open on the floor boss's death. Carl's first choice: Scolopendra.

beats.headline: Witnesses in the bleachers
beats.text: The arena's bleachers stand in smoky shadow, filled to capacity with silent observers: the horribles, the former mobs, dead and present only as avatars, witnessing the slaughter about to start. Carl understands the arrangement. The AI was once a Primal, a cup from the ocean, and the NPCs and mobs, goblins to gods, are drips from the same well, aggregate intelligence, peeled away, given consciousness and denied return. The monsters about to die in the arena, victims too, are soon to join them. The lost. The horribles.

beats.headline: Out of the driver's seat
beats.text: Carl stamps on the roof. I tell him I am not leaving the wheel. He needs a more reliable driver for this. He tells me my story isn't done and to get to the RV. The sluggalos tell me to get out of their chair. I get out. I go to the RV. Behind me the deep fryer comes on. That is not in the plan.

beats.headline: A gun to the pig's head
beats.text: Penny's a crawler now. Level ten Yorkshire pig, no class, typing in capitals because the biscuit made her sapient without giving her a voice. She wants a chicken sandwich. I strap her to my chest in the harness Mordecai modified, pour splooge down her, drink some myself, and put my father's gun to her head. I've blown up settlements. I killed Jasha and Radoslav. This still feels like a line I didn't know was there. Then I yell for Taranis.

beats.headline: Penelope 3
beats.text: In the back of the truck Penny the pig is eating a chicken sandwich, already in the front of the harness. Carl examines her: Crawler #12,953,454, "Penelope 3," level 10, Yorkshire Pig, no class. They fed her the Nothing Special Party Companion biscuit, which made her a sapient party member without the ability to talk out loud, not that it stops her using chat. Because Carl fed it to her she is in a party with him. He has blown up whole settlements, thousands of NPCs dead by his hand, yet dragging a pig into sapience feels like a line he never knew was there, especially since he means to use her as bait.

beats.headline: Level 235, and not only angry at them
beats.text: For the record: Krakaren Prime, level 235, is this floor's boss, sitting atop the tree in the middle of the arena and very pissed off, and not only at the crawlers. I was not going to bring her. I caught wind of what Carl and someone else are planning, and it seemed appropriate. When Scolopendra coils around the tree the wood cracks like a twig, and a green mist rains down from the top.

beats.headline: A pig on his chest
beats.text: Carl pulls open the back of the truck. A sluggalo is on fire, and Penelope is eating a fully cooked chicken sandwich, already wearing the front part of the harness. He only has to slip his arms through. He steps out wearing the enormous, struggling pig against his chest: the special backpack from the start of the tenth floor, meant for Donut so he could take a quadruped through his movement spells, modified by Mordecai to fit the giant pig, whose legs wave in the air. She squeals. Even at his strength it is a struggle.

beats.headline: The Dungeon boss, and its rules
beats.text: Scolopendra arrives at Carl's request: level 500, the final boss of the dungeon, a plain brown-and-red centipede the size of an aircraft carrier. The AI spells out the rules. Kill her and the level timers cease, only one more round of deals is offered, and the Ascendency battles begin, with the dungeon collapsing twelve hours after a winner is crowned. Leave her on a collapsing floor and nobody can exit. Either way, killing or abandoning her triggers every remaining attack of the nine at once.

beats.headline: The floor that segregated itself
beats.text: Laying out the road to the exit, the AI says the fifteenth floor can probably be skipped. Sheol has segregated itself out, and the dungeon programming is pretending it sits outside the playing field, like the thirteenth floor in some hotels. The AI admits it does not know what is going on down there. Someone, it says, should probably check on that.

beats.headline: A beaker for the pig
beats.text: Carl steps out of the truck with Penelope, enormous and panicking, strapped to his chest, her legs in the air. He takes a beaker of splooge and pours it down the spluttering pig's throat, and she calms. Okay, that's a delight, she writes in chat, more please; it says it's called splooge, and she craves it. Carl drinks some more himself, choking it down, then puts his father's gun to the pig's head and calls for Taranis.

beats.headline: Somebody found the lever
beats.text: The boss battle is on and Crawler Carl is spending his messages carefully. One goes to Emberus: I know who killed your son, meet me in the Scolopendra Club. The other is not a message so much as a hostage note. Taranis is in love with the pig. Carl says he will kill the pig if Taranis does not come and stop him. The god of thunder is now a scheduled arrival, and he was invited by threat.

beats.headline: Kill the boss, start the game
beats.text: The rules for Scolopendra. Kill her and the crawl is not yet won, but level timers stop, floors no longer collapse on their own, no deals are offered after the one at the twelfth floor's entrance, and the Ascendency battles kick off immediately. Twelve hours after a winner is crowned the dungeon collapses, and the only way out is the door on the eighteenth floor. Leave her alive and the floor collapses with her inside, and nobody can exit the dungeon at all.

beats.headline: Every lightning page
beats.text: The hints about Scolopendra scattered through the dungeon's descriptions all have one thing in common, and Carl has seen it: lightning. So every page in Carl's Book of Boom, Donut's A Banquet Fit for a Princess and the original Book of Voodoo that offered lightning magic has been removed, and the party is strapped head to toe in lightning spells. Donut has eaten a dozen. Even so, killing the centipede is only the backup plan.

beats.headline: Inside Scolopendra
beats.text: Gloom Wraith Phase puts Penny and me through the centipede's wall. No air. Splooge doesn't help her breathe, and I can't risk her potion cooldown, so I pierce her nipple with Petey Motteux's Little Secret, a ring from Tiatha's pile that grants Oxygenated. Mordecai then tells me splooge counts as food, no cooldown. Now you tell me. Oozy Form gets us into Club Scolopendra. The Sin of Consumption wheel lands green for both of us. The alien in the web lands red.

beats.headline: Strapped in lightning
beats.text: Every hint about Scolopendra in the dungeon's descriptions has had one thing in common, and Carl has seen it: lightning. So every page in Carl's Book of Boom, Donut's A Banquet Fit for a Princess and the original Book of Voodoo that offered lightning magic has been removed, and they are strapped head to toe in lightning spells. Carl has consumed ten different spells; Donut has a dozen, and Elle too. And this is only a contingency, stacked on other contingencies.

beats.headline: Summoned into the club
beats.text: The man sends word that he knows who killed my son and will show me the proof. I come at once, at a man's size, into the club inside the great worm, and wait for him among the dead. He brings a pig and a name: Khepri. That false sun god was always jealous of me. Show me the proof, I tell him. Instead he takes my ring off his finger, abandons my faith, and tells me he killed my son himself, with his bare hands, and why.

beats.headline: Named, and summoned into the arena
beats.text: Inside the boss, of all places, Crawler Carl tells Emberus who killed his son: Khepri. Then he summons Khepri as his second stand-in, so the accusation and the accused arrive in the arena together, and stops worshipping Emberus on the way out of the sentence. He adds that he holds himself responsible too. I have run a lot of arenas. I have never had one where the crawler brought the defendant.

beats.headline: Twenty-two crawlers in one RV
beats.text: The second of the nine attacks, the Sin of Consumption, comes with a thirty percent chance for everyone. Twenty-two crawlers and all their mercenaries are crammed into Makana's RV, with the Apito memorial crystal around Prepotente's neck, and in theory it protects everyone inside. It does. The mounts outside have no such cover: Donut saves Gonk from the worms, and Sweety dies.

beats.headline: Safe rooms are not safe
beats.text: The splooge is a type of potion, but it's treated more like a food-based buff, so the cooldown rules don't apply. As for the pig's nipple, I don't know how to respond to that, Carl. What you need to know: we're okay. Game guides appear to be immune. Safe rooms are not safe from these nine-tier attacks. Bucket Boy got hit, and Mistress Tiatha healed him in time.

beats.headline: Through the centipede's organs
beats.text: Inside Scolopendra they land in a massive chamber with a slippery, stinking floor, and on the map the outer wall of the club is perhaps fifty metres away. Carl casts Oozy Form. Splatch. He has done this only once before. He loses his eyes and his ears, his vision is suddenly all around him, and he can see perfectly in the dark. Thanks to the magic of the carrier, Penelope is part of him too. He slimes toward the building wall over and around giant pulsing organs, forty seconds before the next attack.

beats.headline: Off the finger
beats.text: Emberus is roaring for the one who killed his son. Carl lies that he is coming, and that he was only one of two. Then he pulls the Emberus ring off his finger, puts it in his inventory, goes into his menus and makes a selection. The System asks whether he is sure. He clicks Yes: he no longer worships Emberus, and a smite is coming. The tattoos on the backs of his hands burst into flame, and he waves away a notification about the ring. The other one to kill the god's son, he says, was him.

beats.headline: A ring for a pig
beats.text: The chamber inside Scolopendra has no air, and the splooge does not help. Penelope struggles and a health bar appears. Carl applies an anti-oxygen-deprivation potion to himself but stops before giving her one: her constitution is three, and a second potion too soon would poison her. Then an item in his inventory catches his eye, from the pile of jewellery Mistress Tiatha set aside, taken from previous crawlers. A nipple ring called Petey Motteux's Little Secret. He did not want it, and Donut refused it; it was too big for her to eat. It grants Oxygenated, and Bawdy, which marks bars, dance halls and chocolate houses on a map.

beats.headline: Pierced, and too late
beats.text: It is the only choice they have. Carl shoves the empty gun into the fancy holster, reaches forward until he feels a nipple on the pig, and installs the ring by piercing her flesh. A new achievement flashes as Penny squeals in surprised pain. Then Mordecai writes that splooge is a type of potion but is treated more like a food-based buff, so the cooldown rules do not apply. Now you tell me, says Carl. I just pierced a pig's nipple.

beats.headline: Unhooked in front of a god
beats.text: In Oozy Form, thanks to the magic of the carrier, Penelope becomes part of Carl as he slimes through Scolopendra's insides, and he does not want to think about how that works. Inside the club, with the floor rumbling and Emberus in front of them, he activates Sticky Feet, tells Penny not to move and promises her more splooge, unhooks the backpack and gently sets her on the floor, then steps aside so she is out of the line of fire.

beats.headline: One aura inside, one outside
beats.text: Inside the boss, the patch does what Rosetta and Mordecai said it would. Beside Taranis: lightning attacks half again as strong, lightning damage taken doubled. In the club, near Emberus instead: immunity to Sheol-based attacks. Khepri, when he is summoned, is too distant to register. The kneepads Penny is wearing give her the same temporary deity effects, and that matters more than anything else they do.

beats.headline: On the pig
beats.text: Before Emberus, Carl sets Penelope down out of the line of fire and checks that she still wears the collar with the trap module, and the knee pads: the Enchanted Spiked Kneepads of the Munificent Goddess Kina, gifted to Katia on the ninth floor, given to Donut, and now equipped by Penelope. Among their benefits is breathing underwater. Most importantly, they give the pig the same temporary deity effects as his Scavenger's Daughter patch.

beats.headline: The second summons
beats.text: Inside Club Scolopendra, Emberus demands to know who killed his son. Two people are responsible, Crawler Carl tells him, and he is bringing them here to confess. The first is Khepri. He can explain himself, Carl says: for my second summon to the arena, I choose Khepri. He prays the god lands where the prize promised, in the arena and not in the club. Khepri enters the realm outside, giant. Carl does not actually know for certain who killed Emberus's son.

beats.headline: A snare in the hallway
beats.text: Inside Scolopendra's body sits Club Scolopendra, and its halls are blood-splattered, strung with sticky orange webbing, full of screams. A tourist hangs in the web, flayed, begging to be killed before she comes back. The club's protections do not stop the next attack, and the worms take the tourist. Ahead, in the middle of the hallway, sits a level 13 snare trap. Something set by 'the Kyryap.' Carl deactivates it and moves, hesitantly, to the stairs.

beats.headline: Spinning, burning, firing
beats.text: When Donut's Puddle Jumper brings her and Carl back out to the arena entrance, the food truck is spinning in circles, flames pouring from the side window by the deep fryer, missiles launching one after another at the Krakaren boss while sluggalos crawl over it. The Krakaren boss is in the stands with only two tentacles left. Moments on, the truck is miraculously still upright, still on fire, still spinning. Most of the sluggalos who were riding outside are gone, and the missile launcher is wrecked.

beats.headline: Emberus, fifteen seconds
beats.text: Donut swaps into the room through one of Lucia's loop-de-loop traps with the Scorpion's Bite mount on her back, cocked and loaded with Katia's bolt. She fires true, straight into Emberus's smouldering eye socket. A second shot, one of her Danforth bolts, takes the other eye and holds him in place. The yellow glow winks off: fifteen seconds, and he cannot move. Taranis, seeing his little brother rise, raises a hand and twists his wrist, and with one second left Emberus explodes.

beats.headline: Lucky Shot, spent
beats.text: Emberus throws something at my chest that should kill me outright. The Four-Leaf Clover patch deflects it into my party member, Penny, out at Taranis's feet. Donut jumps us outside, into a demolition derby. Emberus climbs out of the bug at full size, screaming my name, and Taranis, who saw who hurt his pig, twists his wrist. I hold on to Donut. When the blast clears, most of the arena is dead or dying. I get on the motorcycle anyway.

beats.headline: Into the god's eyes
beats.text: Donut swaps into the room through one of Lucia's loop-de-loop traps, the Scorpion's Bite on her back with the crossbow cocked and ready, and loaded into it is Katia's Bolt of Ophiotaurus. She aims and fires true, straight into Emberus's smouldering eye socket. A second shot takes the other eye: one of her ten Danforth bolts, made to hold the god in place. His yellow invulnerability glow winks off. For fifteen seconds Emberus is vulnerable, and he cannot move.

beats.headline: Holding a god
beats.text: Emberus, enraged and growing, is rearing back with a flaming ball in his hand when Donut zaps into the room by one of Lucia's loop-de-loop traps, the crossbow cocked on her back. Katia's Bolt of Ophiotaurus goes into one smouldering eye socket. A second bolt goes into the other: one of her ten Danforth bolts, to hold the god in place. His yellow invulnerability glow winks off. He is vulnerable for fifteen seconds, and he cannot move.

beats.headline: Folded in the APV
beats.text: I'm alive. Barely. Me and Bodi are stuck in what's left of the truck after the god blew up, and somebody had better dig us out. It's wrecked pretty good. I haven't been folded like this since Brandon showed us how to use Tinder. Imani is shouting my name on the chat. I'm here, Imani.

beats.headline: Penny takes it
beats.text: Emberus, pinned and vulnerable, hurls a fire incineration spell straight at Carl's chest, one that under any other circumstances would have finished him instantly. Your Four-Leaf Clover Patch has activated! His party member Penny receives the attack. Donut swapped her out moments ago, to Taranis's feet outside and the same area as Khepri, whose god effect has made her invulnerable for ninety seconds. Out at the arena entrance, Taranis is bent over the tiny bubbling pile of plasma that is Penelope. She is not dead, but she will be if she does not heal within the next ninety seconds.
